label: triangle
snippet: A triangle is a bounded planar region delimited by three straight lines, i.e. it is a polygon with three angles.

label: triangular-wave function
snippet: The arcsine is the inverse function of the sine. Therefore the composition function $$f: x\mapsto \arcsin(\sin{x})$$ is the identity map $x\mapsto x$ on the interval $[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}]$. On this interval, the inner function $\sin$ increases monotonically and continuously from its least value $-1$ to its greatest value 1; then the outer function $\arcsin$ (i.e. the angle corresponding the sine value) and the whole composition correspondingly grows from $-\frac{\pi}{2}$ to $\frac{\pi}{2}$.

label: trigonometric equations
snippet: A trigonometric equation contains values of given trigonometric functions whose arguments are unknown angles. The task is to determine all possible values of those angles. For obtaining the complete solution one needs the following properties of the trigonometric functions: \item Two angles have the same value of sine iff the angles are equal or supplementary angles or differ of each other by a multiple of full angle. \item Two angles have the same value of cosine iff the angles are equal or opposite angles or differ of each other by a multiple of full angle.

label: triple scalar product
snippet: The triple scalar product of three vectors is defined in $\mathbb{R}^3$ as $$\det\left[ {ccc}a_1&b_1&c_1 a_2&b_2&c_2 a_3&b_3&c_3 \right]=\vec{a}\cdot(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})\ā_1\det\left[ {cc}b_2 & c_2 b_3 & c_3 \right] - a_2\det\left[ {cc}b_1 & c_1 b_3 & c_3 \right] + a_3\det\left[ {cc}b_1 & c_1 b_2 & c_2 \right]$$ The determinant above is positive if the three vectors satisfy the right-hand rule and negative otherwise.

label: Turing computable
snippet: A function is Turing computable if the function's value can be computed with a Turing machine.

label: Turing machine
snippet: A Turing machine is an imaginary computing machine invented by Alan Turing to describe what it means to compute something.

label: Tychonoff fixed point theorem
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally convex topological vector space, and let $K\subset X$ be a non-empty, compact, and convex set. Then given any continuous mapping $f\colon K \to K$ there exists $x\in K$ such that $f(x)=x$.

label: type
snippet: Let $L$ be a first order language. Let $M$ be an $L$-structure. Let $B \subseteq M$, and let $a \in M^{n}$. Then we define the type of $a$ over $B$ to be the set of $L$-formulas $\phi(x,\bar{b})$ with parameters $\bar{b}$ from $B$ so that $M \models \phi(a,\bar{b})$. A collection of $L$-formulas is a complete $n$-type over $B$ iff it is of the above form for some $B,M$ and $a \in M^{n}$.

label: uncountable
snippet: Definition A set is uncountable if it is not countable. In other words, a set $S$ is uncountable, if there is no subset of $\N$ (the set of natural numbers) with the same cardinality as $S$.

label: uniform space
snippet: A uniform structure (or uniformity) on a set $X$ is a non empty set $\mathcal{U}$ of subsets of $X \times X$ which satisfies the following axioms: \item Every subset of $X\times X$ which contains a set of $\mathcal{U}$ belongs to $\mathcal{U}$. \item Every finite intersection of sets of $\mathcal{U}$ belongs to $\mathcal{U}$. \item Every set of $\mathcal{U}$ is a reflexive relation on $X$ (i.e. contains the diagonal). \item If $V$ belongs to $\mathcal{U}$, then $V' = \{(y,x): (x,y) \in V\}$ belongs to $\mathcal{U}$.

label: uniformly integrable
snippet: Let $\mu$ be a positive measure on a measurable space. A collection of functions $\{ f_\alpha \} \subset \Le^1(\mu)$ is \defnterm{uniformly integrable}, if for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists $\delta > 0$ such that \absB{ \int_E f_\alpha d\mu } < \epsilon whenever $\mu(E) < \delta$, for any $\alpha$.

label: uniqueness of cardinality
snippet: The cardinality of a set is unique. We will verify the result for finite sets only. Suppose $A$ is a finite set with cardinality $\mid A\mid=n$ and $\mid A\mid=m$. Then there exist bijections $f:\mathbb{N}_n\rightarrow A$ and $g:\mathbb{N}_m\rightarrow A$. Since $g$ is a bijection, it is invertible, and $g^{-1}:A\rightarrow\mathbb{N}_m$ is a bijection. Then the composition $g^{-1}\circ f$ is a bijection from $\mathbb{N}_n$ to $\mathbb{N}_m$. We will show by induction on $n$ that $m=n$.

label: uniqueness of measures extended from a $\pi$-system
snippet: The following theorem allows measures to be uniquely defined by specifying their values on a $\pi$-system instead of having to specify the measure of every possible measurable set. For example, the collection of open intervals $(a,b)\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ forms a $\pi$-system generating the Borel $\sigma$-algebra and consequently the Lebesgue measure $\mu$ is uniquely defined by the equality $\mu((a,b))=b-a$.

label: universal enveloping algebra
snippet: A universal enveloping algebra of a Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ over a field $k$ is an associative algebra $U$ (with unity) over $k$, together with a Lie algebra homomorphism $\iota:\mathfrak{g} \rightarrow U$ (where the Lie algebra structure on $U$ is given by the commutator), such that if $A$ is a another associative algebra over $k$ and $\phi:\mathfrak{g} \rightarrow A$ is another Lie algebra homomorphism, then there exists a unique homomorphism $\psi:U \rightarrow A$ of associative algebras such that the diagram \[\xymatrix{ \mathfrak{g} \ar[dr]_\phi \ar[r]^\iota & U \ar[d]^\psi & A} \]…

label: universal Turing machine
snippet: A universal Turing machine $U$ is a Turing machine with a single binary one-way read-only input tape, on which it expects to find the encoding of an arbitrary Turing machine $M$. The set of all Turing machine encodings must be prefix-free, so that no special end-marker or `blank' is needed to recognize a code's end. Having transferred the description of $M$ onto its worktape, $U$ then proceeds to simulate the behaviour of $M$ on the remaining contents of the input tape. If $M$ halts, then $U$ cleans up its worktape, leaving it with just the output of $M$, and halts too.

label: unlimited register machine
snippet: \subsubsection*{Informal Description} An unlimited register machine, or URM for short, is a mathematical abstraction of a very primitive computer, which consists of a tape, which is left-ended, and stretches indefinitely to the right (hence the word ``unlimited''). The tape is divided into squares called registers, as illustrated by the diagram below {|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c} \hline $r_1$ & $r_2$ & $r_3$ & $r_4$ & $r_5$ & $r_6$ & $r_7$ & $\cdots$ \hline Each register can store a single non-negative integer. The integer in the register is called the content of the register.

snippet: Since the Laplace transforms of the derivatives of $f(t)$ are polynomials in the transform parameter $s$ (see table of Laplace transforms), forming the Laplace transform of a linear differential equation with constant coefficients and initial conditions at $t = 0$ yields generally a simple equation (image equation) for solving the transformed function $F(s)$. Since the initial conditions can be taken into consideration instantly, one needs not to determine the general solution of the differential equation.

label: variety
snippet: Let $X$ be a scheme over a field $k$. Then $X$ is said to be an abstract variety over $k$ if it is integral, separated, and of finite type over $k$. Usually we simply say $X$ is a variety. If $X$ is proper over $k$, it is said to be complete. If the dimension of $X$ is one, then $X$ is said to be a curve. Some authors also require $k$ to be algebraically closed, and some authors require curves to be nonsingular.

label: Veblen's theorem
snippet: The edge set of a graph can be partitioned into cycles if and only if every vertex has even degree.

label: vector space
snippet: Let $F$ be a field (or, more generally, a division ring). A vector space $V$ over $F$ is a set with two operations, $+: V \times V \longrightarrow V$ and $\cdot: F \times V \longrightarrow V$, such that \item $(\u+\v)+\w = \u+(\v+\w)$ for all $\u,\v,\w \in V$ \item $\u+\v=\v+\u$ for all $\u,\v\in V$ \item There exists an element $\0 \in V$ such that $\u+\0=\u$ for all $\u \in V$ \item For any $\u \in V$, there exists an element $\v \in V$ such that $\u+\v=\0$ \item $a \cdot (b \cdot \u) = (a \cdot b) \cdot \u$ for all $a,b \in F$ and $\u \in V$ \item $1 \cdot \u = \u$ for all $\u \in V$ \item…

label: vector subspace
snippet: Definition Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $F$, and let $W$ be a subset of $V$. If $W$ is itself a vector space, then $W$ is said to be a vector subspace of $V$. If in addtition $V\neq W$, then $W$ is a proper vector subspace of $V$.

label: Vitali convergence theorem
snippet: Let $f_1, f_2, \dotsc$ be $\Le^p$-integrable functions on some measure space, for $1 \leq p < \infty$.

label: Vitali's Theorem
snippet: There exists a set $V\subset [0,1]$ which is not Lebesgue measurable. Notice that this result requires the Axiom of Choice.

label: von Neumann algebra
snippet: Let $H$ be an Hilbert space, and let $B(H)$ be the *-algebra of bounded operators in $H$.

label: Wagner's theorem
snippet: \newtheorem{thm}{Theorem} A graph is planar if and only if it contains neither $K_5$ nor $K_{3,3}$ as a minor, where $K_5$ is the complete graph of order 5 and $K_{3,3}$ is the complete bipartite graph of order 6. Wagner's theorem is equivalent to Kuratowski's theorem.

label: Wallis formulae
snippet: Wallis' formula expresses $\pi$ as an infinite product: $$\frac{\pi}{2} = \prod_{n = 1}^{\infty} \frac{4n^{2}}{4n^{2} - 1} = \frac{2}{1}\frac{2}{3}\frac{4}{3}\frac{4}{5} \cdots$$

label: wave equation
snippet: The wave equation is a partial differential equation which describes certain kinds of waves. It arises in various physical situations, such as vibrating strings, sound waves, and electromagnetic waves.

label: weak derivative
snippet: Let $f\colon \Omega\to \R$ and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_n)\colon \Omega\to \R^n$ be locally integrable functions defined on an open set $\Omega\subset \mathbf R^n$. We say that $g$ is the weak derivative of $f$ if the equality \[ \int_\Omega f \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial x_i} = - \int_\Omega g_i \phi \] holds true for all functions $\phi\in\mathcal C^\infty_c(\Omega)$ (smooth functions with compact support in $\Omega$) and for all $i=1,\ldots, n$.

label: weak Hopf C*-algebra
snippet: A weak Hopf $C^*$-algebra is defined as a weak Hopf algebra which admits a faithful $*$--representation on a Hilbert space. The weak C*--Hopf algebra is therefore much more likely to be closely related to a quantum groupoid than the weak Hopf algebra. However, one can argue that locally compact groupoids equipped with a Haar measure are even closer to defining quantum groupoids.

label: weaker version of Stirling's approximation
snippet: One can prove a weaker version of Stirling's approximation without appealing to the gamma function. Consider the graph of $\ln x$ and note that \[\ln(n-1)!\leq \int_1^n \ln x \mathrm{d} x\leq \ln n!\] But $\int \ln x \mathrm{d} x=x\ln x-x$, so \[\ln(n-1)!\leq n\ln n-n+1\leq \ln n!\] and thus \[n\ln n-n+1+\ln n\geq\ln(n-1)!+\ln n=\ln n!\geq n\ln n-n+1\] so \[\ln n-1+\frac{1}{n}+\frac{\ln n}{n}\geq\frac{1}{n}\ln n!\geq\ln n-1+\frac{1}{n}\] As $n$ gets large, the expressions on either end approach $\ln n-1$, so we have

label: Wedderburn-Artin theorem
snippet: If $R$ is a left semisimple ring, then $$R \cong \mathbb{M}_{n_1}(D_1) \times \cdot\cdot\cdot \times \mathbb{M}_{n_r}(D_r)$$ where each $D_i$ is a division ring and $\mathbb{M}_{n_i}(D_i)$ is the matrix ring over $D_i$, $i = 1, 2, \ldots, r$. The positive integer $r$ is unique, and so are the division rings (up to permutation).

label: Wedderburn's theorem
snippet: A finite division ring is a field.

label: Weierstrass approximation theorem
snippet: If $ f $ is a continuous real-valued function on a interval $ [a,b] $ then for all $ \varepsilon>0 $ there exists a polynomial $ P $ which satisfies $ |f(x)-P(x)|<\varepsilon \forall x\in [a,b] $ This theorem also holds for compact subsets of $ \Bbb{R}^n . $ The Stone-Weierstrass theorem is a generalization to even more general situations.

label: weight enumerator
snippet: Let $A$ be an alphabet and $C$ a finite subset of $A^*$. Then the complete weight enumerator of $C$, denoted by $\cwe_C$, is the polynomial in $|A|$ indeterminates $X_a$ labeled by the letters of $a\in A$ with integer coefficients defined by \cwe_C((X_a)_{a\in A}):=\Sum_{c\in C}\Prod_{a\in A}X_a^{\wt_a(c)}, where $\wt_a(c)$ is the $a$-weight of the string $c$.

label: weight (strings)
snippet: Let $A$ be an alphabet, $a\in A$ a letter from $A$ and $c\in A^*$ a string over $a$. Then the $a$-weight of $c$, denoted by $\wt_a(c)$, is the number of times $a$ occurs in $c$.

label: Weil divisors on schemes
snippet: Let $X$ be a noetherian integral separated scheme such that every local ring $\mathcal{O}_x$ of $X$ of dimension one is regular (such a scheme $X$ is said to be regular in codimension one, or non-singular in codimension one).

label: word
snippet: Given a set $\Sigma$, a word (or a string) over $\Sigma$ is a juxtaposition (variously called concatenation or multiplication) of a finite number of elements in $\Sigma$. The juxtaposition is taken as an associative binary operation on $\Sigma$. A word with zero number of elements is called an empty word, typically denoted by $\lambda$ or $\epsilon$. The set of words over $\Sigma$ is denoted $\Sigma^*$.

label: Wronskian determinant
snippet: Given functions $f_1, f_2, \dotsc, f_n$, then the Wronskian determinant (or simply the Wronskian) $W(f_1, f_2, f_3, \dotsc, f_n)$ is the determinant of the square matrix \[ W(f_1, f_2, f_3, \dotsc, f_n) = \left\lvert {@{}ccccc@{}} f_1 & f_2 & f_3 & \cdots & f_n f_1' & f_2' & f_3' & \cdots & f_n' f_1'' & f_2'' & f_3'' & \cdots & f_n'' \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots f_1^{(n-1)} & f_2^{(n-1)} & f_3^{(n-1)} & \cdots & f_n^{(n-1)} \right\rvert \] where $f^{(k)}$ indicates the $k$th derivative of $f$ (not exponentiation).

label: Young inequality
snippet: Let $a,b>0$ and $p,q\in \left]0,\infty\right[$ with $1/p+1/q=1$. Then \[ ab \le \frac{a^p}p + \frac{b^q}q. \]

label: Young's inequality
snippet: Let $\phi : \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous , strictly increasing function such that $\phi(0)=0$ . Then the following inequality holds: $$ ab \leq \int_{0}^a \phi(x) dx + \int_{0}^b \phi^{-1}(y) dy $$ Equality only holds when $b = \phi(a)$. This inequality can be demonstrated by drawing the graph of $\phi(x)$ and by observing that the sum of the two areas represented by the integrals above is greater than the area of a rectangle of sides $a$ and $b$, as is illustrated in an attachment.

label: Zariski topology
snippet: Let $\A_k^n$ denote the affine space $k^n$ over a field $k$. The Zariski topology on $\A_k^n$ is defined to be the topology whose closed sets are the sets $$ V(I) := \{ x \in \A_k^n \mid f(x) = 0 for all f \in I\} \subset \A_k^n, $$ where $I \subset k[X_1, \ldots, X_n]$ is any ideal in the polynomial ring $k[X_1, \ldots, X_n]$. For any affine variety $V \subset \A_k^n$, the Zariski topology on $V$ is defined to be the subspace topology induced on $V$ as a subset of $\A_k^n$.

label: Zeta function of a group
snippet: Let $G$ be a finitely generated group and let $\mathcal{X}$ be a family of finite index subgroups of $G$. Define \[ a_n(\mathcal{X}) = |\{H \in \mathcal{X} \mid |G : H| = n\}|. \] Note that these numbers are finite since a finitely generated group has only finitely many subgroups of a given index. We define the zeta function of the family $\mathcal{X}$ to be the formal Dirichlet series \[ \zeta_{\mathcal{X}}(s) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n(\mathcal{X}) n^{-s}. \]

label: $\ell$-adic étale cohomology
snippet: Let $X$ be a scheme over a field $k$ having algebraic closure $\overline{k}$. Let $(X\otimes_k \overline{k})_ét$ be the small étale site on $X\otimes_k \overline{k}$, and let $\mathbb{Z}/l^n\mathbb{Z}$ denote the sheaf on $(X\otimes_k \overline{k})_ét$ associated to the group scheme $\mathbb{Z}/l^n\mathbb{Z}$ for some fixed prime $l$. Finally, let $\Gamma$ be the global sections functor on the category of étale sheaves on $(X\otimes_k \overline{k})_ét$.

label: étale fundamental group
snippet: Recall that in topology, the fundamental group $\pi_1(T)$ of a connected topological space $T$ is defined to be the group of loops based at a point modulo homotopy. When one wants to obtain something similar in the algebraic category, this definition encounters problems. One cannot simply attempt to use the same definition, since the result will be wrong if one is working in positive characteristic. More to the point, the topology on a scheme fails to capture much of the stucture of the scheme.

label: étale morphism
snippet: A morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$ is étale if it is flat and unramified. This is the appropriate generalization of ``local homeomorphism'' from topology or ``local isomorphism'' from real differential geometry. Equivalently, $f$ is étale if and only if any of the following conditions hold: \item $f$ is locally of finite type and formally étale. \item $f$ is flat and the relative sheaf of differentials vanishes. \item $f$ is smooth of relative dimension zero. \item $f$ locally looks like $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ where the Jacobian vanishes.

snippet: Let $\mathcal{U}$ be a universe (so is, in particular, a set of sets).

snippet: The special linear group over the finite field $\F_3$ is represented by $\mathit{SL}_2(\F_3)$ and consists of the $2\times 2$ invertible matrices with determinant equal to $1$ and whose entries belong to $\F_3$.

snippet:

snippet: Let $C \closedint a b$ be the space of real-valued functions continuous on $\closedint a b$. Let $x \in C \closedint a b$ be a continuous real valued function. snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_1} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_1}$ be the $1$-sequence space. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a separable Banach space over $\GF$. Then there exists a bounded linear surjection $Q : \map {\ell_1} \GF \to X$.

label: 1-Sequence Space is Proper Subset of 2-Sequence Space
snippet: Let $\ell^1$ and $\ell^2$ be the $1$-sequence space and $2$-sequence space respectively. Then $\ell^1$ is a proper subset of $\ell^2$.

snippet: $\ell^1$ space is a separable space.

label: 103 is Smallest Prime whose Period of Reciprocal is One Third of Maximal
snippet: $103$ is the smallest prime number the period of whose decimal expansion of its reciprocal is $\dfrac 1 3$ of its maximum, that is: $34$: $\dfrac 1 {103} = 0 \cdotp \dot 00970 \, 87378 \, 64077 \, 66990 \, 29126 \, 21359 \, 223 \dot 3$

label: 10 Consecutive Integers contain Coprime Integer
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $S := \set {n, n + 1, n + 2, \ldots, n + 9}$ be the set of $10$ consecutive integers starting from $n$. Then at least one element of $S$ is coprime to every other element of $S$.

snippet: $1105$ can be expressed as the sum of two squares in more ways than any smaller integer:

label: 11 is Only Palindromic Prime with Even Number of Digits
snippet: $11$ is the only palindromic prime with an even number of digits when expressed in decimal notation.

label: 121 is Square Number in All Bases greater than 2
snippet: Let $b \in \Z$ be an integer such that $b \ge 3$. Let $n$ be a positive integer which can be expressed in base $b$ as $\sqbrk {121}_b$. Then $n$ is a square number.

label: 1782 is 3 Times Sum of all 2-Digit Numbers from its Digits
snippet: $1782$ equals $3$ multiplied by the sum of all the $2$-digit integers that can be formed from its digits.

label: 17 Consecutive Integers each with Common Factor with Product of other 16
snippet: The $17$ consecutive integers from $2184$ to $2200$ have the property that each one is not coprime with the product of the other $16$.

snippet: Let $T = \struct {\set {0, 1}, \tau_0}$ be a Sierpiński space. The sequence in $T$: $\sigma = \sequence {0, 1, 0, 1, \ldots}$ has $1$ as a limit.

label: 1 plus Perfect Power is not Power of 2
snippet: The equation: $1 + a^n = 2^m$ has no solutions in the integers for $n, m > 1$. This is an elementary special case of Catalan's Conjecture.

label: 1 plus Perfect Power is not Prime Power except for 9
snippet: The only solution to: $x^m = y^n + 1$ is: $\tuple {x, m, y, n} = \tuple {3, 2, 2, 3}$ for positive integers $x, y, m, n > 1$, and $x$ is a prime number. This is a special case of Catalan's Conjecture.

label: 1 plus Power of 2 is not Perfect Power except 9
snippet: The only solution to: $1 + 2^n = a^b$ is: $\tuple {n, a, b} = \tuple {3, 3, 2}$ for positive integers $n, a, b$ with $b > 1$.

label: 1 plus Square is not Perfect Power
snippet: The equation: $x^p = y^2 + 1$ has no solution in the integers for $x, y, p > 1$.

label: 2-Digit Numbers forming Longest Reverse-and-Add Sequence
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer expressed in decimal notation. Let $\map r m$ be the reverse-and-add process on $m$. Let $r$ be applied iteratively to $m$. The $2$-digit integers $m$ which need the largest number of iterations before reaching a palindromic number are $89$ and $98$, both needing $24$ iterations.

label: 2-Digit Permutable Primes
snippet: The $2$-digit permutable primes are: $11, 13, 17, 37, 79$ and their anagrams, and no other.

label: 23 is Largest Integer not Sum of Distinct Perfect Powers
snippet: The largest integer which cannot be expressed as the sum of distinct perfect powers is $23$.

label: 24 divides Square of Odd Integer Not Divisible by 3 plus 23
snippet:
Let $a \in \Z$ be an integer such that: $2 
mid a$ $3 
mid a$ where $
mid$ denotes non-divisibility. Then: $24 \divides \paren {a^2 + 23}$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibility.

label: 2520 equals Sum of 4 Divisors in 6 Ways
snippet: The number $2520$ can be expressed as the sum of $4$ of its divisors in $6$ different ways: This is the maximum possible number of ways it is possible to express an integer as the sum of $4$ of its divisors.

label: 3-Digit Numbers forming Longest Reverse-and-Add Sequence
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer expressed in decimal notation. Let $r \left({m}\right)$ be the reverse-and-add process on $m$. Let $r$ be applied iteratively to $m$. The $3$-digit integers $m$ which need the largest number of iterations before reaching a palindromic number are: $187, 286, 385, 583, 682, 781, 880$ all of which need $23$ iterations. $869$ and $968$ are the result of the first iteration for each of these, and so take $22$ iterations to reach a palindromic number.

label: 3-Digit Permutable Primes
snippet: The $3$-digit permutable primes are: $311, 199, 337$ and their anagrams, and no other.

label: 31 is Smallest Prime whose Reciprocal has Odd Period
snippet: $31$ is the smallest prime number to have a decimal expansion of the reciprocal with an odd period greater than $1$: $\dfrac 1 {31} = 0 \cdotp \dot 03225 \, 80645 \, 1612 \dot 9$

label: 333,667 is Unique Period Prime with Period 9
snippet: $333 \, 667$ is a unique period prime whose reciprocal has a period of $9$: $\dfrac 1 {333 \, 667} = 0 \cdotp \dot 00000 \, 299 \dot 7$

label: 3367 Multiplied by 2-Digit Number
snippet: In order to multiply $3367$ by a $2$-digit integer $\sqbrk {xy}$: divide the $6$-digit integer $\sqbrk {xyxyxy}$ by $3$.

label: 360 divides a^2 (a^2 - 1) (a^2 - 4)
snippet: Let $a \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $360 \divides a^2 \paren {a^2 - 1} \paren {a^2 - 4}$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibility.

label: 3 Configurations of 9 Lines with 3 Intersection Points on each Line
snippet: There exist exactly $3$ essentially different configurations of $9$ straight lines each of which has exactly $3$ points of intersection. This is one: there are two others. 400px

snippet: Let $3$ planes which are pairwise non-parallel be constructed in ordinary $3$-dimensional space. Then that space is divided into $8$ parts by those planes.

snippet: The following triplets of integers in arithmetic sequence with common difference of $60$ can all be expressed as the sum of four $4$th powers: $\tuple {8373, 8433, 8493}, \tuple {8517, 8577, 8637}, \ldots$

label: 3 Proper Integer Heronian Triangles whose Area and Perimeter are Equal
snippet: There are exactly $3$ proper integer Heronian triangles whose area and perimeter are equal. These are the triangles whose sides are: $\tuple {6, 25, 29}$ $\tuple {7, 15, 20}$ $\tuple {9, 10, 17}$

label: 3 is Divisor of one of n, n+2, n+4
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 3$. Then at least one of $n$, $n + 2$, $n + 4$ is divisible by $3$.

snippet: $\map \phi {25 \, 930} = \map \phi {25 \, 935} = \map \phi {25 \, 940} = \map \phi {25 \, 942} = 10 \, 368 = 2^7 \times 3^4$ where $\phi$ denotes the Euler $\phi$ function.

snippet: The following sets of $4$ positive integers which form an arithmetic sequence are the smallest which all have the same Euler $\phi$ value: $72, 78, 84, 90$ $216, 222, 228, 234$ $76 \, 326, 76 \, 332, 76 \, 338, 76 \, 344$

snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be positive $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Suppose that $f = g$ almost everywhere. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \int g \rd \mu$

label: Abel's Limit Theorem
snippet: Let $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty a_k$ be a convergent series in $\R$. Then: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 1^-} \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty a_k x^k} = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty a_k$ where $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 1^-}$ denotes the limit from the left.

label: Abel's Summation Formula
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}_{n \in \N_{>0} }$ be a sequence in $\R$. Let $f : \R_{\ge 1} \to \R$ be a continuously differentiable function. Let $A : \R_{\ge 1} \to \R$ be defined as: $\ds \map A x := \sum_{1 \mathop \le n \mathop \le x} a_n$ Then for all $x \in \R_{\ge 1}$: $\ds \sum_{1 \mathop \le n \mathop \le x} a_n \map f n = \map A x \map f x - \int _1 ^x \map A u \map {f'} u \rd u$

label: Abel's Test
snippet: Let $\ds \sum b_n$ be a convergent real series. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a decreasing sequence of positive real numbers. Then the series $\ds \sum a_n b_n$ is also convergent.

label: Abel's Test for Uniform Convergence
snippet: Let $\sequence {\map {a_n} z}$ and $\sequence {\map {b_n} z}$ be sequences of complex functions on a compact set $K$. Let $\sequence {\map {a_n} z}$ be such that: $\sequence {\map {a_n} z}$ is bounded in $K$ $\ds \sum \size {\map {a_n} z - \map {a_{n + 1} } z}$ is convergent with a sum which is bounded in $K$ $\ds \sum \map {b_n} z$ is uniformly convergent in $K$. Then $\ds \sum \map {a_n} z \map {b_n} z$ is uniformly convergent on $K$.

label: Abel-Ruffini Theorem
snippet: There is no general algebraic solution for determining all the roots of a polynomial of degree $5$ or higher.

label: Abelian Group Factored by Prime
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. Let $p$ be a prime. Factor the order of $G$ as: $\order G = m p^n$ such that $p$ does not divide $m$. Then: $G = H \times K$ where: $H = \set {x \in G : x^{p^n} = e}$ and: $K = \set {x \in G : x^m = e}$ Furthermore: $\order H = p^n$

label: Abelian Group Induces Commutative B-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an abelian group whose identity element is $e$. Let $*$ be the product inverse operation on $G$: $\forall a, b \in G: a * b = a \circ b^{-1}$ where $b^{-1}$ is the inverse element of $b$ under the operation $\circ$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {G, *}$ is a commutative $B$-algebra. That is: $\forall a, b \in G: a * \paren {0 * b} = b * \paren {0 * a}$

label: Abelian Group Induces Entropic Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an abelian group. Let the operation $*$ be defined on $G$ such that: $\forall x, y \in G: x * y = x \circ y^{-1}$ Then $\struct {G, *}$ is an entropic structure.

label: Abelian Group is Simple iff Prime
snippet: Let $G$ be a non-trivial abelian group. Then $G$ is simple $G$ is a prime group.

label: Abelian Group of Order Twice Odd has Exactly One Order 2 Element
snippet: Let $G$ be an abelian group whose identity element is $e$. Let the order of $G$ be $2 n$ such that $n$ is odd. Then there exists exactly one $g \in G$ with $g \ne e$ such that $g = g^{-1}$.

label: Abelian Group of Prime-power Order is Product of Cyclic Groups
snippet: Let $G$ be an abelian group of prime-power order. Let $a$ be an element of maximal order in $G$. Then $G$ can be written in the form $\gen a \times K$ for some $K \le G$.

label: Abelian Group of Semiprime Order is Cyclic
snippet: Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct prime numbers. Let $G$ be an abelian group such that: $\order G = p q$ where $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$. Then $G$ is cyclic.

label: Abelianization of Free Group is Free Abelian Group
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {F_X, \iota}$ be a free group on $X$. Let $F_X^{\mathrm {ab} }$ be its abelianization. Let $\pi : F_X \to F_X^{\mathrm {ab} }$ be the quotient group epimorphism. Then $\struct {F_X^{\mathrm {ab} }, \pi \circ \iota}$ is a free abelian group on $X$.

label: Abelianization of Group is Abelian
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $G^{\mathrm {ab} }$ denote the abelianization of $G$. Then $G^{\mathrm {ab} }$ is an abelian group.

label: Abi-Khuzam Inequality
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Then: $\sin A \cdot \sin B \cdot \sin C \le k A \cdot B \cdot C$ where: $A, B, C$ are measured in radians $k = \paren {\dfrac {3 \sqrt 3} {2 \pi} }^3 \approx 0 \cdotp 56559 \, 56245 \ldots$

label: Absolute Difference Function is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The absolute difference function $\operatorname {adf}: \N^2 \to \N$, defined as: $\map {\operatorname {adf} } {n, m} = \size {n - m}$ where $\size a$ is defined as the absolute value of $a$, is primitive recursive‎.

label: Absolute Net Convergence Equivalent to Absolute Convergence
snippet: Let $V$ be a Banach space. Let $\sequence {v_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of elements in $V$. Let $r \in \R_{\mathop \ge 0}$ Then the following two statements are equivalent: $(1): \quad$ the generalized sum $\ds \sum \set {v_n: n \in \N}$ is absolutely net convergent to $r$ $(2): \quad$ the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty v_n$ is absolutely convergent to $r$

label: Absolute Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Absolute Numbers == Examples of absolute numbers include: $2$, $\sqrt 5$, $1.976$, $\dfrac 2 3$, $\pi$ (pi), $e$ (Euler's number)

label: Absolute Prepolar is Convex Set
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $B \subseteq F$ be non-empty. Let $B_\circ$ be the absolute prepolar of $B$. Then $B_\circ$ is convex.

label: Absolute Value/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Absolute Values ==

label: Absolute Value Function is Completely Multiplicative
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Then: $\size {x y} = \size x \size y$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$. Thus the absolute value function is completely multiplicative.

label: Absolute Value Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $f$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = \size x$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$. Then $f$ is a continuous real function.

label: Absolute Value Function is Convex
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the absolute value function on the real numbers. Then $f$ is convex.

label: Absolute Value Function is Even Function
snippet: Let $\size {\, \cdot \,} : \R \to \R$ denote the absolute value function on $\R$: Then $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ is an even function.

label: Absolute Value Function on Integers induces Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Let $\RR$ be the relation on $\Z$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in \Z: \tuple {x, y} \in \RR \iff \size x = \size y$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$. Then $\RR$ is an equivalence relation.

label: Absolute Value induces Equivalence Compatible with Integer Multiplication
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Let $\RR$ be the relation on $\Z$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in \Z: \struct {x, y} \in \RR \iff \size x = \size y$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$. Then $\RR$ is a congruence relation for integer multiplication.

label: Absolute Value induces Equivalence not Compatible with Integer Addition
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Let $\RR$ be the relation on $\Z$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in \Z: \tuple {x, y} \in \RR \iff \size x = \size y$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$. Then $\RR$ is not a congruence relation for integer addition.

label: Absolute Value is Bounded Below by Zero
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Then the absolute value $\size x$ of $x$ is bounded below by $0$.

label: Absolute Value is Many-to-One
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the absolute value function: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = \begin{cases} x & : x \ge 0 \\ -x & : x < 0 \end{cases}$ Then $f$ is a many-to-one relation.

label: Absolute Value is Norm
snippet: The absolute value is a norm on the set of real numbers $\R$.

label: Absolute Value of Absolutely Continuous Function is Absolutely Continuous
snippet: Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. Let $f : I \to \R$ be an absolutely continuous function. Then $\size f$ is absolutely continuous.

label: Absolute Value of Absolutely Convergent Product is Absolutely Convergent
snippet:
Let $\struct {\mathbb K, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ converge absolutely to $a \in \mathbb K$. Then $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty 
orm {a_n}$ converges absolutely to $
orm a$.

label: Absolute Value of Complex Cross Product is Commutative
snippet: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be complex numbers. Let $z_1 \times z_2$ denote the (complex) cross product of $z_1$ and $z_2$. Then: $\size {z_1 \times z_2} = \size {z_2 \times z_1}$ where $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the absolute value function.

label: Absolute Value of Complex Dot Product is Commutative
snippet: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be complex numbers. Let $z_1 \circ z_2$ denote the (complex) dot product of $z_1$ and $z_2$. Then: $\size {z_1 \circ z_2} = \size {z_2 \circ z_1}$ where $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the absolute value function.

label: Absolute Value of Components of Complex Number no greater than Root 2 of Modulus
snippet: Let $z = x + i y \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\size x + \size y \le \sqrt 2 \cmod z$ where: $\size x$ and $\size y$ denote the absolute value of $x$ and $y$ $\cmod z$ denotes the complex modulus of $z$.

label: Absolute Value of Even Power
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\size {x^{2 n} } = x^{2 n}$

label: Absolute Value of Function is Composite with Absolute Value Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $f: S \to \R$ be real-valued function. Let $\size f$ denote the absolute value of $f$, that is, $\size f$ is the mapping defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {\size f} s = \size{\map f s}$ Then: $\size f = \size{\,\cdot\,} \circ f$ where: $\size{\,\cdot\,} : \R \to \R$ denotes the absoute value function $\size{\,\cdot\,} \circ f$ denotes the composite mapping of $\size{\,\cdot\,}$ and $f$

label: Absolute Value of Infinite Product
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm{\,\cdot\,}}$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence{a_n}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb K$.

label: Absolute Value of Integer is not less than Divisors
snippet: A (non-zero) integer is greater than or equal to its divisors in magnitude: $\forall c \in \Z_{\ne 0}: a \divides c \implies a \le \size a \le \size c$

label: Absolute Value of Measurable Function is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. Then: $\size f$ is a $\Sigma$-measurable function.

label: Absolute Value of Negative
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $\size x = \size {-x}$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$.

label: Absolute Value of Pearson Correlation Coefficient is Less Than or Equal to 1
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Let the variances of $X$ and $Y$ exist and be finite. Then: $\size {\map \rho {X, Y} } \le 1$ where $\map \rho {X, Y}$ denotes the Pearson correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y$.

label: Absolute Value of Power
snippet: Let $x$, $y$ be real numbers. Let $x^y$, $x$ to the power of $y$, be real. Then: $\size {x^y} = \size x^y$

label: Absolute Value of Real-Valued Random Variable is Real-Valued Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a real-valued random variable. Then $\size X$ is a real-valued random variable.

snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a signed measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $\size \mu$ be the variation of $\mu$. Then: $\size {\map \mu A} \le \map {\size \mu} A$ for each $A \in \Sigma$.

snippet:
Let $X$ be a compact topological space. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of continuous mappings $f_n: X 	o \mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly to $f$. Then $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty 
orm {f_n}$ converges uniformly to $
orm f$.

label: Absolutely Continuous Random Variable is Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an absolutely continuous random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Then $X$ is a continuous random variable.

label: Absolutely Continuous Real Function is Uniformly Continuous
snippet: Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. Let $f: I \to \R$ be an absolutely continuous real function. Then $f$ is uniformly continuous.

label: Absolutely Convergent Generalized Sum Converges
snippet: Let $V$ be a Banach space. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$ denote the norm on $V$. Let $d$ denote the corresponding induced metric. Let $\family {v_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed subset of $V$ such that the generalized sum $\ds \sum \set {v_i: i \in I }$ converges absolutely. Then the generalized sum $\ds \sum \set {v_i: i \in I}$ converges.

label: Absolutely Convergent Generalized Sum Converges to Supremum
snippet: Let $V$ be a Banach space. Let $\family {v_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of elements of $V$. Let $\FF$ denote the set of finite subsets of $I$. Let the generalized sum $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} v_i$ converge absolutely to $c \in \R$. Then: $c = \sup \set{\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in F} \norm{v_i} : F \in \FF}$

label: Absolutely Convergent Generalized Sum over Union of Disjoint Index Sets
Absolutely Convergent Product Does not Diverge to Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a valued field. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ be absolutely convergent. Then it is not divergent to $0$.

label: Absolutely Convergent Product is Convergent
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\mathbb K$ be complete. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ be absolutely convergent. Then it is convergent.

label: Absolutely Convergent Series in Banach Space is Unconditionally Convergent
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence such that: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_n$ is absolutely convergent Then: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_n$ is unconditionally convergent.

label: Absolutely Convergent Series in Normed Vector Space is Convergent iff Space is Banach
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. Then $X$ is a Banach space : every absolutely convergent series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ is convergent.

label: Absolutely Convergent Series is Convergent
snippet: Let $V$ be a Banach space with norm $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ be an absolutely convergent series in $V$. Then $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ is convergent.

label: Absorbing Set in Vector Space contains Zero Vector
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be an absorbing subset of $X$. Then: $\mathbf 0_X \in A$ where $\mathbf 0_X$ denotes the zero vector in $X$.

label: Abstract Model of Algebraic Extensions
snippet: Let $K$ be a field and $\alpha \in \overline{K}$ be an element of the algebraic closure of $K$ which is algebraic over $K$. Let $m_\alpha$ be the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $K$. Then: $K[\alpha] \cong K[x]/ \langle m_\alpha\rangle$

label: Acceleration Vector in Polar Coordinates
snippet: Consider a particle $p$ moving in the plane. Let the position of $p$ at time $t$ be given in polar coordinates as $\polar {r, \theta}$. Then the acceleration $\mathbf a$ of $p$ can be expressed as: $\mathbf a = \paren {r \dfrac {\d^2 \theta} {\d t^2} + 2 \dfrac {\d r} {\d t} \dfrac {\d \theta} {\d t} } \mathbf u_\theta + \paren {\dfrac {\d^2 r} {\d t^2} - r \paren {\dfrac {\d \theta} {\d t} }^2} \mathbf u_r$ where: $\mathbf u_r$ is the unit vector in the direction of the radial coordinate of $p$ $\mathbf u_\theta$ is the unit vector in the direction of the angular coordinate of $p$

label: Acceleration is Second Derivative of Displacement with respect to Time
snippet: The acceleration $\mathbf a$ of a body $M$ is the second derivative of the displacement $\mathbf s$ of $M$ from a given point of reference time $t$: $\mathbf a = \dfrac {\d^2 \mathbf s} {\d t^2}$

label: Acceleration of Particle moving in Circle at Constant Speed
snippet: Let $P$ be a particle moving in a circular path $C$ at a constant speed. Then the acceleration of $P$, denoted by $\mathbf a \in \R$, is given as: $\mathbf a = -\dfrac {\size {\mathbf v}^2 \mathbf r} {\size {\mathbf r}^2}$ where: $\mathbf v$ is the instantaneous velocity of $P$ $\mathbf r$ is the vector whose magnitude equals the length of the radius of $C$ and whose direction is from the center of $C$ to $P$ $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the magnitude of a vector.

label: Acceleration of Point in Plane in Intrinsic Coordinates
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be the acceleration of a particle $P$ in space. Let $P$ be moving in a plane $\PP$. Then the motion of $P$ can be expressed in intrinsic coordinates as: $\mathbf a = \dfrac {\d \map v t} {\d t} \mathbf s + \dfrac {\paren {\map v t}^2} \rho \bspsi$ where: $\mathbf s$ denotes the unit vector along the tangential direction of $P$ $\bspsi$ denotes the unit vector toward the center of curvature of the motion of $P$ $\map v t$ is the speed of $P$ at the time $t$ $\rho$ is the radius of curvature of the motion of $P$ at time $t$.

label: Acceleration of Point in Straight Line
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be the acceleration of a particle $P$ in space. Let $P$ be moving along a straight line $\LL$ whose positive direction has been established. Then the motion of $P$ can be defined by: $\mathbf a = \dfrac {\d^2 s} {\d t^2} \mathbf i$ where $\mathbf i$ denotes the unit vector in the positive direction of $\LL$.

label: Acceleration of Rocket in Outer Space
snippet: Let $B$ be a rocket travelling in outer space. Let the velocity of $B$ at time $t$ be $\mathbf v$. Let the mass of $B$ at time $t$ be $m$. Let the exhaust velocity of $B$ be constant at $\mathbf b$. Then the acceleration of $B$ at time $t$ is given by: $\mathbf a = \dfrac 1 m \paren {-\mathbf b \dfrac {\d m} {\d t} }$

label: Accumulation Point of Infinite Sequence in First-Countable Space is Subsequential Limit

label: Accumulation Point of Sequence iff Cluster Point of Net
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$. Let $x \in X$. Then $x$ is an accumulation point of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ as a sequence $x$ is a cluster point of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ as a net.

label: Accumulation Point of Sequence is not necessarily Limit Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $T$. Let $q \in S$ be an accumulation point of $\sequence {a_n}$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $q$ is also a limit of $\sequence {a_n}$.

label: Accumulation Point of Sequence of Distinct Terms is Omega-Accumulation Point of Range
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence of distinct terms of $S$. Let $\alpha$ be an accumulation point of $\sequence {x_n}$. Then $\alpha$ is also an $\omega$-accumulation point of $\set {x_n: n \in \N}$.

label: Accumulation Point of Sequence of Reciprocals and Reciprocals + 1
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ denote the sequence in $\struct {\R, \tau}$ defined as: {{eqn | l = a_n | r = \begin {cases} \dfrac 2 {n + 1} & : \text {$n$ odd} \\ 1 + \dfrac 2 n & : \text {$n$ even} \end {cases} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \sequence {\dfrac 1 1, 1 + \dfrac 1 1, \dfrac 1 2, 1 + \dfrac 1 2, \dfrac 1 3, 1 + \dfrac 1 3, \dotsb} | c = }} Then $0$ is an accumulation point of $\sequence {a_n}$.

label: Accumulation Points of Sequence of Distinct Terms in Infinite Particular Point Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be an infinite particular point space. Let $U \in \tau_p$ be a countably infinite open set of $T$. Let the elements of $U$ be arranged into a sequence $\sequence {a_i}$ of distinct terms in $T$. Then while every element $x$ of $U$ such that $x \ne p$ is a limit point of $U$, there exists no $x \in U$ such that $x$ is an accumulation point of $\sequence {a_i}$.

label: Accuracy of Convergents of Continued Fraction Expansion of Irrational Number
snippet: Let $x$ be an irrational number. Let $(a_0, a_1, \ldots)$ be its continued fraction expansion. Let $\left \langle {C_n}\right \rangle_{n \geq 0}$ be its sequence of convergents. Let $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ and $q_0, q_1, q_2, \ldots$ be its numerators and denominators. Then: $\forall k \ge 1: \left\vert{x - \dfrac {p_{k + 1} } {q_{k + 1} } }\right\vert < \dfrac 1 {q_{k + 1} q_{k + 2} } \le \dfrac 1 {2 q_k q_{k + 1} } < \left\vert{x - \dfrac {p_k} {q_k} }\right\vert$ Thus: The of the inequality gives an indication of how close each convergent gets to its true value.

label: Achilles Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == and a are to have a . Achilles (not surprisingly) is expected to run considerably faster than the tortoise. So, to make it marginally more fair, he gives the tortoise a head start. But it is apparent that Achilles cannot actually catch up with the tortoise. Suppose he gives the tortoise a headstart of $x_0$. By the time he has got to $x_0$, the tortoise has moved on, to $x_1$, say. But by the time Achilles has reached $x_1$, the tortoise has moved on, to $x_2$, say. You can continue this indefinitely.

label: Action in terms of Kinetic Energy
snippet: Let $S$ be a dynamical system Let $A$ be the action for a given segment from point $A$ to point $B$ on the trajectory of $S$ is defined by the line integral: $\ds \sum_i \int_A^B p_i \rd q_i$ Let $A$ act over a time interval of length $t$. Then: $A = 2 K t$ where $K$ denotes the mean kinetic energy of $S$ over $t$.

label: Action of Group on Coset Space is Group Action
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $*: G \times G / H \to G / H$ be the action on the (left) coset space: $\forall g \in G, \forall g' H \in G / H: g * \paren {g' H} := \paren {g g'} H$ Then $G$ is a group action.

label: Addition Law of Probability
snippet: Let $\Pr$ be a probability measure on an event space $\Sigma$. Let $A, B \in \Sigma$. The probability of the occurrence of the union of $A$ and $B$ can be evaluated as: $\map \Pr {A \cup B} = \map \Pr A + \map \Pr B - \map \Pr {A \cap B}$ That is, the probability of either event occurring equals the sum of their individual probabilities less the probability of them both occurring. This is known as the addition law of probability.

label: Addition of 1 in Golden Mean Number System
snippet: == Algorithm == Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. The following algorithm performs the operation of addition of $1$ to $x$ in the golden mean number system. Let $S$ be the representation of $x$ in the golden mean number system in its simplest form. Step $1$: Is the digit immediately to the left of the radix point a zero? If Yes, replace that $0$ with $1$. Go to Step $4$. If No, set $m = 2$ and go to Step $2$. Step $2$: Does the $m$th place after the radix point contain $0$? If Yes, expand the $100$ in the $3$ places ending in the $m$th place with $011$. Subtract $2$ from $m$. Go to Step $3$.

label: Addition of Coordinates on Cartesian Plane under Chebyshev Distance is Continuous Function
snippet: Let $\R^2$ be the real number plane. Let $d_\infty$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\R^2$. Let $f: \R^2 \to \R$ be the real-valued function defined as: $\forall \tuple {x_1, x_2} \in \R^2: \map f {x_1, x_2} = x_1 + x_2$ Then $f$ is continuous.

label: Addition of Coordinates on Euclidean Plane is Continuous Function
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^2, d_2}$ be the real number plane with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Let $f: \R^2 \to \R$ be the real-valued function defined as: $\forall \tuple {x_1, x_2} \in \R^2: \map f {x_1, x_2} = x_1 + x_2$ Then $f$ is continuous.

label: Addition of Cuts is Associative
snippet: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be cuts. Let the operation of $\alpha + \beta$ be the sum of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then: $\paren {\alpha + \beta} + \gamma = \alpha + \paren {\beta + \gamma}$

label: Addition of Cuts is Commutative
snippet: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be cuts. Let the operation of $\alpha + \beta$ be the sum of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then: $\alpha + \beta = \beta + \alpha$

label: Addition of Division Products in Field
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0$ and whose unity is $1$. Let $a, b, c, d \in F$ such that $b \ne 0$ and $d \ne 0$. Then: $\dfrac a b + \dfrac c d = \dfrac {a d + b c} {b d}$ where $\dfrac x z$ is defined as $x \paren {z^{-1} }$.

label: Addition of Linear Transformations
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ and $\struct {H, +_H}$ be abelian groups. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_G}$ and $\struct {H, +_H, \circ_H}$ be $R$-modules. Let $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$ be the set of all linear transformations from $G$ to $H$. Let $\oplus_H$ be defined as pointwise addition on $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$: $\forall \phi, \psi \in \map {\LL_R} {G, H}: \forall x \in G: \map {\paren {\phi \oplus_H \psi} } x := \map \phi x +_H \map \psi x$ Then $\phi \oplus_H \psi: G \to H$ is a linear transformation.

label: Addition of Natural Numbers is Provable
snippet: Let $x, y \in \N$ be natural numbers. Then there exists formal proof of: $\sqbrk x + \sqbrk y = \sqbrk {x + y}$ in minimal arithmetic, where $\sqbrk a$ is the unary representation of $a$.

label: Addition of Numbers is not Distributive over Multiplication
snippet: Addition of numbers is not distributive over multiplication. That is, for numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ it is not necessarily the case that $a + \paren {b \times c} = \paren {a + b} \times \paren {a + c}$.

label: Addition of Real and Imaginary Parts
snippet: Let $z_0, z_1 \in \C$ be two complex numbers. Then: $\map \Re {z_0 + z_1} = \map \Re {z_0} + \map \Re {z_1}$ and: $\map \Im {z_0 + z_1} = \map \Im {z_0} + \map \Im {z_1}$ Here, $\map \Re {z_0}$ denotes the real part of $z_0$, and $\map \Im {z_0}$ denotes the imaginary part of $z_0$.

label: Additive Group and Multiplicative Group of Field are not Isomorphic

label: Additive Group of Complex Numbers is Direct Product of Reals with Reals
snippet: Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Then the direct product $\struct {\R, +} \times \struct {\R, +}$ is isomorphic with $\struct {\C, +}$.

snippet: The set of integers under addition $\struct {\Z, +}$ forms a countably infinite abelian group.

snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Then $\struct {\Z, +}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\C, +}$.

snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Then $\struct {\Z, +}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\R, +}$.

label: Additive Group of Integers is Subgroup of Rationals
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {\Q, +}$ be the additive group of rational numbers. Then $\struct {\Z, +}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {\Q, +}$.

label: Additive Group of Rationals is Normal Subgroup of Complex
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, +}$ be the additive group of rational numbers. Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Then $\struct {\Q, +}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\C, +}$.

snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, +}$ be the additive group of rational numbers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Then $\struct {\Q, +}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\R, +}$.

snippet: Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Then $\struct {\R, +}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\C, +}$.

label: Additive Inverse in Ring of Bounded Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Let $f \in \map {C^*} {S, \R}$. Then: the additive inverse of $f$ is the pointwise negation $-f$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {\paren{-f}} s = - \map f s$

label: Additive Inverse in Ring of Continuous Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {R, +, *, \tau_{_R} }$ be a topological ring with zero $0_R$. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $R$. Let $f \in \map C {S, R}$. Then: the additive inverse of $f$ is the pointwise negation $-f$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {\paren{-f}} s = - \map f s$

label: Additive Inverse in Ring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Let $f \in \map C {S, \R}$. Then: the additive inverse of $f$ is the pointwise negation $-f$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {-f} s = - \map f s$

label: Additive Inverse in Vector Space is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \circ}_F$ be a vector space over a field $F$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Then for every $\mathbf v \in \mathbf V$, the additive inverse of $\mathbf v$ is unique: $\forall \mathbf v \in \mathbf V: \exists! \paren {-\mathbf v} \in \mathbf V: \mathbf v + \paren {-\mathbf v} = \mathbf 0$

label: Additive Regular Representations of Topological Ring are Homeomorphisms
snippet: Let $\struct {R, + , \circ, \tau}$ be a topological ring. Let $x \in R$. Let $\lambda_x$ and $\rho_x$ be the left and right regular representations of $\struct {R, +}$ with respect to $x$. Then $\lambda_x, \,\rho_x: \struct {R, \tau} \to \struct {R, \tau}$ are homeomorphisms with inverses $\lambda_{-x}, \,\rho_{-x}: \struct {R, \tau} \to \struct {R, \tau}$ respectively.

label: Additive and Countably Subadditive Function is Countably Additive
snippet: Let $\Sigma$ be a $\sigma$-algebra over a set $X$. Let $f: \Sigma \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be an additive and countably subadditive function, where $\overline \R_{\ge 0}$ denotes the set of positive extended real numbers. Then $f$ is countably additive.

label: Additivity of Riemannian Length of Admissible Curve
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\gamma : \closedint a b \to M$ with $t \stackrel \gamma \mapsto \map \gamma t$ be an admissible curve. Let $c \in \R$ be a real number such that $a < c < b$. Let $\map {L_g} {\valueat \gamma {\closedint a b} }$ be the Riemannian length of $\gamma$ from $t = a$ to $t = b$. Then: $\map {L_g} {\valueat \gamma {\closedint a b} } = \map {L_g} {\valueat \gamma {\closedint a c} } + \map {L_g} {\valueat \gamma {\closedint c b} }$

label: Adherent Point of Filter iff Superfilter Converges
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF$ be a filter on $S$. Let $x \in S$. Then $x$ is a adherent point of $\FF$ there exists a superfilter $\FF'$ of $\FF$ on $S$ which converges to $x$.

label: Adjoining Commutes with Inverting
snippet: Let $\HH$ and $\KK$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $\map \BB {\HH, \KK}$ be the set of bounded linear transformations from $\HH$ to $\KK$. Let $A \in \map \BB {\HH, \KK}$ be a bounded linear transformation on $\HH$. Let $A^{-1} \in \map \BB {\KK, \HH}$ be an inverse for $A$. Let $A^*$ denote the adjoint of $A$. Then $A^*$, is invertible, and: $\paren {A^*}^{-1} = \paren {A^{-1} }^*$

label: Adjoint is Conjugate Linear
snippet: Let $\HH$ and $\KK$ be Hilbert spaces over $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\map \BB {\HH, \KK}$ be the set of bounded linear transformations from $\HH$ to $\KK$. Let $A, B \in \map \BB {\HH, \KK}$ be bounded linear transformations. Let $\lambda \in \mathbb F$ be a scalar. Then: $\paren {A + \lambda B}^* = A^* + \bar \lambda B^*$ where $A^*$ is the adjoint of $A$ $\bar \lambda$ is the complex conjugate of $\lambda$ That is, the adjoint is conjugate linear.

label: Adjoint is Involutive
snippet: Let $\mathbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ and $\struct {\KK, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be Hilbert spaces over $\mathbb F$. Let $A : \HH \to \KK$ be a bounded linear transformation. Define: $A^{**} = \paren {A^*}^*$ where $A^*$ denotes the adjoint of $A$. Then $*$ is an involutive operation in the sense that: $A^{**} = A$

label: Adjoint of Closure of Closable Densely-Defined Linear Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ be a closable densely-defined linear operator with adjoint $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$. Let $\tuple {\map D {\overline T}, \overline T}$ be the closure of $T$ with adjoint $\tuple {\map D {\paren {\overline T}^\ast}, \paren {\overline T}^\ast}$. Then: $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast} = \tuple {\map D {\paren {\overline T}^\ast}, \paren {\overline T}^\ast}$

label: Adjoint of Composition of Linear Transformations is Composition of Adjoints
snippet: Let $\mathbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\HH$, $\KK$ and $\LL$ be a Hilbert spaces over $\mathbb F$. Let $A : \KK \to \LL$ and $B : \HH \to \KK$ be bounded linear transformations. Then: $\paren {A B}^* = B^* A^*$ where $^*$ denotes adjoining.

label: Adjoint of Densely-Defined Linear Operator is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ be a densely-defined linear operator. Let $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$ be the adjoint of $\tuple {\map D T, T}$. Then $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$ is closed.

label: Adjoint of Densely-Defined Linear Operator reverses Extension of Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ and $\tuple {\map D S, S}$ be densely-defined linear operators such that: $\tuple {\map D S, S}$ extends $\tuple {\map D T, T}$. Let $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$ and $\tuple {\map D {S^\ast}, S^\ast}$ be the adjoints of $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ and $\tuple {\map D S, S}$ respectively. Then $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$ extends $\tuple {\map D {S^\ast}, S^\ast}$.

label: Adjoint of Direct Sum of Bounded Linear Operators on Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\sequence {\family {\HH_i, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a $I$-indexed family of Hilbert spaces over $\GF$. For each $i \in I$, let $T_i : \HH_i \to \HH_i$ be a bounded linear operator. Suppose that: $\ds \sup_{i \mathop \in I} \norm {T_i}_{\map B {\HH_i} } < \infty$ where $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B {\HH_i} }$ is the norm of a bounded linear operator on $\HH_i$.

label: Adjoint of Direct Sum of Densely-Defined Linear Operators on Hilbert Spaces
snippet: Let $\family {\tuple {\HH_n, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_{\HH_n} } }_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of Hilbert spaces over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ be the Hilbert space direct sum of $\family {\tuple {\HH_n, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_n} }_{n \mathop \in \N}$. For each $n \in \N$, let $\tuple {\map D {T_n}, T_n}$ be a densely-defined linear operator with adjoint $\tuple {\map D {T_n^\ast}, T_n^\ast}$. Let $\ds \tuple {\map D T,T}$ be the direct sum of $\sequence {\tuple {\map D {T_n}, T_n} }_{n \mathop \in \N}$ with adjoint $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$.

label: Adjoint of Finite Rank Operator
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ and $\struct {\KK, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\KK}$ be Hilbert spaces over $\GF$. Let $T \in \map {B_{00} } {\HH, \KK}$ be a bounded finite rank operator. Then: $T^* \in \map {B_{00} } {\KK, \HH}$ that is, the adjoint of $T$ is also a bounded finite rank operator.

label: Adjoint of Identity Transformation
snippet: Let $\tuple {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $I_\HH$ be the identity transformation on $\HH$. Then: ${I_\HH}^* = I_\HH$ where ${I_\HH}^*$ denotes the adjoint of $I_\HH$.

label: Adjoint of Normal Operator has Same Eigenvectors and Complex Conjugated Eigenvalues
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\mathbf T: \HH \to \HH$ be a normal operator. Let $\lambda$ be an eigenvalue of $\mathbf T$. Let $\mathbf v$ be a eigenvector of $\mathbf T$ associated with $\lambda$. Then, $\mathbf v$ is also an eigenvector of the adjoint $\mathbf T^*$ with an associated eigenvalue $\overline \lambda$, where $\bar \lambda$ is the complex conjugate of $\lambda$. That is: $\mathbf T^* \mathbf v = \bar \lambda \mathbf v$

label: Adjoint of Symmetric Densely-Defined Linear Operator Extends Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a symmetric densely-defined linear operator. Let $\struct {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$ be the adjoint of $T$. Then $\map D T \subseteq \map D {T^\ast}$ and: $T x = T^\ast x$ for each $x \in \map D T$.

label: Adjunction Induces Counit of Adjunction
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ be an adjunction between $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$. Let $\beta$ be the inverse of the natural isomorphism $\alpha$. Then: there exists a counit of adjunction $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ That is, there exists a natural transformation $\xi: FG \to \operatorname {id}_{\mathbf C}$ where: for each $C$ of $\mathbf C: \xi_{_C} = \map {\beta_{\tuple{GC, C}}} {\operatorname {id}_{GC}}$ $\operatorname {id}_{\mathbf C}$ is the identity functor on $\mathbf C$ $FG$ is the composite functor of $F$ with $G$

label: Adjunction Induces Unit of Adjunction
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ be an adjunction between $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$. Then: there exists a unit of adjunction $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ That is, there exists a natural transformation $\eta: \operatorname {id}_{\mathbf D} \to GF$ where: for each object $D \in \mathbf D: \eta_{_D} = \map {\alpha_{_\tuple{D, FD}}} {\operatorname {id}_{FD}}$ $\operatorname {id}_{\mathbf D}$ is the identity functor on $\mathbf D$ $GF$ is the composite functor of $G$ with $F$

label: Admissible Curve in Riemannian Manifold has Unique Forward Reparametrization by Arc Length
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold with or without boundary. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. Let $\gamma : I \to M$ be an admissible Curve. Then $\gamma$ has a unique forward reparametrization by arc length.

label: Admissible Family of Curves Symmetry Lemma
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $I = \closedint a b$ is a closed real interval. Let $J$ is an open real interval. Let $\Gamma : J \times I \to M$ be an admissible family of curves. Let $\tuple {a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{n - 1}, a_n}$ be a finite subdivision of $I$. Then: $\forall i \in \N_{> 0} : i \le n : \forall s \in J : \forall t \in \closedint {a_{i - 1} }{a_i} : D_s \partial_t \Gamma = D_t \partial_s \Gamma$ where $D_t$ denotes the covariant derivative along the main curve, and $D_s$ denotes the covariant derivative along the transverse curve.

label: Affine Functional is Convex and Concave
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\R$. Let $f : X \to \R$ be an affine functional on $X$. Then $f$ is convex and concave.

label: Affine Group of One Dimension as Semidirect Product
snippet: Let $\map {\operatorname{Af}_1} \R$ be the $1$-dimensional affine group on $\R$. Let $\R^+$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $\R^\times$ be the multiplicative group of real numbers. Let $\phi: \R^\times \to \Aut {\R^+}$ be defined as: $\forall b \in \R^\times: \map \phi b = \paren {a \mapsto a b}$ Let $\R^+ \rtimes_\phi \R^\times$ be the corresponding semidirect product. Then: $\map {\operatorname {Af}_1} \R \cong \R^+ \rtimes_\phi \R^\times$ where $\cong$ denotes (group) isomorphism.

label: Affine Subspace of 3 Dimensional Euclidean Space
snippet: Let $\R^3$ denote the (real) Euclidean $3$-space. Let $\SS$ be an affine subspace of $\R^3$. Then $\SS$ is one of the following: a point a straight line a plane the whole space $\R^3$.

label: Alaoglu-Bourbaki Theorem
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $\map \sigma {E, F}$ be the weak topology on $E$ induced by $\innerprod E F$. Let $V \subseteq E$ be a neighborhood of ${\mathbf 0}_X$ in $\map \sigma {E, F}$. Let $V^\circ$ be the absolute polar of $V$. Let $\map \sigma {F, E}$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $F$ induced by $\innerprod E F$. Then $V^\circ$ is $\map \sigma {F, E}$-compact.

label: Aleph-Null
snippet: Let $\omega$ denote the minimally inductive set. $\omega = \aleph_0$ where $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping.

label: Aleph Product is Aleph
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then: $\left|{\aleph_x \times \aleph_x}\right| = \aleph_x$ where $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping.

label: Aleph Zero is less than Cardinality of Continuum
snippet: $\aleph_0 < \mathfrak c$ where $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping, $\mathfrak c$ denotes the cardinality of the continuum.

label: Aleph is Infinite
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. $\aleph_x \ge \omega$ where: $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping $\omega$ denotes the minimally inductive set.

label: Aleph is Infinite Cardinal
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then $\aleph_x$ is an infinite cardinal where $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping.

label: Alexandroff Extension is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space. Let $p$ be a new element not in $S$. Let $S^* := S \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {S^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $S$. Then $T^*$ is a compact topological space.

label: Alexandroff Extension is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space. Let $p$ be a new element not in $S$. Let $S^* := S \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {S^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $S$. Then $\tau^*$ is a topology on $S^*$.

label: Alexandroff Extension of Rational Number Space is Connected
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $p$ be a new element not in $\Q$. Let $\Q^* := \Q \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {\Q^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$. Then $T^*$ is a connected space.

label: Alexandroff Extension of Rational Number Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $p$ be a new element not in $\Q$. Let $\Q^* := \Q \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {\Q^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$. Then $T^*$ is a sequentially compact space.

label: Alexandroff Extension of Rational Number Space is T1
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $p$ be a new element not in $\Q$. Let $\Q^* := \Q \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {\Q^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$. Then $T^*$ is a $T_1$ space.

label: Alexandroff Extension of Rational Number Space is not T2
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $p$ be a new element not in $\Q$. Let $\Q^* := \Q \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {\Q^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$. Then $T^*$ is not a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

label: Alexandroff Extension which is T2 is also T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space. Let $p$ be a new element not in $S$. Let $S^* := S \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {S^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $S$. Let $T^*$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Then $T^*$ is a $T_4$ space.

label: Algebra Defined by Ring Homomorphism is Algebra
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {S, +, *}$ be a ring. Let $f : R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let the image of $f$ be a subset of the center of $S$. Let $\struct {S_R, *}$ be the algebra defined by the ring homomorphism $f$. Then $\struct {S_R, *}$ is an algebra over $R$.

label: Algebra Defined by Ring Homomorphism is Associative
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {S, +, *}$ be a ring with unity. Let $f: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let the image of $f$ be a subset of the center of $S$. Let $\struct {S_R, *}$ be the algebra defined by the ring homomorphism $f$. Then $\struct {S_R, *}$ is an associative algebra.

label: Algebra Defined by Ring Homomorphism on Commutative Ring is Commutative
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {S, +, *}$ be a commutative ring. Let $f: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $\struct {S_R, *}$ be the algebra defined by the ring homomorphism $f$. Then $\struct {S_R, *}$ is a commutative algebra.

label: Algebra Defined by Ring Homomorphism on Ring with Unity is Unitary
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {S, +, *}$ be a ring with unity. Let $f: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $\struct {S_R, *}$ be the algebra defined by the ring homomorphism $f$. Then $\struct {S_R, *}$ is a unitary algebra.

snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an algebra of sets on $S$. Then: $\O \in \RR$ where $\O$ denotes the empty set.

label: Algebra of Sets contains Underlying Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an algebra of sets on $S$. Then: $S \in \RR$

label: Algebra of Sets is Boolean Algebra
snippet: An algebra of sets is a Boolean algebra.

label: Algebra of Sets is Closed under Intersection
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an algebra of sets on $S$. Then: $\forall A, B \in S: A \cap B \in \RR$

label: Algebra of Sets is Closed under Set Difference
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an algebra of sets on $S$. Then: $\forall A, B \in S: A \setminus B \in \RR$

label: Algebra of all Mappings is Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {A, +_A, \circ_A, \ast_A}$ be an $R$-algebra. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {A^S, +, \circ, \ast}$ the $R$-algebra of all mappings from $S$ to $A$. Then $\struct {A^S, +, \circ, \ast}$ is an $R$-algebra.

snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $E$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $E^\#$ be the algebraic dual of $E$. Then $E^\#$ separates points.

snippet: The set of algebraic integers, under the operations of complex addition and complex multiplication, forms a subring of the set of complex numbers $\C$.

snippet: Let $S = \set {x_1, x_2, \ldots,x_n}$ be a set of algebraic variables. The algebraic invariants for the group of permutations of $S$ are those generated by the elementary symmetric polynomials: {{eqn | l = p_2 | r = x_1 x_2 + x_1 x_3 + \cdots + x_{n - 1} x_n }}

label: Algebraic Numbers are Countable

label: Algebraic Numbers form Countable Subfield of Complex Numbers
snippet: The set $\Bbb A$ of algebraic numbers forms a countable subfield of the field of complex numbers.

label: Algebraic Numbers form Field
snippet: Let $\Bbb A$ denote the set of algebraic numbers in $\C$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\Bbb A, +, \times}$ is a field. In the above, $+$ and $\times$ denote complex addition and complex multiplication respectively.

label: Algebraic Structures formed by Left and Right Operations are not Isomorphic for Cardinality Greater than 1
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\gets$ and $\to$ denote the left operation and right operation respectively. Let $\card S > 1$. The algebraic structures $\struct {S, \gets}$ and $\struct {S, \to}$ are not isomorphic.
