label: Complement of Irreducible Topological Subset is Prime Element
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $X$ be an irreducible subset of $S$ such that: $\relcomp S X \in \tau$ Let $L = \struct {\tau, \preceq}$ be an inclusion ordered set of topology $\tau$. Then $\relcomp S X$ is prime element in $L$.

label: Complement of Limit Inferior is Limit Superior of Complements
snippet: Let $\sequence {E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets. Then: $\ds \map \complement {\liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} \ E_n} = \limsup_{n \mathop \to \infty} \ \map \complement {E_n}$ where $\liminf$ and $\limsup$ denote the limit inferior and limit superior, respectively.

label: Complement of Limit Superior is Limit Inferior of Complements
snippet: Let $\sequence {E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets. Then: $\ds \map \complement {\limsup_{n \mathop \to \infty} \ E_n} = \liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} \ \map \complement {E_n}$ where $\limsup$ and $\liminf$ denote the limit superior and limit inferior, respectively.

label: Complement of Lower Closure is Prime Element in Inclusion Ordered Set of Scott Sigma
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a complete Scott topological lattice. Let $D = \struct {\map \sigma L, \precsim}$ be an inclusion ordered set of the Scott sigma of $L$. Let $x \in S$. Then: $\relcomp S {x^\preceq}$ is a prime element in $D$ and: $\relcomp S {x^\preceq} \ne S$

label: Complement of Normal Subgroup is Isomorphic to Quotient Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group with identity $e$. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $K$ be a complement of $N$. Then the quotient group $G / N$ is isomorphic to $K$.

label: Complement of Open Interval Defined by Absolute Value
snippet: Let $\xi, \delta \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\delta > 0$. Then: $\set {x \in \R: \size {\xi - x} \ge \delta} = \R \setminus \openint {\xi - \delta} {\xi + \delta}$ where: $\openint {\xi - \delta} {\xi + \delta}$ is the open real interval between $\xi - \delta$ and $\xi + \delta$ $\setminus$ denotes the set difference operator.

label: Complement of Preimage equals Preimage of Complement
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $T_1$ be a subset of $T$. Then: $\relcomp S {f^{-1} \sqbrk {T_1} } = f^{-1} \sqbrk {\relcomp T {T_1} }$ where: $\complement_S$ (in this context) denotes relative complement $f^{-1} \sqbrk {T_1}$ denotes preimage. That is: $S \setminus f^{-1} \sqbrk {T_1} = f^{-1} \sqbrk {T \setminus T_1}$ This can be expressed in the language and notation of inverse image mappings as: $\forall T_1 \in \powerset T: \relcomp S {\map {f^\gets} {T_1} } = \map {f^\gets} {\relcomp T {T_1} }$

label: Complement of Relative Complement is Union with Complement
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be sets such that $A \subseteq B \subseteq C$. Then: $\relcomp C {\relcomp B A} = A \cup \relcomp C B$

label: Complement of Set of Rational Pairs in Real Euclidean Plane is Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^2, d}$ be the real number plane with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $S \subseteq \R^2$ be the subset of $\R^2$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in \R^2: \tuple {x, y} \in S \iff x, y \in \Q$ Hence let $A := \R^2 \setminus S$: $\tuple {x, y} \in A$ either $x$ or $y$ or both is irrational. Then $A$ is injectively path-connected.

label: Complement of Singleton Closure is Meet-Irreducible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Then: $S \setminus \set x^-$ is a meet-irreducible open set where $\set x^-$ denotes the closure of $\set x$

label: Complement of Subgroup is not necessarily Unique
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $K$ be a complement of $H$ in $G$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $K$ is the only complement of $H$ in $G$.

label: Complement of Subset with Property (S) is Closed under Directed Suprema
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an up-complete ordered set. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$ with property (S). Then $\relcomp S X$ is closed under directed suprema.

label: Complement of Universal Set is Empty Set
snippet: The complement of the universal set is the empty set: $\map \complement {\mathbb U} = \O$

label: Complement of Upper Closure of Element is Open in Lower Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a relational structure with lower topology. Let $x \in S$. Then $\relcomp S {x^\succeq}$ is open and $x^\succeq$ is closed.

label: Complement of Vertical Section of Set is Vertical Section of Complement
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $E \subseteq X \times Y$. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\paren {\paren {X \times Y} \setminus E}_x = Y \setminus E_x$ where: $\paren {\paren {X \times Y} \setminus E}_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of the set difference $\paren {X \times Y} \setminus E$ $E_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $E$.

label: Complementary Idempotent is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $I$ be an identity operator on $\HH$. Let $A$ be an idempotent operator. Then the complementary idempotent $I - A$ is also idempotent.

label: Complementary Idempotent of Complementary Idempotent is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $I$ be an identity operator on $\HH$. Let $A$ be an idempotent operator. Let $B$ be the complementary idempotent of A. Then the complementary idempotent of $B$ is $A$.

label: Complementary Projection is Complementary Idempotent
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $A$ be a projection. Let $B$ be the complementary projection of A. Then $B$ is the complementary idempotent of $A$.

label: Complementary Projection is Projection
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $A$ be a projection. Then the complementary projection $I - A$ is also a projection.

label: Complementary Projection of Complementary Projection is Projection
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $I$ be an identity operator on $\HH$. Let $A$ be a projection. Let $B$ be the complementary projection of A. Then the complementary projection of $B$ is $A$.

label: Complements of Components of Two-Component Partition form Partition
snippet: Let $S$ be a set with at least two elements. Let $A, B \subseteq S$. Let $\complement_S$ denote the complement relative to $S$. $A \mid B$ is a partition of $S$ $\relcomp S A \mid \relcomp S B$ is a partition of $S$.

label: Complete Archimedean Valued Field is Real or Complex Numbers
snippet:
Let $\struct{k, 
orm{\,\cdot\,}}$ be a complete valued field with Archimedean norm $
orm{\,\cdot\,}$. Then either: $k$ is isomorphic to the real numbers $\R$ and $
orm{\,\cdot\,}$ is equivalent to the absolute value $\size{\,\cdot\,}$ on $\R$ or $k$ is isomorphic to the complex numbers $\C$ and $
orm{\,\cdot\,}$ is equivalent to the complex modulus $\size{\,\cdot\,}$ on $\C$

label: Complete Bipartite Graphs which are Complete Graphs
snippet: Let $K_{m, n}$ be a complete bipartite graph. $K_{0, 0}$ is the complete graph $K_0$ $K_{0, 1}$ and $K_{1, 0}$ are the complete graph $K_1$ $K_{1, 1}$ is the complete graph $K_2$ and no other complete bipartite graphs are complete.

label: Complete Bipartite Graphs which are Trees
snippet: Let $G = \struct {A \mid B, E} =: K_{m, n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $m$ vertices in $A$ and $n$ vertices in $B$. Then: $K_{0, 0}$ is a tree $K_{1, n}$ and $K_{n, 1}$ is a tree for all $n$ and no other complete bipartite graphs are trees.

label: Complete Boolean Lattice is a Frame
snippet: Let $\struct{B, \vee, \wedge, \neg, \preceq}$ be a complete Boolean lattice. Then: $\struct{B, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ is a frame.

label: Complete Boolean Lattice is a Locale
snippet: Let $\struct{B, \vee, \wedge, \neg, \preceq}$ be a complete Boolean lattice. Then: $\struct{B, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ is a locale.

label: Complete Countable Metric Space has Isolated Point
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a countable complete metric space. Then $X$ has an isolated point.

label: Complete Graph K5 is not Planar
snippet: The complete graph $K_5$ is not planar.

label: Complete Graph is Hamiltonian for Order Greater than 2
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 2$. Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph of order $n$. Then $K_n$ is Hamiltonian.

label: Complete Lattice Homomorphism is Frame Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be complete lattices. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a complete lattice homomorphsim between $L_1$ and $L_2$. Then: $\phi$ is a frame homomorphism

label: Complete Lattice Homomorphism is Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be complete lattices. Let $\phi : L_1 \to L_2$ be a complete lattice homomorphism. Then: $\phi : \struct {S_1, \vee_1, \wedge_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct {S_2, \vee_2, \wedge_2, \preceq_2}$ is a lattice homomorphism where: $\wedge_1, \vee_1$ denote the meet and join on $L_1$ $\wedge_2, \vee_2$ denote the meet and join on $L_2$

label: Complete Lattice Isomorphism is Isomorphism in Category CLat
snippet: Let $\mathbf{CLat}$ denote the category of complete lattices. Let $\phi : L_1 \to L_2$ be a morphism of $\mathbf{CLat}$. Then: $\phi$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbf{CLat}$ $\phi$ is a complete lattice isomorphsm

label: Complete Lattice has Both Greatest Element and Smallest Element
snippet: Let $\struct{S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Then: $(\text{1}) \quad \struct{S, \preceq}$ has a smallest element, namely: $\quad \bot := \sup \O$ $(\text{2}) \quad \struct{S, \preceq}$ has a greatest element, namely: $\quad \top := \inf \O$

label: Complete Lattice is Bounded
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Then $L$ is bounded.

label: Complete Lattice is Lattice
snippet: Let $L= \struct{S, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Then: $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ is a lattice where $\vee$ and $\wedge$ denote the join and meet operations on $S$, respectively.

label: Complete Linearly Ordered Space is Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Let $\struct {X, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Then $\struct {X, \tau}$ is compact.

label: Complete Metric Space is Non-Meager
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a complete metric space. Then $M$ is non-meager.

label: Complete Metric Space is not necessarily Compact
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a complete metric space. Then it is not necessarily the case that $M$ is also compact.

label: Complete Metrizability is Topological Property
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces which are homeomorphic. Let $T_1$ be completely metrizable. Then $T_2$ is also completely metrizable.

label: Complete Metrizability is Weakly Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is completely metrizable. Let $V \subseteq S$ be a closed subspace of $T$. Then $V$ is also completely metrizable. That is, complete metrizability is a weakly hereditary property.

label: Complete Metrizability is not Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is completely metrizable. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\struct {H, \tau_H}$ be the topological subspace of $T$ induced by $H$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {H, \tau_H}$ is also completely metrizable. That is, complete metrizability is not a hereditary property.

snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{\ne 0}$ be a non-zero integer. Let $S := \set {r_1, r_2, \dotsb, r_s}$ be a complete residue system modulo $m$. Then $s = m$.

label: Complete and Totally Bounded Metric Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $M$ be complete and totally bounded. Then $M$ is sequentially compact.

label: Completely Irreducible Element equals Infimum of Subset implies Element Belongs to Subset
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $X \subseteq S$, $p \in S$ such that $p$ is completely irreducible and $p = \inf X$ Then $p \in X$

snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a completely metrizable topological space. Then, $\struct {S, \tau}$ is a metrizable space.

label: Completely Metrizable Space is Non-Meager
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a completely metrizable topological space. Then $T$ is non-meager.

label: Completely Multiplicative Function is Multiplicative
snippet: Let $f: \Z \to \Z$ be a function on the integers $\Z$. Let $f$ be completely multiplicative. Then $f$ is multiplicative.

label: Completely Normal Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a completely normal space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a completely normal space. That is: The property of being a completely normal space is hereditary.

label: Completely Normal Property is Not Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a completely normal space, then it is not necessarily the case that so is $T_B$.

label: Completely Normal Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a completely normal space, then so is $T_B$.

label: Completely Normal iff Every Subspace is Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then $T$ is a completely normal space every subspace of $T$ is normal.

label: Completely Prime Filter Induces Meet-Irreducible Open Set
snippet: Let $\struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF$ be a completely prime filter in the complete lattice $\struct{\tau, \subseteq}$. Let $W = \bigcup \set{U \in \tau : U \notin \FF}$. Then: $W$ is a meet-irreducible open set

label: Completely Prime Ideal is Dual of Completely Prime Filter
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $K \subseteq L$. The following are dual statements: $K$ is a completely prime filter of $\struct {L, \preceq}$ $K$ is a completely prime ideal of $\struct {L, \preceq}$

label: Completely Regular Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a completely regular space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a completely regular space. That is: The property of being a completely regular space is hereditary.

label: Completely Regular Property is Not Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a completely regular space, then it is not necessarily the case that so is $T_B$.

label: Completely Regular Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a completely regular space, then so is $T_B$.

label: Completely Regular Space is T2
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a completely regular space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

label: Completely Regular Space is not necessarily Normal
snippet: A topological space which is a completely regular space is not necessarily also a normal space.

label: Completeness Criterion (Metric Spaces)
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, d}$ be a metric space. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a dense subset. Suppose that every Cauchy sequence in $A$ converges in $M$. Then $M$ is complete.

label: Completing the Square
snippet: Let $a, b, c, x$ be real numbers with $a \ne 0$. Then: $a x^2 + b x + c = \dfrac {\paren {2 a x + b}^2 + 4 a c - b^2} {4 a}$ This process is known as completing the square.

label: Completion Theorem (Inner Product Space)
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_V}$ be an inner product space over a subfield $\GF$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_V$ be the inner product norm induced by $\innerprod \cdot \cdot_V$. Let $\struct {H, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_H}$ be a completion of $V$ with respect to $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ given by Completion Theorem (Normed Vector Space). Then $\innerprod \cdot \cdot_V$ can be extended to an inner product $\innerprod \cdot \cdot_H$ on $H$. By definition, $H$ will be a Hilbert space.

label: Completion Theorem (Measure Space)
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Then there exists a completion $\struct {X, \Sigma^*, \bar \mu}$ of $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$.

label: Completion Theorem (Metric Space)
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Then there exists a completion $\tilde M = \struct {\tilde A, \tilde d}$ of $\struct {A, d}$. Moreover, this completion is unique up to isometry. That is, if $\struct {\hat A, \hat d}$ is another completion of $\struct {A, d}$, then there is a bijection $\tau: \tilde A \leftrightarrow \hat A$ such that: {{item|(2):|$\tau$ preserves metrics: $\forall x_1, x_2 \in A : \map {\hat d} {\map \tau {x_1}, \map \tau {x_2} } \map {\tilde d} {x_1, x_2}$}}

label: Completion Theorem (Normed Algebra)
Completion Theorem (Normed Vector Space)
Completion of Metric Space/Examples

label: Completion of Normed Division Ring
snippet:
Let $\struct {R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_R }$ be a normed division ring. Let $\CC$ be the ring of Cauchy sequences over $R$. Let $\NN$ be the set of null sequences. Let $Q = \CC / \NN$ where $\CC / \NN$ denotes a quotient ring. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Q: Q 	o \R_{\ge 0}$ be the norm on the quotient ring $Q$ defined by: $\ds  orall \sequence {x_n} + \NN: 
orm {\sequence {x_n} + \NN }_Q = \lim_{n \mathop 	o \infty} 
orm{x_n}_R$ Then: $\struct {Q, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Q}$ is a normed division ring completion of $\struct {R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_R }$

label: Completion of Valued Field
snippet:
Let $\struct {k, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Then there exists a completion $\struct {k', 
orm {\,\cdot\,}'}$ of $\struct {k, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ such that $\struct {k', 
orm {\,\cdot\,}'}$ is a valued field. Furthermore, every completion of $\struct{k, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ is isometrically isomorphic to $\struct {k', 
orm {\,\cdot\,}'}$.

label: Complex-Differentiable Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $f: D \to \C$ be a complex function, where $D \subseteq \C$ is an open set. Let $f$ be complex-differentiable at $a \in D$. Then $f$ is continuous at $a$.

label: Complex-Valued Function Dominated by Function Vanishing at Infinity also Vanishes at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $g : X \to \C$ be a complex-valued function vanishing at infinity. Let $f : X \to \C$ be such that $\cmod f \le \cmod g$. Then $f$ vanishes at infinity.

label: Complex-Valued Function is Continuous iff Real Part and Imaginary Part are Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a function. Then $f$ is continuous both the real part $\map \Re f$ and the imaginary part $\map \Im f$ are continuous.

label: Complex-Valued Function is Measurable iff Real and Imaginary Part Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\struct {\C, \map \BB \C}$ be the complex numbers made into a measurable space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$ be the real numbers made into a measurable space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a function. Let $\map \Re f : X \to \R$ and $\map \Im f : X \to \R$ be the pointwise real part and imaginary part of $f$ respectively. Then $f$ is $\Sigma/\map \BB \C$-measurable $\map \Re f$ and $\map \Im f$ are $\Sigma/\map \BB \R$-measurable.

label: Complex-Valued Function on Compact Hausdorff Space Vanishes at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a function. Then $f$ vanishes at infinity.

label: Complex Addition/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Addition ==

label: Complex Addition Identity is Zero
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. The identity element of $\struct {\C, +}$ is the complex number $0 + 0 i$.

label: Complex Addition is Associative
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of complex numbers $\C$ is associative: $\forall z_1, z_2, z_3 \in \C: z_1 + \paren {z_2 + z_3} = \paren {z_1 + z_2} + z_3$

label: Complex Addition is Closed
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ is closed under addition: $\forall z, w \in \C: z + w \in \C$

label: Complex Addition is Commutative
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of complex numbers is commutative: $\forall z, w \in \C: z + w = w + z$

label: Complex Algebra/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Algebra ==

label: Complex Algebraic Curve is Riemann Surface
snippet: Let $\CC$ be an algebraic curve over the field of complex numbers. Then $\CC$ is a Riemann surface.

label: Complex Arithmetic/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Arithmetic ==

label: Complex Conjugate/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Conjugates ==

label: Complex Conjugation is Involution
snippet: Let $z = x + i y$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ denote the complex conjugate of $z$. Then the operation of complex conjugation is an involution: $\overline {\paren {\overline z} } = z$

label: Complex Contour Integral as Contour Integrals
snippet: Let $f: D \to \C$ be a complex-differentiable function, where $D \subseteq \C$ is a connected domain. Let $u, v: \R^2 \to \R$ be defined by: $\map f {x + i y} = \map u {x, y} + i \map v {x, y}$ Let $C$ be a contour in $D$. Let $\phi: \R^2 \to \C$ be defined by: $\map \phi {x, y} = x + i y$ Then there exists a piecewise continuously differentiable function $\gamma: \closedint a b \to \R^2$ such that: $\ds \int_C \map f z \rd z = \ds \int_\gamma \tuple {u, -v} \cdot \rd \mathbf l + i \int_\gamma \tuple {v, u} \cdot \rd \mathbf l$ where the integral on the is a complex contour integral, and the…

label: Complex Cosine Function is Unbounded
snippet: The complex cosine function is unbounded.

label: Complex Cross Product/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Cross Product ==

label: Complex Cross Product Distributes over Addition
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2, z_3 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Then: $z_1 \times \paren {z_2 + z_3} = z_1 \times z_2 + z_1 \times z_3$ where $\times$ denotes cross product.

label: Complex Division as Product with Conjugate over Square of Modulus
snippet: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be complex numbers. Then the operation of division can be expressed as: $\dfrac {z_1} {z_2} = \dfrac {z_1 \overline {z_2} } {\cmod {z_2}^2}$ where: $\overline {z_2}$ denotes the complex conjugate of $z_2$ $\cmod {z_2}$ denotes the complex modulus of $z_2$.

label: Complex Dot Product/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Dot Product ==

label: Complex Eigenvalues of Real Matrix occur in Conjugate Pairs
snippet: The complex eigenvalues of a real matrix occur in conjugate pairs. That is, if $\lambda$ is a complex eigenvalues of a real matrix, then so is the complex conjugate $\overline \lambda$.

label: Complex Exponential is Uniformly Continuous on Half-Planes
snippet: Let $a \in \R$. Then $\exp$ is uniformly continuous on the half-plane $\set {z \in \C : \map \Re z \le a}$.

label: Complex Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Functions ==

label: Complex Hyperbolic Functions are Entire
snippet: Let $F$ be a hyperbolic function over the complex numbers. Then $F$ is an entire function.

label: Complex Integration by Substitution
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\phi: \closedint a b \to \R$ be a real function which has a derivative on $\closedint a b$. Let $f: A \to \C$ be a continuous complex function, where $A$ is a subset of the image of $\phi$. If $\map \phi a \le \map \phi b$, then: $\ds \int_{\map \phi a}^{\map \phi b} \map f t \rd t = \int_a^b \map f {\map \phi u} \map {\phi'} u \rd u$ If $\map \phi a > \map \phi b$, then: $\ds \int_{\map \phi b}^{\map \phi a} \map f t \rd t = -\int_a^b \map f {\map \phi u} \map {\phi'} u \rd u$

label: Complex Modulus/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Modulus ==

label: Complex Modulus Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $z_0 \in \C$ be a complex number. Then the complex modulus function is continuous at $z_0$.

label: Complex Modulus equals Complex Modulus of Conjugate
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ denote the complex conjugate of $z$. Let $\cmod z$ denote the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod z = \cmod {\overline z}$

label: Complex Modulus equals Zero iff Zero
snippet: Let $z = a + i b$ be a complex number. Let $\cmod z$ be the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod z = 0 \iff z = 0$

label: Complex Modulus is Non-Negative
snippet: Let $z = a + i b \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\cmod z$ be the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod z \ge 0$

label: Complex Modulus is Norm
snippet: The complex modulus is a norm on the set of complex numbers $\C$.

label: Complex Modulus of Additive Inverse
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $-z$ be the negative of $z$: $z + \paren {-z} = 0$ Then: $\cmod z = \cmod {\paren {-z} }$ where $\cmod z$ denotes the modulus of $z$.

label: Complex Modulus of Difference of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ be arguments of $z_1$ and $z_2$, respectively. Then: $\cmod {z_1 - z_2}^2 = \cmod {z_1}^2 + \cmod {z_2}^2 - 2 \cmod {z_1} \cmod {z_2} \map \cos {\theta_1 - \theta_2}$

label: Complex Modulus of Measurable Function is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\struct {\C, \map \BB \C}$ be the complex numbers made into a measurable space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a $\Sigma/\map \BB \C$-measurable mapping. Let $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$ be the real numbers made into a measurable space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Then $\cmod f : X \to \R$ is $\Sigma/\map \BB \R$-measurable.

label: Complex Modulus of Product of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\cmod z$ be the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod {z_1 z_2} = \cmod {z_1} \cdot \cmod {z_2}$

label: Complex Modulus of Quotient of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers such that $z_2 \ne 0$. Let $\cmod z$ denote the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod {\dfrac {z_1} {z_2} } = \dfrac {\cmod {z_1} } {\cmod {z_2} }$

label: Complex Modulus of Real Number equals Absolute Value
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Then the complex modulus of $x$ equals the absolute value of $x$.

label: Complex Modulus of Reciprocal of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number such that $z \ne 0$. Let $\cmod z$ denote the complex modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod {\dfrac 1 z} = \dfrac 1 {\cmod z}$

label: Complex Modulus of Sum of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ be arguments of $z_1$ and $z_2$, respectively. Then: $\cmod {z_1 + z_2}^2 = \cmod {z_1}^2 + \cmod {z_2}^2 + 2 \cmod {z_1} \cmod {z_2} \, \map \cos {\theta_1 - \theta_2}$

label: Complex Multiplication Distributes over Addition
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of complex numbers $\C$ is distributive over the operation of addition. $\forall z_1, z_2, z_3 \in \C:$ $z_1 \paren {z_2 + z_3} = z_1 z_2 + z_1 z_3$ $\paren {z_2 + z_3} z_1 = z_2 z_1 + z_3 z_1$

label: Complex Multiplication Identity is One
snippet: Let $\C_{\ne 0}$ be the set of complex numbers without zero. The identity element of $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ is the complex number $1 + 0 i$.

label: Complex Multiplication as Geometrical Transformation
snippet: Let $z_1 = \left\langle{r_1, \theta_1}\right\rangle$ and $z_2 = \left\langle{r_2, \theta_2}\right\rangle$ be complex numbers expressed in polar form. Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be represented on the complex plane $\C$ in vector form. Let $z = z_1 z_2$ be the product of $z_1$ and $z_2$. Then $z$ can be interpreted as the result of: rotating $z_1$ about the origin of $\C$ by $\theta_2$ in the positive direction multiplying the modulus of $z_1$ by $r_2$.

label: Complex Multiplication is Associative
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of complex numbers $\C$ is associative: $\forall z_1, z_2, z_3 \in \C: z_1 \paren {z_2 z_3} = \paren {z_1 z_2} z_3$

label: Complex Multiplication is Closed
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ is closed under multiplication: $\forall z, w \in \C: z \times w \in \C$

label: Complex Multiplication is Commutative
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of complex numbers $\C$ is commutative: $\forall z_1, z_2 \in \C: z_1 z_2 = z_2 z_1$

label: Complex Number equals Conjugate iff Wholly Real
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ be the complex conjugate of $z$. Then $z = \overline z$ $z$ is wholly real.

label: Complex Number equals Negative of Conjugate iff Wholly Imaginary
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ be the complex conjugate of $z$. Then $\overline z = -z$ $z$ is wholly imaginary.

label: Complex Number is Algebraic over Real Numbers
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then $z$ is algebraic over $\R$.

label: Complex Numbers are Uncountable
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ is uncountably infinite.

label: Complex Numbers as External Direct Product
snippet: Let $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ be the group of non-zero complex numbers under multiplication. Let $\struct {\R_{> 0}, \times}$ be the group of positive real numbers under multiplication. Let $\struct {K, \times}$ be the circle group. Then: $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times} \cong \struct {\R_{> 0}, \times} \times \struct {K, \times}$

label: Complex Numbers as Quotient Ring of Real Polynomial
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. Let $P \sqbrk x$ be the set of polynomials over real numbers, where the coefficients of the polynomials are real. Let $\ideal {x^2 + 1} = \set {\map Q x \paren {x^2 + 1}: \map Q x \in P \sqbrk x}$ be the ideal generated by $x^2 + 1$ in $P \sqbrk x$. Let $D = P \sqbrk x / \ideal {x^2 + 1}$ be the quotient of $P \sqbrk x$ modulo $\ideal {x^2 + 1}$. Then: $\struct {\C, +, \times} \cong \struct {D, +, \times}$

label: Complex Numbers cannot be Extended to Algebra in Three Dimensions with Real Scalars
snippet: It is not possible to extend the complex numbers to an algebra of $3$ dimensions with real scalars.

label: Complex Numbers cannot be Ordered Compatibly with Ring Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {\C, +, \times}$ be the field of complex numbers. There exists no total ordering on $\struct {\C, +, \times}$ which is compatible with the structure of $\struct {\C, +, \times}$.

label: Complex Numbers form Algebra
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ forms an algebra over the field of real numbers. This algebra is: $(1): \quad$ An associative algebra. $(2): \quad$ A commutative algebra. $(3): \quad$ A normed division algebra. $(4): \quad$ A nicely normed $*$-algebra. However, $\C$ is not a real $*$-algebra.

label: Complex Numbers form Field
snippet: Consider the algebraic structure $\struct {\C, +, \times}$, where: $\C$ is the set of all complex numbers $+$ is the operation of complex addition $\times$ is the operation of complex multiplication Then $\struct {\C, +, \times}$ forms a field.

label: Complex Numbers form Integral Domain
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ forms an integral domain under addition and multiplication: $\struct {\C, +, \times}$.

label: Complex Numbers form Preordered Vector Space
snippet: Consider the complex numbers $\C$ as a vector space over itself. Define the relation $\ge^\C$ by: $z \ge^\C w$ $z - w \in \hointr 0 \infty$ for each $z, w \in \C$. Then $\struct {\C, \ge^\C}$ is a preordered vector space.

label: Complex Numbers form Ring
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ forms a ring under addition and multiplication: $\struct {\C, +, \times}$.

label: Complex Numbers form Subfield of Quaternions
snippet: The field of complex numbers $\struct {\C, +, \times}$ is isomorphic to the subfields of the quaternions $\struct {\mathbb H, +, \times}$ whose underlying subsets are: $(1): \quad \mathbb H_\mathbf i = \set {a \mathbf 1 + b \mathbf i + c \mathbf j + d \mathbf k \in \mathbb H: c = d = 0}$ $(2): \quad \mathbb H_\mathbf j = \set {a \mathbf 1 + b \mathbf i + c \mathbf j + d \mathbf k \in \mathbb H: b = d = 0}$ $(3): \quad \mathbb H_\mathbf k = \set {a \mathbf 1 + b \mathbf i + c \mathbf j + d \mathbf k \in \mathbb H: b = c = 0}$ That is: $(1): \quad \mathbb H_\mathbf i = \set {a \mathbf 1 + b…

label: Complex Numbers form Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\C$ be the complex numbers realised as a normed algebra (this is possible from Complex Numbers form Algebra). Let $\overline {\, \cdot \,}$ be complex conjugation. Then $\tuple {\C, \overline {\, \cdot \,} }$ is a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra.

label: Complex Numbers form Vector Space over Reals
snippet: Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. Then the $\R$-module $\C$ is a vector space.

label: Complex Numbers form Vector Space over Themselves
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$, with the operations of addition and multiplication, forms a vector space.

label: Complex Numbers of Type Rational a plus b root 2 form Field
snippet: Let $\Q \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}$ denote the set: $\Q \sqbrk {\sqrt 2} := \set {x \in \C: x = a + b \sqrt 2: a, b \in \Q}$ that is, all numbers of the form $a + b \sqrt 2$ where $a$ and $b$ are rational numbers. Then the algebraic structure: $\struct {\Q \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}, +, \times}$ where $+$ and $\times$ are conventional addition and multiplication on real numbers, is a number field.

label: Complex Numbers under Addition form Group
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. The structure $\struct {\C, +}$ is a group.

label: Complex Numbers under Addition form Infinite Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. The structure $\struct {\C, +}$ is an infinite abelian group.

label: Complex Numbers under Addition form Monoid
snippet: The set of complex numbers under addition $\left({\C, +}\right)$ forms a monoid.

label: Complex Numbers under Multiplication do not form Group
snippet: The algebraic structure $\struct {\C, \times}$ consisting of the set of complex numbers $\C$ under multiplication $\times$ is not a group.

label: Complex Numbers under Multiplication form Monoid
snippet: The set of complex numbers under multiplication $\struct {\C, \times}$ forms a monoid.

label: Complex Numbers with Complex Modulus form Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. Let $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ be the complex modulus. Then $\struct {\C, \size {\, \cdot \,}}$ is a normed vector space.

label: Complex Plane is Banach Space
snippet: The complex plane, along with the complex modulus, forms a Banach space over $\C$.

label: Complex Plane is Complete Metric Space
snippet: The complex plane, along with the metric induced by the norm given by the complex modulus, forms a complete metric space.

label: Complex Plane is Homeomorphic to Real Plane
snippet: Let $\C$ denote the complex plane. Let $\R^2$ denote the Euclidean plane. Then the function $\phi : \R^2 \to \C$ defined by: $\map \phi {x, y} = x + i y$ is a homeomorphism between $\R^2$ and $\C$.

label: Complex Plane is Metric Space
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of all complex numbers. Let $d: \C \times \C \to \R$ be the function defined as: $\map d {z_1, z_2} = \size {z_1 - z_2}$ where $\size z$ is the modulus of $z$. Then $d$ is a metric on $\C$ and so $\struct {\C, d}$ is a metric space.

label: Complex Plane is Separable
snippet: Let $\struct {\C, \tau_d}$ be the complex number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $\struct {\C, \tau_d}$ is separable.

label: Complex Power/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Powers ==

label: Complex Roots of Polynomial with Real Coefficients occur in Conjugate Pairs
snippet: Let $\map f z = a_n z^n + a_{n - 1} z^{n - 1} + \cdots + a_1 z + a_0$ be a polynomial over complex numbers where $a_0, \ldots, a_n$ are real numbers. Let $\alpha \in \C$ be a root of $f$. Then $\overline \alpha$ is also a root of $f$, where $\overline \alpha$ denotes the complex conjugate of $\alpha$. That is, all complex roots of $f$ appear as conjugate pairs.

label: Complex Roots of Unity/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Roots of Unity==

label: Complex Roots of Unity are Vertices of Regular Polygon Inscribed in Circle
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n \ge 3$. Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number such that $z^n = 1$. Let $U_n = \set {e^{2 i k \pi / n}: k \in \N_n}$ be the set of $n$th roots of unity. Let $U_n$ be plotted on the complex plane. Then the elements of $U_n$ are located at the vertices of a regular $n$-sided polygon $P$, such that: $(1):\quad$ $P$ is circumscribed by a unit circle whose center is at $\tuple {0, 0}$ $(2):\quad$ one of those vertices is at $\tuple {1, 0}$.

label: Complex Roots of Unity in Exponential Form
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 0$. Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number such that $z^n = 1$. Then: $U_n = \set {e^{2 i k \pi / n}: k \in \N_n}$ where $U_n$ is the set of $n$th roots of unity. That is: $z \in \set {1, e^{2 i \pi / n}, e^{4 i \pi / n}, \ldots, e^{2 \paren {n - 1} i \pi / n} }$ Thus for every integer $n$, the number of $n$th roots of unity is $n$. Setting $\omega := e^{2 i \pi / n}$, $U_n$ can then be written as: $U_n = \set {1, \omega, \omega^2, \ldots, \omega^{n - 1} }$

label: Complex Roots of Unity include 1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $U_n = \set {z \in \C: z^n = 1}$ be the set of complex $n$th roots of unity. Then $1 \in U_n$. That is, $1$ is always one of the complex $n$th roots of unity of any $n$.

label: Complex Roots of Unity occur in Conjugate Pairs
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $U_n$ denote the complex $n$th roots of unity: $U_n = \set {z \in \C: z^n = 1}$ Let $\alpha \in U_n$ be the first complex $n$th root of unity. Then: $\forall k \in \Z_{>0}, k < \dfrac n 2: \overline {\alpha^k} = \alpha^{n - k}$ That is, each of the complex $n$th roots of unity occur in conjugate pairs: $\tuple {\alpha, \alpha^{n - 1} }; \tuple {\alpha^2, \alpha^{n - 2} }; \ldots; \tuple {\alpha^s, \alpha^{n - s} }$ where: $s = \dfrac {n - 1} 2$ for odd $n$ $s = \dfrac {n - 2} 2$ for even $n$.

label: Complex Subtraction/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Subtraction ==

label: Complex Subtraction is Closed
snippet: The set of complex numbers is closed under subtraction: $\forall a, b \in \C: a - b \in \C$

label: Complex Trigonometric Functions are Entire
snippet: Let $F$ be a trigonometric function over the complex numbers. Then $F$ is an entire function.

label: Complex Vector Inner Product is Complex Inner Product
snippet: The complex vector inner product is an example of a complex inner product.

label: Complex Vector Space is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\C$ denote the set of complex numbers. Then the complex vector space $\C^n$ is a vector space.

label: Complex Vector Space with Dot Product is Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\C^d$ be a complex vector space with $d$ dimensions. Let $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ be the dot product on $\C^d$. Then $\C^d$ endowed with $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ is a Hilbert space.

label: Component Mappings of Set Coproduct are Injective
snippet: Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be sets. Let $\struct {C, i_1, i_2}$ be a coproduct of $S_1$ and $S_2$. Then $i_1$ and $i_2$ are injections.

label: Component is not necessarily Path Component
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $C$ be a component of $T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $C$ is also an path component of $T$.

label: Component of Complement of Jordan Curve has Curve as Boundary
snippet: Let $\phi : \closedint 0 1 \to \R^2$ be a Jordan curve. Let $J = \phi \closedint 0 1$ be the image of $\phi$. Suppose that $\R^2 \setminus J$ has at least two distinct components. Then, for any component $U$ of $\R^2 \setminus J$: $\partial U = J$ where $\partial U$ denotes the boundary of $U$.

label: Component of Finite Union in Ultrafilter
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $\UU$ be a ultrafilter on $S$. Let $\set {Y_1, \dots, Y_n}$ be a pairwise disjoint set of subsets of $S$ such that $S = Y_1 \cup \cdots \cup Y_n$. Then there is a unique $k \in \set {1, \dots, n}$ such that $Y_k \in \UU$.

label: Component of Locally Connected Space is Open
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a locally connected topological space. Let $G$ be a component of $T$. Then $G$ is open.

label: Component of Point is not always Intersection of its Clopen Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $\map {\operatorname {Comp}_x} T$ denote the component of $x$ in $T$. Let $K_x = \ds \bigcap_{x \mathop \in K} K$ clopen in $T$. Then it is not always the case that $\map {\operatorname {Comp}_x} T = K_x$

label: Component of Resolvent Set of Element in Unital Banach Algebra is Disjoint from or Component of Resolvent Set in Closed Subalgebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $B$ be a closed unital subalgebra of $A$. Let $x \in B$. Let $\map {\rho_A} x$ and $\map {\rho_B} x$ be the resolvent sets of $x$ in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Let $U$ be a component of $\map {\rho_A} x$. Then either: $U$ is a component of $\map {\rho_B} x$ or: $U \cap \map {\rho_B} x = \O$

label: Component of Vector/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Components of Vectors ==

label: Components and Quasicomponents of Arens-Fort Space are Equal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the Arens-Fort space. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a subset of $T$. Then: $A$ is a component of $T$ $A$ is a quasicomponent of $T$.

label: Components are Open iff Union of Open Connected Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. $(1): \quad$ The components of $T$ are open. $(2): \quad S$ is a union of open connected sets of $T$.

label: Components of Integer Reciprocal Space with Zero are Single Points
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set 0 \cup \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space with zero under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then the components of $A$ are singletons.

label: Components of Metric at Origin of Normal Neighborhood of Pseudo-Riemannian Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Let $U_p$ be the normal neighborhood for $p \in M$. Let $\struct {U_p, \tuple {x^i}}$ be a normal coordinate chart. Suppose $g_{ij}$ are the components of metric $g$ in coordinates $\tuple {x^i}$ at $p \in M$. Then: $g_{ij} = \pm_{ij} \delta_{ij}$ where $\delta_{ij}$ denotes the Kronecker delta, and $\pm_{ij}$ is a sign that depends on $i$ and $j$.

label: Components of Metric at Origin of Normal Neighborhood of Riemannian Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Let $U_p$ be the normal neighborhood for $p \in M$. Let $\struct {U_p, \tuple {x^i}}$ be a normal coordinate chart. Suppose $g_{ij}$ are the components of metric $g$ in coordinates $\tuple {x^i}$ at $p \in M$. Then: $g_{ij} = \delta_{ij}$ where $\delta_{ij}$ denotes the Kronecker delta.

label: Components of Separation are Clopen
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \mid B$ be a separation of $T$. Then both $A$ and $B$ are clopen in $T$.

label: Components of Separation are Separated Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \mid B$ be a separation of $T$. Then $A$ and $B$ are separated sets of $T$.

label: Components of Vector between two Points
snippet: Let $A, B$ be points in the Euclidean space $\R^n$. Let their Cartesian coordinates be given by: {{eqn | l = A | r = \tuple {a_1 , a_2, \ldots, a_n } }} {{eqn | l = B | r = \tuple {b_1 , b_2, \ldots, b_n } }} Let $\vec {AB}$ be the vector quantity that represents the directed line segment with startpoint $A$ and endpoint $B$. Then the vector components of $\vec {AB}$ are: $\vec {AB} = \tuple {b_1 - a_1, b_2 - a_2, \ldots, b_n - a_n}$

label: Components of Zero Vector Quantity are Zero
snippet: Let $\mathbf r$ be a vector quantity embedded in a Cartesian $3$-space. Let $\mathbf r$ be expressed in terms of its components: $\mathbf r = x \mathbf i + y \mathbf j + z \mathbf k$ Let $\mathbf r$ be the zero vector. Then: $x = y = z = 0$

label: Composite Complete Lattice Homomorphisms is Complete Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{A_1, \preceq_1}$, $L_2 = \struct{A_2, \preceq_2}$ and $L_3 = \struct{A_3, \preceq_3}$ be complete lattices. Let $\phi_1: L_1 \to L_2$ and $\phi_2: L_2 \to L_3$ be complete lattice homomorphisms. Let $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1 : A_1 \to A_3$ be the composite mapping of $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ Then: $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1$ is a complete lattice homomorphism of $L_1$ to $L_3$

label: Composite Fibonacci Numbers with Prime Index
snippet: The sequence of composite Fibonacci numbers with a prime index begins: $4181, 1 \, 346 \, 269, 24 \, 157 \, 817, 165 \, 580 \, 141, \ldots$ The corresponding sequence of prime indices begins: $19, 31, 37, 41, 53, 59, 61, 67, 71, 73, 79, \ldots$

label: Composite Frame Homomorphism is Frame Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{S_1, \preceq_1}$, $L_2 = \struct{S_2, \preceq_2}$ and $L_3 = \struct{S_3, \preceq_3}$ be frames. Let $\phi_1: L_1 \to L_2$ and $\phi_2: L_2 \to L_3$ be frame homomorphisms. Let $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1 : S_1 \to S_3$ be the composite mapping of $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ Then: $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1$ is a frame homomorphism of $L_1$ to $L_3$

label: Composite Functor is Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf C, \mathbf D$ and $\mathbf E$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ and $G: \mathbf D \to \mathbf E$ be covariant functors. Let $GF: \mathbf C \to \mathbf E$ be the composition of $G$ with $F$. Then $G F$ is also a covariant functor.

label: Composite Mapping is Mapping
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, S_3$ be sets. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ and $g: S_2 \to S_3$ be mappings. Then the composite mapping $g \circ f$ is also a mapping.

label: Composite Mersenne Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Composite Mersenne Numbers ==

label: Composite Number has Prime Factor
snippet: Let $a$ be a composite number. Then there exists a prime number $p$ such that: $p \divides a$ where $\divides$ means is a divisor of.

label: Composite Number has Prime Factor not Greater Than its Square Root
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ and $n = p_1 \times p_2 \times \cdots \times p_j$, $j \ge 2$, where $p_1, \ldots, p_j \in \Bbb P$ are prime factors of $n$. Then $\exists p_i \in \Bbb P$ such that $p_i \le \sqrt n$. That is, if $n \in \N$ is composite, then $n$ has a prime factor $p \le \sqrt n$.

label: Composite Number has Two Divisors Less Than It
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 1}$ such that $n \notin \mathbb P$. Then: $\exists a, b \in \Z: 1 < a < n, 1 < b < n: n = a b$ That is, a non-prime number greater than $1$ can be expressed as the product of two positive integers strictly greater than $1$ and less than $n$. Note that these two numbers are not necessarily distinct.

label: Composite of Antisymmetric Relations is not necessarily Antisymmetric
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be antisymmetric relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is not necessarily also antisymmetric.

label: Composite of Automorphisms is Automorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ be an algebraic structure. Let: $\phi: \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n} \to \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ $\psi: \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n} \to \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ be automorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also an automorphism.

label: Composite of Connected Relation is not necessarily Connected
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be connected relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is not necessarily also connected.

label: Composite of Continuous Mappings at Point between Metric Spaces is Continuous at Point
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {X_1, d_1}, M_2 = \struct {X_2, d_2}, M_3 = \struct {X_3, d_3}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: M_1 \to M_2$ be continuous at $a \in X_1$. Let $g: M_2 \to M_3$ be continuous at $\map f a \in X_2$. Then their composite $g \circ f: M_1 \to M_3$ is continuous at $a \in X_1$.

label: Composite of Continuous Mappings between Metric Spaces is Continuous
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {X_1, d_1}$, $M_2 = \struct {X_2, d_2}$ and $M_3 = \struct {X_3, d_3}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: M_1 \to M_2$ and $g: M_2 \to M_3$ be continuous mappings. Then their composite $g \circ f: M_1 \to M_3$ is continuous.

label: Composite of Continuous Mappings is Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1, T_2, T_3$ be topological spaces. Let $f: T_1 \to T_2$ and $g: T_2 \to T_3$ be continuous mappings. Then the composite mapping $g \circ f: T_1 \to T_3$ is continuous.

label: Composite of Continuous Real Functions at Point is Continuous
snippet: Let $\R$ denote the real numbers. Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions. Let $g$ be continuous at a point $a \in \R$. Let $f$ be continuous at the point $\map g a \in \R$. Then their composite $f \circ g$ is continuous at $a$.

label: Composite of Continuous Real Functions is Continuous
snippet: Let $\R$ denote the real numbers. Let $g: S \to T$ be a real function which is continuous on a real interval $S \subseteq \R$. Let $f: T \to \R$ be a real function which is continuous on a real interval $T \subseteq \R$. Then their composite $f \circ g: I \to \R$ is continuous on $I$.

label: Composite of Endomorphisms is Endomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ be an algebraic structure. Let: $\phi: \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n} \to \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ $\psi: \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n} \to \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ be endomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also an endomorphism.

label: Composite of Epimorphisms is Epimorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {S_1, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n}$ $\struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$ $\struct {S_3, \oplus_1, \oplus_2, \ldots, \oplus_n}$ be algebraic structures. Let: $\phi: \struct {S_1, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n} \to \struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$ $\psi: \struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n} \to \struct {S_3, \oplus_1, \oplus_2, \ldots, \oplus_n}$ be epimorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also an epimorphism.

label: Composite of Evaluation Mapping and Projection
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\family {Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces for some indexing set $I$. Let $\family {f_i : X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of continuous mappings. Let $\ds Y = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} Y_i$ be the product space of $\family {Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be the evaluation mapping induced by $\family{f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let: $pr_i : Y \to Y_i$ denote the $i$th projection on $Y$ Then: $\forall i \in I: pr_i \circ f = f_i$

label: Composite of Group Epimorphisms is Epimorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {G_1, \odot}$ $\struct {G_2, *}$ $\struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be groups. Let: $\phi: \struct {G_1, \odot} \to \struct {G_2, *}$ $\psi: \struct {G_2, *} \to \struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be (group) epimorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (group) epimorphism.

label: Composite of Group Homomorphisms is Homomorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {G_1, \circ}$ $\struct {G_2, *}$ $\struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be groups. Let: $\phi: \struct {G_1, \circ} \to \struct {G_2, *}$ $\psi: \struct {G_2, *} \to \struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be homomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a homomorphism.

label: Composite of Group Isomorphisms is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {G_1, \circ}$, $\struct {G_2, *}$ and $\struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be groups. Let $\phi: \struct {G_1, \circ} \to \struct {G_2, *}$ and $\psi: \struct {G_2, *} \to \struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be group isomorphisms. Then the composite of $\psi$ with $\phi$ is also a group isomorphism.

label: Composite of Group Monomorphisms is Monomorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {G_1, \circ}$ $\struct {G_2, *}$ $\struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be groups. Let: $\phi: \struct {G_1, \circ} \to \struct {G_2, *}$ $\psi: \struct {G_2, *} \to \struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be monomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a monomorphism.

label: Composite of Homeomorphisms between Metric Spaces is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $M_1, M_2, M_3$ be metric spaces. Let $f: M_1 \to M_2$ and $g: M_2 \to M_3$ be homeomorphisms. Then $g \circ f: M_1 \to M_3$ is also a homeomorphism.

label: Composite of Homeomorphisms is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_1, T_2, T_3$ be topological spaces. Let $f: T_1 \to T_2$ and $g: T_2 \to T_3$ be homeomorphisms. Then $g \circ f: T_1 \to T_3$ is also a homeomorphism.

label: Composite of Injection on Surjection is not necessarily Either
snippet: Let $f$ be an injection. Let $g$ be a surjection. Let $f \circ g$ denote the composition of $f$ with $g$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $f \circ g$ is either a surjection or an injection.

label: Composite of Injections is Injection
snippet: A composite of injections is an injection. That is: If $f$ and $g$ are injections, then so is $f \circ g$.

label: Composite of Monomorphisms is Monomorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {S_1, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n}$ $\struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$ $\struct {S_3, \oplus_1, \oplus_2, \ldots, \oplus_n}$ be algebraic structures. Let: $\phi: \struct {S_1, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n} \to \struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$ $\psi: \struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n} \to \struct {S_3, \oplus_1, \oplus_2, \ldots, \oplus_n}$ be monomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a monomorphism.

label: Composite of Orderings is not necessarily Ordering
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be orderings on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is not necessarily also an ordering on $A$.

label: Composite of Permutations is Permutation
snippet: Let $f, g$ are permutations of a set $S$. Then their composite $g \circ f$ is also a permutation of $S$.

label: Composite of Quotient Mappings
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR_1$ be an equivalence on $S$, and $\RR_2$ be an equivalence on the quotient set $S / \RR_1$. We can find an equivalence $\RR_3$ on $S$ such that $\paren {S / \RR_1} / \RR_2$ is in one-to-one correspondence with $S / \RR_3$ under the mapping: $\phi: \paren {S / \RR_1} / \RR_2 \to S / \RR_3: \eqclass {\eqclass x {\RR_1} } {\RR_2} \mapsto \eqclass x {\RR_3}$.

label: Composite of Quotient Mappings in Topology is Quotient Mapping
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$, $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$, $T_3 = \struct {S_3, \tau_3}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ and $g: S_2 \to S_3$ be quotient mappings. Then $g \circ f : S_1 \to S_3$ is a quotient mapping.

label: Composite of Reflexive Relations is Reflexive
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be reflexive relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is also reflexive.

label: Composite of Surjection on Injection is not necessarily Either
snippet: Let $f$ be an injection. Let $g$ be a surjection. Let $g \circ f$ denote the composition of $g$ with $f$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $g \circ f$ is either a surjection or an injection.

label: Composite of Symmetric Relations is not necessarily Symmetric
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be symmetric relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is not necessarily symmetric.

label: Composite of Three Mappings in Cycle forming Injections and Surjection
snippet: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be non-empty sets. Let $f: A \to B$, $g: B \to C$ and $h: C \to A$ be mappings. Let the following hold: $h \circ g \circ f$ is an injection $f \circ h \circ g$ is an injection $g \circ f \circ h$ is a surjection. where: $g \circ f$ (and so on) denote composition of mappings. Then each of $f$, $g$ and $h$ are bijections.

label: Composite of Total Relations is Total
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be total relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is also total.

label: Composite of Transitive Relations is not necessarily Transitive
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be transitive relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is not necessarily also transitive.

label: Composition Mapping of Restriction Mappings
snippet: Let $S$, $T$, and $U$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ and $g: T \to U$ be mappings. Let $A \subseteq S$, $B \subseteq T$ and $C \subseteq U$. Let $f \sqbrk S \subseteq B$ and $g \sqbrk T \subseteq C$. Then: {{eqn| l = \paren{g \circ f} \restriction_{A \times C} | r = \paren{g \restriction_{B \times C} } \circ \paren{f \restriction_{A \times B} } }} where: $\paren{g \circ f} \restriction_{A \times C}$ is the restriction of $g \circ f$ to $A \times C$ $f \restriction_{A \times B}$ is the restriction of $f$ to $A \times B$ $g \restriction_{B \times C}$ is the restriction of $g$ to $B \times C$

label: Composition Series/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Composition Series ==

label: Composition Series of Group of Prime Power Order
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$, and whose order is a prime power: $\order G = p^n, p \in \mathbb P, n \ge 1$ Then $G$ has a composition series: $\set e = G_0 \subset G_1 \subset \ldots \subset G_n = G$ such that: $\order {G_k} = p^k$ where: $G_k \lhd G_{k + 1}$ $G_{k + 1} / G_k$ is cyclic and of order $p$.

label: Composition of 3 Mappings where Pairs of Mappings are Bijections
snippet: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ be sets. Let: $f: A \to B$ $g: B \to C$ $h: C \to D$ be mappings. Let $g \circ f$ and $h \circ g$ be bijections. Then $f$, $g$ and $h$ are all bijections.

label: Composition of Commuting Idempotent Mappings is Idempotent
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be idempotent mappings from $S$ to $S$. Let: $f \circ g = g \circ f$ where $\circ$ denotes composition. Then $f \circ g$ is idempotent.

label: Composition of Compatible Closure Operators
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: \powerset S \to \powerset S$ be closure operators on $S$. Let $\CC_f$ and $\CC_g$ be the sets of closed sets of $S$ with respect to $f$ and $g$ respectively. For each subset $T$ of $S$, let the following hold: $(1): \quad$ If $T$ is closed with respect to $g$, then $\map f T$ is closed with respect to $g$. That is, if $T \in \CC_g$ then $\map f T \in \CC_g$. $(2): \quad$ If $T$ is closed with respect to $f$, then $\map g T$ is closed with respect to $f$. That is, if $T \in \CC_f$ then $\map g T \in \CC_f$. Let $\CC_h = \CC_f \cap \CC_g$.

label: Composition of Computable Real-Valued Functions is Computable
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \R^n$ and $E \subseteq \R^m$ be subsets of real cartesian space. Let $f : D \to \R$ be computable. Let $g_1, g_2, \dotsc, g_n : E \to \R$ be computable. Suppose that, for every $\bsx \in E$: $\tuple {\map {g_1} \bsx, \map {g_2} \bsx, \dotsc, \map {g_n} \bsx} \in D$ Then $h : E \to \R$ defined as: $\map h {x_1, \dotsc, x_m} = \map f {\map {g_1} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}, \dotsc, \map {g_n} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}}$ is computable.

label: Composition of Computably Uniformly Continuous Real-Valued Functions is Computably Uniformly Continuous
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \R^n$ and $E \subseteq \R^m$ be subsets of real cartesian space. Let $f : D \to \R$ be computably uniformly continuous. Let $g_1, g_2, \dotsc, g_n : E \to \R$ be computably uniformly continuous. Suppose that, for every $\bsx \in E$: $\tuple {\map {g_1} \bsx, \map {g_2} \bsx, \dotsc, \map {g_n} \bsx} \in D$ Then $h : E \to \R$ defined as: $\map h {x_1, \dotsc, x_m} = \map f {\map {g_1} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}, \dotsc, \map {g_n} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}}$ is computably uniformly continuous.

label: Composition of Continuous Mapping on Compact Space Preserves Uniform Convergence
snippet: Let $\struct{ X, d_X }$ be a compact metric space. Let $\struct{ Y, d_Y }, \struct{ Z, d_Z }$ be metric spaces. Let $\phi : Y \to Z$ be a continuous mapping. For all $n \in \N$, let $f_n : X \to Y$ be a continuous mapping. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping such that $\sequence {f_n}_{n \in \N}$ converges to $f$ uniformly on $X$. Then the sequence $\sequence {\phi \circ f_n}_{n \in \N}$ converges to $\phi \circ f$ uniformly on $X$.

label: Composition of Dirac Delta Distribution with Function with Simple Zero
snippet: Let $\delta \in \map {\DD'} \R$ be the Dirac delta distribution. Let $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a delta sequence. Let $f : \R \to \R$ be a real function with a simple zero at $x_0$. Let $f$ be strictly monotone. Let $\phi \in \map \DD \R$ be a test function. Then in the distributional sense it holds that: $\map \delta {\map f x} = \dfrac {\map \delta {x - x_0} } {\size {\map {f'} {x_0} } }$ which can be interpreted as: $\ds \int_{-\infty}^\infty \map \delta {\map f x} \map \phi x \rd x = \dfrac {\map \phi {x_0} } {\size {\map {f'} {x_0} } }$ which more strictly…

label: Composition of Direct Image Mappings of Mappings
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be non-empty sets. Let $f: A \to B$ and $g: B \to C$ be mappings. Let: $f^\to: \powerset A \to \powerset B$ and $g^\to: \powerset B \to \powerset C$ be the direct image mappings of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {g \circ f}^\to = g^\to \circ f^\to$

label: Composition of Direct Image Mappings of Relations
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be non-empty sets. Let $\RR_1 \subseteq A \times B, \RR_2 \subseteq B \times C$ be relations. Let: ${\RR_1}^\to: \powerset A \to \powerset B$ and ${\RR_2}^\to: \powerset B \to \powerset C$ be the direct image mappings of $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$. Then: $\paren {\RR_2 \circ \RR_1}^\to = {\RR_2}^\to \circ {\RR_1}^\to$

label: Composition of Direct Sums of Bounded Linear Operators on Hilbert Space
Composition of Distance-Preserving Mappings is Distance-Preserving
snippet: Let: $\struct {X_1, d_1}$ $\struct {X_2, d_2}$ $\struct {X_3, d_3}$ be metric spaces. Let: $\phi: \struct {X_1, d_1} \to \struct {X_2, d_2}$ $\psi: \struct {X_2, d_2} \to \struct {X_3, d_3}$ be distance-preserving mappings. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a distance-preserving mapping.

label: Composition of Functors is Associative
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$, $\mathbf B$, $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf A \to \mathbf B$, $G: \mathbf B \to \mathbf C$ and $H: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be functors. Then composition of functors is associative: $H \paren {G F} = \paren {H G} F$

label: Composition of Idempotent Mappings
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be idempotent mappings. Suppose that $f \circ g$ and $g \circ f$ have the same images. That is, suppose that $f \sqbrk {g \sqbrk S} = g \sqbrk {f \sqbrk S}$. Then $f \circ g$ and $g \circ f$ are idempotent.

label: Composition of Identification Mappings is Identification Mapping
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ and $S_3$ be sets. Let $f_1: S_1 \to S_2$ and $f_2: S_2 \to S_3$ be mappings. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f_1$ and $\tau_1$. Let $\tau_3$ be the identification topology on $S_3$ with respect to $f_2$ and $\tau_2$. Let $\phi: S_1 \to S_3$ be the composition of $f_2$ with $f_1$: $\phi = f_2 \circ f_1$ Then $\phi$ is itself an identification mapping.

label: Composition of Inverse Image Mappings of Mappings
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be non-empty sets. Let $f: A \to B, g: B \to C$ be mappings. Let: $f^\gets: \powerset B \to \powerset A$ and $g^\gets: \powerset C \to \powerset B$ be the inverse image mappings of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {g \circ f}^\gets = f^\gets \circ g^\gets$

label: Composition of Isometries is Isometry
snippet: Let: $\struct {X_1, d_1}$ $\struct {X_2, d_2}$ $\struct {X_3, d_3}$ be metric spaces. Let: $\phi: \struct {X_1, d_1} \to \struct {X_2, d_2}$ $\psi: \struct {X_2, d_2} \to \struct {X_3, d_3}$ be isometries. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also an isometry.

label: Composition of Isomorphisms is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $f: A \to B$ and $g: B \to C$ be isomorphisms with inverses $f^{-1}: B \to A$ and $g^{-1}: C \to B$ respectively. Then: the composition $g \circ f: A \to C$ is an isomorphism with inverse $f^{-1} \circ g^{-1}: C \to A$.

label: Composition of Linear Real Functions
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\theta_{a, b}: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map {\theta_{a, b} } x = a x + b$ Let $\theta_{c, d} \circ \theta_{a, b}$ denote the composition of $\theta_{c, d}$ with $\theta_{a, b}$. Then: $\theta_{c, d} \circ \theta_{a, b} = \theta_{a c, b c + d}$

label: Composition of Linear Transformations is Isomorphic to Matrix Product
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $F$, $G$ and $H$ be free $R$-modules of finite dimension $p, n, m > 0$ respectively. Let $\sequence {a_p}$, $\sequence {b_n}$ and $\sequence {c_m}$ be ordered bases Let $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$ denote the set of all linear transformations from $G$ to $H$. Let $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$ be the $m \times n$ matrix space over $R$. Let $\sqbrk {u; \sequence {c_m}, \sequence {b_n} }$ be the matrix of $u$ relative to $\sequence {b_n}$ and $\sequence {c_m}$.

label: Composition of Linear Transformations is Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X, Y, Z$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $T_1 : X \to Y$ and $T_2 : Y \to Z$ be linear transformations. Then the composition $T_2 \circ T_1 : X \to Z$ is a linear transformation.

label: Composition of Mapping and Inclusion is Restriction of Mapping
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $A \subseteq S$. Then $f \circ i_A = f \restriction A$ where $i_A$ denotes the inclusion mapping of $A$, $f \restriction A$ denotes the restriction of $f$ to $A$.

label: Composition of Mapping with Inclusion is Restriction
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a subset of the domain of $S$. Let $i_A: A \to S$ be the inclusion mapping from $A$ to $S$. Then: $f \circ i_A = f \restriction_A$ where $f \restriction_A$ denotes the restriction of $f$ to $A$.

label: Composition of Mapping with Mapping Restricted to Image
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be sets. Let $f : A \to B, g: B \to C$ be mappings. Let $g \circ f : A \to C$ denote the composite mapping of $f$ with $g$. Let $f \sqbrk A$ denote the image of $A$ under $f$. Let $f \restriction_{A \times f \sqbrk A} : A \to f \sqbrk A$ denote the restriction of $f$ to $A \times f \sqbrk A$. Let $g \restriction_{f \sqbrk A} : f \sqbrk A \to C$ denote the restriction of $g$ to $f \sqbrk A$.

label: Composition of Mappings is Left Distributive over Homomorphism of Pointwise Operation
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ and $\struct {T, \otimes}$ be algebraic structures. Let: $S^A$ denote the set of mappings from $A$ to $S$. Let $f$ be a homomorphism from $S$ to $T$. Let $g, h \in S^A$ be mappings from $A$ to $S$. Then: $f \circ \paren {g \odot h} = \paren {f \circ g} \otimes \paren {f \circ h}$ where: $g \odot h$ denotes the pointwise operation on $S^A$ induced by $\odot$ $f \circ h$ denotes the composition of $f$ with $h$.

label: Composition of Mappings is Right Distributive over Pointwise Operation
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be an algebraic structure. Let: $B^A$ denote the set of mappings from $A$ to $B$ $S^B$ denote the set of mappings from $B$ to $S$. Let $f, g \in S^B$ be mappings from $B$ to $S$. Let $h \in B^A$ be a mapping from $A$ to $B$. Then: $\paren {f \odot g} \circ h = \paren {f \circ h} \odot \paren {g \circ h}$ where: $f \odot g$ denotes the pointwise operation on $S^B$ induced by $\odot$ $g \circ h$ denotes the composition of $g$ with $h$.

label: Composition of Mappings is not Commutative
snippet: The composition of mappings is not in general a commutative binary operation: $f_2 \circ f_1 \ne f_1 \circ f_2$

label: Composition of Measurable Mappings is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X_1, \Sigma_1}$, $\struct {X_2, \Sigma_2}$ and $\struct {X_3, \Sigma_3}$ be measurable spaces. Let $f: X_1 \to X_2$ be a $\Sigma_1 \, / \, \Sigma_2$-measurable mapping. Let $g: X_2 \to X_3$ be a $\Sigma_2 \, / \, \Sigma_3$-measurable mapping. Then their composition $g \circ f: X_1 \to X_3$ is $\Sigma_1 \, / \, \Sigma_3$-measurable.

label: Composition of One-Variable URM Computable Functions
snippet: Let $f: \N \to \N$ and $g: \N \to \N$ be URM computable functions of one variable. Let $f \circ g$ be the composition of $f$ and $g$. Then $f \circ g: \N \to \N$ is a URM computable function.

label: Composition of Open Mappings is Open Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau_X}$, $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ and $\struct {Z, \tau_Z}$ be topological spaces. Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be open mappings. Then $g \circ f : X \to Z$ is an open mapping.

label: Composition of Permutations is not Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\map \Gamma S$ denote the set of permutations on $S$. Let $\pi, \rho$ be elements of $\map \Gamma S$ Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\pi \circ \rho = \rho \circ \pi$ where $\circ$ denotes composition.

label: Composition of Relations Preserves Subsets
snippet: Let $A, B, S, T$ be relations as subsets of Cartesian products. Let $A \subseteq B$ and $S \subset T$. Then: $A \circ S \subseteq B \circ T$

label: Composition of Repeated Compositions of Injections
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an injection. Let the sequence of mappings: $f^0, f^1, f^2, \ldots, f^n, \ldots$ be defined as: $\forall n \in \N: f^n \left({x}\right) = \begin{cases} x & : n = 0 \\ f \left({x}\right) & : n = 1 \\ f \left({f^{n-1} \left({x}\right)}\right) & : n > 1 \end{cases}$ Then: $\forall m, n \in \Z_{\ge 0}: f^n \circ f^m = f^{m + n}$ where $f^n \circ f^m$ denotes composition of mappings.

label: Composition of Ring Automorphisms is Ring Automorphism
snippet: Let $R$ be a set. Let: $\struct {R, +_1, \circ_1}$ $\struct {R, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\struct {R, +_3, \circ_3}$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \struct {R, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\psi: \struct {R, +_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {R, +_3, \circ_3}$ be ring automorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (ring) automorphism.

label: Composition of Ring Endomorphisms is Ring Endomorphism
snippet: Let $R$ be a set. Let: $\struct {R, +_1, \circ_1}$ $\struct {R, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\struct {R, +_3, \circ_3}$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \struct {R, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\psi: \struct {R, +_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {R, +_3, \circ_3}$ be (ring) endomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (ring) endomorphism.

label: Composition of Ring Epimorphisms is Ring Epimorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}$ $\struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\struct {R_3, +_3, \circ_3}$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\psi: \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {R_3, +_3, \circ_3}$ be (ring) epimorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (ring) epimorphism.

label: Composition of Ring Homomorphisms is Ring Homomorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {R_1, +_1, \odot_1}$ $\struct {R_2, +_2, \odot_2}$ $\struct {R_3, +_3, \odot_3}$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \odot_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \odot_2}$ $\psi: \struct {R_2, +_2, \odot_2} \to \struct {R_3, +_3, \odot_3}$ be homomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a homomorphism.

label: Composition of Ring Isomorphisms is Ring Isomorphism
snippet: Let: $\left({R_1, +_1, \circ_1}\right)$ $\left({R_2, +_2, \circ_2}\right)$ $\left({R_3, +_3, \circ_3}\right)$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \left({R_1, +_1, \circ_1}\right) \to \left({R_2, +_2, \circ_2}\right)$ $\psi: \left({R_2, +_2, \circ_2}\right) \to \left({R_3, +_3, \circ_3}\right)$ be (ring) isomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (ring) isomorphism.

label: Composition of Ring Monomorphisms is Ring Monomorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}$ $\struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\struct {R_3, +_3, \circ_3}$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\psi: \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {R_3, +_3, \circ_3}$ be (ring) monomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (ring) monomorphism.

label: Composition of Sequence with Mapping
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_j}_{j \mathop \in B}$ be a sequence. Let $\sigma: A \to B$ be a mapping, where $A \subseteq \N$. Then $\sequence {a_j} \circ \sigma$ is a sequence whose value at each $k \in A$ is $a_{\map \sigma k}$. Thus $\sequence {a_j} \circ \sigma$ is denoted $\sequence {a_{\map \sigma k} }_{k \mathop \in A}$.

label: Composition of Sequentially Computable Real-Valued Functions is Sequentially Computable
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \R^n$ and $E \subseteq \R^m$ be subsets of real cartesian space. Let $f : D \to \R$ be sequentially computable. Let $g_1, g_2, \dotsc, g_n : E \to \R$ be sequentially computable. Suppose that, for every $\bsx \in E$: $\tuple {\map {g_1} \bsx, \map {g_2} \bsx, \dotsc, \map {g_n} \bsx} \in D$ Then $h : E \to \R$ defined as: $\map h {x_1, \dotsc, x_m} = \map f {\map {g_1} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}, \dotsc, \map {g_n} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}}$ is sequentially computable.

label: Composition of Symmetric Relation with Itself is Union of Products of Images
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a symmetric relation on a set $S$. Then: $\RR \circ \RR = \ds \map {\bigcup_{s \mathop \in S} } {\map \RR s \times \map \RR s}$ where $\RR \circ \RR$ is the composition of $\RR$ with itself $\map \RR s$ is the image of $s$ under $\RR$ $\map \RR s \times \map \RR s$ is the Cartesian product of $\map \RR s$ with itself

label: Composition of Symmetries is Associative
snippet: Let $P$ be a geometric figure. Let $S_P$ be the set of all symmetries of $P$. Let $\circ$ denote composition of mappings. Let $\phi, \psi, \chi$ be symmetries of $P$. Then: $\paren {\phi \circ \psi} \circ \chi = \phi \circ \paren {\psi \circ \chi}$ That is, composition of symmetries is associative.

label: Composition of Symmetries is Symmetry
snippet: Let $P$ be a geometric figure. Let $S_P$ be the set of all symmetries of $P$. Let $\circ$ denote composition of mappings. Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be symmetries of $P$. Then $\phi \circ \psi$ is also a symmetry of $P$.

label: Composition of Three Mappings which form Identity Mapping
snippet: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be non-empty sets. Let $f: A \to B$, $g: B \to C$ and $h: C \to A$ be mappings. Let the following hold: where: $g \circ f$ (and so on) denote composition of mappings $I_A$ (and so on) denote the identity mappings. Then each of $f$, $g$ and $h$ are bijections, and: {{eqn | l = f^{-1} | r = h \circ g }} {{eqn | l = g^{-1} | r = f \circ h }} {{eqn | l = h^{-1} | r = g \circ f }} where $f^{-1}$ (and so on) denote the inverse mappings.

label: Composition of Weakly Compact Linear Transformation and Bounded Linear Transformation is Weakly Compact
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$, $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ and $\struct {Z, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Z}$ be Banach spaces over $\GF$. Let $T : X 	o Y$ be a weakly compact linear transformation. Let $A : Y 	o Z$ be a bounded linear transformation. Let $B : Z 	o X$ be a bounded linear transformation. Then: $(1): \quad$ $T B : Z 	o Y$ is weakly compact $(2): \quad$ $A T : X 	o Z$ is weakly compact.

label: Composition with Zero Morphism is Zero Morphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $0$ be a zero object in $\mathbf C$. Let $A, B, C, D$ be objects in $\mathbf C$. Let $f : A \to B$, $g : B \to C$ and $h : C \to D$ be morphisms in $\mathbf C$. Let $g$ be a zero morphism. Then $g \circ f$ and $h \circ g$ are zero morphisms.

label: Compound Distribution of Poisson Distributed Bernoulli Trials has Poisson Distribution
snippet: Let $N$ be a discrete random variable with a Poisson distribution with expectation $\lambda$. Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_N$ be pairwise independent discrete random variables each with a Bernoulli distribution with parameter $P$. Let $S_N : X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_N$ be the resulting compound distribution. Then $S_N$ has a Poisson distribution with expectation $\lambda p$.
