label: Countable Closed Ordinal Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $\Omega$ denote the first uncountable ordinal. Let $\Gamma$ be a limit ordinal which strictly precedes $\Omega$. Let $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ denote the closed ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Then $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ is a second-countable space.

label: Countable Compactness is Preserved under Continuous Surjection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a continuous surjection. If $T_A$ is countably compact, then $T_B$ is also countably compact.

label: Countable Complement Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is a Lindelöf space.

label: Countable Complement Space is not Countably Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a countably compact space.

label: Countable Complement Space is not First-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a first-countable space.

label: Countable Complement Space is not Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a separable space.

label: Countable Complement Space is not T2
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a $T_2$ space.

label: Countable Complement Space is not T3
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a $T_3$ space.

label: Countable Complement Space is not Weakly Countably Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not weakly countably compact.

label: Countable Complement Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement space. Then $\tau$ is a topology on $T$.

label: Countable Cover is Point Countable
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a countable cover of $S$. Then $\CC$ is a point countable cover of $S$.

label: Countable Discrete Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable discrete topological space. Then $T$ is a Lindelöf space.

label: Countable Discrete Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable discrete topological space. Then $T$ is second-countable.

label: Countable Discrete Space is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable discrete topological space. Then $T$ is separable.

label: Countable Discrete Space is Sigma-Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable discrete topological space. Then $T$ is $\sigma$-compact.

label: Countable Excluded Point Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar p} }$ be a countable excluded point space. Then $T$ is a second-countable space.

label: Countable Excluded Point Space is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar p} }$ be a countable excluded point space. Then $T$ is a separable space.

label: Countable Finite Complement Space is not Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable finite complement topology. Then $T$ is not path-connected.

label: Countable Fort Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fort space on a countably infinite set $S$. Then $T$ is a second-countable space.

label: Countable Fort Space is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fort space on a countably infinite set $S$. Then $T$ is a separable space.

label: Countable Function on Power Set of Sample Space is Discrete Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space such that $\Sigma$ is the power set of $\Omega$. Let $f: \Omega \to \R$ be a function such that $\Img f$ is countable. Then $f$ is a discrete random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$.

label: Countable Hypothesis Set has Finished Tableau
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\mathbf H$ be a countable set of WFFs of propositional logic. Then there exists a finished tableau whose root node is $\mathbf H$.

label: Countable Intersection of Events is Event
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an experiment with a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. The event space $\Sigma$ of $\EE$ has the property that: $\quad A_1, A_2, \ldots \in \Sigma \implies \ds \bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^\infty A_i \in \Sigma$ That is, the countable intersection of events is also an event.

label: Countable Local Basis in Compact Complement Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology on $\R$. Let $p \in \R$. Then sets of the form: $\openint \gets {-n} \cup \openint {p - \dfrac 1 n} {p + \dfrac 1 n} \cup \openint n \to$ form a countable local basis for $p$.

label: Countable Open Covers Condition for Separated Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ For all $X \subseteq S$, let $X^-$ denote the closure of $X$ in $T$. Let: $\UU = \set {U_n : n \in \N}$ be a countable open cover of $A : \forall n \in \N : {U_n}^- \cap B = \O$ Let: $\VV = \set {V_n : n \in \N}$ be a countable open cover of $B : \forall n \in \N : {V_n}^- \cap A = \O$ Then: $A$ and $B$ can be separated in $T$

label: Countable Open Ordinal Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $\Omega$ denote the first uncountable ordinal. Let $\Gamma$ be a limit ordinal which strictly precedes $\Omega$. Let $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ denote the open ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Then $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ is a second-countable space.

label: Countable Particular Point Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a countable particular point space. Then $T$ is a Lindelöf apace.

label: Countable Product of First-Countable Spaces is First-Countable
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with countable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be first-countable. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also first-countable.

label: Countable Product of Second-Countable Spaces is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with countable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be second-countable. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also second-countable.

label: Countable Product of Separable Spaces is Separable
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with countable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be separable. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also separable.

label: Countable Product of Sequentially Compact Spaces is Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with countable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be sequentially compact. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also sequentially compact.

label: Countable Set equals Range of Sequence
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then $S$ is countable there exists a sequence $\sequence {s_i}_{i \mathop \in N}$ where $N$ is a subset of $\N$ such that $S$ equals the range of $\sequence {s_i}_{i \mathop \in N}$.

label: Countable Set has Choice Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a countable set. Let $\mathbb S = \powerset S \setminus \set \O$ be the power set of $S$ excluding the empty set $\O$. Then there exists a choice function $C$ for $S$: $\forall x \in \mathbb S: \map C x \in x$

label: Countable Set has Measure Zero
snippet: Let $S$ be a countable set. Then the measure of $S$ is $\map m S = 0$.

label: Countable Set is Null Set under Lebesgue Measure
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \R$ be a countable set. Then $\map \lambda S = 0$, where $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure. That is, $S$ is a $\lambda$-null set.

label: Countable Set is Well-Orderable
snippet: Let $S$ be a countable set. Then $S$ is well-orderable.

label: Countable Set may have Uncountable Limit Points
snippet: Let $S$ be an uncountable set. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a countable subset of $S$. Let $T = \struct {H, \tau}$ be a topological space on the underlying set $H$. Then despite the fact that $H$ is countable, the set of limit points of $T$ may be uncountable.

label: Countable Space is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space where $S$ is a countable set. Then $T$ is a separable space.

label: Countable Stability implies Stability for All Infinite Cardinalities
snippet: Let $T$ be a complete $\LL$-theory whose language $\LL$ is countable. If $T$ is $\omega$-stable, then $T$ is $\kappa$-stable for all infinite $\kappa$.

label: Countable Subset of Minimal Uncountable Well-Ordered Set Has Upper Bound
snippet: Let $\Omega$ denote the minimal uncountable well-ordered set. Let $\omega$ be a countable subset of $\Omega$. Then $\omega$ has an upper bound in $\Omega$.

label: Countable Union of Countable Sets is Countable
snippet: Let the be accepted. Then it can be proved that a countable union of countable sets is countable.

label: Countable Union of Finite Sets is Countable
snippet: in $\mathrm{ZF}^-$: The holds. The union of any countable set of finite sets is countable. {{explain|What is $\mathrm{ZF}^-$? See talk page for a discussion on this.}}

label: Countable Union of Meager Sets is Meager
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\family {A_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a countable set of meager subsets of $X$. Let: $\ds A = \bigcup_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty A_n$ Then $A$ is meager in $X$.

label: Countable Union of Measurable Sets as Disjoint Union of Measurable Sets
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\sequence {A_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a sequence of $\Sigma$-measurable sets. Then there exists a sequence of $\Sigma$-measurable pairwise disjoint sets $\sequence {B_n}_{n \in \N}$ such that: $\ds \bigcup_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty A_n = \bigcup_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty B_n$ That is: any countable union of $\Sigma$-measurable sets can be rewritten as the countable union of pairwise disjoint $\Sigma$-measurable sets.

label: Countable iff Cardinality not greater than Aleph Zero
snippet: Let $X$ be set. $X$ is countable : $\card X \le \aleph_0$ where: $\card X$ denotes the cardinality of $X$ $\aleph_0 = \card \N$ by Aleph Zero equals Cardinality of Naturals.

label: Countably Additive Function Dichotomy by Empty Set
snippet: Let $\AA$ be a $\sigma$-algebra. Let $\overline \R$ denote the extended set of real numbers. Let $f: \AA \to \overline \R$ be a function be a countably additive function. Then the exactly one of the following is true: $\paren 1$: $\map f \O = 0$ $\paren 2$: $\map f \O = + \infty$. Moreover, $\map f A = + \infty$ for all $A \in \AA$. $\paren 3$: $\map f \O = - \infty$. Moreover, $\map f A = - \infty$ for all $A \in \AA$.

label: Countably Additive Function also Finitely Additive
snippet: Let $\AA$ be a $\sigma$-algebra. Let $\overline \R$ denote the extended set of real numbers. Let $f: \AA \to \overline \R$ be a countably additive function. Then $f$ is a finitely additive function.

label: Countably Additive Function of Null Set
snippet: Let $\AA$ be a $\sigma$-algebra. Let $\overline \R$ denote the extended set of real numbers. Let $f: \AA \to \overline \R$ be a function be a countably additive function. Suppose that there exists at least one $A \in \AA$ where $\map f A$ is a finite number. Then: $\map f \O = 0$

label: Countably Compact First-Countable Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: A countably compact first-countable topological space is also sequentially compact.

label: Countably Compact Lindelöf Space is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then: $T$ is a compact space $T$ is both: a Lindelöf space a countably compact space.

label: Countably Compact Metric Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a countably compact metric space. Then $\struct {X, d}$ is bounded.

label: Countably Compact Metric Space is Compact
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $M$ be countably compact. Then $M$ is compact.

label: Countably Compact Metric Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $M$ be a countably compact metric space. Then $M$ is second-countable.

label: Countably Compact Metric Space is Separable
snippet: Let $M$ be a countably compact metric space. Then $M$ is separable.

label: Countably Compact Metric Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $M$ be a countably compact metric space. Then $M$ is sequentially compact.

label: Countably Compact Second-Countable Space is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countably compact second-countable space. Then $T$ is compact.

label: Countably Compact Space is Countably Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countably compact space. Then $T$ is countably paracompact.

label: Countably Compact Space is Pseudocompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countably compact space. Then $T$ is a pseudocompact space.

label: Countably Compact Space is Weakly Countably Compact
snippet: Every countably compact space is a weakly countably compact space.

label: Countably Compact Space satisfies Countable Finite Intersection Axiom
Countably Infinite Set has Uncountable Family of Subsets with Finite Intersection
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a countably infinite set. Then there exists an uncountable family $\SS \subseteq \powerset \CC$ such that for each $A, B \in \SS$, we have that: $A \cap B$ is finite.

label: Countably Infinite Set in Countably Compact Space has Omega-Accumulation Point
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a countably compact topological space. Let $A \subseteq X$ be countably infinite. Then $A$ has an $\omega$-accumulation point in $X$.

label: Countably Metacompact Lindelöf Space is Metacompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Lindelöf space which is also countably metacompact. Then $T$ is metacompact.

label: Countably Paracompact Lindelöf Space is Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Lindelöf space which is also countably paracompact. Then $T$ is paracompact.

label: Counterexample/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Counterexamples ==

label: Counting Measure is Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Then the counting measure $\size {\,\cdot\,}$ on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ is a measure.

label: Counting Theorem
snippet: Every well-ordered set is order isomorphic to a unique ordinal.

label: Covariance as Expectation of Product minus Product of Expectations
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Let the expectations of $X$ and $Y$ exist and be finite. Then the covariance of $X$ and $Y$ is given by: $\cov {X, Y} = \expect {X Y} - \expect X \expect Y$

label: Covariance is Symmetric
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Suppose the covariance $\cov {X, Y}$ exists. Then $\cov {X, Y} = \cov {Y, X}$.

label: Covariance of Linear Combination of Random Variables with Another
snippet: Let $X, Y, Z$ be random variables. Let $a, b$ be real numbers. Then: $\cov {a X + b Y, Z} = a \cov {X, Z} + b \cov {Y, Z}$

label: Covariance of Multiples of Random Variables
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be random variables. Let $a, b$ be real numbers. Then: $\cov {a X, b Y} = a b \cov {X, Y}$

label: Covariance of Random Variable with Itself
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Then $\cov {X, X} = \var X$.

label: Covariance of Sums of Random Variables
snippet: Let $n$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $\sequence {X_i}_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop \le n}$, $\sequence {Y_j}_{1 \mathop \le j \mathop \le n}$ be sequences of random variables. Then: $\ds \cov {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n X_i, \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n Y_j} = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \cov {X_i, Y_j}$

label: Covariant Derivative of Smooth Vector Field along Smooth Vector Field in Smooth Local Frame
snippet:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with or without boundary. Let $TM$ be the tangent bundle of $M$. Let $
abla$ be a connection in $TM$. Let $U \subseteq M$ be an open subset. Suppose $	uple {E_i}$ is a smooth local frame over $U$. Let $\set {\Gamma^k_{ij}}$ be the connection coefficients of $
abla$ $	uple {E_i}$. Let $\map {\mathfrak X} U$ be the space of smooth vector fields on $U$. Let $X, Y \in \map {\mathfrak X} U$ be smooth vector fields. Suppose $X$ and $Y$ read as $X = X^i E_i$ and $Y = Y^i E_i$ $	uple {E_i}$. Then: $
abla_X Y = \paren {\map X {Y^k} + X^i Y^j \Gamma^k_{ij}} E_k$

label: Covariant Hom Functor is Continuous
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $\mathbf C$ be a locally small category. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$, and let $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {C, \cdot}: \mathbf C \to \mathbf{Set}$ be the covariant hom functor based at $C$. Then $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {C, \cdot}$ is a continuous functor.

label: Covariant Hom Functor is Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $\mathbf C$ be a locally small category. Let $C \in \mathbf C_0$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\operatorname{Hom}_\mathbf C \paren {C, \cdot}: \mathbf C \to \mathbf{Set}$ be the covariant hom functor based at $C$. Then $\operatorname{Hom}_\mathbf C \paren {C, \cdot}$ is a functor.

label: Covariant Tensor/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Covariant Tensors ==

label: Cover is Cover of Subset
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a cover of $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Then, $\CC$ is a cover of $T$.

label: Cover is Refinement of Itself
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a cover for $S$. Then $\CC$ is a refinement of $\CC$ itself.

label: Cover of Interval By Closed Intervals is not Pairwise Disjoint
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed interval in $\R$. Let $\JJ$ be a set of two or more closed intervals contained in $\closedint a b$ such that $\ds \bigcup \JJ = \closedint a b$. Then the intervals in $\JJ$ are not pairwise disjoint.

label: Covering Space/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Covering Spaces ==

label: Cowen's Theorem
snippet: Let $g$ be a progressing mapping. Let $x$ be a set. Let $\powerset x$ denote the power set of $x$. Let $M_x$ denote the intersection of the $x$-special subsets of $\powerset x$ $g$. Let $M$ be the class of all $x$ such that $x \in M_x$. Then $M$ is minimally superinductive under $g$.

label: Cowen-Engeler Lemma
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $M$ be a set of mappings from subsets of $X$ to $Y$. Thus each element of $M$ is a partial mapping from $X$ to $Y$. Define a mapping: $\Phi: X \to \powerset Y$ thus: $\map \Phi x = \set {\map f x: f \in M \text{ and } x \in \Dom f}$ That is: $\map \Phi x = \set {y \in Y: \exists f \in M: \tuple {x, y} \in f}$ Suppose that the following hold: Then there exists an element of $M$ with domain $X$.

label: Cramer's Rule
snippet: Let $n \in \N$. Let $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ be real numbers. Let $\mathbf b = \tuple {b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n}^\intercal$. Let $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ be real numbers. Let $\mathbf x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n}^\intercal$. Let $A$ be a nonsingular $n \times n$ matrix whose elements are in $\R$. For each $i \in \set {1, \dots, n}$, let $A_i$ be the matrix obtained by replacing the $i$th column with $\mathbf b$. Let: $A \mathbf x = \mathbf b$ Then: $\mathbf x_i = \dfrac {\map \det {A_i} } {\map \det A}$ for each $i \in \set {1, \dots, n}$.

label: Creation of Orthogonal Vector from Independent Vectors
snippet: Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector space. Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ be vectors of $\mathbf V$ such that $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ form a linearly independent set. Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ be expressed as column vectors. Let $\mathbf b'$ be calculated as: $\mathbf b' = \mathbf b - \dfrac {\mathbf a^\intercal \mathbf b} {\mathbf a^\intercal \mathbf a} \mathbf a$ where $\mathbf a^\intercal$ denotes the transpose of $\mathbf a$. Then $\mathbf b'$ is orthogonal to $\mathbf a$.

label: Criterion for Ring with Unity to be Topological Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity. Let $\tau$ be a topology over $R$. Suppose that $+$ and $\circ$ are $\tau$-continuous mappings. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ, \tau}$ is a topological ring.

label: Critical Line Theorem
snippet: There exist an infinite number of nontrivial zeroes of the Riemann $\zeta$ function on the critical line.

label: Cross-Relation is Congruence Relation
snippet: The cross-relation $\boxtimes$ is a congruence relation on $\struct {S_1 \times S_2, \oplus}$.

label: Cross-Relation is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Then $\boxtimes$ is an equivalence relation on $\struct {S_1 \times S_2, \oplus}$.

label: Cross-Relation on Natural Numbers is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {\N, +}$ be the semigroup of natural numbers under addition. Let $\struct {\N \times \N, \oplus}$ be the (external) direct product of $\struct {\N, +}$ with itself, where $\oplus$ is the operation on $\N \times \N$ induced by $+$ on $\N$. The relation $\boxtimes$ defined on $\N \times \N$ by: $\tuple {x_1, y_1} \boxtimes \tuple {x_2, y_2} \iff x_1 + y_2 = x_2 + y_1$ is an equivalence relation on $\struct {\N \times \N, \oplus}$.

label: Cross-Relation on Real Numbers is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $\R^2$ denote the cartesian plane. Let $\alpha$ denote the relation defined on $\R^2$ by: $\tuple {x_1, y_1} \mathrel \alpha \tuple {x_2, y_2} \iff x_1 + y_2 = x_2 + y_1$ Then $\alpha$ is an equivalence relation on $\R^2$.

label: Cross Product of Antiparallel Vectors is Zero
snippet: Let $\mathbf u$ and $\mathbf v$ be antiparallel vectors. Then: $\mathbf u \times \mathbf v = 0$ where $\times$ denotes vector cross product.

label: Cross Product of Vector with Itself is Zero
snippet: Let $\mathbf x$ be a vector in a vector space of $3$ dimensions: $\mathbf x = x_i \mathbf i + x_j \mathbf j + x_k \mathbf k$ Then: $\mathbf x \times \mathbf x = \mathbf 0$ where $\times$ denotes vector cross product.

label: Crossbar Theorem
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Let $D$ be a point in the interior of $\triangle ABC$. Then there exists a point $E$ such that $E$ lies on both $AD$ and $BC$.

label: Cube Function is Odd
snippet: The cube function on the real numbers: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = x^3$ is an odd function.

label: Cube Modulo 9
snippet: Let $x \in \Z$ be an integer. Then one of the following holds:

label: Cube Number as Sum of Three Consecutive Odd Squares
snippet: $1331 = 11^3 = 19^2 + 21^2 + 23^2$ No other such sequence of $3$ consecutive odd squares has the same property.

label: Cube Root/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cube Roots ==

label: Cube Root of 2 is Irrational
snippet: $\sqrt [3] 2$ is irrational.

label: Cube Root of Unity if Modulus is 1 and Real Part is Minus Half
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number such that: $\cmod z = 1$ $\Re \paren z = -\dfrac 1 2$ where: $\cmod z$ denotes the complex modulus of $z$ $\Re \paren z$ denotes the real part of $z$. Then: $z^3 = 1$

label: Cube of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z = a + i b$ be a complex number. Then its cube is given by: $z^3 = a^3 - 3 a b^2 + i \paren {3 a^2 b - b^3}$

label: Cube of Prime has 4 Positive Divisors
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer which is the cube of a prime number. Then $n$ has exactly $4$ positive divisors.

label: Cube of Prime is Multiplicatively Perfect
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer which is the cube of a prime number. Then $n$ is multiplicatively perfect.

label: Cube which is One Less than a Square
snippet: $8$ is the only cube number which is $1$ less than a square: $2^3 + 1 = 3^2$

label: Cubic Equation whose Roots are Squares of another Cubic Equation
snippet: Let: $(1): \quad a x^3 + b x^2 + c x + d = 0$ be a cubic equation in $x$. Let the roots of $(1)$ be $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$. Then the cubic equation in $y$ whose roots are $\alpha^2$, $\beta^2$ and $\gamma^2$ is: $a^2 y^3 + y^2 \paren {2 a c - b^2} + y \paren {c^2 - 2 b d} - d^2 = 0$

label: Cubic Equation whose Roots are of form r^2+r of another Cubic Equation
snippet: Let: $x^3 + 3 x - 1 = 0$ be a cubic equation in $x$. Let its roots be $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$. Then the cubic equation whose roots are $\alpha^2 + \alpha$, $\beta^2 + \beta$ and $\gamma^2 + \gamma$ is: $x^3 + 6 x^2 + 9 x - 5 = 0$

label: Cubic Equations with Reciprocal Roots
snippet: Let: $(1): \quad a x^3 + b x^2 + c x + d = 0$ be a cubic equation in $x$. Let the roots of $(1)$ be $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$. Then the cubic equation in $y$ whose roots are $\dfrac 1 \alpha$, $\dfrac 1 \beta$ and $\dfrac 1 \gamma$ is: $d y^3 + c y^2 + b y + a = 0$

label: Cubic Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: The only Fibonacci numbers which are also cubes are: $F_1 = 1 = 1^3$ $F_6 = 8 = 2^3 = 3 + 5$

label: Cubical Parabola has Point of Inflection
snippet: The cubical parabola has a point of inflection. When the equation for the cubical parabola is in the form $y = a x^3$, this point of inflection is the origin.

label: Cuboid with Integer Edges and Face Diagonals
snippet: The smallest cuboid whose edges and the diagonals of whose faces are all integers has edge lengths $44$, $117$ and $240$. Its space diagonal, however, is not an integer.

label: Cumulative Distribution Function as Integral of Probability Density Function
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an absolutely continuous random variable. Let $f_X$ be a probability density function for $X$. Let $F_X$ be the cumulative distribution function for $X$. Let $\map \BB \R$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $\R$. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$. Then: $\ds \map {F_X} x = \int_{-\infty}^x f_X \rd \lambda$ for each $x \in \R$, where $\ds \int_{-\infty}^x f_X \rd \lambda$ denotes the Lebesgue integral of $f$ over $\hointl {-\infty} x$.

label: Cumulative Distribution Function for Discrete Distribution
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a discrete random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Then the cumulative distribution function of $X$ is given by: $\map F x = \ds \sum_{x_i \mathop \le x} \map \Pr {X = x_i}$

label: Cumulative Distribution Function is Increasing
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $F_X$ be the cumulative distribution function. Then: $F_X$ is an increasing function.

label: Cumulative Distribution Function is Right-Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a real-valued random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $F_X$ be the cumulative distribution function of $X$. Then: $F_X$ is right-continuous.

label: Cumulative Distribution Function of Binomial Distribution
snippet: The cumulative distribution function of a binomially distributed random variable $X$ is equal to: $\map \Phi x = \ds \sum_{t \mathop \le x} \dbinom n t p^t \paren {1 - p}^{n - t}$ where: $n$ is the number of trials $p$ is the probability of success such that $0 \le p \le 1$.

label: Cumulative Distribution Function of Logistic Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with the logistic distribution. Then the cumulative distribution function of $X$ is: $\map {F_X} x = \dfrac 1 {1 + \map \exp {- \dfrac {x - \mu} s} }$

snippet: == Examples of Cumulative Rounding Error ==

label: Curl Operator/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Curl Operator ==

label: Curl Operator on Vector Space is Cross Product of Del Operator
snippet: Let $R$ be a region of Cartesian $3$-space $\R^3$. Let $\map {\mathbf V} {x, y, z}$ be a vector field acting over $R$. Then $\curl \mathbf V = \nabla \times \mathbf V$ where: $\curl \mathbf V $ denotes the curl of $\mathbf V$ $\nabla$ denotes the del operator.

label: Curl of Curl is Gradient of Divergence minus Laplacian
snippet: Let $\map {\R^3} {x, y, z}$ denote the real Cartesian space of $3$ dimensions. Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector field on $\R^3$. Then: $\curl \curl \mathbf V = \grad \operatorname {div} \mathbf V - \nabla^2 \mathbf V$ where: $\curl$ denotes the curl operator $\operatorname {div}$ denotes the divergence operator $\grad$ denotes the gradient operator $\nabla^2 \mathbf V$ denotes the Laplacian.

label: Curl of Gradient is Zero
snippet: Let $\map {\R^3} {x, y, z}$ denote the real Cartesian space of $3$ dimensions.. Let $\map U {x, y, z}$ be a scalar field on $\R^3$. Then: $\map \curl {\grad U} = \mathbf 0$ where: $\curl$ denotes the curl operator $\grad$ denotes the gradient operator.

label: Curl of Vector Field is Solenoidal
snippet: Let $\map {\R^3} {x, y, z}$ denote the real Cartesian space of $3$ dimensions. Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector field on $\R^3$: Then the curl of $\mathbf V$ is a solenoidal vector field.

label: Curry's Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == Let $P$ be an arbitrary proposition. Let a proposition $C$ be defined: $C \implies P$ that $\neg C$. Then $C \implies P$ is vacuously true. By definition, $C$ is true, a contradiction. This contradiction shows $C$ to be true. By definition, $C \implies P$. By Modus Ponendo Ponens, we conclude $P$, where $P$ is arbitrary. But this means that any proof system expressing the above is inconsistent.

label: Curve/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Curves ==

label: Curve is Involute of Evolute
snippet: Let $C$ be a curve defined by a real function which is twice differentiable. Let the curvature of $C$ be non-constant. Let $E$ be the evolute $C$. Then the involute of $E$ is $C$.

label: Curved Mirror producing Parallel Rays is Paraboloid
snippet: Let $M$ be a curved mirror embedded in a real cartesian $3$- space. Let there be a source of light at the origin. Let $M$ reflect the light in a beam parallel to the $x$-axis. Then $M$ is the solid of revolution produced by rotating about the $x$-axis the parabola whose equation is: $y^2 = 2 c x + c^2$

label: Cut-Off Subtraction is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The partial subtraction function, defined as: $\forall \tuple {n, m} \in \N^2: n \mathop {\dot -} m = \begin{cases} 0 & : n is primitive recursive‎.

label: Cut Associated with 1 is Identity for Multiplication of Cuts
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. Let $1^*$ denote the rational cut (rational) number $1$. Then: $\alpha 1^* = \alpha$ where $\alpha 1^*$ denote the product of $\alpha$ and $1^*$.

snippet: == Examples of Cycles in context of Graph Theory ==

snippet: == Examples of Cycle Decompositions ==

label: Cycle Graph is Bipartite iff Order is Even
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $C_n$ be the cycle graph of order $n$. Then $C_n$ is a bipartite graph $n$ is even.

label: Cycle Graph is Hamiltonian
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n \ge 3$. Let $C_n$ denote the cycle graph of order $n$. Then $C_n$ is Hamiltonian.

label: Cycle does not Contain Subcycles
snippet: Let $G$ be a cycle graph. Then the only cycle graph that is a subgraph of $G$ is $G$ itself.

label: Cycle of Subsets implies Set Equality
snippet: Let $A_1, A_2, \dotsc, A_n$ be sets. Let: $\forall k \in \set {2, 3, \dotsc, n}: A_{k - 1} \subseteq A_k$ and: $A_n \subseteq A_1$ Then: $\forall j, k \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, n}: A_j = A_k$

label: Cyclic Group/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cyclic Groups ==

label: Cyclic Group/Group Presentation
snippet: == Generator of the Cyclic Group of Order $n$ == The presentation of a finite cyclic group of order $n$ is: $C_n = \gen {a: a^n = e}$

label: Cyclic Group Elements whose Powers equal Identity
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group whose identity is $e$ and whose order is $n$. Let $d \divides n$. Then there exist exactly $d$ elements $x \in G$ satisfying the equation $x^d = e$. These are the elements of the group $G_d$ generated by $g^{n / d}$: $G_d = \gen {g^{n / d} }$

label: Cyclic Group is Abelian
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group. Then $G$ is abelian.

label: Cyclic Group is Finitely Generated
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a cyclic group. Then $\CC$ is finitely generated.

label: Cyclic Group is Simple iff Prime
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group. Then $G$ is simple $G$ is a prime group.

label: Cyclic Group of Order 6
snippet: Let $C_n$ be the cyclic group of order $n$. Then: $C_2 \times C_3 \cong C_6$ $C_6$ is the internal group direct product of $C_2$ and $C_3$.

label: Cyclic Group of Order 8 is not isomorphic to Group of Units of Integers Modulo n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be an integer. Let $\struct {\Z / n \Z, +, \cdot}$ be the ring of integers modulo $n$. Let $U = \struct {\paren {\Z / n \Z}^\times, \cdot}$ denote the group of units of $\struct {\Z / n \Z, +, \cdot}$. Let $C_8$ denote the cyclic group of order $8$ Then: $U$ and $C_8$ are not isomorphic.

label: Cyclic Groups of Same Order are Isomorphic
snippet: Two cyclic groups of the same order are isomorphic to each other.

label: Cyclic Permutation of Kaprekar Number
snippet: Let $n$ be a Kaprekar number of $k$ digits. Let $m$ be an integer formed from a cyclic permutation of the digits of $n$. Let $m$ be squared and the result split into $2$ parts, where the $2$nd part is of $k$ digits. Let these two parts be added, in the way of operating on a Kaprekar number. If the result is more than $k$ digits long, split that into $2$ parts, where the $2$nd part is of $k$ digits, and add the parts. The result will be another cyclic permutation of the digits of $n$.

label: Cyclic Permutations of 5-Digit Multiples of 41
snippet: Let $n$ be a multiple of $41$ with $5$ digits. Let $m$ be an integer formed by cyclically permuting the digits of $n$. Then $m$ is a multiple of $41$.

label: Cyclicity Condition for Units of Ring of Integers Modulo n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $\struct {\Z / n \Z, +, \times}$ be the ring of integers modulo $n$. Let $U = \struct {\paren {\Z / n \Z}^\times, \times}$ denote the group of units of $\struct {\Z / n \Z, +, \times}$. Then $U$ is cyclic either: $n = p^\alpha$ or: $n = 2 p^\alpha$ where $p \ge 3$ is prime and $\alpha \ge 0$.

label: Cycloid has Tautochrone Property
snippet: Let a wire $AB$ be curved into the shape of an arc of a cycloid such that: $A$ is at the cusp $B$ is the highest point of the arc and inverted so that its cusps are uppermost and on the same horizontal line. Thus $B$ is the lowest point of the arc. Let $AB$ be embedded in a constant and uniform gravitational field where Acceleration Due to Gravity is $g$. Let a bead $P$ be released from anywhere on the wire between $A$ and $B$ to slide down without friction to $B$.

label: Cyclotomic Polynomial has Integer Coefficients
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer. Then the $n$th cyclotomic polynomial $\map {\Phi_n} x$ has integer coefficients.

label: Cyclotomic Polynomial of Index times Prime Power
snippet: Let $n, k \ge 1$ be natural numbers. Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\Phi_n$ denote the $n$th cyclotomic polynomial. Then $\map {\Phi_{p^k n}} x = \begin{cases} \map {\Phi_n} {x^{p^k}} & \text{if } p \divides n\\ \dfrac {\map {\Phi_n} {x^{p^k}}} {\map {\Phi_n} {x^{p^{k - 1}}}} & \text{if } p \nmid n \end{cases}$

label: Cyclotomic Polynomial of Prime Index
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. The $p$th cyclotomic polynomial is: $\map {\Phi_p} x = x^{p - 1} + x^{p - 2} + \cdots + x + 1$

snippet: Let $t$ be time. Let $x$ be position. Let $\tuple {t, x} \stackrel u {\longrightarrow} \map u {t, x}: \R^2 \to \R$ be a twice-differentiable function in both variables. snippet: Let $F_k$ be the $k$th Fibonacci number. Then: $\forall m, n \in \Z: \paren {-1}^n F_{m - n} = F_m F_{n + 1} - F_n F_{n - 1}$

label: Dandelin's Theorem
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a double napped right circular cone with apex $O$. Let $\EE$ be the conic section arising as the intersection between $\PP$ and $\CC$. Let $\SS$ and $\SS'$ be the Dandelin spheres with respect to $\PP$.

label: Darboux's Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is bounded on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Then: $\ds m \paren {b - a} \le \underline {\int_a^b} \map f x \rd x \le \overline {\int_a^b} \map f x \rd x \le M \paren {b - a}$ where: $M$ is an upper bound of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ $m$ is a lower bound of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ $\ds \overline {\int_a^b} \map f x \rd x$ denotes the upper Darboux integral of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ $\ds \underline {\int_a^b} \map f x \rd x$ denotes the lower Darboux integral of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ If $f$ is Darboux integrable on $\closedint a b$, then in fact: $\ds m…

label: De Polignac's False Conjecture
snippet: == Famous False Conjecture == Every odd number greater than $1$ can be expressed as the sum of a power of $2$ and a prime.

label: De Polignac's Formula
snippet: Let $n!$ be the factorial of $n$. Let $p$ be a prime number. Then $p^\mu$ is a divisor of $n!$, and $p^{\mu + 1}$ is not, where: $\ds \mu = \sum_{k \mathop > 0} \floor {\frac n {p^k} }$ where $\floor {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the floor function.

label: Decimal Expansion of Fourth Power of Pi
snippet: The decimal expansion of the $4$th power of $\pi$ begins: $97 \cdotp 40909 \, 10340 \, 0 \ldots$

label: Decimal Expansion of Number is Terminating or Periodic iff Rational
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Then: the decimal expansion of $x$ is either terminating or recurring $x$ is a rational number.

label: Deck of 52 Cards returns to Original Order after 52 Modified Perfect Faro Shuffles
snippet: Let $D$ be a deck of $52$ cards. Let $D$ be given a sequence of modified perfect faro shuffles. Then after $52$ such shuffles, the cards of $D$ will be in the same order they started in.

label: Decomposition into Product of Power of 2 and Odd Integer is Unique
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then $n$ can be decomposed into the product of a power of $2$ and an odd integer.

label: Decomposition of 2-Form on 4-Dimensional Riemannian Manifold
snippet: Let $M$ be a $4$-dimensional oriented Riemannian manifold. Let $\omega$ be a $2$-form on $M$. Then $\omega$ can be written uniquely as a sum of a self-dual $2$-form and an anti-self-dual $2$-form.

label: Decomposition of Complex Measure into Finite Signed Measures
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a complex measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Then there exists unique finite signed measures $\mu_R$ and $\mu_I$ such that: $\mu = \mu_R + i \mu_I$

label: Decomposition of Matrix Exponential
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix of order $m$ for some $m \in \Z_{\ge 1}$. Let $t \in \R$ be a real number. Let $e^{\mathbf A t}$ denote the matrix exponential of $\mathbf A$. Let $\mathbf P$ be a nonsingular matrix of order $m$. Then: $e^{\mathbf P \mathbf A \mathbf P^{-1} t} = \mathbf P e^{\mathbf A t} \mathbf P^{-1}$ {{explain|Review what is meant by $e^{\mathbf A}$. We have only got $e^{\mathbf A t}$ defined.}}

label: Decomposition of Probability Measures
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, P}$ be a probability space. Suppose that for every $\omega \in \Omega$, it holds that: $\set \omega \in \Sigma$ that is, that $\Sigma$ contains all singletons. Then there exist a unique diffuse measure $\mu$ and a unique discrete measure $\nu$ such that: $P = \mu + \nu$

label: Dedekind's Theorem
snippet: Let $\tuple {L, R}$ be a Dedekind cut of the set of real numbers $\R$. Then there exists a unique real number which is a producer of $\tuple {L, R}$. Thus it is proved that the totally ordered set $\R$ is Dedekind complete, and that is why it is referred to as the continuum.

label: Dedekind-Complete Bounded Ordered Set is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {L, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $L$ have a lower bound $\bot$ and an upper bound $\top$. Let $\struct {L, \preceq}$ be Dedekind-complete. Then $\struct {L, \preceq}$ is a complete lattice.

label: Dedekind Completeness is Self-Dual
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is Dedekind complete every non-empty subset of $S$ that is bounded below admits an infimum in $S$. That is, an ordered set is Dedekind complete its dual is Dedekind complete.

label: Deduction Theorem
snippet: Let $\mathscr H$ be instance 1 of a Hilbert proof system. Then the deduction rule: $\dfrac{U,\mathbf A \vdash \mathbf B}{U \vdash \mathbf A \implies \mathbf B}$ is a derived rule for $\mathscr H$.

label: Deficient Number/Sequence
snippet: == Sequence of Deficient Numbers == The sequence of deficient numbers begins: $2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 21, \ldots$

label: Defining Sequence of Natural Logarithm is Convergent
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 0$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be the sequence of mappings $f_n : \R_{>0} \to \R$ defined as: $\map {f_n} x = n \paren {\sqrt[n] x - 1}$ Then $\sequence {f_n}$ is pointwise convergent.

label: Defining Sequence of Natural Logarithm is Strictly Decreasing
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 0$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be the sequence of mappings $f_n : \R_{>0} \to \R$ defined as: $\map {f_n} x = n \paren {\sqrt [n] x - 1}$ Then $\forall x \in \R_{>0}: \sequence {\map {f_n} x}$ is strictly decreasing.

label: Defining Sequence of Natural Logarithm is Uniformly Convergent on Compact Sets
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 0$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be the sequence of mappings $f_n : \R_{>0} \to \R$ defined as: $\map {f_n} x = n \paren {\sqrt [n] x - 1}$ Let $K \subseteq \R_{>0}$ be compact. Then $\sequence {f_n}$ is uniformly convergent on $K$.

label: Definite Integral from -a to a of Power of a plus x by Power of a minus x
snippet: $\ds \int_{-a}^a \paren {a + x}^{m - 1} \paren {a - x}^{n - 1} \rd x = \paren {2 a}^{m + n - 1} \frac {\map \Gamma m \map \Gamma n} {\map \Gamma {m + n} }$ where: $\Gamma$ denotes the Gamma function $a$, $m$ and $n$ are positive real numbers.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Arcsine of x by Arccosine of x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \frac {\arcsin x \arccos x } x \rd x = \dfrac 7 8 \map \zeta 3$ where $\map \zeta 3$ is Apéry's constant: the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $3$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Difference of Powers of x over Logarithm of x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \frac {x^m - x^n} {\ln x} \rd x = \map \ln {\frac {m + 1} {n + 1} }$ where $m$ and $n$ are real numbers with $m, n > -1$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Even Powers of Logarithm of 1 - x over x
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. $\ds \int_0^1 \map {\ln^{2n} } {\dfrac {1 - x} x} \rd x = \paren {-1}^{n + 1} B_{2 n} \paren {2^{2 n} - 2} \pi^{2 n}$ where $B_{2 n}$ is the $2 n$th Bernoulli number.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Logarithm of One minus x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \frac {\map \ln {1 - x} } x \rd x = -\frac {\pi^2} 6$

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Logarithm of x by Logarithm of One minus x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \ln x \map \ln {1 - x} \rd x = 2 - \frac {\pi^2} 6$

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Logarithm of x by Logarithm of One minus x over One minus x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \dfrac {\ln x \map \ln {1 - x} } {\paren {1 - x} } \rd x = \map \zeta 3$ where $\map \zeta 3$ is Apéry's constant: the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $3$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Logarithm of x over One minus x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \frac {\ln x} {1 - x} \rd x = -\frac {\pi^2} 6$

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Power of x by Power of Logarithm of x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 x^m \paren {\ln x}^n \rd x = \frac {\paren {-1}^n \map \Gamma {n + 1} } {\paren {m + 1}^{n + 1} }$ where: $n$ is a non-negative integer $m$ is a real number with $m > -1$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Zeta of 2 minus Dilogarithm of x over One minus x
snippet: $\ds \int_{\to 0}^{\to 1} \dfrac {\paren {\map \zeta 2 - \map {\Li_2} x } } {1 - x} \rd x = 2 \map \zeta 3$ where: $\map {\Li_2} x$ is the Dilogarithm function of $x$ $\map \zeta 2$ is the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $2$ $\map \zeta 3$ is Apéry's constant: the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $3$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 2 Pi of Logarithm of a plus b Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{2 \pi} \map \ln {a + b \cos x} \rd x = 2 \pi \map \ln {\frac {a + \sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } 2}$ where: $b$ is a real number $a$ is a positive real number with $a \ge \size b$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 2 Pi of Reciprocal of One minus 2 a Cosine x plus a Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{2 \pi} \frac {\d x} {1 - 2 a \cos x + a^2} = \frac {2 \pi} {1 - a^2}$ where $a$ is a real number with $0 < a < 1$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 2 Pi of Reciprocal of Square of a plus b Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{2 \pi} \frac {\d x} {\paren {a + b \cos x}^2} = \frac {2 \pi a} {\paren {a^2 - b^2}^{3/2} }$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > b > 0$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 2 Pi of Reciprocal of Square of a plus b Sine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{2 \pi} \frac {\d x} {\paren {a + b \sin x}^2} = \frac {2 \pi a} {\paren {a^2 - b^2}^{3/2} }$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > b > 0$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to 2 Pi of Reciprocal of a plus b Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{2 \pi} \frac {\d x} {a + b \cos x} = \frac {2 \pi} {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} }$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > b > 0$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Reciprocal of One plus Power of Tan x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac {\d x} {1 + \tan^m x} = \frac \pi 4$ where $m$ is a real number.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Reciprocal of a plus b Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac 1 {a + b \cos x} \rd x = \frac 1 {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } \map \arccos {\frac b a}$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > b > 0$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Square of Logarithm of Sine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \paren {\map \ln {\sin x} }^2 \rd x = \frac \pi 2 \paren {\ln 2}^2 + \frac {\pi^3} {24}$

label: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of Cosine of m x by Cosine of n x
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Then: $\ds \int_0^\pi \cos m x \cos n x \rd x = \begin {cases} 0 & : m \ne n \\ \dfrac \pi 2 & : m = n \end {cases}$ That is: $\ds \int_0^\pi \cos m x \cos n x \rd x = \dfrac \pi 2 \delta_{m n}$ where $\delta_{m n}$ is the Kronecker delta.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of Logarithm of a plus b Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\pi \map \ln {a + b \cos x} \rd x = \pi \map \ln {\frac {a + \sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } 2}$ where: $b$ is a real number $a$ is a positive real number with $a \ge \size b$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of Sec x by Logarithm of One plus b Cosine x over One plus a Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \sec x \map \ln {\frac {1 + b \cos x} {1 + a \cos x} } \rd x = \frac 1 2 \paren {\paren {\arccos a}^2 - \paren {\arccos b}^2}$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $-1 < a, b < 1$.

label: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of Sine of m x by Cosine of n x
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Then: $\ds \int_0^\pi \sin m x \cos n x \rd x = \begin{cases} 0 & : m + n \text { even} \\ \dfrac {2 m} {m^2 - n^2} & : m + n \text { odd} \end{cases}$

label: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of Sine of m x by Sine of n x
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Then: $\ds \int_0^\pi \sin m x \sin n x \rd x = \begin{cases} 0 & : m \ne n \\ \dfrac \pi 2 & : m = n \end{cases}$ That is: $\ds \int_0^\pi \sin m x \sin n x \rd x = \dfrac \pi 2 \delta_{m n}$ where $\delta_{m n}$ is the Kronecker delta.

label: Definite Integral of Constant Multiple of Real Function
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is integrable on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $c \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $\ds \int_a^b c \map f x \rd x = c \int_a^b \map f x \rd x$

label: Definite Integral of Even Function
snippet: Let $f$ be an even function with a primitive on the closedinterval $\closedint {-a} a$, where $a > 0$. Then: $\ds \int_{-a}^a \map f x \rd x = 2 \int_0^a \map f x \rd x$

label: Definite Integral of Function plus Constant
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $c$ be a constant. Then: $\ds \int_a^b \paren {\map f t + c} \rd t = \int_a^b \map f t \rd t + c \paren {b - a}$

label: Definite Integral of Limit of Uniformly Convergent Sequence of Integrable Functions
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ with $a < b$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of Riemann integrable real functions $\closedint a b \to \R$ converging uniformly to $f : \closedint a b \to \R$. Then $f$ is integrable, and: $\ds \int_a^b \map f x \rd x = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int_a^b \map {f_n} x \rd x$

label: Definite Integral of Partial Derivative
snippet: Let $\map f {x, y}$ and $\map {\dfrac {\partial f} {\partial x} } {x, y}$ be continuous functions of $x$ and $y$ on $D = \closedint {x_1} {x_2} \times \closedint a b$. Then: $\ds \frac \d {\d x} \int_a^b \map f {x, y} \rd y = \int_a^b \map {\frac {\partial f} {\partial x} } {x, y} \rd y$ for $x \in \closedint {x_1} {x_2}$.

label: Definite Integral of Step Function
snippet: Let $\alpha, \beta \in \R$ be a real numbers such that $\alpha < \beta$. Let $\map f x$ be a step function defined on the interval $\closedint \alpha \beta$: $\map f x = \lambda_1 \chi_{\mathbb I_1} + \lambda_2 \chi_{\mathbb I_2} + \cdots + \lambda_n \chi_{\mathbb I_n}$ where: $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \ldots, \lambda_n$ are real constants $\mathbb I_1, \mathbb I_2, \ldots, \mathbb I_n$ are intervals, where these intervals partition $\closedint \alpha \beta$ $\chi_{\mathbb I_1}, \chi_{\mathbb I_2}, \ldots, \chi_{\mathbb I_n}$ are characteristic functions of $\mathbb I_1, \mathbb I_2, \ldots,…

label: Definite Integral of Uniformly Convergent Series of Continuous Functions
snippet: Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions. Let each of $\sequence {f_n}$ be continuous on the interval $\hointr a b$. Let the series: $\ds \map f x := \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map {f_n} x$ be uniformly convergent for all $x \in \closedint a b$. Then: $\ds \int_a^b \map f x \rd x = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \int_a^b \map {f_n} x \rd x$

label: Definite Integral on Zero Interval
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is defined on the closed interval $\Bbb I := \closedint a b$, where $a < b$. Then: $\ds \forall c \in \Bbb I: \int_c^c \map f t \rd t = 0$

label: Definite Integral over Reals of Exponential of -(a x^2 plus b x plus c)
snippet: $\ds \int_{-\infty}^\infty \map \exp {-\paren {a x^2 + b x + c} } \rd x = \sqrt {\frac \pi a} \map \exp {\frac {b^2 - 4 a c} {4 a} }$ where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are real numbers with $a > 0$.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Arctangent of p x minus Arctangent of q x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\arctan p x - \arctan q x} x \rd x = \frac \pi 2 \ln \frac p q$ where $p$ and $q$ are strictly positive real numbers.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Cosine m x over x Squared plus a Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\cos m x} {x^2 + a^2} \rd x = \frac \pi {2 a} e^{-m a}$ where $m$ and $a$ are positive real numbers.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Cosine of a x^2
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \cos {a x^2} \rd x = \frac 1 2 \sqrt {\frac \pi {2 a} }$ where $a$ is a positive real number.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Cosine p x minus Cosine q x over x Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\cos p x - \cos q x} {x^2} \rd x = \frac {\pi \paren {\size q - \size p} } 2$ where $p, q$ are real numbers.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Cube of Sine x over x Cubed
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin^3 x} {x^3} \rd x = \frac {3 \pi} 8$

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -(a x^2 plus b x plus c)
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \exp {-\paren {a x^2 + b x + c} } \rd x = \frac 1 2 \sqrt {\frac \pi a} \map \exp {\frac {b^2 - 4 a c} {4 a} } \map \erfc {\frac b {2 \sqrt a} }$ where: $\erfc$ denotes the complementary error function $a$, $b$ and $c$ are real numbers with $a > 0$.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x by Cosine of b x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty e^{-a x} \cos b x \rd x = \frac a {a^2 + b^2}$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > 0$.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x by One minus Cosine x over x Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {e^{-a x} \paren {1 - \cos x} } {x^2} \rd x = \arccot a - \frac a 2 \map \ln {a^2 + 1} + a \ln a$ where $a$ is a positive real number.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x by Sine of b x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty e^{-a x} \sin b x \rd x = \frac b {a^2 + b^2}$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > 0$.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x by Sine of b x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {e^{-a x} \sin b x} x \rd x = \map \arctan {\frac b a}$ where $a$ and $b$ are real number with $a > 0$.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x minus Exponential of -b x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {e^{-a x} - e^{-b x} } x \rd x = \ln \frac b a$ where $a$ and $b$ are strictly positive real numbers.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x minus Exponential of -b x over x by Cosecant of p x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {e^{-a x} - e^{-b x} } {x \csc p x} \rd x = \arctan \frac b p - \arctan \frac a p$ where: $a$ and $b$ are non-negative real numbers $p$ is a non-zero real number.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x minus Exponential of -b x over x by Secant of p x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {e^{-a x} - e^{-b x} } {x \sec p x} \rd x = \frac 1 2 \map \ln {\frac {b^2 + p^2} {a^2 + p^2} }$ where: $a$ and $b$ are non-negative real numbers $p$ is a real number.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -i x^2
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \exp {-i x^2} \rd x = \frac 1 2 \sqrt {\frac \pi 2} \paren {1 - i}$

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -x^2 by Logarithm of x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty e^{-x^2} \ln x \rd x = -\frac {\sqrt \pi} 4 \paren {\gamma + 2 \ln 2}$ where $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -x by Logarithm of x
snippet: Let $\ln t$ denote the natural logarithm function for real $t > 0$. Let $e^{-t}$ denote the real exponential. Then: $\ds \int_{0^+}^{\mathop \to +\infty} \ln t \, e^{-t} \rd t = - \gamma$ where the is an improper integral, and $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni Constant.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Hyperbolic Sine of a x over Exponential of b x minus One
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sinh a x} {e^{b x} - 1} \rd x = \frac 1 {2 a} - \frac \pi {2 b} \cot \frac {a \pi} b$ where: $a$ and $b$ are positive real numbers with $b > a$ $\cot$ denotes the cotangent function.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Power of x by Exponential of -a x^2
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty x^m e^{-a x^2} \rd x = \frac {\map \Gamma {\paren {m + 1}/2} } {2 a^{\paren {m + 1}/2} }$ where $m$ and $a$ are real numbers with $m > -1$ and $a > 0$.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Power of x by Logarithm of x over One plus x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {x^{p - 1} \ln x} {1 + x} \rd x = -\pi^2 \csc p \pi \cot p \pi$ where: $p$ is a real number with $0 < p < 1$ $\csc$ denotes the cosecant function $\cot$ denotes the cotangent function.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Power of x over Hyperbolic Sine of a x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {x^n} {\sinh a x} \rd x = \frac {2^{n + 1} - 1} {2^n a^{n + 1} } \map \Gamma {n + 1} \map \zeta {n + 1}$ where: $a$ and $n$ are positive real numbers $\Gamma$ denotes the gamma function $\zeta$ denotes the Riemann zeta function.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Reciprocal of 1 plus Power of x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac 1 {1 + x^n} \rd x = \frac \pi n \map \csc {\frac \pi n}$ where: $n$ is a real number greater than 1 $\csc$ is the cosecant function.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Reciprocal of Exponential of x minus One minus Exponential of -x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \paren {\frac 1 {e^x - 1} - \frac {e^{-x} } x} \rd x = \gamma$ where $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Reciprocal of x Squared plus a Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \dfrac {\d x} {x^2 + a^2} = \frac \pi {2 a}$ for $a \ne 0$.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Sine m x over x by x Squared plus a Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin m x} {x \paren {x^2 + a^2} } \rd x = \frac \pi {2 a^2} \paren {1 - e^{-m a} }$ where: $a$ is a positive real number $m$ is a non-negative real number.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Sine of a x^2
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \sin {a x^2} \rd x = \frac 1 2 \sqrt {\frac \pi {2 a} }$ where $a$ is a positive real number.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of Sine of m x over Exponential of 2 Pi x minus One
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin m x} {e^{2 \pi x} - 1} \rd x = \frac 1 4 \coth \frac m 2 - \frac 1 {2 m}$ where: $m$ is a non-zero real number $\coth$ is the hyperbolic cotangent function.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of x by Sine m x over x Squared plus a Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {x \sin m x} {x^2 + a^2} \rd x = \frac \pi 2 e^{-m a}$ where $m$ and $a$ are positive real numbers.

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of x over Exponential of x minus One
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac x {e^x - 1} \rd x = \frac {\pi^2} 6$

label: Definite Integral to Infinity of x over Hyperbolic Sine of a x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac x {\sinh a x} \rd x = \frac {\pi^2} {4 a^2}$ where $a$ is a positive real number.

label: Definition:AKS Primality Test
snippet: The AKS primality test is an algorithm that runs in polynomial time that can decide whether a given natural number is prime or not.

snippet: A posteriori knowledge is the sort of knowledge which cannot be known without experience. That is, it cannot be determined by using logic and reasoning from definitions alone.

label: Definition:Abacism
snippet: Abacism means the process of doing arithmetic using an abacus.

label: Definition:Abacism/Abacist
snippet: An abacist is an arithmetician who uses an abacus to do arithmetic, as opposed to an algorist who calculates using algorism.

label: Definition:Abacus
snippet: An abacus is a tool for performing arithmetical calculations. It consists of: a series of lines (for example: grooves in sand, or wires on a frame), upon which are: a number of items (for example: pebbles in the grooves, or beads on the wires), which are manipulated by hand so as to represent number.

label: Definition:Abacus/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on the Abacus == The abacus is the earliest known machine for mathematics, and can be regarded as the earliest ancestor of the electronic computer. Category:Historical Notes

label: Definition:Abacus/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Abacus == The form of abacus is properly abaci, but abacuses is mainstream and usual. Category:Linguistic Notes

label: Definition:Abbreviation of WFF of Propositional Logic
snippet: The WFFs of propositional logic can be made more readable by allowing them to be abbreviated. The resulting strings are not actually WFFs as such, but can be translated back uniquely into full WFFs.

label: Definition:Abbreviation of WFF of Propositional Logic/Justification
snippet: == Justification for Abbreviation of WFFs == The abbreviation of WFFs of propositional logic stems from their semantics. It is only because we "know how binary connectives work" that we are able to allow these abbreviation rules to be defined. In particular, note that the ability to remove brackets from around repeated $\land$ and $\lor$ connectives stems from the Rule of Association which (at the stage of construction of the formal system that is PropLog) has not even been suggested, let alone proved.

label: Definition:Abel's Integral Equation
snippet: Abel's integral equation is an integral equation whose purpose is to solve Abel's mechanical problem, which finds how long it will take a bead to slide down a wire. The purpose of Abel's integral equation is to find the shape of the curve into which the wire is bent in order to yield that result: Let $\map T y$ be a function which specifies the total time of descent for a given starting height.

label: Definition:Abel Summation Method
snippet: The series: $\ds \sum a_n$ can be summed by the Abel method ($A$-method) to the number $S$ if, for any real $x$ such that $0 < x < 1$, the series: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty a_k x^k$ is convergent and: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 1^-} \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty a_k x^k = S$ $\ds \map f x = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a_n e^{-n x} = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a_n z^n$ where $z = \map \exp {−x}$. Then the limit of $\map f x$ as $x$ approaches $0$ through positive reals is the limit of the power series for $\map f z$ as $z$ approaches $1$ from below through positive reals.

label: Definition:Abelian Category/Definition 1
snippet: An abelian category is a pre-abelian category in which: every monomorphism is a kernel every epimorphism is a cokernel

label: Definition:Abelian Category/Definition 2
snippet: An abelian category is a pre-abelian category in which: every monomorphism is the kernel of its cokernel every epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel

label: Definition:Abelian Category/Definition 3
snippet: An abelian category is a pre-abelian category in which for every morphism $f$, the canonical morphism from its coimage to its image $\map {\operatorname {coim} } f \to \Img f$ is an isomorphism.

label: Definition:Abelian Function/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Abelian Function == The foundations for the theory of Abelian functions were laid in 's paper . studied Abelian functions by applying Dirichlet's Principle for Harmonic Functions combined with geometric reasoning. The work on extending our understanding of them continued with , working alone with no contact with other mathematicians. He took up their study as his life's work.

label: Definition:Abelian Group/Also known as
snippet: The usual way of spelling abelian group is without a capital letter, but Abelian is frequently seen. The term commutative group can occasionally be seen.

label: Definition:Abelian Group/Definition 1
snippet: An abelian group is a group $G$ where: $\forall a, b \in G: a b = b a$ That is, every element in $G$ commutes with every other element in $G$.

label: Definition:Abelian Group/Definition 2
snippet: An abelian group is a group $G$ : $G = \map Z G$ where $\map Z G$ is the center of $G$.

label: Definition:Abelian Group/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Abelian Group == The importance of abelian groups was discovered by during the course of his investigations into the theory of equations.

label: Definition:Abelian Group/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Abelian Group == The pronunciation of abelian in the term abelian group is usually either a-bee-lee-an or a-bell-ee-an, putting the emphasis on the second syllable. Note that the term abelian has thus phonetically lost the connection to its eponym (correctly pronounced aah-bl). Category:Linguistic Notes

label: Definition:Abnormal Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is an abnormal subgroup : $\forall g \in G: g \in \gen {H, H^g}$ where $\gen {H, H^g}$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by $H$ and the conjugate of $H$ by $g$.

label: Definition:Abohm
snippet: The abohm is the CGS unrationalised electromagnetic unit of electrical resistance. It is defined as being the electrical resistance between two points of an electrical conductor when a constant electric potential of $1$ abvolt, applied to these points, produces in the conductor an electric current of $1$ abampere, the conductor not being the seat of any electromotive force.

label: Definition:Above
snippet: Numbers: Number $a$ is above number $b$ $a$ is greater than $b$. Solid Geometry: Point $a$ is above point $b$ the height of $a$ a given frame of reference $R$ is greater than the height of $b$ $R$. Plane Geometry: Point $a$ is above point $b$ the $y$ coordinate of $a$ is greater than the $y$ coordinate of $b$.

label: Definition:Above (Number)
snippet: In the context of numbers, above means greater than. Note that this applies to: the natural numbers $\N$ the integers $\Z$ the rational numbers $\Q$ the real numbers $\R$ but specifically not the complex numbers $\C$ because the complex numbers do not have a usual ordering.

label: Definition:Above (Plane Geometry)
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be points in the cartesian plane $\R^2$. Then: $a$ is above $b$ the $y$ coordinate of $a$ is greater than the $y$ coordinate of $b$.

label: Definition:Above (Solid Geometry)
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be points in $3$-dimensional Euclidean space $\R^3$. Let $P$ be an arbitrary plane embedded in $S$ be distinguished and defined as horizontal. Then: $a$ is above $b$ the height of $a$ $P$ is greater than the height of $b$ $P$.

label: Definition:Abridged Multiplication
snippet: Abridged multiplication is multiplication using only so many significant figures as are required to obtain a product with sufficient precision. Let $x$, $y$ and $z$ be real numbers such that $x y = z$. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $z$ be required to be rounded to the nearest $n$th power of $10$. Let $x$ and $y$ be reported to the nearest $n - r$th and $n - s$th power of $10$ respectively.

label: Definition:Abscissa
snippet: Consider the graph $y = \map f x$ of a real function $f$ embedded in a Cartesian plane. 500px The $x$ coordinate of a point $P = \tuple {x, y}$ on $f$ is known as the abscissa of $P$.

label: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\C$.

label: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Numbers/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\C$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + \size {a_n} }$ is convergent.

label: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Numbers/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence of complex numbers. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ is absolutely convergent.

label: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Numbers/Definition 3
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\C$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent there exists $n_0 \in \N$ such that: $a_n \ne -1$ for $n > n_0$ The series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = n_0 + 1}^\infty \log \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent where $\log$ denotes the complex logarithm.

label: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/General Definition
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm{\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb K$.

label: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/General Definition/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb K$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + \norm {a_n} }$ is convergent.

label: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/General Definition/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb K$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ is absolutely convergent.

label: Definition:Absolute Difference
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. The absolute difference between $a$ and $b$ is defined and denoted as: $\size {a - b}$ where $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ is the absolute value function. That is, the result of the smaller number subtracted from the larger.

label: Definition:Absolute Difference/Also known as
snippet: == Absolute Difference: Also known as == The absolute difference between two real numbers is usually referred to just as their difference. However, this usage is ambiguous, so is deprecated on .

label: Definition:Absolute Error/Also defined as
snippet: == Absolute Error: Also defined as == Let $x_0$ be an approximation to a (true) value $x$. The absolute error of $x_0$ in $x$ can also be seen defined as: {{eqn | n = 2 | l = \Delta x | o = := | r = \size {x_0 - x} }} where $\size {x_0 - x}$ denotes the absolute value of $x_0 - x$.

label: Definition:Absolute Galois Group
snippet: == Definition == Let $K$ be a field.

label: Definition:Absolute Galois Group/Definition 1
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. The absolute Galois group of $K$ is the Galois group $\Gal {K^{\operatorname{sep} } \mid K}$ of its separable closure.

label: Definition:Absolute Galois Group/Definition 2
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. The absolute Galois group of $K$ is the automorphism group $\Aut {\overline K \mid K}$ of its algebraic closure.

label: Definition:Absolute Geometry
snippet: Absolute geometry is the study of Euclidean geometry without the parallel postulate.

label: Definition:Absolute Geometry/Also known as
snippet: == Absolute Geometry: Also known as == Absolute geometry is also known as neutral geometry.

label: Definition:Absolute Number
snippet: An absolute number is a number in an expression which has a single value. It is either expressed using actual figures, in an agreed number system, or by a symbol which is understood to represent that specific number.

label: Definition:Absolute Value/Also known as
snippet: == Absolute Value: Also known as == The absolute value of $x$ is sometimes called the modulus or magnitude of $x$, but note that modulus has a more specialized definition in the domain of complex numbers, and that magnitude has a more specialized definition in the context of vectors. Some sources refer to it as the size of $x$. Some sources call it the numerical value. Some call it just the value, but that term is too broad to be reliable.

label: Definition:Absolute Value/Definition 1
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. The absolute value of $x$ is denoted $\size x$, and is defined using the usual ordering on the real numbers as follows: $\size x = \begin{cases} x & : x > 0 \\ 0 & : x = 0 \\ -x & : x < 0 \end{cases}$

label: Definition:Absolute Value/Definition 1/Also presented as
snippet: == Absolute Value: Also presented as == Because $0 = -0$, the value of $\size x$ at $x = 0$ is often included in one of the other two cases, most commonly: $\size x = \begin{cases} x & : x \ge 0 \\ -x & : x < 0 \end{cases}$ but this can be argued as being less symmetrically aesthetic. This form can also be found: $\size x = \begin{cases} x & : x \ge 0 \\ -x & : x \le 0 \end{cases}$

label: Definition:Absolute Value/Definition 2
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. The absolute value of $x$ is denoted $\size x$, and is defined as: $\size x = +\sqrt {x^2}$ where $+\sqrt {x^2}$ is the positive square root of $x^2$.

label: Definition:Absolute Value/Graphical Illustration
snippet: == Graphical Illustration == The graph of the absolute value function can be presented as: 500px

label: Definition:Absolute Value/Number Classes
snippet: The absolute value function applies to the various number classes as follows: Natural numbers $\N$: All elements of $\N$ are greater than or equal to zero, so the concept is irrelevant. Integers $\Z$: As defined here. Rational numbers $\Q$: As defined here. Real numbers $\R$: As defined here. Complex numbers $\C$: As $\C$ is not an ordered set, the definition of the absolute value function based upon whether a complex number is greater than or less than zero cannot be applied. The notation $\cmod z$, where $z \in \C$, is defined as the modulus of $z$ and has a different meaning.

label: Definition:Absolute Value/Ordered Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times, \le}$ be an ordered integral domain whose zero is $0_D$. Then for all $a \in D$, the absolute value of $a$ is defined as: $\size a = \begin {cases} a & : 0_D \le a \\ -a & : a 0_D$ denotes that $\neg \paren {a \le 0_D}$.

label: Definition:Absolute Value/Technical Note
snippet: == Technical Note == has a $\LaTeX$ shortcut for the symbol used to denote absolute value: {{LatexFor|for = \size {x} }} If the argument of the \size command is $1$ character, then the braces {} are usually omitted. Category:Definitions/Absolute Value Function Category:Technical Notes

label: Definition:Absolute Value of Mapping
snippet: Let $D$ be an ordered integral domain. Let $\size {\, \cdot \,}_D$ denote the absolute value function on $D$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to D$ be a mapping. Then the absolute value of $f$, denoted $\size f_D: S \to D$, is defined as: $\forall s \in S: \map {\size f_D} s := \size {\map f s}_D$ Absolute value thence is an instance of a pointwise operation on a mapping.

label: Definition:Absolute Value of Mapping/Extended Real-Valued Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a set, and let $f: S \to \overline \R$ be an extended real-valued function. Then the absolute value of $f$, denoted $\size f: S \to \overline \R$, is defined as: $\forall s \in S: \map {\size f} s := \size {\map f s}$ where $\size {\map f s}$ denotes the extended absolute value function on $\overline \R$. Absolute value thence is an instance of a pointwise operation on extended real-valued functions. Since extended absolute value coincides on $\R$ with the standard ordering, this definition incorporates the definition for real-valued functions.

label: Definition:Absolute Value of Mapping/Real-Valued Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to \R$ be a real-valued function. Then the absolute value of $f$, denoted $\size f: S \to \R$, is defined as: $\forall s \in S: \map {\size f} s := \size {\map f s}$ where $\size {\map f s}$ denotes the absolute value function on $\R$. Absolute value thence is an instance of a pointwise operation on real-valued functions.

label: Definition:Absolutely Consistent Proof System
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr P$ be a consistent proof system for $\LL$. Then $\mathscr P$ is absolutely consistent not all WFF of $\mathscr P$ is a theorem.

label: Definition:Absolutely Continuous Random Variable/Also known as
snippet: == Absolutely Continuous Random Variable: Also known as == Often, particularly in elementary discussions of probability theory, the term continuous random variable is used to mean absolutely continuous random variable as defined here. On we seek to avoid this ambiguity, and it should be made explicit whether a result applies only to absolutely continuous random variables, or general continuous random variables. Category:Definitions/Absolutely Continuous Random Variables

label: Definition:Absolutely Continuous Random Variable/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a real-valued random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $P_X$ be the probability distribution of $X$. Let $\map \BB \R$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\R$. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$. We say that $X$ is an absolutely continuous random variable : $P_X$ is an absolutely continuous measure with respect to $\lambda$.

label: Definition:Absolutely Continuous Random Variable/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a real-valued random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $F_X$ be the cumulative distribution function of $X$. We say that $X$ is an absolutely continuous random variable : $F_X$ is an absolutely continuous real function.

label: Definition:Absolutely Convergent Integral
snippet: Let $I = \ds \int_S \map f x \rd x$ be an improper integral, where $S$ is an unbounded closed interval. $I$ is absolutely convergent $\ds \int_S \size {\map f x} \rd x$ converges. Category:Definitions/Absolute Convergence Category:Definitions/Improper Integrals

label: Definition:Absolutely Convergent Series/Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $S = \ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ be a series in the complex number field $\C$. Then $S$ is absolutely convergent : $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \cmod {a_n}$ is convergent where $\cmod {a_n}$ denotes the complex modulus of $a_n$.

label: Definition:Absolutely Convergent Series/General
snippet: Let $V$ be a normed vector space with norm $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ be a series in $V$. Then the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ in $V$ is absolutely convergent $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \norm {a_n}$ is a convergent series in $\R$.

label: Definition:Absolutely Convergent Series/Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ be a series in the real number field $\R$. Then $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ is absolutely convergent : $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \size {a_n}$ is convergent where $\size {a_n}$ denotes the absolute value of $a_n$.

label: Definition:Absolutely Convex Set
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $A \subseteq X$. We say that $A$ is absolutely convex : $A$ is convex and balanced.

label: Definition:Absolutely Normal Number
snippet: A real number $r$ is absolutely normal if it is normal every number base $b$. That is, its basis expansion in every number base $b$ is such that: no finite sequence of digits of $r$ of length $n$ occurs more frequently than any other such finite sequence of length $n$. In particular, for every number base $b$, all digits of $r$ have the same natural density in the basis expansion of $r$.

label: Definition:Absorbent Set
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$. Let $W \subseteq V$ be a subset of $V$. Let the set $a \cdot W$ be defined as: $a \cdot W := \set {a \cdot y: y \in W}$ where: $a \in K$ $a \cdot y$ denotes the scalar multiplication. Then $W$ is an absorbent set in $V$ : $\ds \bigcup_{a \mathop \in K} a \cdot W = V$ which symbolically can be represented as: $K \cdot W = V$

label: Definition:Absorbing Set
snippet: Let $\GF$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $A \subseteq X$. We say that $A$ is absorbing : for all $x \in X$ there exists $t \in \R_{> 0}$ such that $x \in \alpha C$ for $\cmod \alpha \ge t$ where $t A$ denotes the dilation of $A$ by $t$.
