label: Excess Kurtosis of Binomial Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with a binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$ for some $n \in \N$ and $0 \le p \le 1$: Then the excess kurtosis $\gamma_2$ of $X$ is given by: $\gamma_2 = \dfrac {1 - 6 p q} {n p q}$ where $q = 1 - p$.

label: Excess Kurtosis of Chi-Squared Distribution
snippet: Let $n$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $X \sim \chi^2_n$ where $\chi^2_n$ is the chi-squared distribution with $n$ degrees of freedom. Then the excess kurtosis $\gamma_2$ of $X$ is given by: $\gamma_2 = \dfrac {12} n$

label: Excess Kurtosis of Continuous Uniform Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable which is uniformly distributed on a closed real interval $\closedint a b$. Then the excess kurtosis $\gamma_2$ of $X$ is equal to $-\dfrac 6 5$.

label: Excess Kurtosis of Gamma Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \map \Gamma {\alpha, \beta}$ for some $\alpha, \beta > 0$, where $\Gamma$ is the Gamma distribution. Then the excess kurtosis $\gamma_2$ of $X$ is given by: $\gamma_2 = \dfrac 6 \alpha$

label: Excess Kurtosis of Hat-Check Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with a Hat-Check distribution with parameter $n$. ($n \gt 3$) Then the excess kurtosis $\gamma_2$ of $X$ is given by: $\gamma_2 = 1$

label: Excess Kurtosis of Poisson Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with a Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda$. Then the excess kurtosis $\gamma_2$ of $X$ is given by: $\gamma_2 = \dfrac 1 \lambda$

label: Exchange Principle
snippet: Let $D$ be a strongly minimal set in $\MM$. Let $A$ be a subset of $D$. Let $b, c \in D$. If $b$ is algebraic over $A \cup \set c$ but not over $A$, then $c$ is algebraic over $A \cup \set b$.

label: Exchange of Columns as Sequence of Other Elementary Column Operations
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix. Let $i, j \in \closedint 1 m: i \ne j$ Let $\kappa_k$ denote the $k$th column of $\mathbf A$ for $1 \le k \le n$: $\kappa_k = \begin {pmatrix} a_{1 k} \\ a_{2 k} \\ \vdots \\ a_{m k} \end {pmatrix}$ Let $e$ be the elementary column operation acting on $\mathbf A$ as: {{axiom | n = \text {ERO} 3 | t = Interchange columns $i$ and $j$ | m = \kappa_i \leftrightarrow \kappa_j }} Then $e$ can be expressed as a finite sequence of exactly $4$ instances of the other two elementary column operations.

label: Exchange of Order of Indexed Summations
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a, b, c, d \in \Z$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $b$.

label: Exchange of Order of Product
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ and $S: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be propositional functions on the set of integers. Let $\ds \prod_{\map R i} x_i$ denote a product over $R$. Let the fiber of truth of both $R$ and $S$ be finite. Then: $\ds \prod_{\map R i} \prod_{\map S j} a_{i j} = \prod_{\map S j} \prod_{\map R i} a_{i j}$

label: Exchange of Order of Summation
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ and $S: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be propositional functions on the set of integers. Let $\ds \sum_{\map R i} x_i$ denote a summation over $R$. Let the fiber of truth of both $R$ and $S$ be finite. Then: $\ds \sum_{\map R i} \sum_{\map S j} a_{i j} = \sum_{\map S j} \sum_{\map R i} a_{i j}$

label: Exchange of Order of Summation with Dependency on Both Indices
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers. Let $S: \Z \times \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the Cartesian product of the set of integers with itself. Let $\ds \sum_{\map R i} x_i$ denote a summation over $R$. Let the fiber of truth of both $R$ and $S$ be finite.

label: Exchange of Order of Summations over Finite Sets
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $S, T$ be finite sets. Let $S \times T$ be their cartesian product.

label: Exchange of Rows as Sequence of Other Elementary Row Operations
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix. Let $i, j \in \closedint 1 m: i \ne j$ Let $r_k$ denote the $k$th row of $\mathbf A$ for $1 \le k \le m$: $r_k = \begin {pmatrix} a_{k 1} & a_{k 2} & \cdots & a_{k n} \end {pmatrix}$ Let $e$ be the elementary row operation acting on $\mathbf A$ as: {{axiom | n = \text {ERO} 3 | t = Interchange rows $i$ and $j$ | m = r_i \leftrightarrow r_j }} Then $e$ can be expressed as a finite sequence of exactly $4$ instances of the other two elementary row operations.

label: Excluded Point Space is First-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar p} }$ be an excluded point space. Then $T$ is first-countable.

label: Excluded Point Space is not Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $S$ be a set with at least two distinct elements. Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar p} }$ be an excluded point space. Then $T$ is not injectively path-connected.

label: Excluded Point Topology is Open Extension Topology of Discrete Topology
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $p \in S$. Let $\tau_{\bar p}$ be the excluded point topology on $S$. Let $T = \struct {S \setminus \set p, \tau_D}$ be the discrete topological space on $S \setminus \set p$. Then $T^* = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar p} }$ is an open extension space of $T$.

label: Excluded Point Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar p} }$ be an excluded point space. Then $\tau_{\bar p}$ is a topology on $S$, and $T$ is a topological space.

label: Excluded Set Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar H} }$ be an excluded set space. Then $\tau_{\bar H}$ is a topology on $S$, and $T$ is a topological space.

label: Exist Term in Arithmetic Sequence Divisible by Number
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_k}$ be an $n$-term arithmetic sequence in $\Z$ defined by: $a_k = a_0 + k d$ for $k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, n - 1$. Let $b$ be a (strictly) positive integer such that $b$ and $d$ are coprime and $b \le n$. Then there exists a term in $\sequence {a_k}$ that is divisible by $b$.

label: Existence-Uniqueness Theorem for First-Order Differential Equation
snippet: Let $P$ and $Q$ be continuous real functions on some open interval $I \subseteq \R$. Let $a \in I$. Let $b \in \R$. There exists a unique function $\map f x = y$ on $I$ that satisfies the linear first order ordinary differential equation: $(1): \quad y' + \map P x y = \map Q x$ along with the initial condition: $\map f a = b$ This function is: $\ds \map f x = be^{-\map A x} + e^{-\map A x} \int_a^x \map Q t e^{\map A t} \rd t$ where $\ds \map A x = \int_a^x \map P t \rd t$

label: Existence-Uniqueness Theorem for Homogeneous First-Order Differential Equation
snippet: Let $\map P x$ be a continuous function on an open interval $I \subseteq \R$. Let $a \in I$. Let $b \in \R$. Let $\map f x = y$ be a function satisfying the differential equation: $y' + \map P x y = 0$ and the initial condition: $\map f a = b$ Then there exists a unique function satisfying these initial conditions on the interval $I$. That function takes the form: $\map f x = b e^{-\map A x}$ where: $\ds \map A x = -\int_a^x \map P t \rd t$

label: Existence and Essential Uniqueness of Conditional Expectation Conditioned on Sigma-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an integrable random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $\GG \subseteq \Sigma$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma$. Then there exists an integrable random variable $Z$ on $\struct {\Omega, \GG, \Pr}$ such that: $\ds \int_G Z \rd \Pr = \int_G X \rd \Pr$ for each $G \in \GG$. Further, if $Z$ and $Z'$ are two integrable random variables satisfying this condition, we have: $Z = Z'$ almost everywhere.

label: Existence and Uniqueness Theorem for 1st Order IVPs
snippet: Let $x' = \map f {t, x}$, $\map x {t_0} = x_0$ be an explicit ODE of dimension $n$. Let there exist an open ball $V = \sqbrk {t_0 - \ell_0, t_0 + \ell_0} \times \map {\overline B} {x_0, \epsilon}$ of $\tuple {t_0, x_0}$ in phase space $\R \times \R^n$ such that $f$ is Lipschitz continuous on $V$. {{explain|Notation needs to be explained: $\sqbrk {t_0 - \ell_0, t_0 + \ell_0}$ looks as though it should be an interval (and so needs to be written in Wirth interval notation $\closedint {t_0 - \ell_0} {t_0 + \ell_0}$ so as to abide by house style rules), and $\tuple {t_0, x_0}$ is probably an…

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Adjoint
snippet: Let $\mathbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ and $\struct {\KK, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\KK}$ be Hilbert spaces over $\mathbb F$. Let $A: \HH \to \KK$ be a bounded linear transformation. Then there exists a unique bounded linear transformation $B: \KK \to \HH$ such that: $\innerprod {\map A x} y_\KK = \innerprod x {\map B y}_\HH$ for all $x \in \HH$ and $y \in \KK$. That is: each bounded linear transformation between Hilbert spaces has a unique adjoint.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Adjoint of Densely-Defined Linear Operator
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a densely defined linear operator on $\HH$. For each $y \in \HH$, define the linear functional $f_x : \map D T \to \Bbb F$ by: $\map {f_y} x = \innerprod {T x} y$ for each $x \in \map D T$.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Continuous Functional Calculus
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $x \in A$ be normal. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ denote the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Let $\iota : \map {\sigma_A} x \to \C$ be the inclusion mapping. Then there exists a unique unital $\ast$-algebra homomorphism $\Theta_x : \map \CC {\map {\sigma_A} x} \to A$ such that: $\map {\Theta_x} \iota = x$ where $\map \CC {\map {\sigma_A} x}$ is the space of continuous functions on $\map {\sigma_A} x$. That is, for each $x \in A$ there exists a unique continuous functional calculus.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Cycle Decomposition
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Every element of $S_n$ may be uniquely expressed as a cycle decomposition, up to the order of factors.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Direct Limit of Sequence of Groups
snippet: Let $\sequence {G_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of groups. Let $\sequence {g_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}: g_n: G_n \to G_{n + 1}$ be a sequence of group homomorphisms. Then their direct limit $G_\infty$ exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Distributional Primitive
snippet: Let $T \in \map {\DD'} \R$ be a Schwartz distribution. Then there exists a Schwartz distribution $S \in \map {\DD'} \R$ such that in the distributional sense: $S' = T$ Furthermore, $S$ is unique up to an arbitrary constant.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Dynkin System Generated by Collection of Subsets
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\GG \subseteq \powerset X$ be a collection of subsets of $X$. Then $\map \delta \GG$, the Dynkin system generated by $\GG$, exists and is unique.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Generated Topology
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\SS \subseteq \powerset X$ be a subset of the power set of $X$. Then there exists a unique topology $\map \tau \SS$ on $X$ such that: $(1): \quad \SS \subseteq \map \tau \SS$. $(2): \quad$ For any topology $\TT$ on $X$, the implication $\SS \subseteq \TT \implies \map \tau \SS \subseteq \TT$ holds.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Geodesics
snippet: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold. Let $TM$ be the tangent bundle of $M$. Let $T_p M$ be the tangent space at $p \in M$. Let $\nabla$ be a connection in $TM$. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be an open real interval. Let $\gamma : I \to M$ be a geodesic and $\gamma'$ its velocity. Then: $\forall p \in M : \forall w \in T_p M : \forall t_0 \in \R : \exists I \subseteq \R : t_0 \in I : \exists \gamma : \paren {\map \gamma {t_0} = p} \land \paren {\map {\gamma'} {t_0} = w}$ Furthermore, any two geodesics agree on their common domain.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Identification Topology
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ be a set. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$. Then the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ always exists and is unique.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Lebesgue Measure
snippet: Let $\lambda^n$ be the Lebesgue pre-measure on the half-open $n$-rectangles $\JJ_{ho}^n$. Then Lebesgue measure, the extension of $\lambda^n$ to the Borel $\sigma$-algebra $\map \BB {\R^n}$, exists and is unique.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Magma of Sets Generated by Collection of Subsets
snippet: Let $X$ be a set, and let $\Phi := \set {\phi_i: i \in I}$ be a collection of partial mappings with codomain $\powerset X$, the power set of $X$. Let $\GG \subseteq \powerset X$ be a collection of subsets of $X$. Then the magma of sets generated by $\GG$ exists and is unique.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Maximal Geodesic
snippet: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold. Let $TM$ be the tangent bundle of $M$. Let $T_p M$ be the tangent space at $p \in M$. Let $\nabla$ be a connection in $TM$. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be an open real interval. Let $\gamma : I \to M$ be a geodesic and $\gamma'$ its velocity. Then $\forall p \in M$ and $\forall v \in T_p M$ there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma$ with: $\map \gamma 0 = p$ $\map {\gamma'} 0 = v$ defined on some $I$ with $0 \in I$.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Monotone Class Generated by Collection of Subsets
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\GG \subseteq \powerset X$ be a collection of subsets of $X$. Then $\map {\mathfrak m} \GG$, the monotone class generated by $\GG$, exists and is unique.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Outward-Pointing Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold with boundary $\partial M$. Then the normal bundle to $\partial M$ is a rank-$1$ smooth vector bundle over $\partial M$. Furthermore, there is a unique smooth outward-pointing unit normal vector field along all of $\partial M$.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Positive Nth Root of Positive Element of C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $x \in A$ be positive. Let $n \ge 2$. Then there exists a unique positive element $y \in A$ such that $x = y^n$.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Positive Root of Positive Real Number
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x \ge 0$. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n \ne 0$. Then there always exists a unique $y \in \R: \paren {y \ge 0} \land \paren {y^n = x}$. Hence the justification for the terminology the positive $n$th root of $x$ and the notation $x^{1/n}$.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Reduced Form of Group Word
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $w$ be a group word on $X$. Then $w$ has a unique reduced form.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Sigma-Algebra Generated by Collection of Mappings
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {\struct {X_i, \Sigma_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of measurable spaces. Let $X$ be a set. Let $\family {f_i: X \to X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of mappings. Then $\map \sigma {f_i: i \in I}$, the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$, exists and is unique.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Sigma-Algebra Generated by Collection of Subsets
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\GG \subseteq \powerset X$ be a collection of subsets of $X$. Then $\map \sigma \GG$, the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $\GG$, exists and is unique.

label: Existence and Uniqueness of Solution for Linear Second Order ODE with two Initial Conditions
snippet: Let $\map P x$, $\map Q x$ and $\map R x$ be continuous real functions on a closed real interval $\closedint a b$. Let $x_0$ be any point in $\closedint a b$. Let $y_0$ and ${y_0}'$ be real numbers. Then the linear second order ordinary differential equation: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} + \map P x \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + \map Q x y = \map R x$ has a unique particular solution $\map y x$ on $\closedint a b$ such that: $\map y {x_0} = y_0$ and: $\map {y'} {x_0} = {y_0}'$

label: Existence of Abscissa of Absolute Convergence
snippet: Let $\ds \map f s = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n n^{-s}$ be a Dirichlet series. Let the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \size { a_n n^{-s} }$ not converge for all $s \in \C$, or diverge for all $s \in \C$. Then there exists a real number $\sigma_a$ such that $\map f s$ converges absolutely for all $s = \sigma + it$ with $\sigma > \sigma_a$, and does not converge absolutely for all $s$ with $\sigma < \sigma_a$. We call $\sigma_a$ the abscissa of absolute convergence of the Dirichlet series.

label: Existence of Abscissa of Convergence
snippet: Let $\ds \map f s = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n n^{-s}$ be a Dirichlet series. Let the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \size {a_n n^{-s} }$ not converge for all $s \in \C$, or diverge for all $s \in \C$. Then there exists a real number $\sigma_c$ such that $\map f s$ converges for all $s = \sigma + i t$ with $\sigma > \sigma_c$, and does not converge for all $s$ with $\sigma < \sigma_c$. We call $\sigma_c$ the abscissa of convergence of the Dirichlet series.

label: Existence of Adapted Orthonormal Frames
snippet: Let $\struct {\tilde M, \tilde g}$ be a Riemannian manifold without boundary. Let $M \subseteq \tilde M$ be an embedded smooth submanifold with or without boundary. Let $p \in M$ be a point. Then there exists a neighborhood $\tilde U$ of $p$ in $\tilde M$ and a smooth orthonormal frame for $\tilde M$ on $\tilde U$ that is adapted to $M$.

label: Existence of Approximate Identity of C*-Algebra arising from Dense Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $I$ be an everywhere dense ideal of $A$. Let $\le_A$ be the canonical preordering of $A$. Let $A_{\mathbf{SA} }$ be the set of Hermitian elements of $A$. Let: $\EE = \set {e \in I \cap A_{\mathbf{SA} } : \map {\sigma_A} e \subseteq \hointr 0 1}$ Then $\tuple {\EE, \le_A}$ is directed and $\EE$ is an approximate identity of $A$.

label: Existence of Arbitrarily Long Aliquot Sequences
snippet: It is possible to construct an aliquot sequence of arbitrary length which is monotonically increasing.

label: Existence of Banach Limits
snippet:
Let $\struct {\map {\ell^\infty} \R, 
orm \cdot_\infty}$ be the normed vector space of bounded sequences on $\R$. Let $\struct {\paren {\map {\ell^\infty} \R}^\ast, 
orm \cdot_{\paren {\ell^\infty}^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {\map {\ell^\infty} \R, 
orm \cdot_\infty}$. Then there exists a Banach limit $L \in \paren {\map {\ell^\infty} \R}^\ast$.

label: Existence of Base-N Representation
snippet: Given a number $x \in \hointr 0 1$, there exists a representation of that number in a base-$p$ positional system. Specifically, there exists a sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ such that: $0 \le a_n < p$, and $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {a_n} {p^n}$ converges to $x$. Unless $\sequence {a_n}$ terminates (that is $a_n = 0$ for all sufficiently large $n$), then this representation is unique. If $\sequence {a_n}$ does terminate, then there is exactly one other sequence which satisfies the criteria of the theorem.

label: Existence of Bijection between Coproducts of two Sets
snippet: Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be sets. Let $\struct {C, i_1, i_2}$ and $\struct {D, j_1, j_2}$ be two coproducts on $S_1$ and $S_2$. Then there exists a unique bijection $\theta: D \to C$ such that: $\theta \circ j_i = i_1$ $\theta \circ j_2 = i_2$

label: Existence of Canonical Form of Rational Number
snippet: Let $r \in \Q$. Then: $\exists p \in \Z, q \in \Z_{>0}: r = \dfrac p q, p \perp q$ That is, every rational number can be expressed in its canonical form.

label: Existence of Cartesian Axes for which Products of Inertia are Zero
snippet: Let $B$ be a rigid body which is rotating in space about some axis $\LL$. Let $B$ be embedded in Cartesian $3$-space whose origin lies on $\LL$. Then there exists a set of coordinate axes $\mathbf O x$, $\mathbf O y$ and $\mathbf O z$ such that the products of inertia of $B$ about $\mathbf O x$, $\mathbf O y$ and $\mathbf O z$ are zero.

label: Existence of Choice Function for Family of Finite Non-Empty Sets of Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\FF$ be a family of finite non-empty sets of real numbers. Then there exists a choice function for $\FF$.

label: Existence of Class Complement
snippet: Let $X$ be a class. Then there is a unique class $Z$ such that, for every set $u$: $u \in Z \iff u \notin X$

label: Existence of Class Union
snippet: For any classes $X, Y$, the union $X \cup Y$ exists and is unique. That is: $\forall X, Y: \exists! Z: \forall u: u \in Z \iff u \in X \lor u \in Y$ where $X \cup Y := Z$.

label: Existence of Closed Geodesics
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a compact connected Riemannian manifold. Every nontrivial free homotopy class in $M$ is represented by a closed geodesic that has minimum length among all admissible loops in the given free homotopy class.

label: Existence of Compact Space which Satisfies No Separation Axioms
snippet: There exists at least one example of a compact space for which none of the Tychonoff separation axioms are satisfied.

label: Existence of Complementary Subspace
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space. Let $N \subseteq X$ be a subspace. Then $N$ has a complementary subspace. That is, there exists a subspace $Y \subseteq X$ such that: $X = N \oplus Y$

label: Existence of Connected Space which is Totally Pathwise Disconnected
snippet: There exists at least one example of a topological space which is both connected and totally pathwise disconnected.

label: Existence of Continuous Linear Functional separating Point in Hausdorff Locally Convex Space from Convex Set with Non-Empty Interior
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a Hausdorff locally convex space over $\GF$. Let $X^\ast$ be the topological dual space of $\struct {X, \PP}$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a convex set with non-empty interior. Let $\Int C$ be the interior of $C$. Let $x_0 \in X \setminus C$. Then there exists $f \in X^\ast$ such that: $\map \Re {\map f x} \le \map \Re {\map f {x_0} }$ for each $x \in C$ and: $\map \Re {\map f x} < \map \Re {\map f {x_0} }$ for each $x \in \Int C$.

label: Existence of Cuboid with Integer Edges, Face Diagonals and Space Diagonal
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether there exists a cuboid: whose edges the diagonals of whose faces the space diagonal are all integers.

label: Existence of Cyclic Group of Order n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$. Then there exists a cyclic group of order $n$ which is unique up to isomorphism.

label: Existence of Dedekind Completion
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then there exists a Dedekind completion of $S$. That is, there exists a Dedekind complete ordered set $\tilde S$ and an order embedding $\phi: S \to \tilde S$ such that: For all Dedekind complete ordered sets $X$, and for all order embeddings $f: S \to X$, there exists an order embedding $\tilde f: \tilde S \to X$ such that: $\tilde f \circ \phi = f$

label: Existence of Disjoint Well-Ordered Sets Isomorphic to Ordinals
snippet: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be ordinals. Then there exist two well-ordered sets $a$ and $b$ such that: $a$ and $b$ are order isomorphic to $\alpha$ and $\beta$ respectively $a$ and $b$ are disjoint.

label: Existence of Divisor with Remainder between 2b and 3b
snippet: For every pair of integers $a, b$ where $b > 0$, there exist unique integers $q$ and $r$ where $2 b \le r < 3 b$ such that: $a = q b + r$

label: Existence of Domain of Class Relation
snippet: Let $X$ be a class. Then there is a unique class $Z$ such that: $\forall u: u \in Z \iff \exists v: \tuple {u, v} \in X$ where $\tuple {\cdot, \cdot}$ represents the Kuratowski formalization of ordered pairs. That is, $Z$ is the class of all $z$ which appear as the first coordinate of an ordered pair in $X$.

label: Existence of Dyadic Rational between two Rationals
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be rational numbers such that $a < b$. Then there exist integers $m$ and $r$ such that: $a < \dfrac m {2^r} < b$ That is, there exists a dyadic rational between any pair of rational numbers.

label: Existence of Euler-Mascheroni Constant
snippet: The real sequence: $\ds \sequence {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \frac 1 k - \ln n}$ converges to a limit. This limit is known as the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

label: Existence of Fibonacci Number Divisible by Number
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{\ne 0}$ be an integer. Then in the first $m^2$ Fibonacci numbers there exists at least one Fibonacci number which is divisible by $m$.

label: Existence of Field of Quotients
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain. Then there exists a field of quotients of $\struct {D, +, \circ}$.

label: Existence of Fraction of Number Smaller than Given
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R_{>0}$ be two (strictly) positive real numbers, such that $a > b$. Let the sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ be defined recursively as: $a_i = \begin{cases} a & : i = 1 \\ a_{i - 1} - c: \dfrac {a_{i - 1} } 2 1 \end{cases}$ Then: $\exists n \in \N_{>0}: a_n < b$

label: Existence of Generated C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $S \subseteq A$. Then there exists a $\text C^\ast$-subalgebra $B \subseteq A$ containing $S$ which is $\subseteq$-minimal among $\text C^\ast$-subalgebras with this property.

label: Existence of Greatest Common Divisor
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers such that $a \ne 0$ or $b \ne 0$. Then the greatest common divisor of $a$ and $b$ exists.

label: Existence of Group of Finite Order
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$. Then there exists at least one group whose order is $n$.

label: Existence of Hartogs Number
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then $S$ has a Hartogs number.

label: Existence of Homomorphism between Localizations of Ring
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $S, T \subseteq A$ be multiplicatively closed subsets. $(1): \quad$ There exists an $A$-algebra homomorphism $h : A_S \to A_T$ between localizations, the induced homomorphism. $(2): \quad S$ is a subset of the saturation of $T$. $(3): \quad$ The saturation of $S$ is a subset of the saturation of $T$. $(4): \quad$ Every prime ideal meeting $S$ also meets $T$.

label: Existence of Homomorphism between Localizations of Ring at Elements
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $f, g \in A$. $(1): \quad$ There exists an $A$-algebra homomorphism $h : A_f \to A_g$ between localizations, the induced homomorphism. $(2): \quad f$ divides some power of $g$. $(3): \quad$ There is an inclusion of vanishing sets: $\map V f \subseteq \map V g$. That is, every prime ideal containing $f$ also contains $g$. $(4): \quad$ There is an inclusion of principal open subsets: $\map D f \supseteq \map D g$

label: Existence of Infinite Number of Numbers that are Riesel, Carmichael and Sierpiński
snippet: There exists an infinite number of integers which are simultaneously Sierpiński, Riesel and Carmichael.

label: Existence of Integer Below Given Real Number
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Then there exists an integer less than $x$: $\forall x \in \R: \exists n \in \Z: n < x$

label: Existence of Interval of Convergence of Power Series
snippet: Let $\xi \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\ds \map S x = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a_n \paren {x - \xi}^n$ be a power series about $\xi$. Then the interval of convergence of $\map S x$ is a real interval whose midpoint is $\xi$.

label: Existence of Inverse Elementary Column Operation
snippet: Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a metric space of order $m \times n$ over a field $K$. Let $\mathbf A \in \map \MM {m, n}$ be a matrix. Let $\map e {\mathbf A}$ be an elementary column operation which transforms $\mathbf A$ to a new matrix $\mathbf A' \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Let $\map {e'} {\mathbf A'}$ be the inverse of $e$. Then $e'$ is an elementary column operation which always exists and is unique.

label: Existence of Inverse Elementary Row Operation
snippet: Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a metric space of order $m \times n$ over a field $K$. Let $\mathbf A \in \map \MM {m, n}$ be a matrix. Let $\map e {\mathbf A}$ be an elementary row operation which transforms $\mathbf A$ to a new matrix $\mathbf A' \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Let $\map {e'} {\mathbf A'}$ be the inverse of $e$. Then $e'$ is an elementary row operation which always exists and is unique.

label: Existence of Inverse of Class Relation
snippet: Let $X$ be a class. Then there is a class $Z$ such that, for all sets $u, v$: $\tuple {u, v} \in Z \iff \tuple {v, u} \in X$ where $\tuple {\cdot, \cdot}$ denotes the Kuratowski formalization of ordered pairs.

label: Existence of Latin Squares
snippet: For each $n \in \Z_{>0}$ there exists at least one Latin square of order $n$.

label: Existence of Laurent Series
snippet: Let $z_0 \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $R \in \R_{>0}$ be a real number. Let $\map {B'} {z_0, R}$ be the open punctured disk at $z_0$ of radius $R$. Let $f: \map {B'} {z_0, R} \to \C$ be holomorphic. Then there exists a sequence $\sequence {a_n}_{n \mathop \in \Z}$ such that: $\ds \map f z = \sum_{n \mathop = -\infty}^\infty a_n \paren {z - z_0}^n$ for all $z \in B'(z_0, R)$.

label: Existence of Left Universal Product
snippet: For each $m \in \N_{> 0}$, the following is a theorem of von Neumann-Bernays-Gödel set theory: $\forall X: \exists Z: \forall x: \forall v_1, \dotsc, v_m: \sequence {v_1, \dotsc, v_m, x} \in Z \iff x \in X$ where the notation $\sequence {\cdot, \dotsc, \cdot}$ is defined inductively as: $\sequence {y_1} := y_1$ $\sequence {y_1, \dotsc, y_k, y_{k + 1}} := \tuple {\sequence {y_1, \dotsc, y_k}, y_{k + 1}}$ and $\tuple {\cdot, \cdot}$ denotes the Kuratowski formalization of ordered pairs.

label: Existence of Lowest Common Multiple
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z: a b \ne 0$. The lowest common multiple of $a$ and $b$, denoted $\lcm \set {a, b}$, always exists.

label: Existence of Magma with no Proper Submagma
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $S$ be a set of cardinality $n$: $\card S = n$ Then there exists an operation $\circ$ on $S$ such that: $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a magma $\struct {S, \circ}$ has no submagma $\struct {T, \circ}$ such that $T$ is a non-empty proper subset of $S$.

label: Existence of Matrix Logarithm
snippet: Let $T$ be a square matrix of order $n$. Then there exists a real matrix $S$ such that $e^S = T$ : $(1): \quad T$ is not a singular matrix and: $(2): \quad $for every negative eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $T$ and for every positive integer $k$, the Jordan form of $T$ has an even number of $k \times k$ blocks associated with $\lambda$.

label: Existence of Maximal Commutative Subalgebra
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be an algebra over $K$. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a non-empty set such that: for all $x, y \in S$ we have $x y = y x$. Then there exists a commutative subalgebra of $A$ containing $S$ that is maximal (among all subalgebras) set inclusion.

label: Existence of Maximum and Minimum of Bounded Sequence
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a bounded sequence in $\R$ (which may or may not be convergent). Let $L$ be the set of all real numbers which are the limit of some subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}$. Then $L$ has both a maximum and a minimum.

label: Existence of Middle Universal Product
snippet: For each $m \in \N$, the following is a theorem of von Neumann-Bernays-Gödel set theory: $\forall X: \exists Z: \forall v_1, \dotsc, v_m: \forall x, y: \sequence {x, v_1, \dotsc, v_m, y} \in Z \iff \tuple {x, y} \in X$ where the notation $\sequence {\cdot, \dotsc, \cdot}$ is defined inductively as: $\sequence {y_1} := y_1$ $\sequence {y_1, \dotsc, y_k, y_{k + 1}} := \tuple {\sequence {y_1, \dotsc, y_k}, y_{k + 1}}$ and $\tuple {\cdot, \cdot}$ denotes the Kuratowski formalization of ordered pairs.

label: Existence of Minimal Polynomial for Square Matrix over Field
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $n$ be a natural number. Let $K^{n \times n}$ be the set of $n \times n$ matrices over $K$. Let $A \in K^{n \times n}$. Then the minimal polynomial of $A$ exists and has degree at most $n^2$.

label: Existence of Minimal Uncountable Well-Ordered Set
snippet: There exists a minimal uncountable well-ordered set. That is, there exists an uncountable well-ordered set $\Omega$ with the property that every initial segment in $\Omega$ is countable.

label: Existence of Niven Number for Any Sum of Digits
snippet: Let $b, s$ be integers such that $b > 1$ and $s > 0$. Then there exists a Niven Number in base $b$ with sum of digits $s$.

label: Existence of Non-Empty Finite Infima in Meet Semilattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a meet semilattice. Let $A$ be a non-empty finite subset of $S$. Then $A$ admits a infimum in $\struct {S, \preceq}$.

label: Existence of Non-Empty Finite Suprema in Join Semilattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice. Let $A$ be a non-empty finite subset of $S$. Then $A$ admits a supremum in $\struct {S, \preceq}$.

label: Existence of Non-Locally Connected Space where Components and Quasicomponents are Equal
snippet: There exists at least one example of a topological space which is not locally connected, but whose components and quasicomponents are equal.

label: Existence of Non-Square Residue
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer such that $m > 2$. Let $\Z_m$ be the set of integers modulo $m$: $\Z_m = \set {\eqclass 0 m, \eqclass 1 m, \ldots, \eqclass {m - 1} m}$ Then there exists at least one residue in $\Z_m$ which is not the product modulo $m$ of a residue with itself: $\exists p \in \Z_m: \forall x \in \Z_m: x \cdot_m x \ne p$

label: Existence of Normal Bundle to Pseudo-Riemannian Submanifold
snippet: Let $\struct {\tilde M, \tilde g}$ be a pseudo-Riemannian manifold. Let $M \subseteq \tilde M$ be an embedded pseudo-Riemannian or Riemannian submanifold. Let $NM$ be the normal bundle of $M$. Then $NM$ is a smooth vector subbundle of $\valueat {T \tilde M} M$.

label: Existence of Number to Power of Prime Minus 1 less 1 divisible by Prime Squared
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Then there exists at least one positive integer $n$ greater than $1$ such that: $n^{p - 1} \equiv 1 \pmod {p^2}$

label: Existence of Ordered Dual Basis
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be an $n$-dimensional module over $R$. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be an ordered basis of $G$. Let $G^*$ be the algebraic dual of $G$. Let $\sequence {a'_n}$ be the ordered dual basis of $G^*$. This ordered dual basis $\sequence {a'_n}$ is guaranteed to exist.

label: Existence of Ordinal with no Surjection from Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then, there exists a non-empty ordinal $\alpha$ such that there is no surjection from $S$ to $\alpha$.

label: Existence of Orthonormal Frames
snippet: Let $\struct{M, g}$ be a $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with or without boundary. Let $p \in M$ be a point. Let $TM$ be the tangent bundle of $M$. Let $U \subseteq M$ be an open subset. Suppose $\tuple {X_j}$ is a smooth local frame for $TM$ over $U$. Then for all $p \in M$ there is a smooth orthonormal frame $\tuple {E_j}$ over $U$ such that: $\forall k \in \N : 1 \le k \le n : \map \span {\bigvalueat {E_1} p, \ldots, \bigvalueat {E_n} p} = \map \span {\bigvalueat {X_1} p, \ldots, \bigvalueat {X_n} p}$ In particular, for every $p \in M$ there is a smooth orthonormal frame $\tuple {E_j}$…

label: Existence of Positive Root of Positive Real Number
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 0$. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n \ne 0$. Then there exists a $y \in \R: y \ge 0$ such that $y^n = x$.

label: Existence of Prime-Free Sequence of Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $n$ be a natural number. Then there exists a sequence of consecutive natural numbers of length $n$ which are all composite.

label: Existence of Prime between Prime and Factorial
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Then there exists a prime number $q$ such that: $p < q \le p! + 1$ where $p!$ denotes the factorial of $p$.

label: Existence of Primitive Element for every Prime
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Then there exists a primitive element of the multiplicative group of reduced residues $\Z'_p$.

label: Existence of Probability Space and Discrete Random Variable
snippet: Let $I$ be an arbitrary countable indexing set. Let $S = \set {s_i: i \in I} \subset \R$ be a countable set of real numbers. Let $\set {\pi_i: i \in I} \subset \R$ be a countable set of real numbers which satisfies: $\ds \forall i \in I: \pi_i \ge 0, \sum_{i \mathop \in I} \pi_i = 1$ Then there exists: a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ and: a discrete random variable $X$ on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ such that the probability mass function $p_X$ of $X$ is given by: {{eqn | l = \map {p_X} {s_i} | r = \pi_i | c = if $i \in I$ }} {{eqn | l = \map {p_X} s | r = 0 | c = if…

snippet:

label: Existence of Product of Three Distinct Primes between n and 2n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 15$. Then between $n$ and $2 n$ there exists at least one integer which is the product of $3$ distinct prime numbers.

label: Existence of Pseudo-Riemannian Adapted Orthonormal Frames
snippet: Let $\struct {\tilde M, \tilde g}$ be a pseudo-Riemannian manifold. Let $M \subseteq \tilde M$ be an embedded pseudo-Riemannian or Riemannian submanifold. Then for each $p \in M$, there exists a smooth orthonormal frame on a neighborhood of $p \in \tilde M$ that is adapted to $M$.

label: Existence of Radius of Convergence of Complex Power Series
snippet: Let $\xi \in \C$. Let $\ds \map S z = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a_n \paren {z - \xi}^n $ be a (complex) power series about $\xi$. Then there exists a radius of convergence $R \in \overline \R$ of $\map S z$.

label: Existence of Rational Powers of Irrational Numbers
snippet: There exist irrational numbers $a$ and $b$ such that $a^b$ is rational.

label: Existence of Real Number at Distance Zero from Open Real Interval not in Interval
snippet:
Let $S$ be a subset of the set of real numbers $\R$. Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\map d {x, S}$ denote the distance between $x$ and $S$. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be an open real interval such that $I 
e \O$ and $I 
e \R$. Then: $\exists x 
otin I: \map d {x, I} = 0$

label: Existence of Real Polynomial with no Real Root
snippet: There exist polynomials in real numbers $\R$ which have no roots in $\R$.

label: Existence of Right Universal Product
snippet: For each $m \in \N$, the following is a theorem of von Neumann-Bernays-Gödel set theory: $\forall X: \exists Z: \forall v_1, \dotsc, v_m: \forall x: \tuple {\tuple {\dots \tuple {x, v_1}, \dots}, v_m} \in Z \iff x \in X$ Informally, for any class $X$, there is some class $Z$ such that: $Z = \paren {\dotsm \paren {X \times V} \times \dotsm} \times V$ where there are $m$ copies of $V$, the universal class, combined with $X$ via the cartesian product. Note, however, that the formal statement above allows for additional elements of $Z$ which are not of the form as written.

label: Existence of Scalar for Vector Subspace Dimension One Less
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $M$ be a subspace of the $n$-dimensional vector space $K^n$. Let $\map \dim M = n - 1$. Let $\sequence {\beta_n}$ be a sequence of scalars such that: $M = \set {\tuple {\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_n} \in K^n: \beta_1 \lambda_1 + \cdots + \beta_n \lambda_n = 0}$ Then there is a non-zero scalar $\gamma$ such that: $\forall k \in \closedint 1 n: \beta_k = \gamma \alpha_k$

label: Existence of Schur Decomposition for Square Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix. Then there exists a Schur decomposition for $\mathbf A$.

label: Existence of Sequence in Set of Real Numbers whose Limit is Infimum
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be a non-empty subset of the real numbers. Let $b$ be an infimum of $A$. Then there exists a sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ in $\R$ such that: $(1): \quad \forall n \in \N: a_n \in A$ $(2): \quad \ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} a_n = b$

label: Existence of Sequence in Subset of Metric Space whose Limit is Infimum
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a non-empty subset of $A$. Then there exists a sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of points of $S$ such that: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map d {a, a_n} = \map d {a, S}$

label: Existence of Set is Equivalent to Existence of Empty Set
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Let $P$ be the axiom: $V$ has at least one element. Then $P$ is equivalent to the : The empty class $\O$ is a set.

label: Existence of Set of Ordinals leads to Contradiction
snippet: The existence of the set of all ordinals leads to a contradiction.

label: Existence of Set with Singleton Intersections with Disjoint Collection
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a set of sets all of which are pairwise disjoint. Then: there exists a set $A$ such that $\forall S \in \CC: A \cap S$ is a singleton the axiom of choice holds.

label: Existence of Singleton Set
snippet: Let $a$ be a set. Then the singleton set $\set a$ may be constructed such that: $a \in \set a$

label: Existence of Singular Value Decomposition
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix of order $m \times n$. Then there exists a singular value decomposition of $\mathbf A$.

label: Existence of Smooth Transition Function in One Dimension
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \R$ be real numbers with $a < b < c < d$. Then there exists a smooth function $h : \R \to \closedint 0 1$ such that: $\map h x = 1$ for $x \in \closedint b c$ and: $\map h x = 0$ for $x \in \R \setminus \openint a d$

label: Existence of Subfamily of Cardinality not greater than Weight of Space and Unions Equal
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $\FF$ be a set of open sets of $T$. There exists a subset $\GG \subseteq \FF$ such that: $\ds \bigcup \GG = \bigcup \FF$ and: $\card \GG \le \map w T$ where: $\map w T$ denotes the weight of $T$ $\card \GG$ denotes the cardinality of $\GG$.

label: Existence of Subgroup of Dipper Semigroup
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers such that $m \ge 0, n > 0$. Let $\struct {N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }, +_{m, n} }$ denote the dipper semigroup. Consider the subset $H \subseteq N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ defined as: $H = \set {k \in \N: m \le k < m + n} = \set {m, m + 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ Then the substructure $\struct {H, +_{m, n} }$ is a subgroup of $\struct {N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }, +_{m, n} }$.

label: Existence of Subgroup whose Index is Prime Power
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $H$ be a normal subgroup of $G$ which has a finite index in $G$. Let: $p^k \divides \index G H$ where: $p$ is a prime number $k \in \Z_{>0}$ is a (strictly) positive integer $\divides$ denotes divisibility. Then $G$ contains a subgroup $K$ such that: $\index K H = p^k$

label: Existence of Topological Space which satisfies no Separation Axioms
snippet: There exists at least one example of a topological space for which none of the Tychonoff separation axioms are satisfied.

label: Existence of Uncomputable Mappings
snippet: There exists a mapping that is not computable.

label: Existence of Unique C* Norm on Unitization of Unital C*-Algebra
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $	ext C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\struct {A_+, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_+}$ be the unitization of $A$ as a normed algebra. Define: $	uple {a, \lambda}^\dagger = 	uple {a^\ast, \overline \lambda}$ for each $	uple {a, \lambda} \in A_+$. Then there exists a unique algebra norm $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\ast$ such that $\struct {A_+, \dagger, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\ast}$ is a $	ext C^\ast$-algebra and: $
orm {	uple {a, 0} }_\ast = 
orm a$ for each $a \in A$.

label: Existence of Unique Inverse Element for Addition of Cuts
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. Let $0^*$ be the rational cut associated with the (rational) number $0$: $0^* = \set {r \in \Q: r < 0}$ Then there exists a unique cut $\beta$ such that: $\alpha + \beta = 0^*$ where $+$ denotes the operation of addition of cuts.

label: Existence of Unique Subgroup Generated by Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\O \subset S \subseteq G$. Let $\struct {H, \circ}$ be the subgroup generated by $S$. Then $H = \gen S$ exists and is unique. Also, $\struct {H, \circ}$ is the intersection of all of the subgroups of $G$ which contain the set $S$: $\ds \gen S = \bigcap_i {H_i}: S \subseteq H_i \le G$

label: Existence of Unique Subsemigroup Generated by Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $\O \subset X \subseteq S$. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be the subsemigroup generated by $X$. Then $T = \gen X$ exists and is unique.

label: Existence of Unitization of C*-Algebra
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $	ext C^\ast$-algebra that is not unital as an algebra. Let $A_+$ be the unitization of $A$ as an algebra. Define: $	uple {x, \lambda}^\ast = 	uple {x^\ast, \overline \lambda}$ for each $	uple {x, \lambda} \in A_+$. Then there exists a unique algebra norm $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\ast$ such that $\struct {A_+, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\ast}$ is a unital $	ext C^\ast$-algebra. Further, $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\ast$ extends $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$.

label: Existence of Universal Class
snippet: There exists a unique class $V$ such that: $\forall u: u \in V$ That is, the universal class exists and is unique.

label: Existence of Upper and Lower Numbers of Cut whose Difference equal Given Rational
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. Let $r \in \Q_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive rational number. Then there exist rational numbers $p$ and $q$ such that: $p \in \alpha, q \notin \alpha$ $q - p = r$ such that $q$ is not the smallest upper number of $\alpha$.

label: Existence of Urysohn Function does not guarantee Normal Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a regular space. Let $T$ have the property that: For all closed sets $A, B \subseteq S$ of $T$ such that $A \cap B = \O$, there exists an Urysohn function for $A$ and $B$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is a normal space.

label: Existence of Vector Space Bases implies Axiom of Choice
snippet: The supposition that every vector space has a basis, along with the Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms, implies that the holds.

label: Existence of Vitali Set implies Subset of Unit Interval with Inner Measure Zero and Outer Measure 1
snippet: Let us posit the existence of a Vitali set. Then there exists a subset of the closed unit interval which has an inner measure of $0$ and an outer measure of $1$.

label: Existence of n such that M - 2^n or M + 2^n has no Prime factors less than 331
snippet: Let $M \in \Z$ be an integer. Then there exists a positive integer $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ such that either $M - 2^n$ or $M + 2^n$ has no prime factors less than $331$.

label: Existence of q for which j - qk is Positive
snippet: Let $j, k \in \Z$ be integers such that $k > 0$. Then there exist $q \in \Z$ such that $j - q k > 0$.

label: Existential Statement/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Existential Statements ==

label: Exists Bijection to a Disjoint Set
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Then there exists a bijection from $T$ onto a set $T'$ disjoint from $S$.

label: Exists Divisor in Set of n+1 Natural Numbers no greater than 2n
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of $n + 1$ non-non-zero natural numbers all less than or equal to $2 n$. Then there exists $a, b \in S$ such that $a \divides b$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibility.

label: Exists Element Not in Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then: $\exists x: x \notin S$ That is, for any set, there exists some element which is not in that set.

label: Exists Ordinal Greater than Set of Ordinals
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of ordinals. Then there exists an ordinal greater than every element of $S$: If $S$ contains a greatest ordinal $\alpha$, then $\alpha^+$ is greater than every element of $S$ If $S$ does not contain a greatest ordinal, then $\bigcup S$ is greater than every element of $S$.

label: Exists Rational Cut Between two Cuts
snippet: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be cuts. Let $\alpha < \beta$, where $<$ denotes the strict ordering on cuts. Then there exists a rational cut $r^*$ associated with the rational number $r$ such that: $\alpha < r^* < \beta$

label: Exists Subset which is not Element
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then there exists at least one subset of $S$ which is not an element of $S$.

label: Exp (-x^2) is Schwartz Test Function
snippet: $\map \exp {-x^2}$ is a Schwartz test function.

label: Expansion of Associated Reduced Quadratic Irrational
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\alpha$ be a reduced quadratic irrational which is associated to $n$. Let $\alpha$ be transformed into its integer part and fractional part via: $\alpha = \left \lfloor {\alpha} \right \rfloor + \dfrac 1{\alpha'}$ Then the resulting quadratic irrational $\alpha'$ is also reduced and associated to $n$.

label: Expansion of Included Set Topology
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $A_1 \subseteq S$ and $A_2 \subseteq S$. Let $T_1 = \struct {S, \tau_{A_1} }$ and $T_2 = \struct {S, \tau_{A_2} }$ be included set spaces on $S$. Then: $(1): \quad T_1 \ge T_2 \iff A_1 \subseteq A_2$ $(2): \quad T_1 > T_2 \iff A_1 \subsetneq A_2$ where: $T_1 \ge T_2$ denotes that $T_1$ is finer than $T_2$ $T_1 > T_2$ denotes that $T_1$ is strictly finer than $T_2$.

label: Expectation Preserves Inequality
snippet: Let $X$, $Y$ be random variables. Let $\map \Pr {X \ge Y} = 1$. Then: $\expect X \ge \expect Y$

label: Expectation and Variance of Poisson Distribution equal its Parameter
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda$. Then the expectation of $X$ equals the variance of $X$, that is, $\lambda$ itself.

label: Expectation is Linear
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be integrable random variables on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $\expect X$ denote the expectation of $X$. Then: $\forall \alpha, \beta \in \R: \expect {\alpha X + \beta Y} = \alpha \, \expect X + \beta \, \expect Y$

label: Expectation is Monotone
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be integrable random variables such that: $\forall \omega \in \Omega: \map X \omega \le \map Y \omega$ Then: $\expect X \le \expect Y$

label: Expectation of Binomial Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$ for some $n \in \N$ and $0 \le p \le 1$. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = n p$

label: Expectation of Bounded Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers with $b \ge a$. Let: $\map \Pr {a \le X \le b} = 1$ Then: $a \le \expect X \le b$ where $\expect X$ denotes the expectation of $X$.

label: Expectation of Conditional Expectation
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $\GG \subseteq \Sigma$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra. Let $X$ be a integrable random variable. Let $\expect {X \mid \GG}$ be a version of the conditional expectation of $X$ given $\GG$. Then: $\expect {\expect {X \mid \GG} } = \expect X$

label: Expectation of Continuous Uniform Distribution
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ such that $a < b$. Let $X \sim \ContinuousUniform a b$ be the continuous uniform distribution over $\closedint a b$. Then: $\expect X = \dfrac {a + b} 2$

label: Expectation of Exponential Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable of the exponential distribution with parameter $\beta$ for some $\beta \in \R_{> 0}$ Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \beta$

label: Expectation of Function of Joint Probability Mass Distribution
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be discrete random variables on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $\expect X$ be the expectation of $X$. Let $g: \R^2 \to \R$ be a real-valued function Let $p_{X, Y}$ be the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y$. $\ds \expect {\map g {X, Y} } = \sum_{x \mathop \in \Omega_X} \sum_{y \mathop \in \Omega_Y} \map g {x, y} \map {p_{X, Y} } {x, y}$ whenever the sum is absolutely convergent.

label: Expectation of Geometric Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the geometric distribution with parameter $p$ for some $0 < p < 1$.

label: Expectation of Linear Transformation of Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $a, b$ be real numbers. Let $\expect X$ denote the expectation of $X$. Then we have: $\expect {a X + b} = a \expect X + b$ if that expectation exists.

label: Expectation of Logistic Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable which satisfies the logistic distribution: $X \sim \map {\operatorname {Logistic} } {\mu, s}$ The expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \mu$

label: Expectation of Negative Binomial Distribution (Type 2)/Also defined as
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the type $2$ negative binomial distribution with parameters $r$ and $p$. Let $X$ use the definition as the number of failures before $r$ successes have occurred. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \dfrac {r q} p$ where $q = 1 - p$.

label: Expectation of Non-Negative Random Variable is Non-Negative
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $\map \Pr {X \ge 0} = 1$. Then: $\expect X \ge 0$ where $\expect X$ denotes the expectation of $X$.

label: Expectation of Normal Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim N \paren {\mu, \sigma^2}$ for some $\mu \in \R, \sigma \in \R_{> 0}$, where $N$ is the normal distribution. Then: $\expect X = \mu$ where $\mu$ denotes the expectation of $X$.

label: Expectation of Poisson Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda$. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \lambda$

label: Expectation of Product of Independent Random Variables is Product of Expectations
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be non-negative real-valued random variables that are independent. Then: $\expect {X Y} = \expect X \expect Y$

label: Expectation of Random Variable as Integral with respect to Probability Distribution
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an integrable real-valued random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $P_X$ be the probability distribution of $X$. Then: $\ds \expect X = \int_\R x \map {\rd P_X} x$ where $\expect X$ is the expected value of $X$.

label: Expectation of Real-Valued Discrete Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a discrete real-valued random variable. Then $X$ is integrable : $\ds \sum_{x \in \Img X} \size x \map \Pr {X = x} < \infty$ in which case: $\ds \expect X = \sum_{x \in \Img X} x \map \Pr {X = x}$

label: Expectation of Real-Valued Measurable Function composed with Absolutely Continuous Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an absolutely continuous random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $P_X$ be the probability distribution of $X$. Let $\map \BB \R$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\R$. Let $h : \R \to \R$ be a $\map \BB \R$-measurable function. Let $f_X$ be a probability density function for $X$. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$.

label: Expectation of Student's t-Distribution
snippet: Let $k$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $X \sim t_k$ where $t_k$ is the $t$-distribution with $k$ degrees of freedom. Then the expectation of $X$ is equal to $0$ for $k > 1$, and does not exist otherwise.

label: Expected-Utility Maximization Theorem
snippet: Let $P$ be a rational decision-maker. Let $A$ be a set of possible moves available to $P$. Then there exists a way of assigning values to a payoff function $u: A \to \R$ so that $P$ will always choose the move such that $u$ is a maximum.

label: Expected Number of Rolls until Two Consecutive Heads
snippet: Let $0 < p \le 1$. Consider a coin such that we toss a head with probability $p$. We repeatedly toss this coin until we observe two consecutive heads. The expected number of tosses until we observe two consecutive heads is: $\ds \frac 1 p + \frac 1 {p^2}$ In particular, for a fair coin, the expected value is $6$. {{explain|Does this generalize? That is, until $n$ consecutive heads is it $\ds \sum_{k \mathop 1}^n \dfrac 1 {p^k}$? be nice if it did}}

label: Expected Number of Trials Until N Consecutive Successes
snippet: Let $0 < p \le 1$. Let $N$ be a positive integer. We conduct an experiment with probability of success $p$. We run this experiment until we see $N$ consecutive successes. Then the expected number of trials until we see $N$ consecutive successes is: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^N p^{-k} = \frac 1 p + \frac 1 {p^2} + \ldots + \frac 1 {p^N}$

label: Expected Sum of Randomly Drawn Subset
snippet: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Let $\sqbrk n = \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$ be the set of integers between $1$ and $n$. Equip $\powerset {\sqbrk n}$ with the discrete uniform distribution. Let $\map \Sigma S$ be the sum of a subset $S \in \powerset {\sqbrk n}$. Then: $\ds \expect {\map \Sigma S} = \frac {n \paren {n + 1} } 4$

snippet: == Examples of Experiments ==

label: Explicit Form for Generated C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $S \subseteq A$. Define: $S^\ast = \set {x^\ast : x \in A}$ Let $\map {\text C^\ast} S$ be the $\text C^\ast$-algebra generated by $S$. Then: $\ds \map {\text C^\ast} S = \span \set {x_1^{k_1} x_2^{k_2} \ldots x_n^{k_n} : x_1, \ldots, x_n \in S \cup S^\ast, \, k_1, \ldots, k_n \ge 0}^-$ where $\paren {\cdot}^-$ denotes closure in $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$.

label: Exponent Base of One
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then: $1^x = 1$

label: Exponent Combination Laws
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R_{>0}$ be strictly positive real numbers. Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $a^x$ be defined as $a$ to the power of $x$. Then:

label: Exponent Not Equal to Zero
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x \ne 0$. Then: $x^y \ne 0$

label: Exponent of Convergence is Less Than Order
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function. Let $\omega$ be its order. Let $\tau$ be its exponent of convergence. Then $\tau \le \omega$.

label: Exponential Distribution in terms of Beta Distribution
snippet: Let $\sequence {X_n}$ be a sequence of independent random variables with: $X_n \sim \BetaDist 1 n$ for each natural number $n$, where $\BetaDist 1 n$ denotes the beta distribution with parameters $1$ and $n$. Then: $n X_n \xrightarrow d X$ with: $X \sim \Exponential 1$ where: $\Exponential 1$ denotes the exponential distribution with parameter $1$, $\xrightarrow d$ denotes convergence in distribution.

label: Exponential Dominates Polynomial
snippet: Let $\exp$ denote the real exponential function. Let $k \in \N$. Let $\alpha \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\exists N \in \N: \forall x \in \R_{>N}: \map \exp {\alpha x} > x^k$

label: Exponential Function as Limit of Gaussian Hypergeometric Function
snippet: Let $\map F {a, b; c; x}$ denote the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac { a^{\overline k} b^{\overline k} } { c^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$ Then: $\ds e^x = \lim_{p \mathop \to \infty} \map F {1, p; 1; \dfrac x p}$ where $x$ is a real number.

label: Exponential Function in terms of Hypergeometric Function
snippet: $e^x = \map { {}_1 \operatorname F_1} {p; p; x}$ where: $x$ is a real number with $x \in \R$ $e^x$ denotes the exponential function $\map { {}_1 \operatorname F_1} {a; b; x}$ is the generalized hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac { a^{\overline k} } { b^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$

label: Exponential Function is Superfunction
snippet: The function $f : \C \to \C$, defined as: $\map f z = c^z$ is a superfunction for any complex number $c$.

label: Exponential Function is Well-Defined/Real
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then $\exp x$ is well-defined.

label: Exponential Growth Equation/Special Case
snippet: All solutions of the differential equation $y' = y$ take the form $y = C e^x$.

label: Exponential Sequence Converges Compactly
snippet: For each $n \in \N$, let $f_n : \C \to \C$ be defined as: $\map {f_n} z = \paren {1 + \dfrac z n}^n$ Then, $\sequence {f_n}$ converges compactly to the complex exponential function.

label: Exponential Sequence is Eventually Increasing
snippet: Let $\sequence {E_n}$ be the sequence of real functions $E_n: \R \to \R$ defined as: $\map {E_n} x = \paren {1 + \dfrac x n}^n$ Then, for sufficiently large $n \in \N$, $\sequence {\map {E_n} x}$ is increasing $n$. That is: $\forall x \in \R: \forall n \in \N: n \ge \ceiling {\size x} \implies \map {E_n} x \le \map {E_{n + 1} } x$ where $\ceiling x$ denotes the ceiling of $x$.

label: Exponential Sequence is Eventually Strictly Positive
snippet: Let $\sequence {E_n}$ be the sequence of real functions $E_n: \R \to \R$ defined as: $\map {E_n} x = \paren {1 + \dfrac x n}^n$ Then, for each $x \in \R$ and for sufficiently large $n \in \N$, $\map {E_n} x$ is positive. That is: $\forall x \in \R: \forall n \in \N: n \ge \ceiling {\size x} \implies \map {E_n} x > 0$ where $\ceiling x$ denotes the ceiling of $x$.

label: Exponential Sequence is Uniformly Convergent on Compact Sets
snippet: Let $\EE = \sequence {E_n}$ denote the sequence of complex functions $E_n: \C \to \C$ defined as: $\map {E_n} z = \paren {1 + \dfrac z n}^n$ Let $K$ be a compact subset of $\C$. Then $\EE$ is uniformly convergent on $K$.

label: Exponential Tends to Zero and Infinity
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: $\exp x \to +\infty$ as $x \to +\infty$ $\exp x \to 0$ as $x \to -\infty$ Thus the exponential function has domain $\R$ and image $\openint 0 \infty$.

label: Exponential Time/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Exponential Time ==

label: Exponential is Strictly Convex
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: The function $f \left({x}\right) = \exp x$ is strictly convex.

label: Exponential is Strictly Increasing
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: The function $\map f x = \exp x$ is strictly increasing.

label: Exponential of Category of Sets
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $B$ and $C$ be sets. Let $C^B$ be the set of all mappings from $B$ to $C$. Define a mapping $\epsilon : C^B \times B \to C$ by: $\map \epsilon {f,b} = \map f b$ where $C^B \times B$ denotes the Cartesian product of $C^B$ and $B$. Then $\struct {C^B,\epsilon}$ is an exponential of $C$ by $B$. Moreover, the transpose $\tilde f : A \to C^B$ of $f : A\times B \to C$ is given by: $\map {\tilde f} a = \map f {a, \cdot}$

label: Exponential of Complex Number plus 2 pi i
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\map \exp {z + 2 \pi i} = \map \exp z$

label: Exponential of Natural Logarithm
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$. Then: $\forall x > 0: \map \exp {\ln x} = x$ $\forall x \in \R: \map \ln {\exp x} = x$

label: Exponential of One
snippet: Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: $\exp 1 = e$ where $e$ is Euler's number: $e = 2.718281828\ldots$

label: Exponential of Product
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: $\map \exp {x y} = \paren {\exp y}^x$

label: Exponential of Rational Number is Irrational
snippet: Let $r$ be a rational number such that $r \ne 0$. Then: $e^r$ is irrational where $e$ is Euler's number.

label: Exponential of Real Number is Strictly Positive
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Let $\exp$ denote the (real) exponential function. Then: $\forall x \in \R : \exp x > 0$

label: Exponential of Series Equals Infinite Product
snippet: Let $\sequence {z_n}$ be a sequence of complex numbers. Suppose $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty z_n$ converges to $z \in \C$. Then $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map \exp {z_n}$ converges to $\exp z$.

label: Exponential of Sum of Real Numbers/Corollary
snippet: == Corollary to Exponential of Sum of Real Numbers == Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: $\map \exp {x - y} = \dfrac {\exp x} {\exp y}$

label: Exponential of Zero
snippet: Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: $\exp 0 = 1$

label: Exponential on Complex Plane is Group Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Let $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of complex numbers. Let $\exp: \struct {\C, +} \to \struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ be the mapping: $x \mapsto \map \exp x$ where $\exp$ is the complex exponential function. Then $\exp$ is a group homomorphism.

label: Exponential on Real Numbers is Group Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $\struct {\R_{> 0}, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of positive real numbers. Let $\exp: \struct {\R, +} \to \struct {\R_{> 0}, \times}$ be the mapping: $x \mapsto \map \exp x$ where $\exp$ is the exponential function. Then $\exp$ is a group isomorphism.

label: Exponentiation Functor is Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a Cartesian closed metacategory. Let $A$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\left({-}\right)^A: \mathbf C \to \mathbf C$ be the exponentiation functor. Then $\left({-}\right)^A$ is a functor.

label: Exponents of Primes in Prime Decomposition are Less iff Divisor
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z_{>0}$. Then $a \divides b$ : $(1): \quad$ every prime $p_i$ in the prime decomposition of $a$ appears in the prime decomposition of $b$ and: $(2): \quad$ the exponent of each $p_i$ in $a$ is less than or equal to its exponent in $b$.

label: Expression for Balanced Hull
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be non-empty.. Then the balanced hull $\map {\operatorname {bal} } A$ is well-defined and: $\ds \map {\operatorname {bal} } A = \bigcup_{\lambda \in \GF : \cmod \lambda \le 1} \lambda A$

label: Expression for Closure of Set in Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $A \subseteq X$. Let $\mathcal V$ be the set of open neighborhoods of ${\mathbf 0}_X$. Then: $\ds A^- = \bigcap_{V \in \mathcal V} \paren {A + V}$ where $A^-$ is the closure of $A$.

label: Expression for Integer as Product of Primes is Unique
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer such that $n > 1$. Then the expression for $n$ as the product of one or more primes is unique up to the order in which they appear.

label: Expression for Set of Points at which Sequence of Functions does not Converge to Given Function
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a real function. For each $n \in \N$, let $f_n : X \to \R$ be a real function. Then we have: $\ds \set {x \in X : \sequence {\map {f_n} x}_{n \in \N} \text { does not converge to } \map f x} = \bigcup_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \bigcap_{N \mathop = 1}^\infty \bigcup_{n \mathop = N}^\infty \set {x \in X : \size {\map {f_n} x - \map f x} \ge \frac 1 k}$

label: Expression for bilinear function
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function of two independent variables, $f \in \R \times \R \to \R$. Then: $\map f {x, y}$ is a linear function of $x$ when $y$ is equal to a real constant $\map f {x, y}$ is a linear function of $y$ when $x$ is equal to a real constant $f$ has the form: $\exists a, b, c, d \in \R: \forall {x, y} \in \R: \map f {x, y} = a x y + b x + c y + d$

label: Expression of Vector as Linear Combination from Basis is Unique
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space of dimension $n$. Let $\BB = \set {\mathbf x_1, \mathbf x_2, \ldots, \mathbf x_n}$ be a basis for $V$. Let $\mathbf x \in V$ be any vector of $V$. Then $\mathbf x$ can be expressed as a unique linear combination of elements of $\BB$.

label: Exradius of Triangle in Terms of Circumradius
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides are $a$, $b$ and $c$ opposite vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively. Let $\rho_a$ be the exradius of $\triangle ABC$ $a$. Let $R$ be the circumradius of $\triangle ABC$. Then: $\rho_a = 4 R \sin \dfrac A 2 \cos \dfrac B 2 \cos \dfrac C 2$

label: Extend Theory to Satisfy Witness Property
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a language of predicate logic. Let $T$ be a set of $\LL$-sentences. Then there exists a language $\LL^*$ and a set of $\LL^*$-sentences $T^*$ satisfying the following properties: $T^*$ is finitely satisfiable $T$ is finitely satisfiable. If $T^*$ is satisfiable, then $T$ is also. For every $\LL^*$-WFF of $1$ free variable $\map \phi x$, there exists some constant $c_\phi$ such that: $T^* \models \paren {\exists x: \map \phi x} \implies \map \phi {x := c_\phi}$ $T^*$ satisfies the witness property.

label: Extendability Theorem for Derivatives Continuous on Open Intervals
snippet: Let $f$ be a continuous real function defined on an interval $\closedint a b$ where $a < b$. Then $f$ is continuously differentiable on $\closedint a b$ : $f$ is continuously differentiable on $\openint a b$ and: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \map {f'} x$ and $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to b^-} \map {f'} x$ exist.

label: Extended Completeness Theorem for Propositional Tableaux and Boolean Interpretations
snippet: Tableau proofs (in terms of propositional tableaux) are a strongly complete proof system for boolean interpretations. More precisely, for every countable collection $\mathbf H$ of WFFs of propositional logic and every WFF $\mathbf A$: $\mathbf H \models_{\mathrm{BI} } \mathbf A$ implies $\mathbf H \vdash_{\mathrm{PT} } \mathbf A$

label: Extended Euclidean Algorithm
snippet: == Algorithm == The extended Euclidean algorithm is a method for: finding the greatest common divisor (GCD) $d$ of two strictly positive integers $m$ and $n$ computing two integers $a$ and $b$ such that $a m + b n = d$. Let $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$. $\mathbf 1:$ Initialise. Set $a' \gets b \gets 1, a \gets b\,' \gets 0, c \gets m, d \gets n$. $\mathbf 2:$ Divide. Let $q$ and $r$ be the quotient and remainder respectively of $ c / d$. (Thus we have $c = q d + r$ such that $0 \le r < d$.) $\mathbf 3:$ Remainder zero? If $r = 0$, the algorithm terminates.

label: Extended Mean Value Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$ and differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Let $f'$ be the derivative of $f$. Let $f'$ also be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$ and differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Then: $\exists \xi \in \openint a b: \map f b = \map f a + \paren {b - a} \map {f'} a + \dfrac 1 {2!} \paren {b - a}^2 \map {f' '} \xi$

label: Extended Real Numbers under Multiplication form Commutative Monoid
snippet: Denote with $\overline \R$ the extended real numbers. Denote with $\cdot_{\overline \R}$ the extended real multiplication. The algebraic structure $\struct {\overline \R, \cdot_{\overline \R} }$ is a commutative monoid.

label: Extended Rolle's Theorem
snippet: Let $f: D \to \R$ be differentiable on a closed interval $I \subseteq \R$. Let $x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n \in I$. Let $\map f {x_i} = 0$ for $i = 0, \ldots, n$. Then for all $i = 0, \ldots, n-1$: $\exists \xi_i \in \openint {x_i} {x_{i + 1} }: \map {f'} {\xi_i} = 0$

label: Extended Rule of Implication
snippet: Any sequent can be expressed as a theorem. That is: $P_1, P_2, P_3, \ldots, P_n \vdash Q$ means the same thing as: $\vdash P_1 \implies \paren {P_2 \implies \paren {P_3 \implies \paren {\ldots \implies \paren {P_n \implies Q} \ldots} } }$ The latter expression is known as the corresponding conditional of the former. Thus every sequent containing the symbol $\vdash$ can, if so desired, be expressed in the form of a theorem which has $\implies$.

label: Extension Realizing All Types
snippet: Let $\MM$ be an $\LL$-structure. Let $M$ be its universe. There is an elementary extension $\NN$ of $\MM$ such that every type over $M$ (relative to $\MM$) is realized in $\NN$.

label: Extension Theorem for Homomorphisms
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a commutative semigroup with cancellable elements Let $\struct {C, \circ} \subseteq \struct {S, \circ}$ be the subsemigroup of all cancellable elements of $S$ Let $\struct {S', \circ'}$ be an inverse completion of $\struct {S, \circ}$ Let $\phi$ be a (semigroup) homomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ}$ into a semigroup $\struct {T, *}$ such that $\map \phi y$ is invertible for all $y \in C$.

label: Extension Theorem for Isomorphisms
snippet: Let the following conditions be fulfilled: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a commutative semigroup with cancellable elements Let $\phi$ be an isomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ}$ into a semigroup $\struct {T, *}$ Let $\struct {S', \circ'}$ be an inverse completion of $\struct {S, \circ}$ Let $\struct {T', \circ'}$ be an inverse completion of $\struct {T, \circ}$. Then there is a unique isomorphism $\phi': S' \to T'$ extending $\phi$.

label: Extension Theorem for Positive Linear Functional defined on Cofinal Linear Subspace
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \succeq}$ be a preordered vector space over $\R$. Let $Y$ be a linear subspace of $X$ that is cofinal in $\struct {X, \succeq}$. Let $f_0 : Y \to \R$ be a positive linear functional. Then there exists a positive linear functional $f : X \to \R$ such that: $\map f y = \map {f_0} y$ for each $y \in Y$.

label: Extension of Bounded Linear Transformation from Closed Subspace of Hilbert Space to Whole Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH_1, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_1}$ and $\struct {\HH_2, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_2}$ be Hilbert spaces over $\GF$. Let $\KK_1$ and $\KK_2$ be closed linear subspaces of $\HH_1$ and $\HH_2$ respectively. Let $T_1 : \KK_1 \to \KK_2$ be a bounded linear transformation. Let $\KK_1^\bot$ of $\KK_2^\bot$ be the orthocomplements of $\KK_1$ and $\KK_2$ respectively. Let $T_2 : \KK_1^\bot \to \KK_2^\bot$ be a bounded linear transformation. Define $T : \HH_1 \to \HH_2$ by: $\map T {u + v} = T_1 u + T_2 v$ for each $u \in \KK_1$ and $v \in \KK_1^\bot$.

label: Extension of Continuous Complex-Valued Function Vanishing at Infinity to Alexandroff Extension is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $X^\ast = X \cup \set p$ be the Alexandroff extension of $X$. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a continuous complex-valued function vanishing at infinity. Define $f^\ast : X^\ast \to \C$ by taking: $\map {f^\ast} x = \begin{cases}\map f x & x \in X \\ 0 & x = p\end{cases}$ for each $x \in X^\ast$. Then $f^\ast$ is continuous.

label: Extension of Continuous Mapping is Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T_H = \struct{H, \tau_H}$ be a topological subspace of $T_2$ where $H \subseteq S_2$. Let $f: S_1 \to H$ be a $\tuple { \tau_1 , \tau_H}$-continuous mapping. Define a mapping $g: S_1 \to S_2$ by: $\forall x \in S_1 : \map g x = \map f x$ Then $g$ is $\tuple { \tau_1 , \tau_2}$-continuous.

label: Extension of Directed Suprema Preserving Mapping to Complete Lattice Preserves Directed Suprema
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $L_3 = \struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ be a complete lattice. Suppose that $L_2$ is directed suprema inheriting ordered subset of $L_3$. Let $f:S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping such that $f$ preserves directed suprema. Then $f:S_1 \to S_3$ preserves directed suprema.

label: Extension of Extension of Mapping is Extension
snippet: Let $A, B, C, S$ be sets such that $A \subseteq B \subseteq C$. Let $f: A \to S$, $g: B \to S$ and $h: C \to S$ be mappings such that: $g$ is an extension of $f$ to $B$ $h$ is an extension of $g$ to $C$. Then $h$ is an extension of $f$ to $C$.

label: Extension of Harmonic Number to Non-Integer Argument
snippet: Let $\map H x$ be the real function defined as: $\map H x = \gamma + \dfrac {\map {\Gamma'} {x + 1} } {\map \Gamma {x + 1} }$ where: $\map \Gamma x$ denotes the Gamma function $\map {\Gamma'} x$ denotes the derivative of the Gamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant. Then $H$ is an extension of the mapping $H: \N \to \Q$ defined as: $\forall n \in \N: \map H n = H_n$ where $H_n$ denotes the $n$th harmonic number.

label: Extension of Infima Preserving Mapping to Complete Lattice Preserves Infima
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$, $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $L_3 = \struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ be a complete lattice. Suppose that. $L_2$ is an infima inheriting ordered subset of $L_3$. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping such that: $f$ preserves infima. Then $f: S_1 \to S_3$ preserves infima.

label: Exterior Angle of Regular Polygon
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular polygon with $n$ sides. Then each of the exterior angles of $P$ is equal to $\dfrac {360 \degrees} n$.

label: Exterior of Finite Union equals Intersection of Exteriors
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $n \in \N$. Let $\forall i \in \closedint 1 n: H_i \subseteq S$. Then: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i}^e = \bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i^e$ where $H_i^e$ denotes the exterior of $H_i$.

label: Exterior of Intersection contains Union of Exteriors
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\mathbb H$ be a set of subsets of $TS$. That is, let $\mathbb H \subseteq \powerset S$ where $\powerset S$ is the power set of $S$. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{H \mathop \in \mathbb H} H^e \subseteq \paren {\bigcap_{H \mathop \in \mathbb H} H}^e$ where $H^e$ denotes the exterior of $H$.

label: Exterior of Union of Singleton Rationals is Empty
snippet: Let $B_\alpha$ be the singleton containing the rational number $\alpha$. Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology $\tau_d$. Then the exterior in $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ of the union of all $B_\alpha$ is the empty set: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in \Q} B_\alpha}^e = \O$

label: External Angle of Triangle equals Sum of other Internal Angles

label: External Angle of Triangle is Greater than Internal Opposite

label: External Center of Similitude of Circles with respect to Radii
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be the centers of two circles $\bigcirc Ar$ and $\bigcirc BR$ whose radii are $r$ and $R$ respectively, $r \ne R$. Let $\bigcirc Ar$ and $\bigcirc BR$ be such that neither is completely enclosed inside the other. Let $T$ be the external center of similitude of $\bigcirc Ar$ and $\bigcirc BR$. Let $P$ and $Q$ be points on the circumference of $\bigcirc Ar$ and $\bigcirc BR$ respectively. Then: the radii $AP$ and $QR$ are parallel $T$, $P$ and $Q$ are collinear.
