snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a locally convex space over $\GF$ with its standard topology. Let $K$ be a non-empty compact convex subset of $X$. Let $E$ be an extreme set of $K$. Then $E$ contains an extreme point of $K$.

label: F-Sigma Sets Closed under Intersection
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $F, F'$ be $F_\sigma$ sets of $T$. Then their intersection $F \cap F'$ is also a $F_\sigma$ set of $T$.

label: F-Sigma Sets Closed under Union
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $F, F'$ be $F_\sigma$ sets of $T$. Then their union $F \cup F'$ is also an $F_\sigma$ set of $T$.

label: F-Sigma Sets form Lattice
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF$ be the collection of all $F_\sigma$ sets of $T$. Then $\struct {\FF, \subseteq}$ is a lattice, where $\subseteq$ denotes the subset relation.

label: F-Sigma and G-Delta Subsets of Uncountable Finite Complement Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then countably infinite subsets of $S$ are $F_\sigma$ sets and are neither open nor closed sets. Their relative complements in $S$ are $G_\delta$ sets, and are also neither open nor closed sets.

label: Factor Spaces are Completely Normal if Product Space is Completely Normal
snippet: Let $\SS = \family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of non-empty topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\ds T = \struct {S, \tau} = \prod \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\SS$. Let $T$ be a completely normal space. Then each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ is a completely normal space.

label: Factor Spaces are Normal if Product Space is Normal
snippet: Let $\SS = \family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of non-empty topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\ds T = \struct {S, \tau} = \prod \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\SS$. Let $T$ be a normal space. Then each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ is a normal space.

label: Factor Spaces are T4 if Product Space is T4
snippet: Let $\SS = \family {\struct{S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of non-empty topological spaces for $\alpha$ in some indexing set $I$. Let $\ds T = \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\SS$. Let $T$ be a $T_4$ space. Then each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ is a $T_4$ space.

label: Factor Spaces are T5 if Product Space is T5
snippet: Let $\SS = \family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces for $\alpha$ in some indexing set $I$. Let $\ds T = \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\SS$. Let $T$ be a $T_5$ space. Then each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ is a $T_5$ space.

label: Factor of Mersenne Number Mp is of form 2kp + 1
snippet: Let $p$ and $q$ be prime numbers such that $q$ is a divisor of the Mersenne number $M_p$. Then: $q = 2 k p + 1$ for some integer $k$.

label: Factor of Mersenne Number equivalent to +-1 mod 8
snippet: Let $p$ and $q$ be prime numbers such that $q$ is a divisor of the Mersenne number $M_p$. Then: $q \equiv \pm 1 \pmod 8$

label: Factorial Divides Product of Successive Numbers
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{\ge 1}$ be natural numbers Let $m^{\overline n}$ be $m$ to the power of $n$ rising. Then: $m^{\overline n} \equiv 0 \bmod n!$ That is, the factorial of $n$ divides the product of $n$ successive numbers.

label: Factorial Divisible by Binary Root
snippet: Let $n \in \Z: n \ge 1$. Let $n$ be expressed in binary notation: $n = 2^{e_1} + 2^{e_2} + \cdots + 2^{e_r}$ where $e_1 > e_2 > \cdots > e_r \ge 0$. Let $n!$ be the factorial of $n$. Then $n!$ is divisible by $2^{n - r}$, but not by $2^{n - r + 1}$.

label: Factorial Divisible by Prime Power
snippet: Let $n \in \Z: n \ge 1$. Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $n$ be expressed in base $p$ notation: $\ds n = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^m r_j p^j$ where $0 \le r_j < p$. Let $n!$ be the factorial of $n$. Let $p^\mu$ be the largest power of $p$ which divides $n!$, that is: $p^\mu \divides n!$ $p^{\mu + 1} \nmid n!$ Then: $\mu = \dfrac {n - \map {s_p} n} {p - 1}$ where $\map {s_p} n$ is the digit sum of $n$ to base $p$.

snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 5$. Then $n! > n^3$.

label: Factoring Mapping into Quotient and Injection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then $f$ can be uniquely factored into a quotient mapping, followed by an injection. Thus: $f = h \circ q_{\RR_f}$ where: $q_{\RR_f}: S \to S / \RR_f: \map {q_{\RR_f} } s = \eqclass s {\RR_f}$ $h: S / \RR_f \to T: \map h {\eqclass s {\RR_f} } = \map f s$ $\eqclass s {\RR_f}$ denotes the equivalence class of $s$ with respect to the equivalence relation $\RR$ induced on $S$ by $f$.

label: Factoring Mapping into Surjection and Inclusion
snippet: Every mapping $f:S \to T$ can be uniquely factored into a surjection $g$ followed by the inclusion mapping $i_T$. That is, $f = i_T \circ g$ where: $g: S \to \Img f: \map g x = \map f x$ $i_T: \Img f \to T: \map {i_T} x = x$ This can be illustrated using a commutative diagram as follows: $\quad\quad \begin{xy}\xymatrix@L+2mu@+1em { S \ar@{-->}[r]^*{g} \ar[rd]_*{f = i_T \circ g} & \Img f \ar@{-->}[d]^*{i_T} \\ & T }\end{xy}$

label: Factorisation of z^n+1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then: $z^n + 1 = \ds \prod_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {z - \exp \dfrac {\paren {2 k + 1} i \pi} n}$

label: Factorisation of z^n+a
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $a \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $z^n + a = \ds \prod_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {z - \alpha_k b}$ where: $\alpha_k$ are the complex $n$th roots of negative unity $b$ is any complex number such that $b^n = a$.

label: Factorisation of z^n-a
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $a \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $z^n - a = \ds \prod_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {z - \alpha^k b}$ where: $\alpha$ is a primitive complex $n$th root of unity $b$ is any complex number such that $b^n = a$.

label: Factorization of Continuous Linear Transformation between Topological Vector Spaces
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, \tau_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \tau_X}$ be topological vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $N$ be a vector subspace of $X$ with $N \subseteq \ker T$. Let $\struct {X/N, \tau_N}$ be the quotient topological vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping. Then $T$ is continuous : there exists a continuous linear transformation $\Lambda : X/N \to Y$ such that: $T x = \map \Lambda {\map \pi x}$ for each $x \in X$.

label: Factorization of Limit Ordinals
snippet: Let $x$ be a limit ordinal. Then: $x = \paren {\omega \times y}$ for some $y \in \On$ where $\omega$ is the minimally inductive set.

label: Factorization of Natural Numbers within 4 n + 1 not Unique

label: Factorization of Open Linear Transformation between Topological Vector Spaces
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, \tau_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \tau_X}$ be topological vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $N$ be a vector subspace of $X$ with $N \subseteq \ker T$. Let $\struct {X/N, \tau_N}$ be the quotient topological vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping. Then $T$ is open : there exists a open linear transformation $\Lambda : X/N \to Y$ such that: $T x = \map \Lambda {\map \pi x}$ for each $x \in X$.

label: Factors in Absolutely Convergent Product Converge to One

label: Factors in Uniformly Convergent Product Converge Uniformly to One
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly on $X$. Then $f_n$ converges uniformly to $1$.

snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {H, \circ_2}$ be groups. Let $\struct {G \times H, \circ}$ be the group direct product of $\struct {G, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {H, \circ_2}$. label: Factors of Internal Direct Product of Subsemigroups are Normal Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \odot}$ be a group. Let $\struct {H, \odot_H}$ and $\struct {K, \odot_K}$ be subsemigroups of $\struct {G, \odot}$. label: Factors of Polynomial with Integer Coefficients have Integer Coefficients
snippet: Let $\Q \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial forms over the field of rational numbers in the indeterminate $X$. Let $\map h X \in \Q \sqbrk X$ have coefficients all of which are integers. Let it be possible to express $\map h X$ as: $\map h X = \map f X \, \map g X$ where $\map f X, \map g X \in \Q \sqbrk X$. Then it is also possible to express $\map h X$ as: $\map h X = \map {f'} X \, \map {g'} X$ where: $\map {f'} X, \map {g'} X \in \Q \sqbrk X$ the coefficients of $\map {f'} X$ and $\map {g'} X$ are all integers $\map {f'} X = a \map f X$ and $\map {g'} X = b \map f X$, for $a, b \in \Q$.

label: Factors of Solvable Group are Prime
snippet: Let $G$ be a solvable group. Let $\HH$ be a composition series of $G$. Then all factor groups of $\HH$ must be prime.

label: Factors of Sums of Powers of 100,000
snippet: All integers $n$ of the form: $n = \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^m 10^{5 k}$ for $m \in \Z_{> 0}$ are composite.

label: Faithful Functor Reflects Monomorphisms
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a faithful functor. Let $x$ and $y$ be objects in $\mathbf C$. Let $f: x \to y$ be a morphism in $\mathbf C$. Let $\map F f : \map F x \to \map F y$ be a monomorphism in $\mathbf D$. Then $f$ is a monomorphism in $\mathbf C$.

label: Falling Factorial as Quotient of Factorials
snippet: Let $x \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Then: $x^{\underline n} = \dfrac {x!} {\paren {x - n}!} = \dfrac {\map \Gamma {x + 1} } {\map \Gamma {x - n + 1} }$ where: $x^{\underline n}$ denotes the $n$th falling factorial power of $x$. $\map \Gamma x$ denotes the Gamma function of $x$.

label: Falling Factorial of Complex Number as Summation of Unsigned Stirling Numbers of First Kind
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number whose real part is positive. Then: $z^{\underline r} = \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^m{r \brack r - k} \paren {-1}^k z^{r - k} + \map \OO {z^{r - m - 1} }$ where: $\ds {r \brack r - k}$ denotes the extension of the unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind to the complex plane $z^{\underline r}$ denotes $z$ to the $r$ falling $\map \OO {z^{r - m - 1} }$ denotes big-$\OO$ notation.

label: Falling Factorial of Sum of Integers
snippet: Let $r \in \R$ be a real number. Let $a, b \in \Z$ be (positive) integers. Then: $r^{\underline {a + b} } = r^{\underline a} \paren {r - a}^{\underline b}$ where $r^{\underline a}$ denotes the $a$th falling factorial of $r$.

label: Faltings' Theorem
snippet: Let $C$ be a curve over $\Q$ of genus $g > 1$. Then $C$ has only finitely many rational points.

label: Family of Lipschitz Continuous Functions with same Lipschitz Constant is Uniformly Equicontinuous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ and $\struct {Y, d'}$ be metric spaces. Let $\map \CC {X, Y}$ be the set of continuous functions $X \to Y$. Let $\FF \subset \map \CC {X, Y}$ be a set of Lipschitz continuous functions all with Lipschitz constant $M \ge 0$. Then $\FF$ is uniformly equicontinuous.

label: Fan-Glicksberg-Hoffman Concave Alternative
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\R$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a convex set. Let $f_1, \ldots, f_m : C \to \R$ be concave functions. Then exactly one of the following is true: $(1): \quad$ there exists $x \in C$ such that $\map {f_i} x > 0$ for each $1 \le i \le n$ $(2): \quad$ there exists $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_n \in \R_{\ge 0}$, not all zero, such that: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_i \map {f_i} x \le 0$ for each $x \in C$.

label: Fano Plane is Unique Projective Plane of Order 2
snippet: The Fano plane is the unique finite projective plane of order $2$.

snippet: Let $D_x^k u$ denote the $k$th derivative of a function $u$ $x$. Then: $\ds D_x^n w = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n D_u^j w \sum_{\substack {\sum_{p \mathop \ge 1} k_p \mathop = j \\ \sum_{p \mathop \ge 1} p k_p \mathop = n \\ \forall p \mathop \ge 1: k_p \mathop \ge 0} } n! \prod_{m \mathop = 1}^n \dfrac {\paren {D_x^m u}^{k_m} } {k_m! \paren {m!}^{k_m} }$

label: Feit-Thompson Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == There exist no distinct prime numbers $p$ and $q$ such that: $\dfrac {p^q - 1} {p - 1}$ divides $\dfrac {q^p - 1} {q - 1}$

label: Feit-Thompson Theorem
snippet: All finite groups of odd order are solvable. That is, every non-abelian finite simple group is of even order.

label: Fermat's Last Theorem
snippet: $\forall a, b, c, n \in \Z_{>0}: n > 2$, the equation $a^n + b^n = c^n$ has no solutions.

label: Fermat's Little Theorem
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer such that $p$ is not a divisor of $n$. Then: $n^{p - 1} \equiv 1 \pmod p$

label: Fermat's Two Squares Theorem
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Then $p$ can be expressed as the sum of two squares either: $p = 2$ or: $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ The expression of a prime of the form $4 k + 1$ as the sum of two squares is unique except for the order of the two summands.

label: Fermat Number is not Cube
snippet: There exist no Fermat numbers which are cubes.

label: Fermat Prime Conjecture
snippet: == False Conjecture == All numbers of the form $2^{\paren {2^n} } + 1$, where $n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$ are prime. This was postulated by .

label: Fermat Problem
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle Let the vertices of $\triangle ABC$ all have angles less than $120 \degrees$. Let $\triangle ABG$, $\triangle BCE$ and $\triangle ACF$ be equilateral triangles constructed on the sides of $ABC$. Let $AE$, $BF$ and $CG$ be constructed. Let $P$ be the point at which $AE$, $BF$ and $CG$ meet. 500px Then $P$ is the Fermat-Torricelli point of $\triangle ABC$. If one of vertices of $\triangle ABC$ be of $120 \degrees$ or more, then that vertex is itself the Fermat-Torricelli point of $\triangle ABC$.

label: Fermat Pseudoprime/Base 3/Examples/91
snippet: The smallest Fermat pseudoprime to base $3$ is $91$: $3^{91} \equiv 3 \pmod {91}$ despite the fact that $91$ is not prime: $91 = 7 \times 13$

label: Fermat Quotient of 2 wrt p is Square iff p is 3 or 7
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. The Fermat quotient of $2$ with respect to $p$: $\map {q_p} 2 = \dfrac {2^{p - 1} - 1} p$ is a square $p = 3$ or $p = 7$.

label: Ferrari's Method
snippet: Let $P$ be the quartic equation: $a x^4 + b x^3 + c x^2 + d x + e = 0$ such that $a \ne 0$. Then $P$ has solutions: $x = \dfrac {-p \pm \sqrt {p^2 - 8 q} } 4$ where: {{eqn | l = p | r = \dfrac b a \pm \sqrt {\dfrac {b^2} {a^2} - \dfrac {4 c} a + 4 y_1} }} {{eqn | l = q | r = y_1 \mp \sqrt { {y_1}^2 - \dfrac {4 e} a} }} where $y_1$ is a real solution to the cubic: $y^3 - \dfrac c a y^2 + \paren {\dfrac {b d} {a^2} - \dfrac {4 e} a} y + \paren {\dfrac {4 c e} {a^2} - \dfrac {b^2 e} {a^3} - \dfrac {d^2} {a^2} } = 0$ Ferrari's Method is a technique for solving this quartic.

label: Feuerbach's Theorem
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. The Feuerbach circle of $\triangle ABC$ is tangent to: the incircle of $\triangle ABC$ and: the $3$ excircles of $\triangle ABC$. 800px

label: Fibonacci Number/Sequence

label: Fibonacci Number 2n equals Fibonacci Number n by Lucas Number n
snippet: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. Let $L_n$ denote the $n$th Lucas number. Then: $F_{2 n} = F_n L_n$

label: Fibonacci Number 3n in terms of Fibonacci Number n and Lucas Number 2n
snippet: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. Let $L_n$ denote the $n$th Lucas number. Then: $F_{3 n} = F_n \paren {L_{2 n} + \paren {-1}^n}$

label: Fibonacci Number as Sum of Binomial Coefficients
snippet: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. Then: {{eqn | q = \forall n \in \Z_{>0} | l = F_n | r = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{\floor {\frac {n - 1} 2} } \dbinom {n - k - 1} k | c = }} {{eqn | r = \binom {n - 1} 0 + \binom {n - 2} 1 + \binom {n - 3} 2 + \dotsb + \binom {n - j} {j - 1} + \binom {n - j - 1} j | c = where $j = \floor {\dfrac {n - 1} 2}$ }} where: $\dbinom a b$ denotes a binomial coefficient $\floor x$ denotes the floor function, which is the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$.

label: Fibonacci Number by Golden Mean plus Fibonacci Number of Index One Less
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$. Then: $\phi^n = F_n \phi + F_{n - 1}$ where: $F_n$ denotes the $n$th Fibonacci number $\phi$ denotes the golden mean.

label: Fibonacci Number by One Minus Golden Mean plus Fibonacci Number of Index One Less
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$. Then: $\hat \phi^n = F_n \hat \phi + F_{n - 1}$ where: $F_n$ denotes the $n$th Fibonacci number $\hat \phi$ denotes the $1$ minus the golden mean: $\hat \phi := 1 - \phi$

snippet: {{eqn | q = \forall n \in \Z_{\ge 0} | l = 2^{n - 1} F_n | r = \sum_k 5^k \dbinom n {2 k + 1} | c = }} where: $F_n$ denotes the $n$th Fibonacci number $\dbinom n {2 k + 1} \ $ denotes a binomial coefficient.

label: Fibonacci Number equal to Sum of Sequence of Cubes
snippet: The following Fibonacci number can be expressed as the sum of a sequence of cubes: $F_{18} = 2584 = 7^3 + 8^3 + 9^3 + 10^3$

label: Fibonacci Number greater than Golden Section to Power less Two
snippet: For all $n \in \N_{\ge 2}$: $F_n \ge \phi^{n - 2}$ where: $F_n$ is the $n$th Fibonacci number $\phi$ is the golden section: $\phi = \dfrac {1 + \sqrt 5} 2$

label: Fibonacci Number in terms of Larger Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Let $F_k$ be the $k$th Fibonacci number. Then: $\forall m, n \in \Z_{>0} : \paren {-1}^n F_{m - n} = F_m F_{n - 1} - F_{m - 1} F_n$

label: Fibonacci Number is not Product of Two Smaller Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Suppose $\size m, \size n \ge 3$. Let $F_m$ and $F_n$ be the $m$th and $n$th Fibonacci numbers. Then $F_m \times F_n$ is not a Fibonacci number.

label: Fibonacci Number less than Golden Section to Power less One
snippet: For all $n \in \N_{> 0}$: $F_n \le \phi^{n - 1}$ where: $F_n$ is the $n$th Fibonacci number $\phi$ is the golden section: $\phi = \dfrac {1 + \sqrt 5} 2$

snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $F_{2 n} \phi \bmod 1 = 1 - \phi^{-2 n}$ $F_n$ denotes the $n$th Fibonacci number $\phi$ is the golden mean: $\phi = \dfrac {1 + \sqrt 5} 2$

label: Fibonacci Number of Index 2n as Sum of Squares of Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. Then: $F_{2 n} = {F_{n + 1} }^2 - {F_{n - 1} }^2$

label: Fibonacci Number of Index 3n as Sum of Cubes of Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. Then: $F_{3 n} = {F_{n + 1} }^3 + {F_n}^3 - {F_{n - 1} }^3$

label: Fibonacci Number of Odd Index by Golden Mean Modulo 1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $F_{2 n + 1} \phi \bmod 1 = \phi^{-2 n - 1}$ where: $F_n$ denotes the $n$th Fibonacci number $\phi$ is the golden mean: $\phi = \dfrac {1 + \sqrt 5} 2$

label: Fibonacci Number plus Binomial Coefficient in terms of Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be the sequence defined as: $a_n = \begin{cases} 0 & : n = 0 \\ 1 & : n = 1 \\ a_{n - 2} + a_{n - 1} + \dbinom {n - 2} m & : n > 1 \end{cases}$ where $\dbinom {n - 2} m$ denotes a binonial coefficient. Then $\sequence {a_n}$ can be expressed in Fibonacci numbers as: $a_n = F_{m + 1} F_{n - 1} + \paren {F_{m + 2} + 1} F_n - \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^m \binom {n + m - k} k$

label: Fibonacci Number plus Constant in terms of Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Let $c$ be a number. Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be the sequence defined as: $b_n = \begin{cases} 0 & : n = 0 \\ 1 & : n = 1 \\ b_{n - 2} + b_{n - 1} + c & : n > 1 \end{cases}$ Then $\sequence {b_n}$ can be expressed in Fibonacci numbers as: $b_n = c F_{n - 1} + \paren {c + 1} F_n - c$

label: Fibonacci Number whose Index is Plus or Minus Prime p is Multiple of p
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number distinct from $5$. Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. Then either $F_{p - 1}$ or $F_{p + 1}$ (but not both) is a multiple of $p$.

label: Fibonacci Number with Negative Index
snippet: Let $F_n$ be the $n$th Fibonacci number. Then: $\forall n \in \Z_{> 0} : F_{-n} = \paren {-1}^{n + 1} F_n$

label: Fibonacci Number with Prime Index 2n+1 is Congruent to 5^n Modulo p
snippet: Let $p = 2 n + 1$ be an odd prime. Then: $F_p \equiv 5^n \pmod p$

label: Fibonacci Number with Prime Index is not necessarily Prime
snippet: Let $p \in \Z_{>0}$ be a prime number. Let $F_p$ be the $p$th Fibonacci number. Then $F_p$ is not itself necessarily prime.

label: Field Adjoined Set
snippet: Let $F$ be a field. Let $S \subseteq F$ be a subset of $F$. Let $K \le F$ be a subfield of $F$. The subring $K \sqbrk S$ of $F$ generated by $K \cup S$ is the set of all finite linear combinations of powers of elements of $S$ with coefficients in $K$. The subfield $\map K S$ of $F$ generated by $K \cup S$ is the set of all $x y^{-1} \in F$ with $a, b \in K \sqbrk S$, $b \ne 0$. $\map K S$ is isomorphic to the field of quotients $Q$ of $K \sqbrk S$.

label: Field Norm of Complex Number Equals Field Norm
snippet: Let $z = a + i b$ be a complex number, where $a, b \in \R$. Then the field norm of $z$ is the field norm with respect to the field extension $\C / \R$.

label: Field Norm of Complex Number is Multiplicative Function
snippet: Let $\C$ denote the set of complex numbers. Let $N: \C \to \R_{\ge 0}$ denote the field norm on complex numbers: $\forall z \in \C: \map N z = \cmod z^2$ where $\cmod z$ denotes the complex modulus of $z$. Then $N$ is a multiplicative function on $\C$.

label: Field Norm of Complex Number is Positive Definite
snippet: Let $\C$ denote the set of complex numbers. Let $N: \C \to \R_{\ge 0}$ denote the field norm on complex numbers: $\forall z \in \C: \map N z = \cmod z^2$ where $\cmod z$ denotes the complex modulus of $z$. Then $N$ is positive definite on $\C$.

label: Field Norm of Complex Number is not Norm
snippet: Let $\C$ denote the set of complex numbers. Let $N: \C \to \R_{\ge 0}$ denote the field norm on complex numbers: $\forall z \in \C: \map N z = \cmod z^2$ where $\cmod z$ denotes the complex modulus of $z$. Then $N$ is not a norm on $\C$.

label: Field Norm of Quaternion is Multiplicative
snippet: Let $\mathbf x$ be a quaternion. Let $\overline {\mathbf x}$ be the conjugate of $\mathbf x$. The field norm of $\mathbf x$: $\map n {\mathbf x} := \size {\mathbf x \overline {\mathbf x} }$ is a multiplicative function.

label: Field Norm of Quaternion is Positive Definite
snippet: Let $\mathbf x = a \mathbf 1 + b \mathbf i + c \mathbf j + d \mathbf k$ be a quaternion. Let $\overline {\mathbf x}$ be the conjugate of $\mathbf x$. The field norm of $\mathbf x$: $\map n {\mathbf x} := \cmod {\mathbf x \overline {\mathbf x} }$ is positive definite.

The field norm of $\mathbf x$: $\map n {\mathbf x} := \size {\mathbf x \overline {\mathbf x} }$ is not a norm in the abstract algebraic context of a division ring.

label: Field from Barycentric Charge Distribution
snippet: Let $\map \rho r$ be a barycentric charge density within space and centered at $\CC$ where $r$ is the distance from $\CC$. label: Field has Prime Characteristic p iff exists Monomorphism from Field of Integers Modulo p
snippet: Let $F$ be a field. Then: there exists some prime number $p$ such that $\Char F = p$ there exists a field monomorphism $\phi: \Z_p \to F$ where: $\Char F$ denotes the characteristic of $F$. $\Z_p$ denotes the field of integers modulo $p$.

label: Field has no Proper Zero Divisors
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$. Then $\struct {F, +, \times}$ has no proper zero divisors. That is: $a \times b = 0_F \implies a = 0_F \lor b = 0_F$

label: Field is Galois over Fixed Field of Automorphism Group
snippet: Let $E/F$ be a finite field extension. Let $K = \operatorname{Fix}_E(\operatorname{Aut}(E/F))$ be the fixed field of the automorphism group of $E/F$. Then $E/K$ is Galois.

label: Field of Characteristic Zero has Unique Prime Subfield
snippet: Let $F$ be a field, whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$, with characteristic zero. Then there exists a unique $P \subseteq F$ such that: $(1): \quad P$ is a subfield of $F$ $(2): \quad P$ is isomorphic to the field of rational numbers $\struct {\Q, +, \times}$. That is, $P \cong \Q$ is a unique minimal subfield of $F$, and all other subfields of $F$ contain $P$. This field $P$ is called the prime subfield of $F$.

label: Field of Integers Modulo Prime is Prime Field
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Z_p, +, \times}$‎ be the field of integers modulo $p$. Then $\struct {\Z_p, +, \times}$‎ is a prime field.

label: Field of Prime Characteristic has Unique Prime Subfield
snippet: Let $F$ be a field whose characteristic is $p$. Then there exists a unique $P \subseteq F$ such that: $(1): \quad P$ is a subfield of $F$ $(2): \quad P \cong \Z_p$. That is, $P \cong \Z_p$ is a unique minimal subfield of $F$, and all other subfields of $F$ contain $P$. This field $P$ is called the prime subfield of $F$.

label: Field of Quotients of Ring of Polynomial Forms on Reals that yields Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, +, \times}$ denote the field of real numbers. Let $X$ be transcendental over $\R$. Let $\R \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials in $X$ over $F$. Consider the field of quotients: $\R \sqbrk X / \ideal p$ where: $p = X^2 + 1$ $\ideal p$ denotes the ideal generated by $p$. Then $\R \sqbrk X / \ideal p$ is the field of complex numbers.

label: Field of Uncountable Cardinality K has Transcendence Degree K
snippet: Let $F$ be a field of uncountable cardinality $\kappa$. Then $F$ has transcendence degree $\kappa$ over its prime field.

label: Field with 4 Elements has only Order 2 Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {\GF, +, \times}$ be a field which has exactly $4$ elements. Then: $\forall a \in \GF: a + a = 0_\GF$ where $0_\GF$ is the zero of $\GF$.

label: Fifth Apotome/Example
snippet: == Example of Fifth Apotome== Let $a, b \in \set {x \in \R_{>0} : x^2 \in \Q}$ be two rationally expressible numbers such that $a - b$ is an apotome. By definition, $a - b$ is a fifth apotome : $(1): \quad b \in \Q$ $(2): \quad \dfrac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2}} a \notin \Q$ where $\Q$ denotes the set of rational numbers. Let $a = \sqrt {13}$ and $b = 3$. Then: {{eqn | l = \frac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } a | r = \frac {\sqrt {13 - 9} } {\sqrt {13} } }} {{eqn | r = \sqrt {\frac 4 {13} } | rr= \notin \Q }} Therefore $\sqrt {13} - 3$ is a fifth apotome. Category:Examples of Apotome

label: Fifth Power of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z = a + i b$ be a complex number. Then its fifth power is given by: $z^5 = a^5 - 10 a^3 b^2 + 5 a b^4 + i \paren {5 a^4 b - 10 a^2 b^3 + b^5}$

label: Fifth Sylow Theorem
snippet: The number of Sylow $p$-subgroups of a finite group is a divisor of their common index.

label: Filter Basis Generates Filter
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Let $\BB \subset \powerset S$. Then: $\FF = \set {V \subseteq S: \exists U \in \BB: U \subseteq V}$ is a filter on $S$ $(1): \quad \forall V_1, V_2 \in \BB: \exists U \in \BB: U \subseteq V_1 \cap V_2$ $(2): \quad \O \notin \BB, \BB \ne \O$ That is, $\BB$ is a filter basis of the filter $\FF$, which is generated by $\BB$.

label: Filter Generated by Net Converges iff Net Converges
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ be a directed set. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be a net. Let $\FF$ be the filter generated by $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$. Let $x \in X$. Then $\FF$ converges to $x$ $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ converges to $x$.

label: Filter Generated by Net is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ be a directed set. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be a net. Then the filter generated by $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ is well-defined.

label: Filter Generated by Subnet is Finer than Filter Generated by Net
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ and $\struct {A, \sqsubseteq}$ be directed sets. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be a net. Let $\FF$ be the filter generated by $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$. Let $\family {x_{\map \lambda \alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ be a subnet of $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$. Let $\widetilde \FF$ be the filter generated by $\family {x_{\lambda_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$. Then $\widetilde \FF$ is finer than $\FF$.

label: Filter Property of Dirac Delta Function
snippet: Let $\map \delta x$ denote the Dirac delta function. Let $g$ be a continuous real function. Then: $\ds \int_{-\infty}^{+ \infty} \map {\delta} {x - s} \map g x \rd x = \map g s$

label: Filter is Finer iff Sets of Basis are Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\powerset S$ denote the power set of $S$. Let $\FF, \FF' \subset \powerset S$ be two filters on $S$. Let $\FF$ have a basis $\BB$. Let $\FF'$ have a basis $\BB'$. $\FF$ is finer than $\FF'$ for every set of $\BB'$, there is a set of $\BB$ subset to it.

label: Filter is Ideal in Dual Ordered Set
snippet: Let $P = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X$ is filter in $P$ $X$ is ideal in $P^{-1}$ where $P^{-1} = \struct {S, \succeq}$ denotes the dual of $P$.

label: Filter on Product Space Converges iff Projections Converge
snippet: Let $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of non-empty topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\ds X := \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ be the corresponding product space. Let $\pr_i: X \to X_i$ denote the projection from $X$ onto $X_i$. Let $\FF \subset \powerset X$ be a filter on $X$. Then $\FF$ converges for all $i \in I$ the image filter $\map {\pr_i} \FF$ converges.

label: Filter on Product Space Converges to Point iff Projections Converge to Projections of Point
snippet: Let $\family{X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of non-empty topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\ds X := \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ be the corresponding product space. Let $\FF$ be a filter on $X$. Let $x \in X$. Let $\pr_i: X \to X_i$ denote the projection from $X$ onto $X_i$. Then $\FF$ converges to $x$ : for all $i \in I$ the image filter $\map {\pr_i} \FF$ converges to $x_i := \map {\pr_i} x$.

label: Filter on Product of Hausdorff Spaces Converges iff Projections Converge
snippet: Let $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of non-empty Hausdorff spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\ds X := \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ be the corresponding product space. Let $\pr_i: X \to X_i$ denote the projection from $X$ onto $X_i$. Let $\FF \subset \powerset X$ be a filter on $X$. Then $\FF$ converges for each $i \in I$ the image filter $\map {\pr_i} \FF$ converges.

label: Filter on Set/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Filters on Sets ==

label: Filter on Set is Proper Filter
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\powerset S$ denote the power set of $S$. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ be the poset defined on $\powerset S$ by the subset relation. Let $\FF$ be a filter on $S$. Then $\FF$ is a proper filter on $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$.

label: Filtered iff Finite Subsets have Lower Bounds
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \precsim}$ be a preordered set. Let $H$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $H$ is filtered : for every finite subset $A$ of $H$: $\exists h \in H: \forall a \in A: h \precsim a$

label: Filtered iff Upper Closure Filtered
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \precsim}$ be a preordered set. Let $H$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $H$ is filtered $H^\succsim$ is filtered where $H^\succsim$ denotes the upper closure of $H$.

label: Filtered in Meet Semilattice with Finite Infima
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a meet semilattice. Let $H$ be a non-empty upper section of $S$. Then $H$ is filtered for every non-empty finite subset $A$ of $H$, $\inf A \in H$

label: Filters equal Ideals in Dual Ordered Set
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S, \preceq_1}$ be an ordered set. Let $L_2 = \struct {S, \preceq_2}$ be a dual ordered set of $L_1$. Then $\map {\mathit {Filt} } {L_1} = \map {\mathit {Ids} } {L_2}$ where $\map {\mathit {Filt} } {L_1}$ denotes the set of all filters of $L_1$, $\map {\mathit {Ids} } {L_2}$ denotes the set of all ideals of $L_2$.

label: Filters form Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \wedge, \preceq}\right)$ be a bounded above meet semilattice. Let $F = \left({\mathit{Filt}\left({L}\right), \subseteq}\right)$ be an inclusion ordered set, where $\mathit{Filt}\left({L}\right)$ denotes set of all filters on $L$. Then $F$ is a complete lattice.

label: Filters of Lattice of Power Set form Bounded Above Ordered Set
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $L = \struct {\powerset X, \cup, \cap, \subseteq}$ be an inclusion lattice of power set of $X$. Let $F = \struct {\map {\operatorname{Filt} } L, \subseteq}$ be an inclusion ordered set, where $\map {\operatorname{Filt} } L$ denotes the set of all filters on $L$. Then $F$ is bounded above and $\top_F = \powerset X$ where $\top_F$ denotes the greatest element of $F$.

label: Filters of Lattice of Power Set form Bounded Below Ordered Set
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $L = \struct {\powerset X, \cup, \cap, \subseteq}$ be an inclusion lattice of power set of $X$. Let $F = \struct {\map {\operatorname {Filt} } L, \subseteq}$ be an inclusion ordered set, where $\map {\operatorname {Filt} } L$ denotes the set of all filters on $L$. Then $F$ is bounded below and $\bot_F = \set X$ where $\bot_F$ denotes the smallest element of $F$.

label: Filtration's Lp Spaces are Dense in Limit Filtration's Lp Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a filtration of $\Sigma$. Let $\FF_\infty$ be the limit of $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Let $p \ge 1$. Let $\map {L^p} {\cdot}$ denote the $L^p$ spaces. Then $\ds \bigcup_{n \mathop \ge 0} \map {L^p} {X, \FF_n, \mu}$ is a dense subset of $\map {L^p} {X, \FF_\infty, \mu}$.

label: Final Topology Contains Codomain Topology iff Mappings are Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct{Y, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\family {\struct{X_i, \tau_i}}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces. Let $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of mappings $f_i : X_i \to Y$. Let $\tau'$ be the final topology on $Y$ with respect to $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Then: $\tau \subseteq \tau'$ $\forall i \in I : f_i: \struct{X_i, \tau_i} \to \struct{Y, \tau}$ is continuous.

label: Final Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {\struct {Y_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of topological spaces. Let $\family {f_i: Y_i \to X}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of mappings. Let $\tau$ be the final topology on $X$ with respect to $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Then $\tau$ is a topology on $X$.

label: Final Topology with respect to Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau_X}$ be a topological space. Let $Y$ be a set. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping. Let $\tau_Y$ be the final topology on $Y$ $f$. Then: $\tau_Y = \set {U \subseteq Y : f^{-1} \sqbrk U \in \tau_X}$ Observe that the set on the of the equality is sometimes denoted $f\tau$. Further, the following holds true: $\forall \struct {Z, \tau_Z}$ topological space $\forall g: \struct {Y, f \tau} \to \struct {Z, \tau_Z}$ mapping $g$ is continuous $\iff g \circ f$ is continuous (where $f$ is defined from $\struct {X, \tau_X}$ to $\struct {Y, f \tau}$).

label: Final Value Theorem of Laplace Transform
snippet: Let $\laptrans {\map f t} = \map F s$ denote the Laplace transform of the real function $f$. Then: $\ds \lim_{t \mathop \to \infty} \map f t = \lim_{s \mathop \to 0} s \, \map F s$ if those limits exist.

label: Finding Center of Circle
snippet: For any given circle, it is possible to find its center.

label: Finer Supremum Precedes Supremum
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}\right)$ be a complete lattice. Let $X, Y$ be subsets of $S$ such that $X$ is finer than $Y$. Then $\sup X \preceq \sup Y$ where $\sup X$ denotes the supremum of $X$.

label: Finished Set Lemma
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\Delta$ be a finished set of WFFs of propositional logic. Then any model of the set of basic WFFs in $\Delta$ is a model of $\Delta$.

label: Finite-Dimensional Subspace of Hausdorff Topological Vector Space is Closed
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Hausdorff topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $n \in \N$. Let $Y$ be a subspace of $X$ with dimension $n$. Then $Y$ is closed.

label: Finite Abelian Group is Solvable
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. Then $G$ is solvable.

label: Finite Boolean Lattice is a Locale
snippet: Let $\struct{B, \vee, \wedge, \neg, \preceq}$ be a finite Boolean lattice. Then: $\struct{B, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ is a locale.

label: Finite Cardinals form Infinite Set
snippet: The finite cardinals form a set which is infinite.

label: Finite Cartesian Product of Non-Empty Sets is Non-Empty
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n$ be non-empty sets. Then their cartesian product $S_1 \times S_2 \times \cdots \times S_n$ is non-empty.

label: Finite Chain is Order-Isomorphic to Finite Ordinal
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $C$ be a finite chain in $S$. Then for some finite ordinal $\mathbf n$: $\struct {C, {\preceq \restriction_C} }$ is order-isomorphic to $\mathbf n$. That is: $\struct {C, {\preceq \restriction_C} }$ is order-isomorphic to $\N_n$ where $\N_n$ is the initial segment of $\N$ determined by $n$: $\N_n = \set {k \in \N: k < n} = \set {0, 1, \ldots, n - 1}$

label: Finite Character for Sets of Mappings
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\FF$ be a set of mappings from subsets of $S$ to $T$. That is, let $\FF$ be a set of partial mappings from $S$ to $T$. Then the following are equivalent:

label: Finite Class is Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a finite class. Then $A$ is a set.

label: Finite Complement Space is T0
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on any set $S$ which contains at least two points. Then $T$ is a $T_0$ space.

label: Finite Complement Space is T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on any set $S$ which contains at least two points. Then $T$ is a $T_1$ space.

label: Finite Complement Space is not T2
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the finite complement topology on an infinite set $S$. Then $T$ is not a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

label: Finite Complement Space is not T3
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on an infinite set $S$. Then $T$ is not a $T_3$ space.

label: Finite Complement Topology is Minimal T1 Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement space. Let $\tau'$ be a topology on $S$ such that $T' = \struct {S, \tau'}$ is a $T_1$ space. Then $\tau$ is comparable with $\tau'$ such that $\tau$ is coarser than $\tau'$. That is, of all the topologies on $S$ fulfilling the $T_1$ separation axiom, the finite complement space is the smallest. Thus the finite complement topology is known as the minimal $T_1$ topology on any given set.

label: Finite Complement Topology is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on an infinite set $S$. Then $T$ is a separable space.

label: Finite Connected Simple Graph is Tree iff Size is One Less than Order
snippet: Let $T$ be a finite connected simple graph of order $n$. Then $T$ is a (finite) tree the size of $T$ is $n - 1$.

label: Finite Cover is Locally Finite
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a finite cover for a set $S$. Then $\CC$ is also a locally finite cover for $S$.

label: Finite Cover is Star-Finite
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\CC$ be a finite cover for $T$. Then $\CC$ is star-finite.

label: Finite Cyclic Group has Euler Phi Generators
snippet: Let $C_n$ be a (finite) cyclic group of order $n$. Then $C_n$ has $\map \phi n$ generators, where $\map \phi n$ denotes the Euler $\phi$ function.

label: Finite Cyclic Group is Isomorphic to Integers under Modulo Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a finite group whose identity element is $e$. Then $\struct {G, \circ}$ is cyclic of order $n$ $\struct {G, \circ}$ is isomorphic with the additive group of integers modulo $n$ $\struct {\Z_n, +_n}$.

label: Finite Dimensional Subspace of Normed Vector Space is Closed
snippet: Let $V$ be a normed vector space. Let $W$ be a finite dimensional subspace of $V$. And the ground field $K$ is complete. Then $W$ is closed.

label: Finite Field Extension has Finite Galois Group
snippet: Let $E / F$ be a finite field extension. Then its Galois group is finite.

label: Finite Fourier Series
snippet: Let $\map a n$ be any finite periodic real function on $\Z$ with period $b$. Let $\xi = e^{2 \pi i/ b}$ be the first $b$th root of unity. Then: $\ds \map a n = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{b - 1} \map {a_*} k \xi^{n k}$ where: $\ds \map {a_*} n = \frac 1 b \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{b - 1} \map a k \xi^{-n k}$

label: Finite Generalized Sum Converges to Summation
snippet: Let $G$ be a commutative topological semigroup with identity $0_G$. Let $\set{i_0, i_1, \ldots, i_n}$ be a finite enumeration of a finite set $I$. Let $\family{g_i}_{i \in I}$ be an indexed family of elements of $G$. Then: the generalized sum $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i$ converges to: the summation over finite index $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i$

label: Finite Group has Composition Series
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Then $G$ has a composition series.

label: Finite Group is p-Group iff Order is Power of p
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $G$ be a finite group. Then $G$ is a $p$-group the order of $G$ is a power of $p$.

label: Finite Group whose Subsets form Chain is Cyclic P-Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $G$ be such that its subgroups form a chain. Then $G$ is a cyclic $p$-group.

label: Finite Group with 2 Conjugacy Classes has 2 Elements
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $G$ have exactly $2$ conjugacy classes. Then $G$ has exactly $2$ elements.

label: Finite Group with One Sylow p-Subgroup per Prime Divisor is Isomorphic to Direct Product
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group whose order is $n$ and whose identity element is $e$. Let $G$ be such that it has exactly $1$ Sylow $p$-subgroup for each prime divisor of $n$. Then $G$ is isomorphic to the internal direct product of all its Sylow $p$-subgroups.

label: Finite Hausdorff Measure Implies Zero Higher Dimensional Measure
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $F \subseteq \R^n$ be a subset of the real Euclidean space. Let $s \in \R_{\ge 0}$. Let $\map {\HH^s} \cdot$ denote the $s$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Then: $\map {\HH^s} F s} : \map {\HH^t} F = 0$

label: Finite Infima Set and Upper Closure is Filter
snippet: Let $P = \struct {S, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a meet semilattice. Let $X$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $\map {\operatorname {fininfs} } X^\succeq$ is filter in $P$. where $\map {\operatorname {fininfs} } X$ denotes the finite infima set of $X$, $X^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $X$.

label: Finite Infima Set and Upper Closure is Smallest Filter
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a meet semilattice. Let $X$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $X \subseteq \map {\operatorname {fininfs} } X^\succeq$ and for every a filter $F$ in $L$: $\paren {X \subseteq F \implies \map {\operatorname {fininfs} } X^\succeq \subseteq F}$ where $\map {\operatorname {fininfs} } X$ denotes the finite infima set of $X$, $X^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $X$.

label: Finite Infima Set of Coarser Subset is Coarser than Finite Infima Set
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a meet semilattice. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$ such that $A$ is coarser than $B$. Then $\map {\operatorname{fininfs} } A$ is coarser than $\map {\operatorname{fininfs} } B$ where $\map {\operatorname{fininfs} } B$ denotes the finite infima set of $B$.

label: Finite Integral Domain is Galois Field
snippet: A finite integral domain is a Galois field.

label: Finite Intersection of Absorbing Sets is Absorbing
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A_1, \ldots, A_n \subseteq X$ be absorbing sets. Then: $\ds \bigcap_{j \mathop = 1}^n A_j$ is absorbing.

label: Finite Intersection of Open Sets of Metric Space is Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n$ be open sets in $M$. Then $\ds U = \bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n U_i$ is open in $M$. That is, a finite intersection of open subsets is open.

label: Finite Intersection of Regular Open Sets is Regular Open
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $n \in \N$. Suppose that: $\forall i \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, n}: H_i \subseteq T$ where all the $H_i$ are regular open in $T$. That is: $\forall i \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, n}: H_i = H_i^{- \circ}$ where $H_i^{- \circ}$ denotes the interior of the closure of $H_i$. Then $\ds \bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i$ is regular open in $T$. That is: $\ds \bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i = \paren {\bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i}^{- \circ}$

label: Finite Lexicographic Order on Well-Ordered Sets is Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set which is well-ordered by $\preccurlyeq$. Let $\preccurlyeq_l$ be the lexicographic order on the set $T_n$ of all ordered $n$-tuples of $S$: $\tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} \prec \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n}$ : $\exists k: 1 \le k \le n$ such that $\forall 1 \le j 0}$, $\preccurlyeq_l$ is a well-ordering on $T_n$.

label: Finite Monoid with Left Cancellable Operation is Group
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a finite monoid. Let $\circ$ be a left cancellable operation. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group.

label: Finite Monoid with Right Cancellable Operation is Group
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a finite monoid. Let $\circ$ be a right cancellable operation. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group.

label: Finite Multiplicative Subgroup of Field is Cyclic
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field. Let $\struct {F^*, \times}$ denote the multiplicative group of $F$. Let $C$ be a finite subgroup of $\struct {F^*, \times}$. Then $C$ is cyclic.

label: Finite Non-Empty Subset of Ordered Set has Maximal and Minimal Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a finite, non-empty subset of $S$. Then $T$ has a maximal element and a minimal element.

label: Finite Number of Groups of Given Finite Order
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then there exists a finite number of types of group of order $n$.

label: Finite Order Elements of Infinite Abelian Group form Normal Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be an infinite abelian group. Let $H \subseteq G$ be the subset of $G$ defined as: $H := \set {x \in G: x \text { is of finite order in } G}$ Then $H$ forms a normal subgroup of $G$.

label: Finite Ordinal is equal to Natural Number
snippet: Let $n$ be an element of the minimally inductive set. Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then: $n \sim x \implies n = x$

label: Finite Ordinal is not Subset of one of its Elements
snippet: Let $n$ be a finite ordinal. Then: $\nexists x \in n: n \subseteq x$ that is, $n$ is not a subset of one of its elements.

label: Finite Particular Point Space is Weakly Countably Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a finite particular point space. Then $T$ is weakly countably compact.

label: Finite Product Space is Connected iff Factors are Connected
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}, T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}, \dotsc, T_n = \struct {S_n, \tau_n}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \ds \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n T_i$ be the product space of $T_1, T_2, \ldots, T_n$. Then $T$ is connected each of $T_1, T_2, \ldots, T_n$ are connected.

label: Finite Product of Finite Sets is Finite
snippet: Let $\sequence {S_n}$ be a sequence of finite sets. Let $\ds \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n S_k$ be their Cartesian product. Then $\ds \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n S_k$ is also a finite set.

label: Finite Product of Sigma-Compact Spaces is Sigma-Compact
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\set {\struct {S_i, \tau_i}: 1 \le i \le n}$ be a finite set of topological spaces. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \struct {S_i, \tau_i}$ be the product space of $\set {\struct {S_i, \tau_i}: 1 \le i \le n}$. Let each of $\struct {S_i, \tau_i}$ be $\sigma$-compact. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also $\sigma$-compact.

label: Finite Product of Weakly Locally Compact Spaces is Weakly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\set {\struct {S_i, \tau_i}: 1 \le i \le n}$ be a finite set of topological spaces. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \struct {S_i, \tau_i}$ be the product space of $\set {\struct {S_i, \tau_i}: 1 \le i \le n}$. Let each of $\struct {S_i, \tau_i}$ be weakly locally compact. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also weakly locally compact.

label: Finite Rank Operator is Compact
snippet: Let $H, K$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $T \in \map {B_{00} } {H, K}$ be a bounded finite rank operator. Then $T \in \map {B_0} {H, K}$, that is, $T$ is compact.

label: Finite Rank Operators Dense in Compact Linear Transformations
snippet: Let $H, K$ be Hilbert spaces. Then: $\map {B_{00} } {H, K}$ is everywhere dense in $\map {B_0} {H, K}$ where: $\map {B_{00} } {H, K}$ is the space of continuous finite rank operators from $H$ to $K$ $\map {B_0} {H, K}$ is the space of compact linear transformations from $H$ to $K$. That is, for every $T \in \map {B_0} {H, K}$, there is a sequence $\sequence {T_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ in $\map {B_{00} } {H, K}$ such that: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \norm {T_n - T} = 0$ where $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the norm on bounded linear transformations.

label: Finite Ring with No Proper Zero Divisors is Field
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a finite non-null ring with no proper zero divisors. Then $R$ is a field.

label: Finite Semigroup Equal Elements for Different Powers
snippet: Let $\left({S, \circ}\right)$ be a finite semigroup. Then: $\forall x \in S: \exists m, n \in \N: m \ne n: x^m = x^n$

label: Finite Sequences in Set Form Acyclic Graph
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $V$ be the set of finite sequences in $S$. Let $E$ be the set of unordered pairs $\set {p, q}$ of elements of $V$ such that either: $q$ is formed by extending $p$ by one element or $p$ is formed by extending $q$ by one element. That is: $\card {\Dom p \symdif \Dom q} = 1$, where $\symdif$ is symmetric difference $p \restriction D = q \restriction D$, where $D = \Dom p \cap \Dom q$ Then $T = \struct{V, E}$ is an acyclic graph.

label: Finite Set Contains Subset of Smaller Cardinality
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite sets. Let $\size S = n$ where $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes cardinality. Let $0 \le m \le n$. Then there exists a subset $X \subseteq S$ such that: $\size X = m$

label: Finite Set Formed by Substitution has Larger Intersection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. Let $x \in S \setminus T$. Let $y \in T \setminus S$. Let $R$ be the set formed by substituting $x$ for $y$ in $T$, that is: $R = \paren{T \setminus \set y} \cup \set x$ Then: $\card{R \cap S} = \card{T \cap S} + 1$

label: Finite Set Formed by Substitution has Same Cardinality
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. Let $x \in S \setminus T$. Let $y \in T \setminus S$. Let $R$ be the set formed by substituting $x$ for $y$ in $T$, that is: $R = \paren{T \setminus \set y} \cup \set x$ Then: $\card R = \card T$

label: Finite Set of Continuous Functions between Metric Spaces is Pointwise Equicontinuous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ and $\struct {Y, d'}$ be metric spaces. Let $\map \CC {X, Y}$ be the set of continuous functions $X \to Y$. Let $\FF = \set {f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_n}$ be a finite subset of $\map \CC {X, Y}$. Then $\FF$ is pointwise equicontinuous.

label: Finite Set of Elements in Principal Ideal Domain has GCD
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be a principal ideal domain. Let $a_1, a_2, \dotsc, a_n$ be non-zero elements of $D$. Then $a_1, a_2, \dotsc, a_n$ all have a greatest common divisor.

label: Finite Signed Measure is Complex Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a finite signed measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Then $\mu$ is a complex measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$.

label: Finite Space Satisfies All Compactness Properties
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space where $S$ is a finite set. Then $T$ satisfies the following compactness properties: $T$ is compact. $T$ is sequentially compact. $T$ is countably compact. $T$ is weakly countably compact. $T$ is a Lindelöf space. $T$ is pseudocompact. $T$ is $\sigma$-compact. $T$ is strongly locally compact. $T$ is $\sigma$-locally compact. $T$ is weakly $\sigma$-locally compact. $T$ is locally compact. $T$ is weakly locally compact. $T$ is paracompact. $T$ is countably paracompact. $T$ is metacompact. $T$ is countably metacompact.

label: Finite Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space where $S$ is a finite set. Then $T$ is a second-countable space.

label: Finite Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space where $S$ is a finite set. Then $T$ is sequentially compact.

label: Finite State Machine is Turing Computable
snippet: Let $F = \tuple {S, A, I, \Sigma, T}$ be a finite state machine. Then there exists a Turing machine $T$ that: Has input language $\Sigma$. Accepts exactly the same language as $F$. Halts on every input.

label: Finite Subgroup Test
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H$ be a non-empty finite subset of $G$. Then: $H$ is a subgroup of $G$ $\forall a, b \in H: a \circ b \in H$ That is, a non-empty finite subset of $G$ is a subgroup it is closed.

label: Finite Submodule of Function Space
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $R$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +, \circ}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $S$ be a set. Let $G^S$ the set of all mappings $f: S \to G$. Let $G^{\paren S}$ be the set of all mappings $f: S \to G$ such that $\map f x = e$ for all but finitely many elements $x$ of $S$. Then: $\struct {G^{\paren S}, +', \circ}_R$ is a submodule of $\struct {G^S, +, \circ}_R$ where $+'$ is the operation induced on $G^{\paren S}$ by $+$.

label: Finite Subset Bounds Element of Finite Infima Set and Upper Closure
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \wedge, \preceq}$ be meet semilattice. Let $F$ be filter in $L$. Let $X$ be non empty finite subset of $S$. Let $x \in S$ such that $x \in \paren {\map {\operatorname{fininfs} } {F \cup X} }^\succeq$ where $\operatorname{fininfs}$ denotes the finite infima set $X^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $X$. Then there exists $a \in S$: $a \in F \land x \succeq a \wedge \inf X$

label: Finite Subset of Metric Space has no Limit Points
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $X \subseteq A$ such that $X$ is finite. Then $X$ has no limit points.

label: Finite Subset of Metric Space is Closed
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $S \subseteq A$ be finite. Then $S$ is closed in $M$.

label: Finite Subset of Normed Vector Space is Closed
snippet: Let $M = \struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $F \subseteq X$ be finite. Then $F$ is closed in $M$.

label: Finite Subset of Topological Vector Space is von Neumann-Bounded
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $F$ be a finite subset of $X$. Then $F$ is von Neumann-bounded.

label: Finite Subsets form Directed Ordering
snippet: Let $I$ be a set. Denote with $\FF$ the set of finite subsets of $I$. Let $\subseteq$ be the subset relation on $\FF$. Then $\subseteq$ is a directed ordering on $\FF$.

label: Finite Subsets form Directed Set
snippet: Let $I$ be a set. Denote with $\FF$ the set of finite subsets of $I$. Let $\subseteq$ be the subset relation on $\FF$. Then $\struct {\FF, \subseteq}$ is a directed set.

label: Finite Subsets form Ideal
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\map {\operatorname {Fin} } X$ be the set of all finite subsets of $X$. Then $\map {\operatorname {Fin} } X$ is ideal in $\struct {\powerset X, \subseteq}$ where $\powerset X$ denotes the power set of $X$.

label: Finite Subspace of Dense-in-itself Metric Space is not Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space that is dense-in-itself. Let $U$ be a finite subset of $A$. Then $U$ is not an open set of $M$.

label: Finite Summation does not Change under Permutation
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $f: S \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $\sigma: S \to S$ be a permutation. Then we have the equality of summations over finite sets: $\ds \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \map f s = \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \map f {\map \sigma s}$

label: Finite Suprema Set and Lower Closure is Ideal
snippet: Let $P = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice. Let $X$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $\map {\operatorname{finsups} } X^\preceq$ is ideal in $P$. where $\map {\operatorname{finsups} } X$ denotes the finite suprema set of $X$, $X^\preceq$ denotes the lower closure of $X$.

label: Finite Suprema Set and Lower Closure is Smallest Ideal
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X \subseteq \map {\operatorname {finsups} } X^\preceq$ and for every ideal $I$ in $L$: $X \subseteq I \implies \map {\operatorname {finsups} } X^\preceq \subseteq I$ where $\map {\operatorname {finsups} } X$ denotes the finite suprema set of $X$, $X^\preceq$ denotes the lower closure of $X$.

label: Finite Supremum of Family of Seminorms is Seminorm
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $\PP$ be a set of seminorms on $X$ such that: $\ds \sup_{p \in \PP} \map p x < \infty$ for each $x \in X$. Define $q : X \to \R$ by: $\ds \map q x = \sup_{p \in \PP} \map p x$ for each $x \in X$. Then $q$ is a seminorm on $X$.

label: Finite Symmetric Group is Ambivalent
snippet: Let $n$ be a natural number. Let $S_n$ be a symmetric group of order $n$. Then $S_n$ is ambivalent.

label: Finite T1 Space is Discrete
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_1$ space. Then $\tau$ is the discrete topology on $S$.

label: Finite Topological Space is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space where $S$ is a finite set. Then $T$ is compact.

label: Finite Totally Ordered Set is Well-Ordered
snippet: Every finite totally ordered set is well-ordered.

label: Finite Tree has Leaf Nodes
snippet: Every non-edgeless finite tree has at least two leaf nodes.

label: Finite Union of Bounded Subsets
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Then the union of any finite number of bounded subsets of $M$ is itself bounded.

label: Finite Union of Closed Sets is Closed
Finite Union of Compact Sets is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $\sequence {U_i}_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop \le n}$ be a finite sequence of compact subsets of $T$. Let $\UU_n := \ds \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n U_i$ be the union of $\sequence {U_i}$. Then $\UU_n$ is compact in $T$.

label: Finite Union of Countable Sets is Countable
snippet: The union of a finite number of countable sets is countable.

label: Finite Union of Dilations of Balanced Set
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \ldots, \lambda_n$ be real numbers. Let $W$ be a balanced set. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_i W = \lambda W$ where $\lambda \in \set {\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \ldots, \lambda_n}$ is picked so that $\cmod \lambda$ is maximized.

label: Finite Union of Pointwise Equicontinuous Families of Functions is Pointwise Equicontinuous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d_X}$ and $\struct {Y, d_Y}$ be metric spaces. Let $n \in \N$. Let $\FF_1, \ldots, \FF_n$ be pointwise equicontinuous families of functions $X \to Y$. Let: $\ds \FF = \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^n \FF_j$ Then $\FF$ is pointwise equicontinuous.

label: Finite Union of Regular Closed Sets is Regular Closed
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $n \in \N$. Suppose that: $\forall i \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, n}: H_i \subseteq T$ where all the $H_i$ are regular closed in $T$. That is: $\forall i \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, n}: H_i = H_i^{\circ -}$ where $H_i^{\circ -}$ denotes the closure of the interior of $H_i$ Then $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i$ is regular closed in $T$. That is: $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i = \paren {\bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i}^{\circ -}$

label: Finite Weight Space has Basis equal to Image of Mapping of Intersections
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space with finite weight. Then there exist a basis $\BB$ of $T$ and a mapping $f:X \to \tau$ such that: $\BB = \Img f$ and $\forall x \in X: \paren {x \in \map f x \land \forall U \in \tau: x \in U \implies \map f x \subseteq U}$ where $\Img f$ denotes the image of $f$.

label: Finite iff Cardinality Less than Aleph Zero
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Then $X$ is finite $\card X < \aleph_0$ where: $\card X$ denotes the cardinality of $X$ $\aleph_0 = \card \N$ by Aleph Zero equals Cardinality of Naturals.

label: Finitely Generated Vector Space has Finite Basis
snippet: Let $K$ be a division ring. Let $V$ be a finitely generated vector space over $K$. Then $V$ has a finite basis.

label: Finitely Satisfiable Set of Sentences has Maximal Finitely Satisfiable Extension
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a language of predicate logic. Let $\FF$ be a finitely satisfiable set of $\LL$-sentences. Then there exists a finitely satisfiable set of $\LL$-sentences $\FF' \supseteq \FF$ such that: For all $\LL$-sentences $\phi$, either $\phi \in \FF'$ or $\sqbrk {\neg \phi} \in \FF'$

label: Finitely Satisfiable Theory has Maximal Finitely Satisfiable Extension
snippet: Let $T$ be a finitely satisfiable $\LL$-theory. Then there exists a finitely satisfiable $\LL$-theory $T'$ which contains $T$ as a subset such that: for all $\LL$-sentences $\phi$, either $\phi \in T'$ or $\neg \phi \in T'$.

label: First-Countability is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is first-countable. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is first-countable. That is, the property of first-countability is hereditary.

label: First-Countability is Preserved under Open Continuous Surjection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a surjective open mapping which is also continuous. If $T_A$ is first-countable, then $T_B$ is also first-countable.

label: First-Countability is not Continuous Invariant
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a continuous mapping. If $T_A$ is a first-countable space, then it does not necessarily follow that $T_B$ is also first-countable.

label: First-Countable Space is Hausdorff iff All Convergent Sequences have Unique Limit
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a first-countable topological space. Then $T$ is Hausdorff all convergent sequences on $T$ have a unique limit.

label: First-Countable Space is Sequentially Compact iff Countably Compact
snippet: A first-countable topological space is sequentially compact it is countably compact.

label: First-Countable T2 Countably Compact Space is Regular
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a first-countable $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space which is countably compact. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a regular space.

label: First-Order Reaction
snippet: Let a substance decompose spontaneously in a first-order reaction. Let $x_0$ be a measure of the quantity of that substance at time $t = 0$. Let the quantity of the substance that remains after time $t$ be $x$. Then: $x = x_0 e^{-k t}$ where $k$ is the rate constant.

label: First Apotome/Example
snippet: == Example of First Apotome == Let $a, b \in \set {x \in \R_{>0} : x^2 \in \Q}$ be two rationally expressible numbers such that $a - b$ is an apotome. By definition, $a - b$ is a first apotome : $(1): \quad a \in \Q$ $(2): \quad \dfrac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2}} a \in \Q$ where $\Q$ denotes the set of rational numbers. Let $a = 9$ and $b = \sqrt {17}$. Then: {{eqn | l = \frac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } a | r = \frac {\sqrt {81 - 17} } 9 }} {{eqn | r = \frac {\sqrt {64} } 9 }} Therefore $9 - \sqrt {17}$ is a first apotome. Category:Examples of Apotome

label: First Central Moment is Zero
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable on some probability space with mean $\mu$. Then the first central moment $\mu_1$ of $X$ is equal to $0$.

label: First Derivative of PGF of Negative Binomial Distribution
First Fundamental Group of 1-Sphere
snippet: Let $\mathbb S^1$ be the $1$-sphere. Let $\struct {\map {\pi _1} {\mathbb S^1}, \ast}$ be the first fundamental group of $\mathbb S^1$. Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Then $\struct {\map {\pi _1} {\mathbb S^1}, \ast}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {\Z, +}$.

label: First Isomorphism Theorem
snippet: == Context == This theorem applies for groups, rings, modules, algebras, and any other algebraic structure where you see the word homomorphism. It is a categorical result; that is, it is independent of the structure used.

label: First Occurrence of Prime Gap of 864
snippet: The first occurrence of a prime gap of $864$ is between $6 \, 505 \, 941 \, 701 \, 960 \, 039$ and $6 \, 505 \, 941 \, 701 \, 960 \, 903$.

label: First Order ODE/3 y dy by dx + 5 x = 3
snippet: == Example of First Order Ordinary Differential Equation == The differential equation: $3 y \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + 5 x = 3$ is an example of a first order ordinary differential equation.

label: First Order ODE/dx = (y over (1 - x^2 y^2)) dx + (x over (1 - x^2 y^2)) dy
snippet: The first order ordinary differential equation: $(1): \quad \d x = \dfrac y {1 - x^2 y^2} \rd x + \dfrac x {1 - x^2 y^2} \rd y$ is an exact differential equation with solution: $\map \ln {\dfrac {1 + x y} {1 - x y} } - 2 x = C$ The of this is defined on the set $S$: $S = \set {x, y \in \R: \size {x y} < 1}$ where $x, y \in \R$ such that $\size {x y} < 1$.

label: First Order ODE/dy = 5 x dx
snippet: == Example of First Order Ordinary Differential Equation == The differential equation: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = 5 x$ is an example of a first order ordinary differential equation.

label: First Order ODE/dy = k y dx
snippet: Let $k \in \R$ be a real number. The first order ODE: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = k y$ has the general solution: $y = C e^{k x}$

label: First Order ODE/y' - f (y) phi' (x) over f' (y) = phi (x) phi' (x) over f' (y)
snippet: Let $\map f y$ and $\map \phi x$ be known real functions of $y$ and $x$ respectively. The general solution of: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} - \dfrac {\map f y} {\map {f'} y} \map {\phi'} x = \dfrac {\map \phi x \map {\phi'} x} {\map {f'} y}$ is: $\map f y = C e^{\map \phi x} - \map \phi x - 1$

label: First Order ODE/y dy = k dx
snippet: Let $k \in \R$ be a real number. The first order ODE: $y \, \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = k$ has the general solution: $y^2 = 2 k x + C$

label: First Order ODE/y dy = k x dx
snippet: Let $k \in \R$ be a real number. The first order ODE: $y \rd y = k x \rd x$ has the general solution: $y^2 = k x^2 + C$

label: First Projection on Ordered Pair of Sets
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be sets. Let $w = \tuple {a, b}$ denote the ordered pair of $a$ and $b$. Let $\map {\pr_1} w$ denote the first projection on $w$. Then: $\ds \map {\pr_1} w = \bigcup \bigcap w$ where $\ds \bigcup$ and $\ds \bigcap$ denote union and intersection respectively.

label: First Sequence of Three Consecutive Strictly Decreasing Euler Phi Values
snippet: The first sequence of $3$ consecutive positive integers whose Euler $\phi$ values are strictly decreasing is: $\map \phi {523} > \map \phi {524} > \map \phi {525}$

label: First Subsequence Rule
snippet: Let $T = \struct {A, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff space. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $T$. Suppose $\sequence {x_n}$ has two convergent subsequences with different limits. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ is divergent.

label: First Supplement to Law of Quadratic Reciprocity
snippet: $\quad \paren {\dfrac {-1} p} = \paren {-1}^{\paren {p - 1} / 2} = \begin {cases} +1 & : p \equiv 1 \pmod 4 \\ -1 & : p \equiv 3 \pmod 4 \end {cases}$ where $\paren {\dfrac {-1} p}$ is defined as the Legendre symbol.

label: First Sylow Theorem
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $G$ be a group such that: $\order G = k p^n$ where: $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$ $p$ is not a divisor of $k$. Then $G$ has at least one Sylow $p$-subgroup.

label: First Variation Formula
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $I = \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $J$ be an open real interval. Suppose $\gamma : I \to M$ is a unit-speed admissible curve. Let $\Gamma : J \times I \to M$ be a variation of $\gamma$. Let $T_p M$ be the tangent space at $p \in M$. Let $V : M \to T_\gamma M$ be the variation field of $\Gamma$. Let $L_g$ be the Riemannian length of an admissible curve. Let $\gamma'$ be the velocity of $\gamma$. Let $D_t$ be the covariant derivative along $\gamma$. Let $\tuple {a_0, \ldots, a_k}$ be an admissible subdivision for $\gamma$.

label: First Variation Formula for Proper Variation
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $I = \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $J$ be an open real interval. Suppose $\gamma : I \to M$ is a unit-speed admissible curve. Let $\Gamma : J \times I \to M$ be a proper variation of $\gamma$. Let $T_p M$ be the tangent space at $p \in M$. Let $V : M \to T_\gamma M$ be the variation field of $\Gamma$. Let $L_g$ be the Riemannian length of an admissible curve. Let $\gamma'$ be the velocity of $\gamma$. Let $D_t$ be the covariant derivative along $\gamma$.

label: Five Color Theorem
snippet: A planar graph $G$ can be assigned a proper vertex $k$-coloring such that $k \le 5$.

label: Five Cube Theorem
snippet: Every integer can be expressed as a sum of five cube numbers.

label: Five Lemma
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let: $\begin{xy}\xymatrix@L+2mu@+1em{ M_1 \ar[r]^*{\alpha_1} \ar[d]^*{\phi_1} & M_2 \ar[r]^*{\alpha_2} \ar[d]^*{\phi_2} & M_3 \ar[r]^*{\alpha_3} \ar[d]^*{\phi_3} & M_4 \ar[r]^*{\alpha_4} \ar[d]^*{\phi_4} & M_5 \ar[d]^*{\phi_5} \\ N_1 \ar[r]_*{\beta_1} & N_2 \ar[r]_*{\beta_2} & N_3 \ar[r]_*{\beta_3} & N_4 \ar[r]_*{\beta_4} & N_5 }\end{xy}$ be a commutative diagram of $A$-modules. Suppose that the rows are exact. Then: If $\phi_2$ and $\phi_4$ are surjective and $\phi_5$ is injective then $\phi_3$ is surjective.

label: Five Platonic Solids
snippet: There exist exactly five platonic solids:

label: Fixed-Point Property is Topological
snippet: Let $T \sim T'$ be homeomorphic topological spaces. Suppose every continuous $f : T \to T$ has a fixed point. Then, every continuous $g : T' \to T'$ also has a fixed point.

label: Fixed-Point Representation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Fixed-Point Representation ==

label: Fixed Point Formulation of Explicit ODE
snippet: Let $x' = \map f {t, x}$ with $\map x {t_0} = x_0$ be an explicit ODE of dimension $n$. For $a, b \in \R$, let $\XX = \map {\CC} {\closedint a b; \R^n}$ be the space of continuous functions on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $T: \XX \to \XX$ be the map defined by: $\ds \map {\paren {T x} } t = x_0 + \int_{t_0}^t \map f {s, \map x s} \rd s$ {{explain|Definition of $\paren {T x}$}} Then a fixed point of $T$ in $\XX$ is a solution to the above ODE.

label: Fixed Point Set of Continuous Self-Map on Hausdorff Space is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff space. Let $f: T \to T$ be a continuous mapping on $T$. Let $W$ be the set defined as: $W = \set {x \in T: \map f x = x}$ Then $W$ is closed in $T$.

label: Fixed Point of Idempotent Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an idempotent mapping. Let $\Img f$ be the image of $f$. Let $x \in S$. Then $x$ is a fixed point of $f$ $x \in \Img f$.

label: Fixed Point of Mappings is Fixed Point of Composition
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be mappings. Let $x \in S$ be a fixed point of both $f$ and $g$. Then $x$ is also a fixed point of $f \circ g$, the composition of $f$ and $g$.

label: Fixed Points of Idempotent Operator
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space. Let $T : X \to X$ be an idempotent operator. Then the set of fixed points of $T$ is precisely the range $\Rng T$.

label: Fixed Points of Orthogonal Projection
snippet: Let $\struct {H, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\norm \cdot$ be the inner product norm of $H$. Let $K$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Let $P_K$ denote the orthogonal projection on $K$. Let $h \in H$. Then: $\map {P_K} h = h$ $h \in K$.

label: Fixed Points of Projection in Plane
snippet: Let $M$ and $N$ be distinct lines in the plane. 420px Let $\pr_{M, N}$ be the projection on $M$ along $N$: $\forall x \in \R^2: \map {\pr_{M, N} } x =$ the intersection of $M$ with the line through $x$ parallel to $N$. Then $M$ is the set of fixed points of $\pr_{M, N}$ in the sense that: $x \in M$ $\map {\pr_{M, N} } x = x$

label: Floating-Point Operation may not result in Floating-Point Number
snippet: Let a floating-point operation be performed on two floating-point numbers. Then it is not necessarily the case that the result of that operation is itself a number in floating-point representation.

label: Floor Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Use of Floor Function == === Floor of $0 \cdotp 99999$ ===

label: Floor Function is Continuous on Right at Integer
snippet: Let $f$ be the real function defined as: $\map f x = \floor x$ where $\floor{\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the floor function. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then $\map f x$ is continuous on the right at $n$.

label: Floor Function is Idempotent
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ denote the floor of $x$. Then: $\floor {\floor x} = \floor x$ That is, the floor function is idempotent.

label: Floor Function is Integer
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Then the floor function of $x$ is an integer: $\floor x \in \Z$

label: Floor Function is Not Continuous on Left at Integer
snippet: Let $f$ be the real function defined as: $\map f x = \floor x$ where $\floor{\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the floor function. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then $\map f x$ is not continuous on the left at $n$.

label: Floor defines Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ denote the floor function of $x$. Let $\RR$ be the relation defined on $\R$ such that: $\forall x, y, \in \R: \tuple {x, y} \in \RR \iff \floor x = \floor y$ Then $\RR$ is an equivalence, and $\forall n \in \Z$, the $\RR$-class of $n$ is the half-open interval $\hointr n {n + 1}$.

label: Floor equals Ceiling iff Integer
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ denote the floor of $x$, and $\ceiling x$ denote the ceiling of $x$. Then: $\floor x = \begin {cases} \ceiling x & : x \in \Z \\ \ceiling x - 1 & : x \notin \Z \\ \end {cases}$ or equivalently: $\ceiling x = \begin {cases} \floor x & : x \in \Z \\ \floor x + 1 & : x \notin \Z \\ \end {cases}$ where $\Z$ is the set of integers.

label: Floor of Ceiling is Ceiling
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ be the floor of $x$, and $\ceiling x$ be the ceiling of $x$. Then: $\floor {\ceiling x} = \ceiling x$ That is, the floor of the ceiling is the ceiling.

label: Floor of Half of n+m plus Floor of Half of n-m+1
snippet: Let $n, m \in \Z$ be integers. $\floor {\dfrac {n + m} 2} + \floor {\dfrac {n - m + 1} 2} = n$ where $\floor x$ denotes the floor of $x$.

label: Floor of Negative equals Negative of Ceiling
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ be the floor of $x$, and $\ceiling x$ be the ceiling of $x$. Then: $\floor {-x} = -\ceiling x$

label: Floor of Non-Integer
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $x \notin \Z$. Then: $\floor x < x$ where $\floor x$ denotes the floor of $x$.

label: Floquet's Theorem
snippet: Let $\mathbf A \left({t}\right)$ be a continuous matrix function with period $T$. Let $\Phi \left({t}\right)$ be a fundamental matrix of the Floquet system $\mathbf x' = \mathbf A \left({t}\right) \mathbf x$. Then $\Phi \left({t + T}\right)$ is also a fundamental matrix. Moreover, there exists: A nonsingular, continuously differentiable matrix function $\mathbf P \left({t}\right)$ with period $T$ A constant (possibly complex) matrix $\mathbf B$ such that: $\Phi \left({t}\right) = \mathbf P \left({t}\right) e^{\mathbf Bt}$
