label: Identification Mapping is Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ be a set. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$. Then the identification mapping $f$ is continuous.

label: Identification Topology equals Quotient Topology on Induced Equivalence
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ be a set. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a surjective mapping. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$: $\tau_2 = \set {V \subseteq S_2 : f^{-1} \sqbrk V \in \tau_1}$ Let $\RR_f \subseteq S_1 \times S_1$ be the equivalence on $S_1$ induced by $f$: $\tuple {s_1, s_2} \in \RR_f \iff \map f {s_1} = \map f {s_2}$ Let $q_{\RR_f}$ be the quotient mapping induced by $\RR_f$.

label: Identification Topology is Finest Topology for Mapping to be Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 := \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ be a set. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$. Let $T_2 := \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be the resulting topological space. Then $\tau_2$ is the finest topology on $S_2$ such that $f: T_1 \to T_2$ is continuous.

label: Identification Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ be a set. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$. Then $\tau_2$ is a topology on $S_2$.

label: Identity Element for Addition of Cuts
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. Let $0^*$ be the rational cut associated with the (rational) number $0$: $0^* = \set {r \in \Q: r < 0}$ Then: $\alpha + 0^* = \alpha$ where $+$ denotes the operation of addition of cuts.

label: Identity Element for Power Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma whose underlying set $S$ is non-empty. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the power structure of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then: a subset $J$ of $S$ is an identity element of $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ there exists an identity element $e$ of $\struct {S, \circ}$, such that $J = \set e$.

label: Identity Element is Order Unit on Set of Hermitian Elements of Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\le$ be the canonical preordering on $A$. Let $A_{\mathbf {SA}}$ be the set of Hermitian elements of $A$. Then ${\mathbf 1}_A$ is an order unit for $\tuple {A_{\mathbf{SA}}, \le}$.

label: Identity Element of Addition on Numbers
snippet: On all the number systems: natural numbers $\N$ integers $\Z$ rational numbers $\Q$ real numbers $\R$ complex numbers $\C$ the identity element of addition is zero ($0$).

label: Identity Element of Multiplication on Numbers
snippet: On all the number systems: natural numbers $\N$ integers $\Z$ rational numbers $\Q$ real numbers $\R$ complex numbers $\C$ the identity element of multiplication is one ($1$).

label: Identity Elements occupy Diagonal of Cayley Table in Inverse Row Form
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a finite group. Let $\CC$ be a Cayley table for $\struct {G, \circ}$ presented in inverse row form. Then all the entries in the main diagonal of $\CC$ are instances of the identity element.

label: Identity Functor is Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}: \mathbf C \to \mathbf C$ be the identity functor on $\mathbf C$. Then $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$ is a functor.

label: Identity Functor is Left Identity
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a functor, and let $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf D}$ be the identity functor on $\mathbf D$. Then the composite functor $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf D} F$ satisfies: $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf D} F = F$

label: Identity Functor is Right Identity
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a functor, and let $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$ be the identity functor on $\mathbf C$. Then the composite functor $F \operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$ satisfies: $F \operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C} = F$

label: Identity Mapping between Metrics separated by Scale Factor is Continuous
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be metric spaces on the same underlying set $A$. Let $d_1$ and $d_2$ be such that: $\forall x, y \in A: \map {d_2} {x, y} \le K \map {d_2} {x, y}$ Let $I_A: A \to A$ be the identity mapping on $A$. Then $I_A$ is continuous from $M_1$ to $M_2$.

label: Identity Mapping is Automorphism
snippet: The identity mapping $I_S: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {S, \circ}$ on the algebraic structure $\struct {S, \circ}$ is an automorphism. Its image is $S$.

label: Identity Mapping is Bijection
snippet: The identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ on the set $S$ is a bijection.

label: Identity Mapping is Complete Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L = \struct{A, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $\operatorname{id}_A$ denote the identity mapping on $A$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_A$ is a complete lattice homomorphism of $L$ to $L$

label: Identity Mapping is Continuous
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. The identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ defined as: $\forall x \in S: \map {I_S} x = x$ is a continuous mapping.

label: Identity Mapping is Frame Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L = \struct{S, \preceq}$ be a frame. Let $\operatorname{id}_S$ denote the identity mapping on $S$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_S$ is a frame homomorphism of $L$ to $L$

label: Identity Mapping is Group Endomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Then $I_G: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {G, \circ}$ is a group endomorphism.

label: Identity Mapping is Hermitian
snippet: The identity mapping is Hermitian.

label: Identity Mapping is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. The identity mapping $I_T: T \to T$ defined as: $\forall x \in T: \map {I_T} x = x$ is a homeomorphism.

label: Identity Mapping is Idempotent
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $I_S: S \to S$ be the identity mapping on $S$. Then $I_S$ is idempotent: $I_S \circ I_S = I_S$

label: Identity Mapping is Injection
snippet: On any set $S$, the identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ is an injection.

label: Identity Mapping is Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L = \struct{A, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a lattice. Let $\operatorname{id}_A$ denote the identity mapping on $A$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_A$ is a lattice homomorphism of $L$ to $L$

label: Identity Mapping is Left Identity
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $I_T \circ f = f$ where $I_T$ is the identity mapping on $T$, and $\circ$ signifies composition of mappings.

label: Identity Mapping is Permutation
snippet: The identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ on the set $S$ is a permutation.

label: Identity Mapping is Right Identity
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $f \circ I_S = f$ where $I_S$ is the identity mapping on $S$, and $\circ$ signifies composition of mappings.

label: Identity Mapping on Metric Space is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. The identity mapping $I_A: M \to M$ defined as: $\forall x \in A: \map {I_A} x = x$ is a homeomorphism.

label: Identity Mapping to Coarser Topology is Continuous
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be topologies on $S$. That is, let $T_1 = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $I_S: \struct {S, \tau_1} \to \struct {S, \tau_2}$ denote the identity mapping on $S$: $\forall x \in S: \map {I_S} x = x$ Then: $I_S: T_1 \to T_2$ is a continuous mapping $\tau_2$ is coarser than $\tau_1$.

label: Identity Matrix from Upper Triangular Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_{m n}$ be an upper triangular matrix of order $m \times n$ with no zero diagonal elements. Let $k = \min \set {m, n}$. Then $\mathbf A$ can be transformed into a matrix such that the first $k$ rows and columns form the unit matrix of order $k$.

label: Identity Minus Compact Linear Operator on Banach Space has Index Zero
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\Bbb F$. Let $I : X \to X$ be the identity mapping. Let $C : X \to X$ be a compact linear operator. Then $I - C$ is a Fredholm operator with the index: $\map {\mathrm{ind} } {I - C} = 0$

label: Identity Morphism is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $X$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\operatorname{id}_X : X \to X$ denote the identity morphism of $X$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_X \circ \operatorname{id}_X = \operatorname{id}_X$

label: Identity Morphism is Initial Object in Coslice Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory, and let $C \in \mathbf C_0$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\operatorname{id}_C: C \to C$ be the identity morphism for $C$. Then $\operatorname{id}_C$ is an initial object in the coslice category $C / \mathbf C$.

label: Identity Morphism is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $X$ be an object in $\mathbf C$. Then: the identity morphism $\operatorname{id}_X$ of $X$ is an isomorphism in $\mathbf C$.

label: Identity Morphism is Terminal Object in Slice Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory, and let $C \in \mathbf C_0$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\operatorname{id}_C: C \to C$ be the identity morphism for $C$. Then $\operatorname{id}_C$ is a terminal object in the slice category $\mathbf C \mathop / C$.

label: Identity Morphism is Unique
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $X$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Then the identity morphism $\operatorname{id}_X : X \to X$ is unique.

label: Identity Morphism of Coproduct
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ and $D$ be objects of $\mathbf C$, and let $C \sqcup D$ be a binary coproduct for $C$ and $D$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_{\paren {C \mathop \sqcup D} } = \operatorname{id}_C \sqcup \operatorname{id}_D$ where $\operatorname{id}$ denotes an identity morphism, and $\sqcup$ signifies a coproduct of morphisms.

label: Identity Morphism of Product
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ and $D$ be objects of $\mathbf C$, and let $C \times D$ be a binary product for $C$ and $D$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_{\paren {C \mathop \times D} } = \operatorname{id}_C \times \operatorname{id}_D$ where $\operatorname{id}$ denotes an identity morphism, and $\times$ signifies a product of morphisms.

label: Identity Natural Transformation is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a covariant functor. Let $\operatorname{id}_F$ denote the identity natural transformation on $F$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_F \circ \operatorname{id}_F = \operatorname{id}_F$ where $\operatorname{id}_F \circ \operatorname{id}_F$ denotes the vertical composition of $\operatorname{id}_F$ with itself.

label: Identity Natural Transformation is Left Identity
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F, G : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ be a natural transformation from $F$ to $G$. Let $\operatorname{id}_G$ denote the identity natural transformation on $G$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_G \mathop \circ \eta = \eta$ where $\operatorname{id}_G \mathop \circ \eta$ denotes the verictal composition of $\eta$ and $\operatorname{id}_G$.

label: Identity Natural Transformation is Natural Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a covariant functor. Let $\operatorname{id}_F: F \to F$ denote the identity natural transformation Then: $\operatorname{id}_F$ is a natural isomorphism

label: Identity Natural Transformation is Natural Transformation
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a covariant functor. Let $\operatorname{id}_F: F \to F$ denote the identity natural transformation Then: $\operatorname{id}_F$ is a natural transformation.

label: Identity Natural Transformation is Right Identity
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F, G : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ be a natural transformation from $F$ to $G$. Let $\operatorname{id}_F$ denote the identity natural transformation on $F$. Then: $\eta \circ \operatorname{id}_F = \eta$

label: Identity Theorem
snippet: Let $U$ be an open connected subset of the complex plane $\C$. Let $f$ and $g$ be complex functions whose domain is $U$. Let $S = \set {z \in U: \map f z = \map g z}$. Let $f$ and $g$ be analytic on $U$. Let $S$ have a limit point in $U$. Then: $\forall z \in U: \map f z = \map g z$

label: Identity is in Kernel of Group Homomorphism
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups. Let $e_G$ and $e_H$ be the identity elements of $G$ and $H$ respectively. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a (group) homomorphism from $G$ to $H$. Then: $e_G \in \map \ker \phi$ where $\map \ker \phi$ is the kernel of $\phi$.

label: Identity of Algebraic Structure is Preserved in Substructure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure with identity $e$. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a algebraic substructure of $\struct {S, \circ}$. That is, let $T \subseteq S$. Let $e \in T$. Then $e$ is an identity of $\struct {T, \circ}$.

label: Identity of Cancellable Monoid is Identity of Submonoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid, all of whose elements are cancellable. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a submonoid of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then the identity of $\struct {T, \circ}$ is the same element as the identity of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

label: Identity of Cardinal Product is One
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a cardinal. Then: $\bsone \mathbf a = \mathbf a$ where $\bsone \mathbf a$ denotes the product of the (cardinal) one and $\mathbf a$. That is, $\bsone$ is the identity element of the product operation on cardinals.

label: Identity of Cardinal Sum is Zero
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a cardinal. Then: $\mathbf a + \mathbf 0 = \mathbf a$ where $\mathbf a + \mathbf 0$ denotes the sum of the zero cardinal and $\mathbf a$. That is, $\mathbf 0$ is the identity element of the sum operation on cardinals.

label: Identity of Group is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group which has an identity element $e \in G$. Then $e$ is unique.

label: Identity of Group is in Singleton Conjugacy Class
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $e$ be the identity of $G$. Then $e$ is in its own singleton conjugacy class: $\conjclass e = \set e$

label: Identity of Monoid is Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid. Let $e$ be an identity element of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then $e$ is a cancellable element of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

label: Identity of Monoid is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid. Then $S$ has a unique identity.

label: Identity of Points
snippet: Two points share the same position they are the same points.

label: Identity of Power Set with Intersection
snippet: Let $S$ be a set and let $\powerset S$ be its power set. Consider the algebraic structure $\struct {\powerset S, \cap}$, where $\cap$ denotes set intersection. Then $S$ serves as the identity for $\struct {\powerset S, \cap}$.

label: Identity of Power Set with Union
snippet: Let $S$ be a set and let $\powerset S$ be its power set. Consider the algebraic structure $\struct {\powerset S, \cup}$, where $\cup$ denotes set union. Then the empty set $\O$ serves as the identity for $\struct {\powerset S, \cup}$.

label: Identity of Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of group $G$. Then the identity of $H$ is also $e$.

label: Identity of Subgroup of Dipper Semigroup is not Identity of Dipper
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers such that $m, n > 0$. Let $\struct {N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }, +_{m, n} }$ denote the dipper semigroup. Let $\struct {H, +_{m, n} }$ be the subgroup of $\struct {N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }, +_{m, n} }$ where $H = \set {k \in \N: m \le k < m + n}$ Then the identity of $\struct {H, +_{m, n} }$ is not the identity of $\struct {N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }, +_{m, n} }$.

label: Identity of Submonoid is not necessarily Identity of Monoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a submonoid of $\struct {S, \circ}$ whose identity is $e_T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $e_T = e_S$.

label: If Compact Between then Way Below
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $x, k, y \in S$ such that: $x \preceq k$ and $k \preceq y$ and $k \in \map K L$ where $\map K L$ denotes the compact subset of $L$. Then $x \ll y$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation.

label: If Element Does Not Belong to Ideal then There Exists Prime Ideal Including Ideal and Excluding Element
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a distributive lattice. Let $I$ be an ideal in $L$. Let $x$ be an element of $S$. Suppose $x \notin I$ Then there exists a prime ideal $P$ in $L$: $I \subseteq P$ and $x \notin P$

label: If Every Element Pseudoprime is Prime then Way Below Relation is Multiplicative
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below continuous distributive lattice. Let every element $p \in S$: $p$ is pseudoprime $\implies p$ is prime. Then $\ll$ is multiplicative where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation of $L$.

label: If Ideal and Filter are Disjoint then There Exists Prime Ideal Including Ideal and Disjoint from Filter
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a distributive lattice. Let $I$ be an ideal in $L$. Let $F$ be a filter on $L$ such that $I \cap F = \O$ Then there exists a prime ideal $P$ in $L$: $I \subseteq P$ and $P \cap F = \O$

label: If Infimum of Filtered Subset belongs to Element of Sub-Basis then Subset and Element Intersect implies Infimum of Subset belongs to Closure of Subset
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a complete topological lattice with lower topology. Let $B$ be an analytic sub-basis of $T$. Let $F$ be a filtered subset of $S$ such that $\forall A \in B: \inf F \in A \implies F \cap A \ne \O$ Then $\inf F \in F^-$ where $F^-$ denotes the topological closure of $F$.

label: If Ratio of Cube to Number is as between Two Cubes then Number is Cube
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \Z$ be integers such that: $\dfrac a b = \dfrac {c^3} {d^3}$ Let $a$ be a cube number. Then $b$ is also a cube number.

label: If Ratio of Square to Number is as between Two Squares then Number is Square
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \Z$ be integers such that: $\dfrac a b = \dfrac {c^2} {d^2}$ Let $a$ be a square number. Then $b$ is also a square number.

label: If Set Exists then Empty Set Exists
snippet: If at least one set exists, then there exists an empty set.

label: Ill-Conditioned Problem/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Ill-Conditioned Problems ==

label: Image Filter is Filter
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be sets. Let $\powerset X$ and $\powerset Y$ be the power sets of $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping. Let $\FF \subset \powerset X$ be a filter on $X$. Then the image filter of $\FF$ $f$: $f \sqbrk \FF := \set {U \subseteq Y: f^{-1} \sqbrk U \in \FF}$ is a filter on $Y$.

label: Image is Subset Iff Subset of Preimage
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $\forall A \subseteq S, B \subseteq T : f \sqbrk A \subseteq B$ $A \subseteq f^{-1} \sqbrk B$

label: Image is Subset of Codomain
snippet: Let $\RR = S \times T$ be a relation. For all subsets $A$ of the domain of $\RR$, the image of $A$ is a subset of the codomain of $\RR$: $\forall A \subseteq \Dom \RR: \RR \sqbrk A \subseteq T$ In the notation of direct image mappings, this can be written as: $\forall A \in \powerset S: \map {\RR^\to} A \in \powerset T$

label: Image of Absorbing Set under Surjective Linear Transformation is Absorbing
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be an absorbing set. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a surjective linear transformation. Then $T \sqbrk A$ is an absorbing set.

label: Image of Balanced Set under Linear Transformation is Balanced
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $\Bbb F$. Let $E \subseteq X$ be balanced. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Then $\map T E \subseteq Y$ is balanced.

label: Image of Bijection on Set is Set with Axiom of Choice implies Axiom of Replacement
snippet: Let the be accepted. Let it be accepted as axiomatic that: every class which can be put into one-to-one correspondence with a set is itself a set. Then the holds:

label: Image of Bounded Linear Transformation is Everywhere Dense iff Dual Operator is Injective
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $X^\ast$ and $Y^\ast$ be the normed dual spaces of $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a bounded linear transformation. Let $T^\ast : Y^\ast \to X^\ast$ be the dual operator of $T$. Then $T \sqbrk X$ is everywhere dense in $Y$ $T^\ast$ is injective.

label: Image of Canonical Injection is Normal Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$ be groups with identity elements $e_1$ and $e_2$ respectively. Let $\struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ}$ be the group direct product of $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$. Let: $\inj_1: \struct {G_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ}$ be the canonical injection from $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ to $\struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ}$ $\inj_2: \struct {G_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ}$ be the canonical injection from $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$ to $\struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ}$.

label: Image of Cauchy Sequence in Topological Vector Space is von Neumann-Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a Cauchy sequence. Let: $E = \set {x_n : n \in \N}$ Then $E$ is von Neumann-bounded.

label: Image of Closed Real Interval is Bounded
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Then $f$ is bounded on $\closedint a b$.

label: Image of Closed Set under Linear Isometry from Banach Space to Normed Vector Space is Closed
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {Y, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear isometry. Let $A$ be a closed subset of $X$. Then $T \sqbrk A$ is closed in $X$.

label: Image of Closure Operator Inherits Infima
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $f$ be a closure operator on $L$. Then $R = \struct {f \sqbrk S, \precsim}$ inherits infima, where $\mathord \precsim = \mathord \preceq \cap \paren {f \sqbrk S \times f \sqbrk S}$ $f \sqbrk S$ denotes the image of $f$.

label: Image of Compact Subset under Directed Suprema Preserving Closure Operator is Subset of Compact Subset
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an algebric lattice. Let $c: S \to S$ be a closure operator that preserves directed suprema. Then: $c \sqbrk {\map K L} \subseteq \map K {\struct {c \sqbrk S, \precsim} }$ where: $\map K L$ denotes the compact subset of $L$ $c \sqbrk S$ denotes the image of $S$ under $c$ $\mathord \precsim = \mathord \preceq \cap \paren {c \sqbrk S \times \map c S}$

label: Image of Convex Set under Linear Transformation is Convex
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $\Bbb F$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be convex. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Then $\map T C \subseteq Y$ is convex.

label: Image of Countable Set under Mapping is Countable
snippet: Let $S$ be a countable set. Let $T$ be a set. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then the image of $f$ is countable.

label: Image of Dilation of Set under Linear Transformation is Dilation of Image
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $E \subseteq X$ be a non-empty set. Let $\lambda \in K$. Then: $\map T {\lambda E} = \lambda \map T E$ where $\lambda E$ denotes the dilation of $E$ by $\lambda$.

label: Image of Directed Suprema Preserving Closure Operator is Algebraic Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below algebraic lattice. Let $c: S \to S$ be a closure operator that preserves directed suprema. Let $C = \struct {c \sqbrk S, \precsim}$ be an ordered subset of $L$. Then $C$ is algebraic lattice.

label: Image of Domain of Mapping is Image Set
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. The image of $S$ is the image set of $f$: $f \sqbrk S = \Img f$

label: Image of Domain of Relation is Image Set
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. The image of the domain of $\RR$ is the image set of $\RR$: $\RR \sqbrk {\Dom \RR} = \Img \RR$ where $\Img \RR$ is the image of $\RR$.

label: Image of Doubleton under Mapping
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $\forall x, y \in S: f \sqbrk {\set {x, y} } = \set {\map f x, \map f y}$

label: Image of Element is Subset
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $A \subseteq S$. Then: $s \in A \implies \map \RR s \subseteq \RR \sqbrk A$

label: Image of Element under Cartesian Product of Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq S$ and $B \subseteq T$. Let $\RR$ be the relation defined by the Cartesian product $A \times B$. Then: $\forall x \in A: \map \RR x = B$

label: Image of Element under Inverse Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping such that its inverse $f^{-1}: T \to S$ is also a mapping. Then: $\forall x \in S, y \in T: \map f x = y \iff \map {f^{-1} } y = x$

label: Image of Element under Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Image of Element under Mapping ==

label: Image of Empty Set is Empty Set
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. The image of the empty set is the empty set: $\RR \sqbrk \O = \O$

label: Image of Evaluation Linear Transformation on Banach Space is Closed
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$ be a Banach space. Let $\struct {X^{\ast \ast}, 
orm \cdot_{X^{\ast \ast} } }$ be the second normed dual of $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$. Let $J : X 	o X^{\ast \ast}$ be the evaluation linear transformation. Then: $\map J X$ is closed in $X^{\ast \ast}$.

label: Image of Evaluation Linear Transformation on Banach Space is Closed Linear Subspace of Second Dual
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$ be a Banach space. Let $\struct {X^{\ast \ast}, 
orm \cdot_{X^{\ast \ast} } }$ be the second normed dual of $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$. Let $J : X 	o X^{\ast \ast}$ be the evaluation linear transformation. Then $\map J X$ is a closed linear subspace of $X^{\ast \ast}$.

label: Image of Extreme Point under Injective Linear Isomorphism is Extreme Point
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $\Bbb F$. Let $K \subseteq X$ be convex. Let $T : X \to Y$ be an injective linear transformation. Let $x \in K$. Then $x$ is an extreme point of $K$ $T x$ is an extreme point of $T \sqbrk K$.

label: Image of Frame under Frame Homomorphism is Frame
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be frames. Let $\phi: S_1 \to S_2$ be a frame homomorphism. Let $L_3 = \struct{S_3, \preceq_3}$ be the ordered set where: $S_3$ denotes the image of $S_1$ under $\phi$ $\preceq_3$ denotes the restricted ordering of $\preceq_2$ to the subset $S_3$. Then: $L_3$ is a subframe of $L_2$.

label: Image of Fredholm Operator of Banach Spaces is Closed
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\tuple {X, \norm \cdot_X}, \tuple {Y, \norm \cdot_Y}$ be Banach spaces over $\Bbb F$. Let $T: X \to Y$ be a Fredholm operator. Let $\Img T$ be the image of $T$ . Then $\Img T$ is closed.

label: Image of Generating Set of Vector Space under Linear Transformation is Generating Set of Image
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $G$ be a generating set for $X$. Then $T \sqbrk G$ be a generating set for $T \sqbrk X$.

label: Image of Group Homomorphism is Hausdorff Implies Kernel is Closed
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be topological groups. Let $f: G \to H$ be a morphism. Let its image $\Img f$ be Hausdorff. Then its kernel $\map \ker f$ is closed in $G$.

label: Image of Group Homomorphism is Subgroup
snippet: Let $\phi: G_1 \to G_2$ be a group homomorphism. Then: $\Img \phi \le G_2$ where $\le$ denotes the relation of being a subgroup.

label: Image of Idempotent and Directed Suprema Preserving Mapping is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $f:S \to S$ be a mapping that is idempotent and preserves directed suprema. Let $F = \struct {f \sqbrk S, \precsim}$ be an ordered subset of $L$. Then $F$ inherits directed suprema and is complete lattice.

label: Image of Integer Square Function
snippet: The image of the integer square function is the set of square numbers.

label: Image of Interior of Set under Homeomorphism is Interior of Image
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a homeomorphism. Let $A \subseteq X$. Then: $\paren {f \sqbrk A}^\circ = f \sqbrk {A^\circ}$ where: $A^\circ$ is the interior of $A$ in $X$ $\paren {f \sqbrk A}^\circ$ is the interior of $f \sqbrk A$ in $Y$.

label: Image of Intersection under Injection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $\forall A, B \subseteq S: f \sqbrk {A \cap B} = f \sqbrk A \cap f \sqbrk B$ $f$ is an injection. This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings as: $\forall A, B \subseteq S: \map {f^\to} {A \cap B} = \map {f^\to} A \cap \map {f^\to} B$

label: Image of Intersection under Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $f \sqbrk {S_1 \cap S_2} \subseteq f \sqbrk {S_1} \cap f \sqbrk {S_2}$ This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings as: $\forall S_1, S_2 \in \powerset S: \map {f^\to} {S_1 \cap S_2} \subseteq \map {f^\to} {S_1} \cap \map {f^\to} {S_2}$ That is, the image of the intersection of subsets of a mapping is a subset of the intersection of their images.

label: Image of Intersection under One-to-Many Relation
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Then: $\forall S_1, S_2 \subseteq S: \RR \sqbrk {S_1 \cap S_2} = \RR \sqbrk {S_1} \cap \RR \sqbrk {S_2}$ $\RR$ is one-to-many.

label: Image of Intersection under Relation
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\RR \sqbrk {S_1 \cap S_2} \subseteq \RR \sqbrk {S_1} \cap \RR \sqbrk {S_2}$ That is, the image of the intersection of subsets of $S$ is a subset of the intersection of their images.

label: Image of Inverse Image
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $X$ be a subset of $T$. Then: $f \sqbrk {f^{-1} \sqbrk X} \subseteq X$ where: $f^{-1} \sqbrk X$ denotes the image of $X$ under the relation $f^{-1}$.

label: Image of Linear Combination of Subsets of Vector Space under Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $\lambda, \mu \in K$. Let $A, B \subseteq X$. Then: $T \sqbrk {\lambda A + \mu B} = \lambda T \sqbrk A + \mu T \sqbrk B$

label: Image of Mapping from Finite Set is Finite
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be sets. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping. Let $X$ be a finite set. Then $f \sqbrk X$ is a finite set.

label: Image of Mapping of Infima is Generator Set of Filter
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a meet semilattice. Let $f, g:\N \to S$ be mappings such that: $\forall n \in \N: \map g n = \inf \set {\map f m: m \in \N \land m \le n}$ Let $F$ be a filter such that $f \sqbrk \N$ is generator set of $F$, where $f \sqbrk \N$ denotes the image of $f$. Then $g \sqbrk \N$ is generator set of $F$.

label: Image of Mapping of Intersections is Smallest Basis
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $f: X \to \tau$ be a mapping such that: $\forall x \in X: \paren {x \in \map f x \land \forall U \in \tau: x \in U \implies \map f x \subseteq U}$. Then the image $\Img f$ is subset of every basis of $T$.

label: Image of Open Set under Continuous Mapping in Metric Space may not be Open
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: A_1 \to A_2$ be a $\tuple {d_1, d_2}$-continuous mapping from $A_1$ to $A_2$. Let $U \subseteq A_1$ be an open set of $M_1$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $f \sqbrk U$ is an open set of $M_2$.

label: Image of Operator Generated by Closure System is Set of Closure System
snippet: Let $L = \struct {X, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $S = \struct {T, \precsim}$ be a closure system of $L$. Then $\map {\operatorname {operator} } S \sqbrk X = T$ where $\map {\operatorname {operator} } S$ denotes the operator generated by $S$.

label: Image of P-adic Norm
snippet:
Let $
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rationals $\Q$ for some prime number $p$. Then the image of $
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ is: $\Img {
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p} = \set {p^n : n \in \Z} \cup \set 0$

label: Image of Path is Path-Connected Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $I \subset \R$ be the closed real interval $\closedint a b$. Let $\gamma: I \to S$ be a path. Then: $\map \gamma I$ is a path-connected set of $T$.

label: Image of Point under Central Dilatation Mapping with Fixed Point at Origin
snippet: Let $f$ be a central dilatation mapping whose center of enlargement $C$ is located at the origin of a coordinate system. Let the scale factor of $f$ be $k$. Let the position vector of a point $P$ be $\mathbf r$. Then the image of $P$ under $f$ has position vector $k \mathbf r$.

label: Image of Point under Negative Scale Factor
snippet: Let $f$ be a central dilatation mapping with center of enlargement $C$. Let the scale factor of $f$ be negative. Let the image of a point $P$ be $P'$. Then $PCP'$ is a straight line such that $C$ is between $P$ and $P'$.

label: Image of Point under Neighborhood of Diagonal is Neighborhood of Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct{X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\tau_{X \times X}$ denote the product topology on the cartesian product $X \times X$. Let $V$ be a neighborhood of the diagonal $\Delta_X$ of $X \times X$ in the product space $\struct {X \times X, \tau_{X \times X} }$. Then: $\forall x \in X : \map V x$ is a neighborhood of $x$ in $T$

label: Image of Point under Open Neighborhood of Diagonal is Open Neighborhood of Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct{X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\tau_{X \times X}$ denote the product topology on the cartesian product $X \times X$. Let $U$ be an open neighborhood of the diagonal $\Delta_X$ of $X \times X$ in the product space $\struct {X \times X, \tau_{X \times X} }$. Then: $\forall x \in X : \map U x$ is an open neighborhood of $x$ in $T$

label: Image of Pointwise Scalar Multiplication of Subset of Scalars with Subset of Vectors under Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $S \subseteq K$ and $D \subseteq X$ be non-empty sets. Then: $T \sqbrk {S D} = S T \sqbrk D$ where: $S D = \set {\lambda x : \lambda \in S, \, x \in D}$

label: Image of Positive Element of C*-Algebra under *-Algebra Homomorphism is Positive
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_A}$ and $\struct {B, \square, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_B}$ be $\text C^\ast$-algebras. Let $\phi : A \to B$ be a $\ast$-algebra homomorphism. Let $a \in A$ be positive. Then $\map \phi a$ is positive.

label: Image of Preimage under Relation is Subset
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Then: $B \subseteq T \implies \paren {\RR \circ \RR^{-1} } \sqbrk B \subseteq B$ where: $\RR \sqbrk B$ denotes the image of $B$ under $\RR$ $\RR^{-1} \sqbrk B$ denotes the preimage of $B$ under $\RR$ $\RR \circ \RR^{-1}$ denotes composition of $\RR$ and $\RR^{-1}$.

label: Image of Projection in Plane
snippet: Let $M$ and $N$ be distinct lines in the plane. 420px Let $\pr_{M, N}$ be the projection on $M$ along $N$: $\forall x \in \R^2: \map {\pr_{M, N} } x =$ the intersection of $M$ with the line through $x$ parallel to $N$. Then $M$ is the image of $\pr_{M, N}$.

label: Image of Real Interval under Continuous Real Function is Real Interval
snippet: Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $f: I \to \R$ be a continuous real function. Then the image of $f$ is a real interval.

label: Image of Real Natural Logarithm
snippet: Let $\ln$ be the natural logarithm function on the real numbers. Then the image of $\ln$ is the set of real numbers: $\Img \ln = \R$

label: Image of Relative Complement under Bijection is Relative Complement of Image
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a bijection. Let $H \subseteq S$. Let $f \sqbrk H = K$ be the image of $H$ under $f$. Let $\relcomp S H$ denote the relative complement of $H$ in $S$. Then: $f \sqbrk {\relcomp S H} = \relcomp T K$

label: Image of Set Difference under Injection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be subsets of $S$. Let $S_1 \setminus S_2$ denote the set difference between $S_1$ and $S_2$. Then: $\forall S_1, S_2 \subseteq S: f \sqbrk {S_1} \setminus f \sqbrk {S_2} = f \sqbrk {S_1 \setminus S_2}$ $f$ is an injection.

label: Image of Set Difference under Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. The set difference of the images of two subsets of $S$ is a subset of the image of the set difference. That is: Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $f \sqbrk {S_1} \setminus f \sqbrk {S_2} \subseteq f \sqbrk {S_1 \setminus S_2}$ where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

label: Image of Set Difference under Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\RR \sqbrk A \setminus \RR \sqbrk B \subseteq \RR \sqbrk {A \setminus B}$ where: $\setminus$ denotes set difference $\RR \sqbrk A$ denotes image of $A$ under $\RR$.

label: Image of Set under Mapping is Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\mathrm U$ denote the universal class. Let $f: A \to \mathrm U$ be a class mapping. Let $S$ be a subset of $A$. Then the image $f \sqbrk S$ is also a set. If $A$ is a set, then this result is known as the Axiom of Replacement in Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory.

label: Image of Set under Mapping is Set iff Restriction is Set
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe Let $f: V \to V$ be a mapping. Let $x$ be a set. Let $f \sqbrk x$ denote the image of $x$ under $f$. Let $f {\restriction} x$ denote the restriction of $f$ to $x$. Then $f \sqbrk x$ is a set $f {\restriction} x$ is a set.

label: Image of Singleton under Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then the image of an element of $S$ is equal to the image of a singleton containing that element, the singleton being a subset of $S$: $\forall s \in S: \set {\map f s} = f \sqbrk {\set s}$

label: Image of Singleton under Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Then the image of an element of $S$ is equal to the image of a singleton containing that element, the singleton being a subset of $S$: $\forall s \in S: \map \RR s = \RR \sqbrk {\set s}$

label: Image of Small Class under Mapping is Small
snippet: Let $A$ be a mapping. Let $a$ be a small class. Then, the image of $a$ under $A$ is small.

label: Image of Submodule under Linear Transformation is Submodule
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_G}_R$ and $\struct {H, +_H, \circ_H}_R$ be $R$-modules. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a linear transformation. Let $M$ be a submodule of $G$. Then $\phi \sqbrk M$ is a submodule of $H$.

label: Image of Subset under Mapping equals Union of Images of Elements
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping from $S$ to $T$. Let $X \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Then: $\ds f \sqbrk X = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in X} \map f x$ where: $f \sqbrk X$ is the image of the subset $X$ under $f$ $\map f x$ is the image of the element $x$ under $f$.

label: Image of Subset under Mapping is Subset of Image
snippet: == Corollary to Image of Subset under Relation is Subset of Image == Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping from $S$ to $T$. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ such that $A \subseteq B$. Then the image of $A$ is a subset of the image of $B$: $A \subseteq B \implies f \sqbrk A \subseteq f \sqbrk B$ This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings as: $\forall A, B \in \powerset S: A \subseteq B \implies \map {f^\to} A \subseteq \map {f^\to} B$

label: Image of Subset under Neighborhood of Diagonal is Neighborhood of Subset
snippet: Let $T = \struct{X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\tau_{X \times X}$ denote the product topology on the cartesian product $X \times X$. Let $V$ be a neighborhood of the diagonal $\Delta_X$ of $X \times X$ in the product space $\struct {X \times X, \tau_{X \times X} }$. Then: $\forall A \subseteq X : V \sqbrk A$ is a neighborhood of $A$ in $T$

label: Image of Subset under Open Neighborhood of Diagonal is Open Neighborhood of Subset
snippet: Let $T = \struct{X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\tau_{X \times X}$ denote the product topology on the cartesian product $X \times X$. Let $U$ be an open neighborhood of the diagonal $\Delta_X$ of $X \times X$ in the product space $\struct {X \times X, \tau_{X \times X} }$. Then: $\forall A \subseteq X : U \sqbrk A$ is an open neighborhood of $A$ in $T$

label: Image of Subset under Relation equals Union of Images of Elements
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $X \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Then: $\ds \RR \sqbrk X = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in X} \map \RR x$ where: $\RR \sqbrk X$ is the image of the subset $X$ under $\RR$ $\map \RR x$ is the image of the element $x$ under $\RR$.

label: Image of Subset under Relation is Subset of Image
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation from $S$ to $T$. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ such that $A \subseteq B$. Then the image of $A$ is a subset of the image of $B$: $A \subseteq B \implies \RR \sqbrk A \subseteq \RR \sqbrk B$ In the notation of direct image mappings, this can be written: $A \subseteq B \implies \map {\RR^\to} A \subseteq \map {\RR^\to} B$

label: Image of Successor Mapping forms Peano Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {P, s, 0}$ be a Peano structure. Let $P'$ be the set $s \sqbrk P$, that is: $P' = \set {\map s n: n \in P}$ Let $s'$ be the restriction of $s$ to $P'$. Then $\struct {P', s', \map s 0}$ is also a Peano structure.

label: Image of Symmetric Set under Linear Transformation is Symmetric
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over a subfield of $\C$. Let $C$ be a symmetric subset of $X$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Then $\map T C$ is a symmetric subset of $Y$.

label: Image of Translation of Set under Linear Transformation is Translation of Image
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $E \subseteq X$ be a non-empty set. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\map T {E + x} = \map T E + T x$ where $E + x$ denotes the translation of $E$ by $x$.

label: Image of Transpose of Linear Transformation is Annihilator of Kernel
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be $n$-dimensional vector spaces over a field. Let $\map \LL {G, H}$ be the set of all linear transformations from $G$ to $H$. Let $u \in \map \LL {G, H}$. Let $u^\intercal$ be the transpose of $u$. Then: The image of $u^\intercal$ is the annihilator of $\map \ker u$. where $\map \ker u$ denotes the kernel of $u$.

label: Image of Ultrafilter is Ultrafilter
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be sets. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping. Let $\FF$ be an ultrafilter on $X$. Then the image filter $f \sqbrk \FF$ is an ultrafilter on $Y$.

label: Image of Union under Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $f \sqbrk {A \cup B} = f \sqbrk A \cup f \sqbrk B$ This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings as: $\forall A, B \in \powerset S: \map {f^\to} {A \cup B} = \map {f^\to} A \cup \map {f^\to} B$

label: Image of Union under Relation
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\RR \sqbrk {S_1 \cup S_2} = \RR \sqbrk {S_1} \cup \RR \sqbrk {S_2}$ That is, the image of the union of subsets of $S$ is equal to the union of their images.

label: Image of Vector Subspace under Linear Transformation is Vector Subspace
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $U$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Then $T \sqbrk U$ is a vector subspace of $Y$.

label: Image of von Neumann-Bounded Set under Equicontinuous Family of Linear Transformations is Contained in von Neumann-Bounded Set
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $\family {T_\alpha}_{\alpha \in I}$ be an equicontinuous family of linear transformations. Let $E \subseteq X$ be von Neumann-bounded. Then there exists a von Neumann-bounded set $F \subseteq Y$ such that: $T_\alpha \sqbrk E \subseteq F$ for each $\alpha \in I$.

label: Image under Inclusion Mapping
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $S \subseteq X$, $Z \subseteq S$. Then $i_S \sqbrk Z = Z$ where $i_S$ denotes the inclusion mapping of $S$ $i_S \sqbrk Z$ denotes the image of $Z$ under $i_S$.

label: Image under Increasing Mapping equal to Special Set is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $f: S \to S$ be an increasing mapping. Let $P = \struct {M, \precsim}$ be an ordered subset of $L$ such that $M = \set {x \in S: x = \map f x}$ Then $P$ is complete lattice.

label: Image under Projection from Closed Set of Product Topology is not necessarily Closed
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \struct {T_1 \times T_2, \tau}$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$, where $\tau$ is the product topology on $S$. Let $\pr_1: T \to T_1$ and $\pr_2: T \to T_2$ be the first and second projections from $T$ onto its factors. Let $K \subseteq S_1 \times S_2$ be closed in $T$. Then $\pr_1 \sqbrk K$ is not necessarily closed in $T_1$.

label: Image under Subset of Relation is Subset of Image under Relation
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR_1 \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation in $S \times T$. Let $\RR_2 \subseteq \RR_1$. Let $A \subseteq S$. Then: $\RR_2 \sqbrk A \subseteq \RR_1 \sqbrk A$ where $\RR_1 \sqbrk A$ denotes the image of $A$ under $\RR_1$.

label: Images of Elements under Repeated Composition of Injection form Equivalence Classes
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an injection. Let the sequence of mappings: $f^0, f^1, f^2, \ldots, f^n, \ldots$ be defined as: $\forall n \in \N: \map {f^n} x = \begin {cases} x & : n = 0 \\ \map f x & : n = 1 \\ \map f {\map {f^{n - 1} } x} & : n > 1 \end {cases}$ Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be the relation on $S$ defined as: $\RR = \set {\tuple {a, b} \in S \times S: \exists k \in \Z: b = \map {f^k} a \lor \exists j \in \Z: a = \map {f^j} b}$ Then $\RR$ is an equivalence relation.

label: Imaginary Numbers under Addition form Group
snippet: Let $\II$ denote the set of complex numbers of the form $0 + i y$ That is, let $\II$ be the set of all wholly imaginary numbers. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\II, +}$ is a group.

label: Imaginary Numbers under Multiplication do not form Group
snippet: Let $\II$ denote the set of complex numbers of the form $0 + i y$ for $y \in \R_{\ne 0}$. That is, let $\II$ be the set of all wholly imaginary non-zero numbers. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\II, \times}$ is not a group.

label: Imaginary Part as Mapping is Endomorphism for Complex Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $f: \C \to \R$ be the mapping from the complex numbers to the real numbers defined as: $\forall z \in \C: \map f z = \map \Im z$ where $\map \Im z$ denotes the imaginary part of $z$. Then $f: \struct {\C, +} \to \struct {\R, +}$ is a group epimorphism. Its kernel is the set: $\map \ker f = \R$ of (wholly) real numbers.

label: Imaginary Part as Mapping is Surjection
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \R$ be the projection from the complex numbers to the real numbers defined as: $\forall z \in \C: \map f z = \map \Im z$ where $\map \Im z$ denotes the imaginary part of $z$. Then $f$ is a surjection.

label: Imaginary Part of Complex Exponential Function
snippet: Let $z = x + i y \in \C$ be a complex number, where $x, y \in \R$. Let $\exp z$ denote the complex exponential function. Then: $\map \Im {\exp z} = e^x \sin y$ where: $\map \Im z$ denotes the imaginary part of a complex number $z$ $e^x$ denotes the real exponential function of $x$ $\sin y$ denotes the real sine function of $y$.

label: Imaginary Part of Complex Product
snippet: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be complex numbers. Then: $\map \Im {z_1 z_2} = \map \Re {z_1} \, \map \Im {z_2} + \map \Im {z_1} \, \map \Re {z_2}$

label: Imaginary Part of Integer Power of Complex Number is Harmonic
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $z^n$ denote $z$ raised to the $n$th power. Then the imaginary part $\map \Im {z^n}$ of $z^n$ is a harmonic polynomial.

label: Imaginary Part of Linear Functional is Linear Functional
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\C$. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a linear functional. Define $h : X \to \R$ by: $\map h x = \map \Im {\map f x}$ for each $x \in X$. Then $f$ is $\R$-linear.

label: Imaginary Part of Sine of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z = x + i y \in \C$ be a complex number, where $x, y \in \R$. Let $\sin z$ denote the complex sine function. Then: $\Im \paren {\sin z} = \cos x \sinh y$ where: $\Im z$ denotes the imaginary part of a complex number $z$ $\sin$ denotes the complex sine function $\cos$ denotes the real cosine function $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function.

label: Imaginary Unit to Power of Itself
snippet: $i^i = e^{-\pi / 2}$ where $i$ is the imaginary unit. Its decimal expansion is: $0 \cdotp 20787 \, 95763 \, 50761 \, 90854 \, 6955 \ldots$

label: Implications of Stokes' Theorem
snippet: Stokes' Theorem implies all of the following results: Classical Stokes' Theorem Green's Theorem Gauss's Theorem Fundamental Theorem of Calculus Cauchy's Residue Theorem

snippet: == Examples of Implicit Differentiation ==

snippet: == Examples of Implicit Functions ==

label: Implicit Function Theorem
snippet: The Implicit Function Theorem gives conditions on derivatives which ensure that an implicitly defined set is the graph of a function.

label: Implicit Function Theorem for Lipschitz Contraction at Point
snippet: Let $M$ and $N$ be metric spaces. Let $M$ be complete. Let $f: M \times N \to M$ be a uniform contraction. Then for all $t \in N$ there exists a unique $\map g t \in M$ such that $\map f {\map g t, t} = \map g t$, and if $f$ is Lipschitz continuous at a point $\tuple {\map g t, t}$, then $g$ is Lipschitz continuous at $t$.

label: Implicit Function Theorem for Lipschitz Contractions
snippet: Let $M$ and $N$ be metric spaces. Let $M$ be complete. Let $f : M \times N \to M$ be a Lipschitz continuous uniform contraction. Then for all $t\in N$ there exists a unique $\map g t \in M$ such that $\map f {\map g t, t} = \map g t$, and the mapping $g : N \to M$ is Lipschitz continuous.

label: Implicit Set Definition/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Implicit Set Definition ==

label: Impossible Proposition Strictly Implies Every Proposition
snippet: Let $P$ be a proposition of modal logic. Let $P$ be not possibly true. Then: $\forall Q: P \implies Q$ where $Q$ is an arbitrary proposition in the universe of discourse.

label: Improved Euler Method
snippet: == Proof Technique == Consider the first order ODE: $(1): \quad y' = \map f {x, y}$ subject to the initial condition $\map y {x_0} = y_0$ where $\map f {x, y}$ is continuous. Let $\map y x$ be the particular solution of $(1)$. For all $n \in \N_{>0}$, we define: $x_n = x_{n - 1} + h$ where $h \in \R_{>0}$. Then for all $n \in \N_{>0}$ such that $x_n$ is in the domain of $y$: $y_{n + 1} = y_n + \dfrac h 2 \paren {\map f {x_n, y_n} + \map f {x_{n + 1}, z_{n + 1} } }$ where: $z_{n + 1} = y_n + h \map f {x_n, y_n}$ is an approximation to $\map y {x_{n + 1} }$.

label: Impulse equals Change in Momentum
snippet: Let a force $\mathbf F$ be applied to a particle $P$. Then the impulse $\mathbf J$ imparted to $P$ is equal to the change of momentum of $P$.

label: In Connected Smooth Manifold Any Two Points can be Joined by Admissible Curve
snippet: Let $M$ be a connected smooth manifold with or without a boundary. Let $p, q \in M$ be points. Let $\gamma : \closedint a b \to M$ be an admissible curve. Then: $\forall p, q \in M : \exists \gamma \subset M : \paren {\map \gamma a = p} \land \paren {\map \gamma b = q}$

label: Included Set Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_H}$ be an included set space. Then $\tau_H$ is a topology on $S$, and $T$ is a topological space.

label: Included Set Topology on Finite Intersection
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space on a set $S$. Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ be a finite set of subsets of $S$: $\forall i \in \closedint 1 n: A_i \subseteq S$ Let $\forall i \in \closedint 1 n: \map T {A_i} = \struct {S, \tau_{A_i} }$ be the included set spaces on $S$ by $A_i$. Let: $\forall i \in \closedint 1 n: \map T {A_i} \le T$ where $\map T {A_i} \le T$ denotes that $\map T {A_i}$ is coarser than $T$. Then: $\ds \map T {\bigcap A_i} \le T$ where $\ds \map T {\bigcap A_i}$ is the included set space on $S$ by $\ds \bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_i$.

label: Included Set Topology on Union
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space on a set $S$. Let $\family {A_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of subsets of $S$ indexed by the indexing set $I$: $\forall i \in I: A_i \subseteq S$ Let $\forall i \in I: \map T {A_i} = \struct {S, \tau_{A_i} }$ be the included set spaces on $S$ by $A_i$. Let: $\forall i \in I: \map T {A_i} \ge T$ where $\map T {A_i} \ge T$ denotes that $\map T {A_i}$ is finer than $T$. Then: $\ds \map T {\bigcup A_i} \ge T$ where $\ds \map T {\bigcup A_i}$ is the included set space on $S$ by $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} A_i$.

label: Inclusion-Exclusion Principle
snippet: Let $\SS$ be an algebra of sets. Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ be finite sets. Let $f: \SS \to \R$ be an additive function. Then: {{eqn | l = \map f {\bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_i} | r = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map f {A_i} | c = }} {{eqn | o = | ro= - | r = \sum_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop < j \mathop \le n} \map f {A_i \cap A_j} | c = }} {{eqn | o = | ro= + | r = \sum_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop < j \mathop < k \mathop \le n} \map f {A_i \cap A_j \cap A_k} | c = }} {{eqn | o = | ro= + | r = \paren {-1}^{n - 1} \map f {\bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_i} | c = }}

label: Inclusion Functor is Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf D$ be a metacategory, and let $\mathbf C$ be a subcategory of $\mathbf D$. Let $\Iota_{\mathbf C}: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be the inclusion functor on $\mathbf C$ Then: $\Iota_{\mathbf C}$ is a (covariant) functor

label: Inclusion Mapping is Continuous
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$ be a topological subspace of $T$ where $H \subseteq S$. Let $i_H: H \to S$ be the inclusion mapping on $H$. Then $i_H$ is a $\struct {\tau_H, \tau}$-continuous mapping.

label: Inclusion Mapping is Embedding
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T_H = \struct{H, \tau_H}$ be a topological subspace of $T$, where $H \subseteq S$. Let $i_H : H \to S$ be the inclusion mapping of $H$ into $S$. Then $i_H$ is a embedding of $T_H$ into $T$.

label: Inclusion Mapping is Injection
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets such that $S$ is a subset of $T$. Then the inclusion mapping $i_S: S \to T$ defined as: $\forall x \in S: \map {i_S} x = x$ is an injection. For this reason the inclusion mapping can be known as the canonical injection of $S$ to $T$.

label: Inclusion Mapping is Monomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic substructure of $S$. Let $\iota: T \to S$ be the inclusion mapping from $T$ to $S$. Then $\iota$ is a monomorphism.

label: Inclusion Mapping is Restriction of Identity
snippet: Let $T$ be a set. Let $S \subseteq T$ be a subset of $T$. Let $i_S: S \to T$ be the inclusion mapping on $S$. Then $i_S$ is the restriction of the identity mapping $I_T: T \to T$ on $T$.

label: Inclusion Mapping is Surjection iff Identity
snippet: Let $T$ be a set. Let $S\subseteq T$ be a subset. Let $i_S: S \to T$ be the inclusion mapping. Then: $i_S: S \to T$ is surjective $i_S: S \to T = I_S: S \to S$ where $I_S: S \to S$ denotes the identity mapping on $S$. Alternatively, this theorem can be worded as: $i_S: S \to S = I_S: S \to S$ It follows directly that from Surjection by Restriction of Codomain‎, the surjective restriction of $i_S: S \to T$ to $i_S: S \to \Img {i_S}$ is itself the identity mapping.

label: Inclusion Mapping on Metric Space is Continuous
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\struct {H, d_H}$ be a metric subspace of $M$. Then the inclusion mapping $i_H: H \to A$ is continuous from $\struct {H, d_H}$ to $\struct {A, d}$.

label: Inclusion Mapping on Subgroup is Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\struct {H, \circ_{\restriction H} }$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $i: H \to G$ be the inclusion mapping from $H$ to $G$. Then $i$ is a group homomorphism.

label: Inclusion Mapping on Subring is Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {S, +{\restriction_S}, \circ {\restriction_S}}$ be a subring of $R$. Let $i_S: S \to R$ be the inclusion mapping from $S$ to $R$. Then ${i_S}$ is a ring homomorphism.

label: Inclusion Mapping on Subring is Monomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {S, +{\restriction_S}, \circ {\restriction_S} }$ be a subring of $R$. Let $i_S: S \to R$ be the inclusion mapping from $S$ to $R$. Then $i_S$ is a ring monomorphism.

label: Inclusion Mappings to Topological Sum from Components
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau_1}$ and $\struct {Y, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $\struct {Z, \tau_3}$ be the topological sum of $X$ and $Y$ where $\tau_3$ is the topology generated by $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$. Then $\tau_3$ is the finest topology on $Z$ in which the inclusion mappings from $\struct {X, \tau_1}$ and $\struct {Y, \tau_2}$ to $\struct {Z, \tau_3}$ are continuous.

label: Inclusion of Natural Numbers in Integers is Epimorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Mon}$ be the category of monoids. Let $\struct {\N, +}$ denote the monoid of natural numbers as on Natural Numbers under Addition form Commutative Monoid. Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ denote the additive group of integers. Denote with $\iota: \N \to \Z$ the inclusion mapping. Then $\iota: \N \to \Z$ is an epimorphism in $\mathbf{Mon}$.

label: Increasing Alternating Sum of Binomial Coefficients
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n \paren {-1}^{n + 1} j \binom n j = 0$ where $\dbinom n k$ denotes a binomial coefficient. That is: $1 \dbinom n 1 - 2 \dbinom n 2 + 3 \dbinom n 3 - \cdots + \paren {-1}^{n + 1} n \dbinom n n = 0$

label: Increasing Mappings Satisfying Inclusion in Lower Closure is Isomorphic to Auxiliary Relations
snippet: Let $R = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $\map {\operatorname{Ids} } R$ be the set of all ideals in $R$. Let $L = \struct {\map {\operatorname{Ids} } R, \precsim}$ be an ordered set where $\precsim \mathop = \subseteq\restriction_{\map {\operatorname{Ids} } R \times \map {\operatorname{Ids} } R}$. Let $M = \struct {F, \preccurlyeq}$ be the ordered set of increasing mappings $g:S \to \map {\operatorname{Ids} } R$ satisfying $\forall x \in S: \map g x \subseteq x^\preceq$. Let $\map {\operatorname{Aux} } R$ be the set of all auxiliary relations on $S$.

label: Increasing Martingale Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a probability space. Let $f$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Given sub-$\sigma$-algebra $\CC \subseteq \Sigma$, let $\expect {f \mid \CC}$ denote the conditional expectation of $f$ on $\CC$. Let $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a filtration of $\Sigma$. Let $\FF_\infty$ be the limit of $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \expect {f \mid \FF_n} = \expect {f \mid \FF_\infty}$ holds in $L^1$ norm, and $\mu$-almost surely.

label: Increasing Real Function has Countably Many Discontinuities
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be an increasing real function. Then $f$ has at most countably many discontinuities.

label: Increasing Second Argument of Ackermann-Péter Function is Not Greater than Increasing First Argument
snippet: For all $x, y \in \N$: $\map A {x + 1, y} \ge \map A {x, y + 1}$ where $A$ is the Ackermann-Péter function.

label: Increasing Sequence in Ordered Set Terminates iff Maximal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {P, \le}$ be an ordered set. $(1): \quad$ Every increasing sequence $x_1 \le x_2 \le x_3 \le \cdots$ with $x_i \in P$ eventually terminates: there is $n \in \N$ such that $x_n = x_{n + 1} = \cdots$. $(2): \quad$ Every non-empty subset of $P$ has a maximal element.

label: Increasing Sequence of Sets induces Partition on Limit
snippet: Let $\sequence {S_n}_{n \mathop \in \N} \uparrow S$ be an increasing sequence of sets with limit $S$. Define $T_1 = S_1$, and, for $n \in \N$, $T_{n + 1} = S_{n + 1} \setminus S_n$, where $\setminus$ denotes set difference. Then $\sequence {T_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a countable partition of $S$.

label: Increasing Sum of Binomial Coefficients
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n j \binom n j = n 2^{n - 1}$ where $\dbinom n k$ denotes a binomial coefficient. That is: $1 \dbinom n 1 + 2 \dbinom n 2 + 3 \dbinom n 3 + \dotsb + n \dbinom n n = n 2^{n - 1}$

label: Increasing Union of Ideals is Ideal
Indecomposable Lattice of Subgroups does not necessarily form Totally Ordered Set
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a Group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of subgroups of $G$. Let $\struct {\mathbb G, \subseteq}$ be the complete lattice formed by the subset ordering on $\mathbb G$. Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an indecomposable group. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {\mathbb G, \subseteq}$ is totally ordered.

label: Independence System Induced from Set of Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\mathscr A$ be a non-empty set of subsets of $S$. Let $\mathscr I = \set {X \subseteq S : \exists A \in \mathscr A : X \subseteq A}$. Then $\struct {S, \mathscr I}$ is an independence system.

snippet: == Examples of Independent Equations ==

label: Independent Events are Independent of Complement
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be events in a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Then $A$ and $B$ are independent $A$ and $\Omega \setminus B$ are independent.

label: Independent Sets of Dual Matroid
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $\mathscr B$ be the set of bases of the matroid $M$. Then the independent subsets of the dual $M^*$ of $M$ is: $\mathscr I^* = \set{X \subseteq S : \exists B \in \mathscr B : X \subseteq \paren{S \setminus B}}$

label: Independent Subset Contains No Dependent Subset
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $X \subseteq S$ be any independent subset of $M$. Then: No dependent subset $D$ of $M$ is a subset of $X$.

label: Index Laws for Field
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \circ}$ be a field with zero $0_F$ and unity $1_F$. Let $F^* = F \setminus {0_F}$ denote the set of elements of $F$ without the zero $0_F$. Then the following hold:

label: Index Laws for Monoids
snippet: These results are an extension of the results in Index Laws for Semigroup in which the domain of the indices is extended to include all integers. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e$. Let $a \in S$ be invertible for $\circ$. Let $n \in \N$. Let $a^n$ be the $n$th power of $a$: $a^n = \begin{cases} e : & n = 0 \\ a^{n - 1} \circ a : & n > 0 \\ \paren {a^{-n}}^{-1} : & n < 0 \end{cases}$ Then we have the following results:

label: Index is One iff Subgroup equals Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity element is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then: $\index G H = 1 \iff G = H$ where $\index G H$ denotes the index of $H$ in $G$.

label: Index of Proper Subgroup of Symmetric Group
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number such that $n > 4$. Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $A_n$ denote the alternating group on $n$ letters. $A_n$ is the only proper subgroup of $S_n$ whose index is less than $n$.

label: Index of Subsequence not Less than its Index
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \ge 1}$ be a sequence in a set $S$. Let $\sequence {x_{n_r} }$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}$. Then: $\forall n \in \N_{>0}: n_r \ge r$
