label: Inverse Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inverse Mappings ==

label: Inverse Mapping in Induced Structure of Homomorphism to Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, \oplus}$ be an abelian group. Let $f$ be a homomorphism from $S$ into $T$. Let $f^*$ be the pointwise inverse of $f$. Then $f^*$ is a homomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ}$ into $\struct {T, \oplus}$.

label: Inverse Mapping is Bijection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ and $g: T \to S$ be inverse mappings of each other. Then $f$ and $g$ are bijections.

label: Inverse Morphism is Unique
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $f: C \to D$ be an isomorphism of $\mathbf C$. Then $f$ admits a unique inverse morphism $g: D \to C$.

label: Inverse Probability/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inverse Probability ==

label: Inverse Relation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inverse Relations ==

label: Inverse Relation Equal iff Subset
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. If $\RR$ is a subset or superset of its inverse, then it equals its inverse. {{eqn | n = 1 | l = \RR | o = \subseteq | r = \RR^{-1} }} {{eqn | n = 2 | l = \RR^{-1} | o = \subseteq | r = \RR }} {{eqn | n = 3 | l = \RR | r = \RR^{-1} }}

label: Inverse Relation Functor is Contravariant Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Rel}$ be the category of relations. Let $C: \mathbf{Rel} \to \mathbf{Rel}$ be the inverse relation functor. Then $C$ is a contravariant functor.

label: Inverse for Complex Addition
snippet: Let $z = x + i y \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $-z = -x - i y \in \C$ be the negative of $z$. Then $-z$ is the inverse element of $z$ under the operation of complex addition: $\forall z \in \C: \exists -z \in \C: z + \paren {-z} = 0 = \paren {-z} + z$

label: Inverse for Complex Multiplication
Inverse for Integer Addition
snippet: Each element $x$ of the set of integers $\Z$ has an inverse element $-x$ under the operation of integer addition: $\forall x \in \Z: \exists -x \in \Z: x + \paren {-x} = 0 = \paren {-x} + x$

label: Inverse for Rational Addition
snippet: Each element $x$ of the set of rational numbers $\Q$ has an inverse element $-x$ under the operation of rational number addition: $\forall x \in \Q: \exists -x \in \Q: x + \paren {-x} = 0 = \paren {-x} + x$

label: Inverse for Rational Multiplication
Inverse for Real Addition
snippet: Each element $x$ of the set of real numbers $\R$ has an inverse element $-x$ under the operation of real number addition: $\forall x \in \R: \exists -x \in \R: x + \paren {-x} = 0 = \paren {-x} + x$

label: Inverse for Real Multiplication
Inverse in Group is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Then every element $x \in G$ has exactly one inverse: $\forall x \in G: \exists_1 x^{-1} \in G: x \circ x^{-1} = e^{-1} = x^{-1} \circ x$ where $e$ is the identity element of $\struct {G, \circ}$.

label: Inverse in Monoid is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid. Then an element $x \in S$ can have at most one inverse for $\circ$.

label: Inverse is Mapping implies Mapping is Injection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let the inverse $f^{-1} \subseteq T \times S$ itself be a mapping. Then $f$ is an injection.

label: Inverse is Mapping implies Mapping is Injection and Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let the inverse $f^{-1} \subseteq T \times S$ itself be a mapping. Then: $(1): \quad f$ is an injection $(2): \quad f$ is a surjection.

label: Inverse is Mapping implies Mapping is Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let the inverse $f^{-1} \subseteq T \times S$ itself be a mapping. Then $f$ is a surjection.

label: Inverse not always Unique for Non-Associative Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\circ$ be a non-associative operation. Then for any $x \in S$, it is possible for $x$ to have more than one inverse element.

label: Inverse of Algebraic Structure Isomorphism is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a mapping. Then $\phi$ is an isomorphism $\phi^{-1}: \struct {T, *} \to \struct {S, \circ}$ is also an isomorphism.

label: Inverse of Bijective Complete Lattice Homomorphism is Bijective Complete Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {A_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {A_2, \preceq_2}$ be complete lattices. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a bijective complete lattice homomorphism. Let $\phi^{-1} : A_2 \to A_1$ be the inverse of $\phi : A_1 \to A_2$. Then: $\phi^{-1} : L_2 \to L_1$ is a bijective complete lattice homomorphism.

label: Inverse of Circle Not Through Inversion Center
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle in the plane on center $O$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be an inversive transformation with $\CC$ as the inversion circle. Then $O$ is the inversion center. Let $K$ be an arbitrary circle distinct from $\CC$ and not through $O$. Then the image under $T$ of all the points on $K$ lie on the same circle, distinct from both $K$ and $\CC$.

label: Inverse of Circle Through Inversion Center is Straight Line Not Through Inversion Center
snippet: Let an arbitrary circle $K$ be drawn in the plane. Let $A'$ and $P'$ be arbitrary points on $K$. Let $T$ be an inversive transformation such that: the inversion center of $T$ is $O$ the inversion circle $O$ for $T$ is chosen such that $OA'$ is a diameter of $K$ the radius of $O$ is $r$. Let $A$ and $P$ be the images of $A'$ and $P'$ under $T$ respectively. Let $L$ be a straight line drawn perpendicular to the extension of $OA'$ at point $A$. Then $P$ lies on $L$.

label: Inverse of Commuting Pair
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $x, y \in S$ such that $x$ and $y$ are both invertible. Then $x$ commutes with $y$ : $\struct {x \circ y}^{-1} = x^{-1} \circ y^{-1}$

label: Inverse of Complete Lattice Isomorphism is Complete Lattice Isomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {A_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {A_2, \preceq_2}$ be complete lattices. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a complete lattice isomorphism. Let $\phi^{-1} : A_2 \to A_1$ be the inverse of $\phi : A_1 \to A_2$. Then: $\phi^{-1} : L_2 \to L_1$ is a complete lattice isomorphism

label: Inverse of Composition of Subsets of Topological Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \odot, \tau}$ be a topological group. Let $A, B \subseteq G$. Then: $\paren {A \odot B}^{-1} = B^{-1} \odot A^{-1}$

label: Inverse of Curve under Inversive Transformation
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle embedded in a Cartesian plane $\EE$ whose center $O$ is at the origin $\tuple {0, 0}$ and whose radius is $r$. Let $f$ be the inversive transformation of $\EE$ $\CC$. Let $P = \tuple {x, y}$ be an arbitrary point of $\CC$. The inverse point $P' = \tuple {x', y'}$ of $P$ under $f$ is given by: {{eqn | l = x' | r = \dfrac {r^2 x} {x^2 + y^2} }} {{eqn | l = y' | r = \dfrac {r^2 y} {x^2 + y^2} }}

label: Inverse of Diagonal Matrix
snippet: Let: $\mathbf D = \begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & a_{22} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & a_{nn} \\ \end{bmatrix}$ be an $n \times n$ diagonal matrix. Then its inverse is given by: $\mathbf D^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac 1 {a_{11}} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & \dfrac 1 {a_{22}} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {a_{nn}} \\ \end{bmatrix}$ provided that none of the diagonal elements are zero. If any of the diagonal elements are zero, $\mathbf D$ is singular.

label: Inverse of Diagonal Relation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\Delta_S$ denote the diagonal relation on $S$. Let ${\Delta_S}^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $\Delta_S$. Then: ${\Delta_S}^{-1} = \Delta_S$

label: Inverse of Direct Image Mapping does not necessarily equal Inverse Image Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $\RR^\to$ be the direct image mapping of $\RR$. Let $\RR^\gets$ be the inverse image mapping of $\RR$. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\paren {\RR^\to}^{-1} = \RR^\gets$ where $\paren {\RR^\to}^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $\RR^\to$. That is, the inverse of the direct image mapping of $\RR$ does not always equal the inverse image mapping of $\RR$.

label: Inverse of Direct Image Mapping is Direct Image Mapping of Inverse
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f :S \to T$ be a bijection. Let $f^\to$ be the direct image mapping of $f$. Then: $\paren {f^\to}^{-1} = \paren {f^{-1} }^{\to}$ where $f^{-1}$ and $\paren{f^\to}^{-1}$ denote the inverses of $f$ and $f^\to$ respectively

label: Inverse of Field Product with Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0$ and whose unity is $1$. Let $a, b \in F$ such that $a \ne 0$. Then: $\paren {a \times b^{-1} }^{-1} = b \times a^{-1}$ This can also be expressed using the notation of division as: $1 / \paren {a / b} = b / a$

label: Inverse of Generator of Cyclic Group is Generator
snippet: Let $\gen g = G$ be a cyclic group. Then: $G = \gen {g^{-1} }$ where $g^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $g$. Thus, in general, a generator of a cyclic group is not unique.

label: Inverse of Group Isomorphism is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {H, *}$ be groups. Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {H, *}$ be a mapping. Then $\phi$ is an isomorphism $\phi^{-1}: \struct {H, *} \to \struct {G, \circ}$ is also an isomorphism.

label: Inverse of Group Product
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $a, b \in G$, with inverses $a^{-1}, b^{-1}$. Then: $\paren {a \circ b}^{-1} = b^{-1} \circ a^{-1}$

label: Inverse of Homeomorphism between Metric Spaces is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A_1, d_1}, M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: M_1 \to M_2$ be a homeomorphism. Then $f^{-1}: M_2 \to M_1$ is also a homeomorphism.

label: Inverse of Homeomorphism is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T, T'$ be topological spaces. Let $f: T \to T'$ be a homeomorphism. Then $f^{-1}: T' \to T$ is also a homeomorphism.

label: Inverse of Identity Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $I_S: S \to S$ be the identity mapping on $S$. Then the inverse of $I_S$ is itself: $\paren {I_S}^{-1} = I_S$

label: Inverse of Inverse of Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a nonsingular matrix. Then: $\paren {\mathbf A^{-1} }^{-1} = \mathbf A$ That is, a nonsingular matrix equals the inverse of its inverse.

label: Inverse of Linear Function on Real Numbers
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ be real numbers such that $a \ne 0$. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = a x + b$ Then the inverse of $f$ is given by: $\forall y \in \R: \map {f^{-1} } y = \dfrac {y - b} a$

label: Inverse of Linear Operator is Linear Operator
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space. Let $A : X \to X$ be an invertible (in the sense of a mapping) linear transformation with inverse mapping $A^{-1} : X \to X$. Then $A^{-1}$ is a linear operator.

label: Inverse of Linear Transformation is Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $V$ and $U$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $A : V \to U$ be an invertible (in the sense of a mapping) linear transformation with inverse mapping $A^{-1} : U \to V$. Then $A^{-1}$ is a linear transformation.

label: Inverse of Mapping to Annihilator on Algebraic Dual is Bijection
snippet: Let $G$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over a field. Let $J: G \to G^{**}$ be the evaluation isomorphism. Let $G^*$ be the algebraic dual of $G$. Let $M$ be an $m$-dimensional subspace of $G$. Let $M^\circ$ be the annihilator of $M$. Let $N$ be a $p$-dimensional subspace of $G^*$. Let $G_m$ denote the set of all $m$-dimensional subspaces of $G$. Let ${G^*}_{n - m}$ denote the set of all $n - m$-dimensional subspaces of $G^*$.

label: Inverse of Matrix Exponential
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix. Let $t \in \R$ be a real number. Let $e^{\mathbf A t}$ denote the matrix exponential of $\mathbf A$. Then: $\paren {e^{\mathbf A t} }^{-1} = e^{-\mathbf A t}$ where $\paren {e^{\mathbf A t} }^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $e^{\mathbf A t}$.

label: Inverse of Matrix Product
snippet: Let $\mathbf {A, B}$ be square matrices of order $n$ Let $\mathbf I$ be the $n \times n$ unit matrix. Let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be nonsingular. Then the matrix product $\mathbf {AB}$ is also nonsingular, and: $\paren {\mathbf A \mathbf B}^{-1} = \mathbf B^{-1} \mathbf A^{-1}$

label: Inverse of Matrix is Scalar Product of Adjugate by Reciprocal of Determinant
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_n$ be a nonsingular square matrix of order $n$. Let $\map \det {\mathbf A}$ be the determinant of $\mathbf A$. Let $\adj {\mathbf A}$ be the adjugate of $\mathbf A$. Then: $\mathbf A^{-1} = \dfrac 1 {\map \det {\mathbf A} } \cdot \adj {\mathbf A}$ where $\mathbf A^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $\mathbf A$

label: Inverse of Neighborhood of Diagonal Point is Neighborhood
snippet: Let $T = \struct{X, \tau}$ be a topological Space. Let $\tau_{X \times X}$ denote the product topology on the cartesian product $X \times X$. Let $x \in X$. Let $R$ be a neighborhood of $\tuple{x,x}$ in the product space $\struct{X \times X, \tau_{X \times X}}$. Let $R^{-1}$ denote the inverse relation of $R$ where $R$ is viewed as a relation on $X \times X$. Then: $R^{-1}$ is a neighborhood of $\tuple{x,x}$ in $\struct{X \times X, \tau_{X \times X}}$.

label: Inverse of Nonsingular 2 x 2 Real Square Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be an nonsingular $2 \times 2$ real square matrix defined as: $\mathbf A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$ Then its inverse matrix $\mathbf A^{-1}$ is: $\mathbf A^{-1} = \dfrac 1 {\map \det {\mathbf A} } \begin {pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end {pmatrix} = \dfrac 1 {a d - b c} \begin {pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end {pmatrix}$

label: Inverse of Open Set in Product Space is Open in Inverse Product Space
snippet: Let $\struct{S_1, \tau_1}$ and $\struct{S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $\tau_{S_1 \times S_2}$ be the product topology on the Cartesian product $S_1 \times S_2$. Let $\tau_{S_2 \times S_1}$ be the product topology on the Cartesian product $S_2 \times S_1$. Let $V \subseteq S_1 \times S_2$. Let $V^{-1} \subseteq S_2 \times S_1$ denote the inverse of $V$ viewed as a relation on $S_1 \times S_2$. Then: $V$ is open in $\struct{S_1 \times S_2, \tau_{S_1 \times S_2}}$ $V^{-1}$ is open in $\struct{S_2 \times S_1, \tau_{S_2 \times S_1}}$

label: Inverse of Pascal's Triangle expressed as Matrix
snippet: Consider Pascal's triangle expressed as a (square) matrix $\mathbf M$, with the top left element holding $\dbinom 0 0$. $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 3 & 3 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 4 & 6 & 4 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 5 & 10 & 10 & 5 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 6 & 15 & 20 & 15 & 6 & 1 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 7 & 21 & 35 & 35 & 21 & 7 & 1 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 8 & 28 & 56 & 70 & 56 & 28 & 8 & 1 & \cdots \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots…

label: Inverse of Permutation is Permutation
snippet: If $f$ is a permutation of $S$, then so is its inverse $f^{-1}$.

label: Inverse of Plane Reflection Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf R$ be the matrix associated with a reflection in the plane. $\mathbf R = \begin{bmatrix} \cos 2\alpha & \sin 2\alpha \\ \sin 2\alpha & -\cos 2\alpha \end{bmatrix}$ Then its inverse matrix $\mathbf R^{-1}$ is itself.

label: Inverse of Plane Rotation Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf R$ be the matrix associated with a rotation of the plane about the origin through an angle of $\alpha$: $\mathbf R = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \alpha & -\sin \alpha \\ \sin \alpha & \cos \alpha \end{bmatrix}$ Then its inverse matrix $\mathbf R^{-1}$ is: $\mathbf R^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \alpha & \sin \alpha \\ -\sin \alpha & \cos \alpha \end{bmatrix}$

label: Inverse of Similarity Mapping
snippet: Let $G$ be a vector space over a field $K$. Let $\beta \in K$ such that $\beta \ne 0$. Let $s_\beta: G \to G$ be the similarity on $G$ defined as: $\forall \mathbf x \in G: \map {s_\beta} {\mathbf x} = \beta \mathbf x$ Let $\paren {s_\beta}^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $s_\beta$. Then: $\paren {s_\beta}^{-1} = s_{\beta^{-1} }$ where $\beta^{-1}$ is the multiplicative inverse in $K$ of $\beta$.

label: Inverse of Square Matrix over Field is Unique
snippet: Let $\Bbb F$ be a field, usually one of the standard number fields $\Q$, $\R$ or $\C$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\map \MM n$ denote the matrix space of order $n$ square matrices over $\Bbb F$. Let $\mathbf B$ be an inverse matrix of $\mathbf A$. Then $\mathbf B$ is the only inverse matrix of $\mathbf A$.

label: Inverse of Stirling's Triangle expressed as Matrix
snippet: Consider Stirling's triangle of the first kind (signed) expressed as a (square) matrix $\mathbf A$, with the top left element holding $\map s {0, 0}$. $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 1 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 0 & -6 & 11 & -6 & 1 & 0 & \cdots \\ 0 & 24 & -50 & 35 & -10 & 1 & \cdots \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots \\ \end{pmatrix}$ Then consider Stirling's triangle of the second kind expressed as a (square) matrix $\mathbf B$, with the top left element…

label: Inverse of Straight Line Not Through Inversion Center is Circle Through Inversion Center
snippet: Let $C$ be a circle on center $O$ in the plane. Let $T : X \to Y$ be an inversive transformation with $C$ as the inversion circle. Then $O$ is the inversion center. Let $L$ be an arbitrary straight line not containing $O$. Let $P$ be an arbitrary point on $L$. Let $P'$ be the image of $P$ under $T$. Then $P'$ lies on a circle through $O$.

label: Inverse of Subset of Relation is Subset of Inverse
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets Let $\RR_1 = S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR_2 \subseteq \RR_1$. Then: $\RR_2^{-1} \subseteq \RR_1^{-1}$ where $\RR_1^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $\RR_1$.

label: Inverse of Transitive Relation is Transitive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Let $\RR$ be transitive. Then its inverse $\RR^{-1}$ is also transitive.

label: Inverse of Transpose of Matrix is Transpose of Inverse
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix over a field. Let $\mathbf A^\intercal$ denote the transpose of $\mathbf A$. Let $\mathbf A$ be an nonsingular matrix. Then $\mathbf A^\intercal$ is also nonsingular and: $\paren {\mathbf A^\intercal}^{-1} = \paren {\mathbf A^{-1} }^\intercal$ where $\mathbf A^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $\mathbf A$.

label: Inverse of Unit in Centralizer of Ring is in Centralizer
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a subset of $R$. Let $\map {C_R} S$ denote the centralizer of $S$ in $R$ Let $u \in R$ be a unit of $R$. Then: $u \in \map {C_R} S \implies u^{-1} \in \map {C_R} S$

label: Inverse of Vandermonde Matrix
snippet: Let $V_n$ be the Vandermonde matrix of order $n$ given by: $V_n = \begin {bmatrix} x_1 & x_2 & \cdots & x_n \\ x_1^2 & x_2^2 & \cdots & x_n^2 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ x_1^n & x_2^n & \cdots & x_n^n \end{bmatrix}$ Then its inverse $V_n^{-1} = \sqbrk b_n$ can be specified as: $b_{i j} = \begin {cases} \paren {-1}^{j - 1} \paren {\dfrac {\ds \sum_{\substack {1 \mathop \le m_1 \mathop

label: Inverse of a Line Through Circle Center is a Line
snippet: Let $C$ be a circle in the plane on center $O$. Let the radius of $C$ be $r$. Let $L$ be an arbitrary ray through $O$. Let $P$ be an otherwise arbitrary point, but lying on $L$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be an inversive transformation with $C$ as the inversion circle. Then $O$ is the inversion center. Then the image of $P$ under $T$ also lies on $L$.

label: Inverse reverses Preorder of Positive Invertible Elements of Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\le_A$ be the canonical preordering on $A$. Let $a, b \in A$ be positive and invertible such that: $a \le_A b$ Then we have: $0 \le_A b^{-1} \le_A a^{-1}$

label: Inversion Mapping is Automorphism iff Group is Abelian
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\iota: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping on $G$, defined as: $\forall g \in G: \map \iota g = g^{-1}$ Then $\iota$ is an automorphism $G$ is abelian.

label: Inversion Mapping is Isomorphism from Ordered Abelian Group to its Dual
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered Abelian group. Let $\struct {G, \circ, \succcurlyeq}$ be the dual of $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$. Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq} \to \struct {G, \circ, \succcurlyeq}$ be the inversion mapping from $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ to $\struct {G, \circ, \succcurlyeq}$ defined as: $\forall x \in G: \map \phi x = x^{-1}$ where $x^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $x$ in $\struct {G, \circ}$. Then $\phi$ is an isomorphism.

label: Inversion Mapping is Isomorphism to Opposite Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\struct {G, *}$ be its opposite group. That is: $\forall g, h \in G: g \circ h = h * g$ Let $\iota: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping for $\struct {G, \circ}$. Then $\iota: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {G, *}$ is a group isomorphism.

label: Inversion Mapping is Permutation
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\iota: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping on $G$. Then $\iota$ is a permutation on $G$.

label: Inversion Mapping on Topological Group is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T = \struct {G, \circ, \tau}$ be a topological group. Let $\phi: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping of $T$. Then $\phi$ is a homeomorphism.

label: Invertibility of Identity Minus Operator
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator such that: $\norm T_{\map \BB X} < 1$ where $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map \BB X}$ denotes the norm of a bounded linear operator. Then $I - T$ is invertible as a bounded linear operator. In particular: $\ds \paren {I - T}^{-1} = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty T^n$

label: Invertible Element of Associative Structure is Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure where $\circ$ is associative. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity element $e_S$. An element of $\struct {S, \circ}$ which is invertible is also cancellable.

label: Invertible Elements of Monoid form Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity element is $e$. Let $U \subseteq S$ be the subset of $S$ consisting of the invertible elements of $S$. Then $\struct {U, \circ}$ forms a subgroup of $S$.

label: Invertible Elements of Monoid form Subgroup of Cancellable Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $C$ be the set of all cancellable elements of $S$. Let $T$ be the set of all invertible elements of $S$. Then $\struct {T, \circ}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {C, \circ}$.

label: Invertible Matrix Corresponds with Change of Basis
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $G$ be an $n$-dimensional unitary $R$-module. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be an ordered basis of $G$. Let $\mathbf P = \sqbrk \alpha_n$ be a square matrix of order $n$ over $R$. Let $\ds \forall j \in \closedint 1 n: b_j = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \alpha_{i j} a_i$. Then $\sequence {b_n}$ is an ordered basis of $G$ $\mathbf P$ is nonsingular.

label: Involution is Permutation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an involution. Then $f$ is a permutation.

label: Irrational Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Irrational Numbers ==

label: Irrational Number Space is Completely Metrizable
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is completely metrizable.

label: Irrational Number Space is Completely Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is a completely normal space.

label: Irrational Number Space is Non-Meager
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is non-meager.

label: Irrational Number Space is Paracompact
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is paracompact.

label: Irrational Number Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is second-countable.

label: Irrational Number Space is Separable
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is separable.

label: Irrational Number Space is not Scattered
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is not scattered.

label: Irrational Number divided by Rational Number is Irrational
snippet: Let $x$ be a irrational number. Let $y$ be a non-zero rational number. Then: $\dfrac x y$ is irrational.

label: Irrational Numbers are Uncountably Infinite
snippet: The set $\R \setminus \Q$ of irrational numbers is uncountable.

label: Irrational Numbers form G-Delta Set in Reals
snippet: Let $\R \setminus \Q$ denote the set of irrational numbers. Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $\R \setminus \Q$ forms a $G_\delta$ set in $\R$.

label: Irrational Numbers form Metric Space
snippet: Let $\mathbb I = \R \setminus \Q$ be the set of all irrational numbers. Let $d: \mathbb I \times \mathbb I \to \R$ be defined as: $\map d {x_1, x_2} = \size {x_1 - x_2}$ where $\size x$ is the absolute value of $x$. Then $d$ is a metric on $\mathbb I$ and so $\struct {\mathbb I, d}$ is a metric space.

label: Irrational Slope Space is T2
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

label: Irrational Slope Space is not Regular
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is not a regular space.

label: Irrational Slope Space is not T2.5
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is not a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space.

label: Irrationality of Logarithm
snippet: Let $a, b \in \N_{>0}$ such that both $\nexists m, n \in \N_{>0}: a^m = b^n$. Then $\log_b a$ is irrational.

label: Irreducible Component is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $Y$ be an irreducible component of $T$. Then $Y$ is closed in $T$.

label: Irreducible Components of Hausdorff Space are Points
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty Hausdorff space. Then the irreducible components of $T$ are the singleton sets.

label: Irreducible Elements of 5th Cyclotomic Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {i \sqrt 5}, +, \times}$ denote the $5$th cyclotomic ring. The following elements of $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {i \sqrt 5}, +, \times}$ are irreducible: $2$ $3$ $1 + i \sqrt 5$ $1 - i \sqrt 5$

label: Irreducible Elements of Ring of Integers
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ be the ring of integers. The irreducible elements of $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ are the prime numbers and their negatives.

label: Irreducible Hausdorff Space is Singleton
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space which is irreducible and Hausdorff. Then $S$ is a singleton.

label: Irreducible Polynomial/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Irreducible Polynomials ==

label: Irreducible Representations of Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \cdot}$ be a finite abelian group. Let $V$ be a non-null vector space over an algebraically closed field $K$. Let $\rho: G \to \GL V$ be a linear representation. Then $\rho$ is irreducible $\map {\dim_K} V = 1$, where, $\dim_K$ denotes dimension.

label: Irreducible Space is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is irreducible. Then $T$ is connected.

label: Irreducible Space is Locally Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is irreducible. Then $T$ is locally connected.

label: Irreducible Space is Pseudocompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is irreducible. Then $T$ is pseudocompact.

label: Irreducible Space is not necessarily Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is irreducible. Then $T$ is not necessarily path-connected.

label: Irreducible Space is not necessarily Ultraconnected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is irreducible. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is ultraconnected.

label: Irreducible Subspace is Contained in Irreducible Component
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S_1, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space. Let $S_2$ be an irreducible subset of $S_1$. Then there exists an irreducible component $S_3$ of $T$ such that $S_2 \subseteq S_3$.

label: Is 2 to the power of Euler's Number Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether $2$ to the power of Euler's number $e$: $2^e$ is rational or irrational.

label: Is 2 to the power of Pi Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether $2$ to the power of $\pi$ (pi): $2^\pi$ is rational or irrational.

label: Is Apéry's Constant Transcendental?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether Apéry's constant $\map \zeta 3$ is transcendental or not.

label: Is Catalan's Constant Irrational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether Catalan's constant is rational or irrational.

label: Is Euler's Number Normal?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether Euler's Number $e$ is normal.

label: Is Euler's Number to the power of Euler's Number Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether Euler's number $e$ to the power of itself: $e^e$ is rational or irrational.

label: Is Euler's Number to the power of Pi Squared Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether Euler's number $e$ to the power of $\pi$ (pi) squared: $e^{\pi^2}$ is rational or irrational. Category:Open Questions

label: Is Euler-Mascheroni Constant Irrational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not even known whether the Euler-Mascheroni constant $\gamma$ is irrational, let alone whether it is transcendental or not.

label: Is Log of Pi Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether the logarithm of $\pi$ (pi): $\ln \pi$ is rational or irrational.

label: Is Pi Normal?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether $\pi$ (pi) is normal.

label: Is Pi multiplied by Euler's Number Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether the product of $\pi$ (pi) and Euler's number $e$: $\pi \times e$ is rational or irrational.

label: Is Pi plus Euler's Number Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether the sum of $\pi$ (pi) and Euler's number $e$: $\pi + e$ is rational or irrational.

label: Is Pi to the power of Euler's Number Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether $\pi$(pi) to the power of Euler's number $e$: $\pi^e$ is rational or irrational. Its decimal expansion gives its value to be approximately: $\pi^e \approx 22 \cdotp 45915 \, 77183 \, 61045 \, 47342 \, 7152 \ldots$

label: Is there an Infinite Number of Primes of Form n^2 + 1?
snippet: == Open Question == Is there an infinite number of prime numbers of the form $n^2 + 1$?

label: Isolated Point in Metric Space iff Isolated Point in Topological Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $T = \struct {A, \tau}$ be the topological space with the topology induced by $d$. Let $H \subseteq A$. Let $x \in H$ Then: $x$ is an isolated point of $H$ in $M$ $x$ is an isolated point of $H$ in $T$

label: Isolated Point of Closure of Subset is Isolated Point of Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq T$ be a subset of $T$. Let $\map \cl H$ denote the closure of $H$. Let $x \in \map \cl H$ be an isolated point of $\map \cl H$. Then $x$ is also an isolated point of $H$.

label: Isolated Points in Subsets of Modified Fort Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{a, b} }$ be a modified Fort space. Let $H \subseteq S$ contain more than two points. Then $H$ contains an isolated point.

label: Isometric Image of Cauchy Sequence is Cauchy Sequence
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, d_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be an isometry. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a Cauchy sequence in $S_1$. Let $\sequence {y_n} = \sequence {\map f {x_n} }$ be the image of $\sequence {x_n}$ under $f$. Then $\sequence {y_n}$ is a Cauchy sequence.

label: Isometric Metric Spaces/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Isometric Metric Spaces ==

label: Isometric Metric Spaces are Homeomorphic
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be isometric. Then $M_1$ and $M_2$ are homeomorphic.

label: Isometry Invariance of Riemannian Distance Function
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ and $\struct {\tilde M, \tilde g}$ be connected Riemannian manifolds with or without boundaries. Let $\phi : M \to \tilde M$ be an isometry. Let $x, y \in M$ be points. Let $\map {d_g} {x, y}$ be the Riemannian distance between $x$ and $y$. Then: $\map {d_{\tilde g} } {\map \phi x, \map \phi y} = \map {d_g} {x, y}$

label: Isometry Invariance of Riemannian Length of Admissible Curve
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ and $\struct {\tilde M, \tilde g}$ be Riemannian manifolds with or without boundary. Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\gamma : \closedint a b \to M$ with $t \stackrel \gamma \mapsto \map \gamma t$ be an admissible curve. Let $\phi : M \to \tilde M$ be an isometry. Let $\map {L_g} \gamma$ be the Riemannian length of $\gamma$ from $t = a$ to $t = b$. Then: $\map {L_g} {\gamma} = \map {L_{\tilde g} } {\phi \circ \gamma}$ where $\circ$ denotes the composition of mappings.

label: Isometry Preserves Sequence Convergence
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {S_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {S_2, d_2}$ both be metric spaces or pseudometric spaces. Let $\phi: S_1 \to S_2$ be an isometry. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be an infinite sequence in $S_1$. Suppose that $\sequence {x_n}$ converges to a point $p \in S_1$. Then $\sequence {\map \phi {x_n}}$ converges to $\map \phi p$.

label: Isometry between Metric Spaces is Continuous
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $\phi: M_1 \to M_2$ be an isometry. Then $\phi: M_1 \to M_2$ is a continuous mapping.

label: Isometry is Homeomorphism of Induced Topologies
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, d_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces or pseudometric spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be an isometry from $\struct {S_1, d_1}$ to $\struct {S_2, d_2}$. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be the topologies induced on $S_1$ and $S_2$ by the metrics $d_1$ and $d_2$, respectively. Then $f$ is a homeomorphism from $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ to $\struct {S_2, \tau_2}$.

label: Isometry of Metric Spaces is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be metric spaces. Let $M_1 \sim M_2$ denote that $M_1$ and $M_2$ are isometric. The relation $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

label: Isometry of Metric Spaces is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: M_1 \to M_2$ be an isometry. Then $f$ is a homeomorphism from $M_1$ to $M_2$.

label: Isomorphic Ordinals are Equal
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be ordinals that are order isomorphic. Then $A = B$.

snippet: == Examples of Isomorphisms ==

label: Isomorphism (Category Theory) is Epic
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ and $D$ be objects of $\mathbf C$. Let $f: C \to D$ be an isomorphism. Then $f: C \twoheadrightarrow D$ is epic.

label: Isomorphism (Category Theory) is Monic
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ and $D$ be objects of $\mathbf C$. Let $f: C \to D$ be an isomorphism. Then $f: C \rightarrowtail D$ is monic.

label: Isomorphism Preserves Commutativity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an isomorphism. Then $\circ$ is commutative $*$ is commutative.

label: Isomorphism Preserves Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an isomorphism. Then $\circ$ has an identity $e_S$ $\map \phi {e_S}$ is the identity for $*$.

label: Isomorphism between Additive Group Modulo 16 and Multiplicative Group Modulo 17
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z_{16}, +}$ denote the additive group of integers modulo $16$. Let $\struct {\Z'_{17}, \times}$ denote the multiplicative group of reduced residues modulo $17$. Let $\phi: \struct {\Z_{16}, +} \to \struct {\Z'_{17}, \times}$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall \eqclass k {16} \in \struct {\Z_{16}, +}: \map \phi {\eqclass k {16} } = \eqclass {3^k} {17}$ Then $\phi$ is a group isomorphism.

label: Isomorphism between Algebraic Structures induces Isomorphism between Induced Structures
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ and $\struct {T, \otimes}$ be algebraic structures. Let: $S^A$ denote the set of mappings from $A$ to $S$ $T^A$ denote the set of mappings from $A$ to $T$. Let: $\struct {S^A, \odot}$ denote the algebraic structure on $S^A$ induced by $\odot$ $\struct {T^A, \otimes}$ denote the algebraic structure on $T^A$ induced by $\otimes$. Let $\phi$ be an isomorphism from $S$ to $T$. Let $\chi: S^A \to T^A$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall f \in S^A: \map \chi f = \phi \circ f$ where: $\phi \circ f$ denotes the composition of $\phi$ with $f$.

label: Isomorphism between Gaussian Integer Units and Integers Modulo 4 under Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {U_\C, \times}$ be the group of Gaussian integer units under complex multiplication. Let $\struct {\Z_n, +_4}$ be the integers modulo $4$ under modulo addition. Then $\struct {U_\C, \times}$ and $\struct {\Z_4, +_4}$ are isomorphic algebraic structures.

label: Isomorphism between Group of Units Ring of Integers Modulo 2^n and C2 x C2^(n-2)
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer and $n \ge 2$. Let $R = \struct {\Z / 2^n \Z, +, \times}$ be the ring of integers modulo $2^n$. Let $U = \struct {\paren {\Z / 2^n \Z}^\times, \times}$ denote the group of units of $R$. Let $C_2$ be cyclic group of order $2$. Let $C_{2^{n - 2} }$ be the cyclic group of order $2^{n - 2}$. Then $U$ is isomorphic to the group direct product of $C_2$ and $C_{2^{n - 2} }$.

label: Isomorphism between Group of Units of Ring of Integers Modulo p^n and C((p-1)p^(n-1))
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $R = \struct {\Z / p^n \Z, +, \times}$ be the ring of integers modulo $p^n$. Let $U = \struct {\paren {\Z / p^n \Z}^\times, \times}$ denote the group of units of $R$. Let $C_{(p - 1)p^{n - 1}}$ be be cyclic group of order $(p - 1)p^{n - 1}$. Then $U$ is isomorphic to $C_{(p - 1)p^{n - 1}}$.

label: Isomorphism between Roots of Unity under Multiplication and Integers under Modulo Addition
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {R_n, \times}$ be the complex $n$th roots of unity under complex multiplication. Let $\struct {\Z_n, +_n}$ be the integers modulo $n$ under modulo addition. Then $\struct {R_n, \times}$ and $\struct {\Z_n, +_n}$ are isomorphic algebraic structures.

label: Isomorphism between Symmetry Group of Regular Pentagon and Subgroup of Symmetric Group
snippet: Let $\PP = ABCDE$ denote a regular pentagon. Let $\struct {\PP, \circ}$ be the symmetry group of $\PP$, where the various symmetries are identified as: the identity mapping $e$ the rotations $r, r^2, r^3, r^4$ of $72^\circ, 144^\circ, 216^\circ, 288^\circ$ around the center of $\PP$ anticlockwise respectively the reflections $t_A, t_B, t_C, t_D, t_E$ about the lines through the center of $\PP$ and the vertices $A$ to $E$ respectively. 600px Let $\struct {S_5, \circ}$ denote the symmetry group on $5$ letters. Then $\PP$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\struct {S_5, \circ}$ of order $10$.

label: Isomorphism from Cartesian Space to Finite-Dimensional Subspace of Hausdorff Topological Vector Space is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Hausdorff topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $n \in \N$. Let $Y$ be a subspace of $X$ with dimension $n$. Let $f : \GF^n \to Y$ be a vector space isomorphism. Then $f$ is a homeomorphism.

label: Isomorphism iff Isomorphism in Dual Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $\mathbf C^{\operatorname{op}}$ be the dual category of $\mathbf C$. Let $f$ be a morphism of $\mathbf C$. Then $f$ is an isomorphism in $\mathbf C$ $f^{\operatorname{op}}$ is an isomorphism in $\mathbf C^{\operatorname{op}}$.

label: Isomorphism in Isomorphic Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be an isomorphism of categories. Let $f$ be a morphism of $\mathbf C$. Then $f$ is an isomorphism in $\mathbf C$ $Ff$ is an isomorphism in $\mathbf D$.

label: Isomorphism is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Isomorphism is an equivalence on a set of magmas. This result applies to all magmas: rings, groups, R-algebraic structures etc.

label: Isomorphism of Abelian Groups
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {H, *}$ be a group isomorphism. Then $\struct {G, \circ}$ is abelian $\struct {H, *}$ is abelian.

label: Isomorphism of External Direct Products
snippet: Let: $\struct {S_1 \times S_2, \circ}$ be the external direct product of two algebraic structures $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$ $\struct {T_1 \times T_2, *}$ be the external direct product of two algebraic structures $\struct {T_1, *_1}$ and $\struct {T_2, *_2}$ $\phi_1$ be an isomorphism from $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ onto $\struct {T_1, *_1}$ $\phi_2$ be an isomorphism from $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$ onto $\struct {T_2, *_2}$.

label: Isomorphism of Finite Group with Permutations of Quotient with Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $H$ contain no non-trivial normal subgroup of $G$. Let $G / H$ denote the left coset space of $G$ by $H$. Then $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of the group of permutations $\map \Gamma {G / H}$ of $G / H$.

label: Isomorphism of Functor Over Object Comma Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $G : \mathbf E \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\paren{G \downarrow C}$ denote the comma category $G$ over $C$. Let $k : \tuple{E_1, g_1} \to \tuple{E_2, g_2}$ be a morphism in $\paren{G \downarrow C}$. Then: $k$ is an isomorphism in $\paren{G \downarrow C}$ $k: E_1 \to E_2 \in \mathbf E$ is an isomorphism such that $g_1 = g_2 \circ G k$

label: Isomorphism of Functor Under Object Comma Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $F : \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\paren{C \downarrow F}$ denote the comma category $F$ under $C$. Let $h : \tuple{D_1, f_1} \to \tuple{D_2, f_2}$ be a morphism in $\paren{C \downarrow F}$. Then: $h$ is an isomorphism in $\paren{C \downarrow F}$ $h: D_1 \to D_2 \in \mathbf D$ is an isomorphism such that $f_2 = F h \circ f_1$

label: Isomorphisms between Additive Group of Integers Modulo 4 and Reduced Residue System Modulo 5 under Multiplication
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z_4, +_4}$ denote the additive group of integers modulo $4$. Let $\struct {\Z'_5, \times_5}$ denote the multiplicative group of reduced residues modulo $5$. There are $2$ (group) isomorphisms from $\struct {\Z_4, +_4}$ onto $\struct {\Z'_5, \times_5}$.

label: Isosceles Triangle has Two Equal Angles
snippet: In isosceles triangles, the angles at the base are equal to each other. Also, if the equal straight lines are extended, the angles under the base will also be equal to each other.

label: Isotropic at Point and Homogeneous Riemannian Manifold is Isotropic
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $M$ be isotropic at any $p \in M$. Let $M$ be homogeneous. Then $M$ is isotropic.

label: Jacobi's Equation is Variational Equation of Euler's Equation
snippet: The Variational equation of Euler's equation is Jacobi's equation.

label: Jacobi's Necessary Condition
snippet: Let $J$ be a functional, such that: $J \sqbrk y = \ds \int_a^b \map F {x, y, y'} \rd x$ Let $\map y x$ correspond to the minimum of $J$. Let: $F_{y'y'}>0$ along $\map y x$. Then the open interval $\openint a b$ contains no points conjugate to $a$.

label: Jacobi's Theorem
snippet: Let $\mathbf y = \sequence {y_i}_{1 \le i \le n}$, $\boldsymbol \alpha = \sequence {\alpha_i}_{1 \le i \le n}$, $\boldsymbol \beta = \sequence {\beta_i}_{1 \le i \le n}$ be vectors, where $\alpha_i$ and $ \beta_i$ are parameters. Let $S = \map S {x, \mathbf y, \boldsymbol \alpha}$ be a a complete solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Let: $\begin {vmatrix} \dfrac {\partial^2 S} {\partial \alpha_i \partial y_k} \end{vmatrix} \ne 0$ where $\begin {vmatrix} \cdot \end{vmatrix}$ is a determinant.

label: Jadhav Theorem
snippet: Let $a, b, c$ be real numbers in arithmetic sequence. Let the common difference of this arithmetic sequence be $d$. Then: $b^2 - a c = d^2$

label: Jensen's Formula
snippet: Let $S$ be an open subset of the complex plane containing the closed disk: $D_r = \set {z \in \C : \cmod z \le r}$ of radius $r$ about $0$. Let $f: S \to \C$ be holomorphic on $S$. Let $f$ have no zeroes on the circle $\cmod z = r$. Let $\map f 0 \ne 0$. Let $\rho_1, \ldots, \rho_n$ be the zeroes of $f$ in $D_r$, counted with multiplicity. Then: $(1): \quad \ds \frac 1 {2 \pi} \int_0^{2 \pi} \ln \cmod {\map f {r e^{i \theta} } } \rd \theta = \ln \cmod {\map f 0} + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {\ln r - \ln \size {\rho_k} }$

label: Jensen's Inequality
snippet: Jensen's Inequality (Real Analysis) Jensen's Inequality (Complex Analysis) Jensen's Inequality (Measure Theory) Conditional Jensen's Inequality Category:Jensen's Inequality

label: Jensen's Inequality (Complex Analysis)
snippet: Let $D \subset \C$ be an open set with $0 \in D$. Let $R > 0$ be such that $\map B {0, R} \subset D$. Let $f: D \to \C$ be analytic with $\map f 0 \ne 0$. Let $\cmod {\map f z} \le M$ for $\cmod z \le R$. Let $0 < r <R$. Then the number of zeroes of $f$, counted with multiplicity, for $\cmod z \le r$, is at most: $\dfrac {\map \log {M / \cmod {\map f 0} } } {\map \log {R / r} }$

label: Jensen's Inequality (Measure Theory)
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function such that $f \ge 0$ pointwise.

label: Jensen's Inequality (Real Analysis)
snippet: Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $\phi: I \to \R$ be a convex function. Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in I$. Let $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \ldots, \lambda_n \ge 0$ be real numbers, at least one of which is non-zero. Then: $\ds \map \phi {\frac {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_k x_k} {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_k} } \le \frac {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_k \map \phi {x_k} } {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_k}$ For $\phi$ strictly convex, equality holds $x_1 = x_2 = \cdots = x_n$.

label: Joachimsthal's Section-Formulae
snippet: Let $P = \tuple {x_1, y_1}$ and $Q = \tuple {x_2, y_2}$ be points in the Cartesian plane. Let $R = \tuple {x, y}$ be a point on $PQ$ dividing $PQ$ in the ratio: $PR : RQ = l : m$ Then: {{eqn | l = x | r = \dfrac {l x_2 + m x_1} {l + m} }} {{eqn | l = y | r = \dfrac {l y_2 + m y_1} {l + m} }}

label: Join Operation on Ordered Set such that Every Doubleton admits Supremum is Entropic
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be such that every doubleton subset of $S$ admits a supremum. Let $\vee$ be the join operation on $S$, defined as: $\forall a, b \in S: a \vee b = \sup_\preccurlyeq \set {a, b}$ Then $\vee$ is an entropic operation.

label: Join Semilattice Ideal iff Ordered Set Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice. Let $I \subseteq S$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then: $I$ is a join semilattice ideal of $\struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ $I$ is an ordered set ideal of $\struct {S, \preceq}$.

label: Join Semilattice Ordered Subset Not Always Subsemilattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semilattice. Let $\preceq$ be the ordering on $S$ defined by: $a \preceq b \iff \paren {a \circ b} = b$ Let $T$ be a subset of $S$. Let the ordered subset $\struct {T, \preceq \restriction_T}$ be a join semilattice. Let $\vee$ be the binary operation on $T$ defined by: for all $a, b \in T$: $a \vee b$ is the join of $a$ and $b$ $\preceq \restriction_T$. Then: $\struct {T, \vee}$ may not be a subsemilattice of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

label: Join and Meet in Inclusion Ordered Set of Topology
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $L = \left({\tau, \preceq}\right)$ be an inclusion ordered set of $\tau$. Let $X, Y \in \tau$. Then $X \vee Y = X \cup Y$ and $X \wedge Y = X \cap Y$

label: Join in Inclusion Ordered Set
snippet: Let $P = \left({X, \subseteq}\right)$ be an inclusion ordered set. Let $A, B \in X$ such that $A \cup B \in X$ Then $A \vee B = A \cup B$

label: Join of Finite Sub-Sigma-Algebras Generates Join of Finite Partitions
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $\BB, \CC \subseteq \Sigma$ be finite sub-$\sigma$-algebras. Then: $\map \xi {\BB \vee \CC} = \map \xi \BB \vee \map \xi \CC$ where: $\map\xi\cdot$ denotes the generated finite partition $\vee$ on the denotes the join of finite sub-$\sigma$-algebras $\vee$ on the denotes the join of finite partitions

label: Join of Sets of Integer Multiples is Set of Integer Multiples of GCD
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$. Let $m \Z$ denote the set of integer multiples of $m$ Let $r \in \Z$ such that: $m \Z \subseteq r \Z$ and: $n \Z \subseteq r \Z$ Then: $\gcd \set {m, n} \Z \subseteq r \Z$ where $\gcd$ denotes greatest common divisor.

label: Joining Arcs makes Another Arc
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $\mathbb I \subseteq \R$ be the closed unit interval $\closedint 0 1$. Let $a, b, c$ be three distinct points of $T$. Let $f, g: \mathbb I \to T$ be arcs in $T$ from $a$ to $b$ and from $b$ to $c$ respectively. Let $h: \mathbb I \to T$ be the mapping given by: $\map h x = \begin {cases} \map f {2 x} & : x \in \closedint 0 {\dfrac 1 2} \\ \map g {2 x - 1} & : x \in \closedint {\dfrac 1 2} 1 \end {cases}$ Then either: $h$ is an arc in $T$ or There exists some restriction of $h$ which, possibly after reparametrisation, is an arc in $T$.

label: Joining Injective Paths makes Another Injective Path
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $\mathbb I \subseteq \R$ be the closed unit interval $\closedint 0 1$. Let $a, b, c$ be three distinct points of $T$. Let $f, g: \mathbb I \to T$ be injective paths in $T$ from $a$ to $b$ and from $b$ to $c$ respectively. Let $h: \mathbb I \to T$ be the mapping given by: $\map h x = \begin{cases} \map f {2 x} & : x \in \closedint 0 {\dfrac 1 2} \\ \map g {2 x - 1} & : x \in \closedint {\dfrac 1 2} 1 \end{cases}$ Then either: $h$ is an injective path in $T$ or There exists some restriction of $h$ which, possibly after reparametrisation, is an injective path…

label: Joining Paths makes Another Path
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be the closed real interval $\closedint 0 1$. Let $f, g: I \to T$ be paths in $T$ from $a$ to $b$ and from $b$ to $c$ respectively. Let $h: I \to T$ be the mapping given by: $\map h x = \begin{cases} \map f {2x} & : x \in \closedint 0 {\dfrac 1 2} \\ \map g {2x - 1} & : x \in \closedint {\dfrac 1 2} 1 \end{cases}$ Then $h$ is a path in $T$.

label: Joins of Homeomorphic Spaces are Homeomorphic
snippet: Let $X, Y, X', Y'$ be topological spaces. Suppose that: $X \sim X'$ $Y \sim Y'$ where $\sim$ denotes homeomorphic spaces. Then: $(X \ast Y) \sim (X' \ast Y')$ where $\ast$ denotes the join.

label: Jordan's Lemma
snippet: Let $r > 0$ be a real number. Let: $C_r = \set {r e^{i \theta}: 0 \le \theta \le \pi}$ Let $g : C_r \to \C$ be a continuous function. Define $f : C_r \to \C$ by: $\map f z = e^{i a z} \map g z$ for each $z \in C_r$, for some real number $a > 0$. Then: $\ds \size {\int_{C_r} \map f z \rd z} \le \frac \pi a \paren {\max_{0 \mathop \le \theta \mathop \le \pi} \size {\map g {r e^{i \theta} } } }$

label: Jordan-Hölder Theorem
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $\HH_1$ and $\HH_2$ be two composition series for $G$. Then: $\HH_1$ and $\HH_2$ have the same length Corresponding factors of $\HH_1$ and $\HH_2$ are isomorphic.

label: Jordan Curve Bounding Loop in Euclidean Plane
snippet: Let $f : \closedint 0 1 \to \R^2$ be a loop in the Euclidean plane $\R^2$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Then there exists a Jordan curve $\gamma : \closedint 0 1 \to \R^2$ such that $\Img f \subseteq \Int \gamma$, and for all $t \in \closedint 0 1$: $\map d {\map \gamma t, \Img f} < \epsilon$ where $\map d {\map \gamma t, \Img f}$ denotes the Euclidean distance between $\map \gamma t$ and $\Img f$. Here $\Img f$ denotes the image of $f$, and $\Int \gamma$ denotes the interior of $\gamma$.

label: Jordan Curve Characterization of Simply Connected Set
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \R^2$ be an open path-connected subset of the Euclidean plane. Then $D$ is simply connected, the following condition holds: For all Jordan curves $\gamma : \closedint 0 1 \to \R^2$ with $\Img \gamma \subseteq D$, we have: $\Int \gamma \subseteq D$ Here $\Img \gamma$ denotes the image of $\gamma$, and $\Int \gamma$ denotes the interior of $f$.

label: Jordan Curve Image Equals Set Homeomorphic to Circle
snippet: Let $C \subseteq \R^2$ be a subset of the Euclidean space $\R^2$. Let $\mathbb S^1$ denote the unit circle whose center is at the origin of the Euclidean space $\R^2$. Let $\tau_C$ and $\tau_{\mathbb S^1}$ be the subspace topologies on $C$ respectively $\mathbb S^1$ induced by the Euclidean topology on $\R^2$. Then $\struct{ C, \tau_C }$ is homeomorphic to $\struct { \mathbb S^1 , \tau_{\mathbb S^1} }$, there exists a Jordan curve $\gamma : \closedint 0 1 \to \R^2$ with image equal to $C$.

label: Jordan Curve Theorem
snippet: Let $\gamma: \closedint 0 1 \to \R^2$ be a Jordan curve. Let $\Img \gamma$ denote the image of $\gamma$. Then $\R^2 \setminus \Img \gamma$ is a union of two disjoint connected components. Both components are open in $\R^2$, and both components have $\Img \gamma$ as their boundary. One component is bounded, and is called the interior of $\gamma$. The other component is unbounded, and is called the exterior of $\gamma$.

label: Jordan Curve and Jordan Arc form Two Jordan Curves
snippet: Let $\gamma: \closedint a b \to \R^2$ be a Jordan curve, where $\closedint a b$ is the closed real interval between $a, b \in \R$ with $a < b$. Let the interior of $\gamma$ be denoted $\Int \gamma$. Let the image of $\gamma$ be denoted $\Img \gamma$. Let $\sigma: \closedint c d \to \R^2$ be a Jordan arc such that: $\map \sigma c, \map \sigma d \in \Img \gamma$ and: $\forall t \in \openint c d: \map \sigma t \in \Int \gamma$ Let $t_1 = \map {\gamma^{-1} } {\map \sigma c}$. Let $t_2 = \map {\gamma^{-1} } {\map \sigma d}$. Let $t_1 < t_2$.

label: Jordan Decomposition Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a signed measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $\tuple {P, N}$ be a Hahn decomposition of $\mu$. Then there exists measures $\mu^+$ and $\mu^-$ on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ such that: $\mu = \mu^+ - \mu^-$ Further, at least one of $\mu^+$ and $\mu^-$ is finite.

label: Jordan Polygon Interior and Exterior Criterion
snippet: Let $P$ be a polygon embedded in $\R^2$. Let $q \in \R^2 \setminus \partial P$, where $\partial P$ denotes the boundary of $P$. Let $\mathbf v \in \R^2 \setminus \set \bszero$ be a non-zero vector. Let $\LL = \set {q + s \mathbf v: s \in \R_{\ge 0} }$ be a ray with start point $q$. Let $\map N q \in \N$ be the number of crossings between $\LL$ and $\partial P$.

label: Jordan Polygon Parity Lemma
snippet: Let $P$ be a polygon embedded in $\R^2$. Let $U \subseteq \R^2 \setminus \partial P$ be a path-connected subset of $\R^2 \setminus \partial P$. Let $q \in U$, and let $\mathbf v \in \R^2 \setminus \set {\mathbf 0}$ be a non-zero vector. Let $\LL = \set {q + s \mathbf v: s \in \R_{\ge 0} }$ be a ray with start point $q$. Then: $(1): \quad$ The parity $\map {\operatorname{par} } q$ is independent of the choice of $v$. $(2): \quad$ All points in $U$ have the same parity.

label: Jordan Polygon Theorem
snippet: Let $P$ be a polygon embedded in $\R^2$. Denote the boundary of $P$ as $\partial P$. Then, $\R^2 \setminus \partial P$ is a union of two connected components. Both components are open in $\R^2$. One component is bounded, and is called the interior of $P$. The other component is unbounded, and is called the exterior of $P$.

label: Josephus Problem
snippet: == Classic Problem == This is the original Josephus problem, of which all others are variants. , along with $40$ comrades in arms, have opted to commit suicide rather than fall into the hands of the Romans. Because he really wants to stay alive, he suggests that they all stand in a circle, and count around it. Every $3$rd person counted was to drop out of the circle and die. Where did place himself, and his companion who also did not want to die, so that the two of them would remain the last two standing?
