snippet: == Lemma == Let $G$ be a finite group such that $\order G = k p^n$ where $p \nmid k$. Let $\mathbb S = \set {S \subseteq G: \order S = p^n}$ Let $G$ act on $\mathbb S$ by the group action defined in Group Action on Sets with k Elements: $\forall S \in \mathbb S: g * S = g S = \set {x \in G: x = g s: s \in S}$ Then:

label: Orchard Planting Problem
snippet: == Classic Problem == A given number $n$ of trees are to be planted in an orchard so as to make the number of rows of $k$ trees the largest number possible. That is: $n$ points are to be configured in the plane so that the number of straight lines that can be drawn through exactly $k$ of these points is maximised.

label: Order-Convex Subset of Ordered Set is not necessarily Interval
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $C$ be an order-convex subset of $S$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $C$ is an interval of $S$.

label: Order-Extension Principle
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\preceq$ be an ordering on $S$. Then there exists a total ordering $\le$ on $S$ such that: $\forall a, b \in S: \paren {a \preceq b \implies a \le b}$

label: Order-Preserving Identity Mapping between Ordered Structures not necessarily Isomorphism
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be orderings on $A$ such that: $\forall a, b \in A: a \mathrel \RR b \implies a \mathrel \SS b$ Let $I_A$ denote the identity mapping on $A$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $I_A$ is an order isomorphism from the ordered structures $\struct {A, \RR}$ and $\struct {A, \SS}$.

label: Order 2 Square Matrices with Zero Diagonals do not form Ring
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of square matrices of order $2$ whose diagonal elements are zero. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {S, +, \times}$ is not a ring. Note that $\times$ denotes conventional matrix multiplication.

label: Order Embedding/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Order Embeddings ==

label: Order Embedding into Image is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $S'$ be the image of a mapping $\phi: \struct {S, \preceq_1} \to \struct {T, \preceq_2}$. Then: $\phi$ is an order embedding from $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ into $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ $\phi$ is an order isomorphism from $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ into $\struct {S', \preceq_2 \restriction_{S'} }$.

label: Order Generating iff Every Element is Infimum
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X$ is order generating $\forall x \in S: \exists Y \subseteq X: x = \inf Y$

label: Order Generating iff Every Superset Closed on Infima is Whole Space
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X$ is order generating $\forall Y \subseteq S: Y \supseteq X \land \paren {\forall Z \subseteq Y: \inf Z \in Y} \implies Y = S$

label: Order Generating iff Not Preceding implies There Exists Element Preceding and Not Preceding
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X$ is order generating $\forall x, y \in S: \paren {y \npreceq x \implies \exists p \in X: x \preceq p \land y \npreceq p}$

label: Order Isomorphism/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Order Isomorphisms ==

label: Order Isomorphism Preserves Infima and Suprema
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ and $L' = \struct {S', \preceq'}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: S \to S'$ be an order isomorphism between $L$ and $L'$. Then $f$ preserves infima and suprema.

label: Order Isomorphism between Ordinals and Proper Class
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \prec}$ be a strict well-ordering. Let $A$ be a proper class. Let the initial segment of $x$ be a set for every $x \in A$. Then we may make the following definitions: Set $G$ equal to the collection of ordered pairs $\tuple {x, y}$ such that: $y \in A \setminus \Img x$ $\paren {A \setminus \Img x} \cap A_y = \O$ Use the First Principle of Transfinite Recursion to construct a mapping $F$ such that: The domain of $F$ is the class of all ordinals $\On$ For all ordinals $x$, $\map F x = \map G {F {\restriction_x} }$ Then $F: \On \to A$ is an order isomorphism between $\struct…

label: Order Isomorphism between Tosets is not necessarily Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be tosets. Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1} \cong \struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$, that is, let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be order isomorphic. Then it is not necessarily the case that there is exactly one mapping $f: S_1 \to S_2$ such that $f$ is an order isomorphism.

label: Order Isomorphism is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Order isomorphism between ordered sets is an equivalence relation. So any given family of ordered sets can be partitioned into disjoint classes of isomorphic sets.

label: Order Isomorphism on Strictly Well-Founded Relation preserves Strictly Well-Founded Structure
snippet: Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be classes. Let $\prec_1$ and $\prec_2$ be relations. Let $\phi: \struct {A_1, \prec_1} \to \struct {A_2, \prec_2}$ be an order isomorphism. Then $\struct {A_1, \prec_1}$ is a strictly well-founded structure $\struct {A_2, \prec_2}$ is also a strictly well-founded structure.

label: Order Isomorphism on Well-Ordered Set preserves Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\phi: \struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1} \to \struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be an order isomorphism. Then $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ is a well-ordered set $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is also a well-ordered set.

label: Order Modulo n of Power of Integer
snippet: Let $a$ have multiplicative order $c$ modulo $n$. Then for any $k \ge 1$, $a^k$ has multiplicative order $\dfrac c {\gcd \set {c, k}}$ modulo $n$.

label: Order Statistic/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Order Statistics ==

label: Order Sum of Well-Founded Orderings is Well-Founded Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\preccurlyeq_1$ and $\preccurlyeq_2$ be well-founded. Then the order sum $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1} \oplus \struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ of $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is also well-founded.

label: Order Type Addition is not Commutative
snippet: The operation of order type addition is not commutative.

label: Order Type of Integers under Usual Ordering
snippet: Consider the ordered structure $\struct {\Z, \le}$ that is the set of integers under the usual ordering. Then: $\map \ot {\Z, \le} = \omega^* + \omega$ where: $\ot$ denotes order type $\omega$ denotes the order type of the natural numbers $\N$ $\omega^*$ denotes the dual of $\omega$ $+$ denotes addition of order types.

label: Order is Maximum of Exponent of Convergence and Degree
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function. Let $\omega$ be its order. Let $\tau$ be its exponent of convergence. Let $h$ be the degree of the polynomial in its canonical factorization. Then: $\omega = \map \max {\tau, h}$

label: Order is Preserved on Positive Reals by Squaring
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R: x > 0, y >0$. Then: $x < y \iff x^2 < y^2$

label: Order of 5 in Units of Ring of Integers Modulo 2^n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer and $n \ge 2$. Let $\struct {\Z / 2^n \Z, +, \times}$ be the ring of integers modulo $2^n$. Let $U = \struct {\paren {\Z / 2^n \Z}^\times, \times}$ denote the group of units of $\struct {\Z / 2^n \Z, +, \times}$. The order of $5$ in $U$ is $2^{n - 2}$.

label: Order of Alternating Group
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 1$. Let $A_n$ be the alternating group on $n$ letters. Then: $\order {A_n} = \dfrac {n!} 2$ where $\order {A_n}$ denotes the order of $A_n$.

label: Order of Automorphism Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group whose order is greater than $2$. Let $\Aut G$ be the automorphism group of $G$. Then the order of $\Aut G$ is greater than $1$.

label: Order of Automorphism Group of Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $C_n$ denote the cyclic group of order $n$. Let $\Aut {C_n}$ denote the automorphism group of $C_n$. Then: $\order {\Aut {C_n} } = \map \phi n$ where: $\order {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the order of a group $\map \phi n$ denotes the Euler $\phi$ function.

label: Order of Automorphism Group of Dihedral Group
snippet: Let $D_n$ denote the dihedral group of order $n$. Let $\Aut {D_n}$ denote the automorphism group of $D_n$. Then: $\order {\Aut {D_n} } = n \cdot \map \phi n$ where: $\order {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the order of a group $\map \phi n$ is the Euler $\phi$ function.

label: Order of Automorphism Group of Prime Group
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $G$ be a group of order $p$. Let $\Aut G$ denote the automorphism group of $G$. Then: $\order {\Aut G} = p - 1$ where $\order {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the order of a group.

label: Order of Convergence Implies Convergence
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be an real sequence that converges to $\alpha$ with order $p$, where $p \ge 1$. Then, $\sequence {x_n}$ converges to $\alpha$.

label: Order of Cyclic Group equals Order of Generator
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite cyclic group which is generated by $a \in G$. Then: $\order a = \order G$ where: $\order a$ denotes the order of $a$ in $G$ $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$.

label: Order of Differential Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Orders of Differential Equations ==

label: Order of Dihedral Group
snippet: The dihedral group $D_n$ is of order $2 n$.

label: Order of Divisor Count Function
snippet: For all $x \ge 1$: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop \le x} \map {\sigma_0} n = x \log x + \paren {2 \gamma - 1} x + \map \OO {\sqrt x}$ where: $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant $\map {\sigma_0} n$ is the divisor count function.

label: Order of Element Divides Order of Finite Group
snippet: In a finite group, the order of a group element divides the order of its group: $\forall x \in G: \order x \divides \order G$

label: Order of Element divides Order of Centralizer
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $x \in G$ be an element of $G$. Let $\map {C_G} x$ denote the centralizer of $x$. Then: $\order x \divides \order {\map {C_G} x}$ where: $\order x$ denotes the order of $x$ in $G$ $\divides$ denotes divisibility $\order {\map {C_G} x}$ denotes the order of $\map {C_G} x$.

label: Order of Element in Group equals its Order in Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H \le G$, where $\le$ denotes the property of being a subgroup. Let $x \in H$. Then the order of $x$ in $H$ equals the order of $x$ in $G$.

label: Order of Element in Quotient Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $G / H$ be the quotient group of $G$ by $H$. The order of $a H \in G / H$ divides the order of $a \in G$.

label: Order of Elements in Quaternion Group
snippet: Let $Q = \Dic 2$ be the quaternion group, whose group presentation is given by: $\Dic 2 = \gen {a, b: a^4 = e, b^2 = a^2, a b a = b}$ Then $\Dic 2$ has: $1$ element of order $2$ and: $6$ elements of order $4$.

label: Order of Finite Abelian Group with p+ Order p Elements is Divisible by p^2
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $G$ be a finite abelian group whose identity is $e$. Let $G$ have at least $p$ elements of order $p$. Then: $p^2 \divides \order G$ where: $\divides$ denotes divisibility $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$.

label: Order of Finite p-Group is Power of p
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $p$ be a prime number. Let all elements of $G$ have order a power of $p$. Then $G$ is a $p$-group.

label: Order of Floor Function
snippet: Let $\floor x$ denote the floor function of $x$. Then: $\floor x = x + \map \OO 1$ where $\OO$ is big-O notation.

label: Order of General Linear Group over Galois Field
snippet: Let $\GF$ be a Galois field with $p$ elements. Then the order of the general linear group $\GL {n, \GF}$ is: $\ds \prod_{j \mathop = 1}^n \paren {p^n - p^{j - 1} }$

label: Order of Group Element/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Order of Group Element ==

label: Order of Group Element in Group Direct Product
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be finite groups. Let $g \in G: \order g = m, h \in H: \order h = n$. Then $\order {\tuple {g, h} }$ in $G \times H$ is $\lcm \set {m, n}$.

label: Order of Group equals Sum of Squares of Degrees of Characters
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $S$ be a set of representatives of the conjugacy classes of $G$: one such representative from each conjugacy class. Let $n$ be defined as: $n = \ds \sum_{x \mathop \in S} \paren {\map \deg {\map {\chi_\rho} x} }^2$ where $\map \deg {\map {\chi_\rho} x}$ denotes the degree of the character of an arbitrary irreducible linear representation of $G$. Then: $n = \order G$ where $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$.

label: Order of Group of Units of Integers Modulo n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be an integer. Let $\struct {\Z / n \Z, +, \cdot}$ be the ring of integers modulo $n$. Let $U = \struct {\paren {\Z / n \Z}^\times, \cdot}$ denote the group of units of this ring. Then: $\order U = \map \phi n$ where $\phi$ denotes the Euler $\phi$-function.

label: Order of Homomorphic Image of Group Element
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups whose identities are $e_G$ and $e_H$ respectively. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a homomorphism. Let $g \in G$ be of finite order. Then: $\forall g \in G: \order {\map \phi g} \divides \order g$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibility.

label: Order of Monomorphic Image of Group Element
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups whose identities are $e_G$ and $e_H$ respectively. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a monomorphism. Let $g \in G$ be of finite order. Then: $\forall g \in G: \order {\map \phi g} = \order g$

label: Order of Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z'_m, \times_m}$ denote the multiplicative group of reduced residues modulo $m$. The order of $\struct {\Z'_m, \times_m}$ is $\map \phi m$, where $\phi$ denotes the Euler $\phi$ function.

label: Order of Möbius Function
snippet: Let $\mu$ denote the Möbius function . Then: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop \le N} \map \mu n = \map o N$ where $o$ denotes little-o notation.

label: Order of Natural Logarithm Function
snippet: Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number. Then: $\ln x = \map \OO {x^\epsilon}$ as $x \to \infty$ and: $\ln x = \map \OO {x^{-\epsilon} }$ as $x \to 0^+$ where $\OO$ is big-O notation.

label: Order of Product of Abelian Group Elements Divides LCM of Orders of Elements
snippet: Let $G$ be an abelian group. Let $a, b \in G$. Then: $\order {a b} \divides \lcm \set {\order a, \order b}$ where: $\order a$ denotes the order of $a$ $\divides$ denotes divisibility $\lcm$ denotes the lowest common multiple.

label: Order of Product of Entire Function with Polynomial
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function of order $\omega$. Let $P: \C \to \C$ be a nonzero polynomial. Then $f \cdot P$ has order $\omega$.

label: Order of Quotient Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $G / N$ be the quotient group of $G$ by $N$. Then: $\dfrac {\order G} {\order N} = \order {G / N}$ where $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$.

label: Order of Second Chebyshev Function
snippet: Let $x \ge 2$ be a real number. Then: $\ds \map \psi x = \sum_{p \mathop \le x} \ln p + \map \OO {\sqrt x \paren {\ln x}^2}$ where: $\OO$ is big-O notation $\psi$ is the Second Chebyshev Function the sum runs over the primes less than or equal to $x$.

label: Order of Shifted Entire Function
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function of order $\alpha$. Let $a \in \C$. Then $\map f {z + a}$ has order $\alpha$.

label: Order of Squares in Ordered Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ be an ordered ring whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $x, y \in \struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ such that $0_R \le x, y$. Then: $x \le y \implies x \circ x \le y \circ y$ When $R$ is one of the standard sets of numbers, that is $\Z, \Q, \R$, then this translates into: If $x, y$ are positive then $x \le y \implies x^2 \le y^2$.

label: Order of Squares in Totally Ordered Ring without Proper Zero Divisors
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ be a totally ordered ring without proper zero divisors whose zero is $0_R$. Let $x, y \in R$ be positive, that is, $0_R \le x, y$. Then $x \le y \iff x \circ x \le y \circ y$. That is, the square mapping is an order embedding of $\struct {R_{\ge 0}, \le}$ into itself. When $R$ is one of the standard sets of numbers $\Z, \Q, \R$, then this translates into: If $x, y$ are positive, then $x \le y \iff x^2 \le y^2$.

label: Order of Subgroup Product
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of $G$. Then: $\order {H K} = \dfrac {\order H \order K} {\order {H \cap K} }$ where: $H K$ denotes subset product $\order H$ denotes the order of $H$. {{questionable|The does not make sense if $\order {H \cap K} +\infty$, because it is then $\dfrac {+\infty}{+\infty}$. Can someone check the source?}}

label: Order of Subgroup of Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $C_n = \gen g$ be the cyclic group of order $n$ which is generated by $g$ whose identity is $e$. Let $a \in C_n: a = g^i$. Let $H = \gen a$. Then: $\order H = \dfrac n {\gcd \set {n, i} }$ where: $\order H$ denotes the order of $H$ $\gcd \set {n, i}$ denotes the greatest common divisor of $n$ and $i$.

label: Order of Sum of Reciprocal of Primes
snippet: Let $x \ge 2$ be a real number. We have: $\ds \sum_{p \mathop \le x} \frac 1 p = \map \ln {\ln x} + \map \OO 1$ where: $\ds \sum_{p \mathop \le x}$ sums over the primes less than or equal to $x$ $\OO$ is big-$\OO$ notation.

label: Order of Sum over Primes of Logarithm of p over p
snippet: We have: $\ds \sum_{p \mathop \le x} \frac {\ln p} p = \ln x + \map \OO 1$ where: $\ds \sum_{p \mathop \le x}$ sums over the primes less than or equal to $x$ $\OO$ is big-$\OO$ notation.

label: Order of Symmetric Group
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set of cardinality $n$. Let $\struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$ be the symmetric group on $S$. Then $\struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$ has $n!$ elements (see factorial).

label: Ordered Basis for Coordinate Plane
snippet: Let $a_1, a_2 \in \R^2$ such that $\set {a_1, a_2}$ forms a linearly independent set. Then $\tuple {a_1, a_2}$ is an ordered basis for the $\R$-vector space $\R^2$. Hence the points on the plane can be uniquely identified by means of linear combinations of $a_1$ and $a_2$.

label: Ordered Field with Archimedean Property on which Monotone Convergence Theorem Holds has Continuum Property
snippet: Let $\FF$ be an ordered field on which the Archimedean property holds. Let $\FF$ be such that every sequence which is increasing and bounded above is convergent. Then every non-empty subset of $\FF$ which is bounded above has a supremum.

label: Ordered Pair/Kuratowski Formalization/Motivation
snippet: The only reason for the Kuratowski formalization of ordered pairs: $\tuple {a, b} = \set {\set a, \set {a, b} }$ is so their existence can be justified in the strictures of the axiomatic set theory, in particular Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory (ZF). Once that has been demonstrated, there is no need to invoke it again. The fact that this formulation allows that: $\tuple {a, b} = \tuple {c, d} \iff a = c, b = d$ is its stated aim. The fact that $\set {a, b} \in \tuple {a, b}$ is an unfortunate side-effect brought about by means of the definition.

label: Ordered Pair/Kuratowski Formalization/Warning
snippet: == Warning == The weakness of the Kuratowski formalization of the ordered pair shows up when $a = b$: {{eqn | l = \tuple {a, a} | r = \set {\set a, \set {a, a} } | c = }} {{eqn | r = \set {\set a, \set a} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \set {\set a} | c = }} Thus the ordered pair degenerates into the set $\set {\set a}$. Most works on this subject gloss over this point, and indeed, completely fail to mention it.

label: Ordered Semigroup Monomorphism into Image is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, *, \preccurlyeq}$ be ordered semigroups. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ, \preceq} \to \struct {T, *, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered semigroup monomorphism. Let $S'$ be the image of $\phi$. Then $\phi$ is an ordered semigroup isomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ into $\struct {S', * {\restriction_{S'} }, \preccurlyeq \restriction_{S'} }$. Here: $* {\restriction_{S'}}$ denotes the restriction of $*$ to $S' \times S'$ $\preccurlyeq \restriction_{S'}$ denotes the restriction of $\preccurlyeq$ to $S' \times S'$.

label: Ordered Set may not have Maximal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. It may be the case that $S$ has no maximal elements.

label: Ordered Set may not have Minimal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. It may be the case that $S$ has no minimal elements.

label: Ordered Set of All Mappings is Lattice iff Codomain is Lattice or Domain is Empty
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\struct {T^S, \preccurlyeq}$ denote the ordered set of all mappings from $S$ to $T$. Then: $\struct {T^S, \preccurlyeq}$ is a lattice either: $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq}$ is a lattice or: $S = \O$

label: Ordered Set of All Mappings is Ordered Set
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X$ be a set. Then $L^X$ is also an ordered set.

label: Ordered Set of Auxiliary Relations is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $\map {\operatorname {Aux} } L$ be the set of all auxiliary relations on $S$. Let $P = \struct {\map {\operatorname {Aux} } L, \precsim}$ be an ordered set where $\precsim \mathop = \subseteq \restriction_{\map {\operatorname {Aux} } L \times \map {\operatorname {Aux} } L}$ Then $P$ is a complete lattice.

label: Ordered Set of Closure Operators and Dual Ordered Set of Closure Systems are Isomorphic
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}\right)$ be a complete lattice. Then $\operatorname{Closure}\left({L}\right)$ and $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)^{-1}$ are order isomorphic where $\operatorname{Closure}\left({L}\right)$ denotes the ordered set of closure operators of $L$, $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)$ denotes the ordered set of closure systems oj $L$, $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)^{-1}$ denotes the dual to $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)$.

label: Ordered Set of Closure Systems is Ordered Set
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Then $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)$ is an ordered set, where $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)$ denotes the ordered set of closure systems.

label: Ordered Set with Greatest Element whose Subsets have Infimum is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set such that: $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ has a greatest element $u$ every non-empty subset of $S$ admits an infimum. Then $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ is a complete lattice.

label: Ordered Subset of Ordered Set is Ordered Set
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\struct {S', \preceq'}$ be an ordered subset of $L$. Then $\struct {S', \preceq'}$ is an ordered set.

label: Ordering/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Orderings ==

label: Ordering Induced by Injection is Ordering
snippet: Let $\left({T, \le}\right)$ be an ordered set, and let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Then $\le_f$, the ordering induced by $f$, is an ordering.

label: Ordering Principle
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then there exists a total ordering on $S$.

label: Ordering is Equivalent to Subset Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then there exists a set $\mathbb S$ of subsets of $S$ such that: $\struct {S, \preceq} \cong \struct {\mathbb S, \subseteq}$ where: $\struct {\mathbb S, \subseteq}$ is the relational structure consisting of $\mathbb S$ and the subset relation $\cong$ denotes order isomorphism. Hence any ordering on a set can be modelled uniquely by a set of subsets of that set under the subset relation. Specifically: Let $\mathbb S := \set {a^\preceq: a \in S}$ where $a^\preceq$ is the lower closure of $a$.

label: Ordering is Preordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an ordering on $S$. Then $\RR$ is also a preordering on $S$.

label: Ordering is Preserved on Integers by Addition
snippet: The usual ordering on the integers is preserved by the operation of addition: $\forall a, b, c, d, \in \Z: a \le b, c \le d \implies a + c \le b + d$

label: Ordering of Cardinality of Sets is Well-Defined
snippet: The relation $\le$ in the context of cardinalities of sets is well-defined in the sense that: if $\card A = \card {A'}$ and $\card B = \card {B'}$, then there exists an injection from $A$ into $B$ there exists an injection from $A'$ into $B'$.

label: Ordering of Cardinals Compatible with Cardinal Product
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be cardinals. Then: $\mathbf a \le \mathbf b \implies \mathbf a \mathbf c \le \mathbf b \mathbf c$ where $\mathbf a \mathbf c$ denotes the product of $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf c$.

label: Ordering of Cardinals Compatible with Cardinal Sum
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be cardinals. Then: $\mathbf a \le \mathbf b \implies \mathbf a + \mathbf c \le \mathbf b + \mathbf c$ where $\mathbf a \mathbf c$ denotes the sum of $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf c$.

label: Ordering of Natural Numbers is Provable
snippet: Let $x, y \in \N$. Suppose $x < y$. Let $\sqbrk a$ denote the unary representation of $a \in \N$. Then $\sqbrk x < \sqbrk y$ is a theorem of minimal arithmetic.

label: Ordering of Rational Cuts preserves Ordering of Associated Rational Numbers
snippet: Let $p \in\ Q$ and $q \in \Q$ be rational numbers. Let $p^*$ and $q^*$ denote the rational cuts associated with $p$ and $q$. Then: $p^* < q^* \iff p < q$ where $p^* < q^*$ denotes the strict ordering on cuts defined as: $\beta < \gamma \iff \exists p \in \Q: p \in \beta, p \notin \gamma$

label: Ordering of Real Numbers is Reversed by Negation
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ in $\R$ be real numbers such that: $x \le y$ Then: $-y \le -x$ where $-y$ and $-x$ are the negatives of $y$ and $x$ respectively.

label: Ordering of Reciprocals
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers such that $x, y \in \openint 0 \to$ or $x, y \in \openint \gets 0$ Then: $x \le y \iff \dfrac 1 y \le \dfrac 1 x$

label: Ordering on Closure Operators iff Images are Including
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be closure operators on $L$. Then: $f \preceq g$ $g \sqbrk S \subseteq f \sqbrk S$ where $\preceq$ denotes the ordering on mappings $f \sqbrk S$ denotes the image of $f$.

label: Ordering on Cuts is Total
snippet: Let $\CC$ denote the set of cuts. Let $<$ denote the strict ordering on cuts defined as: $\forall \alpha, \beta \in \CC: \alpha < \beta \iff \exists p \in \Q: p \in \alpha, p \notin \beta$ Then $<$ is a (strict) total ordering on $\CC$.

label: Ordering on Integers is Transitive
snippet: Let $\eqclass {a, b} {}$ denote an integer, as defined by the formal definition of integers. Then: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = \le | r = \eqclass {c, d} {} | c = }} {{eqn | lo= \land | l = \eqclass {c, d} {} | o = \le | r = \eqclass {e, f} {} | c = }} {{eqn | ll= \implies | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = \le | r = \eqclass {e, f} {} | c = }} That is, ordering on the integers is transitive.

label: Ordering on Multiindices is Partial Order
snippet: Let $Z$ be the set of multiindices indexed by a set $J$. The ordering on $Z$ is a partial ordering.

label: Ordering on Ordinal is Subset Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be an ordinal. Then $\forall x, y \in S:$ $x \in y \iff x \prec y \iff S_x \subsetneqq S_y \iff x \subsetneqq y$ where $S_x$ and $S_y$ are the initial segments of $S$ determined by $x$ and $y$ respectively. Thus there is no need to specify what the ordering on an ordinal is -- it is always the subset relation.

label: Ordering on Partition Determines Preordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\PP$ be a partition of $S$. Let $\phi: S \to \PP$ be the quotient mapping. Let $\preceq$ be a ordering of $\PP$. Define a relation $\precsim$ on $S$ by letting $p \precsim q$ : $\map \phi p \preceq \map \phi q$ Then: $\precsim$ is a preordering on $S$. $\precsim$ is the only preordering on $S$ that induces the $\preceq$ ordering on $\PP$.

label: Ordering on Real Numbers from Decimal Expansion
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $x$ and $y$ be expressed by their decimal expansions: Let $\preccurlyeq_l$ be the lexicographic ordering on $\R$ defined as: $x \preccurlyeq_l y$ : $m \prec n$ or: $m = n$ and $\exists k \in \Z_{>0}: \paren {\forall j: 1 \le j 0}: d_j = e_j$. Then: $x \le y$ where $\le$ denotes the usual ordering on $\R$.

label: Orderings on Set with 3 Elements
snippet: == Examples of Orderings == Let $S = \set {a, b, c}$ be an arbitrary set with $3$ elements. The following are all the orderings that can be applied to $S$, grouped into isomorphism classes. In the below, $\tuple {x, y}$ indicates that $x \preccurlyeq y$ for the ordering $\preccurlyeq$ under consideration.

label: Orderings on Set with 4 Elements
snippet: == Examples of Orderings == Let $S$ be an arbitrary set with $4$ elements. The following are the Hasse diagrams for the $15$ isomorphism classes of all the possible orderings on $S$: 600px Of the above, $\text{(l)}$ and $\text{(o)}$ are lattice orderings.

label: Ordinal Addition/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Ordinal Addition ==

label: Ordinal Addition by Zero
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $\O$ be the zero ordinal. Then: $x + \O = x = \O + x$ where $+$ denotes ordinal addition.

label: Ordinal Addition is Associative
snippet: Ordinal addition is associative, i.e.: $\paren {x + y} + z = x + \paren {y + z}$ holds for all ordinals $x$, $y$ and $z$.

label: Ordinal Addition is Closed
snippet: Let $\On$ be the class of all ordinals. Then: $\forall x, y \in \On: x + y \in \On$ That is: the sum $x+y$ is an ordinal.

label: Ordinal Addition is Left Cancellable
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $\paren {z + x} = \paren {z + y} \implies x = y$ That is, ordinal addition is left cancellable.

label: Ordinal Data/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Ordinal Data ==

label: Ordinal Equal to Rank
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $S$ be a small class. Let $\map V x$ denote the von Neumann hierarchy on the ordinal $x$. Then $x$ equals the rank of $S$ $S \in \map V {x + 1} \land S \notin \map V x$.

label: Ordinal Exponentiation is Closed
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $x^y \in \On$ That is, ordinal exponentiation is closed.

label: Ordinal Exponentiation of Terms
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Let $n$ be a finite ordinal. Let $x$ be a limit ordinal. Let $y, z, n$ all be greater than $0$. Then: $\paren {x^y \times n}^z = x^{y \mathop \times z} \times n$ if $z$ is not a limit ordinal $\paren {x^y \times n}^z = x^{y \mathop \times z}$ if $z$ is a limit ordinal.

label: Ordinal Exponentiation via Cantor Normal Form/Corollary
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x$ be a limit ordinal and let $y > 0$. Let $\sequence {a_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals that is strictly decreasing on $1 \le i \le n$. Let $\sequence {b_i}$ be a sequence of natural numbers. Then: $\ds \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n x^{a_i} \times b_i}^{x^y} = x^{a_1 \mathop \times x^y}$

label: Ordinal Exponentiation via Cantor Normal Form/Limit Exponents
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x$ and $y$ be limit ordinals. Let $\sequence {a_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals that is strictly decreasing on $1 \le i \le n$. Let $\sequence {b_i}$ be a sequence of natural numbers. Then: $\ds \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n x^{a_i} \times b_i}^y = x^{a_1 \mathop \times y}$

label: Ordinal Less than Successor Aleph
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $y < \aleph_{x + 1} \iff y < \aleph_x \lor y \sim \aleph_x$

label: Ordinal Membership is Asymmetric
snippet: Let $m$ and $n$ be ordinals. Then it is not the case that $m \in n$ and $n \in m$.

label: Ordinal Membership is Trichotomy
snippet: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be ordinals. Then: $\paren {\alpha = \beta} \lor \paren {\alpha \in \beta} \lor \paren {\beta \in \alpha}$ where $\lor$ denotes logical or.

label: Ordinal Multiplication by One
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $1$ denote the ordinal one.

label: Ordinal Multiplication by Zero
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal.

label: Ordinal Multiplication is Associative
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Let $\times$ denote ordinal multiplication. Then: $x \times \paren {y \times z} = \paren {x \times y} \times z$

label: Ordinal Multiplication is Closed
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. $x \cdot y \in \On$

label: Ordinal Multiplication is Left Cancellable
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Let $z \ne 0$. Then: $\ds \paren {z \cdot x} = \paren {z \cdot y} \implies x = y$ That is, ordinal multiplication is left cancellable.

label: Ordinal Multiplication is Left Distributive
snippet: Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be ordinals. Let $\times$ denote ordinal multiplication. Let $+$ denote ordinal addition. Then: $x \times \paren {y + z} = \paren {x \times y} + \paren {x \times z}$

label: Ordinal Multiplication via Cantor Normal Form/Infinite Exponent
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x > 1$. Let $y \ge \omega$ where $\omega$ denotes the minimally inductive set. Let $\sequence {a_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals that is strictly decreasing on $1 \le i \le n$. Let $\sequence {b_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals such that $0 < b_i < x$ for all $1 \le i \le n$. Then: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {x^{a_i} b_i} \times x^y = x^{a_1 \mathop + y}$

label: Ordinal Multiplication via Cantor Normal Form/Limit Base
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x$ be a limit ordinal. Let $y > 0$. Let $\sequence {a_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals that is strictly decreasing on $1 \le i \le n$. Let $\sequence {b_i}$ be a sequence of finite ordinals. Then: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {x^{a_i} b_i} \times x^y = x^{a_1 \mathop + y}$

label: Ordinal Number Equivalent to Cardinal Number
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $\card x$ denote the cardinal number of $x$. Then: $x \sim \card x$ where $\sim$ denotes set equivalence.

label: Ordinal Power of Power
snippet: Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be ordinals. Then: $\paren {x^y}^z = x^{y \mathop \times z}$

label: Ordinal Subset is Well-Ordered
snippet: Let $S$ be a class. Let every element of $S$ be an ordinal. Then $\struct {S, \in}$ is a strict well-ordering.

label: Ordinal Subset of Ordinal is Initial Segment
snippet: Let $S$ be an ordinal. Let $T \subset S$ also be an ordinal. Then $\exists a \in S: T = S_a$, where $S_a$ is the initial segment of $S$ determined by $a$. That is, $T = S_a = a \in S$.

label: Ordinal Subtraction when Possible is Unique
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals such that $x \le y$. Then there exists a unique ordinal $z$ such that $x + z = y$. That is: $x \le y \implies \exists! z \in \On: x + z = y$

label: Ordinal Sum of Powers
snippet: Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be ordinals. Then: $x^y \times x^z = x^{y + z}$

label: Ordinal Variable/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Ordinal Variables ==

label: Ordinal equals Successor of its Union
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. Then: $\bigcup \alpha^+ = \alpha$ where: $\alpha^+$ denotes the successor set of $\alpha$ $\bigcup \alpha^+$ denotes the union of $\alpha^+$.

label: Ordinal equals its Initial Segment
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Let $<$ denote the (strict) usual ordering of $\On$. Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. Then $\alpha$ is equal to its own initial segment: $\alpha = \set {\beta \in \On: \beta < \alpha}$

label: Ordinal in Aleph iff Cardinal in Aleph
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $x \in \aleph_y \iff \card x \in \aleph_y$ where $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping.

label: Ordinal is Finite iff Natural Number
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then $x$ is a finite set $x$ is an element of the minimally inductive set.

label: Ordinal is Less than Ordinal times Limit
snippet: Let $y$ be a limit ordinal. Let $x$ and $z$ be ordinals. Then: $z < x \times y \iff \exists w \in y: z < x \times w$

label: Ordinal is Less than Ordinal to Limit Power
snippet: Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be ordinals. Let $z$ be a limit ordinal. Then: $x < y^z \iff \exists w \in z: x < y^w$

label: Ordinal is Less than Successor
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $x^+$ denote the successor of $x$. Then: $x \in x^+$ $x \subset x^+$

label: Ordinal is Less than Sum
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le \paren {x + y}$ $x \le \paren {y + x}$

label: Ordinal is Member of Class of All Ordinals
snippet: Let $A$ be an ordinal. Then: $A \in \On \lor A = \On$ where $\On$ denotes the class of all ordinals.

label: Ordinal is Proper Subset of Successor
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. Then: $\alpha \subsetneqq \alpha^+$ where $\alpha^+$ denotes the successor set of $\alpha$. That is: $\alpha$ is a proper subset of $\alpha^+$.

label: Ordinal is Subset of Class of All Ordinals
snippet: Suppose $A$ is an ordinal. Then: $A \subseteq \On$ where $\On$ represents the class of all ordinals.

label: Ordinal is Subset of Rank of Small Class iff Not in Von Neumann Hierarchy
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $S$ be a small class. Let $\map V x$ denote the von Neumann hierarchy on the ordinal $x$. Then $x$ is a subset of the rank of $S$ $S \notin \map V x$.

label: Ordinal is Subset of Successor
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $y^+$ denote the successor of $y$. Then: $x \subseteq y^+ \iff \left({x \subseteq y \lor x = y^+}\right)$

label: Ordinal is Transitive
snippet: Every ordinal is a transitive set.

label: Ordinal is not Element of Itself
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then: $x \notin x$

label: Ordinals Isomorphic to the Same Well-Ordered Set
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be ordinals. Let $\left({\prec, S}\right)$ be a strict well-ordering. Let $\left({\in, A}\right)$ and $\left({\prec, S}\right)$ be order isomorphic. Let $\left({\in, B}\right)$ and $\left({\prec, S}\right)$ be order isomorphic. Then: $A = B$

label: Ordinals are Totally Ordered
snippet: The ordinals are totally ordered.

label: Ordinals are Well-Ordered
snippet: The ordinals are well-ordered.

label: Ordinals have No Zero Divisors
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $\paren {x \cdot y} = 0 \iff \paren {x = 0 \lor y = 0}$

label: Ordinals under Addition form Monoid
snippet: $\struct {\On, +}$ forms an monoid, where: $\On$ denotes the class of all ordinals $+$ denotes ordinal addition.

label: Ordinals under Multiplication form Monoid
snippet: $\struct {\On, \times}$ forms an monoid, where: $\On$ denotes the class of all ordinals $\times$ denotes ordinal multiplication.

label: Ore's Theorem
snippet: Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a simple graph of order $n \ge 3$. Let $G$ be an Ore graph, that is: For each pair of non-adjacent vertices $u, v \in V$: $(1): \quad \deg u + \deg v \ge n$ Then $G$ is Hamiltonian.

label: Orientation of Simple Closed Contour is with Respect to Interior
snippet: Let $C$ be a simple closed contour in the complex plane $\C$. Let $\Int C$ denote the interior of $C$. $C$ is positively oriented, $C$ is positively oriented with respect to $\Int C$. $C$ is negatively oriented, $C$ is negatively oriented with respect to $\Int C$.

label: Orthocenter, Centroid and Circumcenter Coincide iff Triangle is Equilateral
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle ABC$. Let $G$ be the centroid of $\triangle ABC$. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of $\triangle ABC$. Then $O$, $G$ and $H$ are the same points $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral. If $\triangle ABC$ is not equilateral, then $O$, $G$ and $H$ are all distinct.

label: Orthocenter and Incenter Coincide if Triangle is Equilateral
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be an equilateral triangle. Let $G$ be the orthocenter of $\triangle ABC$. Then: $G$ is the incenter of $\triangle ABC$.

label: Orthocomplement Reverses Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space space. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $V$ with $A \subseteq B$. Then: $B^\perp \subseteq A^\perp$ where $\perp$ denotes orthocomplementation.

label: Orthocomplement is Closed Linear Subspace

label: Orthocomplement of Closure
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space. Let $S \subseteq V$ be non-empty. Then: $S^\bot = \map \cl S^\bot$ where $\bot$ denotes orthocomplementation.

label: Orthocomplement of Subset of Orthocomplement is Superset

label: Orthogonal Difference is Closed Linear Subspace

snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $H$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb F$ with inner product $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$. Let $K$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Let $P_K$ denote the orthogonal projection on $K$. Then $P_K$ is a linear transformation on $H$.

snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $K$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Let $P_K$ denote the orthogonal projection onto $K$. Then $P_K$ is a projection.

snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\map \BB X$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $X$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. label: Outer Jordan Content Never Smaller than Inner Jordan Content
snippet: Let $M$ be a bounded subspace of Euclidean space. Then: $\map {m^*} M \ge \map {m_*} M$ where: $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content $m_*$ denotes the inner Jordan content

label: Outer Jordan Content of Closed Rectangle
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq \R^n$ be a closed $n$-rectangle. Then: $\map {m^*} \RR = \map V \RR$ where: $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content $V$ denotes the content of a rectangle

label: Outer Jordan Content of Degenerate Set
snippet: Let $M \subseteq \R^n$ be a bounded subset of Euclidean $n$-space. Suppose that, for every $\tuple {x_1, \dots, x_n} \in M$, we have that: $x_k = \gamma$ for some fixed $k \in \set {1, \dots, n}$ and $\gamma \in \R$. Then: $\map {m^*} M = 0$ where $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content.

label: Outer Jordan Content of Separated Union
snippet: Let $M \subseteq \R^n$ be a bounded subset of Euclidean $n$-space. Fix $k \in \set {1, 2, \dots, n}$ and $\gamma \in \R$. For $\vec x \in \R^n$, let $\vec x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n}$ Let: $A = \set {\vec x \in M : x_k \gamma}$ Then: $\map {m^*} M = \map {m^*} A + \map {m^*} B$ where $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content.

label: Outer Jordan Content of Subdivision
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq \R^n$ be a closed $n$-rectangle. Let $M \subseteq \RR$ be a subset. Let $P$ be a finite subdivision of $\RR$. Then: $\ds \map {m^*} M = \sum_{R \mathop \in P} \map {m^*} {M \cap R^\circ}$ where: $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content $R \in P$ denotes that $R$ is a subrectangle of $P$ $R^\circ$ denotes the interior of $R$

label: P-Norm of Real Sequence is Strictly Decreasing Function of P
snippet: Let $p \ge 1$ be a real number. Let ${\ell^p}_\R$ denote the real $p$-sequence space. Let $\mathbf x = \sequence {x_n} \in {\ell^p}_\R$. Suppose $\mathbf x$ is not a sequence of zero elements. Let $\norm {\mathbf x}_p$ denote the $p$-norm of $\mathbf x$ where $p \ge 1$. Then the mapping $p \to \norm {\mathbf x}_p$ is strictly decreasing $p$.

label: P-Product Metric Induces Product Topology
snippet: Let $M_A = \struct{A, d_A}$ and $M_B = \struct{B, d_B}$ be metric spaces. Let $\tau_A$ and $\tau_B$ be the topologies on $A$ and $B$ induced by $d_A$ and $d_B$, respectively. Let $p \ge 1$ be an extended real number. Let $M = \struct{A \times B, d}$ be the $p$-product of $M_A$ and $M_B$. We have that $M$ is a metric space. Let $\tau$ be the topology on $A \times B$ induced by $d$. Then $\struct{A \times B, \tau}$ is the product space of $\struct{A, \tau_A}$ and $\struct{B, \tau_B}$.

label: P-Product Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $M_{1'} = \struct {A_{1'}, d_{1'} }, M_{2'} = \struct {A_{2'}, d_{2'} }, \ldots, M_{n'} = \struct {A_{n'}, d_{n'} }$ be metric spaces. Let $\ds \AA = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_{i'}$ be the cartesian product of $A_{1'}, A_{2'}, \ldots, A_{n'}$. Let $p \in \R_{\ge 1}$. Let $d_p: \AA \times \AA \to \R$ be the $p$-product metric on $\AA$: $\ds \map {d_p} {x, y} := \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {\map {d_{i'} } {x_i, y_i} }^p}^{\frac 1 p}$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n} \in \AA$. Then $d_p$ is a metric.

label: P-Product Metric on Real Vector Space is Metric
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be an $n$-dimensional real vector space. Let $p \in \R_{\ge 1}$. Let $d_p: \R^n \times \R^n \to \R$ be the $p$-product metric on $\R^n$: $\ds \map {d_p} {x, y} := \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \size {x_i - y_i}^p}^{\frac 1 p}$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n} \in \R^n$. Then $d_p$ is a metric.

label: P-Product Metrics are Lipschitz Equivalent
snippet: Let $M_A = \left({A, d_A}\right)$ and $M_B = \left({B, d_B}\right)$ be metric spaces. Let $\tau_A$ and $\tau_B$ be the topologies on $A$ and $B$ induced by $d_A$ and $d_B$, respectively. For all extended real numbers $p \ge 1$, let $M_p = \left({A \times B, d_p}\right)$ be the $p$-product of $M_A$ and $M_B$. Then all the metrics $\left\{{d_p: p \ge 1}\right\}$ are Lipschitz equivalent.

label: P-Product Metrics on Real Vector Space are Topologically Equivalent
snippet: For $n \in \N$, let $\R^n$ be an Euclidean space. Let $p \in \R_{\ge 1}$. Let $d_p$ be the $p$-product metric on $\R^n$. Let $d_\infty$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\R^n$. Then $d_p$ and $d_\infty$ are topologically equivalent.

label: P-Sequence Space admits Schauder Basis
snippet: Let $1 \le p < \infty$. Let $\ell^p$ be the $p$-sequence space. Let $\sequence {\mathbf e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N } \in \ell^p$ be a sequence such that: $\mathbf e_n = \tuple {\underbrace{0, \ldots, 0}_n, 1, 0, \ldots}$ Then $\set {\mathbf e_n : n \in \N}$ is a Schauder basis for $\ell^p$.

label: P-Sequence Space of Real Sequences is Metric Space
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} x_i^2$ is convergent. Let $d_p$ be the $p$-sequence metric on $\R$. Then $\ell^p := \struct {A, d_p}$ is a metric space.

label: P-Sequence Space with P-Norm forms Banach Space
snippet: Let $\ell^p$ be a p-sequence space. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_p$ be a p-norm. Then $\struct {\ell^p, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ is a Banach space.

label: P-Sequence Space with Pointwise Addition and Pointwise Scalar Multiplication on Ring of Sequences forms Vector Space
snippet: Let $\ell^p$ be the p-sequence space. Let $\struct {\R, +_\R, \times_\R}$ be the field of real numbers. Let $\paren +$ be the pointwise addition on the ring of sequences. Let $\paren {\, \cdot \,}$ be the pointwise multiplication on the ring of sequences. Then $\struct {\ell^p, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ is a vector space.

label: P-adic Closed Ball is Instance of Closed Ball of a Norm
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $B \subseteq \Q_p$. Then: $B$ is a closed ball in $p$-adic numbers with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ $B$ is a closed ball of the normed division ring $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ That is, the definition of a closed ball in $p$-adic numbers is a specific instance of the general definition of a closed ball in a normed division ring.

label: P-adic Expansion Less Initial Zero Terms Represents Same P-adic Number
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a$ be a $p$-adic number, that is left coset, in $\Q_p$. Let $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = m}^\infty d_i p^i$ be a $p$-adic expansion that represents $a$. Let $l$ be the first index $i \ge m$ such that $d_i \ne 0$ Then the series: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = l}^\infty d_i p^i$ also represents $a$.

label: P-adic Expansion Representative of P-adic Number is Unique
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a$ be a $p$-adic number, that is left coset, in $\Q_p$. Let $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = m}^\infty d_i p^i$ and $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = k}^\infty e_i p^i$ be $p$-adic expansions that represent $a$. Then: $(1) \quad m = k$ $(2) \quad \forall i \ge m : d_i = e_i$ That is, the $p$-adic expansions $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = m}^\infty d_i p^i$ and $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = k}^\infty e_i p^i$ are identical.

label: P-adic Expansion is a Cauchy Sequence in P-adic Norm
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rationals numbers $\Q$. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = m}^\infty d_n p^n$ be a $p$-adic expansion. Then the sequence of partial sums of the series: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = m}^\infty d_n p^n$ is a Cauchy sequence in the valued field $\struct{\Q, \norm{\,\cdot\,}_p}$.

label: P-adic Expansion of P-adic Unit

label: P-adic Integer has Unique Coherent Sequence Representative
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a$ be a $p$-adic number, that is left coset, in $\Q_p$ such that $\norm a _p \le 1$. Then $a$ has exactly one representative that is a coherent sequence.

label: P-adic Integer is Limit of Unique Coherent Sequence of Integers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Let $x \in \Z_p$. Then there exists a unique coherent sequence $\sequence {\alpha_n}$: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \alpha_n = x$

label: P-adic Integer is Limit of Unique P-adic Expansion
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Let $x \in \Z_p$. Then $x$ is the limit of a unique $p$-adic expansion of the form: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty d_n p^n$

label: P-adic Number has Unique P-adic Expansion Representative
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a$ be a $p$-adic number, that is left coset, in $\Q_p$. Then $a$ has exactly one representative that is a $p$-adic expansion.

label: P-adic Number is Limit of Unique P-adic Expansion
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $x \in \Q_p$. Then $x$ is the limit of a unique $p$-adic expansion.

label: P-adic Number times Integer Power of p is P-adic Integer
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Then: $\forall a \in \Q_p: \exists n \in \N: p^n a \in \Z_p$

label: P-adic Number times P-adic Norm is P-adic Unit
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p^\times$ be the $p$-adic units. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Then there exists $n \in \Z$ such that: $p^n a \in \Z_p^\times$ where $p^n = \norm a_p$

label: P-adic Numbers are Generated Ring Extension of P-adic Integers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Then: $Q_p = \Z_p \sqbrk {1 / p}$ where $\Z_p \sqbrk {1 / p}$ denotes the ring extension generated by $1 / p$.

label: P-adic Numbers are Uncountable
snippet: Let $p$ be any prime number. The set of $p$-adic numbers $\Q_p$ is an uncountable set.

label: P-adic Numbers is Hausdorff Topological Space
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\tau_p$ be the topology induced by the non-Archimedean norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$. Then the topological space $\struct{\Q_p, \tau_p}$ is Hausdorff.

label: P-adic Numbers is Locally Compact Topological Space
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\tau_p$ be the topology induced by the non-Archimedean norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$. Then the topological space $\struct {\Q_p, \tau_p}$ is locally compact.

label: P-adic Numbers is Second Countable Topological Space
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\tau_p$ be the topology induced by the non-Archimedean norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$. Then the topological space $\struct {\Q_p, \tau_p}$ is second-countable.

label: P-adic Numbers is Totally Disconnected Topological Space
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\tau_p$ be the topology induced by the non-Archimedean norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$. Then the topological space $\struct {\Q_p, \tau_p}$ is totally disconnected.

label: P-adic Open Ball is Instance of Open Ball of a Norm
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $B \subseteq \Q_p$. Then: $B$ is an open ball in $p$-adic numbers with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ $B$ is an open ball of the normed division ring $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ . That is, the definition of an open ball in $p$-adic numbers is a specific instance of the general definition of an open ball in a normed division ring.

label: P-adic Sphere is Instance of Sphere of a Norm
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $S \subseteq \Q_p$. Then: $S$ is a sphere in $p$-adic numbers with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ $S$ is a sphere of the normed division ring $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ That is, the definition of a closed ball in $p$-adic numbers is a specific instance of the general definition of a sphere in a normed division ring.

label: P-adic Unit has Norm Equal to One
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ denote the $p$-adic integers. Let $x \in \Q_p$. Then x is a $p$-adic unit $\norm x_p = 1$

label: PGF of Sum of Independent Discrete Random Variables
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be independent discrete random variables on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $Z$ be a discrete random variable such that $Z = X + Y$. Then: $\map {\Pi_Z} s = \map {\Pi_X} s \, \map {\Pi_Y} s$ where $\map {\Pi_Z} s$ is the probability generating function of $Z$.

label: PGF of Sum of Random Number of Independent Discrete Random Variables
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let: $N, X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be independent discrete random variables such that the $X$'s have the same probability distribution. Let: $\map {\Pi_N} s$ be the PGF of $N$ $\map {\Pi_X} s$ be the PGF of each of the $X$'s. Let: $Z = X_1 + X_2 + \ldots + X_N$ Then: $\map {\Pi_Z} s = \map {\Pi_N} {\map {\Pi_X} s}$

label: P versus NP
snippet: == Open Question == The class of problems for which an algorithm can find a solution in polynomial time is termed $P$. The class of problems for which an algorithm can verify a solution in nondeterministic polynomial time is termed $NP$. The $P$ versus $NP$ question is: Are all problems in $NP$ also in $P$?

snippet: The only known pair of consecutive integers which are both powerful numbers such that the first of the pair is odd is: $\tuple {675, 676}$

snippet: The integers defined as: $1\,159\,142\,985 \times 2^{2304} \pm 1$ are a pair of twin primes each with $703$ digits.

snippet: The integers defined as: $190 \, 116 \times 3003 \times 10^{5120} \pm 1$ are a pair of titanic twin primes. That is: $570 \, 918 \, 347 \paren 9_{5820}$ and: $570 \, 918 \, 348 \paren 0_{5819} 1$ where $\paren a_b$ means $b$ instances of $a$ in a string.

snippet: The following sequence of integers are those $n$ which fulfil the equation: $\map {\sigma_0} n = \map {\sigma_0} {n + 1} = 6$ where $\map {\sigma_0} n$ denotes the divisor count function. That is, they are the first of pairs of consecutive integers which each have $6$ divisors: $44, 75, 98, 116, 147, 171, 242, 243, 244, 332, \ldots$

label: Pairwise Disjoint Subsets in Semiring Part of Partition
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\mathbb S$ be a semiring of sets. Let $A, A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ all belong to $\mathbb S$. Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ all be pairwise disjoint subsets of $A$. Then there exists a finite expansion of $A$: $\ds \exists s \ge n: A = \bigcup_{k \mathop = 1}^s A_k$ with $A_1, \ldots, A_n$ as its first $n$ elements, such that: $(1): \quad \forall k, 1 \le k \le s: A_k \in \mathbb S$ $(2): \quad \forall k, l, 1 \le k \le s, 1 \le l \le s: k \ne l \implies A_k \cap A_l = \O$.

label: Pairwise Independence does not imply Independence
snippet: Just because all the events in a family of events in a probability space are pairwise independent, it does not mean that the family is independent.

label: Palindromes in Base 10 and Base 2
snippet: The following $n \in \Z$ are palindromic in both decimal and binary: $0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 33, 99, 313, 585, 717, 7447, 9009, 15 \, 351, 32 \, 223, 39 \, 993, \ldots$

label: Palindromic Primes in Base 10 and Base 2
snippet: The following $n \in \Z$ are prime numbers which are palindromic in both decimal and binary: $3, 5, 7, 313, 7 \, 284 \, 717 \, 174 \, 827, 390 \, 714 \, 505 \, 091 \, 666 \, 190 \, 505 \, 417 \, 093, \ldots$ It is not known whether there are any more.

snippet: Certain pandigital integers remain pandigital when multiplying them by certain single-digit integers: The sequence: $1039675824, 1053826974, 1068253974, 1068379524, 1073968254, 1075396824, 1098765432, 1204756839, 1234567890, 1357802469$ contains all pandigital integers with at least $4$ nontrivial pandigital multiples, of which: $1098765432, 1234567890$ has $5$.

label: Pappus's Hexagon Theorem
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be a set of collinear points. Let $a, b, c$ be another set of collinear points. Let $X, Y, Z$ be the points of intersection of each of the straight lines $Ab$ and $aB$, $Ac$ and $aC$, and $Bc$ and $bC$. Then $X, Y, Z$ are collinear points. 400px

label: Parabolic Riemann Surface is Plane, Punctured Plane or Torus

label: Paracompact Space is Countably Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a paracompact space. Then $T$ is a countably paracompact space.

label: Paracompact T2 Space is Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space which is paracompact. Then $T$ is a normal space.

label: Paracompactness is Preserved under Projections
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let $\pr_\alpha: \struct {S, \tau} \to \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the projection on the $\alpha$ coordinate. If $\struct {S, \tau}$ is paracompact, then each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ is also paracompact.

label: Paracompactness is not always Preserved under Open Continuous Mapping
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {X_A, \tau_A}$ be a topological space which is paracompact. Let $T_B = \struct {X_B, \tau_B}$ be another topological space. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a mapping which is both continuous and open. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T_B$ is also paracompact.

label: Parallactic Angle in terms of Azimuth and Declination
snippet: Let $x$ be a point on the celestial sphere. Let $q$ denote the parallactic angle of $x$. Then: $\sin q := \dfrac {\cos \phi \sin A} {\sin \delta}$ where: $\phi$ is the terrestrial latitude $A$ is the azimuth $\delta$ is the declination.

label: Parallactic Angle in terms of Hour Angle and Zenith Distance
snippet: Let $x$ be a point on the celestial sphere. Let $q$ denote the parallactic angle of $x$. Then: $\sin q := \dfrac {\cos \phi \sin t} {\sin \zeta}$ where: $\phi$ is the terrestrial latitude $t$ is the hour angle $\zeta$ is the zenith distance.

label: Parallel Law for Extremal Length
snippet: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface. Let $\Gamma_1, \Gamma_2$ be families of rectifiable curves (or, more generally, families of disjoint unions of rectifiable curves) on $X$. Let $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ be disjoint, in the sense that: there exist disjoint Borel subsets $A_1, A_2 \subseteq X$ such that: for any $\gamma_1 \in \Gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2 \in \Gamma_2$, we have $\gamma_1 \subseteq A_1$ and $\gamma_2 \subseteq A_2$. Let $\Gamma$ be a third curve family, with the property that every element $\Gamma_1$ and every element of $\Gamma_2$ contains some element of $\Gamma$.

label: Parallel Transport Determines Covariant Differentiation
snippet: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with or without boundary. Let $TM$ be the tangent bundle of $M$. Let $\nabla$ be a connection in $TM$. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be an open real interval. Let $\gamma : I \to M$ be a smooth curve. Let $P_{t_1 t_0}^\gamma$ be the parallel transport map along $\gamma$. Let $D_t$ be the covariant derivative along $\gamma$. Suppose that $V$ is a smooth vector field along $\gamma$. Then: $\ds \forall t_0 \in I : \map {D_t V} {t_0} = \lim_{t_1 \to t_0} \frac {P^\gamma_{t_1 t_0} \map V {t_1} - \map V {t_0} }{t_1 - t_0}$

label: Parallelism is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of straight lines in the plane. For $l_1, l_2 \in S$, let $l_1 \parallel l_2$ denote that $l_1$ is parallel to $l_2$. Then $\parallel$ is an equivalence relation on $S$.

label: Parallelism is Reflexive Relation
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of straight lines in the plane. For $l_1, l_2 \in S$, let $l_1 \parallel l_2$ denote that $l_1$ is parallel to $l_2$. Then $\parallel$ is a reflexive relation on $S$.

snippet: Let $S$ be the set of straight lines in the plane. For $l_1, l_2 \in S$, let $l_1 \parallel l_2$ denote that $l_1$ is parallel to $l_2$. Then $\parallel$ is a symmetric relation on $S$.

snippet: Parallelism between straight lines is a transitive relation.

label: Parallelogram on Same Base as Triangle has Twice its Area

snippet: Let $\Box ABCD$ be a parallelogram. Let one angle of $\Box ABCD$ be a right angle. Then $\Box ABCD$ is a rectangle.

label: Parity Addition is Associative
snippet: Let $R := \struct {\set {\text{even}, \text{odd} }, +, \times}$ be the parity ring. The operation $+$ is associative: $\forall a, b, c \in R: \paren {a + b} + c = a + \paren {b + c}$

snippet: Let $R := \struct {\set {\text{even}, \text{odd} }, +, \times}$ be the parity ring. The operation $+$ is commutative: $\forall a, b \in R: a + b = b + a$

label: Parity Function is Homomorphism
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $\pi \in S_n$. Let $\map \sgn \pi$ be the sign of $\pi$. Let the parity function of $\pi$ be defined as: Parity of $\pi = \begin {cases} \mathrm {Even} & : \map \sgn \pi = 1 \\ \mathrm {Odd} & : \map \sgn \pi = -1 \end {cases}$ The mapping $\sgn: S_n \to C_2$, where $C_2$ is the cyclic group of order 2, is a homomorphism.

label: Parity Group is Only Group with 2 Elements

label: Parity Multiplication is Associative
snippet: Let $R := \struct {\set {\text{even}, \text{odd} }, +, \times}$ be the parity ring. The operation $\times$ is associative: $\forall a, b, c \in R: \paren {a \times b} \times c = a \times \paren {b \times c}$

label: Parity Multiplication is Commutative
snippet: Let $R := \struct {\set {\text{even}, \text{odd} }, +, \times}$ be the parity ring. The operation $\times$ is commutative: $\forall a, b \in R: a \times b = b \times a$

label: Parity of Integer equals Parity of Positive Power
snippet: Let $p \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a strictly positive integer. Then $p$ is even $p^n$ is even. That is, the parity of an integer equals the parity of all its (strictly) positive powers.

label: Partial Denominators of Continued Fraction Expansion of Irrational Square Root
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ such that $n$ is not a square. Let the continued fraction expansion of $\sqrt n$ be expressed as: $\sqbrk {a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots}$ Then the partial denominators of this continued fraction expansion can be calculated as: $a_r = \floor {\dfrac {\floor {\sqrt n} + P_r} {Q_r} }$ where: $P_r = \begin{cases} 0 & : r = 0 \\ a_{r - 1} Q_{r - 1} - P_{r - 1} & : r > 0 \\ \end{cases}$ $Q_r = \begin{cases} 1 & : r = 0 \\ \dfrac {n - {P_r}^2} {Q_{r - 1} } & : r > 0 \\ \end{cases}$

label: Partial Sum Congruent to P-adic Integer Modulo Power of p
snippet: Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers for some prime $p$. Let $a \in \Z_p$. Let $\ds a = \sum_{j=0}^\infty d_j p^j$ be the $p$-adic expansion of $a$ For all $n \in \N$, let $\ds a_n = \sum_{j=0}^n d_j p^j$ be the $n$-th partial sum of the $p$-adic expansion of $a$ Then: $\forall n \in \N : a_n \equiv a \pmod{p^{n+1}\Z_p}$ where $a_n \equiv a \pmod{p^{n+1}\Z_p}$ denotes congruence modulo the ideal $\Z_p$.

label: Partial Sums of P-adic Expansion forms Coherent Sequence

label: Partial Sums of Power Series with Fibonacci Coefficients

label: Partition of Non-Regular Prime Stellated Cyclic Polygons into Rotation Classes
snippet: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $C$ be a circle whose center is $O$. Consider the set $P$ of $p$ points on the circumference of $C$ dividing it into $p$ equal arcs. Let $S$ be the set of all non-regular stellated $p$-gons whose vertices are the elements of $P$. Let $\sim$ denote the equivalence relation on $S$ defined as: $\forall \tuple {a, b} \in S \times S: a \sim b \iff$ there exists a plane rotation about $O$ transforming $a$ to $b$. Then the $\sim$-equivalence classes of $S$ into which $S$ can thereby be partitioned all have cardinality $p$.

label: Partition of Singletons yields Discrete Topology

Then: $\map \sigma T = \map {\sigma_p} T \cup \map {\sigma_s} T \cup \map {\sigma_r} T$ where: $\map {\sigma_p} T$ is the point spectrum of $T$ $\map {\sigma_s} T$ is the continuous spectrum of $T$. $\map {\sigma_r} T$ is the residual spectrum of $T$

label: Pascal's Rule
snippet: Let $\dbinom n k$ be a binomial coefficient. For positive integers $n, k$ with $1 \le k \le n$: $\dbinom n {k - 1} + \dbinom n k = \dbinom {n + 1} k$ This is also valid for the real number definition: $\forall r \in \R, k \in \Z: \dbinom r {k - 1} + \dbinom r k = \dbinom {r + 1} k$ Thus the binomial coefficients can be defined using the following recurrence relation: $\dbinom n k = \begin{cases} 1 & : k = 0 \\ 0 & : k > n \\ \dbinom {n - 1} {k - 1} + \dbinom {n - 1} k & : \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$

label: Pascal's Theorem
snippet: Let $ABCDEF$ be a hexagon whose $6$ vertices lie on a conic section and whose opposite sides are not parallel. Then the points of intersection of the opposite sides, when produced as necessary, all lie on a straight line.

label: Pasch's Theorem
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d$ be points on a line. Let $\tuple {a, b, c}$ denote that $b$ lies between $a$ and $c$. Then $\tuple {a, b, c}$ and $\tuple {b, c, d}$ together imply that $\tuple {a, b, d}$. That is, if: $b$ is between $a$ and $c$ and: $c$ is between $b$ and $d$ then: $b$ is between $a$ and $d$.

snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space which is path-connected. Then $T$ is connected.

label: Path-Connectedness is Equivalence Relation

label: Path-Connectedness is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {T_1, \tau_1}, \struct {T_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_1 \to T_2$ be a homeomorphism. Let $S \subseteq T_1$ be a subset of $T_1$. Let $S$ be path-connected in $\struct {T_1, \tau_1}$. Then $\phi \sqbrk S$ is path-connected in $\struct {T_2, \tau_2}$. That is, path-connectedness is a topological property.

label: Path-Homotopic Paths have Path Homotopy
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $f, g: \closedint 0 1 \to X$ be paths. Then $f$ and $g$ are path-homotopic, there exists a path homotopy between $f$ and $g$.

snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a perfect number. Then $n$ has at least two distinct prime factors.

label: Perimeter of Circle
snippet: The perimeter $C$ of a circle with radius $r$ is given by: $C = 2 \pi r$

label: Perimeter of Ellipse
snippet: Let $K$ be an ellipse whose major axis is of length $2 a$ and whose minor axis is of length $2 b$. The perimeter $\PP$ of $K$ is given by: $\PP = 4 a \map E e$ where: $\ds \map E e = \int_0^{\pi / 2} \sqrt{1 - e^2 \sin^2 \theta} \rd \theta$ is the complete elliptic integral of the second kind $e = \dfrac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } a$ is the eccentricity of $K$.

label: Perimeter of Regular Polygon
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular $n$-sided polygon whose side length is $b$. Then the perimeter $L$ of $P$ is given by: $L = n b$

label: Perimeter of Regular Polygon by Circumradius
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular $n$-gon. Let $C$ be a circumcircle of $P$. Let the radius of $C$ be $r$. Then the perimeter $\PP$ of $P$ is given by: $\PP = 2 n r \sin \dfrac \pi n$

label: Perimeter of Regular Polygon by Inradius
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular $n$-gon. Let $C$ be an incircle of $P$. Let the radius of $C$ be $r$. Then the perimeter $\PP$ of $P$ is given by: $\PP = 2 n r \tan \dfrac \pi n$

label: Perimeter of Triangle
snippet: Let $ABC$ be a triangle. Then the perimeter $P$ of $ABC$ is given by: $P = a + b + c$ where $a, b, c$ are the lengths of the sides of $ABC$.

label: Period of Harmonic Wave

label: Period of Periodic Wave
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a periodic wave expressed as: $\forall x, t \in \R: \map \phi {x, t} = \map f {x - c t}$ The period $\tau$ of $\phi$ can be expressed as: $\tau = \dfrac \lambda c$ where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of $\phi$.

label: Period of Reciprocal of Prime
snippet: Consider the decimal expansion of the reciprocal $\dfrac 1 p$ of a prime $p$. If $p \nmid a$, the decimal expansion of $\dfrac 1 p$ is periodic in base $a$ and its period of recurrence is the order of $a$ modulo $p$. If $p \divides a$, the decimal expansion of $\dfrac 1 p$ in base $a$ terminates.

snippet: The decimal expansion of the reciprocal of the repunit prime $R_{1031}$ has a period of $1031$. $\dfrac 1 {R_{1031}} = 0 \cdotp \underbrace{\dot 000 \ldots 000}_{1030} \dot 9$ This is the only prime number to have a period of exactly $1031$.

label: Period of Revolution of Conical Pendulum
snippet: Let $P$ be a conical pendulum. Let $h$ be the height of the pivot of $P$ above the circle in which $P$ is moving. Then the period of revolution of $P$ around the circle is given by: $T = 2 \pi \sqrt {\dfrac h g}$ where $g$ is the acceleration on $P$ caused by the gravitational field in which $P$ is suspended.

label: Period of Rotation of Plane of Oscillation of Foucault's Pendulum
snippet: Let $P$ be a Foucault pendulum. The plane of oscillation of $P$ rotates through a full circle in time $T$, where: $T = \dfrac D {\sin \lambda}$ where: $\lambda$ denotes the latitude on Earth at which $P$ is located $D$ denotes the length of a sidereal day.

label: Periodic Function as Mapping from Unit Circle
snippet: Let $\SS$ denote the unit circle whose center is at the origin of the Cartesian plane $\R^2$. Let $p: \R \to \SS$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map p x = \tuple {\cos x, \sin x}$ Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a periodic real function whose period is $2 \pi$. Then there exists a well-defined real-valued function $f': \SS \to \R$ such that: $f = f' \circ p$ where $f' \circ p$ denotes the composition of $f'$ with $p$.

snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$ be the symmetric group on $S$, where $\circ$ denotes the composition operation. Let $\struct {H, \circ}$ be a set of permutations of $S$ which forms a group under $\circ$. Then $\struct {H, \circ}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$.

snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $\pi \in S_n$. Let $\RR_\pi$ be the relation defined by: $i \mathrel {\RR_\pi} j \iff \exists k \in \Z: \map {\pi^k} i = j$ Then $\RR_\pi$ is an equivalence relation.

snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $X$ be a set. Let $\map \Gamma X$ be the symmetric group of $X$. Let $\rho: G \to \map \Gamma X$ be a permutation representation, that is, a homomorphism. The mapping $\phi: G \times X \to X$ associated to $\rho$, defined by: $\map \phi {g, x} = \map {\map \rho g} x$ is a group action.

label: Permutation is Cyclic iff At Most One Non-Trivial Orbit
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\rho: S \to S$ be a permutation on $S$. Then: $\rho$ is a cyclic permutation $S$ has no more than one orbit under $\rho$ with more than one element.

label: Permutation of Cosets
snippet: Let $G$ be a group and let $H \le G$. Let $\mathbb S$ be the set of all distinct left cosets of $H$ in $G$. Then: $(1): \quad$ For any $g \in G$, the mapping $\theta_g: \mathbb S \to \mathbb S$ defined by $\map {\theta_g} {x H} = g x H$ is a permutation of $\mathbb S$. $(2): \quad$ The mapping $\theta$ defined by $\map \theta g = \theta_g$ is a homomorphism from $G$ into the symmetric group on $\mathbb S$. $(3): \quad$ The kernel of $\theta$ is the subgroup $\ds \bigcap_{x \mathop \in G} x H x^{-1}$.

label: Permutation of Indices
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers. Let the fiber of truth of $R$ be finite. Let $\pi$ is a permutation on the fiber of truth of $R$. Then:

label: Permutation of Indices of Product
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers. Let the fiber of truth of $R$ be finite. Then: $\ds \prod_{\map R j} a_j = \prod_{\map R {\map \pi j} } a_{\map \pi j}$ where: $\ds \prod_{\map R j} a_j$ denotes the continued product over $a_j$ for all $j$ that satisfy the propositional function $\map R j$ $\pi$ is a permutation on the fiber of truth of $R$.

label: Permutation of Indices of Summation
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers. Let the fiber of truth of $R$ be finite. Then: $\ds \sum_{\map R j} a_j = \sum_{\map R {\map \pi j} } a_{\map \pi j}$ where: $\ds \sum_{\map R j} a_j$ denotes the summation over $a_j$ for all $j$ that satisfy the propositional function $\map R j$ $\pi$ is a permutation on the fiber of truth of $R$.

label: Permutation of Set is Automorphism of Set under Left Operation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \gets}$ be the algebraic structure formed from $S$ under the left operation. Let $f$ be a permutation on $S$. Then $f$ is an automorphism of $f$.

label: Permutation on Polynomial is Group Action
snippet: Let $n \in \Z: n > 0$. Let $F_n$ be the set of all polynomials in $n$ variables $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$: $F = \set {\map f {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}: f \text{ is a polynomial in $n$ variables} }$ Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $*: S_n \times F \to F$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall \pi \in S_n, f \in F: \pi * \map f {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} = \map f {x_{\map \pi 1}, x_{\map \pi 2}, \ldots, x_{\map \pi n} }$ Then $*$ is a group action.

label: Perpendicular Axes Theorem
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a lamina. Let $O_x$ and $O_y$ be axes of rotation in the plane of $\LL$ perpendicular to each other and intersecting at $O$. Let $O_z$ be an axis of rotation of $\LL$ through $O$ perpendicular to both $O_x$ and $O_y$. Let $I_x$, $I_y$ and $I_z$ be the moments of inertia of $\LL$ about $O_x$, $O_y$ and $O_z$ respectively. Then: $I_z = I_x + I_y$

label: Perpendicular Bisector is Locus of Points Equidistant from Endpoints
snippet: Let $AB$ be a straight line segment. The locus of points which are equidistant from $A$ and $B$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$.

label: Perpendicular Bisector is Unique
snippet: Let $AB$ be a straight line segment in a Euclidean geometry. Let $\LL$ be the perpendicular bisector of $AB$. Then $\LL$ is unique.

label: Perpendicular Bisector of Triangle is Altitude of Medial Triangle

snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. The perpendicular bisectors of $AB$, $BC$ and $AC$ all intersect at the same point.

label: Perpendicular Distance from Point to Plane
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a plane embedded in a cartesian $3$-space, given by the equation: $a x + b y + c z + d = 0$ Let $p$ be a point in the cartesian $3$-space whose coordinates are given by: $p = \tuple {x_0, y_0, z_0}$ Then the perpendicular distance $D$ from $p$ to $\PP$ is given by: $D = \dfrac {\size {a x_0 + b y_0 + c z_0 + d} } {\sqrt {a^2 + b^2 + c^2} }$

label: Perpendicular Distance from Straight Line in Plane to Origin
snippet: Let $L$ be the straight line embedded in the cartesian plane whose equation is given as: $a x + b y = c$ Then the perpendicular distance $d$ between $L$ and $\tuple {0, 0}$ is given by: $d = \size {\dfrac c {\sqrt {a^2 + b^2} } }$

snippet: Let $a, b, c \in \C$. Let $\size x \map \Re b > 0$. snippet: Let $M$ be an $n$-manifold. Let its $n$th homology group $\map {H_n} M$ be infinite and cyclic (that is, that $M$ is an orientable manifold). Then $\map {H_r} M$ is homeomorphic to the $\paren {n - r}$th cohomology group $\map {H^{n - r} } M$ for all $r$.

label: Poincaré Recurrence Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \BB, \mu, T}$ be a measure-preserving dynamical system. Then for each $A \in \BB$: $\ds \map \mu {A \setminus \bigcap_{N \mathop = 1}^\infty \bigcup_{n \mathop = N}^\infty T^{-n} \sqbrk A} = 0$ That is, for $\mu$-almost all $x\in A$ there are integers $0 < n_1 < n_2 < \cdots$ such that $\map {T^{n_i} }x \in A$.
