label: Projection from Product Topology is Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \struct {T_1 \times T_2, \tau}$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$, where $\tau$ is the product topology on $S$. Let $\pr_1: T \to T_1$ and $\pr_2: T \to T_2$ be the first and second projections from $T$ onto its factors. Then both $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are are continuous.

label: Projection from Product Topology is Open
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \struct {T_1 \times T_2, \tau}$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$, where $\tau$ is the product topology on $S$. Let $\pr_1: T \to T_1$ and $\pr_2: T \to T_2$ be the first and second projections from $T$ onto its factors. Then both $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are open.

label: Projection from Product Topology is Open and Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \struct {T_1 \times T_2, \tau}$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$, where $\tau$ is the product topology on $S$. Let $\pr_1: T \to T_1$ and $\pr_2: T \to T_2$ be the first and second projections from $T$ onto its factors. Then both $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are open and continuous.

label: Projection from Topological Product is Identification Mapping
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \struct {T_1 \times T_2, \tau}$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$, where $\tau$ is the product topology on $S$. Let $\pr_1: T \to T_1$ and $\pr_2: T \to T_2$ be the first and second projections from $T$ onto its factors. Then $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are identification mappings.

label: Projection in Plane between Lines passing through Origin is Linear Operator
snippet: Let $M$ and $N$ be distinct straight lines through the plane through the origin. Let $\pr_{M, N}$ be the projection on $M$ along $N$. Then $\pr_{M, N}$ is a linear operator.

label: Projection in Plane on X-Axis along Y-Axis
snippet: Let $\pr_{X, Y}$ denote the projection on the $x$-axis along the $y$-axis: $\forall P \in \R^2: \map {\pr_{X, Y} } P =$ the intersection of the $x$-axis with the line through $P$ parallel to the $y$-axis. Let $P = \tuple {\lambda_1, \lambda_2}$ be an arbitrary point in $\R^2$. Then: $\map {\pr_{X, Y} } {\lambda_1, \lambda_2} = \tuple {\lambda_1, 0}$

label: Projection in Plane on Y-Axis along X-Axis
snippet: Let $\pr_{Y, X}$ denote the projection on the $y$-axis along the $x$-axis: $\forall P \in \R^2: \map {\pr_{Y, X} } P =$ the intersection of the $y$-axis with the line through $P$ parallel to the $x$-axis. Let $P = \tuple {\lambda_1, \lambda_2}$ be an arbitrary point in $\R^2$. Then: $\map {\pr_{Y, X} } {\lambda_1, \lambda_2} = \tuple {0, \lambda_2}$

label: Projection is Epimorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {\SS, \circ}$ be the external direct product of the algebraic structures $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$. Then: $\pr_1$ is an epimorphism from $\struct {\SS, \circ}$ to $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ $\pr_2$ is an epimorphism from $\struct {\SS, \circ}$ to $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$ where $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are the first and second projection respectively of $\struct {\SS, \circ}$.

label: Projection is Injection iff Factor is Singleton
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n$ be non-empty sets. Let $\ds S = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n S_i$ be the cartesian product of $S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n$. Let $\pr_j: S \to S_j$ be the $j$th projection on $S$. Then $\pr_j$ is an injection $S_k$ is a singleton for all $k \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, n}$ where $k \ne j$.

label: Projection is Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be non-empty sets. Let $S \times T$ be the Cartesian product of $S$ and $T$. Let $\pr_1: S \times T \to S$ and $\pr_2: S \times T \to T$ be the first projection and second projection respectively on $S \times T$. Then $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are both surjections.

label: Projection of Complement Contains Complement of Projection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be non-empty sets. Let $X \subseteq S \times T$ be a subset of the Cartesian product $S \times T$. Denote with $\pr_1, \pr_2$ and $\complement$ the first and second projections, and the complement operation, respectively. Then: {{eqn|l = \map \complement {\map {\pr_1} X} |o = \subseteq |r = \map {\pr_1} {\map \complement X} }} {{eqn|l = \map \complement {\map {\pr_2} X} |o = \subseteq |r = \map {\pr_2} {\map \complement X} }}

label: Projection of Conic Section is Conic Section
snippet: Let $K$ be a conic section. Let $K'$ be a projection of $K$. Then $K'$ is also a conic section.

label: Projection of Product Manifold onto Factor Manifold is Riemannian Submersion
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g^M}$ and $\struct {N, g^N}$ be Riemannian manifolds. Let $M \times N$ be the product manifold endowed with the product metric $g = g^M \oplus g^N$. Let $\pi_M$, $\pi_N$ be projections such that: $\pi_M : M \times N \to M$ $\pi_N : M \times N \to N$ Then $\pi_M$ and $\pi_N$ are Riemannian submersions.

label: Projection of Subset is Open iff Saturation is Open
snippet: Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on a topological space $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $p$ denote the quotient mapping induced by $\sim$. Let $\tau_\sim$ be the quotient topology on $X / \sim$ by $p$. Let $\struct {X / \sim, \tau_\sim}$ be the quotient space of $X$ by $\sim$. label: Proof by Contraposition
snippet: == Proof Technique == Proof by Contraposition is a rule of inference used in proofs. This rule infers a conditional statement from its contrapositive. label: Quotient Group of Ideal is Coset Space
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $\struct {R / J, +}$ be the quotient group of $\struct {R, +}$ by $\struct {J, +}$. Then each element of $\struct {R / J, +}$ is a coset of $J$ in $R$, that is, is of the form $x + J = \set {x + j: j \in J}$ for some $x \in R$. The rule of addition of these cosets is: $\paren {x + J} + \paren {y + J} = \paren {x + y} + J$. The identity of $\struct {R / J, +}$ is $J$ and for each $x \in R$, the inverse of $x + J$ is $\paren {-x} + J$.

label: Quotient Group of Infinite Cyclic Group by Subgroup
snippet: Let $C_n$ be the cyclic group of order $n$. Then: $C_n \cong \dfrac {\struct {\Z, +} } {\struct {n \Z, +} } = \dfrac \Z {n \Z}$ where: $\Z$ is the additive group of integers $n \Z$ is the additive group of integer multiples $\Z / n \Z$ is the quotient group of $\Z$ by $n \Z$. Thus, every cyclic group is isomorphic to one of: $\Z, \dfrac \Z \Z, \dfrac \Z {2 \Z}, \dfrac \Z {3 \Z}, \dfrac \Z {4 \Z}, \ldots$

label: Quotient Group of Integers by Multiples
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {m \Z, +}$ be the additive group of integer multiples of $m$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ be the additive group of integers modulo $m$. Then the quotient group of $\struct {\Z, +}$ by $\struct {m \Z, +}$ is $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$. Thus: $\index \Z {m \Z} = m$

label: Quotient Group of Quadratic Residues Modulo 2 of 2-adic Units
snippet: Let $\Q_2$ be the $2$-adic numbers. Let $\Q_2^\times$ denote the set of invertible elements of $\Q_2$. Let $\paren{\Q_2^\times}^2 = \set{a^2 : a \in \Q_2^\times}$ Then the multiplicative quotient group $\Q_2^\times \mathop/ \paren{\Q_2^\times}^2$ has order $8$ with: $\set{1, -1, 5, -5, 2, -2, 10, -10}$ is a transversal

label: Quotient Group of Quadratic Residues Modulo p of P-adic Units
snippet: Let $\Q_p$ be the $p$-adic numbers for some prime $p \ne 2$. Let $\Q_p^\times$ denote the set of invertible elements of $\Q_p$. Let $\paren{\Q_p^\times}^2 = \set{a^2 : a \in \Q_p^\times}$ Then the multiplicative quotient group $\Q_p^\times \mathop/ \paren{\Q_p^\times}^2$ has order $4$: $\exists c \in \Q_p^\times \setminus \paren{\Q_p^\times}^2 : \set{1, p, c, cp}$ is a transversal

label: Quotient Group of Reals by Integers is Circle Group
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $K$ be the circle group. Then the quotient group of $\struct {\R, +}$ by $\struct {\Z, +}$ is isomorphic to $K$.

label: Quotient Group of Solvable Group is Solvable
snippet: Let $G$ be a solvable group. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Then, $G / N$, the quotient group of $G$ by $N$ is solvable.

label: Quotient Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Quotient Mappings ==

label: Quotient Mapping Induces Homeomorphism between Quotient Space and Image
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a quotient mapping. Let $\RR_f \subseteq S_1 \times S_1$ be the equivalence on $S_1$ induced by $f$: $\tuple {s_1, s_2} \in \RR_f \iff \map f {s_1} = \map f {s_2}$ Let $q_{\RR_f}: S_1 \to S_1 / \RR_f$ be the quotient mapping induced by $\RR_f$. Let $\tau_{\RR_f}$ be the quotient topology on $S_1 / \RR_f$ by $q_{\RR_f}$. Then there exists a uniquely defined homeomorphism $\tilde f: S_1 / \RR_f \to S_2$ such that $f = \tilde f \circ q_{\RR_f}$.

label: Quotient Mapping and Continuous Mapping Induces Continuous Mapping
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$, $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$, $T_3 = \struct {S_3, \tau_3}$ be topological spaces. Let $p: S_1 \to S_2$ be a quotient mapping. Let $g: S_2 \to S_3$ be a mapping such that for all $s_1, s_2 \in S_1$ with $\map p {s_1} = \map p {s_2}$, we have $\map g {s_1} = \map g {s_2}$. Then $g$ induces a mapping $f: S_2 \to S_3$ such that $f \circ p = g$. The induced mapping $f$ is a continuous mapping $g$ is a continuous mapping.

label: Quotient Mapping equals Surjective Identification Mapping
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping. Then $f$ is a quotient mapping, : $f$ is surjective, and $\tau_2$ is the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f$ and $T_1$.

label: Quotient Mapping is Coequalizer
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $S$ be a Set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Let $r_1, r_2: \RR \to S$ be the projections corresponding to the inclusion mapping $\RR \hookrightarrow S \times S$. Let $q: S \to S / \RR$ be the quotient mapping induced by $\RR$. Then $q$ is a coequalizer of $r_1$ and $r_2$ in $\mathbf{Set}$.

label: Quotient Mapping is Injection iff Equality
snippet: Let $\RR$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Then the quotient mapping $q_\RR: S \to S / \RR$ is an injection $\RR$ is the equality relation.

label: Quotient Mapping is Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $V$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $M$ be a subspace of $V$. Let $V / M$ be the quotient vector space. Let $Q: V \to V / M$ be the quotient mapping. Then $Q$ is a linear transformation.

label: Quotient Mapping is Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Then the quotient mapping $q_\RR: S \to S / \RR$ is a surjection.

label: Quotient Mapping on Quotient Topological Vector Space is Open Mapping
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $N$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $\struct {X/N, \tau_N}$ be the quotient topological vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : \struct {X, \tau} \to \struct {X/N, \tau_N}$ be the quotient mapping. Then $\pi$ is an open mapping.

label: Quotient Mapping on Structure is Epimorphism
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a congruence relation on an algebraic structure $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then the quotient mapping from $\struct {S, \circ}$ to the quotient structure $\struct {S / \RR, \circ_\RR}$ is an epimorphism: $q_\RR: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {S / \RR, \circ_\RR}: \forall x, y \in S: \map {q_\RR} {x \circ y} = \map {q_\RR} x \circ_\RR \map {q_\RR} y$

label: Quotient Metric on Vector Space induces Quotient Topology
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $d$ be an invariant metric such that the induced topology $\tau$ makes $\struct {X, \tau}$ a topological vector space. Let $N$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\struct {X/N, \tau_N}$ be the quotient topological vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $d_N$ be the quotient metric on $X/N$ induced by $d$. Then $d_N$ induces $\tau_N$.

label: Quotient Metric on Vector Space is Invariant Metric iff Vector Subspace is Closed
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $d$ be an invariant metric on $X$. Let $N$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping. Let $d_N$ be the quotient metric on $X/N$ induced by $d$. Then $d_N$ is an invariant metric $N$ is closed.

label: Quotient Metric on Vector Space is Invariant Pseudometric
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $d$ be an invariant metric on $X$. Let $N$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping. Let $d_N$ be the quotient metric on $X/N$ induced by $d$. Then $d_N$ is an invariant pseudometric.

label: Quotient Metric on Vector Space is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $d$ be an invariant metric on $X$. Let $N$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping. Then the mapping $d_N : X/N \times X/N \to \hointr 0 \infty$ defined by: $\ds \map {d_N} {\map \pi x, \map \pi y} = \inf_{z \mathop \in N} \map d {x - y, z}$ for each $\map \pi x, \map \pi y \in X/N$, is well-defined.

label: Quotient Norm is Norm
snippet:
Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $N$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X/N}$ be the quotient norm on $X/N$. Then $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X/N}$ is indeed a norm.

label: Quotient Norm on Quotient of C*-Algebra by Closed Ideal in terms of Positive Elements of Closed Unit Ball
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $	ext C^\ast$-algebra. Let $I$ be a closed ideal of $A$. Let $\struct {A/I, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{A/I} }$ be the quotient normed algebra of $A$ modulo $I$. Let $\pi : A 	o A/I$ be the quotient mapping. Let $B_I$ be the closed unit ball of $I$. Let $B_I^+ \subseteq B_I$ be the set of positive elements of $A$ contained in $B_I$. Then: $
orm {\map \pi a}_{A/I} = \inf \set {
orm {a - a x} : x \in B_I^+}$ for each $a \in A$.

label: Quotient Ring is Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $\struct {R / J, +, \circ}$ be the quotient ring of $R$ by $J$. Then $R / J$ is also a ring.

label: Quotient Ring of Cauchy Sequences is Division Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed division ring. Let $\CC$ be the ring of Cauchy sequences over $R$. Let $\NN$ be the set of null sequences. Then the quotient ring $\CC / \NN$ is a division ring.

label: Quotient Ring of Cauchy Sequences is Normed Division Ring
snippet:
Let $\struct {R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed division ring. Let $\CC$ be the ring of Cauchy sequences over $R$ Let $\NN$ be the set of null sequences. For all $\sequence {x_n} \in \CC$, let $\eqclass {x_n} {}$ denote the left coset $\sequence {x_n} + \NN$ Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_1: \CC \, ig / \NN 	o \R_{\ge 0}$ be defined by: $\ds  orall \eqclass {x_n} {} \in \CC \, ig / \NN: 
orm {\eqclass {x_n} {} }_1 = \lim_{n \mathop 	o \infty} 
orm {x_n}$ Then: $\struct {\CC \, ig / \NN, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_1 }$ is a normed division ring.

label: Quotient Ring of Ring with Unity is Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $\struct {R / J, +, \circ}$ be the quotient ring defined by $J$. Then $\struct {R / J, +, \circ}$ is a ring with unity, and its unity is $1_R + J$.

label: Quotient Rule for Derivatives
snippet: Let $\map j x, \map k x$ be real functions defined on the open interval $I$. Let $\xi \in I$ be a point in $I$ at which both $j$ and $k$ are differentiable. Define the real function $f$ on $I$ by: $\ds \map f x = \begin {cases} \dfrac {\map j x} {\map k x} & : \map k x \ne 0 \\ 0 & : \text {otherwise} \end {cases}$ Then, if $\map k \xi \ne 0$, $f$ is differentiable at $\xi$, and furthermore: $\map {f'} \xi = \dfrac {\map {j'} \xi \map k \xi - \map j \xi \map {k'} \xi} {\paren {\map k \xi}^2}$ It follows from the definition of derivative that if $j$ and $k$ are both differentiable on the…

label: Quotient Set Determined by Relation Induced by Partition is That Partition
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\PP$ be a partition of $S$. Let $\RR$ be the equivalence relation induced by $\PP$. Then the quotient set $S / \RR$ of $S$ is $\PP$ itself.

label: Quotient Space of Compact Space is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a compact topological space. Let $\RR \subseteq X \times X$ be an equivalence relation on $X$. Then, the quotient space: $T / \RR$ is compact.

label: Quotient Space of Hausdorff Space is not necessarily Hausdorff
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Let $T_\RR := \struct {S / \RR, \tau_\RR}$ be the quotient space of $S$ by $\RR$. Then $T_\RR$ is not necessarily also a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

label: Quotient Space of Real Line may be Indiscrete
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\Q$ denote the set of rational numbers. Let $\mathbb I$ denote the set of irrational numbers. Then $\set {\Q, \mathbb I}$ is a partition of $\R$. Let $\sim$ be the equivalence relation induced on $\R$ by $\set {\Q, \mathbb I}$. Let $T_\sim := \struct {\R / {\sim}, \tau_\sim}$ be the quotient space of $\R$ by $\sim$. Then $T_\sim$ is an indiscrete space.

label: Quotient Space of Real Line may be T0 but not T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on $\R$. Let $\struct {\R / {\sim}, \tau_\sim}$ be the quotient space of $\R$ by $\sim$. Then it is possible for $\struct {\R / {\sim}, \tau_\sim}$ to be a $T_0$ space but not a $T_1$ space.

label: Quotient Space of Real Line may not be T0
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then there exists an equivalence relation $\sim$ on $\R$ such that the quotient space $\struct {\R / {\sim}, \tau_\sim}$ is not a $T_0$ space.

label: Quotient Structure of Abelian Group is Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a congruence relation on an abelian group $\struct {G, \circ}$. Then the quotient structure $\struct {G / \RR, \circ_\RR}$ is an abelian group.

label: Quotient Structure of Group is Group
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a congruence relation on a group $\struct {G, \circ}$. Then the quotient structure $\struct {G / \RR, \circ_\RR}$ is a group.

label: Quotient Structure of Monoid is Monoid
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a congruence relation on a monoid $\struct {S, \circ}$ with an identity $e$. Then the quotient structure $\struct {S / \RR, \circ_\RR}$ is a monoid.

label: Quotient Theorem
snippet: Polynomial Factor Theorem Quotient-Remainder Theorem, also known as the Division Theorem A series of theorems in abstract algebra: Quotient Theorem for Epimorphisms Quotient Theorem for Group Epimorphisms Quotient Theorem for Monomorphisms Quotient Theorem for Sets Quotient Theorem for Surjections The terms factor and quotient are frequently interchangeable. Category:Abstract Algebra

label: Quotient Theorem for Group Homomorphisms
snippet: Let $\phi: G \to G'$ be a (group) homomorphism between two groups $G$ and $G'$. Then $\phi$ can be decomposed into the form: $\phi = \alpha \beta \gamma$ where: $\alpha: \Img \phi \to G'$ is a monomorphism $\beta: G / \map \ker \phi \to \Img \phi$ is an isomorphism $\gamma: G \to G / \map \ker \phi$ is an epimorphism.

label: Quotient Theorem for Sets
snippet: A mapping $f: S \to T$ can be uniquely factored into a surjection, followed by a bijection, followed by an injection. Thus: $f = i \circ r \circ q_{\RR_f}$ where: {{eqn | ll= q_{\RR_f}: | lo= S \to S / \RR_f: | l = \map {q_{\RR_f} } s | r = \eqclass s {\RR_f} | c = Quotient Mapping }} {{eqn | ll= r: | lo= S / \RR_f \to \Img f: | l = \map r {\eqclass s {\RR_f} } | r = \map f s | c = Renaming Mapping }} where: $\RR_f$ is the equivalence induced by $f$ $S / \RR_f$ is the quotient set of $S$ induced by $\RR_f$ This can be illustrated using a commutative diagram as follows: $\quad\quad \begin {xy}…

label: Quotient Theorem for Surjections
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a surjection. Then there is one and only one bijection $r: S / \RR_f \to T$ such that: $r \circ q_{\RR_f} = f$ where: $\RR_f$ is the equivalence induced by $f$ $r: S / \RR_f \to T$ is the renaming mapping $q_{\RR_f}: S \to S / \RR_f$ is the quotient mapping induced by $\RR_f$. This can be illustrated using a commutative diagram as follows: $\quad\quad \begin {xy} \xymatrix@L + 2mu@ + 1em { S \ar@{-->}[rr]^*{f = r \circ q_{\RR_f} } \ar[dd]_*{q_{\RR_f} } && T \\ \\ S / \RR_f \ar[urur]_*{r} } \end {xy}$

label: Quotient Topological Vector Space is Hausdorff iff Linear Subspace is Closed
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $N$ be a linear subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\tau_N$ be the quotient topology on $X/N$. Then $\struct {X/N, \tau_N}$ is Hausdorff : $N$ is a closed linear subspace.

label: Quotient Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Let $q_\RR: S \to S / \RR$ be the quotient mapping induced by $\RR$. Let $\tau_\RR$ be the quotient topology on $S / \RR$ by $q_\RR$. Then $\tau_\RR$ is a topology on $S$.

label: Quotient Topology of Partition Topology is Discrete Space
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a partition of a set $S$. Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the partition space formed from $\PP$. Let $S / \PP$ be the quotient set of $S$ by $\PP$. Then the quotient topology $\tau_{S / \PP}$ is a discrete topology.

label: Quotient Vector Space is Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $N$ be a linear subspace of $X$. Define: $X/N = \set {x + N : x \in X}$ where $x + N$ is the Minkowski sum of $x$ and $N$. Define: $\paren {x + N} +_{X/N} \paren {y + N} = \paren {x + y} + N$ for $x, y \in X$, and: $\alpha \circ_{X/N} {x + N} = \paren {\alpha x} + N$ for $\alpha \in K$ and $x \in X$. Then $\paren {X/N, +_{X/N}, \circ_{X/N} }_K$ is a vector space.

label: Quotient and Remainder to Number Base
snippet: Let $n \in \Z: n > 0$ be an integer. Let $n$ be expressed in base $b$: $\ds n = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^m {r_j b^j}$ that is: $n = \sqbrk {r_m r_{m - 1} \ldots r_2 r_1 r_0}_b$ Then: $\ds \floor {\frac n b} = \sqbrk {r_m r_{m - 1} \ldots r_2 r_1}_b$ $n \bmod b = r_0$ where: $\floor {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the floor function; $n \bmod b$ denotes the modulo operation.

label: Quotient is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N$ be natural numbers. Let us define the function $\operatorname {quot}: \N^2 \to \N$: $\map {\operatorname {quot} } {n, m} = \begin{cases} \text{the quotient when } n \text{ is divided by } m & : m \ne 0 \\ 0 & : m = 0 \end{cases}$ where the $\text {quotient}$ and $\text {remainder}$ are as defined in the Division Theorem: If $n = m q + r$, where $0 \le r < m$, then $q$ is the quotient. Then $\operatorname {quot}$ is primitive recursive.

label: Quotient of Banach Space by Topologically Complemented Subspace is Linearly Isomorphic to Topological Complement
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $Y$ be a closed vector subspace of $X$ that is topologically complemented. From Closed Subspace of Banach Space is Topologically Complemented iff has Topological Complement, $Y$ has a topological complement $Z$. Let $\struct {X/Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X/Y} }$ be the normed quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $Y$. Then $\struct {X/Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X/Y} }$ is linearly isomorphic to $Z$.

label: Quotient of C*-Algebra by Closed Ideal is C*-Algebra
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $	ext C^\ast$-algebra. Let $I$ be a closed ideal of $A$. Let $\struct {A/I, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{A/I} }$ be the quotient normed algebra of $A$ modulo $I$. Define $\ast : A/I 	o A/I$ by: $\paren {a + I}^\ast = a^\ast + I$ for each $a \in I$. Then $\struct {A/I, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{A/I} }$ is a $	ext C^\ast$-algebra.

label: Quotient of Cauchy Sequences is Metric Completion
snippet: Let $\struct {R, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed division ring. Let $d$ be the metric induced by $\struct {R, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Let $\CC$ be the ring of Cauchy sequences over $R$. Let $\NN$ be the set of null sequences in $R$. Let $\CC \,\big / \NN$ be the quotient ring of Cauchy sequences of $\CC$ by the maximal ideal $\NN$.

label: Quotient of Complex Conjugates
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\overline z$ be the complex conjugate of the complex number $z$. Then: $\overline {\paren {\dfrac {z_1} {z_2} } } = \dfrac {\paren {\overline {z_1} } } {\paren {\overline {z_2} } }$ for $z_2 \ne 0$.

label: Quotient of Divisible Module is Divisible
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $M$ be a divisible left $R$-module. Let $N \subseteq M$ be an $R$-submodule. Then the quotient module $M / N$ is divisible.

label: Quotient of F-Space by Closed Linear Subspace is F-Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, d}$ be an $F$-space. Let $N$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $d_N$ be the quotient metric on $X/N$ induced by $d$. Then $\struct {X/N, d_N}$ is an $F$-Space.

label: Quotient of Group by Center Cyclic implies Abelian
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $\map Z G$ be the center of $G$. Let $G / \map Z G$ be the quotient group of $G$ by $\map Z G$. Let $G / \map Z G$ be cyclic. Then $G$ is abelian, so $G = \map Z G$. That is, the group $G / \map Z G$ cannot be a cyclic group which is non-trivial.

label: Quotient of Group by Itself
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $G / G$ be the quotient group of $G$ by itself. Then: $G / G \cong \set e$ That is, the quotient of a group by itself is isomorphic to the trivial group.

label: Quotient of Modulo Operation with Modulus
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $x \bmod y$ denote the modulo operation: $x \bmod y := \begin{cases} x - y \floor {\dfrac x y} & : y \ne 0 \\ x & : y = 0 \end{cases}$ where $\floor {\dfrac x y}$ denotes the floor of $\dfrac x y$. Let $y \ne 0$. Then: $0 \le \dfrac x y - \floor {\dfrac x y} = \dfrac {x \bmod y} y < 1$

label: Quotient of Rationally Expressible Numbers is Rational
Quotient of Rationals by Integers is Injective
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, +}$ be the abelian group of rational numbers. Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the abelian group of integers, considered as a subgroup of $\struct {\Q, +}$. Then the quotient group $\Q / \Z$ is an injective object in the category of abelian groups.

label: Quotient of Ring of Polynomials in Ring Element on Integral Domain by that Polynomial is that Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an integral domain. Let $X \in R$ be transcencental over $D$. Let $D \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials in $X$ over $D$. Let $D \sqbrk X / \ideal X$ denote the quotient ring of $D \sqbrk X$ by the ideal of $D$ generated by $X$. Then: $D \sqbrk X / \ideal X \cong D$

label: Quotient of Sylow P-Subgroup
snippet: Let $P$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of a finite group $G$. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Then $P N / N$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G / N$.

label: Quotient of Symmetric Group by Alternating Group is Parity Group
snippet: Let $n \ge 2$ be a natural number. Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $A_n$ be the alternating group on $n$ letters. Then the quotient of $S_n$ by $A_n$ is the parity group $C_2$.

label: Quotients of 3 Unequal Numbers are Unequal
snippet: Let $x, y, z \in \R_{\ne 0}$ be non-zero real numbers which are not all equal. Then $\dfrac x y, \dfrac y z, \dfrac z x$ are also not all equal.

label: Quotients of Homeomorphic Spaces are Homeomorphic
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi : X \to Y$ be a homeomorphism from $X$ to $Y$. Let: $\RR_X \subseteq X \times X$ $\RR_Y \subseteq Y \times Y$ be equivalence relations on $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Suppose that, for all $x, x' \in X$: $\map {\RR_X} {x, x'} \iff \map {\RR_Y} {\map \phi x, \map \phi {x'}}$ Then: $X / \RR_X \sim Y / \RR_Y$ where $\sim$ denotes homeomorphic spaces.

label: Rabbit Problem
snippet: == Classic Problem == Let there be a pair of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbit rabbits]. For the purpose of this exercise, the following assumptions are made. Rabbits take one month to reach an age at which they may give birth. Every month thereafter, a breeding pair of rabbits produce one further pair of rabbits. Rabbits never die and never stop being able to produce further rabbits. How many pairs of rabbits will be produced from this single pair of rabbits after one year?

label: Radial Distance Function in Normal Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Let $U_p$ be the normal neighborhood of $p \in M$. Let $r : U_p \to \R$ be the radial distance function. Then $r$ is well-defined in $U_p$ independently of the choice of normal coordinates. Furthermore, $r$ is smooth on $U_p \setminus \set p$, where $\setminus$ denotes the set difference, and $r^2$ is smooth on $U_p$.

label: Radial Geodesic Connecting Two Points in Geodesic Ball is Unique Minimizing Curve
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $U = \map {\exp_p} {\map {B_\epsilon} 0 }$ be a geodesic ball centered at $p \in M$. Suppose $q \in U$. Suppose $\gamma$ is a radial geodesic from $p$ to $q$. Then, up to reparametrization, $\gamma$ is the unique minimizing curve from $p$ to $q$.

label: Radial Vector Field in Normal Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Let $U_p$ be the normal neighborhood of $p \in M$. Let $\partial_r$ be the radial vector field on $U_p \setminus \set p$, where $\setminus$ denotes the set difference. Then $\partial_r$ is well-defined in $U_p \setminus \set p$ independently of the choice of normal coordinates. Furthermore, $\partial_r$ is smooth on $U_p \setminus \set p$.

label: Radical of Prime Ideal
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $R$. Let $\map \Rad {\mathfrak p}$ be the radical of $\mathfrak p$. Then: $\map \Rad {\mathfrak p} = \mathfrak p$

label: Radical of Sum of Ideals

Radius of Curvature in Cartesian Form
snippet: Let $C$ be a curve defined by a real function which is twice differentiable. Let $C$ be embedded in a cartesian plane. The radius of curvature $\rho$ of $C$ at a point $P = \tuple {x, y}$ is given by: $\rho = \dfrac {\paren {1 + y'^2}^{3/2} } {\size {y' '} }$ where: $y' = \dfrac {\d y} {\d x}$ is the derivative of $y$ $x$ at $P$ $y' ' = \dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2}$ is the second derivative of $y$ $x$ at $P$.

label: Radius of Curvature in Parametric Cartesian Form
snippet: Let $C$ be a curve defined by a real function which is twice differentiable. Let $C$ be embedded in a cartesian plane and defined by the parametric equations: $\begin{cases} x = \map x t \\ y = \map y t \end{cases}$ The radius of curvature $\rho$ of $C$ at a point $P = \tuple {x, y}$ is given by: $\rho = \size {\dfrac {\tuple {x'^2 + y'^2}^{3/2} } {x' y - y' x} }$ where: $x' = \dfrac {\d x} {\d t}$ is the derivative of $x$ $t$ at $P$ $y' = \dfrac {\d y} {\d t}$ is the derivative of $y$ $t$ at $P$ $x$ and $y$ are the second derivatives of $x$ and $y$ $t$ at $P$.

label: Radius of Curvature in Whewell Form
snippet: Let $C$ be a curve defined by a real function which is twice differentiable. The radius of curvature $\kappa$ of $C$ at a point $P$ can be expressed in the form of a Whewell equation as: $\rho = \size {\dfrac {\d s} {\d \psi} }$ where: $s$ is the arc length of $C$ $\psi$ is the turning angle of $C$ $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the absolute value function.

label: Rank Plus Nullity Theorem
snippet: Let $G$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space. Let $H$ be a vector space. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a linear transformation. Let $\map \rho \phi$ and $\map \nu \phi$ be the rank and nullity respectively of $\phi$. Then the image of $\phi$ is finite-dimensional, and: $\map \rho \phi + \map \nu \phi = n$ By definition of rank and nullity, it can be seen that this is equivalent to the alternative way of stating this result: $\map \dim {\Img \phi} + \map \dim {\map \ker \phi} = \map \dim G$
