snippet: == Examples of Regular Star Polygons ==

label: Relation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Relations ==

label: Relation Contains Mapping is Equivalent to AoC
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Then: there exists a mapping $f \subseteq \RR$ whose domain is the same as the preimage of $\RR$ the axiom of choice holds.

label: Relation Induced by Mapping is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $\RR_f \subseteq S \times S$ be the relation induced by $f$: $\tuple {s_1, s_2} \in \RR_f \iff \map f {s_1} = \map f {s_2}$ Then $\RR_f$ is an equivalence relation.

label: Relation Induced by Partition is Equivalence
snippet: Let $\mathbb S$ be a partition of a set $S$. Let $\RR$ be the relation induced by $\mathbb S$. Then: $(1): \quad \RR$ is unique $(2): \quad \RR$ is an equivalence relation on $S$. Hence $\mathbb S$ is the quotient set of $S$ by $\RR$, that is: $\mathbb S = S / \RR$

label: Relation Induced by Quotient Set is Equivalence
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Let $S / \RR$ be the quotient set of $S$ determined by $\RR$. Let $\RR'$ be the equivalence relation induced by $S / \RR$ on $S$. Then $\RR' = \RR$.

label: Relation Intersection Inverse is Greatest Symmetric Subset of Relation
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Let $\powerset \RR$ be the power set of $\RR$. By definition, $\powerset \RR$ is the set of all relations on $S$ that are subsets of $\RR$. Then the greatest element of $\powerset \RR$ that is symmetric is: $\RR \cap \RR^{-1}$

label: Relation Isomorphism Preserves Equivalence Relations
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be relational structures. Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be (relationally) isomorphic. Then $\RR_1$ is an equivalence relation $\RR_2$ is also an equivalence relation.

label: Relation Isomorphism is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Relation isomorphism is an equivalence relation.

label: Relation Partitions Set iff Equivalence
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Then $S$ can be partitioned into subsets by $\RR$ $\RR$ is an equivalence relation on $S$. The partition of $S$ defined by $\RR$ is the quotient set $S / \RR$.

label: Relation Segment is Increasing
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR, \QQ$ be relations on $S$ such that $\RR \subseteq \QQ$ Let $x \in S$. Then $x^\RR \subseteq x^\QQ$ where $x^\RR$ denotes the $\RR$-segment of $x$.

label: Relation Symmetry
snippet: Every non-null relation has exactly one of these properties: it is either: symmetric, asymmetric or non-symmetric.

label: Relation between Direction Cosines
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a line embedded in a Cartesian $3$-space. Let $l$, $m$ and $n$ be the direction cosines of $\LL$ the $x$-axis, $y$-axis and $z$-axis respectively. Then: $l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1$

label: Relation between Floor and Ceiling
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\left \lfloor {x}\right \rfloor$ be the floor of $x$, and $\left \lceil {x}\right \rceil$ be the ceiling of $x$. Then the following results apply:

label: Relation between Geodesic and Exponential Map
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g, \nabla}$ be a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold without boundary endowed with the Levi-Civita connection. Let $TM$ be the tangent bundle of $M$. Let $\exp$ be the exponential map. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be an open real interval. Let $\gamma_v : I \to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic such that: $\map {\gamma '} 0 = v$ where $v \in TM$. Then: $\forall t \in I : \forall v \in TM : \map {\gamma_v} t = \map \exp {t v}$

label: Relation between Normal Neighborhood Charts on Riemannian Manifold
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Let $\tuple {x^i}$ and $\tuple {\tilde x^j}$ be normal neighborhood charts on $M$. Let $\map O {n, \R}$ be the orthogonal group. Let $A^j_i \in \map O {n, \R}$ be a constant matrix. Then: $\forall \tuple {x^i} : \forall \tuple {\tilde x^i} : \exists A^j_i \in \map O {n, \R} : \tilde x^j = A^j_i x^i$

label: Relation between Product and Box Topology
snippet: == Product and Box Topology ==

label: Relation between Square of Fibonacci Number and Square of Lucas Number
snippet: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. Let $L_n$ denote the $n$th Lucas number. Then: $5 {F_n}^2 + 4 \paren {-1}^n = {L_n}^2$

label: Relation between Two Ordinals
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be ordinals. Then either $S \subseteq T$ or $T \subseteq S$.

label: Relation between Volume Forms of Conformally Related Metrics on Oriented Riemannian Manifold
snippet: Let $M$ be an $n$-dimensional oriented Riemannian manifold. Let $g_1$ and $g_2$ be conformally related Riemannian metrics. That is, suppose: $g_2 = f g_1$ where $f \in \map {C^\infty} M$ is a positive smooth real function. Let $\rd V_{g_1}$ and $\rd V_{g_2}$ be Riemannian volume forms associated with $g_1$ and $g_2$. Then: $\ds \rd V_{g_2} = f^{\frac n 2} \rd V_{g_1}$

label: Relation is Antireflexive iff Disjoint from Diagonal Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on a set $S$. Then: $\RR$ is antireflexive $\Delta_S \cap \RR = \O$ where $\Delta_S$ is the diagonal relation.

label: Relation is Antisymmetric and Reflexive iff Intersection with Inverse equals Diagonal Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on a set $S$. Then $\RR$ is both antisymmetric and reflexive : $\RR \cap \RR^{-1} = \Delta_S$ where $\Delta_S$ denotes the diagonal relation.

label: Relation is Antisymmetric iff Intersection with Inverse is Coreflexive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$. Then: $\RR$ is antisymmetric $\RR \cap \RR^{-1}$ is coreflexive where $\RR^{-1}$ is the inverse of $\RR$. That is, : $\RR \cap \RR^{-1} \subseteq \Delta_S$

label: Relation is Connected and Reflexive iff Total
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$. Then: $\RR$ is both a connected relation and a reflexive relation $\RR$ is a total relation.

label: Relation is Connected iff Union with Inverse and Diagonal is Trivial Relation
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is a connected relation : $\RR \cup \RR^{-1} \cup \Delta_S = S \times S$ where $\RR^{-1}$ is the inverse of $\RR$ and $\Delta_S$ is the diagonal relation.

label: Relation is Equivalence iff Reflexive and Circular
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation in $S$. Then: $\RR$ is reflexive and circular $\RR$ is an equivalence relation.

label: Relation is Reflexive Symmetric and Antisymmetric iff Diagonal Relation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation in $S$. Then: $\RR$ is reflexive, symmetric and antisymmetric $\RR$ is the diagonal relation $\Delta_S$.

label: Relation is Reflexive and Coreflexive iff Diagonal
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is reflexive and coreflexive : $\RR = \Delta_S$ where $\Delta_S$ is the diagonal relation.

label: Relation is Set implies Domain and Image are Sets
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Let $\RR \subseteq V \times V$ be a relation. Let $\RR$ be a set. Then $\Dom \RR$ and $\Img \RR$ are also sets.

label: Relation is Symmetric and Antisymmetric iff Coreflexive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation in $S$. Then: $\RR$ is both symmetric and antisymmetric $\RR$ is coreflexive.

label: Relation is Total iff Union with Inverse is Trivial Relation
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is a total relation : $\RR \cup \RR^{-1} = S \times S$ where: $\RR^{-1}$ is the inverse of $\RR$. $S \times S$ is the trivial relation on $S$.

label: Relation on Empty Set is Equivalence
snippet: Let $S = \O$, that is, the empty set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is the null relation and is an equivalence relation.

label: Relation on Set of Cardinality 1 is Symmetric and Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is equal to $1$: $\card S = 1$ Let $\odot \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$. Then $\odot$ is both symmetric and transitive.

label: Relation on Set of Cardinality 2 cannot be Non-Symmetric and Non-Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is equal to $2$: $\card S = 2$ Let $\odot \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$. Then it is not possible for $\odot$ to be not symmetric and also not transitive.

label: Relation to Empty Set is Mapping iff Domain is Empty
snippet: Let $S$ be a set Let $S \times \O$ denote the cartesian product of $S$ with the empty set $\O$. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times \O$ be a relation in $S$ to $\O$. Then $\RR$ is a mapping $S = \O$.

label: Relational Closure Exists for Set-Like Relation
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\prec$ be a relation on $A$. Furthermore, let $\map {\prec^{-1} } a$ be a small class for each $a \in A$. Let $S$ be a small class that is a subset of the class $A$. Let $G$ be a mapping such that: $\map G x = A \cap \paren {\map {\prec^{-1} } x}$ Let $F$ be defined using the Principle of Recursive Definition: $\map F 0 = S$ $\map F {n^+} = \map F n \cup \map G {\map F n}$ Let $\ds T = \bigcup_{n \mathop \in \omega} \map F n$.

label: Relational Closure from Transitive Closure
snippet: Let $A$ be a set or class. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $A$. Let $\RR^+$ be the transitive closure of $\RR$. Let $B \subseteq A$. Let $B' = B \cup \inv {\paren {\RR^+} } B$. Let $C$ be an $\RR$-transitive subset or subclass of $A$ such that $B \subseteq C$. Then: $B'$ is $\RR$-transitive $B' \subseteq C$ If $B$ is a set and $\RR$ is set-like then $B'$ is a set. That is, $B'$ is the relational closure of $B$ under $\RR$.

label: Relational Structure admits Lower Topology
snippet: Let $R = \left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be a relational structure. Then there exists a relational structure with lower topology $T = \left({S, \preceq, \tau}\right)$ such that $T$ is a topological space.

label: Relational Structure with Topology of Subsets with Property (S) is Topological Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a relational structure with topology where $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is an up-complete ordered set $\tau$ is the set of all subsets of $S$ with property (S). Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is topological space.

label: Relations Compatible with Operation Form Complete Distributive Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $C$ be the set of relations on $S$ compatible with $\circ$. Then $\struct {C, \cap, \cup, \subseteq}$ is a complete distributive lattice.

label: Relations of Finite Partition and Finite Sub-Sigma-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $\eta, \gamma$ be finite partitions of $\Omega$. Let $\BB, \CC \subseteq \Sigma$ be finite sub-$\sigma$-algebras. Let: $\map \xi \cdot$ denote the generated finite partition $\map \sigma \cdot$ denote the generated $\sigma$-algebra $\le$ denote the order by refinement of partition. Then the following results hold:

label: Relations with Combinations of Reflexivity, Symmetry and Transitivity Properties
snippet: Let $S$ be a set which has at least $3$ elements. Then it is possible to set up a relation $\circledcirc$ on $S$ which has any combination of the $3$ properties: Reflexivity Symmetry Transitivity but this is not possible for a set which has fewer than $3$ elements.

label: Relationship between Component Types
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $p \in S$. Let: $A$ be the arc component of $p$ $J$ be the injective path component of $p$ $P$ be the path component of $p$ $C$ be the component of $p$ $Q$ be the quasicomponent of $p$. Then: $A \subseteq P \subseteq C \subseteq Q$ In general, the inclusions do not hold in the other direction.

label: Relationship between Limit Inferior and Lower Limit
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $f: S \to \R \cup \set {-\infty, \infty}$ be an extended real-valued function. Let $\sequence {s_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a convergent sequence in $S$ such that $s_n \to \bar s$. Then the lower limit of $f$ at $\bar s$ is bounded above by the limit inferior of $\sequence {\map f {s_n} }$: $\ds \liminf_{s \mathop \to \bar s} \map f s \le \liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map f {s_n}$

label: Relationship between Limit Point Types
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \subseteq X$. Let: $C$ be the set of condensation points of $A$ $W$ be the set of $\omega$-accumulation points of $A$ $L$ be the set of limit points of $A$ $D$ be the set of adherent points of $A$. Then: $C \subseteq W \subseteq L \subseteq D$ That is: Every condensation point is an $\omega$-accumulation point Every $\omega$-accumulation point is a limit point Every limit point is an adherent point. In general, the inclusions do not hold in the other direction.

label: Relationship between Transitive Closure Definitions
snippet: Let $x$ be a set. Let $a$ be the smallest set such that $x \in a$ and $a$ is transitive. Let $b$ be the smallest set such that $x \subseteq b$ and $b$ is transitive. Then $a = b \cup \set x$.

label: Relative Algebraic Closure with Algebraically Closed Extension is Algebraic Closure
snippet: Let $L$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $L/K$ be a field extension. Then the relative algebraic closure of $K$ contained in $L$ is an algebraic closure of $K$.

label: Relative Complement/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Relative Complement ==

label: Relative Complement Mapping on Powerset is Bijection
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\complement_S: \powerset S \to \powerset S$ denote the relative complement mapping on the power set of $S$. Then $\complement_S$ is a bijection. Thus each $T \subseteq S$ is in one-to-one correspondence with its relative complement.

label: Relative Complement inverts Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $A \subseteq S, B \subseteq S$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $A \subseteq B \iff \relcomp S B \subseteq \relcomp S A$ where $\complement_S$ denotes the complement relative to $S$.

label: Relative Complement inverts Subsets of Relative Complement
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $A \subseteq S, B \subseteq S$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $A \subseteq \relcomp S B \iff B \subseteq \relcomp S A$ where $\complement_S$ denotes the complement relative to $S$.

label: Relative Complement of Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Let $X \subseteq A$ and $Y \subseteq B$. Then: $\relcomp {A \mathop \times B} {X \times Y} = \paren {A \times \relcomp B Y} \cup \paren {\relcomp A X \times B}$

label: Relative Complement of Decreasing Sequence of Sets is Increasing
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\sequence {E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a decreasing sequence of sets in $X$. Then $\sequence {X \setminus E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is an increasing sequence of sets in $X$.

label: Relative Complement of Empty Set
snippet: The relative complement of the empty set is the set itself: $\relcomp S \O = S$

label: Relative Complement of Relative Complement
snippet: The relative complement of the relative complement of a set is itself: $\relcomp S {\relcomp S T} = T$ Thus, considered as a mapping on the power set of $S$: $\complement_S: \powerset S \to \powerset S: \relcomp S T = S \setminus T$ $\complement_S$ is an involution.

label: Relative Complement with Self is Empty Set
snippet: The relative complement of a set in itself is the empty set: $\relcomp S S = \O$

label: Relative Homotopy is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces. Let $K \subseteq X$ be a (possibly empty) subset of $X$. Let $\map \CC {X, Y}$ be the set of all continuous mappings from $X$ to $Y$. Define a relation $\sim$ on $\map \CC {X, Y}$ as: $f \sim g$ $f$ and $g$ are homotopic relative to $K$. Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

Relative Lengths of Lines Outside Circle
Relative Matrix of Composition of Linear Transformations
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $M, N, P$ be free $R$-modules of finite dimension $m, n, p > 0$ respectively. Let $\AA, \BB, \CC$ be ordered bases of $M, N, P$. Let $f: M \to N$ and $g : N \to P$ be linear transformations, and $g \circ f$ be their composition. Let $\mathbf M_{f, \BB, \AA}$ and $\mathbf M_{g, \CC, \BB}$ be their matrices relative to $\AA, \BB$ and $\BB, \CC$ respectively. Then the matrix of $g \circ f$ relative to $\AA$ and $\CC$ is: $\mathbf M_{g \mathop \circ f, \CC, \AA} = \mathbf M_{g, \CC, \BB} \cdot \mathbf M_{f, \BB, \AA}$

snippet: == Examples of Relative Matrices of Linear Transformations ==

label: Relative Sizes of Angles in Segments
snippet: In a circle: the angle in a semicircle is right the angle in a segment greater than a semicircle is acute the angle in a segment less than a semicircle is obtuse. Further: the angle of a segment greater than a semicircle is obtuse the angle of a segment less than a semicircle is acute.

label: Relative Sizes of Definite Integrals
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions which are continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$, where $a < b$. If: $\forall t \in \closedint a b: \map f t \le \map g t$ then: $\ds \int_a^b \map f t \rd t \le \int_a^b \map g t \rd t$ Similarly, if: $\forall t \in \closedint a b: \map f t < \map g t$ then: $\ds \int_a^b \map f t \rd t < \int_a^b \map g t \rd t$

label: Relativized Eberlein-Šmulian Theorem
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. $(1): \quad$ $\struct {A, w}$ is relatively compact in $\struct {X, w}$ $(2): \quad$ $\struct {A, w}$ is sequentially compact in $\struct {X, w}$ $(3): \quad$ $\struct {A, w}$ is relatively countably compact in $\struct {X, w}$.

label: Remainder Theorem
snippet: Chinese Remainder Theorem Polynomial Remainder Theorem, also known as the Little Bézout Theorem. Category:Chinese Remainder Theorem Category:Little Bézout Theorem Category:Named Theorems

label: Remainder of Fibonacci Number Divided by Fibonacci Number is Plus or Minus Fibonacci Number
snippet: Let $F_n$ and $F_m$ be Fibonacci numbers. By the Division Theorem, let: $F_n = q F_m + r$ where: $q \in \Z$ $r \in \Z: 0 \le r < \size {F_m}$ Then either $r$ or $\size {F_m} - r$, or both, is a Fibonacci number.

label: Remainder on Division is Least Positive Residue
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers such that $a \ge 0$ and $b \ne 0$. Let $r$ be the remainder resulting from the operation of integer division of $a$ by $b$: $a = q b + r, 0 \le r < \size b$ Then $r$ is equal to the least positive residue of $a \pmod b$.

label: Removable Singularity at Infinity implies Constant Function
snippet: Let $f : \C \to \C$ be an entire function. Let $f$ have an removable singularity at $\infty$. Then $f$ is constant.

label: Renaming Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Renaming Mappings ==

label: Renaming Mapping from Set of Mappings on Single Element
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $E$ be the set of all mappings from $X$ to $Y$. Let $b \in X$. Let $\RR \subseteq E \times E$ be the relation on $E$ defined as: $\RR := \set {\tuple {f, g} \in \RR: \map f b = \map g b}$ Let $e_b: E / \RR \to Y$ be the renaming mapping induced by $\RR$. Then $e_b$ is a bijection.

label: Renaming Mapping is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $r: S / \RR_f \to \Img f$ be the renaming mapping, defined as: $r: S / \RR_f \to \Img f: \map r {\eqclass x {\RR_f} } = \map f x$ where: $\RR_f$ is the equivalence induced by the mapping $f$ $S / \RR_f$ is the quotient set of $S$ determined by $\RR_f$ $\eqclass x {\RR_f}$ is the equivalence class of $x$ under $\RR_f$. The renaming mapping is always well-defined.

label: Repeated Composition of Injection is Injection
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an injection. Let the sequence of mappings: $f^0, f^1, f^2, \ldots, f^n, \ldots$ be defined as: $\forall n \in \N: \map {f^n} x = \begin {cases} x & : n = 0 \\ \map f x & : n = 1 \\ \map f {\map {f^{n - 1} } x} & : n > 1 \end{cases}$ Then for all $n \in \N$, $f^n$ is an injection.

label: Repeated Simpson's Rule/Also known as
snippet: == Repeated Simpson's Rule: Also known as == The repeated Simpson's rule is also known as just Simpson's rule. It is also known as the parabolic formula. It can also be seen as Simpson's formula, but this may be confused with Simpson's formulas, which are a set of completely different results.

label: Repeated Sum of Cubes of Digits of Multiple of 3
snippet: Let $k \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer. Let $f: \Z_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall m \in \Z_{>0}: \map f m = $ the sum of the cubes of the digits of $n$. Let $n_0 \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer which is a multiple of $3$. Consider the sequence: $s_n = \begin{cases} n_0 & : n = 0 \\ \map f {s_{n - 1} } & : n > 0 \end{cases}$ Then: $\exists r \in \N_{>0}: s_r = 153$ That is, by performing $f$ repeatedly on a multiple of $3$ eventually results in the pluperfect digital invariant $153$.

label: Replicative Function of x minus Floor of x is Replicative
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $f$ be a replicative function. Let $g: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\map g x = \map f {x - \floor x}$ Then $g$ is also a replicative function.

label: Representation of Degree One is Irreducible
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \cdot}$ be a finite group. Let $\rho: G \to \GL V$ be a linear representation of $G$ on $V$ of degree $1$. Then $\rho$ is an irreducible linear representation.

label: Representation of Integers in Balanced Ternary
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. $n$ can be represented uniquely in balanced ternary: $\ds n = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^m r_j 3^j$ $\sqbrk {r_m r_{m - 1} \ldots r_2 r_1 r_0}$ such that: where: $m \in \Z_{>0}$ is a strictly positive integer such that $3^m < \size {2 n} < 3^{m + 1}$ all the $r_j$ are such that $r_j \in \set {\underline 1, 0, 1}$, where $\underline 1 := -1$.

label: Representation of Number Base in that Base
snippet: Let $b \in \Z$ be an integer such that $b > 1$. Then $b$ is expressed in base $b$ as $10$.

label: Representation of Ternary Expansions
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $x$ be represented in base $3$ notation. While it may be possible for $x$ to have two different such representations, for example: $\dfrac 1 3 = 0.100000 \ldots_3 = 0.022222 \ldots_3$ it is not possible for $x$ be written in more than one way without using the digit $1$.

label: Representative of P-adic Number is Representative of Equivalence Class
snippet: Let $p$ be any prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $x \in \Q_p$. Then for any sequence $\sequence{y_n}$ of the rational numbers $\Q$: $\sequence{y_n}$ is a representative of the $p$-adic number $x$ $\sequence{y_n}$ is a representative of the equivalence class $x$.

label: Representatives of same P-adic Number iff Difference is Null Sequence
snippet:
Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rational numbers $\Q$. Let $\struct {\Q_p, 
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\sequence{\alpha_n}$ and $\sequence{ eta_n}$ be Cauchy sequences in $\struct {Q, 
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$. Then: $\sequence {\alpha_n}$ and $\sequence { eta_n}$ are representatives of the same $p$-adic number in $\Q_p$ the sequence $\sequence {\alpha_n -  eta_n}$ is a null sequence.

label: Repunit 19 is Unique Period Prime with Period 19
snippet: The repunit prime $R_{19}$ is a unique period prime whose reciprocal has a period of $19$: $\dfrac 1 {1 \, 111 \, 111 \, 111 \, 111 \, 111 \, 111} = 0 \cdotp \dot 00000 \, 00000 \, 00000 \, 000 \dot 9$

label: Repunit in Base 9 is Triangular
snippet: Let $m$ be a repunit base $9$. Then $m$ is a triangular number.

label: Residue Classes form Partition of Integers
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\Z_m$ be the set of residue classes modulo $m$: $\Z_m = \set {\eqclass 0 m, \eqclass 1 m, \dotsc, \eqclass {m - 1} m}$ Then $\Z_m$ forms a partition of $\Z$.

label: Residue Field of P-adic Norm on Rationals
snippet: Let $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rationals $\Q$ for some prime $p$. The induced residue field on $\struct {\Q,\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ is isomorphic to the field $\F_p$ of integers modulo $p$.

label: Residue at Multiple Pole
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be a function meromorphic on some region, $D$, containing $a$. Let $f$ have a single pole in $D$, of order $N$, at $a$. Then the residue of $f$ at $a$ is given by: $\ds \Res f a = \frac 1 {\paren {N - 1}!} \lim_{z \mathop \to a} \frac {\d^{N - 1} } {\d z^{N - 1} } \paren {\paren {z - a}^N \map f z}$

label: Residue at Simple Pole
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be a function meromorphic on some region, $D$, containing $a$. Let $f$ have a simple pole at $a$. Then the residue of $f$ at $a$ is given by: $\ds \Res f a = \lim_{z \mathop \to a} \paren {z - a} \map f z$

label: Residue of Fibonacci Number Modulo Fibonacci Number
snippet: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. Let $m, r$ be non-negative integers. Then: $F_{m n + r} \equiv \paren {\begin{cases} F_r & : m \bmod 4 = 0 \\ \paren {-1}^{r + 1} F_{n - r} & : m \bmod 4 = 1 \\ \paren {-1}^n F_r & : m \bmod 4 = 2 \\ \paren {-1}^{r + 1 + n} F_{n - r} & : m \bmod 4 = 3 \end{cases} } \pmod {F_n}$

label: Resolvent Mapping Converges to 0 at Infinity
snippet: Let $B$ be a Banach space. Let $\map \LL {B, B}$ be the set of bounded linear operators from $B$ to itself. Let $T \in \map \LL {B, B}$. Let $\map \rho T$ be the resolvent set of $T$ in the complex plane. Then the resolvent mapping $f : \map \rho T \to \map \LL {B, B}$ given by $\map f z = \paren {T - z I}^{-1}$ is such that $\ds \lim_{z \mathop \to \infty} \norm {\map f z}_* = 0$.

label: Resolvent Set of Bounded Linear Operator equal to Resolvent Set as Densely-Defined Linear Operator
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $T : \HH \to \HH$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $\map {\rho_1} T$ be the resolvent set of $T$ as a bounded linear operator. Let $\map {\rho_2} T$ be the resolvent set of $T$ as a densely-defined linear operator $\struct {\HH, T}$. Then: $\map {\rho_1} T = \map {\rho_2} T$

label: Resolvent Set of Bounded Linear Operator is Open
snippet: Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\C$. Let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $\map \rho T$ be the resolvent set of $T$. Then $\map \rho T$ is open.

label: Resolvent Set of Element in Closed Unital Subalgebra of Banach Algebra is Clopen in Resolvent Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a Banach algebra. Let $B$ be a closed unital subalgebra of $A$. Let $x \in B$. Let $\map {\rho_A} x$ and $\map {\rho_B} x$ be the resolvent sets of $x$ in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Then $\map {\rho_B} x$ is clopen in $\map {\rho_A} x$.

label: Resolvent Set of Element in Subalgebra
snippet: Let $A$ be a Banach algebra. Let $B$ be a closed unital subalgebra of $A$. Let $x \in B$. Let $\map {\rho_A} x$ and $\map {\rho_B} x$ be the resolvent sets of $x$ in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Then: $\map {\rho_B} x \subseteq \map {\rho_A} x$

label: Resolvent Set of Element of Banach Algebra is Open
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\rho_A} x$ be the resolvent set of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\rho_A} x$ is open.

label: Restricted Dipper Operation is Associative
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the initial segment of the natural numbers: $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {0, 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ Let $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the set defined as $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } \setminus \set 0$: $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {1, 2, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ The restricted dipper operation $+^*_{m, n}$ on $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ is associative.

label: Restricted Dipper Operation is Commutative
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the initial segment of the natural numbers: $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {0, 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ Let $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the set defined as $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } \setminus \set 0$: $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {1, 2, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ The restricted dipper operation $+^*_{m, n}$ on $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ is commutative.

label: Restricted Dipper Relation is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\RR^*_{m, n}$ be the restricted dipper relation on $\N$: $\forall x, y \in \N_{>0}: x \mathrel {\RR^*_{m, n} } y \iff \begin {cases} x = y \\ m \le x < y \text { and } n \divides \paren {y - x} \\ m \le y < x \text { and } n \divides \paren {x - y} \end {cases}$ Then $\RR^*_{m, n}$ is an equivalence relation.

label: Restricted Measure is Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\Sigma'$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma$. Then the restricted measure $\mu \restriction_{\Sigma'}$ is a measure on the measurable space $\struct {X, \Sigma'}$.

label: Restricted P-adic Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $p \in \N$ be a prime. Let $d^\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic metric on $\Z$: $\forall x, y \in \Z: \map {d^\Z_p} {x, y} = \norm {x - y}_p$ where $\norm {x - y}_p$ denotes the $p$-adic norm. Then $d^\Z_p$ is a metric.

label: Restriction is Subset of Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $X \subseteq S$. Then the restriction of $\RR$ to $X$ is a subset of $\RR$.

label: Restriction of Antireflexive Relation is Antireflexive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an antireflexive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is an antireflexive relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Antisymmetric Relation is Antisymmetric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an antisymmetric relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is an antisymmetric relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Antitransitive Relation is Antitransitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an antitransitive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is an antitransitive relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Asymmetric Relation is Asymmetric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a asymmetric relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a asymmetric relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Canonical Surjection to Restricted Dipper Semigroup is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\N_{0}$ to the restricted dipper semigroup $\struct {\map {D^*} {m, n}, \oplus^*_{m, n} }$. Then $\phi^*_{m, n}$ is an isomorphism from $\struct {\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }, +^*_{m, n} }$ to $\struct {\map {D^*} {m, n}, \oplus^*_{m, n} }$.

label: Restriction of Composition is Composition of Restriction
snippet: Let $X, Y, Z$ be sets. Let $f: X \to Y$ and $g: Y \to Z$ be mappings. Let $S \subseteq X$. Then: $\paren {g \circ f} \restriction S = g \circ \paren {f \restriction S}$

label: Restriction of Congruence Relation is Congruence
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\RR$ be a congruence relation for $\circ$ on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a congruence relation for $\circ_T$ on $T$.

label: Restriction of Connected Relation is Connected
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a connected relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a connected relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Continuous Mapping is Continuous
Restriction of Dipper Operation to Non-Zero Initial Segment is Closed
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the initial segment of the natural numbers: $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {0, 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ Let $+_{m, n}$ denote the dipper operation on $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$: $\forall a, b \in \N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }: a +_{m, n} b = \begin{cases} a + b & : a + b < m \\ a + b - k n & : a + b \ge m \end{cases}$ where $k$ is the largest integer satisfying: $m + k n \le a + b$ Let $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the set defined as $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }…

label: Restriction of Equivalence Relation is Equivalence
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is an equivalence relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Homeomorphism is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$, $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a homeomorphism between $T_1$ and $T_2$. Let $S$ be a subset of $S_1$. Let $f {\restriction_{S \times f \sqbrk S} } : S \to f \sqbrk S$ be the restriction of $f$ to $S \times f \sqbrk S$. Let $S$ and $f \sqbrk S$ bear their respective subspace topologies. Then $f {\restriction_{S \times f \sqbrk S} }$ is a homeomorphism.

label: Restriction of Homomorphism is Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, \odot}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a homomorphism. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Then the restriction of $\phi$ to $A \times \Img A$ is also a homomorphism.

label: Restriction of Homomorphism to Image is Epimorphism
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a homomorphism. Then a surjective restriction of $\phi$ can be produced by limiting the codomain of $\phi$ to its image $\Img \phi$.

label: Restriction of Identity Mapping is Identity Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $A$ be a subset of $S$. Then: $I_S \restriction_{A \times A} = I_A$ where: $I_S$ denotes the identity mapping on $S$ $I_S \restriction_{A \times A}$ denotes the restriction of $I_S$ to $A \times A$ $I_A$ denotes the identity mapping on $A$

label: Restriction of Injection is Injection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Let $X \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $f \sqbrk X$ denote the image of $X$ under $f$. Let $Y \subseteq T$ be a subset of $T$ such that $f \sqbrk X \subseteq Y$. The restriction $f \restriction_{X \times Y}$ of $f$ to $X \times Y$ is an injection from $X$ to $Y$.

label: Restriction of Inverse is Inverse of Restriction
snippet: Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be sets. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a bijection. Let $S \subseteq S_1$ be a subset of $S_1$. Let $f \sqbrk S$ be the image of $S$ under $f$. Let $f^{-1}$ be the inverse of $f$. Let $f {\restriction_{S \mathop \times f \sqbrk S}}$ be the restriction of $f$ to $S \times f \sqbrk S$. Let $f^{-1} {\restriction_{f \sqbrk S \mathop \times S}}$ be the restriction of $f^{-1}$ to $f \sqbrk S \times S$.

label: Restriction of Mapping is Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $X \subseteq S$. Let $f \restriction_X$ be the restriction of $f$ to $X$. Then $f \restriction_X: X \to T$ is a mapping: whose domain is $X$ whose preimage is $X$.

label: Restriction of Mapping to Small Class is Small
snippet: Let $F$ be a mapping. Let $A$ be a small class. Then the restriction $F {\restriction_A}$ is a small class.

label: Restriction of Measure to Trace Sigma-Algebra of Measurable Set is Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $A \in \Sigma$. Let $\Sigma_A$ be the trace $\sigma$-algebra of $A$ in $\Sigma$. Let $\mu \restriction_{\Sigma_A}$ be the restriction of $\mu$ to $\Sigma_A$. Then $\mu \restriction_{\Sigma_A}$ is a measure on $\struct {A, \Sigma_A}$.

label: Restriction of Non-Connected Relation is Not Necessarily Non-Connected
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a non-connected relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is not necessarily a non-connected relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Non-Continuous Mapping on Metric Space to Subspace may be Continuous
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be a metric spaces. Let $f: A_1 \to A_2$ be a mapping. Let $Y \subseteq A_1$. Let $f {\restriction_Y}: Y \to A_2$ be the restriction of $f$ to $Y$. Let $f {\restriction_Y}$ be $\tuple {d_Y, d_2}$-continuous. Then it is not necessarily the case that $f$ is also $\tuple {d_1, d_2}$-continuous.

label: Restriction of Non-Reflexive Relation is Not Necessarily Non-Reflexive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a non-reflexive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is not necessarily a non-reflexive relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Non-Symmetric Relation is Not Necessarily Non-Symmetric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a non-symmetric relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \ \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is not necessarily a non-symmetric relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Non-Transitive Relation is Not Necessarily Non-Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a non-transitive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is not necessarily a non-transitive relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Norm on Vector Space to Subspace is Norm
snippet:
Let $\Bbb F$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $
orm \cdot_X : X 	o \hointr 0 \infty$ be a norm on $X$. Let $Y$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $
orm \cdot_Y$ denote the restriction of $
orm \cdot_X$ to $Y$. Then $
orm \cdot_Y$ is a norm on $Y$.

label: Restriction of Ordering is Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\preceq$ be an ordering on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\preceq \restriction_T$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then $\preceq \restriction_T$ is an ordering on $T$.

label: Restriction of Reflexive Relation is Reflexive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a reflexive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a reflexive relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Ringed Space to Open Set is Ringed Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \OO_X}$ be a ringed space. Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset of $X$. Let $\struct {U, \OO_X {\restriction_U}}$ denote the restriction of $\struct {X, \OO_X}$ to $U$. Then $\struct {U, \OO_X {\restriction_U}}$ is a ringed space.

label: Restriction of Serial Relation is Not Necessarily Serial
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a serial relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is not necessarily a serial relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Sheaf to Open Set is Sheaf
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\FF$ be a sheaf of sets on $X$. Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset. Then the restriction $\FF {\restriction_U}$ of $\FF$ to $U$ is a sheaf.

label: Restriction of Strictly Well-Founded Relation is Strictly Well-Founded
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a strictly well-founded relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a strictly well-founded relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Symmetric Relation is Symmetric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a symmetric relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a symmetric relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Total Ordering is Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a total ordering. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $\preceq \restriction_T$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then $\preceq \restriction_T$ is a total ordering of $T$.

label: Restriction of Transitive Relation is Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a transitive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a transitive relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Union of Mappings which Agree Equals Mapping
snippet: Let $Y$ be a set. Let $\family {A_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of sets indexed by $I$. Let $\family {f_i: A_i \to Y}$ be a family of mappings indexed by $I$. Let $X = \ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} A_i$. Let $f = \ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} f_i : X \to Y$ where $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} f_i$ is the union of relations. Let for all $i, j \in I$, $f_i$ and $f_j$ agree on $A_i \cap A_j$. Let $f \restriction_{A_i} : A_i \to Y$ denote the restriction of $f$ to $A_i$. Then: $\forall i \in I: f \restriction_{A_i} = f_i: A_i \to Y$.

label: Restriction of Well-Founded Ordering is Well-Founded
snippet: Let $S$ be a set or class. Let $T$ be a subset or subclass of $S$. Let $\preceq$ be a well-founded ordering of $A$. Let $\preceq'$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then $\preceq'$ is a well-founded ordering of $T$.

label: Restriction of Well-Founded Relation is Well-Founded
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $\RR$ be a well-founded relation on $S$. Let $T$ be a subset or subclass of $S$. Let $\RR'$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\preceq'$ is a well-founded relation on $T$.

label: Restriction of Well-Ordering is Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set or class. Let $\preceq$ be a well-ordering of $S$. Let $T$ be a subset or subclass of $S$. Let $\preceq'$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then $\preceq'$ is a well-ordering of $T$.

label: Restriction to Subset of Strict Total Ordering is Strict Total Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set or class. Let $\prec$ be a strict total ordering on $A$. Let $T$ be a subset or subclass of $A$. Then the restriction of $\prec$ to $B$ is a strict total ordering of $B$.

label: Reversal of Number Multiplied by 11
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a number for which, when written in decimal notation, no two adjacent digits total to more than $9$. Let $n'$ denote the reversal of $n$. Then $n \times 11$ is the reversal of $n' \times 11$.

snippet: Let $p, q \in \R_{>0}$ be strictly positive real numbers such that $\dfrac 1 p - \dfrac 1 q = 1$. Suppose that the sequences $\mathbf x = \sequence {x_n}$ and $\mathbf y = \sequence {y_n}$ in $\C$ (or $\R$) are such that the series $\ds \paren {\sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \size {x_n}^p}^{1/p}$ and $\ds \paren {\sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \size {y_n}^{-q} }^{-1/q}$ are convergent. label: Reversed Directed Smooth Curve is Directed Smooth Curve
snippet: Let $C$ be a directed smooth curve in $\C$. Let $C$ be parameterized by the smooth path $\gamma: \left[{a \,.\,.\, b}\right] \to \C$. Define $\psi: \left[{a \,.\,.\, b}\right] \to \left[{a \,.\,.\, b}\right]$ by $\psi \left({t}\right) = a + b - t$. Define $\rho: \left[{a \,.\,.\, b}\right] \to \C$ by $\rho = \gamma \circ \psi$. Then $\rho$ is a smooth path which parameterizes a directed smooth curve $-C$. The directed smooth curve $-C$ is independent of the parameterization $\gamma$.

label: Rhombus is Equilateral but not Equiangular

label: Richard's Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == Certain expressions of natural language define real numbers unambiguously, while other expressions of natural language do not. For example: The real number whose integer part is $17$ and whose $n$th decimal place is $0$ if $n$ is even and $1$ if $n$ is odd defines the real number $17.1010101 \ldots = \dfrac {1693} {99}$. However, the phrase: the capital of France does not define a real number. Neither does the phrase: the smallest positive integer not definable in under sixty letters because the expression does not define a number unambiguously (see Berry's Paradox).

label: Riemann-Christoffel Tensor in Two Dimensions is Gaussian Curvature
snippet: Let $M$ be a Riemannian manifold of dimension $2$. Then the Riemann-Christoffel tensor on $M$ reduces to the Gaussian curvature on $M$.

label: Riemann-Hurwitz Formula
snippet: Now assume that $S$ and $S'$ are Riemann surfaces, and that the map $\pi$ is complex analytic. The map $\pi$ is said to be ramified at a point $P$ in $S'$ if there exist analytic coordinates near $P$ and $π(P)$ such that $π$ takes the form $π(z) = z^n$, and $n>1$. An equivalent way of thinking about this is that there exists a small neighborhood $U$ of $P$ such that $π(P)$ has exactly one preimage in $U$, but the image of any other point in $U$ has exactly $n$ preimages in $U$. The number $n$ is called the ramification index at $P$ and is denoted by $e_P$.

label: Riemann-Lebesgue Lemma
snippet: == Lemma == Let $f \in L^1$. Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int \map f x e^{i n x} \rd x = 0$ That is, the Fourier transform of an $L^1$ function vanishes at infinity.

label: Riemann-Lebesgue Theorem
snippet: Let $f: \closedint a b \to \R$ be a bounded mapping. Let $\mu$ be a one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Then $f$ is Darboux integrable the set of all discontinuities of $f$ is a $\mu$-null set.

label: Riemann Hypothesis
snippet: == Hypothesis == All the nontrivial zeroes of the analytic continuation of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$ have a real part equal to $\dfrac 1 2$.

label: Riemann Hypothesis implies Odd Number is Sum of at most 5 Primes
snippet: Let the truth of the Riemann Hypothesis be assumed. Let $n$ be an odd integer. Then $n$ is the sum of at most $5$ primes.

label: Riemann Integrable Dirac Function does not Exist
snippet: Let $\delta : \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $\phi : \R \to \R$ be a smooth function vanishing outside $\closedint a b$. Let $a \in \R_{> 0}$ be a real number. Suppose $\delta$ is Riemann integrable on $\closedint {-a} a$. Suppose for every $\phi$ we have that: $\ds \int_{-a}^a \map \delta x \map \phi x = \map \phi 0$ Then $\delta$ does not exist.

label: Riemann Integral Operator is Linear Mapping
snippet: Let $C \closedint a b$ be the space of continuous Riemann integrable functions. Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. Let $I : C \closedint a b \to \R$ be the Riemann integral operator. Then $I$ is a linear mapping.

label: Riemann Mapping Theorem/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Riemann Mapping Theorem == The Riemann Mapping Theorem arose during 's work on clarifying the nature of multiple-valued functions in the complex plane by means of Riemann surfaces.

snippet: Let: $\map f z = \operatorname P \set {\begin{matrix} a & b & c \\ \alpha & \beta & \gamma & z \\ \alpha' & \beta' & \gamma' \end{matrix} }$ where: $\operatorname P$ is the Riemann $P$-symbol $\alpha + \beta + \gamma + \alpha' + \beta' + \gamma' = 1$ $\alpha - \alpha'$ is not a negative integer. label: Riemann Removable Singularities Theorem
snippet: Let $U \subset \C$ be a domain. Let $z_0 \in U$. Let $f: U \setminus \set {z_0} \to \C$ be holomorphic. {{item|(4):|$\map f z \map o {\dfrac 1 {\cmod {z - z_0} } }$ as $z \to z_0$}}

label: Riemann Sphere is only Elliptic Riemann Surface
snippet: The Riemann sphere is the only elliptic Riemann surface (up to conformal isomorphism).

label: Riemann Surface/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Riemann Surfaces ==

label: Riemann Surface admits Metric of Constant Curvature
snippet: A Riemann surface admits a metric of constant curvature.

label: Riemann Surface is Metrizable
snippet: A Riemann surface is metrizable.

label: Riemann Surface is Path-Connected
snippet: A Riemann surface is path-connected.

label: Riemann Uniformization Theorem
snippet: Every connected $2$-dimensional manifold has a complete Riemannian metric with the constant Gaussian curvature.

label: Riemann Zeta Function Converges where Real Part Greater than 1
snippet: Let $\zeta$ denote the Riemann zeta function: $\forall s = \sigma + i t \in \C: \ds \map \zeta s = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 {n^s}$ Then $\map \zeta s$ is convergent when $\sigma > 1$.

label: Riemann Zeta Function and Prime Counting Function
snippet: For $\map \Re s > 1$: $\ds \log \map \zeta s = s \int_0^{\mathop \to \infty} \frac {\map \pi x} {x \paren {x^s - 1} } \rd x$ where: $\zeta$ denotes the Riemann Zeta Function $\pi$ denotes the Prime-Counting Function.

label: Riemann Zeta Function as a Multiple Integral
snippet: For $n \in \Z_{> 0}$, the Riemann zeta function is given by: $\ds \map \zeta n = \int_{\closedint 0 1^n} \frac 1 {1 - \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n x_i} \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \rd x_i$ where $\closedint 0 1^n$ denotes the Cartesian $n$th power of the closed real interval $\closedint 0 1$.

label: Riemann Zeta Function at Even Integers
snippet: The Riemann $\zeta$ function can be calculated for even integers as follows: {{eqn | l = \map \zeta {2 n} | r = \paren {-1}^{n + 1} \dfrac {B_{2 n} 2^{2 n - 1} \pi^{2 n} } {\paren {2 n}!} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \frac 1 {1^{2 n} } + \frac 1 {2^{2 n} } + \frac 1 {3^{2 n} } + \frac 1 {4^{2 n} } + \cdots | c = }} where: $B_n$ are the Bernoulli numbers $n$ is a positive integer.

label: Riemann Zeta Function at Non-Positive Integers
snippet: Let $n \ge 0$ be a integer. Then: $\map \zeta {-n} = \paren {-1}^n \dfrac {B_{n + 1} } {n + 1}$ where: $B_n$ is the $n$th Bernoulli number $\zeta$ is the Riemann Zeta function

label: Riemann Zeta Function at Odd Integers
snippet: == Unsolved Problem == The value of the Riemann $\zeta$ function for odd integers has not been determined. For certain values it has been calculated to whatever number of places, but an exact expression has never been found.

label: Riemann Zeta Function in terms of Dirichlet Eta Function
snippet: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function. Let $\eta$ be the Dirichlet eta function. Let $s \in \C$ be a complex number with real part $\sigma > 1$. Then: $\map \zeta s = \dfrac 1 {1 - 2^{1 - s} } \map \eta s$

label: Riemann Zeta Function of 1000
snippet: To at least $100$ decimal places: $\map \zeta {1000} \approx 1$ where $\zeta$ denotes the Riemann zeta function.

snippet: The Riemann zeta function of $4$ is given by: {{eqn | l = \map \zeta 4 | r = \dfrac 1 {1^4} + \dfrac 1 {2^4} + \dfrac 1 {3^4} + \dfrac 1 {4^4} + \cdots | c = }} {{eqn | r = \dfrac {\pi^4} {90} | c = }}

snippet: The Riemann zeta function of $6$ is given by: {{eqn | l = \map \zeta 6 | r = \dfrac 1 {1^6} + \dfrac 1 {2^6} + \dfrac 1 {3^6} + \dfrac 1 {4^6} + \cdots | c = }} {{eqn | r = \dfrac {\pi^6} {945} | c = }}

snippet: The Riemann zeta function of $8$ is given by: {{eqn | l = \map \zeta 8 | r = \dfrac 1 {1^8} + \dfrac 1 {2^8} + \dfrac 1 {3^8} + \dfrac 1 {4^8} + \cdots | c = }} {{eqn | r = \dfrac {\pi^8} {9450} | c = }}

label: Riemann Zeta Has No Zeroes With Real Part One
snippet: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function. Then for all $t \in \R$: $\map \zeta {1 + i t} \ne 0$

label: Riemannian Geodesic is Locally Minimizing
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $\gamma$ be a geodesic. Then $\gamma$ is locally minimizing.

label: Riemannian Manifold as Metric Space
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a connected Riemannian manifold with or without boundary. Let $d_g$ be the Riemannian distance. Then $\struct {M, d_g}$ is a metric space whose metric topology is the same as the given manifold topology.

label: Riemannian Manifold has Zero Gaussian Curvature iff Euclidean
snippet: Let $M$ be a Riemannian manifold of dimension $2$. The Gaussian curvature on $M$ is zero the Riemannian metric on $M$ is the same as the Euclidean metric.

label: Riemannian Volume Form of Orientable Hypersurface
snippet: Let $\struct {\tilde M, \tilde g}$ be an oriented Riemannian manifold. Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an orientable hypersurface with an induced metric. Let $N$ be a unit global normal vector for $M$. Let $\rd V_g$ be the Riemannian volume form. Then Riemannian volume form is given by: $\rd V_g = \valueat {\paren {N \lrcorner \rd V_{\tilde g} } } M$ where $\lrcorner$ denotes the interior multiplicaiton.

label: Riemannian Volume Form under Orientation-Preserving Isometry
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ and $\struct {\tilde M, \tilde g}$ be oriented Riemannian manifolds. Let $\phi : M \to \tilde M$ be an orientation-preserving isometry. Let $\rd V_g$ be the Riemannian volume form. Then: $\phi^* \rd V_{\tilde g} = \rd V_g$

label: Riesz's Convergence Theorem
Riesz-Fischer Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $p \in \R$, $p \ge 1$. The Lebesgue $p$-space $\map {\LL^p} \mu$, endowed with the $p$-norm $\norm {\cdot}_p$, is a Banach space.

label: Riesz-Kakutani Representation Theorem
snippet:
Let $X$ be a Hausdorff compact space. Let $\map \BB X$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $X$. Let $\map C {X, \R}$ be the space of real-valued continuous functions. Let $

label: Riesz-Markov-Kakutani Representation Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $\map {C_c} X$ be the space of continuous complex functions with compact support on $X$. Let $\Lambda$ be a positive linear functional on $\map {C_c} X$. There exists a $\sigma$-algebra $\MM$ over $X$ which contains the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\struct {X, \tau}$. There exists a unique complete Radon measure $\mu$ on $\MM$ such that: $\ds \forall f \in \map {C_c} X: \Lambda f = \int_X f \rd \mu$

label: Riesz Representation Theorem (Hilbert Spaces)
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $L$ be a bounded linear functional on $H$. Then there is a unique $h_0 \in H$ such that: $\forall h \in H: L h = \innerprod h {h_0}$

label: Right-Truncatable Prime/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Right-Truncatable Primes ==

label: Right Adjoint Functor is Unique up to Natural Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ be an adjunction between $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$. Then: the right adjoint functor $G$ of $F$ is unique up to isomorphism in the functor category $\operatorname{Funct} \tuple{C, D}$. That is: right adjoint functor $G$ is unique up to natural isomorphism.

label: Right Angle to Tangent of Circle goes through Center
Right Cancellable Commutative Operation is Left Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\circ$ be right cancellable and also commutative. Then $\circ$ is also left cancellable.

label: Right Congruence Class Modulo Subgroup is Right Coset
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H \le G$ be a subgroup. Let $\RR^r_H$ be the equivalence defined as right congruence modulo $H$. The equivalence class $\eqclass g {\RR^r_H}$ of an element $g \in G$ is the right coset $H g$. This is known as the right congruence class of $g \bmod H$.

label: Right Congruence Modulo Subgroup is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$. Let $x \equiv^r y \pmod H$ denote the relation that $x$ is right congruent modulo $H$ to $y$ Then the relation $\equiv^r$ is an equivalence relation.

label: Right Coset Space forms Partition
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H \le G$ be a subgroup. The right coset space of $H$ forms a partition of its group $G$: {{eqn | l = \neg \paren {x \equiv^r y} \pmod H | o = \iff | r = H x \cap H y = \O }}

label: Right Distributive Law for Natural Numbers
snippet: The operation of multiplication is right distributive over addition on the set of natural numbers $\N_{> 0}$: $\forall x, y, n \in \N_{> 0}: \paren {x + y} \times n = \paren {x \times n} + \paren {y \times n}$

label: Right Inverse Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Right Inverse Mappings ==

label: Right Limit Function is Right-Continuous
snippet: Let $I$ be an open interval. Let $f : I \to \R$ be a real function such that: for each $x \in I$, the right limit: $\ds \lim_{y \mathop \to x^+} \map f y$ exists. Define $f_\leftarrow : I \to \R$ by: $\ds \map {f_\leftarrow} x = \lim_{y \mathop \to x^+} \map f y$ for each $x \in I$. Then $f_\leftarrow$ is right-continuous. Further, if $f$ is right-continuous at $x$, then $\map {f_\leftarrow} x = \map f x$.

label: Right Module Does Not Necessarily Induce Left Module over Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct{G, +_G, \circ}$ be a right module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\circ' : R \times G \to G$ be the binary operation defined by: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: \lambda \circ' x = x \circ \lambda$ Then $\struct{G, +_G, \circ'}$ is not necessarily a left module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$

label: Right Operation has no Right Identities
snippet: Let $S$ be a set with more than $1$ element. Let $\struct {S, \to}$ be an algebraic structure in which the operation $\to$ is the right operation. Then $\struct {S, \to}$ has no right identities.

label: Right Operation is Closed for All Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\rightarrow$ be the right operation on $S$. That is: $\forall x, y \in S: x \rightarrow y = y$ Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Then for all $T \in \powerset S$, $\rightarrow$ is closed on $T$. Thus, for all $T \in \powerset S$: $\struct {T, \rightarrow}$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \rightarrow}$.

label: Right Order Topology on Real Numbers is Topology
snippet: Let $\tau$ be the right order topology on $\R$. Then $\tau$ forms a topology on $\R$. That is: $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ is a topological space.

label: Right Order Topology on Strictly Positive Integers as Neighborhood Space
snippet: Let $\Z_{>0}$ denote the set of (strictly) positive integers. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$. Let $U \subseteq \Z_{>0}$ be defined as being a neighborhood of $n$ $\forall m \in \Z: m \ge n \implies m \in U$ Then the set $\NN$ of all $U$ for all $n \in \Z_{>0}$ forms a neighborhood space which is the same as the right order space on $\Z_{>0}$.

label: Right Order Topology on Strictly Positive Integers is Topology
snippet: Let $\Z_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive integers. Let $\tau$ be the right order topology on $\Z_{>0}$. Then $\tau$ forms a topology on $\Z_{>0}$. That is: $T = \struct {\Z_{>0}, \tau}$ is a topological space.

label: Right Order Topology on Strictly Positive Integers is not Metrizable
snippet: Let $\Z_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive integers. Let $T = \struct {\Z_{>0}, \tau}$ denote the right order space on $\Z_{>0}$. Then $T = \struct {\Z_{>0}, \tau}$ is not a metrizable space.

label: Right Product with Degenerate Linear Transformation is Degenerate
snippet: Let $U, V, W$ be vector spaces over a field $K$. Let $G: U \to V$ be a degenerate linear transformation. Let $M: V \to W$ be a linear transformation. Then $M \circ G$ is degenerate.

label: Right Regular Representation by Inverse is Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $*: G \times G \to G$ be the operation: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = \map {\rho_{g^{-1} } } h$ where $\rho_g$ is the right regular representation of $G$ with respect to $g$. Then $*$ is a group action.

label: Right Regular Representation by Inverse is Transitive Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $*: G \times G \to G$ be the group action: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = \map {\rho_{g^{-1} } } h$ where $\rho_g$ is the right regular representation of $G$ with respect to $g$. Then $*$ is a transitive group action.

label: Right Regular Representation of Subset Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\rho_a: S \to S$ be the right regular representation of $S$ with respect to $a$. Then: $\rho_a \sqbrk T = T \circ \set a = T \circ a$ where $T \circ a$ denotes subset product with a singleton.

label: Right Whiskered Composite of Natural Transformation is Double-sided Whiskered Composite
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ and $\mathbf E$ be categories. Let $F, G : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ be a natural transformation. Let $K : \mathbf D \to \mathbf E$ be a covariant functor. Let $K \eta: K \circ F \to K \circ G$ denote the right whiskered composite of $\eta$ by $K$.

label: Right Whiskered Composite of Natural Transformation is Natural Transformation
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ and $\mathbf E$ be categories. Let $F, G : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ be a natural transformation. Let $K : \mathbf D \to \mathbf E$ be a covariant functor. Let $K \eta : K \circ F \to K \circ G$ denote the right whiskered composite of $\eta$ by $K$. Then: $K \eta$ is a natural transformation.

label: Right and Left Regular Representations in Topological Group are Homeomorphisms
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \cdot, \tau}$ be a topological group. Let $g \in G$ be an element of $G$. Then the left and right regular representations with respect to $g$: $L_g: \struct {G, \tau} \to \struct {G, \tau}$ and: $R_g: \struct {G, \tau} \to \struct {G, \tau}$ are homeomorphisms.

label: Ring Epimorphism Preserves Unity
snippet: Let $A$ be a ring with unity $1$. Let $B$ be a ring. Let $f: A \to B$ be a ring epimorphism. Then $\map f 1$ is a unity of $B$.

label: Ring Epimorphism from Integers to Integers Modulo m
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ be the ring of integers. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$ be the ring of integers modulo $m$. Let $\phi: \struct {\Z, +, \times} \to \struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall x \in \Z: \map \phi x = \eqclass x m$ where $\eqclass x m$ is the residue class modulo $m$. Then $\phi$ is a ring epimorphism, but specifically not a ring monomorphism. The image of $\phi$ is $\struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$. The kernel of $\phi$ is $m \Z$, the set of integer multiples of $m$.

label: Ring Homomorphism Preserves Negatives
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring homomorphism. Then: $\forall x \in R_1: \map \phi {-x} = -\paren {\map \phi x}$

label: Ring Homomorphism Preserves Subrings
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $S$ be a subring of $R_1$. Then $\phi \sqbrk S$ is a subring of $R_2$.

label: Ring Homomorphism Preserves Zero
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring homomorphism. Let: $0_{R_1}$ be the zero of $R_1$ $0_{R_2}$ be the zero of $R_2$. Then: $\map \phi {0_{R_1} } = 0_{R_2}$

label: Ring Homomorphism by Idempotent
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring. Let $e \in A$ be an idempotent element. Let $\ideal e$ be the ideal of $A$ generated by $e$. Then the mapping: $f: A \to \ideal e: a \mapsto e a$ is a surjective ring homomorphism with kernel the ideal $\ideal {1 - e}$ generated by $1 - e$.

label: Ring Homomorphism from Division Ring is Monomorphism or Zero Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \circ}$ and $\struct {S, +_S, *}$ be rings whose zeros are $0_R$ and $0_S$ respectively. Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. If $R$ is a division ring, then either: $(1): \quad \phi$ is a monomorphism (that is, $\phi$ is injective) $(2): \quad \phi$ is the zero homomorphism (that is, $\forall a \in R: \map \phi a = 0_S$).

label: Ring Homomorphism from Field is Monomorphism or Zero Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +_F, \circ}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$. Let $\struct {S, +_S, *}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_S$. Let $\phi: F \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Then either: $(1): \quad \phi$ is a monomorphism (that is, $\phi$ is injective) or $(2): \quad \phi$ is the zero homomorphism (that is, $\forall a \in F: \map \phi a = 0_S$).

label: Ring Homomorphism from Ring with Unity to Integral Domain Preserves Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \circ_R}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {D, +_D, \circ_D}$ be an integral domain whose zero is $0_D$ and whose unity is $1_D$. Let $\phi: R \to D$ be a ring homomorphism such that: $\map \ker \phi \ne R$ where $\map \ker \phi$ denotes the kernel of $\phi$. Then $\map \phi {1_R} = 1_D$.

label: Ring Homomorphism of Addition is Group Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring homomorphism. Then $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2}$ is a group homomorphism.

label: Ring Monomorphism from Integers to Rationals
snippet: Let $\phi: \Z \to \Q$ be the mapping from the integers $\Z$ to the rational numbers $\Q$ defined as: $\forall x \in \Z: \map \phi x = \dfrac x 1$ Then $\phi$ is a (ring) monomorphism, but specifically not an epimorphism.

label: Ring Operations on Coset Space of Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\powerset R$ be the power set of $R$. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be cosets of $J$. Let $X +_\PP Y$ be the sum of $X$ and $Y$, where $+_\PP$ is the operation induced on $\powerset R$ by $+$. label: Ring by Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {A, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $e$ be an idempotent element of $A$. Then the ideal $I := \ideal e$ generated by $e$ is a commutative ring with unity $\struct {I, +, \circ}$ with unity $e$.

label: Ring is Module over Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ}_R$ is an $R$-module.

label: Ring is not Empty
snippet: A ring cannot be empty.

label: Ring of Arithmetic Functions is Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\AA$ be the set of all arithmetic functions. Let $*$ denote Dirichlet convolution, and $+$ the pointwise sum of functions. The ring of arithmetic functions $\struct {\AA, +, *}$ is a commutative ring with unity.

label: Ring of Bounded Continuous Functions is Subring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ is a subring of $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$

label: Ring of Bounded Continuous Real-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct{\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ is a commutative ring

label: Ring of Continuous Mappings is Subring of All Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {R, +, *, \tau_{_R} }$ be a topological ring. Let $\struct {R^S, +, *}$ be the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $R$. Then: $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ is a subring of $\struct {R^S, +, *}$

label: Ring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct{\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ is a commutative ring

snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ is a ring

label: Ring of Endomorphisms is Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \oplus}$ be an abelian group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all group endomorphisms of $\struct {G, \oplus}$. Let $\struct {\mathbb G, \oplus, *}$ denote the ring of endomorphisms on $\struct {G, \oplus}$. Then $\struct {\mathbb G, \oplus, *}$ is a ring with unity.

label: Ring of Endomorphisms is not necessarily Commutative Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \oplus}$ be an abelian group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all group endomorphisms of $\struct {G, \oplus}$. Let $\struct {\mathbb G, \oplus, *}$ denote the ring of endomorphisms on $\struct {G, \oplus}$. Then $\struct {\mathbb G, \oplus, *}$ is not necessarily a commutative ring with unity.

label: Ring of Idempotents of Commutative and Unitary Ring is Boolean Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative and unitary ring. Let $\struct {A, \oplus, \circ}$ be its ring of idempotents. Then $\struct {A, \oplus, \circ}$ is a Boolean ring.

label: Ring of Integers Modulo Prime is Field
snippet: Let $m \in \Z: m \ge 2$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$‎ be the ring of integers modulo $m$. Then: $m$ is prime $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$ is a field.

label: Ring of Integers Modulo Prime is Integral Domain

label: Ring of Integers Modulo m cannot be Ordered Integral Domain

snippet: The integers $\Z$ form a principal ideal domain.

label: Ring of Integers of Number Field is Dedekind Domain
snippet: Let $K$ be an algebraic number field. Let $\OO_K$ be its ring of integers. Then $\OO_K$ is a Dedekind domain.

label: Ring of Integers of Number Field is Free Z-Module
snippet: Let $K$ be an algebraic number field. Let $\OO_K$ be its ring of integers. Let $\sqbrk {K : \Q}$ denote the degree of field extension $K : \Q$. Then $\OO_K$ is a free $\Z$-module of dimension $\sqbrk {K : \Q}$.

label: Ring of Linear Operators is Ring
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +}$ be an abelian group.. Let $\struct {G, +, \circ}_R$ be an $R$-module. Then $\struct {\map {\LL_R} G, +, \circ}$ is a ring.

label: Ring of Polynomial Forms is Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral subdomain of $R$. Let $X \in R$ be transcendental over $D$. Let $D \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials in $X$ over $D$. Then $D \sqbrk X$ is an integral domain.

label: Ring of Polynomial Forms is not necessarily Isomorphic to Ring of Polynomial Functions
snippet: Let $D$ be an integral domain. Let $D \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial forms in $X$ over $D$. Let $\map P D$ be the ring of polynomial functions over $D$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $D \sqbrk X$ is isomorphic with $\map P D$.

label: Ring of Polynomial Forms over Field is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose unity is $1_F$. Let $F \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials over $F$. Then $F \sqbrk X$ is a vector space over $F$.

label: Ring of Quaternions is Ring
snippet: The set $\mathbb H$ of quaternions forms a ring under the operations of addition and multiplication.

label: Ring of Square Matrices over Real Numbers

label: Ring of Square Matrices over Ring is Ring

label: Row Equivalence is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Row equivalence is an equivalence relation.

label: Row Equivalent Matrix for Homogeneous System has same Solutions
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix in the matrix space $\map {\MM_\R} {m, n}$ such that: $\mathbf A \mathbf x = \mathbf 0$ represents a homogeneous system of linear equations. Let $\mathbf H$ be row equivalent to $\mathbf A$. Then the solution set of $\mathbf H \mathbf x = \mathbf 0$ equals the solution set of $\mathbf A \mathbf x = \mathbf 0$. That is: $\mathbf A \sim \mathbf H \implies \set {\mathbf x: \mathbf A \mathbf x = \mathbf 0} = \set {\mathbf x: \mathbf H \mathbf x = \mathbf 0}$ where $\sim$ represents row equivalence.

label: Row Operation has Inverse
snippet: Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a metric space of order $m \times n$ over a field $K$. Let $\mathbf A \in \map \MM {m, n}$ be a matrix. Let $\Gamma$ be a row operation which transforms $\mathbf A$ to a new matrix $\mathbf B \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Then there exists another row operation $\Gamma'$ which transforms $\mathbf B$ back to $\mathbf A$.

label: Row Operation is Equivalent to Pre-Multiplication by Product of Elementary Matrices
snippet: Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a metric space of order $m \times n$ over a field $K$. Let $\mathbf A \in \map \MM {m, n}$ be a matrix. Let $\Gamma$ be a row operation which transforms $\mathbf A$ to a new matrix $\mathbf B \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Then there exists a unique nonsingular square matrix $\mathbf R$ of order $m$ such that: $\mathbf R \mathbf A = \mathbf B$ where $\mathbf R$ is the product of a finite sequence of elementary row matrices.

label: Row Operation to Clear First Column of Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_{m n}$ be an $m \times n$ matrix over a field $K$. Then there exists a row operation to convert $\mathbf A$ into another $m \times n$ matrix $\mathbf B = \sqbrk b_{m n}$ with the following properties: $(1): \quad$ Except possibly for element $b_{1 1}$, all the elements of column $1$ are $0$ $(2): \quad$ If $b_{1 1} \ne 0$, then $b_{1 1} = 1$. This process is referred to as clearing the first column.

label: Row Rank of Matrix equals Rank of Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix. The row rank of $\mathbf A$ is equal to the rank of $\mathbf A$.

label: Rule for Extracting Random Variable from Conditional Expectation of Product
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $\GG \subseteq \Sigma$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra. Let $X$ and $Y$ be integrable random variables such that: $X Y$ is integrable and: $Y$ is $\GG$-measurable. Let $\expect {X \mid \GG}$ be a version of the conditional expectation of $X$ given $\GG$. Let $\expect {X Y \mid \GG}$ be a version of the conditional expectation of $X Y$ given $\GG$. Then: $\expect {X Y \mid \GG} = Y \expect {X \mid \GG}$ almost everywhere.

label: Sample Matrix Independence Test
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space of real or complex-valued functions on a set $J$. Let $f_1, \ldots, f_n$ be functions in $V$. Let $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ from $J$ be given. Define the sample matrix: $S = \begin{bmatrix} \map {f_1} {x_1} & \cdots & \map {f_n} {x_1} \\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ \map {f_1} {x_n} & \cdots & \map {f_n} {x_n} \\ \end{bmatrix}$ Let $S$ be nonsingular. label: Sandwich Principle
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $g: A \to A$ be a mapping on $A$ such that: for all $x, y \in A$, either $\map g x \subseteq y$ or $y \subseteq x$. Then: $\forall x, y \in A: x \subseteq y \subseteq \map g x \implies x = y \lor y = \map g x$ That is, there is no element $y$ of $A$ such that: $x \subset y \subset \map g x$ where $\subset$ denotes a proper subset.

label: Satisfiability preserved in Supersignature
snippet: Let $\LL, \LL'$ be signatures for the language of predicate logic. Let $\LL'$ be a supersignature of $\LL$. Let $\Sigma$ be a set of $\LL$-sentences. $\AA \models_{\mathrm{PL} } \Sigma$ for some $\LL$-structure $\AA$ $\AA' \models_{\mathrm{PL} } \Sigma$ for some $\LL'$-structure $\AA'$ where $\models_{\mathrm{PL} }$ is the models relation. That is to say, the notion of satisfiability is preserved in passing to a supersignature.

label: Saturated Implies Universal
