snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a preordered set. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$ such that $A$ is coarser than $B$ and $B$ is an upper section. Then: $A \subseteq B$

label: Set Complement/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Set Complement ==

label: Set Complement inverts Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Then: $S \subseteq T \iff \map \complement T \subseteq \map \complement S$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $\complement$ denotes set complement.

label: Set Consisting of Empty Set is not Empty
snippet: Let $S$ be the set defined as: $S = \set \O$ Then $S$ is not the empty set. That is: $\O \ne \set \O$

label: Set Contained in Smallest Transitive Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then there exists a transitive set $G$ such that: $S \subseteq G$ and: if $Q$ is any transitive set such that $S \subseteq Q$, then $G \subseteq Q$.

label: Set Containing Only Zero is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The subset $\left\{{0}\right\} \subset \N$ is primitive recursive.

label: Set Definition by Predicate/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Set Definition by Predicate ==

label: Set Difference/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Set Difference ==

label: Set Difference Intersection with First Set is Set Difference
snippet: The intersection of the set difference with the first set is the set difference. Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \setminus T} \cap S = S \setminus T$

label: Set Difference Intersection with Second Set is Empty Set
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. The intersection of the set difference of $S$ and $T$ with $T$ is the empty set: $\paren {S \setminus T} \cap T = \O$

label: Set Difference Union First Set is First Set
snippet: The union of a set difference with the first set is the set itself: Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \setminus T} \cup S = S$

label: Set Difference Union Intersection
snippet: $S = \paren {S \setminus T} \cup \paren {S \cap T}$

label: Set Difference Union Second Set is Union
snippet: The union of a set difference with the second set is the union of the two sets. That is, let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \setminus T} \cup T = S \cup T$

label: Set Difference and Intersection are Disjoint
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Then: $S \setminus T$ and $S \cap T$ are disjoint where $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference and $S \cap T$ denotes set intersection.

label: Set Difference and Intersection form Partition
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that: $S \setminus T \ne \O$ $S \cap T \ne \O$ where $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference and $S \cap T$ denotes set intersection. Then $S \setminus T$ and $S \cap T$ form a partition of $S$.

label: Set Difference as Intersection with Complement
snippet: Set difference can be expressed as the intersection with the set complement: $A \setminus B = A \cap \map \complement B$

label: Set Difference is Right Distributive over Set Intersection
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be sets. Then: $\paren {A \cap B} \setminus C = \paren {A \setminus C} \cap \paren {B \setminus C}$ where: $A \cap B$ denotes set intersection $A \setminus C$ denotes set difference. That is, set difference is right distributive over set intersection.

label: Set Difference is Right Distributive over Union
snippet: Set difference is right distributive over union. Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {R \cup S} \setminus T = \paren {R \setminus T} \cup \paren {S \setminus T}$ where: $R \setminus S$ denotes set difference $R \cup T$ denotes set union.

label: Set Difference is Subset
snippet: Set difference is a subset of the first set: $S \setminus T \subseteq S$

label: Set Difference is Subset of Union of Differences
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $R \setminus S \subseteq \paren {R \setminus T} \cup \paren {T \setminus S}$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes subset $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference $S \cup T$ denotes set union.

label: Set Difference is not Associative
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. The expression: $\paren {R \setminus S} \setminus T = R \setminus \paren {S \setminus T}$ holds exactly when $R \cap T = \O$. Here $R \setminus S$ denotes set difference. Thus, set difference is not associative.

label: Set Difference of Cartesian Products
snippet: $\paren {S_1 \times S_2} \setminus \paren {T_1 \times T_2} = \paren {S_1 \times \paren {S_2 \setminus T_2} } \cup \paren {\paren {S_1 \setminus T_1} \times S_2}$

label: Set Difference of Events is Event
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an experiment with a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. The event space $\Sigma$ of $\EE$ has the property that: $A, B \in \Sigma \implies A \setminus B \in \Sigma$ That is, the difference of two events is also an event in the event space.

label: Set Difference of Intersection with Set is Empty Set
snippet: The set difference of the intersection of two sets with one of those sets is the empty set. Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \cap T} \setminus S = \O$ $\paren {S \cap T} \setminus T = \O$

label: Set Difference of Larger Set with Smaller is Not Empty
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. Let $\card S > \card T$. Then: $S \setminus T \ne \O$

label: Set Difference of Matroid Dependent Set with Independent Set is Non-empty
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $I$ be an independent subset of $M$. Let $D$ be a dependent subset of $M$. Then: $D \setminus I \ne \O$

label: Set Difference over Subset
snippet: Let $A$, $B$, and $S$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq B$. Then: $A \setminus S \subseteq B \setminus S$

label: Set Difference with Disjoint Set
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $S \cap T = \O \iff S \setminus T = S$ where: $S \cap T$ denotes set intersection $\O$ denotes the empty set $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference.

label: Set Difference with Empty Set is Self
snippet: The set difference between a set and the empty set is the set itself: $S \setminus \O = S$

label: Set Difference with Intersection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets.

label: Set Difference with Intersection is Difference
snippet: The set difference with the intersection is just the set difference. Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $S \setminus \paren {S \cap T} = S \setminus T$

label: Set Difference with Non-Empty Proper Subset is Non-Empty Proper Subset
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T \subsetneq S$ be a non-empty proper subset of $S$. Let $S \setminus T$ denote the set difference between $S$ and $T$. Then: $S \setminus T$ is a non-empty proper subset of $S$

label: Set Difference with Proper Subset
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T \subsetneq S$ be a proper subset of $S$. Let $S \setminus T$ denote the set difference between $S$ and $T$. Then: $S \setminus T \ne \O$ where $\O$ denotes the empty set.

label: Set Difference with Self is Empty Set
snippet: The set difference of a set with itself is the empty set: $S \setminus S = \O$

label: Set Difference with Set Difference
snippet: The set difference with the set difference of two sets is the intersection of the two sets: $S \setminus \paren {S \setminus T} = S \cap T = T \setminus \paren {T \setminus S}$

label: Set Difference with Set Difference is Union of Set Difference with Intersection
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $R \setminus \paren {S \setminus T} = \paren {R \setminus S} \cup \paren {R \cap T}$ where: $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference $S \cup T$ denotes set union $S \cap T$ denotes set intersection.

label: Set Difference with Subset is Superset of Set Difference
snippet: Let $A, B, S$ be sets or classes. Suppose that $A \subseteq B$. Then: $S \setminus B \subseteq S \setminus A$ where $\setminus$ represents set difference.

label: Set Difference with Superset is Empty Set
snippet: $S \subseteq T \iff S \setminus T = \O$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $S \setminus T$ denotes the set difference between $S$ and $T$ $\O$ denotes the empty set.

label: Set Difference with Union
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $R \setminus \paren {S \cup T} = \paren {R \cup T} \setminus \paren {S \cup T} = \paren {R \setminus S} \setminus T = \paren {R \setminus T} \setminus S$ where: $R \setminus S$ denotes set difference $R \cup T$ denotes set union.

label: Set Difference with Union is Set Difference
snippet: The set difference between two sets is the same as the set difference between their union and the second of the two sets: Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \cup T} \setminus T = S \setminus T$

label: Set Equality is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Set equality is an equivalence relation on the power set $\powerset S$ of $S$.

label: Set Equals Itself
snippet: All sets are equal to themselves: $\forall S: S = S$

label: Set Equation:Intersection
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Consider the set equation: $A \cap X = B$ The solution set of this is: $\O$ if $B \nsubseteq A$ $\set {B \cup Y: A \nsubseteq Y}$ otherwise.

label: Set Equation:Union
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Consider the set equation: $A \cup X = B$ The solution set of this is given by: $X = \begin {cases} \O & : A \nsubseteq B \\ \set {\paren {B \setminus A} \cup Y: Y \subseteq A} & : \text {otherwise} \end {cases}$

label: Set Equivalence Less One Element
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets which are equivalent: $S \sim T$ Let $a \in S$ and $b \in T$. Then: $S \setminus \set a \sim T \setminus \set b$ where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

label: Set Equivalence behaves like Equivalence Relation
snippet: Set equivalence behaves like an equivalence relation. That is: where $S, T, S_1, S_2, S_3$ are sets.

label: Set Equivalence of Regular Representations
snippet: If $S$ is a finite subset of a group $G$, then: $\card {a \circ S} = \card S = \left|{S \circ a}\right|$ That is, $a \circ S$, $S$ and $S \circ a$ are equivalent: $a \circ S \sim S \sim S \circ a$.

label: Set Finite iff Injection to Initial Segment of Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then $S$ is finite for some $n \in \N$ there exists an injection $f: S \to \N_{< n}$. Here, $\N_{< n}$ denotes an initial segment of $\N$.

label: Set Finite iff Surjection from Initial Segment of Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then $S$ is finite for some $n \in \N$ there exists a surjection $f: \N_{<n} \to S$. Here, $\N_{<n}$ denotes an initial segment of $\N$.

label: Set Intersection/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Set Intersection ==

label: Set Intersection Distributes over Set Difference
snippet: Set intersection is distributive over set difference. Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {R \setminus S} \cap T = \paren {R \cap T} \setminus \paren {S \cap T}$ $R \cap \paren {S \setminus T} = \paren {R \cap S} \setminus \paren {R \cap T}$ where: $R \setminus S$ denotes set difference $R \cap T$ denotes set intersection.

label: Set Intersection Not Cancellable
snippet: Let $S$ be a set and let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Let $S_1, S_2, T \in \powerset S$. Suppose that $S_1 \cap T = S_2 \cap T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $S_1 = S_2$.

label: Set Intersection Preserves Subsets
snippet: Let $A, B, S, T$ be sets. Then: $A \subseteq B, \ S \subseteq T \implies A \cap S \subseteq B \cap T$

label: Set Intersection expressed as Intersection Complement
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of a universal set $\Bbb U$. Let $\uparrow$ denote the operation on $A$ and $B$ defined as: $\paren {A \uparrow B} \iff \paren {\relcomp {\Bbb U} {A \cap B} }$ where $\relcomp {\Bbb U} A$ denotes the complement of $A$ in $\Bbb U$. Then: $A \cap B = \paren {A \uparrow B} \uparrow \paren {A \uparrow B}$

label: Set Intersection is Idempotent
snippet: Set intersection is idempotent: $S \cap S = S$

label: Set Intersection is Self-Distributive
snippet: Set intersection is self-distributive: $\forall A, B, C: \paren {A \cap B} \cap \paren {A \cap C} = A \cap B \cap C = \paren {A \cap C} \cap \paren {B \cap C}$ where $A, B, C$ are sets.

label: Set Less than Cardinal Product
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $T$ be nonempty. Suppose that $S \times T \sim \card {S \times T}$. Then: $\card S \le \card {S \times T}$

label: Set Partition/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Set Partitions ==

label: Set Products on Same Set are Equivalent
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\struct {P, \phi_1, \phi_2}$ and $\struct {Q, \psi_1, \psi_2}$ be products of $S$ and $T$. Then there exists a unique bijection $\chi: Q \to P$ such that: $\phi_1 \circ \chi = \psi_1$ $\phi_2 \circ \chi = \psi_2$

label: Set System Closed under Symmetric Difference is Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a system of sets. Let $\SS$ be such that: $\forall A, B \in \SS: A \symdif B \in \SS$ where $A \symdif B$ denotes the symmetric difference between $A$ and $B$. Then $\struct {\SS, \symdif}$ is an abelian group.

label: Set Theory/Examples
snippet: == Examples in Set Theory ==

label: Set Union/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Set Union ==

label: Set Union Preserves Subsets
snippet: Let $A, B, S, T$ be sets. Then: $A \subseteq B, \ S \subseteq T \implies A \cup S \subseteq B \cup T$

label: Set Union can be Derived using Axiom of Abstraction
snippet: Let $a$ be a set of sets. By application of the , the union $\bigcup a$ can be formed. Hence the union $\bigcup a$ can be derived as a valid object in Frege set theory.

label: Set Union expressed as Intersection Complement
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of a universal set $\Bbb U$. Let $\uparrow$ denote the operation on $A$ and $B$ defined as: $\paren {A \uparrow B} \iff \paren {\relcomp {\Bbb U} {A \cap B} }$ where $\relcomp {\Bbb U} A$ denotes the complement of $A$ in $\Bbb U$. Then: $A \cup B = \paren {A \uparrow A} \uparrow \paren {B \uparrow B}$

label: Set Union is Self-Distributive
snippet: Set union is self-distributive: $\forall A, B, C: \paren {A \cup B} \cup \paren {A \cup C} = A \cup B \cup C = \paren {A \cup C} \cup \paren {B \cup C}$ where $A, B, C$ are sets.

label: Set between Connected Set and Closure is Connected
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $H$ be a connected set of $T$. Let $H \subseteq K \subseteq H^-$, where $H^-$ denotes the closure of $H$. Then $K$ is connected.

label: Set equals Union of Power Set
snippet: Let $x$ be a set of sets. Let $\powerset x$ denote the power set of $x$. Let $\map \bigcup {\powerset x}$ denote the union of $\powerset x$. Then: $x = \map \bigcup {\powerset x}$

label: Set has Rank
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then $S$ has a rank.

label: Set in Standard Discrete Metric Space has no Limit Points
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, d}$ be the standard discrete metric space on a set $A$. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Then $H$ has no limit points.

label: Set is Clopen iff Boundary is Empty
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Then $H$ is both closed and open in $T$ : $\partial H = \O$ where $\partial H$ is the boundary of $H$.

label: Set is Closed iff Equals Topological Closure
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq T$. Then $H$ is closed in $T$ : $H = \map \cl H$ That is, a closed set equals its closure (which makes semantic sense).

label: Set is Closed iff it Contains its Boundary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Then $H$ is closed in $T$ : $\partial H \subseteq H$ where $\partial H$ is the boundary of $H$.

label: Set is Closed in Metric Space iff Closed in Induced Topological Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\tau$ be the topology induced by the metric $d$. Let $F$ be a subset of $M$. Then: $F$ is closed in $M$ $F$ is closed in $\struct {A, \tau}$

label: Set is Countable if Cardinality equals Cardinality of Countable Set
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be sets. Let: $\card X = \card Y$ where $\card X$ denotes the cardinality of $X$. If $X$ is countable then $Y$ is countable.

label: Set is Countable iff Cardinality not greater Aleph Zero
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Then: $X$ is countable $\size X \le \aleph_0$ where $\size X$ denotes the cardinality of $X$, $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping.

label: Set is Element of Successor
snippet: Let $x$ be a set. Let $x^+$ be the successor of $x$. Then $x \in x^+$.

label: Set is Element of its Power Set
snippet: A set is an element of its power set: $S \in \powerset S$

label: Set is Equivalent to Image under Injection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Then the image of $S$ under $f$ is equivalent to $S$.

label: Set is Equivalent to Itself
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then: $S \sim S$ where $\sim$ denotes set equivalence.

label: Set is Equivalent to Proper Subset of Power Set
snippet: Every set is equivalent to a proper subset of its power set: $\forall S: \exists T \subset \powerset S: S \sim T$

label: Set is G-Set iff Element of G-Ordered Set
snippet: Let $g$ be a progressing mapping. Let $x$ be a set. Then: $x$ is a $g$-set $x$ is an element of a $g$-ordered set.

label: Set is Infinite iff exist Subsets of all Finite Cardinalities
snippet: A set $S$ is infinite for all $n \in \N$, there exists a subset of $S$ whose cardinality is $n$.

label: Set is Neighborhood of Subset iff Neighborhood of all Points of Subset
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $N \subseteq S$ be a subset of $T$. Let $A \subseteq N$ be a subset of $T$. Then: $N$ is a neighborhood of $A$ in $T$ $N$ is a neighborhood of all points in $A$

label: Set is Not Element of Itself
snippet: There cannot exist a set which is an element of itself. That is: $\neg \exists a: a \in a$

label: Set is Open iff Disjoint from Boundary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Then $H$ is open in $T$ : $\partial H \cap H = \O$ where $\partial H$ is the boundary of $H$ in $T$.

label: Set is Open iff Neighborhood of all its Points
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $V \subseteq S$ be a subset of $T$. Then: $V$ is an open set of $T$ $V$ is a neighborhood of all the points in $V$.

label: Set is Open iff Union of Open Balls
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $U \subseteq A$. Then $U$ is open in $M$ it is a union of open balls.

label: Set is Ordinal iff Every Transitive Proper Subset is Element of it
snippet: Let $x$ be a set. Then: $x$ is an ordinal every transitive proper subset of $x$ is an element of $x$.

label: Set is Recursive iff Set and Complement are Recursively Enumerable
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \N$ be a set of natural numbers. Then: $S$ is a recursive set $S$ and $\N \setminus S$ are recursively enumerable sets.

label: Set is Recursively Enumerable iff Domain of Recursive Function
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \N$ be a set of natural numbers. Then: $S$ is recursively enumerable There exists a recursive function $f : \N \to \N$ such that $S = \Dom f$ where $\Dom f$ is the domain of $f$.

label: Set is Small Class
snippet: Let $x$ be a set. Then $x$ is a small class.

label: Set is Subset of Finite Infima Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X \subseteq \map {\operatorname{fininfs} } X$ where $\map {\operatorname{fininfs} } X$ denotes the finite infima set of $X$.

label: Set is Subset of Finite Suprema Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X \subseteq \map {\mathrm {finsups} } X$ where $\map {\mathrm {finsups} } X$ denotes finite suprema set of $X$.

label: Set is Subset of Intersection of Supersets
snippet: Let $S$, $T_1$ and $T_2$ be sets. Let $S$ be a subset of both $T_1$ and $T_2$. Then: $S \subseteq T_1 \cap T_2$ That is: $\paren {S \subseteq T_1} \land \paren {S \subseteq T_2} \implies S \subseteq \paren {T_1 \cap T_2}$

label: Set is Subset of Itself
snippet: Every set is a subset of itself: $\forall S: S \subseteq S$ Thus, by definition, the relation is a subset of is reflexive.

label: Set is Subset of Lower Closure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X \subseteq X^\preceq$ where $X^\preceq$ denotes the lower closure of $X$.

label: Set is Subset of Power Set of Union
snippet: Let $x$ be a set of sets. Let $\bigcup x$ denote the union of $x$. Let $\powerset {\bigcup x}$ denote the power set of $\bigcup x$. Then: $x \subseteq \powerset {\bigcup x}$

label: Set is Subset of Union
snippet: The union of two sets is a superset of each: $S \subseteq S \cup T$ $T \subseteq S \cup T$

label: Set is Subset of Upper Closure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X \subseteq X^\succeq$ where $X^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $X$.

label: Set is Subset of its Topological Closure
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq T$. Let $H^-$ be the closure of $H$ in $T$. Then: $H \subseteq H^-$

label: Set is Transitive iff Subset of Power Set
snippet: A set $a$ is transitive : $a \subseteq \powerset a$ where $\powerset a$ denotes the power set of $a$.

label: Set of 2-Dimensional Indefinite Real Orthogonal Matrices is not Compact in Normed Real Square Matrix Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^{2 \times2}, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the normed real matrix vector space. Let $\map O {1, 1} := \set {\mathbf R \in \R^{2 \times2} : \mathbf R^\intercal \mathbf J_{1,1} \mathbf R = \mathbf J_{1,1}}$ be the indefinite orthogonal group of degree $\paren {1, 1}$ over real numbers where: $\mathbf J_{1, 1} := \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 0 & -1 \\ \end{bmatrix}$ Then $\map O {1, 1}$ is not a compact set in $\struct {\R^{2 \times 2}, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$.

label: Set of 2-Dimensional Real Orthogonal Matrices is Compact in Normed Real Square Matrix Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^{2 \times2}, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the normed 2-dimensional real square matrix vector space. Let $\map O 2 := \set {\mathbf R \in \R^{2 \times2}: \mathbf R^\intercal \mathbf R = \mathbf I_2}$ be the orthogonal group of degree $2$ over real numbers. Then $\map O 2$ is a compact set in $\struct {\R^{2 \times 2}, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$.

label: Set of 3 Integers each Divisor of Sum of Other Two
snippet: There exists exactly one set of distinct coprime positive integers such that each is a divisor of the sum of the other two: $\set {1, 2, 3}$

label: Set of 5 Triplets whose Sums and Products are Equal
snippet: The following set of $5$ triplets of integers have the property that: the sum of the integers in each triplet are equal and: the product of the integers in each triplet are equal: $\tuple {6, 480, 495}$, $\tuple {11, 160, 810}$, $\tuple {12, 144, 825}$, $\tuple {20, 81, 880}$, $\tuple {33, 48, 900}$ The sum is $981$, and the product is $1 \, 425 \, 600$. This is the only known such set of $5$ triplets of integers with this property.

label: Set of 7 Anagrams which are Square
Set of Affine Mappings on Real Line under Composition forms Group
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of all real functions $f: \R \to \R$ of the form: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = r x + s$ where $r \in \R_{\ne 0}$ and $s \in \R$ Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be the algebraic structure formed from $S$ and the composition operation $\circ$. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group.

label: Set of All Completely Irreducible Elements is Smallest Order Generating
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below algebraic lattice. Then $\map {\operatorname {Irr} } L$ is order generating and $\forall X \subseteq S: X$ is order generating $\implies \map {\operatorname {Irr} } L \subseteq X$ where $\map {\operatorname {Irr} } L$ denotes the set of all completely irreducible elements of $L$.

label: Set of All Mappings is Small Class
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be small classes. It follows that the set of all mappings $S^T$ is a small class.

label: Set of All Mappings of Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $R$, $S$, and $T$ be sets. Then: $R^{S \times T} \sim \paren {R^S}^T$ where $R^{S \times T}$ denotes the set of all mappings from $S \times T$ to $R$.

label: Set of All Real Intervals is Semiring of Sets
snippet: Let $\mathbb S$ be the set of all real intervals. Then $\mathbb S$ is a semiring of sets, but is not a ring of sets.

label: Set of All Relations is a Monoid
snippet: The set of all relations $\Bbb E = \set {\RR: \RR \subseteq S \times S}$ on a set $S$ forms a monoid in which the operation is composition of relations. The only invertible elements of $\Bbb E$ are permutations. If $\RR$ is invertible, its inverse is $\RR^{-1}$.

label: Set of Associating Elements forms Subsemigroup of Magma
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\oplus$ be an operation on $S$ such that $\struct {S, \oplus}$ is a magma. Let $T \subseteq S$ be the subset of $S$ defined as: $T = \set {x \in S: \paren {x \oplus y} \oplus z = x \oplus \paren {y \oplus z} }$ Suppose $T \ne \O$. Then $\struct {T, \oplus {\restriction_T} }$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \oplus}$.

label: Set of Cardinality not Greater than Cardinality of Finite Set is Finite
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be sets such that $\card X \le \card Y$ and $Y$ is finite, where $\card X$ denotes the cardinality of $X$. Then $X$ is finite.

label: Set of Closed Elements wrt Closure Operator under Subset Operation is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\cl$ be a closure operator on the power set $\powerset S$ of $S$. Let $\mathscr C$ be the set of all subsets $T$ of $S$ such that: $\map \cl T = T$ Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\mathscr C, \subseteq}$ forms a complete lattice.

label: Set of Closed Subsets of Power Structure of Entropic Structure is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be a magma. Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be an entropic structure. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \odot_\PP}$ be the power structure of $\struct {S, \odot}$. Let $\TT$ be the set of all submagmas of $\struct {S, \odot}$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\TT, \odot_\PP}$ is a submagma of $\struct {\powerset S, \odot_\PP}$ which is itself an entropic structure.

label: Set of Codes for URM Programs is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $\operatorname{Prog}$ be the set of all code numbers of URM programs. Then $\operatorname{Prog}$ is a primitive recursive set.

label: Set of Column Matrices under Entrywise Addition forms Vector Space
snippet: == Corollary to Set of Matrices under Entrywise Addition forms Vector Space == Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\map {\MM_\GF} {m, 1}$ be set of all column matrices over a field $\GF$. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_\GF} {m, 1}, +}$ denote the abelian group formed from $\map {\MM_\GF} {m, 1}$ under matrix entrywise addition. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_\GF} {m, 1}, +, \times}_\GF$ denote the unitary module over $\GF$ where $\times$ denotes the matrix scalar product. Then $\struct {\map {\MM_\GF} {m, 1}, +, \times}_\GF$ forms a vector space.

label: Set of Common Divisors of Integers is not Empty
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. Let $S$ be the set of common divisors of $a$ and $b$. Then $S$ is not empty.

label: Set of Condensation Points is Monotone
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $A \subseteq B \implies {A^0} \subseteq B^0$ where $A^0$ denotes the set of condensation points of $A$

label: Set of Condensation Points is Subset of Derivative
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $A$ be a subset of $S$. Then: $A^0 \subseteq A'$ where $A^0$ denotes the set of condensation points of $A$ $A'$ denotes the derivative of $A$

label: Set of Condensation Points of Countable Set is Empty
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A$ be a subset of $S$. Then: if $A$ is countable, then $A^0 = \O$.

label: Set of Condensation Points of Union is Union of Sets of Condensation Points
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\left({A \cup B}\right)^0 = A^0 \cup B^0$

label: Set of Congruence Relations on Algebraic Structure forms Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\map \RR \odot$ be the set of all congruence relations on $\struct {S, \odot}$. Then $\struct {\map \RR \odot, \subseteq}$ is a complete lattice.

label: Set of Cuts forms Ordered Field
snippet: Let $\CC$ denote the set of cuts. Let $\struct {\CC, +, \times, \le}$ denote the ordered structure formed from $\CC$ and: the operation $+$ of addition of cuts the operation $\times$ of multiplication of cuts the ordering $\le$ of cuts. Then $\struct {\CC, +, \times, \le}$ is an ordered field.

label: Set of Cuts under Addition forms Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\CC$ denote the set of cuts. Let $\struct {\CC, +}$ denote the algebraic structure formed from $\CC$ and the operation $+$ of addition of cuts. Then $\struct {\CC, +}$ forms an abelian group.

label: Set of Discontinuities of Baire Function is Meager
snippet: Let $X \subseteq \R$. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a Baire function. Let $D$ be the set of points for which $f$ is discontinuous. Let $d$ be the Euclidean metric on $\R$. Then $D$ is meager in the metric space $\struct {X, d}$.

label: Set of Distributional Derivatives of Dirac Delta Distribution is Linearly Independent
snippet: Let $\delta \in \map {\DD'} \R$ be the Dirac delta distribution. Then for any $n \in \N$ the set of distributional derivatives $\set {\delta, \delta' \ldots, \delta^{\paren n} }$ is linearly independent in $\map {\DD'} \R$.

label: Set of Division Subrings forms Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be a division ring. Let $\mathbb K$ be the set of all division subrings of $K$. Then $\struct {\mathbb K, \subseteq}$ is a complete lattice.

label: Set of Divisors of Integer
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>1}$. Let $n$ be expressed in its prime decomposition: $n = p_1^{k_1} p_2^{k_2} \dotsm p_r^{k_r}$ where $p_1 < p_2 < \dotsb < p_r$ are distinct primes and $k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_r$ are positive integers. The set of divisors of $n$ is: $\set {p_1^{h_1} p_2^{h_2} \dotsm p_r^{h_r}: 0 \le h_i \le k_i, i = 1, 2, \ldots, r}$

label: Set of Doubletons of Natural Numbers is Countable
snippet: Let $S$ be the set defined as: $S = \set {\set {n_1, n_2}: n_1, n_2 \in \N, n_1 \ne n_2}$ where $\N$ denotes the set of natural numbers. Then $S$ is countably infinite.

label: Set of Elementary Events belonging to k Events is Event
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an experiment with a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_m$ be events in the event space $\Sigma$ of $\EE$. Let $S$ denote the set of all elementary events of $\EE$ which are elements of exactly $k$ of the events $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_m$. Then $S$ is an event of $\Sigma$.

label: Set of Endomorphisms of Non-Abelian Group is not Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \oplus}$ be a group which is non-abelian. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all group endomorphisms of $\struct {G, \oplus}$. Let $*: \mathbb G \times \mathbb G \to \mathbb G$ be the operation defined as: $\forall u, v \in \mathbb G: u * v = u \circ v$ where $u \circ v$ is defined as composition of mappings. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\mathbb G, \oplus, *}$ is not a ring.

label: Set of Endomorphisms on Entropic Structure is Closed in Induced Structure on Set of Self-Maps
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be a magma. Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be an entropic structure. Let $S^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to itself. Let $\struct {S^S, \oplus}$ denote the algebraic structure on $S^S$ induced by $\odot$. Let $T \subseteq S^S$ denote the set of endomorphisms on $\struct {S, \odot}$. Then $\struct {T, \oplus_T}$ is closed in $\struct {S^S, \oplus}$.

label: Set of Even Integers is Countably Infinite
snippet: Let $\Bbb E$ be the set of even integers. Then $\Bbb E$ is countably infinite.

label: Set of Even Integers is Equivalent to Set of Integers
snippet: Let $\Z$ denote the set of integers. Let $2 \Z$ denote the set of even integers. Then: $2 \Z \sim \Z$ where $\sim$ denotes set equivalence.

label: Set of Even Numbers is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $E \subseteq \N$ be the set of all even natural numbers. Then $E$ is primitive recursive.

label: Set of Finite Character with Choice Function is Type M
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of sets of finite character. Let $S$ have a choice function $C$ for its union $\ds \bigcup S$. Then $S$ is of type $M$. That is: every element of $S$ is a subset of a maximal element of $S$ under the subset relation.

label: Set of Finite Character with Choice Function is of Type M
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of sets with finite character. Let there exist a choice function for $S$. Then $S$ is of type $M$, that is: every element of $S$ is a subset of a maximal element of $S$ under the subset relation.

label: Set of Finite Character with Countable Union is Type M
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of sets of finite character. Let its union $\bigcup S$ be countable. Then $S$ is of type $M$. That is: every element of $S$ is a subset of a maximal element of $S$ under the subset relation.

label: Set of Finite Subsets of Countable Set is Countable
snippet: Let $A$ be a countable set. Then the set of finite subsets of $A$ is countable.

label: Set of Finite Subsets under Induced Operation is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the power structure of $\struct {S, \circ}$ Let $T \subseteq \powerset S$ be the set of all finite subsets of $S$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {T, \circ_\PP}$ is closed.

label: Set of Finite Suprema is Directed
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice. Let $X$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $\set {\sup A: A \in \map {\operatorname {Fin} } X \land A \ne \O}$ is directed. where $\map {\operatorname {Fin} } X$ denotes the set of all finite subsets of $X$.

label: Set of Finitely Supported Functions on Integers is Countable
snippet: Let $\SS$ be the set of functions $f : \Z \to \Z$ for which there exists $N \in \N$ such that: $\map f n = 0$ for all $n \in \Z$ with $\size n > N$. Then $\SS$ is countable.

label: Set of Homomorphisms to Abelian Group is Subgroup of All Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, \oplus}$ be an abelian group. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the algebraic structure on $T^S$ induced by $\oplus$. Then the set of all homomorphisms from $\struct {S, \circ}$ into $\struct {T, \oplus}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$.

label: Set of Ideals forms Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\mathbb K$ be the set of all ideals of $K$. Then $\struct {\mathbb K, \subseteq}$ is a complete lattice.

label: Set of Idempotent Elements of Entropic Structure is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be an algebraic structure such that $\odot$ is entropic. Let $T \subseteq S$ be the set of idempotent elements of $S$. Then $\struct {T, \odot}$ is closed.

label: Set of Images of Reflexive Relation is Cover of Set
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a reflexive relation in $S$. Let $\II = \set{\map \RR x : x \in S}$ be the set of images under $\RR$. Then: $\II$ is a cover of $S$

label: Set of Infima for Sequence is Directed
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $\struct {A, \precsim}$ be a non-empty directed set. Let $Z: A \to S$ be a net. Let $D = \set {\map \inf {Z \sqbrk {\map \precsim j} }: j \in A}$ be a subset of $S$. Then $D$ is directed.

label: Set of Infinite Sequences is Uncountable
snippet: Let $S$ be a set which contains more than one element. Let $S^\infty$ denote the set of all sequences of elements of $S$. Then $S^\infty$ is uncountable.

label: Set of Integer Combinations equals Set of Multiples of GCD
snippet: The set of all integer combinations of $a$ and $b$ is precisely the set of all integer multiples of the GCD of $a$ and $b$: $\gcd \set {a, b} \divides c \iff \exists x, y \in \Z: c = x a + y b$

label: Set of Integer Combinations includes Zero
snippet: == Lemma == Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. Let $S = \set {a x + b y: x, y \in \Z}$ be the set of integer combinations of $a$ and $b$. Then $0 \in S$.

label: Set of Integer Combinations includes those Integers
snippet: == Lemma == Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. Let $S = \set {a x + b y: x, y \in \Z}$ be the set of integer combinations of $a$ and $b$. Then $a \in S$ and $b \in S$.

label: Set of Integer Multiples/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Sets of Integer Multiples ==

label: Set of Integer Multiples is Integral Ideal
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $m \Z$ denote the set of integer multiples of $m$. Then $m \Z$ is an integral ideal.

label: Set of Integer Multiples of GCD
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$. Let $m \Z$ denote the set of integer multiples of $m$ Then: $m \Z \cup n \Z \subseteq \gcd \set {m, n} \Z$ where $\gcd$ denotes greatest common divisor.

label: Set of Integers Bounded Above by Integer has Greatest Element
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Let $\le$ be the ordering on the integers. Let $\O \subset S \subseteq \Z$ such that $S$ is bounded above in $\struct {\Z, \le}$. Then $S$ has a greatest element.

label: Set of Integers Bounded Above by Real Number has Greatest Element
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Let $\le$ be the usual ordering on the real numbers $\R$. Let $\O \subset S \subseteq \Z$ such that $S$ is bounded above in $\struct {\R, \le}$. Then $S$ has a greatest element.

label: Set of Integers Bounded Below by Integer has Smallest Element
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Let $\le$ be the ordering on the integers. Let $\O \subset S \subseteq \Z$ such that $S$ is bounded below in $\struct {\Z, \le}$. Then $S$ has a smallest element.

label: Set of Integers Bounded Below by Real Number has Smallest Element
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Let $\le$ be the usual ordering on the real numbers $\R$. Let $\O \subset S \subseteq \Z$ such that $S$ is bounded below in $\struct {\R, \le}$. Then $S$ has a smallest element.

label: Set of Integers can be Well-Ordered
snippet: The set of integers $\Z$ can be well-ordered with an appropriately chosen ordering.

label: Set of Integers is not Bounded
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as an Euclidean space. The set $\Z$ of integers is not bounded in $\R$.

label: Set of Integers is not Compact
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Then $\Z$ is not compact.

label: Set of Integers is not Well-Ordered by Usual Ordering
snippet: The set of integers $\Z$ is not well-ordered under the usual ordering $\le$.

label: Set of Integers under Addition is Isomorphic to Set of Even Integers under Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the algebraic structure formed by the set of integers under the operation of addition. Let $\struct {2 \Z, +}$ be the algebraic structure formed by the set of even integers under the operation of addition. Then $\struct {\Z, +}$ and $\struct {2 \Z, +}$ are isomorphic.

label: Set of Integers with GCD of 1 are not necessarily Pairwise Coprime
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of integers such that $S$ has more than $2$ elements: $S = \set {s_1, s_2, \ldots, s_n}$ Let: $\map \gcd S = 1$ where $\gcd$ denotes the GCD of $S$. Then it is not necessarily the case that there exist a pair of elements of $S$ which are themselves pairwise coprime: $\exists i, j \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}: \gcd \set {s_i, s_j} = 1$

label: Set of Intersections with Superset is Cover
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a cover of $S$. Let $T \supseteq S$ be a superset of $S$. Then: $\set {C \cap T : C \in \CC}$ is a cover of $S$.

label: Set of Inverse Positive Integers with Zero is Compact
snippet: Let $K$ be the set of inverse positive integers with zero: $\ds K := \set {1, \frac 1 2, \frac 1 3, \dots} \cup \set 0$ Let $\struct {\R, \size {\, \cdot \,}}$ be the normed vector space of real numbers. Then $K$ is compact in real numbers.

label: Set of Invertible Continuous Transformations is Open Subset of Continuous Linear Transformations in Supremum Operator Norm Topology
snippet: Let $X$ be a Banach space. Let $\map {CL} X$ be the continuous linear operator space on $X$. Let $\map {GL} X$ denote the set of all invertible continuous linear operators on $X$. Then $\map {GL} X \subseteq \map {CL} X$ in the supremum operator norm topology.

label: Set of Invertible Mappings forms Symmetric Group
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\GG$ be the set of all invertible mappings from $S$ to $S$. Then $\struct {\GG, \circ}$ is the symmetric group on $S$.

label: Set of Isolated Points of Metric Space is Disjoint from Limit Points
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$ be a subset of $A$. Let $H'$ be the set of limit points of $H$. Let $H^i$ be the set of isolated points of $H$. Then: $H' \cap H^i = \O$

label: Set of Isometries in Complex Plane under Composition forms Group
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of all bijective complex functions $f: \C \to \C$ which preserve distance when embedded in the complex plane. That is: $\size {\map f a - \map f b} = \size {a - b}$ where $\size z$ denotes the complex modulus of $z \in \C$. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be the algebraic structure formed from $S$ and the composition operation $\circ$. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group.

label: Set of Isometries in Euclidean Space under Composition forms Group
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^n, d}$ be a real Euclidean space of $n$ dimensions. Let $S$ be the set of all mappings $f: \R^n \to \R^n$ which preserve distance: That is: $\map d {\map f a, \map f b} = \map d {a, b}$ Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be the algebraic structure formed from $S$ and the composition operation $\circ$. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group.

label: Set of Linear Combinations of Finite Set of Elements of Principal Ideal Domain is Principal Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be a principal ideal domain. Let $a_1, a_2, \dotsc, a_n$ be non-zero elements of $D$. Let $J$ be the set of all linear combinations in $D$ of $\set {a_1, a_2, \dotsc, a_n}$ Then for some $x \in D$: $J = \ideal x$ where $\ideal x$ denotes the principal ideal generated by $x$.

label: Set of Linear Subspaces is Closed under Intersection
snippet: Let $\struct {V, +, \circ}_K$ be a $K$-vector space. Let $\family {M_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of subspaces of $V$. Then $M := \ds \bigcap_{i \mathop \in I} M_i$ is also a subspace of $V$.

label: Set of Linear Transformations is Isomorphic to Matrix Space
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $F$, $G$ and $H$ be free $R$-modules of finite dimension $p, n, m > 0$ respectively. Let $\sequence {a_p}$, $\sequence {b_n}$ and $\sequence {c_m}$ be ordered bases Let $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$ denote the set of all linear transformations from $G$ to $H$. Let $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$ be the $m \times n$ matrix space over $R$. Let $\sqbrk {u; \sequence {c_m}, \sequence {b_n} }$ be the matrix of $u$ relative to $\sequence {b_n}$ and $\sequence {c_m}$.

label: Set of Linear Transformations over Commutative Ring forms Submodule of Module of All Mappings
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ and $\struct {H, +_H, \circ}_R$ be $R$-modules. Let $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$ be the set of all linear transformations from $G$ to $H$. Then $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$ is a submodule of the $R$-module $H^G$.

label: Set of Linear Transformations under Pointwise Addition forms Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ and $\struct {H, +_H}$ be abelian groups. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ and $\struct {H, +_H, \circ}_R$ be $R$-modules. Let $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$ be the set of all linear transformations from $G$ to $H$. Let $\oplus_H$ be defined as pointwise addition on $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$: $\forall u, v \in \map {\LL_R} {G, H}: \forall x \in G: \map {\paren {u \oplus_H v} } x := \map u x +_H \map v x$ Then $\struct {\map {\LL_R} {G, H}, \oplus_H}$ is an abelian group.

label: Set of Liouville Numbers is Uncountable
snippet: The set of Liouville numbers is uncountable.

label: Set of Literals Satisfiable iff No Complementary Pairs
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of literals. Then $S$ is satisfiable it contains no complementary pairs.

label: Set of Local Minimum is Countable
snippet: Let $X$ be a subset of $\R$. The set: $\leftset {x \in X: x}$ is local minimum in $\rightset X$ is countable.

label: Set of Mappings can be Ordered by Subset Relation
snippet: Let $S \times T$ be the product of two sets. Let $\FF$ be a set of mappings on $S \times T$. Then $\FF$ can be ordered by the subset relation.

label: Set of Mappings from Integers to Boolean Set is Uncountable
snippet: == Example of Use of Cantor's Diagonal Argument == Let $S$ be the Boolean set defined as: $S = \set {0, 1}$ Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all mappings from the integers $\Z$ to $S$: $\mathbb G = \set {f: \Z \to S}$ Then $\mathbb G$ is uncountably infinite.

label: Set of Mappings which map to Same Element induces Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $E$ be the set of all mappings from $X$ to $Y$. Let $b \in X$. Let $\RR \subseteq E \times E$ be the relation on $E$ defined as: $\RR := \set {\tuple {f, g} \in \RR: \map f b = \map g b}$ Then $\RR$ is an equivalence relation.

label: Set of Matrices under Entrywise Addition forms Vector Space
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$ be (strictly) positive integers. Let $\map {\MM_\GF} {m, n}$ be the $m \times n$ matrix space over a field $\GF$. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_\GF} {m, n}, +}$ denote the abelian group formed from $\map {\MM_\GF} {m, n}$ under matrix entrywise addition. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_\GF} {m, n}, +, \times}_\GF$ denote the unitary module over $\GF$ where $\times$ denotes the matrix scalar product. Then $\struct {\map {\MM_\GF} {m, n}, +, \times}_\GF$ forms a vector space.

label: Set of Meet Irreducible Elements Excluded Top is Order Generating
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a continuous complete lattice. Let $X = \map {\mathit {IRR} } L \setminus \set \top$ where: $\map {\mathit {IRR} } L$ denotes the set of all meet irreducible element of $S$ $\top$ denotes the top of $L$. Then $X$ is order generating.

label: Set of Monomials is Closed Under Multiplication
snippet: Let $M$ be the set of all monomials on the set $\set {X_j: j \in J}$, with multiplication $\circ$ defined by: $\ds \paren {\prod_{j \mathop \in J} X_j^{k_j} } \circ \paren {\prod_{j \mathop \in J} X_j^{k_j'} } = \paren {\prod_{j \mathop \in J} X_j^{k_j + k_j'} }$ Then $M$ is closed under $\circ$.

label: Set of Natural Numbers Equals its Union
snippet: Let $\omega$ denote the set of natural numbers as defined by the von Neumann construction on a Zermelo universe $V$. Then: $\bigcup \omega = \omega$

label: Set of Natural Numbers can be Derived using Axiom of Abstraction
snippet: Let $\N$ denote the set of natural numbers. By application of the , $\N$ can be derived as a valid object in Frege set theory.

label: Set of Natural Numbers is Limit Ordinal
snippet: The set of natural numbers $\N$ is a limit ordinal.

label: Set of Natural Numbers is Ordinal
snippet: The set of natural numbers $\N$ is an ordinal.

label: Set of Natural Numbers is Smallest Ordinal Greater than All Natural Numbers
snippet: The set of natural numbers $\N$ is the smallest ordinal which is greater than all natural numbers.

label: Set of Non-Negative Real Numbers is not Well-Ordered by Usual Ordering
snippet: The set of non-negative real numbers $\R_{\ge 0}$ is not well-ordered under the usual ordering $\le$.

label: Set of Non-Zero Natural Numbers is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $\N^*$ be defined as $\N^* = \N \setminus \set 0$. The subset $\N^* \subset \N$ is primitive recursive.

label: Set of Normal Subgroups of Group is Subsemigroup of Power Set Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\circ_\PP$ be the operation induced by $\circ$ on $\powerset G$, the power set of $G$. Let $\HH$ be the set of all normal subgroups of $\struct {G, \circ}$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\HH, \circ_\PP}$ is a subsemigroup of the algebraic structure $\struct {\powerset G, \circ_\PP}$.

label: Set of Normal Subgroups of Group is Subsemigroup of Power Set under Intersection
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\HH$ be the set of all normal subgroups of $\struct {G, \circ}$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\HH, \cap}$ is a subsemigroup of the algebraic structure $\struct {\powerset G, \cap}$.

label: Set of Null Strings forms Formal Language
snippet: == Example of Formal Language == The set consisting of the null string $\epsilon$ forms a formal language.

label: Set of Numbers of form n - 1 over n is Bounded Above
snippet: Let $S$ be the subset of the set of real numbers $\R$ defined as: $S = \set {\dfrac {n - 1} n: n \in \Z_{>0} }$ $S$ is bounded above with supremum $1$. $S$ has no greatest element.

label: Set of Odd Integers is Countably Infinite
snippet: Let $\Bbb O$ be the set of odd integers. Then $\Bbb O$ is countably infinite.

label: Set of Orbits forms Partition
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $X$ be a set. Let $G$ act on $X$. Then the set of orbits of the group action forms a partition of $X$.

label: Set of Order 3 Vectors under Cross Product does not form Ring
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of all vectors in a vector space of dimension $3$. Let $\times$ denote the cross product operation. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {S, +, \times}$ is not a ring.

label: Set of Order m times n Matrices does not form Ring
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers such that $m > n$. Let $S$ be the set of all matrices of order $m \times n$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {S, +, \times}$ is not a ring. Note that $\times$ denotes conventional matrix multiplication.

label: Set of Ordered Pairs of Integers is Countable Infinite
snippet: The set of all ordered pairs of integers $\Z$ is countably infinite.

label: Set of Pairwise Disjoint Intervals is Countable
snippet: Let $X$ be a subset of $\powerset \R$ such that: $(1): \quad X$ is pairwise disjoint: $\forall A, B \in X: A \ne B \implies A \cap B = \O$. $(2): \quad$ every element of $X$ contains an open interval: $\forall A \in X: \exists x, y \in \R: x < y \land \openint x y \subseteq A$. Then $X$ is countable.

label: Set of Palindromes over 0, 1 forms Formal Language
snippet: == Example of Formal Language == The set of palindromes over $\set {0, 1}$ forms a formal language.

label: Set of Palindromes over Infinite Set does not form Formal Language
snippet: == Example of Formal Language == The set of palindromes over an infinite set of symbols does not form a formal language.

label: Set of Permutations is Largest Effective Transformation Group
snippet: The set of permutations of a set $X$ forms the largest effective transformation group of $X$.

label: Set of Points Equidistant from Line Segment
snippet: Let $AB$ be a line segment. The locus of points equidistant from $AB$ consists of: a pair of line segments parallel to $AB$ $2$ semicircles: 400px

label: Set of Points at which Sequence of Measurable Functions does not Converge to Given Measurable Function is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. For each $n \in \N$, let $f_n : X \to \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. Then: $\ds \set {x \in X : \sequence {\map {f_n} x}_{n \in \N} \text { does not converge to } \map f x}$ is $\Sigma$-measurable.

label: Set of Points for which Measurable Function is Real-Valued is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable. Then: $\set {x \in X : \map f x \in \R}$ is $\Sigma$-measurable.

label: Set of Points for which Seminorm is Zero is Vector Subspace
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $p$ be a seminorm on $X$. Let: $U = \set {x \in X : \map p x = 0}$ Then $U$ is a vector subspace of $X$.

label: Set of Points in Metric Space for which Pointwise Equicontinuous Sequence of Continuous Functions Converges to Continuous Function is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d_X}$ and $\struct {Y, d_Y}$ be metric spaces. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous function. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a pointwise equicontinuous sequence of continuous functions $X \to Y$. Let: $C = \set {x \in X : \map {f_n} x \to \map f x \text { as } n \to \infty}$ Then $C$ is closed in $X$.

label: Set of Points on Line Segment is Infinite
snippet: The set of points on a line segment is infinite.

label: Set of Polynomials over Infinite Set has Same Cardinality
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of infinite cardinality $\kappa$. Let $S \sqbrk x$ be the set of polynomial forms over $S$ in the indeterminate $x$. Then $S \sqbrk x$ has cardinality $\kappa$.

label: Set of Polynomials over Integral Domain is Subring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral subdomain of $R$. Then $\forall x \in R$, the set $D \sqbrk x$ of polynomials in $x$ over $D$ is a subring of $R$.

label: Set of Positive Elements of C*-Algebra is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $A^+$ be the set of positive elements of $A$. Then $A^+$ is closed.

label: Set of Positive Elements of C*-Algebra is Convex Cone
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $A^+$ be the set of positive elements of $A$. Then $A^+$ is a convex cone.

label: Set of Positive Elements of C*-Algebra is Set of Products of Element with its Star
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $a \in A$. Let $A^+$ be the set of positive elements of $A$. We have: $A^+ = \set {a^\ast a : a \in A}$

label: Set of Positive Elements of Everywhere Dense Ideal is Dense in Set of Positive Elements of C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $I$ be an everywhere dense ideal of $A$. Let $A^+$ be the set of positive elements of $A$. Let $I^+ = I \cap A^+$. Then $I^+$ is everywhere dense in $A^+$.

label: Set of Positive Integers does not form Ring
snippet: Let $\Z_{\ge 0}$ denote the set of positive integers. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\Z_{\ge 0}, +, \times}$ does not form a ring.

label: Set of Prime Numbers is Infinite
snippet: The number of primes is infinite.

label: Set of Prime Numbers is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The set $\Bbb P$ of prime numbers is primitive recursive.

label: Set of Rational Cuts forms Ordered Field
snippet: Let $\RR$ denote the set of rational cuts. Let $\struct {\RR, +, \times, \le}$ denote the ordered structure formed from $\RR$ and: the operation $+$ of addition of cuts the operation $\times$ of multiplication of cuts the ordering $\le$ of cuts. Then $\struct {\RR, + \times, \le}$ is an ordered field.

label: Set of Rational Numbers Strictly between Zero and One has no Greatest or Least Element
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \Q$ be the subset of the set of rational numbers defined as: $S = \set {r \in \Q: 0 < r < 1}$ Then $S$ has no greatest or smallest element. However, $S$ has a supremum $1$ and an infimum $0$.

label: Set of Rational Numbers is not Closed in Reals
snippet: Let $\Q$ be the set of rational numbers. Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $\Q$ is not closed in $\R$.

label: Set of Rational Numbers is not G-Delta Set in Reals
snippet: Let $\Q$ be the set of rational numbers. Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $\Q$ is not a $G_\delta$ set in $\R$.

label: Set of Rational Numbers whose Numerator Divisible by p is Closed under Addition
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $A_p$ be the set of all rational numbers which, when expressed in canonical form has a numerator which is divisible by $p$. Then $A_p$ is closed under rational addition.

label: Set of Rational Numbers whose Numerator Divisible by p is Closed under Multiplication
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $A_p$ be the set of all rational numbers which, when expressed in canonical form has a numerator which is divisible by $p$. Then $A_p$ is closed under rational multiplication.

label: Set of Rationals Greater than Root 2 has no Smallest Element
snippet: Let $B$ be the set of all positive rational numbers $p$ such that $p^2 > 2$. Then $B$ has no smallest element.

label: Set of Rationals Less than Root 2 has no Greatest Element
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all positive rational numbers $p$ such that $p^2 < 2$. Then $A$ has no greatest element.

label: Set of Real Numbers is Bounded Below iff Set of Negatives is Bounded Above
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of the real numbers $\R$. Let $T = \set {x \in \R: -x \in S}$ be the set of negatives of the elements of $S$. Then: $S$ is bounded below $T$ is bounded above.

label: Set of Real Vector Spaces is Category
snippet: The set of real vector spaces is a category such that: the vector spaces are its objects the linear transformations are its morphisms.

label: Set of Reciprocals of Positive Integers is Nowhere Dense in Reals
snippet: Let $N$ be the set defined as: $N := \set {\dfrac 1 n: n \in \Z_{>0} }$ where $\Z_{>0}$ is the set of (strictly) positive integers. Let $\R$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Then $N$ is nowhere dense in $\R$.

label: Set of Relations can be Ordered by Subset Relation
snippet: Let $S \times T$ be the product of two sets. Let $\RR$ be a set of relations on $S \times T$. Then $\RR$ can be ordered by the subset relation.

label: Set of Ring Elements forming Zero Product with given Element is Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring whose zero is $0_R$. Let $a \in R$ be an arbitrary element of $R$. Let $A$ be the subset of $R$ defined as: $A = \set {x \in R: x \circ a = 0_R}$ Then $A$ is an ideal of $A$.

label: Set of Rotations in Space about Fixed Point forms Infinite Group
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a rigid body in space. Let $O$ be a fixed point in space. The set of all rotations of $\SS$ through some straight line through $O$ forms an infinite group.

label: Set of Rotations is Subgroup of Symmetry Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a symmetry group. Let $H$ be the subset of $G$ consisting of the rotations in $G$ about a given axis. Then $H$ is a subgroup of $G$.

label: Set of Row Matrices under Entrywise Addition forms Vector Space
snippet: == Corollary to Set of Matrices under Entrywise Addition forms Vector Space == Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\map {\MM_\GF} {1, n}$ be set of all row matrices over a field $\GF$. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_\GF} {1, n}, +}$ denote the abelian group formed from $\map {\MM_\GF} {1, n}$ under matrix entrywise addition. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_\GF} {1, n}, +, \times}_\GF$ denote the unitary module over $\GF$ where $\times$ denotes the matrix scalar product. Then $\struct {\map {\MM_\GF} {1, n}, +, \times}_\GF$ forms a vector space.

label: Set of Sequence Codes is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $\operatorname{Seq}$ be the set of all code numbers of finite sequences in $\N$. Then $\operatorname{Seq}$ is primitive recursive.

label: Set of Sets/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Sets of Sets ==

label: Set of Sets can be Defined as Family
snippet: Let $\Bbb S$ be a set of sets. Then $\Bbb S$ can be defined as an indexed family of sets.

label: Set of Singletons is Smallest Basis of Discrete Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a discrete topological space. Let $\BB = \set {\set x : x \in S}$. Then $\BB$ is the smallest basis of $T$. That is: $\BB$ is a basis of $T$ and: for every basis $\CC$ of $T$, $\BB \subseteq \CC$.

label: Set of Strictly Negative Integers is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $N \subseteq \N$ be the set of all $n \in \N$ such that: $n$ codes an integer $k$ such that $k < 0$. Then $N$ is a primitive recursive set.

label: Set of Strictly Positive Integers is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $P \subseteq \N$ be the set of all $n \in \N$ such that: $n$ codes an integer $k$ such that $k > 0$. Then $P$ is a primitive recursive set.

label: Set of Subfields forms Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \circ}$ be a field. Let $\mathbb F$ be the set of all subfields of $F$. Then $\struct {\mathbb F, \subseteq}$ is a complete lattice.

label: Set of Subgroups forms Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all subgroups of $G$. Then: $\struct {\mathbb G, \subseteq}$ is a complete lattice. where for every set $\mathbb H$ of subgroups of $G$: the infimum of $\mathbb H$ necessarily admitted by $\mathbb H$ is $\ds \bigcap \mathbb H$.

label: Set of Subgroups of Abelian Group form Subsemigroup of Power Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an abelian group. Let $\struct {\powerset G, \circ_\PP}$ denote the power structure of $\struct {G, \circ}$. Let $\SS$ be the set of all subgroups of $G$. Then $\struct {\SS, \circ_\PP}$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {\powerset G, \circ_\PP}$.

label: Set of Submagmas of Magma under Subset Relation forms Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \odot}$ be a magma. Let $\SS$ be the set of submagmas of $A$. Then: the ordered set $\struct {\SS, \subseteq}$ is a complete lattice where for every subset $\TT$ of $\SS$: the infimum of $\TT$ necessarily admitted by $\TT$ is $\bigcap \TT$.

label: Set of Submodules of Module is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group. Let $M = \struct {G, +, \circ}_R$ be an $R$-module. Ordered by $\subseteq$, the set of all submodules of $M$ is a complete lattice.

label: Set of Subrings forms Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\mathbb K$ be the set of all subrings of $K$. Then $\struct {\mathbb K, \subseteq}$ is a complete lattice.

label: Set of Subsemigroups forms Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $\mathbb S$ be the set of all subsemigroups of $S$. Then: $\struct {\mathbb S, \subseteq}$ is a complete lattice. where for every set $\mathbb H$ of subsemigroups of $S$: the infimum of $\mathbb H$ necessarily admitted by $\mathbb H$ is $\ds \bigcap \mathbb H$.

label: Set of Subsemigroups of Commutative Semigroup form Subsemigroup of Power Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a commutative semigroup. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ denote the power structure of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Let $\TT$ be the set of all subsemigroups of $S$. Then $\struct {\TT, \circ_\PP}$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$.

label: Set of Subset of Reals with Cardinality less than Continuum has not Interval in Union Closure
snippet: Let $\BB$ be a set of subsets of $\R$, the set of all real numbers. Let: $\card \BB < \mathfrak c$ where $\card \BB$ denotes the cardinality of $\BB$ $\mathfrak c = \card \R$ denotes continuum. Let $\FF = \set {\bigcup \GG: \GG \subseteq \BB}$. Then: $\exists x, y \in \R: x < y \land \hointr x y \notin \FF$

label: Set of Subsets is Cover iff Set of Complements is Free
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a set of sets. Then $\CC$ is a cover for $S$ $\set {\relcomp S X: X \in \CC}$ is free.

label: Set of Subsets of Element of Minimally Inductive Class under Progressing Mapping is Finite
snippet: Let $M$ be a class which is minimally inductive under a progressing mapping $g$. Let $x \in M$. Let $S$ be the set of all $y \in M$ such that $y \subseteq x$. Then $S$ is finite.

label: Set of Subsets of Finite Character of Countable Set is of Type M
snippet: Let $D$ be a countable set. Let $S$ be a set of subsets of $D$ such that $S$ is of finite character. Then $S$ is of type $M$, that is: every element of $S$ is a subset of a maximal element of $S$ under the subset relation.

label: Set of Subsets of Reals with Cardinality less than Continuum Cardinality of Local Minimums of Union Closure less than Continuum
snippet: Let $\BB$ be a set of subsets of $\R$. Let: $\size \BB < \mathfrak c$ where $\size \BB$ denotes the cardinality of $\BB$ $\mathfrak c = \size \R$ denotes the cardinality of the continuum. Let $X = \leftset {x \in \R: \exists U \in \set {\bigcup \GG: \GG \subseteq \BB}: x}$ is a local minimum in $\rightset U$ Then: $\size X < \mathfrak c$

label: Set of Subsets which contains Set and Intersection of Subsets is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\SS$ be a set of subsets of $A$ such that: $A \in \SS$ for every non-empty subset $\TT$ of $\SS$, $\ds \bigcap \TT \in \SS$, where $\ds \bigcap \TT$ denotes the intersection of $\TT$. Then: the ordered set $\struct {\SS, \subseteq}$ is a complete lattice where: $\ds \bigcap \TT$ is the infimum necessarily admitted by $\TT$.

label: Set of Successive Numbers contains Unique Multiple
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{\ge 1}$. Then $\set {m, m + 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ contains a unique integer that is a multiple of $n$. That is, in any set containing $n$ successive integers, $n$ divides exactly one of those integers.

label: Set of Transpositions is not Subgroup of Symmetric Group
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set with $n$ elements such that $n > 2$. Let $G = \struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$ denote the symmetric group on $S$. Let $H \subseteq G$ denote the set of all transpositions of $S$ along with the identity mapping which moves no elements of $S$. Then $H$ does not form a subgroup of $G$.

label: Set of Upper Closures of Compact Elements is Basis implies Complete Scott Topological Lattice is Algebraic
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a complete Scott Definition:Topological Lattice. Let $\BB = \set {x^\succeq: x \in \map K L}$ be a basis of $L$, where: $x^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $x$, $\map K L$ denotes the compact subset of $L$. Then $L$ is algebraic.

label: Set of Vectors defined by Directed Line Segments in Space forms Vector Space
snippet: Let $\R^3$ be a real cartesian space of $3$ dimensions. Consider the set $S$ of directed line segments in $\R^3$. Let the equivalence relation $\sim$ be applied to $\R^3$ such that: $\forall L_1, L_2 \in \R^3: L_1 \sim L_2$ there exists a translation $T$ such that $\map T {L_1} = L_2$ Let $\mathbb V$ denote the set of equivalence classes of $\sim$ on $S$.

label: Set of all Self-Maps under Composition forms Monoid
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $S^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to itself. Let the operation $\circ$ represent composition of mappings. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {S^S, \circ}$ is a monoid whose identity element is the identity mapping on $S$.

label: Set of all Self-Maps under Composition forms Semigroup
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $S^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to itself. Let the operation $\circ$ represent composition of mappings. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {S^S, \circ}$ is a semigroup.

label: Set together with Condensation Points is not necessarily Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Let $\CC$ denote the set of condensation points of $H$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $H \cup \CC$ is a closed set of $T$.

label: Set together with Omega-Accumulation Points is not necessarily Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Let $\Omega$ denote the set of $\omega$-accumulation points of $H$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $H \cup \Omega$ is a closed set of $T$.

label: Set which is Equivalent to Countable Set is Countable
snippet: == Lemma == Let $S$ be countable set. Let $T$ be a set. Let $T$ be equivalent to $S$. Then $T$ is countable.

label: Set which is Superinductive under Progressing Mapping has Fixed Point
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $g: S \to S$ be a progressing mapping on $S$. Let $S$ be superinductive under $g$. Then there exists $x \in S$ such that $x$ is a fixed point of $g$.

label: Set with Choice Function is Well-Orderable
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let there exist a choice function for $S$. Then $S$ is well-orderable.

label: Set with Complement forms Partition
snippet: Let $\O \subset S \subset \mathbb U$. Then $S$ and its complement $\map \complement S$ form a partition of the universal set $\mathbb U$.

label: Set with Dispersion Point is Biconnected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a connected set in $T$. Let $p \in H$ be a dispersion point of $H$. Then $H$ is biconnected.

label: Set with Slowly Progressing Mapping on Power Set with Self as Fixed Point is Well-Orderable
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of sets. Let there exist a slowly progressing mapping $g: \powerset S \to \powerset S$, where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$. Let $g$ have exactly one fixed point $S$. Then $S$ is well-orderable.

label: Set with no Limit Point is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be such that $H$ has no limit point. Then $H$ is a closed set of $T$.

label: Sets in Modified Fort Space are Disconnected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{a, b}}$ be a modified Fort space. Let $H$ be a subset of $S$ with more than one point. Then $H$ is disconnected.

label: Sets of Permutations of Equivalent Sets are Equivalent
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets such that: $A \sim B$ where $\sim$ denotes set equivalence. Let $\map \Gamma A$ denote the set of permutations on $A$. Then: $\map \Gamma A \sim \map \Gamma B$

label: Sexagesimal System/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Numbers represented in the Sexagesimal System ==

label: Shape of Cosecant Function
snippet: The nature of the cosecant function on the set of real numbers $\R$ is as follows: $(1): \quad$ strictly decreasing on the intervals $\hointr {-\dfrac \pi 2} 0$ and $\hointl 0 {\dfrac \pi 2}$ $(2): \quad$ strictly increasing on the intervals $\hointr {\dfrac \pi 2} \pi$ and $\hointl \pi {\dfrac {3 \pi} 2}$ $(3): \quad$ $\csc x \to +\infty$ as $x \to 0^+$ $(4): \quad$ $\csc x \to +\infty$ as $x \to \pi^-$ $(5): \quad$ $\csc x \to -\infty$ as $x \to \pi^+$ $(6): \quad$ $\csc x \to -\infty$ as $x \to 2 \pi^-$

label: Shape of Cosine Function
snippet: The cosine function is: $(1): \quad$ strictly decreasing on the interval $\closedint 0 \pi$ $(2): \quad$ strictly increasing on the interval $\closedint \pi {2 \pi}$ $(3): \quad$ concave on the interval $\closedint {-\dfrac \pi 2} {\dfrac \pi 2}$ $(4): \quad$ convex on the interval $\closedint {\dfrac \pi 2} {\dfrac {3 \pi} 2}$

label: Shape of Cotangent Function
snippet: The nature of the cotangent function on the set of real numbers $\R$ is as follows: $\cot x$ is continuous and strictly decreasing on the interval $\openint 0 \pi$ $\cot x \to +\infty$ as $x \to 0^+$ $\cot x \to -\infty$ as $x \to \pi^-$ $\cot x$ is not defined on $\forall n \in \Z: x = n \pi$, at which points it is discontinuous $\forall n \in \Z: \map \cot {n + \dfrac 1 2} \pi = 0$

label: Shape of Secant Function
snippet: The nature of the secant function on the set of real numbers $\R$ is as follows: $(1): \quad \sec x$ is continuous and strictly increasing on the intervals $\hointr 0 {\dfrac \pi 2}$ and $\hointl {\dfrac \pi 2} \pi$ $(2): \quad \sec x$ is continuous and strictly decreasing on the intervals $\hointr {-\pi} {-\dfrac \pi 2}$ and $\hointl {-\dfrac \pi 2} 0$ $(3): \quad \sec x \to + \infty$ as $x \to -\dfrac \pi 2^+$ $(4): \quad \sec x \to + \infty$ as $x \to \dfrac \pi 2^-$ $(5): \quad \sec x \to - \infty$ as $x \to \dfrac \pi 2^+$ $(6): \quad \sec x \to - \infty$ as $x \to \dfrac {3 \pi} 2^-$

label: Shape of Sine Function
snippet: The sine function is: $(1): \quad$ strictly increasing on the interval $\closedint {-\dfrac \pi 2} {\dfrac \pi 2}$ $(2): \quad$ strictly decreasing on the interval $\closedint {\dfrac \pi 2} {\dfrac {3 \pi} 2}$ $(3): \quad$ concave on the interval $\closedint 0 \pi$ $(4): \quad$ convex on the interval $\closedint \pi {2 \pi}$

label: Shape of Tangent Function
snippet: The nature of the tangent function on the set of real numbers $\R$ is as follows: $\tan x$ is continuous and strictly increasing on the interval $\openint {-\dfrac \pi 2} {\dfrac \pi 2}$ $\tan x \to +\infty$ as $x \to \dfrac \pi 2 ^-$ $\tan x \to -\infty$ as $x \to -\dfrac \pi 2 ^+$ $\tan x$ is not defined on $\forall n \in \Z: x = \paren {n + \dfrac 1 2} \pi$, at which points it is discontinuous $\forall n \in \Z: \map \tan {n \pi} = 0$.

label: Sheaf Associated to Injective Module over Noetherian Ring is Flasque
snippet: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring. Let $I$ be an injective $A$-module. Then the sheaf $\tilde I$ associated to $I$ on $\Spec A$ is flasque.

label: Sheldon Conjecture
snippet: There is only $1$ Sheldon prime, and that is $73$.

label: Shell Theorem
snippet: Let $P$ be a charged particle in space. Let $P$ generate a field whose vector quantity $\mathbf F$ at a position $\mathbf r$ $P$ is given by the inverse square law: $\mathbf F = \dfrac {k Q} {r^2} \hat {\mathbf r}$ where: $\mathbf F$ is the vector field quantity $r := \size {\mathbf r}$ denotes the magnitude of $\mathbf r$, that is, the distance from $P$ $k$ is a constant $Q$ is the charge that generates the field, for example: mass for gravity electric charge for electrostatic fields and so on.

label: Shift Mapping is Lower Adjoint iff Meet is Distributive with Supremum
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Then: $\forall x \in S, f: S \to S: \paren {\forall y \in S: \map f y = x \wedge y} \implies f$ is lower adjoint of a Galois connection $\forall x \in S, X \subseteq S: x \wedge \sup X = \sup \set {x \wedge y: y \in X}$

snippet: The shortest distance between $2$ points is a straight line.

label: Side of Spherical Triangle is Supplement of Angle of Polar Triangle
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Let $\triangle A'B'C'$ be the polar triangle of $\triangle ABC$. Then $A'$ is the supplement of $a$. That is: $A' = \pi - a$ and it follows by symmetry that: $B' = \pi - b$ $C' = \pi - c$
