label: Spectrum of Compact Linear Operator on Infinite-Dimensional Banach Space contains Zero
snippet: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space over $\C$. Let $T : X \to X$ be a compact linear operator. Let $\map \sigma T$ be the spectrum of $T$. Then $0 \in \map \sigma T$. That is, $T$ is not invertible as a bounded linear operator.

label: Spectrum of Element in Maximal Commutative Subalgebra of Unital Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital Banach algebra. Let $C$ be a commutative subalgebra of $A$ that is maximal with respect to set inclusion. Let $x \in C$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ and $\map {\sigma_C} x$ be the spectra of $x$ in $A$ and $C$ respectively. Then: $\map {\sigma_C} x = \map {\sigma_A} x$

label: Spectrum of Element of Banach Algebra is Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x$ is bounded, and in particular: $\cmod \lambda \le \norm x$ for all $\lambda \in \map {\sigma_A} x$

label: Spectrum of Element of Banach Algebra is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x$ is closed.

label: Spectrum of Element of Banach Algebra is Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x$ is compact.

label: Spectrum of Element of Banach Algebra is Non-Empty
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x \ne \O$.

label: Spectrum of Element of Space of Continuous Functions Vanishing at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $A = \map {\CC_0} X$ be the Banach algebra of continuous complex-valued functions vanishing at infinity. Let $f \in \map {\CC_0} X$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} f = f \sqbrk X \cup \set 0$ where $\sigma_A$ denotes the spectrum in $A$.

label: Spectrum of Element of Space of Continuous Functions on Compact Hausdorff Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $A = \map \CC K$ be the space of continuous functions on $K$ considered as a Banach algebra. Let $f \in \map \CC K$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} f = f \sqbrk K$ where $\sigma_A$ denotes spectrum in $A$.

label: Spectrum of Element of Unital C*-Subalgebra of Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra with identity element ${\mathbf 1}_A$. Let $B \subseteq A$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-subalgebra of $A$. Let $\sigma_A$ and $\sigma_B$ be the spectrum in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Let $x \in B$. Then we have: $\map {\sigma_A} x = \map {\sigma_B} x$

label: Spectrum of Element of Unital Commutative Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a commutative unital Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $\Phi_A$ be the spectrum of $A$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} x = \set {\map \phi x : \phi \in \Phi_A}$

label: Spectrum of Hermitian Element in Unital C*-Algebra is Real
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $x \in A$ be Hermitian. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ denote the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x \subseteq \R$.

label: Spectrum of Locale as Completely Prime Filters is Sober Space
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \preceq}$ be a locale. Let $\map {\operatorname{Sp}} L$ denote the spectrum as completely prime filters of $L$. Then: $\map {\operatorname{Sp}} L$ is a sober space.

label: Spectrum of Locale is Sober Space
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \preceq}$ be a locale. Let $\map {\operatorname{Sp}} L$ denote the spectrum of $L$. Then: $\map {\operatorname{Sp}} L$ is a sober space.

label: Spectrum of Product of Elements of Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $\sigma_A$ denote spectrum in $A$. Let $x, y \in A$. Then we have: $\map {\sigma_A} {x y} \setminus \set 0 = \map {\sigma_A} {y x} \setminus \set 0$

label: Spectrum of Projection in *-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $p$ be a projection on $A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} p$ be the spectrum of $p$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} p \subseteq \set {0, 1}$.

label: Spectrum of Self-Adjoint Bounded Linear Operator is Real
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $T : \HH \to \HH$ be a bounded self-adjoint operator. Let $\map \sigma T$ be the spectrum of $T$. Then: $\map \sigma T \subseteq \R$

label: Spectrum of Self-Adjoint Densely-Defined Linear Operator is Real and Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a self-adjoint densely-defined linear operator. Let $\map \sigma T$ be the spectrum of $\struct {\map D T, T}$. Then $\map \sigma T$ is a closed subset of $\C$ and: $\map \sigma T \subseteq \R$

label: Spectrum of Unitary Element in Unital C*-Algebra is Subset of Unit Circle
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $x \in A$ be unitary. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ denote the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x \subseteq \set {z \in \C : \cmod z = 1}$.

label: Speed of Body under Free Fall from Height
snippet: Let an object $B$ be released above ground from a point near the Earth's surface and allowed to fall freely. Let $B$ fall a distance $s$. Then: $v = \sqrt {2 g s}$ where: $v$ is the speed of $B$ after having fallen a distance $s$ $g$ is the Acceleration Due to Gravity at the height through which $B$ falls. It is supposed that the distance $s$ is small enough that $g$ can be considered constant throughout.

label: Sphere in Normed Division Ring is Sphere in Induced Metric
Sphere is Disjoint Union of Open Balls in P-adic Numbers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. For all $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$: let $\map {S_\epsilon} a$ denote the sphere of $a$ of radius $\epsilon$. let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ denote the open ball of $a$ of radius $\epsilon$. Then: $\ds \forall n \in Z: \map {S_{p^{-n} } } a = \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^{p - 1} \map {B_{p^{-n} } } {a + i p^n}$

label: Sphere is Locus of Equidistant Points from Point in Space
snippet: Let $P$ be a point in space. The locus of points which are equidistant from $P$ is the sphere whose center is $P$.

label: Sphere is Set Difference of Closed Ball with Open Ball
snippet: Let $M = \struct{A, d}$ be a metric space or pseudometric space. Let $a \in A$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $\map {{B_\epsilon}^-} {a; d}$ denote the closed $\epsilon$-ball of $a$ in $M$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} {a; d}$ denote the open $\epsilon$-ball of $a$ in $M$. Let $\map {S_\epsilon} {a; d}$ denote the $\epsilon$-sphere of $a$ in $M$. Then: $\map {S_\epsilon} {a; d} = \map { {B_\epsilon}^-} {a; d} \setminus \map {B_\epsilon} {a; d}$

label: Spheres in 24 Dimensions in Leech Lattice
snippet: Let a set of identical spheres in a $24$-dimensional space be arranged in a Leech lattice. Then each sphere will touch $196 \, 560$ other spheres. This is believed to be the densest possible sphere packing in $24$ dimensions.

label: Spherical Coordinate Form of Laplace's Equation
snippet: Laplace's equation can be expressed in spherical coordinates as: $\dfrac 1 {r^2} \map {\dfrac \partial {\partial r} } {r^2 \dfrac {\partial V} {\partial r} } + \dfrac 1 {r^2 \sin^2 \theta} \dfrac {\partial^2 V} {\partial \phi^2} + \dfrac 1 {r^2 \sin \theta} \map {\dfrac \partial {\partial \theta} } {\sin \theta \dfrac {\partial V} {\partial \theta} } = 0$

label: Spherical Law of Cosines
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\cos a = \cos b \cos c + \sin b \sin c \cos A$

label: Spherical Law of Sines
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\dfrac {\sin a} {\sin A} = \dfrac {\sin b} {\sin B} = \dfrac {\sin c} {\sin C}$

label: Spherical Triangle is Polar Triangle of its Polar Triangle
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Let $\triangle A'B'C'$ be the polar triangle of $\triangle ABC$. Then $\triangle ABC$ is the polar triangle of $\triangle A'B'C'$.

label: Split Epimorphism is Epic
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ and $D$ be objects of $\mathbf C$. Let $f: C \to D$ be a split epimorphism. Then $f: C \twoheadrightarrow D$ is epic.

label: Split Monomorphism is Monic
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ and $D$ be objects of $\mathbf C$. Let $f: C \to D$ be a split monomorphism. Then $f: C \rightarrowtail D$ is monic.

label: Sprague's Property of Root 2
snippet: Let $S = \sequence {s_n}$ be the sequence of fractions defined as follows: Let the numerator of $s_n$ be: $\floor {n \sqrt 2}$ where $\floor x$ denotes the floor of $x$. Let the denominators of the terms of $S$ be the (strictly) positive integers missing from the numerators of $S$: $S := \dfrac 1 3, \dfrac 2 6, \dfrac 4 {10}, \dfrac 5 {13}, \dfrac 7 {17}, \dfrac 8 {20}, \ldots$ Then the difference between the numerator and denominator of $s_n$ is equal to $2 n$.

label: Square-Bracing Problem

snippet: After $1$, there exists exactly one Fibonacci number which is also square: $F_{12} = 144 = 12^2$ which is also coincidentally the square of its index.

label: Square Inscribed in Circle is greater than Half Area of Circle
snippet: A square inscribed in a circle has an area greater than half that of the circle.

label: Square Matrices over Real Numbers under Multiplication form Monoid
snippet: Let $\map {\MM_\R} n$ be a $n \times n$ matrix space over the set of real numbers $\R$. Then the set of all $n \times n$ real matrices $\map {\MM_\R} n$ under matrix multiplication (conventional) forms a monoid.

label: Square Matrices with +1 or -1 Determinant under Multiplication forms Group

Let $\struct {S, \times}$ denote the algebraic structure formed by $S$ whose operation is (conventional) matrix multiplication. Then $\struct {S, \times}$ is a group.

snippet: If two rows of a square matrix over a commutative ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ are the same, then its determinant is zero.

snippet: Let $x$ be a real number such that $x^2 < 1$. Then: $x \in \openint {-1} 1$ where $\openint {-1} 1$ is the open interval $\left\{{x \in \R: -1 < x < 1}\right\}$.

snippet: == Binary Expansion == The binary expansion of the square root of $2$ starts: $\sqrt 2 \approx 1 \cdotp 01101 \, 01000 \, 00 \ldots$

snippet: The square root of $2$ is an algebraic number of degree $2$.

snippet: $\sqrt 2$ is irrational.

label: Square Root of Number Minus Square Root
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be (strictly) positive real numbers such that $a^2 - b > 0$. Then: $\ds \sqrt {a - \sqrt b} = \sqrt {\dfrac {a + \sqrt {a^2 - b} } 2} - \sqrt {\dfrac {a - \sqrt {a^2 - b} } 2}$

label: Square Root of Number Plus Square Root
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be (strictly) positive real numbers such that $a^2 - b > 0$. Then: $\ds \sqrt {a + \sqrt b} = \sqrt {\dfrac {a + \sqrt {a^2 - b} } 2} + \sqrt {\dfrac {a - \sqrt {a^2 - b} } 2}$

label: Square Root of Prime is Irrational
snippet: The square root of a prime number is irrational.

label: Square and Tetrahedral Numbers
snippet: The only positive integers which are simultaneously tetrahedral and square are: $1, 4, 19 \, 600$

label: Square equals Sum of Squares implies Right Triangle
Square of 1 Less than Number Base
snippet: Let $b \in \Z$ be an integer such that $b > 2$. Let $n = b - 1$. The square of $n$ is expressed in base $b$ as: $n^2 = \left[{c1}\right]_b$ where $c = b - 2$.

label: Square of Complex Conjugate is Complex Conjugate of Square
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ denote the complex conjugate of $z$. Then: $\overline {z^2} = \left({\overline z}\right)^2$

label: Square of Complex Modulus equals Complex Modulus of Square
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\cmod z$ be the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod {z^2} = \cmod z^2$

label: Square of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z = a + i b$ be a complex number. Then its square is given by: $z^2 = a^2 - b^2 + i \paren {2 a b}$

label: Square of Covariance is Less Than or Equal to Product of Variances
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Let the variances of $X$ and $Y$ exist and be finite. Then: $\paren {\cov {X, Y} }^2 \le \var X \, \var Y$ where $\cov {X, Y}$ denotes the covariance of $X$ and $Y$.

label: Square of Difference
snippet: $\forall x, y \in \R: \paren {x - y}^2 = x^2 - 2 x y + y^2$

label: Square of Expectation of Product is Less Than or Equal to Product of Expectation of Squares
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Let the expectation of $X Y$, $\expect {X Y}$, exist and be finite. Then: $\paren {\expect {X Y} }^2 \le \expect {X^2} \expect {Y^2}$

label: Square of Golden Mean equals One plus Golden Mean
snippet: $\phi^2 = \phi + 1$ where $\phi$ denotes the golden mean.

label: Square of Metric does not necessarily form Metric
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $d_4: A^2 \to \R$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in A^2: \map {d_4} {x, y} = \paren {\map d {x, y} }^2$ Then $d_4$ may or may not be a metric for $A$.

label: Square of Modulo less One equals One
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $\Z_m$ be the set of integers modulo $m$: $\Z_m = \set {\eqclass 0 m, \eqclass 1 m, \ldots, \eqclass {m - 1} m}$ Then: $\eqclass {m - 1} m \times_m \eqclass {m - 1} m = \eqclass 1 m$ where $\times_m$ denotes multiplication modulo $m$.

label: Square of Number Always Exists
snippet: Let $x$ be a number. Then its square $x^2$ is guaranteed to exist.

label: Square of Pythagorean Prime is Hypotenuse of Pythagorean Triangle
snippet: Let $p$ be a Pythagorean prime. Then $p^2$ is the hypotenuse of a Pythagorean triangle.

label: Square of Quadratic Gauss Sum
snippet: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $a$ be an integer coprime to $p$. Let $\map g {a, p}$ denote the quadratic Gauss sum of $a$ and $p$. Then: $\map g {a, p}^2 = \paren {\dfrac {-1} p} \cdot p$

label: Square of Real Number is Non-Negative
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Then: $0 \le x^2$

label: Square of Reversal of Small-Digit Number
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer whose decimal representation consists of sufficiently small digits. Then the reversal of the square of $n$ is the square of the reversal of $n$.

label: Square of Riemann Zeta Function
snippet: $\ds \map {\zeta^2} z = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\map {\sigma_0} k} {k^z}$ where: $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function $\sigma_0$ is the divisor count function.

label: Square of Sample Correlation Coefficient is no greater than 1
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of paired observations of a statistic from a population. The sample correlation coefficient $r$ of $S$ satisfies the inequality: $r^2 \le 1$

label: Square of Small-Digit Palindromic Number is Palindromic
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer such that the sum of the squares of the digits of $n$ in decimal representation is less than $10$. Let $n$ be palindromic. Then $n^2$ is also palindromic. The sequence of such numbers begins: $0, 1, 2, 3, 11, 22, 101, 111, 121, 202, 212, 1001, 1111, \dots$

label: Square of Standard Normal Random Variable has Chi-Squared Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \Gaussian 0 1$ where $\Gaussian 0 1$ is the standard normal distribution. Then $X^2 \sim \chi^2_1$ where $\chi^2_1$ is the chi-square distribution with $1$ degree of freedom.

label: Square of Sum
snippet: $\forall x, y \in \R: \paren {x + y}^2 = x^2 + 2 x y + y^2$

label: Square of Sum less Square
snippet: $\forall x, y \in \R: \paren {2x + y} y = \paren {x + y}^2 - x^2$

label: Square of Sum with Double
snippet: $\forall a, b \in \R: \paren {a + 2 b}^2 = a^2 + 4 a b + 4 b^2$

label: Square of V Operator on Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\struct {\HH \times \HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_{\HH \times \HH} }$ be the Hilbert space direct sum of $\HH$ with itself. Define $V : \HH \times \HH \to \HH \times \HH$ by: $\map V {x, y} = \tuple {-y, x}$ for each $\tuple {x, y} \in \HH \times \HH$. Then $V^2 = -I$.

label: Square of Vector Cross Product
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ be vectors in a vector space $\mathbf V$ of $3$ dimensions. Let $\mathbf a \times \mathbf b$ denote the vector cross product of $\mathbf a$ with $\mathbf b$. Then: $\paren {\mathbf a \times \mathbf b}^2 = \mathbf a^2 \mathbf b^2 - \paren {\mathbf a \cdot \mathbf b}^2$ where: $\paren {\mathbf a \times \mathbf b}^2$ denotes the square of $\mathbf a \times \mathbf b$ $\mathbf a \cdot \mathbf b$ denotes the dot product of $\mathbf a \times \mathbf b$.

label: Square of Vector Quantity in Coordinate Form
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a vector in a vector space $\mathbf V$ of $n$ dimensions: $\ds \mathbf a = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k \mathbf e_k$ where $\tuple {\mathbf e_1, \mathbf e_2, \ldots, \mathbf e_n}$ is the standard ordered basis of $\mathbf V$. Then: $\ds \mathbf a^2 = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k^2$ where $\mathbf a^2$ denotes the square of $\mathbf a$.

label: Square of n such that 2n-1 is Composite is not Sum of Square and Prime
snippet: Let $n^2$ be a square such that $2 n - 1$ is composite. Then $n^2$ cannot be expressed as the sum of a square and a prime.

snippet: The $4 \times 4$ square is the only square whose area in square units equals its perimeter in units. The area and perimeter of this square are $16$.

snippet: Let $n$ be a square number whose decimal representation ends in the pattern $\mathtt {xyxyxyxyxy}$. Then $\mathtt {xy}$ is one of: $21, 29, 61, 69, 84$ The smallest examples of such numbers are: {{eqn | l = 508 \, 853 \, 989^2 | r = \phantom {0 \,} 258 \, 932 \, 38 \mathbf {2 \, 121 \, 212 \, 121} }} {{eqn | l = 162 \, 459 \, 327^2 | r = \phantom {0 \, 0} 26 \, 393 \, 03 \mathbf {2 \, 929 \, 292 \, 929} }} {{eqn | l = 1 \, 318 \, 820 \, 881^2 | r = 1 \, 739 \, 288 \, 51 \mathbf {6 \, 161 \, 616 \, 161} }} {{eqn | l = 541 \, 713 \, 187^2 | r = \phantom {0 \,} 293 \, 453 \, 17 \mathbf {6 \, 969…

label: Squares Ending in Repeated Digits
snippet: A square number $n^2$ can end in a repeated digit either: $(1): \quad n^2$ is a multiple of $100$, in which case $n$ is a multiple of $10$ $(2): \quad n^2$ ends in $44$ and $n$ ends in $12, 38, 62$ or $88$.

label: Squares Ending in n Occurrences of m-Digit Pattern
snippet: Suppose there exists some integer $x$ such that $x^2$ ends in some $m$-digit pattern ending in an odd number not equal to $5$ and is preceded by another odd number, i.e.: $\exists x \in \Z: x^2 \equiv \sqbrk {1 a_1 a_2 \cdots a_m} \pmod {2 \times 10^m}$ where $a_m$ is odd, $a_m \ne 5$ and $m \ge 1$. Then for any $n \ge 1$, there exists some integer with not more than $m n$-digits such that its square ends in $n$ occurrences of the $m$-digit pattern.

label: Squares equal to Sum of 2 Cubes
snippet: == Sequence == The sequence of integers whose square can be expressed as the sum of $2$ coprime cubes begins: $3, 228, 671, 1261, 6371, 9765, 35 \, 113, 35 \, 928, 40 \, 380, 41 \, 643, 66 \, 599, \ldots$

label: Squares of Diagonals of Parallelogram
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram. 400px Then: $AC^2 + BD^2 = AB^2 + BC^2 + CD^2 + DA^2$

label: Squares which are 4 Less than Cubes
snippet: The only two square numbers which are $4$ less than a cube are: $2^2 + 4 = 2^3$ $11^2 + 4 = 5^3$

label: Squares whose Digits form Consecutive Decreasing Integers
snippet: The sequence of integers whose squares have a decimal representation consisting of the concatenation of $2$ consecutive decreasing integers begins: $91, 9079, 9901, 733 \, 674, 999 \, 001, 88 \, 225 \, 295, 99 \, 990 \, 001, \ldots$

label: Squares whose Digits form Consecutive Increasing Integers
snippet: The sequence of integers whose squares have a decimal representation consisting of the concatenation of $2$ consecutive increasing integers begins: $428, 573, 727, 846, 7810, 36 \, 365, 63 \, 636, 326 \, 734, \ldots$

label: Squares whose Digits form Consecutive Integers
snippet: The sequence of integers whose squares have a decimal representation consisting of the concatenation of $2$ consecutive integers, either increasing or decreasing begins: $91, 428, 573, 727, 846, 7810, 9079, 9901, 36 \, 365, 63 \, 636, 326 \, 734, 673 \, 267, 733 \, 674, \ldots$ This sequence can be divided into two subsequences: Those where the consecutive integers are increasing: $428, 573, 727, 846, 7810, 36 \, 365, 63 \, 636, 326 \, 734, 673 \, 267, \ldots$ Those where the consecutive integers are decreasing: $91, 9079, 9901, 733 \, 674, 999 \, 001, 88 \, 225 \, 295, \ldots$

label: Squares with All Odd Digits
snippet: The only squares whose digits (when written in base $10$ notation) are all odd are $1$ and $9$.

label: Squaring the Circle
snippet: == Classic Problem == Squaring the Circle is creating a square with the same area as that of a given circle.

label: Squaring the Circle by Archimedean Spiral
snippet: Let $C$ be a circle. It is possible to construct a square of the same area as $C$ using an Archimedean spiral.

label: Squaring the Circle by Compass and Straightedge Construction is Impossible
snippet: There is no compass and straightedge construction to allow a square to be constructed whose area is equal to that of a given circle.

label: Squeeze Theorem for Absolutely Convergent Series
snippet: Let $\ds \sum \size {a_n}$ be an absolutely convergent series in $\R$. Suppose that: $\ds -\sum \size {a_n} = \sum \size {a_n}$ Then $\ds \sum a_n$ equals the above two series.

label: Squeeze Theorem for Real Sequences/Corollary
snippet: == Corollary to Squeeze Theorem for Real Sequences == Let $\sequence {y_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$ which is null, that is: $y_n \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ Let: $\forall n \in \N: \size {x_n - l} \le y_n$ Then $x_n \to l$ as $n \to \infty$.

label: Stabilizer in Group of Transformations
snippet: Let $X$ be any set with $n$ elements (where $n \in \Z_{>0}$). Consider the symmetric group on $n$ letters $S_n$ as a group of transformations on $X$. Let $x \in X$. Then the stabilizer of $x$ is isomorphic to $S_{n - 1}$.

label: Stabilizer is Normal iff Stabilizer of Each Element of Orbit
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $S$ be a set. Let $*: G \times S \to S$ be a group action. Let $x \in S$. Let $\Stab x$ denote the stabilizer of $x$ under $*$. Let $\Orb x$ denote the orbit of $x$ under $*$. Then $\Stab x$ is normal in $G$ $\Stab x$ is also the stabilizer of every element in $\Orb x$.

label: Stabilizer is Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group which acts on a set $X$. Let $\Stab x$ be the stabilizer of $x$ by $G$. Then for each $x \in X$, $\Stab x$ is a subgroup of $G$.

label: Stabilizer of Cartesian Product of Group Actions
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $*_S: G \times S \to S$ and $*_T: G \times T \to T$ be group actions. Let the group action $*: G \times \paren {S \times T} \to S \times T$ be defined as: $\forall \tuple {g, \tuple {s, t} } \in G \times \paren {S \times T}: g * \tuple {s, t} = \tuple {g *_S s, g *_T t}$ Then the stabilizer of $\tuple {s, t} \in S \times T$ is given by: $\Stab {s, t} = \Stab s \cap \Stab t$ where $\Stab s$ and $\Stab t$ are the stabilizers of $s$ and $t$ under $*_S$ and $*_T$ respectively.

label: Stabilizer of Coset Action on Set of Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\powerset G$ denote the power set of $G$. Let $\HH \subseteq \powerset G$ denote the set of subgroups of $G$. Let $*$ be the subset product action on $\HH \subseteq \powerset G$ defined as: $\forall g \in G: \forall H \in \HH: g * H = g \circ H$ where $g \circ H$ is the (left) coset of $g$ by $H$. Then the stabilizer of $H$ in $\powerset G$ is $H$ itself: $\Stab H = H$

label: Stabilizer of Coset under Group Action on Coset Space
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $*: G \times G / H \to G / H$ be the action on the (left) coset space: $\forall g \in G, \forall g' H \in G / H: g * \paren {g' H} := \paren {g g'} H$ Then the stabilizer of $a H$ under $*$ is given by: $\Stab {a H} = a H a^{-1}$

label: Stabilizer of Element after Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $S$ be a set. Let $*_S: G \times S \to S$ be a group action. Let $x \in S, a \in G$. Then: $\Stab {a * x} = a^{-1} \circ \Stab x \circ a$

label: Stabilizer of Element of Group Acting on Itself is Trivial
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $*$ be the group action of $\struct {G, \circ}$ on itself by the rule: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = g \circ h$ Then the stabilizer of an element $x \in G$ is given by: $\Stab x = \set e$

label: Stabilizer of Polynomial
snippet: Let $n \in \Z: n > 0$. Let $\map f {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ be a polynomial in $n$ variables $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $\pi, \rho \in S_n$. Let the group action $\pi * f$ be defined as the permutation on the polynomial $f$ by $\pi$. Then the stabilizer of $f$ is the set of permutations on $n$ letters which fix $f$.

label: Stabilizer of Subgroup Action is Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\struct {H, \circ}$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $*: H \times G \to G$ be the subgroup action defined for all $h \in H, g \in G$ as: $\forall h \in H, g \in G: h * g := h \circ g$ The stabilizer of $x \in G$ is $\set e$: $\Stab x = \set e$

label: Stabilizer of Subgroup Action on Left Coset Space
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of $G$. Let $K$ act on the left coset space $G / H^l$ by: $\forall \tuple {k, g H} \in K \times G / H^l: k * \paren {g H} := \paren {k g} H$ The stabilizer of $g H$ is $K \cap H^g$, where $H^g$ denotes the $G$-conjugate of $H$ by $g$.

label: Stabilizer of Subset Product Action on Power Set
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\powerset G$ be the power set of $\struct {G, \circ}$. Let $*: G \times \powerset G \to \powerset G$ be the subset product action on $\powerset G$ defined as: $\forall g \in G: \forall S \in \powerset G: g * S = g \circ S$ where $g \circ S$ is the subset product $\set g \circ S$. Then the stabilizer of $S$ in $\powerset G$ is the set: $\Stab S = S$

label: Stabilizer of Subspace stabilizes Orthogonal Complement
snippet: Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex Hilbert space (that is, inner product space). Let $t: H \to H$ be a normal operator on $H$. Let $t$ stabilize a subspace $V$. Then $t$ also stabilizes its orthogonal complement $V^\perp$.

label: Stabilizers of Elements in Same Orbit are Conjugate Subgroups
snippet: Let $G$ be a group acting on a set $X$. Let: $y, z \in \Orb x$ where $\Orb x$ denotes the orbit of some $x \in X$. Then their stabilizers $\Stab y$ and $\Stab z$ are conjugate subgroups.

label: Standard Bounded Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\bar d: A^2 \to \R$ be the standard bounded metric of $d$: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in A^2: \map {\bar d} {x, y} = \min \set {1, \map d {x, y} }$ Then $\bar d$ is a metric for $A$.

label: Standard Cauchy Distribution as Quotient of Normal Distributions
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables on a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ have a normal distribution. Then the probability distribution $Z$ defined as: $Z = \dfrac X Y$ has a standard Cauchy distribution.

label: Standard Discrete Metric is Metric
snippet: The standard discrete metric is a metric.

label: Standard Machinery
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\map {\LL^1_{\overline \R} } \mu$ be the space of $\mu$-integrable functions. Let $\map P {f_1, \ldots, f_n}$ be a proposition, where the variables $f_i$ denote $\mu$-measurable functions $f_i: X \to \overline \R$. Let every occurrence of an $f_i$ be of the form: $\ds \int \map \Phi {f_i} \rd \mu$ for a suitable index set $I$ and multilinear mapping $\Phi: \map {\LL^1_{\overline \R} } \mu^I \to \map {\LL^1_{\overline \R} } \mu$.

label: Standard Normal Random Variable as Transformation of Normal Random Variable
snippet: Let $\mu$ be a real number. Let $\sigma$ be a positive real number. Let $X \sim \Gaussian \mu {\sigma^2}$ where $\Gaussian \mu {\sigma^2}$ is the normal distribution with parameters $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$. Then: $\dfrac {X - \mu} \sigma \sim \Gaussian 0 1$ where $\Gaussian 0 1$ is the standard normal distribution.

label: Standard Ordered Basis Vectors are Orthogonal
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \circ}_{\mathbb F}$ be a vector space over a field $\mathbb F$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Let $\tuple {\mathbf e_1, \mathbf e_2, \ldots, \mathbf e_n}$ be the standard ordered basis of $\mathbf V$. Let $\mathbf e_i$ and $\mathbf e_j$ be elements of $\tuple {\mathbf e_1, \mathbf e_2, \ldots, \mathbf e_n}$ such that $i \ne j$. $\mathbf e_i$ and $\mathbf e_j$ are orthogonal.

label: Standard Ordered Basis is Basis
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $n$ be a positive integer. For each $j \in \closedint 1 n$, let $e_j$ be the ordered $n$-tuple of elements of $R$ whose $j$th entry is $1_R$ and all of whose other entries is $0_R$. Then $\sequence {e_n}$ is an ordered basis of the $R$-module $R^n$. This ordered basis is called the standard ordered basis of $R^n$. The corresponding set $\set {e_1, e_2, \ldots, e_n}$ is called the standard basis of $R^n$.

label: Standard Schauder Basis in P-Sequence Space Multiplied by Bounded Sequence is Equivalent to Original Basis
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $p \in \hointr 1 \infty$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ be the $p$-sequence space. Let $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be the standard Schauder basis given by P-Sequence Space admits Schauder Basis. Let $m, M > 0$. Let $\sequence {\lambda_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\GF$ such that: $0 < m \le \cmod {\lambda_n} \le M$ Then $\sequence {\lambda_n e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is equivalent to $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$.

label: Star-Finite Set is Locally Finite
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\FF$ be a set of subsets of $S$ which is star-finite. Then $\FF$ is locally finite.

label: Star Convex Set is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $A$ be a star convex subset of a topological vector space $V$ over $\R$ or $\C$. Then $A$ is path-connected.

label: Star Convex Set is Simply Connected
snippet: Let $A$ be a star convex subset of a topological vector space $\struct {V, \tau}$ over $\R$ or $\C$. Let $\tau_A$ be the subspace topology on $A$ induced by $\tau$. Then $\struct {A, \tau_A}$ is simply connected.

label: State Space of C*-Algebra is Weak-* Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $S_A$ be the set of states on $A$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology. Then $\struct {S_A, w^\ast}$ is compact.

label: State Space of Unital C*-Algebra is Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $S_A$ be the set of states on $A$. Then $S_A$ is convex.

label: State on Unital C*-Subalgebra extends to whole C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $B$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-subalgebra of $A$. Let $f_1 : B \to \C$ be a state. Then there exists a state $f : A \to \C$ extending $f_1$.

label: Steiner's Calculus Problem
snippet: Let $f: \R_{>0} \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R_{>0}: \map f x = x^{1/x}$ Then $\map f x$ reaches its maximum at $x = e$ where $e$ is Euler's number.

label: Steiner-Lehmus Theorem
snippet: Let $ABC$ be a triangle. Denote the lengths of the angle bisectors through the vertices $A$ and $B$ by $\omega_\alpha$ and $\omega_\beta$. Let $\omega_\alpha = \omega_\beta$. Then $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle. 250px

label: Steiner Inellipse is Unique
snippet: For every triangle, there is one and only one Steiner inellipse.

label: Steinitz's Theorem
snippet: Let $E / F$ be a finite field extension. $(1): \quad E / F$ is simple: there exists $\alpha \in E$ such that $E = \map F \alpha$ $(2): \quad$ there are only finitely many intermediate fields between $E$ and $F$.

label: Step Function satisfies Dirichlet Conditions
snippet: Let $\alpha, \beta \in \R$ be a real numbers such that $\alpha < \beta$. Let $\map f x$ be a step function defined on the interval $\openint \alpha \beta$. Then $f$ satisfies the Dirichlet conditions.

label: Stewart's Theorem
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with sides $a, b, c$. Let $CP$ be a cevian from $C$ to $P$. 400px Then: $a^2 \cdot AP + b^2 \cdot PB = c \paren {CP^2 + AP \cdot PB}$

label: Stirling's Formula
snippet: The factorial function can be approximated by the formula: $n! \sim \sqrt {2 \pi n} \paren {\dfrac n e}^n$ where $\sim$ denotes asymptotically equal.

label: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of n with n-1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be an integer greater than $0$. Then: $\ds {n \brace n - 1} = \binom n 2$ where: $\ds {n \brace n - 1}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind $\dbinom n 2$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

label: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of n with n-2
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 2}$ be an integer greater than or equal to $2$. Then: $\ds {n \brace n - 2} = \binom {n + 1} 4 + 2 \binom n 4$ where: $\ds {n \brace n - 2}$ denotes an Stirling number of the second kind $\dbinom n 4$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

label: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of n with n-3
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 3}$ be an integer greater than or equal to $3$. Then: $\ds {n \brace n - 3} = \binom {n + 2} 6 + 8 \binom {n + 1} 6 + 6 \binom n 6$ where: $\ds {n \brace n - 3}$ denotes an Stirling number of the second kind $\dbinom n 6$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

label: Stokes's Law
snippet: == Physical Law == Stokes's Law is an empirical law for the drag exerted on a spherical body $\BB$ with a small Reynolds number in a viscous fluid $\FF$. It is formulated as: $\mathbf F_{\rm d} = 6 \pi \mu r \mathbf v$ where: $\mathbf F_{\rm d}$ is the Stokes's drag acting on the boundary between $\FF$ and $\BB$ in newtons $\mu$ is the dynamic viscosity in pascal-seconds $r$ is the radius of $\BB$ in metres $\mathbf v$ is the velocity of $\FF$ relative to $\BB$ in metres per second.

label: Stolz-Cesàro Theorem
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence. {{explain|Domain of $\sequence {a_n}$ -- $\R$ presumably but could it be $\C$?}} Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be a sequence of (strictly) positive real numbers such that: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^\infty b_n = \infty$ If: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \dfrac {a_n} {b_n} = L \in \R$ then also: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \dfrac {a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_n} {b_1 + b_2 + \cdots + b_n} = L$

label: Stone's Representation Theorem for Boolean Algebras
snippet: Let $B$ be a Boolean algebra. Let $S$ be the Stone space of $B$. Then: The set of clopen sets in $S$ is a Boolean algebra under union, intersection, and complementation in $S$. That Boolean algebra is isomorphic to $B$.

label: Stone Space of Boolean Lattice is Hausdorff
snippet: Let $B = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be a Boolean lattice. Let $\map S B = \struct {U, \tau}$ be the Stone space of $B$. Then, $\map S B$ is a Hausdorff space.

label: Stone Space of Boolean Lattice is Topological Space
snippet: Let $\struct {B, \preceq, \wedge, \vee}$ be a Boolean lattice. Let $\struct {U, \tau}$ be the Stone space of $B$. Then $\struct {U, \tau}$ is a topological space.

label: Stopped Sigma-Algebra is Sigma-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $T$ be a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let $\FF_T$ be the stopped $\sigma$-algebra associated with $T$. Then $\FF_T$ is a $\sigma$-algebra.

label: Stopped Supermartingale is Supermartingale
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {X_n}_{n \ge 0}$ be an $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-supermartingale. Let $T$ be a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let $\sequence {X_n^T}_{n \ge 0}$ be the stopped process. Then $\sequence {X_n^T}_{n \ge 0}$ is a $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-supermartingale.
