Straight Line cut in Extreme and Mean Ratio plus its Greater Segment
Straight Line making Larger Angle with Perpendicular to Straight Line is Longer
snippet: Let $AB$ be a straight line. Let $C$ be a point which is not on $AB$. Let $D$ be a point on $AB$ such that $CD$ is perpendicular to $AB$. Let $E, F$ be points on $AB$ such that $\angle DCE > \angle DCF$. Then $CE > CF$.

label: Straight Line which cuts Harmonic Pencil forms Harmonic Range
snippet: Let $AB$ and $PQ$ be line segments on a straight line such that $\tuple {AB, PQ}$ is a harmonic range. Let $O$ be a point which is not on the straight line $AB$. Let $\map O {AB, PQ}$ be the harmonic pencil formed from $O$ and $\tuple {AB, PQ}$. Let a straight line intersect $OA$, $OB$, $OP$ and $OQ$ at $A'$, $B'$, $P'$ and $Q'$ respectively. 480px Then $A'$, $B'$, $P'$ and $Q'$ themselves form a harmonic range $\tuple {A'B', P'Q'}$.

label: Straight Lines Subtending Two Consecutive Angles in Regular Pentagon cut in Extreme and Mean Ratio
Straight Lines cut in Same Ratio by Parallel Planes
Straight Lines which make Equal Angles with Perpendicular to Straight Line are Equal
snippet: Let $AB$ be a straight line. Let $C$ be a point which is not on $AB$. Let $D$ be a point on $AB$ such that $CD$ is perpendicular to $AB$. Let $E, F$ be points on $AB$ such that $\angle DCE = \angle DCF$. Then $CE = CF$.

label: Strassen Algorithm/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Use of the Strassen Algorithm ==

label: Strict Hypograph of Continuous Real Function is Open
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Consider $X \times \GF$ as the direct product of $X$ and $\GF$ as topological vector spaces. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a function. Let $\map {\operatorname {hypo}_S} f$ be the strict hypograph of $f$. Then $\map {\operatorname {hypo}_S} f$ is open in $X \times \GF$.

label: Strict Lower Closure in Restricted Ordering
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$, and let $\preceq \restriction_T$ be the restricted ordering on $T$. Then for all $t \in T$: $t^{\prec T} = T \cap t^{\prec S}$ where: $t^{\prec T}$ is the strict lower closure of $t$ in $\left({T, \preceq \restriction_T}\right)$ $t^{\prec S}$ is the strict lower closure of $t$ in $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$.

label: Strict Lower Closure of G-Tower is Set of Elements which are Proper Subsets
snippet: Let $M$ be a class. Let $g: M \to M$ be a progressing mapping on $M$. Let $M$ be a $g$-tower. Let $x \in M$. Then the strict lower closure of $x$ is the set of all elements of $M$ that are proper subsets of $M$.

label: Strict Ordering can be Expanded to Compare Additional Pair
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be an ordered set. Let $a$ and $b$ be distinct, $\prec$-incomparable elements of $S$. That is, let: $a \nprec b$ and $b \nprec a$. Let $\prec' = {\prec} \cup \set {\tuple {a, b} }$. Define a relation $\prec'^+$ by letting $p \prec'^+ q$ : $p \prec q$ or: $p \preceq a$ and $b \preceq q$ where $\preceq$ is the reflexive closure of $\prec$. Then: $\prec'^+$ is a strict ordering $\prec^+$ is the transitive closure of $\prec'$.

label: Strict Ordering on Integers is Asymmetric
snippet: Let $\eqclass {a, b} {}$ denote an integer, as defined by the formal definition of integers. Then: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {c, d} {} | c = }} {{eqn | lo= \implies | l = \eqclass {c, d} {} | o = \nless | r = \eqclass {a, b} {} | c = }} That is, strict ordering on the integers is asymmetric.

label: Strict Ordering on Integers is Transitive
snippet: Let $\eqclass {a, b} {}$ denote an integer, as defined by the formal definition of integers. Then: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {c, d} {} | c = }} {{eqn | lo= \land | l = \eqclass {c, d} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {e, f} {} | c = }} {{eqn | ll= \implies | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {e, f} {} | c = }} That is, strict ordering on the integers is transitive.

label: Strict Ordering on Integers is Trichotomy
snippet: Let $\eqclass {a, b} {}$ and $\eqclass {c, d} {}$ be integers, as defined by the formal definition of integers. Then exactly one of the following holds: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = | r = \eqclass {c, d} {} | c = }} That is, strict ordering is a trichotomy.

label: Strict Ordering on Integers is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\eqclass {a, b} {}$ denote an integer, as defined by the formal definition of integers. Let: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | r = \eqclass {a', b'} {} | c = }} {{eqn | l = \eqclass {c, d} {} | r = \eqclass {c', d'} {} | c = }} Then: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {c, d} {} | c = }} {{eqn | ll= \leadstoandfrom | l = \eqclass {a', b'} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {c', d'} {} | c = }}

label: Strict Upper Closure in Restricted Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$, and let $\preceq \restriction_T$ be the restricted ordering on $T$. Then for all $t \in T$: $t^{\succ T} = T \cap t^{\succ S}$ where: $t^{\succ T}$ is the strict upper closure of $t$ in $\struct {T, \preceq \restriction_T}$ $t^{\succ S}$ is the strict upper closure of $t$ in $\struct {S, \preceq}$.

label: Strict Weak Ordering Induces Partition
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be a relational structure such that $\prec$ is a strict weak ordering on $S$. Then $S$ can be partitioned into equivalence classes whose equivalence relation is "is non-comparable". That is, each of the partitions $A$ of $S$ is a relational structure $\struct {\mathbb S, <}$ such that: $\mathbb S$ is the set of these partitions of $S$; $<$ is the strict total ordering on $\mathbb S$ induced by $\prec$.

label: Strict Well-Ordering Isomorphic to Unique Ordinal under Unique Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be a strict well-ordering. Then there exists a unique ordinal $x$ and unique mapping $f$ such that $f: x \to S$ is an order isomorphism.

label: Strictly Increasing Infinite Sequence of Integers is Cofinal in Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $S = \left\langle{x_n}\right\rangle$ be an infinite sequence of integers which is strictly increasing. Then $S$ is a cofinal subset of $\left({\Z, \le}\right)$ where $\le$ is the usual ordering on the integers.

label: Strictly Increasing Infinite Sequence of Positive Integers is Cofinal in Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $S = \sequence {x_n}$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers which is strictly increasing. Then $S$ is a cofinal subset of $\struct {\N, \le}$ where $\le$ is the usual ordering on the natural numbers.

label: Strictly Increasing Mapping Between Wosets Implies Order Isomorphism
snippet: Let $J$ and $E$ be well-ordered sets. Let there exist a mapping $k: J \to E$ which is strictly increasing. Then $J$ is order isomorphic to $E$ or an initial segment of $E$.

label: Strictly Increasing Sequence induces Partition
snippet: Let $\sequence {r_k}_{0 \mathop \le k \mathop \le n}$ be a strictly increasing finite sequence of natural numbers. Let: $\forall k \in \closedint 1 n: A_k := \closedint {r_{k - 1} + 1} {r_k}$ Then: $\set {A_k: k \in \closedint 1 n}$ is a partition of $\closedint {r_0 + 1} {r_n}$.

label: Strictly Increasing Sequence on Ordered Set
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $\sequence {r_k}_{p \mathop \le k \mathop \le q}$ be a finite sequence of elements of $\struct {S, \preceq}$. Then $\sequence {r_k}_{p \mathop \le k \mathop \le q}$ is strictly increasing : $\forall k \in \closedint {p + 1} q: r_{k - 1} \prec r_k$

label: Strictly Inductive Semigroup is Inductive Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a strictly inductive semigroup. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is an inductive semigroup.

label: Strictly Maximal Element is Maximal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $m \in T$ be a strictly maximal element of $T$ under $\RR$. Then $m$ is a maximal element of $T$ under $\RR$.

label: Strictly Minimal Element is Minimal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $m \in T$ be a strictly minimal element of $T$ under $\RR$. Then $m$ is a minimal element of $T$ under $\RR$.

label: Strictly Positive Hausdorff Measure implies Infinite Lower Dimensional Measure
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $F \subseteq \R^n$ be a subset of the real Euclidean space. Let $\map {\HH^s} \cdot$ denote the $s$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Let $s \in \R_{\ge 0}$. Then: $\map {\HH^s} F > 0 \implies \forall t \in \hointr 0 s : \map {\HH^t} F = +\infty$

label: Strictly Positive Integer Power Function Strictly Succeeds Each Element
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ be an ordered ring with unity. Let $\struct {R, \le}$ be a directed set with no upper bound. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $f: R \to R$ be defined by: $\forall x \in R: \map f x = \circ^n x$ Then the image of $f$ has elements strictly succeeding each elements of $R$.

label: Strictly Positive Integer Power Function is Unbounded Above
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real numbers with the usual ordering. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be defined by: $\map f x = x^n$ Then $f$ is unbounded above.

label: Strictly Positive Integers have same Cardinality as Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $\Z_{>0} := \set {1, 2, 3, \ldots}$ denote the set of strictly positive integers. Let $\N := \set {0, 1, 2, \ldots}$ denote the set of natural numbers. Then $\Z_{>0}$ has the same cardinality as $\N$.

label: Strictly Positive Power of Strictly Positive Element Greater than One Succeeds Element
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ be an ordered ring with unity. Let $x \in R$ with $x > 1$ and $x > 0$. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Then: $\circ^n x \ge x$

label: Strictly Positive Rational Numbers are Closed under Addition
snippet: Let $\Q_{>0}$ denote the set of strictly positive rational numbers: $\Q_{>0} := \set {x \in \Q: x > 0}$ where $\Q$ denotes the set of rational numbers. The algebraic structure $\struct {\Q_{>0}, +}$ is closed in the sense that: $\forall a, b \in \Q_{>0}: a + b \in \Q_{>0}$ where $+$ denotes rational addition.

label: Strictly Positive Rational Numbers under Multiplication form Countably Infinite Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\Q_{> 0}$ be the set of strictly positive rational numbers, i.e. $\Q_{> 0} = \set {x \in \Q: x > 0}$. The structure $\struct {\Q_{> 0}, \times}$ is a countably infinite abelian group.

label: Strictly Positive Rational Numbers under Multiplication form Subgroup of Non-Zero Rational Numbers
Strictly Positive Real Numbers are Closed under Division
snippet: The set $\R_{>0}$ of strictly positive real numbers is closed under division: $\forall a, b \in \R_{>0}: a \div b \in \R_{>0}$

label: Strictly Positive Real Numbers are Closed under Multiplication
snippet: The set $\R_{>0}$ of strictly positive real numbers is closed under multiplication: $\forall a, b \in \R_{> 0}: a \times b \in \R_{> 0}$

label: Strictly Positive Real Numbers are not Closed under Subtraction
snippet: The set $\R_{>0}$ of strictly positive real numbers is not closed under subtraction.

label: Strictly Positive Real Numbers under Multiplication form Subgroup of Non-Zero Real Numbers
Strictly Positive Real Numbers under Multiplication form Uncountable Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\R_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive real numbers: $\R_{>0} = \set {x \in \R: x > 0}$ The structure $\struct {\R_{>0}, \times}$ is an uncountable abelian group.

label: Strictly Well-Founded Relation determines Strictly Minimal Elements
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\RR$ be a strictly well-founded relation on $A$. Let $B$ be a nonempty class such that $B \subseteq A$. Then $B$ has a strictly minimal element under $\RR$.

label: Strictly Well-Founded Relation has no Relational Loops
snippet: Let $\prec$ be a strictly well-founded relation on $A$ and let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in A$. Then: $\neg \paren {x_1 \prec x_2 \land x_3 \prec x_4 \cdots \land x_n \prec x_1}$ That is, there are no relational loops within $A$.

label: Strictly Well-Founded Relation is Antireflexive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a strictly well-founded relation on a set or class $A$. Then $\RR$ is antireflexive.

label: Strictly Well-Founded Relation is Asymmetric
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure, where $S$ is a set or a proper class. Let $\RR$ be a strictly well-founded relation. Then $\RR$ is asymmetric.

label: Strong Separation Theorem
snippet: Let $C \subset \R^\ell$ be closed and convex. Let $D = \set {\mathbf v} \subset C^c$. Then $C$ and $D$ can be strongly separated.

label: Strong Twin Prime Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == It is conjectured that the number of twin primes less than or equal to $N \in \N$ is asymptotically equal to: $2 C_2 \ds \int_2^N \dfrac {\d x} {\paren {\ln x}^2} = \dfrac {2 C_2 N} {\paren {\ln N}^2}$ The above is true only if the Twin Prime Conjecture holds.

label: Structure Induced by Abelian Group Operation is Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an abelian group whose identity is $e$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {G^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $G^S$ induced by $\circ$. Then $\struct {G^S, \oplus}$ is an abelian group.

label: Structure Induced by Absorbing Operations is Absorbing
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ, *}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus, \otimes}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$ and $*$. Let $\circ$ and $*$ satisfy the absorption law: $\forall a, b \in S: a \circ \paren {a * b} = a$ Then the pointwise operations $\oplus$ and $\otimes$ on $T^S$ also satisfy the absorption law: $\forall f, g \in T^S: f \oplus \paren {f \otimes g} = f$

label: Structure Induced by Associative Operation is Associative
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Let $\circ$ be associative. Then the pointwise operation $\oplus$ induced on $T^S$ by $\circ$ is also associative.

label: Structure Induced by Commutative Operation is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Let $\circ$ be a commutative operation. Then the pointwise operation $\oplus$ induced on $T^S$ by $\circ$ is also commutative.

label: Structure Induced by Commutative Ring Operations is Commutative Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the structure on $R^S$ induced by $+'$ and $\circ'$. Then $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a commutative ring.

label: Structure Induced by Distributive Operation is Distributive
snippet: Let $\struct {T, +, \times}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus, \otimes}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $+$ and $\times$. Let $\times$ be distributive over $+$: $\forall a, b, c \in S$: $a \times \paren {b + c} = \paren{a \times b} + \paren{a \times c}$ and: $\paren {b + c} \times a= \paren{b \times a} + \paren{c \times a}$ Then the pointwise operation $\otimes$ is distributive over the pointwise operation $\oplus$ on $T^S$: $\forall f, g, h \in T^S$: $f \otimes \paren {g \oplus h} = \paren{f \otimes g} \oplus \paren{f \otimes h}$ and: $\paren…

label: Structure Induced by Group Operation is Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {G^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $G^S$ induced by $\circ$. Then $\struct {G^S, \oplus}$ is a group.

label: Structure Induced by Idempotent Operation is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Let $\circ$ be an idempotent operation. Then the pointwise operation $\oplus$ induced on $T^S$ by $\circ$ is also idempotent.

label: Structure Induced by Lattice Operations is Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {L, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a lattice. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {L^S, \veebar, \barwedge}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\vee$ and $\wedge$. Let $\precsim$ be the ordering on $S$ defined by: $\forall f, g \in L^S: f \precsim g$ $f \veebar g = g$ as on Semilattice Induces Ordering. Then $\struct {L^S, \veebar, \barwedge, \precsim}$ is a lattice.

label: Structure Induced by Left Distributive Operation is Left Distributive
snippet: Let $\struct {T, +, \times}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus, \otimes}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $+$ and $\times$. Let $\times$ be left distributive over $+$: $\forall a, b, c \in S: a \times \paren {b + c} = \paren{a \times b} + \paren{a \times c}$ Then the pointwise operation $\otimes$ is left distributive over the pointwise operation $\oplus$ on $T^S$: $\forall f, g, h \in T^S: f \otimes \paren {g \oplus h} = \paren{f \otimes g} \oplus \paren{f \otimes h}$

label: Structure Induced by Right Distributive Operation is Right Distributive
snippet: Let $\struct {T, +, \times}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus, \otimes}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $+$ and $\times$. Let $\times$ be right distributive over $+$: $\forall a, b, c \in S: \paren {b + c} \times a= \paren{b \times a} + \paren{c \times a}$ Then the pointwise operation $\otimes$ is left distributive over the pointwise operation $\oplus$ on $T^S$: $\forall f, g, h \in T^S: \paren {g \oplus h} \otimes f = \paren{g \otimes f} \oplus \paren{h \otimes f}$

label: Structure Induced by Ring Operations is Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a set. Then $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a ring, where $+'$ and $\circ'$ are the pointwise operations induced on $R^S$ by $+$ and $\circ$.

label: Structure Induced by Ring with Unity Operations is Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the structure on $R^S$ induced by $+'$ and $\circ'$. Then $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a ring with unity whose unity is $f_{1_R}: S \to R$, defined by: $\forall s \in S: \map {f_{1_R} } s = 1_R$

label: Structure Induced by Semigroup Operation is Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Then $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ is a semigroup.

label: Structure Induced by Semilattice Operation is Semilattice
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a semilattice. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Then $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ is a semilattice.

label: Structure Induced on Set of All Mappings to Ordered Semigroup is Ordered Semigroup
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T, \odot, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered semigroup. Let $\struct {T^S, \otimes, \preccurlyeq}$ denote the algebraic structure on $T^S$ induced by $\odot$. Then $\struct {T^S, \otimes, \preccurlyeq}$ is an ordered semigroup.

label: Structure of Cardinality 3+ where Every Permutation is Automorphism is Idempotent
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is at least $3$. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure on $S$ such that every permutation on $S$ is an automorphism on $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then $\circ$ is an idempotent operation.

label: Structure of Correlation Matrix
snippet: Let $\sequence a_n$ and $\sequence b_n$ be sequences of $n$ observations. Let $\mathbf C$ be the correlation matrix $\sequence a_n$ and $\sequence b_n$. Then $\mathbf C$ is symmetric with entries on the main diagonal all equal to $1$.

label: Structure of Moore-Penrose Pseudoinverse
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix of order $m \times n$ over the complex numbers $\C$. Let $\mathbf A^+$ be the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of $\mathbf A$. Let $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf D \mathbf V^*$ be a singular value decomposition of $\mathbf A$. Then: $\mathbf A^+ = \mathbf V \mathbf D^+ \mathbf U^*$ where $\mathbf D^+$ is obtained by inverting the non-zero diagonal elements of $\mathbf D$. In the above, recall that $\mathbf V^*$ denotes the Hermitian conjugate of $\mathbf V$.

label: Structure of Recurring Decimal
snippet: Let $\dfrac 1 m$, when expressed as a decimal expansion, recur with a period of $p$ digits with no nonperiodic part. Let $\dfrac 1 n$, when expressed as a decimal expansion, terminate after $q$ digits. Then $\dfrac 1 {m n}$ has a nonperiodic part of $q$ digits, and a recurring part of $p$ digits.

label: Structure of Simple Algebraic Field Extension
snippet: Let $F / K$ be a field extension. Let $\alpha \in F$ be algebraic over $K$. Let $\mu_\alpha$ be the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $K$. Let $K \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial functions. Let $\gen {\mu_\alpha}$ be the ideal of $K \sqbrk X$ generated by $\mu_\alpha$. Let $K \sqbrk \alpha$ be the subring of $F$ generated by $K \cup \set \alpha$. Let $\map K \alpha$ be the subfield of $F$ generated by $K \cup \set \alpha$.

label: Structure with Commutative Idempotent Associative Operations satisfying Absorption Laws is Lattice
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\vee$ and $\wedge$ be binary operations which, when applied to $S$, are both: closed operations commutative operations idempotent operations associative operations. Furthermore, let $\vee$ and $\wedge$ satisfy the absorption laws: $\forall a, b \in S: a \vee \paren {a \wedge b} = a = a \wedge {a \vee b}$ Then there exists a unique lattice ordering $\preccurlyeq$ on $S$ such that: $\forall a, b \in S$: $x \vee y = \sup \set {a, b}$ $x \wedge y = \inf \set {a, b}$ That is: $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preccurlyeq}$ is a lattice.

label: Sturm-Liouville Problem
snippet: Let: $P \in C^\infty \map P x > 0$ $Q \in C^0$ $-\paren {P y'}' + Q y = \lambda y$ $\map y a = \map y b = 0$ Then the Sturm-Liouville problem has an infinite sequence of eigenvalues $\set {\lambda^{\paren n} }$, and to each $\lambda^{\paren n}$ corresponds an eigenfunction $y^{\paren n}$, unique up to a constant factor.

label: Sub-Basis for Initial Topology in terms of Sub-Bases of Target Spaces
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {\struct {Y_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. For each $i \in I$, let $S_i$ be a synthetic basis for $\struct {Y_i, \tau_i}$. Let $\family {f_i: X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of mappings indexed by $I$. Let $\tau$ be the initial topology on $X$ with respect to $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Then: $\SS = \set {f_i^{-1} \sqbrk U : i \in I, \, U \in S_i}$ is a synthetic sub-basis for $\struct {X, \tau}$.

label: Sub-Basis for Real Number Line
snippet: Let the real number line $\R$ be considered as a topology under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $\BB := \set {\openint \gets a, \openint b \to: a, b \in \R}$ is a sub-basis for $\R$.

label: Sub-Basis for Topological Subspace
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $K$ be a sub-basis for $\tau$. Let $\struct {S, \tau'}$ be a subspace of $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $K' = \set {U \cap S: U \in K}$. That is, $K'$ consists of the $\tau'$-open sets in $S$ corresponding to elements of $K$. Then $K'$ is a sub-basis for $\tau'$.

label: Subadditivity of Invariant Metric on Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $d$ be an invariant metric on $X$. Then: $\map d {n x, {\mathbf 0}_X} \le n \map d {x, {\mathbf 0}_X}$ for each $n \in \N$ and $x \in X$.

label: Subband iff Idempotent under Induced Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a band. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the algebraic structure consisting of the power set of $S$ and the operation induced on $\powerset S$ by $\circ$. Let $X \in \powerset S$. Then $X$ is idempotent $\struct {X, \circ}$ is a subband of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

label: Subband of Induced Operation is Set of Subbands
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a band. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the algebraic structure consisting of: the power set $\powerset S$ of $S$ and the operation $\circ_\PP$ induced on $\powerset S$ by $\circ$. Let $T \subseteq \powerset S$. Let $\struct {T, \circ_\PP}$ be a subband of $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$. Then every element of $T$ is a subband of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

label: Subclass of Set is Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\map \phi x$ be a condition in which $x$ is taken to be a set. Then there exists a set that consists of all of the elements of $A$ that satisfies this condition. In ZF, this result is known as the Axiom of Specification.

label: Subcover is Refinement of Cover
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a cover for $S$. Let $\VV$ be a subcover of $\CC$. Then $\VV$ is a refinement of $\CC$.

label: Subcover of Open Cover is Open
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\CC$ be an open cover of $T$. Let $\CC'$ be a subcover of $S$. Then $\CC'$ is also an open cover of $T$.

label: Subdivision (Graph Theory)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subdivisions in the context of Graph Theory ==

label: Subdomain Test
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of an integral domain $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $\struct {S, + {\restriction_S}, \circ {\restriction_S} }$ is a subdomain of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ these conditions hold: $(1): \quad \struct {S, + {\restriction_S}, \circ {\restriction_S} }$ is a subring of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ $(2): \quad$ The unity of $R$ is also in $S$, that is $1_R = 1_S$.

label: Subextensions of Separable Field Extension are Separable
snippet: Let $E / K / F$ be a tower of fields. Let $E / F$ be separable. Then $E / K$ and $K / F$ are separable.

label: Subfield Test
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$. Let $K$ be a subset of $F$.

label: Subfield of Subfield is Subfield
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $K_1, K_2$ be fields, such that: $K_1$ is a subfield of $R$ $K_2$ is a subfield of $K_1$ Then $K_2$ is a subfield of $R$.

label: Subframe is a Frame
snippet: Let $L = \struct{S, \preceq}$ be a frame. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $M = \struct{T, \preceq \restriction_T}$ be a subframe of $L$ where $\preceq \restriction_T$ is the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then $M$ is a frame.

label: Subgroup/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subgroups ==

label: Subgroup Action is Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\struct {H, \circ}$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $*: H \times G \to G$ be the subgroup action defined for all $h \in H, g \in G$ as: $\forall h \in H, g \in G: h * g := h \circ g$ Then $*$ is a group action.

label: Subgroup Containing all Squares of Group Elements is Normal
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ with the property that: $\forall x \in G: x^2 \in H$ Then $H$ is normal in $G$.

label: Subgroup Generated by Commuting Elements is Abelian
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $S \subseteq G$ such that: $\forall x, y \in S: x \circ y = y \circ x$ Then the subgroup generated by $S$ is abelian.

label: Subgroup Generated by Infinite Order Element is Infinite
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $a \in G$ be of infinite order. Let $\gen a$ be the subgroup generated by $a$. Then $\gen a$ is of infinite order.

label: Subgroup Generated by One Element is Cyclic
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $a \in G$. Then $\gen a$, the subgroup generated by $a$, is cyclic:

label: Subgroup Generated by One Element is Set of Powers
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $a \in G$. Then the subgroup generated by $a$ is the set of powers: $\gen a = \set {a^n : n \in \Z}$

label: Subgroup Generated by Subgroup and Element
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. Let $H$ be a proper subgroup of $G$. Let $a \in G \setminus H$. Let $n$ be the indicator of $a$ in $H$. Then: $K = \left\{{x a^k: x \in H, \ 0 \le k < n}\right\}$ is a subgroup of $G$ such that $H \subseteq K$, and each element of $K$ has a unique representation in this form. Moreover: $K = \left\langle{H, a}\right\rangle$ where $\left\langle{H, a}\right\rangle$ denotes the subgroup generated by $\left\{{H, a}\right\}$, and: $\left\vert{K}\right\vert = n \left\vert{H}\right\vert$ where $\left\vert{K}\right\vert$ denotes the order of $K$.

label: Subgroup Product is Internal Group Direct Product iff Surjective
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $\sequence {H_n}$ be a sequence of subgroups of $G$. Let $\ds \phi: \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n H_k \to G$ be a mapping defined by: $\ds \map \phi {h_1, h_2, \ldots, h_n} = \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n h_k$ Then $\phi$ is surjective : $\ds G = \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n H_k$ That is, $G$ is the internal group direct product of $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_n$.

label: Subgroup equals Conjugate iff Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $N$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $N$ is normal in $G$ (by definition 1) : $\forall g \in G: g \circ N \circ g^{-1} = N$ $\forall g \in G: g^{-1} \circ N \circ g = N$

label: Subgroup is Closed iff Quotient is Hausdorff
snippet: Let $G$ be a topological group. Let $H \le G$ be a subgroup. Let $G / H$ be their quotient.

label: Subgroup is Normal Subgroup of Normalizer
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. A subgroup $H \le G$ is a normal subgroup of its normalizer: $H \le G \implies H \lhd \map {N_G} H$

label: Subgroup is Normal iff Left Cosets are Right Cosets
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $N$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $N$ is normal in $G$ (by definition 1) : Every right coset of $N$ in $G$ is a left coset or equivalently: The right coset space of $N$ in $G$ equals its left coset space.

label: Subgroup is Normal iff it contains Product of Inverses
snippet: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is normal : $\forall a, b \in G: a b \in H \implies a^{-1} b^{-1} \in H$

label: Subgroup is Subgroup of Normalizer
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. A subgroup $H \le G$ is a subgroup of its normalizer: $H \le G \implies H \le \map {N_G} H$

label: Subgroup is Subset of Conjugate iff Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $N$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $N$ is normal in $G$ (by definition 1) : $\forall g \in G: N \subseteq g \circ N \circ g^{-1}$ $\forall g \in G: N \subseteq g^{-1} \circ N \circ g$

label: Subgroup is Superset of Conjugate iff Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $N$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $N$ is normal in $G$ (by definition 1) : $\forall g \in G: g \circ N \circ g^{-1} \subseteq N$ $\forall g \in G: g^{-1} \circ N \circ g \subseteq N$

label: Subgroup of Abelian Group is Abelian
snippet: A subgroup of an abelian group is itself abelian.

label: Subgroup of Abelian Group is Normal
snippet: Every subgroup of an abelian group is normal.

label: Subgroup of Cyclic Group is Cyclic
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is cyclic.

label: Subgroup of Direct Product is not necessarily Direct Product of Subgroups
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups. Let $G \times H$ denote the direct product of $G$ and $H$. Let $K$ be a subgroup of $G \times H$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $K$ is of the form: $G' \times H'$ where: $G'$ is a subgroup of $G$ $H'$ is a subgroup of $H$.

label: Subgroup of Elements whose Order Divides Integer
snippet: Let $A$ be an abelian group. Let $k \in \Z$ and $B$ be a set of the form: $\left\{{x \in A : x^k = e}\right\}$ Then $B$ is a subgroup of $A$.

label: Subgroup of Finite Cyclic Group is Determined by Order
snippet: Let $G = \gen g$ be a cyclic group whose order is $n$ and whose identity is $e$. Let $d \divides n$, where $\divides$ denotes divisibility. Then there exists exactly one subgroup $G_d = \gen {g^{n / d} }$ of $G$ with $d$ elements.

label: Subgroup of Free Group is Free Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a free group. Let $H \le G$ be a subgroup of $G$ such that $H$ is not the trivial group. Then $H$ is also a free group.

label: Subgroup of Index 2 contains all Squares of Group Elements
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ whose index is $2$. Then: $\forall x \in G: x^2 \in H$

label: Subgroup of Index 2 is Normal
snippet: A subgroup of index $2$ is always normal.

label: Subgroup of Index 3 does not necessarily contain all Cubes of Group Elements
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ whose index is $3$. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\forall x \in G: x^3 \in H$

label: Subgroup of Index Least Prime Divisor is Normal
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group of order $n>1$. Let $p$ be the least prime divisor of $n$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ such that: $\index G H = p$ where $\index G H$ denotes the index of $H$ in $G$. Then $H$ is normal.

label: Subgroup of Infinite Cyclic Group is Infinite Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $G = \gen a$ be an infinite cyclic group generated by $a$, whose identity is $e$. Let $g \in G, g \ne e: \exists k \in \Z, k \ne 0: g = a^k$. Let $H = \gen g$. Then $H \le G$ and $H \cong G$. Thus, all non-trivial subgroups of an infinite cyclic group are themselves infinite cyclic groups. A subgroup of $G = \gen a$ is denoted as follows: $n G := \gen {a^n}$ This notation is usually used in the context of $\struct {\Z, +}$, where $n \Z$ is (informally) understood as the set of integer multiples of $n$.

label: Subgroup of Integers is Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Every subgroup of $\struct {\Z, +}$ is an ideal of the ring $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$.

label: Subgroup of Order p in Group of Order 2p is Normal
snippet: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $G$ be a group of order $2 p$. Let $a \in G$ be of order $p$. Let $K = \gen a$ be the subgroup of $G$ generated by $a$. Then $K$ is normal in $G$.

label: Subgroup of Real Numbers is Discrete or Dense
snippet: Let $G$ be a subgroup of the additive group of real numbers. Then one of the following holds: $G$ is dense in $\R$. $G$ is discrete and there exists $a \in \R$ such that $G = a \Z$, that is, $G$ is cyclic.

label: Subgroup of Solvable Group is Solvable
snippet: Let $G$ be a solvable group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is solvable.

label: Subgroup of Subgroup with Prime Index
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $K$ be a subgroup of $H$. Let: $\index G K = p$ where: $p$ denotes a prime number $\index G K$ denotes the index of $K$ in $G$. Then either: $H = K$ or: $H = G$

label: Subgroup of Symmetric Group that Fixes n
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $H$ denote the subgroup of $S_n$ which consists of all $\pi \in S_n$ such that: $\map \pi n = n$ Then: $H = S_{n - 1}$ and the index of $H$ in $S_n$ is given by: $\index {S_n} H = n$

label: Subgroups of Additive Group of Integers
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $n \Z$ be the additive group of integer multiples of $n$. Every non-trivial subgroup of $\struct {\Z, +}$ has the form $n \Z$.

label: Subgroups of Additive Group of Integers Modulo m
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ denote the additive group of integers modulo $m$. The subgroups of $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ are the additive groups of integers modulo $k$ where: $k \divides m$

label: Subgroups of Symmetry Group of Regular Hexagon
snippet: Let $\HH = ABCDEF$ be a regular hexagon. Let $D_6$ denote the symmetry group of $\HH$. 520px Let $e$ denote the identity mapping Let $\alpha$ denote rotation of $\HH$ anticlockwise through $\dfrac \pi 3$ radians ($60 \degrees$) Let $\beta$ denote reflection of $\HH$ in the $AD$ axis. The subsets of $D_6$ which form its subgroups are as follows: Order $1$: $\set e$ Order $2$: $\set {e, \alpha^3}$ $\set {e, \beta}$ $\set {e, \alpha \beta}$ $\set {e, \alpha^2 \beta}$ $\set {e, \alpha^3 \beta}$ $\set {e, \alpha^4 \beta}$ $\set {e, \alpha^5 \beta}$ Order $3$: $\set {e, \alpha^2, \alpha^4}$ Order…

label: Sublinear Functional is Linear Functional iff Dominates Unique Linear Functional
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\R$. Let $p : X \to \R$ be a sublinear functional. Then $p$ is linear there exists a unique linear functional $f : X \to \R$ such that: $\map f x \le \map p x$ for each $x \in X$.

label: Submodule Test
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring with unity $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +, \circ}_R$ be a unitary $R$-module. Let $H$ be a non-empty subset of $G$. Then $\struct {H, +, \circ}_R$ is a submodule of $G$ :

label: Submodule is Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_G}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $\struct {H, +_H, \circ_H}_R$ be an $R$-submodule of $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_G}_R$. Then $H$ is a subgroup of $G$.

label: Submodule of Module of Polynomial Functions
snippet: Let $K$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\map P K$ be the set of all polynomial functions on $K$. Consider the set $\map {P_m} K$ of all the polynomial functions: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{m - 1} \alpha_k {I_K}^k$ for some $m \in \N^*$ where: $\sequence {\alpha_k}_{k \in \closedint 0 {m - 1} }$ is any sequence of $m$ terms of $K$. Then $\map {P_m} K$ is a submodule of $\map P K$.

label: Subobject Class in Category of Sets
snippet: Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\map {\overline {\mathbf {Sub} }_{\mathbf {Set} } } S$ be the category of subobject classes of $S$. Let $\powerset S$ be the order category on the power set of $S$ induced by Subset Relation on Power Set is Partial Ordering. Then $\map {\overline {\mathbf {Sub} }_{\mathbf {Set} } } S \cong \powerset S$.

label: Subring Generated by Unity of Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let the mapping $g: \Z \to R$ be defined as $\forall n \in \Z: \map g n = n 1_R$, where $n 1_R$ the $n$th power of $1_R$. Let $\ideal x$ be the principal ideal of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ generated by $x$. Then $g$ is an epimorphism from $\Z$ onto the subring $S$ of $R$ generated by $1_R$. If $R$ has no proper zero divisors, then $g$ is the only nonzero homomorphism from $\Z$ into $R$.

label: Subring Module is Module
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {S, +_S, \times_S}$ be a subring of $R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $\circ_S$ be the restriction of $\circ$ to $S \times G$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_S}_S$ be subring module induced by $S$. Then $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_S}_S$ is an $S$-module.

label: Subring Test
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of a ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $\struct {S, +, \circ}$ is a subring of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ these all hold: $(1): \quad S \ne \O$ $(2): \quad \forall x, y \in S: x + \paren {-y} \in S$ $(3): \quad \forall x, y \in S: x \circ y \in S$

label: Subring is not necessarily Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {S, +_S, \circ_S}$ be a subring of $R$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $S$ is also an ideal of $R$.

label: Subsemigroup/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subsemigroups ==

label: Subsemigroup of Cancellable Mappings is Subgroup of Invertible Mappings
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $S^S$ denote the set of mappings from $S$ to itself. Let $\CC \subseteq S^S$ denote the set of cancellable mappings on $S$. Let $\MM \subseteq S^S$ denote the set of invertible mappings on $S$. Then: the subsemigroup $\struct {\CC, \circ}$ of $\struct {S^S, \circ}$ coincides with the subgroup $\struct {\MM, \circ}$ of $\struct {S^S, \circ}$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings.

label: Subsemigroup of Monoid is not necessarily Monoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \circ}$ Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {T, \circ}$ has an identity.

label: Subsequence Characterization of Cauchy Sequence in Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a Cauchy sequence : for all strictly increasing sequences $\sequence {n_k}_{k \mathop \in \N}$ and $\sequence {m_k}_{k \mathop \in \N}$ in $\N$, we have that: $\norm {x_{n_k} - x_{m_k} }_X \to 0$.

label: Subsequence Characterization of Cauchy Sequence in Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a Cauchy sequence : for all strictly increasing sequences $\sequence {n_k}_{k \mathop \in \N}$ and $\sequence {m_k}_{k \mathop \in \N}$ in $\N$, we have that: $x_{n_k} - x_{m_k} \to {\mathbf 0}_X$ in $\struct {X, \tau}$.

label: Subsequence of Basic Sequence in Banach Space is Basic Sequence
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a basic sequence in $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $\sequence {x_{n_k} }_{k \mathop \in \N}$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Then $\sequence {x_{n_k} }_{k \mathop \in \N}$ is a basic sequence in $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$.

label: Subsequence of Real Sequence Diverging to Negative Infinity Diverges to Negative Infinity
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a real sequence with $x_n \to -\infty$. Let $\sequence {x_{n_j} }_{j \mathop \in \N}$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Then: $x_{n_j} \to -\infty$

label: Subsequence of Real Sequence Diverging to Positive Infinity Diverges to Positive Infinity
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a real sequence with $x_n \to +\infty$. Let $\sequence {x_{n_j} }_{j \mathop \in \N}$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Then: $x_{n_j} \to +\infty$

label: Subsequence of Sequence in Metric Space with Limit
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $M$. Let $x$ be a limit point of $S = \set {x_n: n \in \N}$, the set of members of $\sequence {x_n}$. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ has a subsequence which converges to $x$.

label: Subsequence of Subsequence
snippet: Let $s$ be a set. Let $\sequence {s_n}$ be a sequence in $S$. Let $\sequence {s_m}$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {s_n}$. Let $\sequence {s_k}$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {s_m}$. Then $\sequence {s_k}$ is a subsequence of $\sequence {s_n}$.

label: Subset/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subsets ==

label: Subset Equivalences
snippet: == Definitions == In the following: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $S \cup T$ denotes the union of $S$ and $T$ $S \cap T$ denotes the intersection of $S$ and $T$ $S \setminus T$ denotes the set difference between $S$ and $T$ $\O$ denotes the empty set $\mathbb U$ denotes the universal set $\complement$ denotes set complement.

label: Subset Intersection Set Difference is Empty Iff Subset of Second Set
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq S$. Then: $A \cap S \setminus T = \O$ $A \subseteq T$

label: Subset Product/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subset Product == Let $G$ be a group.

label: Subset Product Action is Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\powerset G$ be the power set of $\struct {G, \circ}$. For any $S \in \powerset G$ and for any $g \in G$, the subset product action: $\forall g \in G: \forall S \in \powerset G: g * S = g \circ S$ is a group action.

label: Subset Product of Abelian Subgroups
snippet: Let $\left({G, \circ}\right)$ be an abelian group. Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be subgroups of $G$. Then $H_1 \circ H_2$ is a subgroup of $G$.

label: Subset Product of Normal Subgroups is Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $N$ and $N'$ be normal subgroups of $G$. Then $N N'$ is also a normal subgroup of $G$.

label: Subset Product of Normal Subgroups with Trivial Intersection
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H, K$ be normal subgroups of $G$. Let $H \cap K = e$. Then $H K$ is isomorphic to $H \times K$ where: $H K$ denotes the subset product of $H$ and $K$ $H \times K$ denotes the direct product of $H$ and $K$.

label: Subset Product of Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H, K$ be subgroups of $G$. Then $H \circ K$ is a subgroup of $G$ $H$ and $K$ are permutable. That is: $H \circ K$ is a subgroup of $G$ : $H \circ K = K \circ H$ where $H \circ K$ denotes subset product.

label: Subset Product with Normal Subgroup as Generator
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let: $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Then: $N \lhd \gen {N, H} = N H = H N \le G$ where: $\le$ denotes subgroup $\lhd$ denotes normal subgroup $\gen {N, H}$ denotes a subgroup generator $N H$ denotes subset product.

label: Subset Product with Normal Subgroup is Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let: $(1): \quad H$ be a subgroup of $G$ $(2): \quad N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $H N$ denote subset product. Then $H N$ and $N H$ are both subgroups of $G$.

label: Subset Products of Normal Subgroup with Normal Subgroup of Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let: $(1): \quad H$ be a subgroup of $G$ $(2): \quad K$ be a normal subgroup of $H$ $(3): \quad N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$ Then: $N K \lhd N H$ where: $N K$ and $N H$ denote subset product $\lhd$ denotes the relation of being a normal subgroup.

label: Subset Relation is Antisymmetric
snippet: The subset relation is antisymmetric: $\paren {x \subseteq y} \land \paren {y \subseteq x} \iff x = y$ where $x$ and $y$ are sets.

label: Subset Relation is Compatible with Subset Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the power structure of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then the subset relation on $S$ is compatible with $\circ_\PP$. That is: {{eqn | q = \forall X, Y, Z \in \powerset S | l = X \subseteq Y | o = \implies | r = \paren {X \circ_\PP Z} \subseteq \paren {Y \circ_\PP Z} | c = }} {{eqn | l = X \subseteq Y | o = \implies | r = \paren {Z \circ_\PP X} \subseteq \paren {Z \circ_\PP Y} | c = }}

label: Subset Relation is Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Let $\mathbb S \subseteq \powerset S$ be any subset of $\powerset S$, that is, an arbitrary set of subsets of $S$. Then $\subseteq$ is an ordering on $\mathbb S$. In other words, let $\struct {\mathbb S, \subseteq}$ be the relational structure defined on $\mathbb S$ by the subset relation $\subseteq$. Then $\struct {\mathbb S, \subseteq}$ is an ordered set.

label: Subset Relation is Transitive
snippet: The subset relation is transitive: $\paren {R \subseteq S} \land \paren {S \subseteq T} \implies R \subseteq T$

label: Subset Relation on Power Set is Partial Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ be the relational structure defined on $\powerset S$ by the subset relation $\subseteq$. Then $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ is an ordered set. The ordering $\subseteq$ is partial $S$ is neither empty nor a singleton; otherwise it is total.

label: Subset equals Preimage of Image implies Injection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ be the direct image mapping of $f$. Similarly, let $f^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S$ be the inverse image mapping of $f$. Let: $\forall A \in \powerset S: A = \map {\paren {f^\gets \circ f^\to} } A$ Then $f$ is an injection.

label: Subset has 2 Conjugates then Normal Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $S$ be a subset of $G$. Let $S$ have exactly two conjugates in $G$. Then $G$ has a proper non-trivial normal subgroup.

label: Subset implies Cardinal Inequality
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that $S \subseteq T$. Furthermore, let: $T \sim \card T$ where $\card T$ denotes the cardinality of $T$. Then: $\card S \le \card T$

label: Subset in Neighborhood Space is Neighborhood iff it contains Open Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \NN}$ be a neighborhood space. Let $x \in S$ be a point of $S$. Let $N \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Then $N$ is a neighborhood of $x$ there exists an open set $U$ of $\struct {S, \NN}$ such that $x \in U \subseteq N$.

label: Subset in Subsets
snippet: Let $S, B$ be sets. Let $A$ be subset of $S$. Then: $A \subseteq B \iff \forall x \in S: x \in A \implies x \in B$

label: Subset is Compatible with Ordinal Addition
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $(1): \quad x \le y \implies \paren {z + x} \le \paren {z + y}$ $(2): \quad x \le y \implies \paren {x + z} \le \paren {y + z}$

label: Subset is Compatible with Ordinal Multiplication
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $(1): \quad x \le y \implies \paren {z \cdot x} \le \paren {z \cdot y}$ $(2): \quad x \le y \implies \paren {x \cdot z} \le \paren {y \cdot z}$

label: Subset is Compatible with Ordinal Successor
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals and let $x^+$ denote the successor set of $x$. Let $x \in y$. Then: $x^+ \in y^+$

label: Subset is Element of Power Set
snippet: Let $x$ be a set. Let $\powerset x$ denote the power set of $x$. Then: $y \in \powerset x \iff y \subseteq x$

label: Subset is Left Compatible with Ordinal Addition
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le y \implies \paren {z + x} \le \paren {z + y}$

label: Subset is Left Compatible with Ordinal Multiplication
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le y \implies \paren {z \cdot x} \le \paren {z \cdot y}$

label: Subset is Right Compatible with Ordinal Addition
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le y \implies \paren {x + z} \le \paren {y + z}$

label: Subset is Right Compatible with Ordinal Exponentiation
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le y \implies x^z \le y^z$

label: Subset is Right Compatible with Ordinal Multiplication
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le y \implies \paren {x \cdot z} \le \paren {y \cdot z}$

label: Subset not necessarily Submagma
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $T \subseteq S$. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\struct {T, \circ} \subseteq \struct {S, \circ}$ That is, it does not always follow that $\struct {T, \circ}$ is a submagma of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

label: Subset of Abelian Group Generated by Product of Element with Inverse Element is Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an abelian group. Let $S \subset G$ be a non-empty subset of $G$ such that $\struct {S, \circ}$ is closed. Let $H$ be the set defined as: $H := \set {x \circ y^{-1}: x, y \in S}$ Then $\struct {H, \circ}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {G, \circ}$.

label: Subset of Banach Space Bounded Away from Zero including Zero Vector in Weak Closure contains Basic Sequence with Basis Constant Arbitrarily Close to 1
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Let $\cl_w$ be the closure taken in $\struct {X, w}$. Let $S \subseteq X$ be such that: $\ds \inf_{x \mathop \in S} \norm x_X > 0$ and: ${\mathbf 0}_X \in \map {\cl_w} S$ Let $\epsilon > 0$. Then there exists a basic sequence in $S$ with basis constant $K_b \le 1 + \epsilon$.

label: Subset of Bounded Above Set is Bounded Above
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers such that $A \subseteq B$. Let $B$ be bounded above. Then $A$ is also bounded above.

label: Subset of Bounded Below Set is Bounded Below
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers such that $A \subseteq B$. Let $B$ be bounded below. Then $A$ is also bounded below.

label: Subset of Bounded Subset of Metric Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $B$ be a bounded subset of $M$. Let $\map \diam B$ denote the diameter of $B$. Let $C \subseteq B$ be a subset of $B$. Then $C$ is a bounded subset of $M$ such that: $\map \diam C \le \map \diam B$

label: Subset of Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of ordered pairs. Then $S$ is the subset of the cartesian product of two sets.

label: Subset of Cartesian Product not necessarily Cartesian Product of Subsets
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Let $A$ and $B$ both have at least two distinct elements. Then there exists $W \subseteq A \times B$ such that $W$ is not the cartesian product of a subset of $A$ and a subset of $B$.

label: Subset of Codomain is Superset of Image of Preimage
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $B \subseteq T \implies \paren {f \circ f^{-1} } \sqbrk B \subseteq B$ where: $f \sqbrk B$ denotes the image of $B$ under $f$ $f^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $f$ $f \circ f^{-1}$ denotes composition of $f$ and $f^{-1}$. This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings and inverse image mappings as: $\forall B \in \powerset T: \map {\paren {f^\to \circ f^\gets} } B \subseteq B$

label: Subset of Countable Set is Countable
snippet: A subset of a countable set is countable.

label: Subset of Countably Infinite Set is Countable
snippet: Every subset of a countably infinite set is countable.

label: Subset of Cover is Cover of Subset
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a cover of $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let: $\CC_T = \set {C \in \CC : C \cap T \ne \O}$ Then $\CC_T$ is a cover of $T$: $T \subseteq \bigcup \CC_T$

label: Subset of Discrete Set of Subsets is Discrete
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF \subseteq \powerset S$ be a set of subsets of $S$. Let $\GG \subseteq \FF$. If $\FF$ is discrete then $\GG$ is discrete.

label: Subset of Empty Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Then: $A$ is a subset of the empty set $\O$ $A$ is equal to the empty set: $A \subseteq \O \iff A = \O$

label: Subset of Empty Set iff Empty
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\O$ denote the empty set. Then $S \subseteq \O$ $S = \O$.

label: Subset of Euclidean Plane whose Product of Coordinates are Greater Than or Equal to 1 is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^2, \tau_d}$ be the real number plane with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $A \subseteq R^2$ be the set of all points defined as: $A := \set {\tuple {x, y} \in \R^2: x y \ge 1}$ Then $A$ is a closed set in $\struct {\R^2, d}$.

label: Subset of Finite Dimensional Normed Vector Space is Compact iff Closed and Bounded/Sufficient Condition
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\,\cdot\,}}$ be a finite-dimensional normed vector space. Let $K \subset X$ be a compact subset. Then $K$ is closed and bounded.

label: Subset of Finite Set is Finite
snippet: Let $X$ be a finite set. If $Y$ is a subset of $X$, then $Y$ is also finite.

label: Subset of Hilbert Sequence Space with Non-Empty Interior is not Compact
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} {x_i}^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Let $H$ be a subset of $\ell^2$ whose interior is non-empty. Then $H$ is not compact in $\ell^2$.

label: Subset of Indiscrete Space is Dense-in-itself
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$ containing more than one point. Then $H$ is dense-in-itself.

label: Subset of Indiscrete Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: $H \subseteq S$ is sequentially compact in an indiscrete topological space $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$.

label: Subset of Join Semilattice on Total Ordering is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $\struct {S, \vee, \preccurlyeq}$ be the join semilattice with respect to $\preccurlyeq$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be an arbitrary subset of $S$. Then $\struct {T, \vee, \preccurlyeq}$ is closed under $\vee$.

label: Subset of Linear Code with Even Weight Codewords
snippet: Let $C$ be a linear code. Let $C^+$ be the subset of $C$ consisting of all the codewords of $C$ which have even weight. Then $C^+$ is a subgroup of $C$ such that either $C^+ = C$ or such that $\order {C^+} = \dfrac {\order C} 2$.

label: Subset of Linearly Independent Set is Linearly Independent
snippet: A subset of a linearly independent set is also linearly independent.

label: Subset of Linearly Ordered Space which is Order-Complete and Closed but not Compact
snippet: Let $X = \hointr 0 1 \cup \openint 2 3 \cup \set 4$. Let $\preceq$ be the ordering on $X$ induced by the usual ordering of the real numbers. Let $\tau$ be the $\preceq$ order topology on $X$. Let $Y = \hointr 0 1 \cup \set 4$. Let $\tau'$ be the $\tau$-relative subspace topology on $Y$. Then: $\struct {Y, \preceq}$ is a complete lattice $Y$ is closed in $X$ but: $\struct {Y, \tau'}$ is not compact.

label: Subset of Locally Finite Set of Subsets is Locally Finite
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF \subseteq \powerset S$ be a set of subsets of $S$. Let $\GG \subseteq \FF$. If $\FF$ is locally finite then $\GG$ is locally finite.

label: Subset of Meager Set is Meager Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A$ be meager in $T$. Let $B \subseteq A$. Then $B$ is meager in $T$.

label: Subset of Metric Space contains Limits of Sequences iff Closed
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$. Then $H$ is closed in $M$ : for each sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of points of $H$ that converges to a point $a \in A$, it follows that $a \in H$.

label: Subset of Metric Space is Closed iff contains all Zero Distance Points
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$. Then $H$ is closed in $M$ : $\forall x \in A: \map d {x, H} = 0 \implies x \in H$ where $\map d {x, H}$ denotes the distance between $x$ and $H$.

label: Subset of Metric Space is Subset of its Closure
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$ be a subset of $A$. Then: $H \subseteq H^-$ where $H^-$ denotes the closure of $H$.

label: Subset of Module Containing Identity is Linearly Dependent
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $H \subseteq G$ such that $e \in H$. Then $H$ is a linearly dependent set.

label: Subset of Natural Numbers is either Finite or Denumerable
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of the natural numbers $\N$. Then $S$ is either finite or denumerable.

label: Subset of Natural Numbers under Max Operation is Monoid
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \N$ be a subset of the natural numbers $\N$. Let $\struct {S, \max}$ denote the algebraic structure formed from $S$ and the max operation. Then $\struct {S, \max}$ is a monoid. Its identity element is the smallest element of $S$.

label: Subset of Naturals is Finite iff Bounded
snippet: Let $X$ be a subset of the natural numbers $\N$. Then $X$ is finite it is bounded.

label: Subset of Normed Vector Space is Everywhere Dense iff Closure is Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}}$ be a normed vector space. Let $D \subseteq X$ be a subset of $X$. Let $D^-$ be the closure of $D$. Then $D$ is dense $D^- = X$.

label: Subset of Normed Vector Space is von Neumann-Bounded in Weak Topology iff Norm Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $B \subseteq X$. Then $B$ is bounded in $X$ it is von Neumann-bounded in $\struct {X, w}$.

label: Subset of Normed Vector Space providing Bounded Point Evaluations is Norm Bounded
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $S \subseteq X$. Suppose that: $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in S} \cmod {\map f x} < \infty$ for each $f \in X^\ast$. Then we have: $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in S} 
orm x_X < \infty$ Hence $S$ is bounded.

label: Subset of Nowhere Dense Subset is Nowhere Dense
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \subseteq S$ be nowhere dense in $T$. Let $B \subseteq A$. Then $B$ is nowhere dense in $T$.

label: Subset of Open Reciprocal-N Balls forms Neighborhood Basis in Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\R$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Let $a \in \R$ be a point in $\R$. Let $k \in \Z$ be some fixed integer. Let $\BB_a$ be defined as: $\BB_a := \set {\map {B_\epsilon} a: \epsilon \in \set {\dfrac 1 n: n \in \N, n > k} }$ that is, the set of all open $\epsilon$-balls of $a$ for $\epsilon$ which are reciprocals of integers greater than $k$. Then the $\BB_a$ is a basis for the neighborhood system of $a$.

label: Subset of Ordinal implies Cardinal Inequality
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $x$ be an ordinal such that $S \subseteq x$. Then: $\card S \le \card x$ where $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$.

label: Subset of Ordinals has Minimal Element
snippet: Let $A$ be an ordinal (we shall allow $A$ to be a proper class). Let $B$ be a nonempty subset of $A$. Then $B$ has an $\Epsilon$-minimal element. That is: $\exists x \in B: B \cap x = \O$

label: Subset of Particular Point Space is either Open or Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be any subset of $T$. Then $H$ is either open or closed in $T$. The only sets which are both closed and open in $T$ are $S$ and $\O$.

label: Subset of Partition Space is Open iff Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then $T$ is a partition space : $\forall U \subseteq S: U \in \tau \iff \relcomp S U \in \tau$ That is, a topological space is a partition space : all open sets are closed all closed sets are also open. That is, all open sets and closed sets of a partition space are clopen.

label: Subset of Real Numbers is Interval iff Connected
snippet: Let the real number line $\R$ be considered as a topological space. Let $S$ be a subspace of $\R$. Then $S$ is connected $S$ is an interval of $\R$. That is, the only subspaces of $\R$ that are connected are intervals.

label: Subset of Real Numbers is Path-Connected iff Interval
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as an Euclidean space. Let $S \subseteq \R$ be a subset of $\R$. Then $S$ is a path-connected metric subspace of $\R$ $S$ is a real interval.

label: Subset of Satisfiable Set is Satisfiable
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be an $\mathscr M$-satisfiable set of formulas from $\LL$. Let $\FF'$ be a subset of $\FF$. Then $\FF'$ is also $\mathscr M$-satisfiable.

label: Subset of Set Difference iff Disjoint Set
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq S$ Then: $A \cap T = \O \iff A \subseteq S \setminus T$ where: $A \cap T$ denotes set intersection $\O$ denotes the empty set $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference.

label: Subset of Set is Coarser than Set
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be a preordered set. Let $A, B$ be subset of $S$ such that $A \subseteq B$ Then $A$ is coarser than $B$.

label: Subset of Set with Propositional Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $P: S \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on $S$. Then: $\set {x \in S: \map P x} \subseteq S$

label: Subset of Set with Zero Outer Measure has Zero Outer Measure
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\mu^\ast$ be an outer measure on $X$. Let $B \subseteq X$ be such that $\map {\mu^\ast} B = 0$. Let $A \subseteq B$. Then $\map {\mu^\ast} A = 0$.

label: Subset of Sigma-Locally Finite Set of Subsets is Sigma-Locally Finite
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF \subseteq \powerset S$ be a set of subsets of $S$. Let $\GG \subseteq \FF$. If $\FF$ is $\sigma$-locally finite then $\GG$ is $\sigma$-locally finite.

label: Subset of Standard Discrete Metric Space is Neighborhood of Each Point
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space where $d$ is the standard discrete metric. Let $S \subseteq A$. Let $a \in S$. Then $S$ is a neighborhood of $a$. That is, every subset of $A$ is a neighborhood of each of its points.

label: Subset of Standard Discrete Metric Space is Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a standard discrete metric space. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a subset of $A$. Then $S$ is an open set of $M$.

label: Subset of Totally Ordered Set can be Uniquely Expressed as Partition of Maximal Order-Convex Sets
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$ Then $H$ can be uniquely expressed as a partition whose components are maximally order-convex sets.

label: Subset of Well-Founded Relation is Well-Founded
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $\RR$ be a well-founded relation on $S$. Let $\QQ$ be a subset of $\RR$. Then $\QQ$ is also a well-founded relation on $S$.

label: Subset of Well-Ordered Set is Well-Ordered
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a well-ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\preceq'$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then the relational structure $\struct {T, \preceq'}$ is a well-ordered set.

label: Subset of von Neumann-Bounded Set is von Neumann-Bounded
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $E \subseteq X$ be von Neumann-bounded. Let $F \subseteq X$. Then $F$ is von Neumann-bounded.

label: Subsets Greater Than and Less Than Identity of Ordered Abelian Group are Isomorphic Ordered Semigroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered abelian group whose identity element is $e$. Let $G^+$ and $G^-$ denote the subsets of $G$ defined as: $G^+ = \set {x \in G: e \preccurlyeq x}$ $G^- = \set {x \in G: x \preccurlyeq e}$ Then $\struct {G^+, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ and $\struct {G^-, \circ, \succcurlyeq}$ are subsemigroups of $G$ such that the inversion mapping $\iota: G \to G$ defined as: $\forall g \in G: \map \iota g = g^{-1}$ is: an isomorphism from $\struct {G^+, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ to $\struct {G^-, \circ, \succcurlyeq}$ and: an isomorphism from $\struct {G^-, \circ,…

label: Subsets Satisfy Formulation 1 Matroid Base Axiom Iff Complements Satisfy Formulation 5
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\mathscr B$ be a non-empty set of subsets of $S$. Let $\mathscr B^* = \set{S \setminus B : B \in \mathscr B}$. Then: $\mathscr B$ satisfies formulation $1$ base axiom: $\mathscr B^*$ satisfies formulation $5$ base axiom: {{axiom | n = \text B 5 | q = \forall B^*_1, B^*_2 \in \mathscr B^* | mr= x \in B^*_1 \setminus B^*_2 \implies \exists y \in B^*_2 \setminus B^*_1 : \paren {B^*_2 \setminus \set y} \cup \set x \in \mathscr B }}

label: Subsets Satisfy Formulation 5 Matroid Base Axiom Iff Complements Satisfy Formulation 1
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\mathscr B$ be a non-empty set of subsets of $S$. Let $\mathscr B^* = \set{S \setminus B : B \in \mathscr B}$. Then: $\mathscr B$ satisfies formulation $5$ base axiom: $\mathscr B^*$ satisfies formulation $1$ base axiom: {{axiom | n = \text B 1 | q = \forall B^*_1, B^*_2 \in \mathscr B^* | mr= x \in B^*_1 \setminus B^*_2 \implies \exists y \in B^*_2 \setminus B^*_1 : \paren {B^*_1 \setminus \set x} \cup \set y \in \mathscr B^* }}

label: Subsets in Increasing Union
snippet: Let $S_0, S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_i, \ldots$ be a nested sequence of sets, that is: $S_0 \subseteq S_1 \subseteq S_2 \subseteq \ldots \subseteq S_i \subseteq \ldots$ Let $S$ be the increasing union of $S_0, S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_i, \ldots$: $\ds S = \bigcup_{i \mathop \in \N} S_i$ Then: $\forall s \in S: \exists k \in \N: \forall j \ge k: s \in S_j$

label: Subsets of Equidecomposable Subsets are Equidecomposable
snippet: Let $A, B \subseteq \R^n$ be equidecomposable. Let $S \subseteq A$. Then there exists $T \subseteq B$ such that $S$ and $T$ are equidecomposable.

label: Subspace Topology is Initial Topology with respect to Inclusion Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $Y$ be a non-empty subset of $X$. Let $\iota: Y \to X$ be the inclusion mapping. Let $\tau_Y$ be the initial topology on $Y$ with respect to $\iota$. Then $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ is a topological subspace of $\struct {X, \tau}$. That is: $\tau_Y = \set {U \cap Y: U \in \tau}$

label: Subspace Topology on Initial Topology is Initial Topology on Restrictions
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {\struct {Y_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\family {f_i: X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of mappings indexed by $I$. Let $\tau$ be the initial topology on $X$ with respect to $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ be a topological subspace of $X$. Then $\tau_Y$ is the initial topology on $Y$ with respect to $\family {f_i \restriction_Y}_{i \mathop \in I}$.

label: Subspace of Complete Metric Space is Closed iff Complete
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a complete metric space. Let $\struct {S, d}$ be a subspace of $\struct {M, d}$. Then $S$ is closed $S$ is complete.

label: Subspace of Complete Metric Space is Relatively Compact iff Every Sequence has Cauchy Subsequence
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a complete metric space. Let $\struct {H, d_H}$ be a metric subspace of $\struct {X, d}$. Then $\struct {H, d_H}$ is relatively compact : every sequence in $H$ has a Cauchy subsequence.

label: Subspace of Complete Metric Space is Relatively Compact iff Totally Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a metric space. Let $A \subseteq M$. We have that $A$ is relatively compact in $\struct {M, d}$ $A$ is totally bounded.

label: Subspace of Either-Or Space less Zero is not Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the either-or space. Let $H = S \setminus \set 0$ be the set $S$ without zero. Then the topological subspace $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$ is not a Lindelöf space.

label: Subspace of Euclidean Space is Closed
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be a Euclidean space. Every subspace of $\R^n$ is closed in $\R^n$.

label: Subspace of Finite Complement Topology is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on an infinite set $S$. Then every topological subspace of $T$, including $T$ itself, is a compact space.

label: Subspace of Metric Space is Metric Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$. Let $d_H: H \times H \to \R$ be the restriction $d \restriction_{H \times H}$ of $d$ to $H$. Let $\struct {H, d_H}$ be a metric subspace of $\struct {A, d}$. Then $d_H$ is a metric on $H$.

label: Subspace of Metrizable Space is Metrizable Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a metrizable topological space. Let $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ be a subspace of $\struct{X, \tau}$. Then: $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ is a metrizable topological space

label: Subspace of Product Space has Initial Topology with respect to Restricted Projections
snippet: Let $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\XX$ be the cartesian product of $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$: $\ds \XX := \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ For each $i \in I$, let $\pr_i: \XX \to X_i$ denote the projection of $\XX$ onto $X_i$. Let $Y \subseteq \XX$ be a non-empty subset of $\XX$. For each $i \in I$, let $\pr_i \restriction_Y$ denote the restriction of $\pr_i$ to $Y$. Let $\tau_\XX$ be the product topology on $\XX$. Let $\tau_Y$ be the subspace topology on $Y$.

label: Subspace of Product Space is Homeomorphic to Factor Space
snippet: Let $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\ds \struct {X, \tau} = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} \struct {X_i, \tau_i}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$. Suppose that $X$ is non-empty. Then for each $i \in I$ there is a subspace $Y_i \subseteq X$ which is homeomorphic to $\struct {X_i, \tau_i}$.

label: Subspace of Real Continuous Functions
snippet: Let $\mathbb J = \set {x \in \R: a \le x \le b}$ be a closed interval of the real number line $\R$. Let $\map C {\mathbb J}$ be the set of all continuous real functions on $\mathbb J$. Then $\struct {\map C {\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$ is a subspace of the $\R$-vector space $\struct {\R^{\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$.

label: Subspace of Real Differentiable Functions
snippet: Let $\mathbb J$ be an open interval of the real number line $\R$. Let $\map \DD {\mathbb J}$ be the set of all differentiable real functions on $\mathbb J$. Then $\struct {\map \DD {\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$ is a subspace of the $\R$-vector space $\struct {\R^{\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$.

label: Subspace of Real Functions of Differentiability Class
snippet: Let $\mathbb J = \set {x \in \R: a < x < b}$ be an open interval of the real number line $\R$. Let $\map {C^m} {\mathbb J}$ be the set of all continuous real functions on $\mathbb J$ in differentiability class $m$. Then $\struct {\map {C^m} {\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$ is a subspace of the $\R$-vector space $\struct {\R^{\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$.

label: Subspace of Riemann Integrable Functions
snippet: Let $\mathbb J = \set {x \in \R: a \le x \le b}$ be a closed interval of the real number line $\R$. Let $\map \RR {\mathbb J}$ be the set of all Riemann integrable functions on $\mathbb J$. Then $\struct {\map \RR {\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$ is a subspace of the $\R$-vector space $\struct {\R^{\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$.

label: Subspace of Separable Metric Space is Separable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a separable metric space. Let $\struct {Y, d_Y}$ be a metric subspace of $\struct {X, d}$. Then $Y$ is separable.

label: Subspace of Smooth Real Functions
snippet: == Corollary to Subspace of Real Functions of Differentiability Class == Let $\mathbb J = \set {x \in \R: a < x < b}$ be an open interval of the real number line $\R$. Let $\map {C^\infty} {\mathbb J}$ denote the set of all continuous real functions on $\mathbb J$ which are differentiable on $\mathbb J$ at all orders. Then $\struct {\map {C^\infty} {\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$ is a subspace of the $\R$-vector space $\struct {\R^{\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$.

label: Subspace of Subspace is Subspace
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a non-empty subset of $S$ and $\tau_H$ be the subspace topology on $H$. Let $K \subseteq S$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then the subspace topology on $K$ induced by $\tau$ equals the subspace topology on $K$ induced by $\tau_H$.

label: Substitution of Elements
snippet: Let $a$, $b$, and $x$ be sets. $a = b \implies \paren {a \in x \iff b \in x}$

label: Substitutivity of Class Equality
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Let $\map P A$ be a well-formed formula of the language of set theory. Let $\map P B$ be the same proposition $\map P A$ with all instances of $A$ replaced with instances of $B$. Let $=$ denote class equality. $A = B \implies \paren {\map P A \iff \map P B}$

label: Substitutivity of Equality
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be sets. Let $\map P x$ be a well-formed formula of the language of set theory. Let $\map P y$ be the same proposition $\map P x$ with some (not necessarily all) free instances of $x$ replaced with free instances of $y$. Let $=$ denote set equality. $x = y \implies \paren {\map P x \iff \map P y}$

label: Subtraction has no Identity Element
snippet: The operation of subtraction on numbers of any kind has no identity.

label: Subtraction of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $z_1 := a_1 + i b_1$ and $z_2 := a_2 + i b_2$ be complex numbers. The subtraction operation on $z_1$ and $z_2$ is: $z_1 - z_2 = \paren {a_1 - a_2} + i \paren {b_1 - b_2}$

label: Subtraction on Numbers is Anticommutative
snippet: The operation of subtraction on the numbers is anticommutative. That is: $a - b = b - a \iff a = b$

label: Subtraction on Numbers is Not Associative
snippet: The operation of subtraction on the numbers is not associative. That is, in general: $a - \paren {b - c} \ne \paren {a - b} - c$

label: Successive Solutions of Phi of n equals Phi of n + 2
snippet: Let $\phi$ denote the Euler $\phi$ function. $7$ and $8$ are two successive integers which are solutions to the equation: $\map \phi n = \map \phi {n + 2}$

label: Successor Mapping on Natural Numbers has no Fixed Element
snippet: Let $\N$ denote the set of natural numbers. Then: $\forall n \in \N: n + 1 \ne n$

label: Successor Mapping on Natural Numbers is Progressing
snippet: Let $\omega$ denote the set of natural numbers as defined by the von Neumann construction. Let $s: \omega \to \omega$ denote the successor mapping on $\omega$. Then $s$ is a progressing mapping.

label: Successor Mapping on Ordinals is Strictly Progressing
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Let $s$ denote the successor mapping on $\On$: $\forall \alpha \in \On: \map s \alpha := \alpha \cup \set \alpha$ where $\alpha$ is an ordinal. Then $s$ is a strictly progressing mapping.

label: Successor Set of Ordinal is Ordinal
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Let $\alpha \in \On$ be an ordinal. Then its successor set $\alpha^+ = \alpha \cup \set \alpha$ is also an ordinal.

label: Successor Sets of Linearly Ordered Set Induced by Convex Component Partition
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Let $A$ and $B$ be separated sets of $T$. Let $A^*$ and $B^*$ be defined as: {{eqn | l = A^* | r = \bigcup \set {\closedint a b: a, b \in A, \closedint a b \cap B^- = \O} }} {{eqn | l = B^* | r = \bigcup \set {\closedint a b: a, b \in B, \closedint a b \cap A^- = \O} }} where $A^-$ and $B^-$ denote the closure of $A$ and $B$ in $T$.

label: Successor is Less than Successor
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals and let $x^+$ denote the successor set of $x$. Then, $x \in y \iff x^+ \in y^+$.

label: Successor of Element of Ordinal is Subset
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $x \in y \iff x^+ \subseteq y$

label: Sufficient Condition for Quotient Group by Intersection to be Abelian

label: Sufficient Condition for Vector Equals Inverse iff Zero

label: Sufficient Condition for Weak Convergence of Bounded Sequence in Hilbert Space in terms of Everywhere Dense Set

label: Sufficient Conditions for Basis of Finite Dimensional Vector Space

label: Sum Less Maximum is Minimum
snippet: For all numbers $a, b$ where $a, b$ in $\N, \Z, \Q$ or $\R$: $a + b - \max \set {a, b} = \min \set {a, b}$.

label: Sum Over Divisors of von Mangoldt is Logarithm
snippet: Let $\Lambda$ be von Mangoldt's function. Then for $n \ge 1$: $\ds \sum_{d \mathop \divides n} \map \Lambda d = \ln n$
