label: Tree has Center or Bicenter
snippet: Every tree has either: $(1): \quad$ Exactly one center or: $(2): \quad$ Exactly one bicenter, but never both. That is, every tree is either central or bicentral.

label: Trefoil Knot in Paper forms Pentagon
snippet: Take a strip of paper with parallel edges. Tie a simple trefoil knot in it. Flatten the knot and pull the paper tight. The knot will be in the shape of a regular pentagon. The edges of the paper strip trace out a pentagram. 500px

label: Triangle Angle-Side-Angle Congruence
snippet: If two triangles have: two angles equal to two angles, respectively the sides between the two angles equal then the remaining angles are equal, and the remaining sides equal the respective sides. That is to say, if two pairs of angles and the included sides are equal, then the triangles are congruent.

label: Triangle Conjugacy is Mutual
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle. Let $\triangle PQR$ be a triangle. Let $\triangle P'Q'R'$ be such that: $P'$ is the pole of $QR$ $Q'$ is the pole of $PR$ $R'$ is the pole of $PQ$ $\CC$. Then: $P$ is the pole of $Q'R'$ $Q$ is the pole of $P'R'$ $R$ is the pole of $P'Q'$ $\CC$. That is, $\triangle PQR$ and $\triangle P'Q'R'$ are conjugate triangles $\CC$.

label: Triangle Inequality for Complex Numbers/Corollary 1
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\cmod z$ be the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod {z_1 + z_2} \ge \cmod {z_1} - \cmod {z_2}$

label: Triangle Inequality for Complex Numbers/Corollary 2
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\cmod z$ be the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod {z_1 + z_2} \ge \cmod {\cmod {z_1} - \cmod {z_2} }$

label: Triangle Inequality for Complex Numbers/Corollary 3
snippet: {{refactor|We could (and perhaps should) merge this with Triangle Inequality for Complex Numbers as $\cmod {z_1 \pm z_2} \le \cmod {z_1} + \cmod {z_2}$ (that's how it's done in Abramowitz and Stegun) and make the latter as general as it can be made. Would make it more streamlined as the corollaries can then be collapsed. Same applies to Reverse Triangle Inequality, merge them all together better.}}

label: Triangle Inequality for Conditional Expectation
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $\GG \subseteq \Sigma$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra. Let $X$ be an integrable random variable. Let $\expect {X \mid \GG}$ be a version of the conditional expectation of $X$ given $\GG$. Let $\expect {\size X \mid \GG}$ be a version of the conditional expectation of $\size X$ given $\GG$. Then we have: $\size {\expect {X \mid \GG} } \le \expect {\size X \mid \GG}$ almost everywhere.

label: Triangle Inequality for Generalized Sums
snippet:
Let $V$ be a Banach space. Let $
orm {\,\cdot\,}$ denote the norm on $V$. Let $ amily {v_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed subset of $V$. Let the generalized sum $\ds \sum \set {v_i: i \in I}$ converge absolutely. Then: $(1): \quad \ds 
orm {\sum \set {v_i: i \in I} } \le \sum \set {
orm {v_i}: i \in I}$

label: Triangle Inequality for Indexed Summations
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a,b$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f : \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ denote the standard absolute value. Let $\vert f \vert$ be the absolute value of $f$. Then we have the inequality of indexed summations: $\ds \size {\sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i} \le \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \size {\map f i}$

label: Triangle Inequality for Integrals
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Then: $\ds \size {\int_X f \rd \mu} \le \int_X \size f \rd \mu$

label: Triangle Inequality for Summation over Finite Set
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $f : S \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $\size {\, \cdot\,}$ denote the standard absolute value. Let $\size f$ be the absoute value of $f$. Then we have the inequality of summations on finite sets: $\ds \size {\sum_{s \mathop \in S} \map f s} \le \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \size {\map f s}$

label: Triangle Inequality for Variation of Complex Measure
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be measurable space. Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be two complex measures. Let $\cmod {\mu + 
u}$, $\cmod \mu$ and $\cmod 
u$ be the variation of $\mu + 
u$, $\mu$ and $
u$ respectively. Then: $\cmod {\mu + 
u} \le \cmod \mu + \cmod 
u$

label: Triangle Inequality on Distance from Point to Subset
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$. Then: $\forall x, y \in A: \map d {x, H} \le \map d {x, y} + \map d {y, H}$ where $\map d {x, H}$ denotes the distance between $x$ and $H$.

label: Triangle Right-Angle-Hypotenuse-Side Congruence
snippet: If two right triangles have: their hypotenuses equal another of their respective sides equal they will also have: their third sides equal the remaining two angles equal to their respective remaining angles.

label: Triangle Side-Angle-Angle Congruence
snippet: If two triangles have: two angles equal to two angles, respectively the sides opposite one pair of equal angles equal then the remaining angles are equal, and the remaining sides equal the respective sides. That is to say, if two pairs of angles and a pair of opposite sides are equal, then the triangles are congruent.

label: Triangle Side-Angle-Side Congruence
snippet: If $2$ triangles have: $2$ sides equal to $2$ sides respectively the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal they will also have: their third sides equal the remaining two angles equal to their respective remaining angles, namely, those which the equal sides subtend.

label: Triangle Side-Side-Side Congruence
snippet: Let two triangles have all $3$ sides equal. Then they also have all $3$ angles equal. Thus two triangles whose sides are all equal are themselves congruent.

label: Triangle is Convex Set
snippet: The interior of a triangle embedded in $\R^2$ is a convex set.

label: Triangle is Medial Triangle of Larger Triangle
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. $\triangle ABC$ is the medial triangle of a larger triangle.

label: Triangle is Orthic Triangle of Triangle formed from Excenters
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides are $a$, $b$ and $c$ opposite vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively. Let $I$ be the incenter of $\triangle ABC$. Let $I_a$, $I_b$ and $I_c$ be the excenters of $\triangle ABC$ $a$, $b$ and $c$ respectively. Let $\triangle I_a I_b I_c$ be the triangle whose vertices are those excenters of $I_a$, $I_b$ and $I_c$. Then: $\triangle ABC$ is the orthic triangle of $\triangle I_a I_b I_c$ and: $I$ is the orthocenter of $\triangle I_a I_b I_c$.

label: Triangle is Self-Conjugate to Unique Circle
snippet: Let $\triangle PQR$ be a triangle. Then there exists exactly one circle $\CC$ such that $\triangle PQR$ is self-conjugate with respect to $\CC$.

label: Triangle of Forces
snippet: Let $3$ forces act on a particle. Let the magnitude and direction of these forces be represented by vectors in space such that the magnitude of the forces is proportional to the length of the vectors. Then the forces are in equilibrium the vectors form a triangle. This is known as a triangle of forces.

label: Triangle with Three Right Angles
snippet: == Puzzle == To make a triangle that has $3$ right angles.

label: Triangle with Two Equal Angles is Isosceles
snippet: If a triangle has two angles equal to each other, the sides which subtend the equal angles will also be equal to one another. Hence, by definition, such a triangle will be isosceles.

label: Triangles with Equal Base and Same Height have Equal Area
Triangles with Integer Area and Integer Sides in Arithmetical Sequence
snippet: The triangles with the following sides in arithmetic sequence have integer areas: $3, 4, 5$ $13, 14, 15$ $15, 28, 41$ $15, 26, 37$ Their areas are: $6, 84, 126, 156$

label: Triangles with One Equal Angle and Two Other Sides Proportional are Similar
snippet: Let two triangles be such that one of the angles of one triangle equals one of the angles of the other. Let two corresponding sides which are adjacent to one of the other angles, be proportional. Let the third angle in both triangles be either both acute or both not acute. Then all of the corresponding angles of these triangles are equal. Thus, by definition, such triangles are similar.

label: Trivial Estimate for Cyclotomic Polynomials
snippet: Let $n \ge 1$ be a natural number. Let $\Phi_n$ be the $n$th cyclotomic polynomial. Let $\phi$ be the Euler totient function. Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\size {\size z - 1}^{\map \phi n} \le \size {\map {\Phi_n} z} \le \paren {\size z + 1}^{\map \phi n}$ where: the first inequality becomes an equality only if: $n = 1$ and $z \in \R_{\ge 0}$ or: $n = 2$ and $z \in \R_{\le 0}$ the second inequality becomes an equality only if: $n = 1$ and $z \in \R_{\le 0}$ or: $n = 2$ and $z \in \R_{\ge 0}$

label: Trivial Field Extension is Galois
snippet: Let $F$ be a field. The trivial field extension $F / F$ is Galois.

label: Trivial Gradation is Gradation
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {M, e, \cdot}$ be a monoid. Let $\ds R = \bigoplus_{m \mathop \in M} R_m$ be the trivial $M$-gradation on $R$. This is a gradation on $R$.

label: Trivial Group Action is Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $*: G \times S \to S$ be the trivial group action: $\forall \tuple {g, s} \in G \times S: g * s = s$ Then $*$ is indeed a group action.

label: Trivial Group is Abelian
snippet: The trivial group is an abelian group.

label: Trivial Group is Cyclic Group
snippet: The trivial group is a cyclic group.

label: Trivial Group is Initial Object
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Grp}$ be the category of groups. Let $1 = \set e$ be the trivial group. Then $1$ is an initial object of $\mathbf{Grp}$.

label: Trivial Group is Smallest Group
snippet: Let $G = \struct {\set e, \circ}$ be a trivial group. Then $G$ is the smallest group possible, in that there exists no set with lower cardinality which is the underlying set of a group.

label: Trivial Group is Terminal Object of Category of Groups
snippet: Let $\mathbf {Grp}$ be the category of groups. Let $\set e$ be the trivial group. Then $\set e$ is a terminal object of $\mathbf {Grp}$.

label: Trivial Module is Module
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group whose identity is $e_G$. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \circ_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ be the trivial $R$-module, such that: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: \lambda \ast x = e_G$ Then $\struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ is a module.

label: Trivial Module is Not Unitary
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group whose identity is $e_G$. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \circ_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be the trivial $R$-module, such that: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: \lambda \circ x = e_G$ Then unless $R$ is a ring with unity and $G$ contains only one element, this is not a unitary module.

label: Trivial Ordering is Universally Compatible
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be the trivial ordering on $S$. Then $\RR$ is universally compatible.

label: Trivial Quotient is a Bijection
snippet: Let $\Delta_S$ be the diagonal relation on a set $S$. Let $q_{\Delta_S}: S \to S / \Delta_S$ be the trivial quotient of $S$. Then $q_{\Delta_S}: S \to S / \Delta_S$ is a bijection.

label: Trivial Relation is Equivalence
snippet: The trivial relation on $S$: $\RR = S \times S$ is always an equivalence in $S$.

label: Trivial Relation is Largest Equivalence Relation
snippet: The trivial relation $\TT$ on $S$ is the largest equivalence in $S$, in the sense that: $\forall \EE \subseteq S \times S: \EE \subseteq \TT$ where $\EE$ denotes a general equivalence relation.

label: Trivial Relation is Universally Congruent
snippet: The trivial relation $\RR = S \times S$ on a set $S$ is universally congruent on $S$.

snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a trivial ring. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ is a commutative ring.

Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be a first-countable space. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a first-countable space.

label: Uncountable Product of Second-Countable Spaces is not always Second-Countable
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with uncountable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be a second-countable space. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a second-countable space.

label: Uncountable Product of Separable Spaces is not always Separable
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with uncountable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be a separable space. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a separable space.

label: Uncountable Product of Sequentially Compact Spaces is not always Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with uncountable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be sequentially compact. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also sequentially compact.

label: Uncountable Set less Countable Set is Uncountable
snippet: Let $S$ be an uncountable set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a countable subset of $S$. Then: $S \setminus T$ is uncountable where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

label: Uncountable Subset of Countable Complement Space Intersects Open Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Let $H \subseteq S$ be an uncountable subset of $S$. Then the intersection of $H$ with an arbitrary non-empty open set of $T$ is uncountable.

label: Underlying Set of Topological Space is Clopen
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then the underlying set $S$ of $T$ is both open and closed in $T$.

label: Underlying Set of Topological Space is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then the underlying set $S$ of $T$ is closed in $T$.

label: Underlying Set of Topological Space is Everywhere Dense
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then the underlying set $S$ of $T$ is everywhere dense in $T$.

label: Uniform Absolute Convergence of Infinite Product of Complex Functions
snippet: Let $X$ be a compact metric space. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of continuous functions $X \to \C$. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly absolutely on $X$. Then: $\map f x = \ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + \map {f_n} x}$ converges uniformly absolutely on $X$ $f$ is continuous there exists $n_0 \in \N$ such that $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = n_0}^\infty \paren {1 + \map {f_n} x}$ has no zeroes.

label: Uniform Antiprism is Semiregular Polyhedron
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a uniform antiprism whose bases are specifically not (equilateral) triangles. Then $\PP$ is a semiregular polyhedron.

label: Uniform Continuity on Metric Space does not imply Compactness
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: A_1 \to A_2$ be a uniformly continuous mapping on $A_1$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $M_1$ is a compact metric space.

label: Uniform Contraction Mapping Theorem
snippet: Let $M$ and $N$ be metric spaces. Let $M$ be complete. Let $f : M \times N \to M$ be a continuous uniform contraction. Then for all $t \in N$ there exists a unique $\map g t \in M$ such that $\map f {\map g t, t} = \map g t$, and the mapping $g: N \to M$ is continuous.

label: Uniform Convergence is Hereditary
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of mappings defined on $A$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be uniformly convergent on $S \subseteq A$. Then $\sequence {f_n}$ is uniformly convergent on every metric subspace of $S$. That is, uniform convergence is a hereditary property of a metric space.

label: Uniform Convergence of General Dirichlet Series
snippet: Let $\map \arg z$ denote the argument of the complex number $z \in \C$. Let $\ds \map f s = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n e^{-\map {\lambda_n} s}$ be a general Dirichlet series. Let $\map f s$ converge at $s_0 = \sigma_0 + i t_0$. Then $\map f s$ converges uniformly for all $s$ such that: $\cmod {\map \arg {s - s_0} } \le a < \dfrac \pi 2$

label: Uniform Limit Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d_M}$ and $\struct {N, d_N}$ be metric spaces. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of mappings from $M$ to $N$ such that: $(1): \quad \forall n \in \N: f_n$ is continuous at every point of $M$ $(2): \quad \sequence {f_n}$ converges uniformly to $f$ Then: $f$ is continuous at every point of $M$.

label: Uniform Limit of Analytic Functions is Analytic
snippet: Let $U$ be an open subset of $\C$. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of analytic functions $f_n : U \to \C$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ converge locally uniformly to $f$ on $U$. Then $f$ is analytic.

label: Uniform Limit of Sequence of Continuous Complex-Valued Functions Vanishing at Infinity Vanishes at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of functions $f_n : X \to \C$ that vanishes at infinity. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a function such that: $f_n - f$ is bounded for each $n \in \N$ and: $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in X} \cmod {\map {f_n} x - \map f x} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Then $f$ vanishes at infinity.

label: Uniform Mean Ergodic Theorem
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb F$. Let $U : \HH \to \HH$ be a bounded linear operator such that: $\forall f \in \HH : \norm {\map U f} \le \norm f$ Then for each $f \in \HH$: $\ds \lim_{N - M \mathop \to \infty} \dfrac 1 {N - M} \sum_{n \mathop = M}^{N - 1} \map {U^n} f = \map P f$ i.e.

label: Uniform Prism is Semiregular Polyhedron
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a uniform prism whose bases are specifically not square. Then $\PP$ is a semiregular polyhedron.

label: Uniform Prism is Uniform Polyhedron
snippet: Let $P$ be a uniform prism. Then $P$ is a uniform polyhedron.

label: Uniform Prisms are Countably Infinite
snippet: There are countably infinite different varieties of uniform prisms.

label: Uniform Product of Continuous Functions is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$ be a metric space. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm{\,\cdot\,}}$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded continuous mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. Let the product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly to $f$. Then $f$ is continuous.

label: Uniform Space whose Topology is Metrizable is not necessarily Metrizable
snippet: Let $\UU$ be a uniformity on a set $S$. Let $\struct {\struct {S, \UU}, \tau}$ be the uniform space generated from $\UU$. Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the uniformizable space yielded by $\struct {\struct {S, \UU}, \tau}$. Let $T$ be a metrizable space. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\UU$ is itself a metrizable uniformity.

label: Uniform Tubular Neighborhood Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $S$ be a submanifold of $M$. Suppose $S$ is compact. Then $S$ has a uniform tubular neighborhood in $M$.

label: Uniformity iff Quasiuniformity has Symmetric Basis
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\UU$ be a quasiuniformity on $S$. Then $\UU$ is a uniformity $\UU$ has a symmetric filter basis.

label: Uniformly Absolutely Convergent Product is Uniformly Convergent
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\mathbb K$ be complete. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly absolutely on $X$. Then it converges uniformly.

label: Uniformly Bounded Sequence of Bounded Linear Transformations is Uniformly Equicontinuous
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be normed vector spaces. Let $\map \BB {X, Y}$ be the space of bounded linear transformations $X 	o Y$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map \BB {X, Y} }$ be the norm on $\map \BB {X, Y}$. Let $\sequence {T_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\map \BB {X, Y}$ such that: $\ds \sup_{n \mathop \in \N} 
orm {T_n}_{\map \BB {X, Y} } < \infty$ Then $\sequence {T_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is uniformly equicontinuous.

label: Uniformly Continuous Function Preserves Uniform Convergence
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $M = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $N = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $\sequence {g_n}$ be a sequence of mappings $g_n: X \to A_1$. Let $g_n$ converge to $g$ uniformly on $X$ as $n \to \infty$. Let $f: A_1 \to A_2$ be uniformly continuous on $A_1$. Then the sequence $\sequence {f \circ g_n}$ converges to $g \circ f$ uniformly on $X$ as $n \to \infty$.

label: Uniformly Continuous Function to Complete Metric Space has Unique Continuous Extension to Closure of Domain
snippet: Let $\tuple {X, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\tuple {Y, d'}$ be a complete metric space. Let $A \subseteq X$. Let $f : A \to Y$ be a uniformly continuous function. Then there exists a unique continuous function $g : A^- \to Y$ such that: $\map g a = \map f a$ for all $a \in A$, where $A^-$ denotes the topological closure of $A$. Furthermore, $g$ is uniformly continuous.

label: Uniformly Continuous Semigroup Bounded on Compact Intervals
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\family {\map T t}_{t \ge 0}$ be a uniformly continuous semigroup. Let $\struct {\map B X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B X} }$ be the space of bounded linear transformations equipped with the canonical norm. Let $T > 0$ be a real number. Then there exists $M > 0$ such that: $\norm {\map T t}_{\map B X} \le M$ for $t \in \closedint 0 T$.

label: Uniformly Convergent Product Satisfies Uniform Cauchy Criterion
snippet: Let $X$ be a compact topological space. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of continuous mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly on $X$. Then $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ satisfies the uniform Cauchy condition for products.

label: Uniformly Convergent Sequence Evaluated on Convergent Sequence
snippet: Let $X = \struct {A, d_X}$ and $Y = \struct {B, d_Y}$ be metric spaces. Let $K$ be a subspace of $X$. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping. Let $\FF = \sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of continuous mappings $f_n: X \to Y$ that converges to $f$ uniformly on $K$. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a convergent sequence in $K$ with limit $a \in K$. Then the sequence $\sequence {\map {f_n} {a_n} }$ is convergent such that: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {f_n} {a_n} = \map f a$

label: Uniformly Convergent Sequence Multiplied with Function
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $V$ be a normed vector space over $\mathbb K$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of mappings $f_n: X \to V$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be uniformly convergent. Let $g: X \to \mathbb K$ be bounded. Then $\sequence {f_n g}$ is uniformly convergent.

label: Uniformly Convergent Sequence of Bounded Functions is Uniformly Bounded
snippet: Let $X = \left({A, d}\right)$ and $Y = \left({B, \rho}\right)$ be metric spaces. Let $\left \langle{f_i}\right \rangle_{i \in I}$ be a uniformly convergent sequence of mappings $f_i: X \to Y$. $\forall i \in I$, let $f_i$ be bounded. Then $\left \langle{f_i}\right \rangle$ is uniformly bounded.

label: Uniformly Convergent Sequence of Continuous Functions Converges to Continuous Function
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \R$. Let $x \in S$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions $S \to \R$ converging uniformly to $f: S \to \R$. Let $f_n$ be continuous at $x$ for all $n \in \N$. Then $f$ is continuous at $x$.

label: Uniformly Convergent Sequence of Continuous Functions is Pointwise Equicontinuous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d_X}$ and $\struct {Y, d_Y}$ be metric spaces. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous function. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of continuous functions converging uniformly to $f$. Then $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is pointwise equicontinuous.

label: Uniformly Convergent Sequence on Dense Subset
snippet: Let $X$ be a metric space. Let $Y \subset X$ be dense. Let $V$ be a Banach space. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of continuous mappings $f_n : X\to V$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be uniformly convergent on $Y$. Then $\sequence {f_n}$ is uniformly convergent on $X$.

label: Uniformly Convergent Series of Continuous Functions Converges to Continuous Function
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \R$. Let $x \in S$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions. Let $f_n$ be continuous at $x$ for all $n \in \N$. Let the infinite series: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ be uniformly convergent to a real function $f : S \to \R$. Then $f$ is continuous at $x$.

label: Uniformly Convergent Series of Continuous Functions is Continuous
snippet: Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions. Let each of $\sequence {f_n}$ be continuous on the interval $\hointr a b$. Let the series: $\ds \map f x := \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map {f_n} x$ be uniformly convergent for all $x \in \closedint a b$. {{explain|Is $f$ really defined at $xb$? What are the domains of $\sequence {f_n}$?}} Then $f$ is continuous on $\hointr a b$.

label: Uniformly Convergent iff Difference Under Supremum Metric Vanishes
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {Y, d}$ be a metric space. Let $S$ be the set of all bounded mappings from $X$ to $Y$. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $S$. Let $f \in S$. Let $d_S: S \times S \to Y$ denote the supremum metric on $S$. Then: $\sequence {f_n}$ converges uniformly to $f$ on $S$ $\map {d_S} {f_n, f} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

label: Uniformly Normal Neighborhood Lemma
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $U \subseteq M$ be a neighborhood of $p \in M$. Then there is a uniformly normal subset which is a neighborhood of $p \in M$ and is contained in $U$.

label: Union Distributes over Intersection
snippet: Set union is distributive over set intersection: $R \cup \paren {S \cap T} = \paren {R \cup S} \cap \paren {R \cup T}$

label: Union Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Union Mappings ==

label: Union Operation on Supersets of Subset is Closed
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a given subset of $S$. Let $\powerset S$ denote the power set of $S$ Let $\mathscr S$ be the subset of $\powerset S$ defined as: $\mathscr S = \set {Y \in \powerset S: T \subseteq Y}$ Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\mathscr S, \cup}$ is closed.

label: Union as Symmetric Difference with Intersection
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Then: $A \cup B = \paren {A \symdif B} \symdif \paren {A \cap B}$ where: $A \cup B$ denotes set union $A \cap B$ denotes set intersection $A \symdif B$ denotes set symmetric difference

label: Union equals Intersection iff Sets are Equal
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \cup T = S} \land \paren {S \cap T = S} \iff S = T$ where: $S \cup T$ denotes set union $S \cap T$ denotes set intersection.

label: Union from Synthetic Basis is Topology
snippet: Let $\BB$ be a synthetic basis on a set $X$. Let $\ds \tau = \set {\bigcup \AA: \AA \subseteq \BB}$. Then $\tau$ is a topology on $X$.

label: Union is Commutative
snippet: Set union is commutative: $S \cup T = T \cup S$

label: Union is Dominated by Disjoint Union
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. For all $i \in I$, let $S_i$ be a set. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} S_i \preccurlyeq \bigsqcup_{i \mathop \in I} S_i$ where $\preccurlyeq$ denotes domination, $\bigcup$ denotes union, and $\bigsqcup$ denotes disjoint union.

label: Union is Empty iff Sets are Empty
snippet: If the union of two sets is the empty set, then both are themselves empty: $S \cup T = \O \iff S = \O \land T = \O$

label: Union is Increasing
snippet: Let $U$ be a set. Let $\FF$ and $\GG$ be sets of subsets of $U$. Then $\FF \subseteq \GG \implies \bigcup \FF \subseteq \bigcup \GG$. That is, $\bigcup$ is an increasing mapping from $\struct {\powerset {\powerset U}, \subseteq}$ to $\struct {\powerset U, \subseteq}$, where $\powerset U$ is the power set of $U$.

label: Union is Increasing Sequence of Sets
snippet: Let $\sequence {D_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets. Then: the sequence $\ds \sequence {\bigcup_{k \mathop = 1}^n D_k}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is increasing.

label: Union is Smallest Superset
snippet: Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be sets. Then $S_1 \cup S_2$ is the smallest set containing both $S_1$ and $S_2$. That is: $\paren {S_1 \subseteq T} \land \paren {S_2 \subseteq T} \iff \paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \subseteq T$

label: Union of Adjacent Open Intervals is Locally Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be the union of adjacent open intervals: $S = \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ where: $a, b, c \in \R: a < b < c$. $\tau_S$ is the subspace topology induced on $S$ by the usual topology $\tau_d$ on the real numbers $\R$. Then $T$ is locally injectively path-connected.

label: Union of Adjacent Open Intervals is Locally Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be the union of adjacent open intervals: $S = \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ where: $a, b, c \in \R: a < b < c$. $\tau_S$ is the subspace topology induced on $S$ by the usual topology $\tau_d$ on the real numbers $\R$. Then $T$ is locally path-connected.

label: Union of Adjacent Open Intervals is not Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be the union of adjacent open intervals: $S = \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ where: $a, b, c \in \R: a < b < c$. $\tau_S$ is the subspace topology induced on $S$ by the usual topology $\tau_d$ on the real numbers $\R$. Then $T$ is not injectively path-connected.

label: Union of Adjacent Open Intervals is not Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be the union of adjacent open intervals: $S = \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ where: $a, b, c \in \R: a < b < c$. $\tau_S$ is the subspace topology induced on $S$ by the usual topology $\tau_d$ on the real numbers $\R$. Then $T$ is not path-connected.

label: Union of Antisymmetric Relation with Inverse is Antisymmetric iff Diagonal
snippet: Let $\RR$ be an antisymmetric relation on a set $S$. Then: $\RR \cup \RR^{-1}$ is antisymmetric $\RR = \Delta_S$ where: $\RR^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $\RR$ $\Delta_S$ denotes the diagonal relation $\cup$ denotes set union.

label: Union of Balanced Sets in Vector Space is Balanced
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\sequence {E_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of balanced subsets of $X$. Then: $\ds E = \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} E_\alpha$ is balanced.

label: Union of Bijections with Disjoint Domains and Codomains is Bijection
snippet: Let $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ be sets or classes. Let $A \cap B = C \cap D = \O$. Let $f: A \to C$ and $g: B \to D$ be bijections. Then $f \cup g: A \cup B \to C \cup D$ is also a bijection.

label: Union of Blocks is Set of Points
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \BB}$ be a pairwise balanced design. That is, let $\struct {X, \BB}$ be a design, with $\size X \ge 2$, and the number of occurrences of each pair of distinct points in $\BB$ be $\lambda$ for some $\lambda > 0$ constant. Then the set union of all the subset elements in $\BB$ is precisely $X$.

label: Union of Boundaries
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\partial A \cup \partial B = \map \partial {A \cup B} \cup \map \partial {A \cap B} \cup \paren {\partial A \cap \partial B}$ where $\partial A$ denotes the boundary of $A$.

label: Union of Bounded Above Real Subsets is Bounded Above
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers. Let $A$ and $B$ be bounded above. Then $A \cup B$ is also bounded above.

label: Union of Bounded Below Real Subsets is Bounded Below
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers. Let $A$ and $B$ be bounded below. Then $A \cup B$ is also bounded below.

label: Union of Chain in Set of Finite Character with Countable Union is Maximal Element
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of sets of finite character. Let its union $\ds \bigcup S$ be countable. Then $\ds \bigcup S$ is a maximal element of $S$ under the subset relation.

label: Union of Chain of Convex Sets in Vector Space is Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $\Gamma$ be a chain of convex sets. Let: $\ds C = \bigcup \Gamma$ Then $C$ is convex.

label: Union of Chain of Orderings is Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $C$ be a non-empty chain of orderings on $S$. Then $\bigcup C$ is an ordering on $S$.

label: Union of Chain of Proper Ideals is Proper Ideal
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $\struct {P, \subseteq}$ be the ordered set consisting of all ideals of $R$, ordered by inclusion. Let $\sequence {I_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ be a non-empty chain of proper ideals in $P$. Let $\ds I = \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in A} I_\alpha$ be their union. Then $I$ is a proper ideal of $R$.

label: Union of Chain of Submodules is Submodule
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let $\NN$ be a chain of submodules with respect to inclusion. Let: $N = \bigcup \NN$ Then $N$ is a submodule of $M$.

label: Union of Closed Intervals of Positive Reals is Set of Positive Reals
snippet: Let $\R_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive real numbers. For all $x \in \R_{> 0}$, let $B_x$ be the closed real interval $\closedint 0 x$. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{x \mathop \in \R_{>0} } B_x = \R_{\ge 0}$

label: Union of Closed Locally Finite Set of Subsets is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF$ be a closed locally finite set of subsets of $T$. Let $E = \ds \bigcup \FF$. Then: $E$ is closed in $T$.

label: Union of Closure with Closure of Complement is Whole Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $H^-$ denote the closure of $H$ in $T$. Let $S \setminus H$ denote the complement of $H$ relative to $S$. Then: $H^- \cup \paren {S \setminus H}^- = S$

label: Union of Closures of Elements of Locally Finite Set is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\AA$ be a locally finite set of subsets of $T$. Then: $\ds \paren {\bigcup \AA}^- = \bigcup \set{A^- : A \in \AA}$ where $A^-$ denotes the closure of $A$ in $T$.

label: Union of Closures of Singleton Rationals is Rational Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the usual (Euclidean) topology $\tau_d$. Let $B_\alpha$ denote the singleton containing the rational number $\alpha$. Then the union of the closures in the set of real numbers $\R$ of all $B_\alpha$ is $\Q$: $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in \Q} \map \cl {B_\alpha} = \Q$

label: Union of Conjugacy Classes is Normal
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H \le G$. Then $H$ is normal in $G$ $H$ is a union of conjugacy classes of $G$.

label: Union of Connected Sets with Common Point is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ be a family of connected sets of $T$. Let $\exists x \in \ds \bigcap \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$. Then $\ds \bigcup \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ is a connected set of $T$.

label: Union of Connected Sets with Non-Empty Intersections is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\AA = \family {A_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of subsets of $S$, all connected in $T$. Let $\AA$ be such that no two of its elements are disjoint: $\forall B, C \in \AA: B \cap C \ne \O$ Then $\ds \bigcup \AA$ is itself connected.

label: Union of Countable Sets of Sets
snippet: Let $\AA$ and $\BB$ be countable sets of sets. Then: $\set {A \cup B: A \in \AA, B \in \BB}$ is also countable.

label: Union of Derivatives is Subset of Derivative of Union
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let: $\FF \subseteq \powerset S$ be a set of subsets of $S$ where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{A \mathop \in \FF} A' \subseteq \paren {\bigcup_{A \mathop \in \FF} A}'$ where $A'$ denotes the derivative of $A$.

label: Union of Disjoint Singletons is Doubleton
snippet: Let $\set a$ and $\set b$ be singletons such that $a \ne b$. Then: $\set a \cup \set b = \set {a, b}$

label: Union of Doubleton
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be sets. Let $\set {x, y}$ be a doubleton. Then $\bigcup \set {x, y}$ is a set such that: $\bigcup \set {x, y} = x \cup y$

label: Union of Elements of Power Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then: $\ds S = \bigcup_{X \mathop \in \powerset S} X$ where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$.

label: Union of Empty Set
snippet: Consider the set of sets $\mathbb S$ such that $\mathbb S$ is the empty set $\O$. Then the union of $\mathbb S$ is $\O$: $\mathbb S = \O \implies \bigcup \mathbb S = \O$

label: Union of Equivalence Classes is Whole Set
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an equivalence on a set $S$. Then the set of $\RR$-classes constitutes the whole of $S$.

label: Union of Equivalences
snippet: The union of two equivalence relations is not necessarily an equivalence relation itself.

label: Union of Event with Complement is Certainty
snippet: Let the probability space of an experiment $\EE$ be $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $A \in \Sigma$ be an events of $\EE$, so that $A \subseteq \Omega$. Then the union of $A$ with its complementary event can be evaluated as: $A \cup \overline A = \Omega$ where $\overline A$ denotes the complementary event to $A$. That is: $A \cup \overline A$ is a certainty or: $\map \Pr {A \cup \overline A} = 1$

label: Union of Events/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Unions of Events ==

label: Union of Family/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Unions of Families ==

label: Union of Filtered Sets is Filtered
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a preordered set. Let $A$ be a set of subsets of $S$ such that $\forall X \in A: X$ is filtered and $\forall X, Y \in A: \exists Z \in A: X \cup Y \subseteq Z$ Then: $\bigcup A$ is also filtered.

label: Union of Finite Sets is Finite
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. Then $S \cup T$ is a finite set.

label: Union of Functions Theorem
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\sequence {X_i: i \in \N}$ be an exhausting sequence of sets on $X$. For each $i \in \N$, let $g_i: X_i \to Y$ be a mapping such that: $g_{i + 1} \restriction X_i = g_i$ where $g_{i + 1} \restriction X_i$ denotes the restriction of $g_{i + 1}$ to $g_i$. Then: $\ds \bigcup \set {g_i: i \in \N}$ is a mapping from $X$ to $Y$.

label: Union of Horizontal Sections is Horizontal Section of Union
snippet: Let $X$, $Y$ and $A$ be sets. Let $\set {E_\alpha : \alpha \in A}$ be a set of subsets of $X \times Y$. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in A} E_\alpha}^y = \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in A} \paren {E_\alpha}^y$ where: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in A} E_\alpha}^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in A} E_\alpha$ $\paren {E_\alpha}^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $E_\alpha$.

label: Union of Image of Convergent Sequence and Limit in Topological Space is Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a convergent sequence such that: $x_n \to x$ Then: $\ds \set {x_n : n \in \N} \cup \set x$ is compact.

label: Union of Indexed Family of Sets Equal to Union of Disjoint Sets
snippet: Let $\family {E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a countable indexed family of sets where at least two $E_n$ are distinct. Then there exists a countable indexed family of disjoint sets $\family {F_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ defined by: $\ds F_k = E_k \setminus \paren {\bigcup_{j \mathop = 0}^{k \mathop - 1} E_j}$ satisfying: $\ds \bigsqcup_{n \mathop \in \N} F_n = \bigcup_{n \mathop \in \N} E_n$ where $\bigsqcup$ denotes disjoint union.

label: Union of Initial Segments is Initial Segment or All of Woset
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \preccurlyeq}$ be a well-ordered non-empty set. Let $A \subseteq X$. Let: $\ds J = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in A} S_x$ be a union of initial segments defined by the elements of $A$. Then either: $J = X$ or: $J$ is an initial segment of $X$.

label: Union of Interiors and Boundary Equals Whole Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A$ be a subset of $T$. Then: $S = \Int A \cup \partial A \cup \Int {A'}$ where: $A' = S \setminus A$ denotes the complement of $A$ relative to $S$ $\Int A$ denotes the interior of $A$ $\partial A$ denotes the boundary of $A$.

label: Union of Interiors is Subset of Interior of Union
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $\H$ be a set of subsets of $T$. That is, let $\H \subseteq \powerset T$ where $\powerset T$ is the power set of $T$. Then the union of the interiors of the elements of $\H$ is a subset of the interior of the union of $\H$: $\ds \bigcup_{H \mathop \in \H} H^\circ \subseteq \paren {\bigcup_{H \mathop \in \H} H}^\circ $

label: Union of Intersections of 2 from 3 equals Intersection of Unions of 2 from 3
snippet: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be sets. Then: $\paren {A \cap B} \cup \paren {B \cap C} \cup \paren {C \cap A} = \paren {A \cup B} \cap \paren {B \cup C} \cap \paren {C \cup A}$

label: Union of Left-Total Relations is Left-Total
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be sets or classes. Let $\RR_1 \subseteq S_1 \times T_1$ and $\RR_2 \subseteq S_2 \times T_2$ be left-total relations. Then $\RR_1 \cup \RR_2$ is left-total.

label: Union of Local Bases is Basis
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. For each $x \in X$, let $\BB_x$ be a local basis at $x$ which consists entirely of open sets. Then $\ds \BB = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in X} \BB_x$ is a basis for the topology $\tau$.

label: Union of Many-to-One Relations with Disjoint Domains is Many-to-One
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be sets or classes. Let $\RR_1$ be a many-to-one relation on $S_1 \times T_1$. Let $\RR_2$ be a many-to-one relation on $S_2 \times T_2$. Suppose that the domains of $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$ are disjoint. Then $\RR_1 \cup \RR_2$ is a many-to-one relation on $\paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \times \paren {T_1 \cup T_2}$.

label: Union of Mappings which Agree is Mapping
snippet: Let $A, B, Y$ be sets. Let $f: A \to Y$ and $g: B \to Y$ be mappings. Let $X = A \cup B$. Let $f$ and $g$ agree on $A \cap B$. Then $f \cup g: X \to Y$ is a mapping.

label: Union of Mappings with Disjoint Domains is Mapping
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be sets. Let $f: S_1 \to T_1$ and $g: S_2 \to T_2$ be mappings. Let $h = f \cup g$ be their union. If $S_1 \cap S_2 = \O$, then $h: S_1 \cup S_2 \to T_1 \cup T_2$ is a mapping whose domain is $S_1 \cup S_2$.

label: Union of Meager Sets is Meager Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A$ and $B$ be meager in $T$. Then $A \cup B$ is meager in $T$.

label: Union of Nest of Mappings is Mapping
snippet: Let $N$ be a nest of mappings. Then: $\bigcup N$ is a mapping where $\bigcup N$ denotes the union of $N$.

label: Union of Non-Disjoint Bounded Subsets of Metric Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $B$ and $C$ be bounded subsets of $M$ such that $B \cap C \ne \O$. Let $\map \diam B$ and $\map \diam C$ denote the diameters of $B$ and $C$. Then $B \cup C$ is a bounded subset of $M$ such that: $\map \diam {B \cup C} \le \map \diam B + \map \diam C$

label: Union of One-to-Many Relations with Disjoint Images is One-to-Many
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be sets or classes. Let $\RR_1$ be a one-to-many relation on $S_1 \times T_1$. Let $\RR_2$ be a one-to-many relation on $S_2 \times T_2$. Suppose that the images of $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$ are disjoint. Then $\RR_1 \cup \RR_2$ is a one-to-many relation on $\paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \times \paren {T_1 \cup T_2}$.

label: Union of Open Intervals of Positive Reals is Set of Strictly Positive Reals
snippet: Let $\R_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive real numbers. For all $x \in \R_{>0}$, let $A_x$ be the open real interval $\openint 0 x$. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{x \mathop \in \R_{>0} } A_x = \R_{>0}$

label: Union of Open Sets Not in System of Open Neighborhoods is Complement of Singleton Closure
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $\map \UU x$ denote the system of open neighborhoods of $x$. Let $\set x^-$ denote the topological closure of $\set x$. Then: $\bigcup \set{U \in \tau : U \notin \map \UU x} = S \setminus \set x^-$

label: Union of Open Sets of Metric Space is Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. The union of a set of open sets of $M$ is open in $M$.

label: Union of Open Sets of Normed Vector Space is Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. The union of a set of open sets of $M$ is open in $M$.

label: Union of Orderings is not necessarily Ordering
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be orderings on $A$. Then $\RR \cup \SS$ is not necessarily an ordering on $A$.

label: Union of Ordinal is Subset of Itself
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. Then: $\bigcup \alpha \subseteq \alpha$ where $\bigcup \alpha$ denotes the union of $\alpha$.

label: Union of Ordinals is Least Upper Bound
snippet: Let $A \subset \On$. That is, let $A$ be a class of ordinals (every member of $A$ is an ordinal). Then $\bigcup A$, the union of $A$, is the least upper bound of $A$: $\ds \forall x \in A: x \le A$ $\ds \forall y \in A: y \le x \implies \bigcup A \le x$

label: Union of Overlapping Order-Convex Sets in Toset is Order-Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $U$ and $V$ be order-convex sets in $S$. Let $U \cap V \ne \O$. Then $U \cup V$ is also order-convex.

label: Union of Path-Connected Sets with Common Point is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ be a family of path-connected sets of $T$. Let $\exists x \in \ds \bigcap \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$. Then $\ds \bigcup \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ is a path-connected set of $T$.

label: Union of Power Sets
snippet: The union of the power sets of two sets $S$ and $T$ is a subset of the power set of their union: $\powerset S \cup \powerset T \subseteq \powerset {S \cup T}$

label: Union of Power Sets not always Equal to Powerset of Union
snippet: The union of the power sets of two sets $S$ and $T$ is not necessarily equal to the power set of their union.

label: Union of Primitive Recursive Sets
snippet: Let $A, B \subseteq \N$ be subsets of the set of natural numbers $\N$. Let $A$ and $B$ both be primitive recursive. Then $A \cup B$, the union of $A$ and $B$, is primitive recursive.

label: Union of Recursively Enumerable Sets
snippet: Let $S, T \subseteq \N$ be recursively enumerable sets. Then $S \cup T$ is recursively enumerable.

label: Union of Regular Open Sets is not necessarily Regular Open
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $U$ and $V$ be regular open sets of $T$. Then $U \cup V$ is not also necessarily a regular open set of $T$.

label: Union of Relation with Inverse is Symmetric Relation
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Let $\RR^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $\RR$. Then $\RR \cup \RR^{-1}$, the union of $\RR$ with $\RR^{-1}$, is symmetric.

label: Union of Relations is Relation
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\FF$ be a family of relations from $S$ to $T$. Let $\ds \RR = \bigcup \FF$, the union of all the elements of $\FF$. Then $\RR$ is a relation from $S$ to $T$.

label: Union of Relative Complements of Nested Subsets
snippet: Let $R \subseteq S \subseteq T$ be sets with the indicated inclusions. Then: $\relcomp T S \cup \relcomp S R = \relcomp T R$ where $\complement$ denotes relative complement. Phrased via Set Difference as Intersection with Relative Complement: $\paren {T \setminus S} \cup \paren {S \setminus R} = T \setminus R$ where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

label: Union of Right-Total Relations is Right-Total
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be sets or classes. Let $\RR_1 \subseteq S_1 \times T_1$ and $\RR_2 \subseteq S_2 \times T_2$ be right-total relations. Then $\RR_1 \cup \RR_2$ is right-total.

label: Union of Set of Dense-in-itself Sets is Dense-in-itself
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $\FF \subseteq \powerset T$ such that: every element of $\FF$ is dense-in-itself. Then the union $\bigcup \FF$ is also dense-in-itself.

label: Union of Set of Ordinals is Ordinal
snippet: Let $A$ be a set of ordinals. Then $\bigcup A$ is an ordinal.

label: Union of Set of Sets when a Set Intersects All
snippet: Let $F$ be a set of sets. Let $S$ be a set or class. Suppose that: $\forall A \in F: A \cap S \ne \O$ Then: $\ds F = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in S} \set {A \in F: x \in A}$

label: Union of Set of Singletons
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T = \set {\set x: x \in S}$ be the set of all singletons of elements of $S$. Then: $\ds \bigcup T = S$ where $\ds \bigcup T$ denotes the union of $T$.

label: Union of Sigma-Algebras may not be Sigma-Algebra
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {X, \Sigma_1}$ and $\struct {X, \Sigma_2}$ be $\sigma$-algebras. Then $\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_2$ may not be a $\sigma$-algebra on $X$.

label: Union of Simply Connected Sets with Path-Connected Intersection is Simply Connected
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \tau}$ be a topological space. Consider all subsets of $T$ as subspaces, equipped with the subspace topology induced by $\tau$. Let $U$ and $V$ be open subsets of $T$ that are simply connected. Let $U \cap V$ be non-empty and path-connected. Let $U \cup V = T$. Then $\struct {T, \tau}$ is simply connected.

label: Union of Singleton
snippet: Consider the set of sets $A$ such that $A$ consists of just one set $x$: $A = \set x$ Then the union of $A$ is $x$: $\bigcup A = x$

label: Union of Slowly Well-Ordered Class under Subset Relation is Well-Orderable
snippet: Let $N$ be a class. Let $N$ be slowly well-ordered under the subset relation. Then $\bigcup N$ is well-orderable.

label: Union of Subset of Family is Subset of Union of Family
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {A_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of subsets of a set $S$. Let $J \subseteq I$ Then: $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in J} A_\alpha \subseteq \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} A_\alpha$ where $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} A_\alpha$ denotes the union of $\family {A_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$.

label: Union of Subsets is Subset
snippet: Let $S_1$, $S_2$, and $T$ be sets. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ both be subsets of $T$. Then: $S_1 \cup S_2 \subseteq T$ That is: $\paren {S_1 \subseteq T} \land \paren {S_2 \subseteq T} \implies \paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \subseteq T$

label: Union of Successor Ordinal
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $x^+$ denote the successor of $x$. Then: $\map \bigcup {x^+} = x$

label: Union of Symmetric Differences
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {R \symdif S} \cup \paren {S \symdif T} = \paren {R \cup S \cup T} \setminus \paren {R \cap S \cap T}$ where $R \symdif S$ denotes the symmetric difference between $R$ and $S$.

label: Union of Topologies is not necessarily Topology
snippet: Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be topologies on a set $S$. Then $\tau_1 \cup \tau_2$ is not necessarily also a topology on $S$.

label: Union of Topologies on Singleton or Doubleton is Topology
snippet: Let $S$ be a set which is either a singleton or a doubleton. Let $\family {\tau_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an arbitrary non-empty indexed set of topologies on $S$. Then $\tau := \ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} {\tau_i}$ is also a topology on $S$.

label: Union of Total Ordering with Lower Sections is Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {Y, \preceq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $X$ be the disjoint union of $Y$ with the set of lower sections of $Y$. Define a relation $\preceq'$ on $X$ extending $\preceq$ by letting: $y_1 \preceq' y_2 \iff y_1 \preceq y_2$ $y \preceq' L \iff y \in L$ $L_1 \preceq' L_2 \iff L_1 \subseteq L_2$ $L \preceq' y \iff y \in Y \setminus L$ Then $\preceq'$ is a total ordering.

label: Union of Turing Machines
snippet: Let $T_1, T_2$ be Turing machines. Let $\Sigma_1, \Sigma_2$ be the input symbols of $T_1, T_2$, respectively. Let $L_1, L_2$ be the languages accepted by $T_1, T_2$, respectively. There exists a Turing machine $T$ such that: The input symbols of $T$ are $\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_2$. The language accepted by $T$ is $L_1 \cup L_2$. $T$ halts on some input it is in the accepted language, or both $T_1$ and $T_2$ halt on it.

label: Union of Two Compact Sets is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological spaces. Let $H$ and $K$ be compact subsets of $T$. Then $H \cup K$ is compact in $T$.

label: Union of Union of Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets such that $A \ne \O$ and $B \ne \O$. Let the ordered pair $\tuple {a, b}$ be defined using the Kuratowski formalization: $\tuple {a, b} := \set {\set a, \set {a, b} }$ Then: $\ds \bigcup \bigcup \paren {A \times B} = A \cup B$ where: $\cup$ denotes union $\times$ denotes Cartesian product.

label: Union of Union of Cartesian Product with Empty Factor
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets such that either $A = \O$ or $B = \O$. Let the ordered pair $\tuple {a, b}$ be defined using the Kuratowski formalization: $\tuple {a, b} := \set {\set a, \set {a, b} }$ Then: $\ds \bigcup \bigcup \paren {A \times B} = A \cup B \iff A = B = \O$ where: $\cup$ denotes union $\times$ denotes Cartesian product. That is, if either $A$ or $B$ is empty: $\ds \bigcup \bigcup \paren {A \times B} = A \cup B$ holds they are both empty

label: Union of Upper Sections is Upper
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a preordered set. Let $A$ be a set of subsets of $S$ such that: $\forall X \in A: X$ is an upper section. Then: $\bigcup A$ is also an upper section.

label: Union of Vertical Sections is Vertical Section of Union
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $\set {E_\alpha : \alpha \in A}$ be a set of subsets of $X \times Y$. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \in A} E_\alpha}_x = \bigcup_{\alpha \in A} \paren {E_\alpha}_x$ where: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \in A} E_\alpha}_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \in A} E_\alpha$ $\paren {E_\alpha}_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $E_\alpha$.

label: Union of g-Tower is Greatest Element and Unique Fixed Point
snippet: Let $M$ be a set. Let $g: M \to M$ be a progressing mapping on $M$. Let $M$ be a $g$-tower. Then: $\ds \bigcup M \in M$ $\ds \bigcup M$ is the greatest element (under the subset relation) of $M$ $\ds \bigcup M$ is the unique fixed point of $M$.

label: Union with Complement
snippet: The union of a set and its complement is the universal set: $S \cup \map \complement S = \mathbb U$

label: Union with Empty Set
snippet: The union of any set with the empty set is the set itself: $S \cup \O = S$

label: Union with Intersection equals Intersection with Union iff Subset
snippet: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be sets. Then: $\paren {A \cap B} \cup C = A \cap \paren {B \cup C} \iff C \subseteq A$

label: Union with Relative Complement
snippet: The union of a set $T$ and its relative complement in $S$ is the set $S$: $\relcomp S T \cup T = S$

label: Union with Superset is Superset
snippet: $S \subseteq T \iff S \cup T = T$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $S \cup T$ denotes the union of $S$ and $T$.

label: Union with Universal Set
snippet: The union of a set with the universal set is the universal set: $\mathbb U \cup S = \mathbb U$

label: Unique Accumulation Point of Sequence in Weakly Countably Compact Subset of Banach Space is Limit of Sequence
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be countably compact in $\struct {X, w}$. Let $x \in X$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $A$ such that: $x$ is the unique accumulation point of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ in $\struct {X, w}$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges weakly to $x$.

label: Unique Code for URM Instruction
snippet: Each basic instruction $I$ in a URM Program can be identified with a unique code number $\beta \left({I}\right)$. We also define the following sets: $\operatorname{Zinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Zero instructions $\operatorname{Sinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Successor instructions $\operatorname{Cinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Copy instructions $\operatorname{Jinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Jump instructions. Then we define $\operatorname{Instr}$ to be the set of codes of all basic URM instructions.

label: Unique Code for URM Program
snippet: Any URM program can be assigned a unique code number.

label: Unique Constant in Category of Monoids
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Mon}$ be the category of monoids. Then every object $M$ of $\mathbf{Mon}$ has precisely one constant.

label: Unique Epimorphism from Quotient Group to Quotient Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G_1, \circledcirc}$ and $\struct {G_2, \circledast}$ be groups. Let $\phi: \struct {G_1, \circledcirc} \to \struct {G_2, \circledast}$ be a group epimorphism. Let $K$ be the kernel of $\phi$. Let $H_1$ be a normal subgroup of $\struct {G_1, \circledcirc}$. Let $H_2 := \phi \sqbrk {H_1}$ be the image of $H_1$ under $\phi$.

label: Unique Factorization Theorem for Gaussian Integers
snippet: The ring of Gaussian integers: $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ forms a unique factorization domain. That is, every Gaussian integer can be expressed as the product of one or more Gaussian primes, uniquely up to the order in which they appear.

label: Unique Integer Close to Rational in Valuation Ring of P-adic Norm
snippet:
Let $
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rationals $\Q$ for some prime number $p$. Let $x \in \Q$ such that $
orm{x}_p \le 1$. Then for all $i \in \N$ there exists a unique $\alpha \in \Z$ such that: $(1): \quad 
orm {x - \alpha}_p \le p^{-i}$ $(2): \quad 0 \le \alpha \le p^i - 1$

label: Unique Isomorphism between Ordinal Subset and Unique Ordinal
snippet: Let $\On$ be the class of all ordinals. Let $S \subset \On$ where $S$ is a set. Then there exists a unique mapping $\phi$ and a unique ordinal $x$ such that $\phi : x \to S$ is an order isomorphism.

label: Unique Linear Transformation Between Vector Spaces
snippet: == Corollary to Unique Linear Transformation Between Modules == Let $G$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space. Let $H$ be a $K$-vector space (not necessarily finite-dimensional). Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a linearly independent sequence of vectors of $G$. Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be a sequence of vectors of $H$. Then there is a unique linear transformation $\phi: G \to H$ satisfying: $\forall k \in \closedint 1 n: \map \phi {a_k} = b_k$

label: Unique Minimal Element may not be Smallest
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ have a unique minimal element. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ has a smallest element.

label: Unique Ordinal Exponentiation Inequality
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x > 1$ and $y > 0$. Then there exists a unique ordinal $z$ such that: $x^z \le y$ and $y < x^{z^+}$

label: Unique Period Prime/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Unique Period Primes == In base $10$, the prime numbers $3$, $11$, $37$, and $101$ are the only ones with periods $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$ respectively. Hence they are unique period primes. But: $41$ and $271$ both have period $5$ $7$ and $13$ both have period $6$ $239$ and $4649$ both have period $7$ $73$ and $137$ both have period $8$. Thus these primes are not unique period primes.

label: Unique Point of Minimal Distance to Closed Convex Subset of Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space, and let $h \in H$. Let $K \subseteq H$ be a closed, convex, non-empty subset of $H$. Then there is a unique point $k_0 \in K$ such that: $\norm {h - k_0} = \map d {h, K}$ where $d$ denotes distance to a set.

label: Unique Point of Minimal Distance to Closed Linear Subspace of Hilbert Space iff Orthogonal
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space, and let $h \in H$. Let $K \subseteq H$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Then the unique point $k_0 \in K$ from Unique Point of Minimal Distance to Closed Convex Subset of Hilbert Space such that: $\norm {h - k_0} = \map d {h, K}$ where $d$ denotes distance to a set, is characterised by: $\norm {h - k_0} = \map d {h, K} \iff \paren {h - k_0} \perp K$ where $\perp$ signifies orthogonality.

label: Unique Representation by Ordered Basis
snippet: Let $G$ be a unitary $R$-module. Then $\sequence {a_n}$ is an ordered basis of $G$ : For every $x \in G$ there exists one and only one sequence $\sequence {\lambda_n}$ of scalars such that $\ds x = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_k a_k$.

label: Unique Representation in Polynomial Forms
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral subdomain of $R$. Let $X \in R$ be transcendental over $D$. Let $D \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials in $X$ over $D$. Then each non-zero member of $D \left[{X}\right]$ can be expressed in just one way in the form: $\ds f \in D \sqbrk X: f = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n {a_k \circ X^k}$

label: Unique Representation of Complex Number in Spherical Form
snippet: Let $\PP$ be the complex plane. Let $\mathbb S$ be the unit sphere which is tangent to $\PP$ at $\tuple {0, 0}$ (that is, where $z = 0$). Let the diameter of $\mathbb S$ perpendicular to $\PP$ through $\tuple {0, 0}$ be $NS$ where $S$ is the point $\tuple {0, 0}$. Let the point $N$ be referred to as the north pole of $\mathbb S$ and $S$ be referred to as the south pole of $\mathbb S$. 900px Let $A$ be a point on $P$. Let the line $NA$ be constructed. Then $NA$ passes through exactly one point $A'$ on the surface of $\mathbb S$ apart from $N$.

label: Unique Sequence of Consecutive Odd Numbers which are Prime
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 3$. Then $n$, $n + 2$, $n + 4$ cannot all be prime. That is, the only set of $3$ consecutive odd numbers all of which are prime is $\set {3, 5, 7}$.

label: Unique Subgroup of a Given Order is Normal
snippet: Let a group $G$ have only one subgroup of a given order. Then that subgroup is normal.

label: Unique Tree of Order 2
snippet: There exists exactly one tree of order $2$: 200px

label: Uniqueness of Normal Coordinates
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold. Let $U_p$ be the normal neighborhood for $p \in M$. Then for every normal coordinate chart on $U_p$ centered at $p \in M$ the coordinate basis is orthonormal at $p$. Furthermore, for every orthonormal basis $\tuple {b_i}$ for $T_p M$, there is a unique normal coordinate chart $\tuple {x^i}$ on $U_p$ such that: $\ds \forall i \in \N_{> 0} : i \le n : \valueat{\partial_i} p = b_i$

label: Uniqueness of Polynomial Ring in One Variable
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\struct {R \sqbrk X, \iota, X}$ and $\struct {R \sqbrk Y, \kappa, Y}$ be polynomial rings in one variable over $R$. Then there exists a unique ring homomorphism $f: R \sqbrk X \to R \sqbrk Y$ such that: $f \circ \iota = \kappa$ $\map f X = Y$ and it is an isomorphism.

label: Uniqueness of Positive Root of Positive Real Number
Uniqueness of Real z such that x Choose n+1 Equals y Choose n+1 Plus z Choose n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers which satisfy: $n \le y \le x \le y + 1$ Then there exists a unique real number $z$ such that: $\dbinom x {n + 1} = \dbinom y {n + 1} + \dbinom z n$ where $n - 1 \le z \le y$.

label: Uniqueness of Representing Objects
snippet: Let $C$ be a locally small category. Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $F : \mathbf C \to \mathbf{Set}$ be a covariant functor. Let $(A, \eta)$ and $(B, \xi)$ be representations of $F$. Then there exists a unique isomorphism $f : A \to B$ such that $\eta \circ h^f = \xi$, where: $h^f$ is the precomposition natural transformation $\circ$ denotes vertical composition of natural transformations

label: Unit-Speed Admissible Curve is Critical Point of Riemannian Length iff Geodesic
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $\gamma$ be a unit-speed admissible curve. Let $L_g$ the Riemannian length of some admissible curve. Then $\gamma$ is the critical point of $L_g$ $\gamma$ is geodesic.

label: Unit-Speed Minimizing Curve is Geodesic
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $I = \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\gamma : I \to M$ be an admissible curve. Suppose $\gamma$ is parametrized so that $\gamma$ is a unit-speed curve. Suppose $\gamma$ is minimizing. Then $\gamma$ is a geodesic.

label: Unit Matrix is Identity for Matrix Multiplication
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\map {\MM_R} n$ denote the metric space of square matrices of order $n$ over $R$. Let $\mathbf I_n$ denote the unit matrix of order $n$: Then: $\forall \mathbf A \in \map {\MM_R} n: \mathbf A \mathbf I_n = \mathbf A = \mathbf I_n \mathbf A$ That is, the unit matrix $\mathbf I_n$ is the identity element for (conventional) matrix multiplication over $\map {\MM_R} n$.

label: Unit Matrix is Unity of Ring of Square Matrices
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ denote the ring of square matrices of order $n$ over $R$. The unit matrix over $R$: $\mathbf I_n = \begin {pmatrix} 1_R & 0_R & 0_R & \cdots & 0_R \\ 0_R & 1_R & 0_R & \cdots & 0_R \\ 0_R & 0_R & 1_R & \cdots & 0_R \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0_R & 0_R & 0_R & \cdots & 1_R \end {pmatrix}$ is the identity element of $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$.

label: Unit Sphere as Surface of Revolution
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^3, d}$ be the Euclidean space. Let $S_C \subseteq \R^3$ be the surface of revolution. Let $C$ be a semi-circle defined by $x^2 + y^2 = 1$ in the open upper half-plane. Let the smooth local parametrization of $C$ be: $\map \gamma \phi = \tuple {\cos \phi, \sin \phi}$ where $\phi \in \openint 0 \pi$. Then the induced metric on $S_C$ is: $g = \d \phi^2 + \sin^2 \phi \rd \theta^2$

label: Unit Tangent Bundle is Connected iff Manifold is Connected
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold of dimension $n > 1$. Let $UTM$ be the unit tangent bundle of $M$. Then $UTM$ is connected $M$ is connected.

label: Unit Vectors in Complex Plane which are Vertices of Equilateral Triangle
snippet: Let $\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2, \epsilon_3$ be complex numbers embedded in the complex plane such that: $\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2, \epsilon_3$ all have modulus $1$ $\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2 + \epsilon_3 = 0$ Then: $\paren {\dfrac {\epsilon_2} {\epsilon_1} }^3 = \paren {\dfrac {\epsilon_3} {\epsilon_2} }^2 = \paren {\dfrac {\epsilon_1} {\epsilon_3} }^2 = 1$

label: Unit n-Sphere under Euclidean Metric is Metric Subspace of Euclidean Real Vector Space
snippet: Let $\Bbb S^n$ be the unit $n$-sphere. Let $d_S: \Bbb S^n \times \Bbb S^n \to \R$ be the real-valued function defined as: $\ds \forall x, y \in \Bbb S^n: \map {d_S} {x, y} = \sqrt {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^{n + 1} \paren {x_i - y_i}^2}$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{n + 1} }, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_{n + 1} }$. Then $\struct {\Bbb S^n, d_S}$ is a metric subspace of $\struct {\R^{n + 1}, d}$, where $d$ is the Euclidean metric on the real vector space $\R^{n + 1}$.

label: Unit of Ring is not Zero Divisor
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a non-null ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $x$ be a unit of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $x$ is neither a left zero divisor nor a right zero divisor of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$.

label: Unit of Ring of Mappings iff Image is Subset of Ring Units
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity $1_R$. Let $U_R$ be the set of units in $R$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of mappings on the set of mappings $R^S$. Then: $f \in R^S$ is a unit of $R^S$ $\Img f \subseteq U_R$ where $\Img f$ is the image of $f$. In this case, the inverse of $f$ is the mapping $f^{-1} : S \to U_R$ defined by: $\forall x \in S : \map {f^{-1} } x = \map f x^{-1}$

label: Unital C*-Algebra is Unital Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra that is unital as an algebra, with identity element ${\mathbf 1}_A \ne {\mathbf 0}_A$. Then $A$ is unital as a Banach algebra.

label: Unital Ring Homomorphism by Idempotent
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $e \in A$ be an idempotent element. Let $\ideal e$ be the ideal of $A$ generated by $e$. Then the mapping: $f: A \to \ideal e: a \mapsto e a$ is a surjective unital ring homomorphism from $\struct {A, +, \circ}$ to $\struct {\ideal e, +, \circ}$ with kernel the ideal $\ideal {1 - e}$ generated by $1 - e$.

label: Unitary Group is Group
snippet: The set of unitary $n \times n$ matrices forms a group under (conventional) matrix multiplication.

label: Unitary Module of All Mappings is Unitary Module
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be a unitary $R$-module. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {G^S, +_G', \circ}_R$ be the module of all mappings from $S$ to $G$. Then $\struct {G^S, +_G', \circ}_R$ is a unitary module.

label: Unitary R-Modules with n-Element Bases are Isomorphic
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be unitary $R$-modules for some ring with unity $R$. Let $G$ and $G$ both have bases with $n$ elements. Then $G$ and $H$ are isomorphic.

label: Unitization of Algebra over Field is Unital Algebra over Field
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be an algebra over $K$. Let $\struct {A_+, +_{A_+}, \cdot_{A_+}, \circ_{A_+} }_K$ be the unitization of $A$. Then $\struct {A_+, +_{A_+}, \cdot_{A_+}, \circ_{A_+} }_K$ is a unital algebra over $K$.

snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {A, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed algebra over $\GF$ that is not unital as an algebra. Let $\struct {A_+, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{A_+} }$ be the normed unitization of $\struct {A, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Then $\struct {A_+, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{A_+} }$ is a Banach algebra $\struct {A, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ is a Banach algebra.

label: Units of Gaussian Integers
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ be the ring of Gaussian integers. The set of units of $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ is $\set {1, i, -1, -i}$.

label: Units of Gaussian Integers form Group
snippet: Let $U_\C$ be the set of units of the Gaussian integers: $U_\C = \set {1, i, -1, -i}$ where $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i = \sqrt {-1}$. Let $\struct {U_\C, \times}$ be the algebraic structure formed by $U_\C$ under the operation of complex multiplication. Then $\struct {U_\C, \times}$ forms a cyclic group under complex multiplication.

label: Units of Quadratic Integers over 2
snippet: Let $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}$ denote the set of quadratic integers over $2$: $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2} := \set {a + b \sqrt 2: a, b \in \Z}$ that is, all numbers of the form $a + b \sqrt 2$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers. Let $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}, +, \times}$ be the integral domain where $+$ and $\times$ are conventional addition and multiplication on real numbers. Then numbers of the form $a + b \sqrt 2$ such that $a^2 - 2 b^2 = \pm 1$ are all units of $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}, +, \times}$.

label: Units of Ring of Polynomial Forms over Commutative Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a non-null commutative ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $R \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial forms in an indeterminate $X$ over $R$. Let $\map P X = a_0 + a_1 X + \cdots + a_n X^n \in R \sqbrk X$. Then: $\map P X$ is a unit of $R \sqbrk X$ $a_0$ is a unit of $R$ Also, for $i = 1, \ldots, n$, $a_i$ is nilpotent in $R$.

label: Unity and Negative form Subgroup of Units
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity. Then: $\struct {\set {1_R, -1_R}, \circ} \le U_R$ That is, the set consisting of the unity and its negative forms a subgroup of the group of units.

label: Unity is Unit
snippet: The unity in a ring is a unit.

label: Unity of Integral Domain is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an integral domain. Then the unity of $\struct {D, +, \times}$ is unique.

label: Unity of Ring is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\left({R, +, \circ}\right)$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. Then $1_R$ is an idempotent element of $R$ under the ring product $\circ$: $1_R \circ 1_R = 1_R$

label: Unity of Ring is Unique
snippet: A ring can have no more than one unity.

label: Unity of Ring of Bounded Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: the unity of $\struct{\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $1_{\R^S} : S \to \R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {1_{\R^S}} s = 1$.

label: Unity of Ring of Continuous Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {R, +, *, \tau_{_R} }$ be a topological ring with unity $1_R$. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $R$. Then: the unity of $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $1_{R^S} : S \to R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {1_{R^S}} s = 1_R$.

label: Unity of Ring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: the unity of $\struct{\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $1_{\R^S} : S \to \R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {1_{\R^S}} s = 1$.

label: Unity of Subfield is Unity of Field
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose unity is $1$. Let $\struct {K, +, \times}$ be a subfield of $F$. The unity of $\struct {K, +, \times}$ is also $1$.

label: Unity of Subring is not necessarily Unity of Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {S, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_S$. Let $\struct {T, + \circ}$ be a subring of $\struct {S, + \circ}$ whose unity is $1_T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $1_T = 1_S$.

label: Unity plus Negative of Nilpotent Ring Element is Unit
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $x \in R$ be nilpotent. Then $1_R - x$ is a unit of $R$.

label: Universal Class is Proper
snippet: Let $V$ denote the universal class. Then $V$ is a proper class.

label: Universal Class less Set is not Transitive
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Let $a \in V$ be a set. Then: $V \setminus \set a$ is not a transitive class where $\setminus$ denotes class difference.

label: Universal Cover is Covering Space for Every Connected Covering Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $C = \struct {X, \phi}$ be a universal cover for $T$. Let $C' = \struct {X', \phi'}$ be an arbitrary connected covering space for $T$. Then $C$ is also a covering space for $C'$.

label: Universal Cover is Unique when it Exists
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let there exist a universal cover $C = \struct {X, \phi}$ for $T$. Then $C$ is unique up to homeomorphism.

label: Universal Morphism from Functor to Object is Unique up to Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $F: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\tuple{R_1, u_1}$ and $\tuple{R_2, u_2}$ be a universal morphisms from $F$ to $C$. Then: there exists an isomorphism $i: R_2 \to R_1$ such that $u_2 = u_1 \circ Fi$

label: Universal Morphism from Object to Functor is Unique up to Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $F: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor.
