label: Universal Property of Abelianization of Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $G^{\operatorname {ab} }$ be its abelianization. Let $\pi : G \to G^{\operatorname {ab} }$ be the quotient group epimorphism. Let $H$ be an abelian group. Let $f: G \to H$ be a group homomorphism. Then there exists a unique group homomorphism $g : G^{\operatorname {ab}} \to H$ such that $g \circ \pi = f$: $\xymatrix { G \ar[d]_\pi \ar[r]^{\forall f} & H\\ G^{\operatorname {ab} } \ar[ru]_{\exists ! g} }$

label: Universal Property of Free Abelian Group on Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {\Z^{\paren S}, \iota}$ be the free abelian group on $S$. Let $\struct {G, +}$ be an abelian group. Let $f: S \to G$ be a mapping. Then there exists a unique group homomorphism $g : \Z^{\paren S} \to G$ with $g \circ \iota = f$: $\xymatrix{S \ar[d]_\iota \ar[r]^{\forall f} & G\\ \Z^{\paren S} \ar@{-->}[ru]_{\exists ! g} & }$

label: Universal Property of Free Module on Set
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $R^{\paren I}$ be the free $R$-module on $I$. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let $\family {m_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of elements of $M$. Then there exists a unique $R$-module morphism: $\Psi: R^{\paren I} \to M$ that sends the $i$th canonical basis element to $m_i$, for all $i \in I$. Moreover: $\ds \map \Psi {\family {r_i}_{i \mathop \in I} } = \sum_{i \mathop \in I} r_i m_i$

label: Universal Property of Free Modules
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be a free $R$-module with basis $\set {e_i: i\in I}$. Let $N$ be an $R$-module. Let $\set {n_i: i \in I}$ be a family of elements of $N$. Then there exists a unique $R$-module homomorphism that maps $e_i$ to $n_i$ for all $i\in I$.

label: Universal Property of Group Ring
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $G$ be a group. Let $R \sqbrk G$ be the corresponding group ring. Let $S$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $\beta : G \to S^\times$ be a group homomorphism, where $S^\times$ is the multiplicative group of $S$. Then there exists a unique ring homomorphism from $R \sqbrk G$ to $S$ which extends $\phi$ and $\beta$.

snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. The different definitions of a polynomial ring $\struct {\map R x, \iota, x}$ on $R$ satisfy the universal property of a polynomial ring:

label: Universal Property of Quotient Group
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups. Let $N \trianglelefteq G$ be an normal subgroup. Let $\pi: G \to G / N$ be the quotient epimorphism. Let $f: G \to H$ be a group homomorphism with $N \subseteq \ker f$. Then there exists a unique group homomorphism $\overline f: G / N \to H$ such that $f = \overline f \circ \pi$. $\xymatrix{ G \ar[d]^\pi \ar[r]^{\forall f} & H \\ G/N \ar[ru]_{\exists ! \bar f} }$

label: Universal Property of Quotient Ring
snippet: Let $R, S$ be commutative rings. Let $I \trianglelefteq R$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $\pi : R \to R / I$ be the quotient epimorphism. Let $f: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism with $\map f I = \set 0$. Then there exists a unique ring homomorphism $\overline f: R / I \to S$ such that $f = \overline f \circ \pi$. $\xymatrix { R \ar[d]_\pi \ar[r]^{\forall f} & S \\ R/I \ar[ru]_{\exists ! \bar f} }$

label: Universal Property of Quotient Set
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on $X$. Let $\pi: X \to X / {\sim}$ be the quotient mapping to the quotient set. Let $f: X \to Y$ be $\sim$-invariant. Then there exists a unique mapping $\overline f : X / {\sim} \to Y$ such that $f = \overline f \circ \pi$. $\xymatrix{ X \ar[d]_\pi \ar[r]^f & Y\\ X/\sim \ar@{.>}[ru]_{\overline f} }$

label: Universal Property of Quotient Space
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces. Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on $X$. Let $\pi : X \to X / {\sim}$ be the quotient mapping. Let $f : X \to Y$ be continuous and $\sim$-invariant. Then there exists a unique continuous map $\overline f : X / {\sim} \to Y$ such that $f = \overline f \circ \pi$.

label: Universal Property of Quotient of Topological Group
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be topological groups. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $\pi : G \to G/N$ be the quotient mapping. Let $f : G \to H$ be a continuous group homomorphism whose kernel contains $N$. Then there exists a unique continuous group homomorphism $\overline f: G / N \to H$ such that: $f = \overline f \circ \pi$

label: Universal URM Computable Functions
snippet: For each integer $k \ge 1$, there exists a URM computable function: $\Phi_k: \N^{k+1} \to \N$ such that for each URM computable function $f: \N^k \to \N$ there exists a natural number $e$ such that: $\forall \left({n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right) \in \N^k: f \left({n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right) \approx \Phi_k \left({e, n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right)$. This function $\Phi_k$ is universal for URM computable functions of $k$ variables.

label: Universal URM Programs
snippet: For each integer $k \ge 1$, there exists a URM program $P_k$ such that: For each URM program $P$ there exists a natural number $e$ such that: For all $\left({n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right) \in \N^k$, the computation using the program $P_k$ with input $\left({e, n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right)$ has the same output as the computation using the program $P$ with input $\left({n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right)$. This function $P_k$ is a universal program for URM computations with $k$ inputs.

label: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of n+1 with 1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Then: $\ds {n + 1 \brack 1} = n!$ where: $\ds {n + 1 \brack 1}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $n!$ denotes $n$ factorial.

label: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of n with n-1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be an integer greater than $0$. Then: $\ds {n \brack n - 1} = \binom n 2$ where: $\ds {n \brack n - 1}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\dbinom n 2$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

label: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of n with n-2
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 2}$ be an integer greater than or equal to $2$. Then: $\ds {n \brack n - 2} = \binom n 4 + 2 \binom {n + 1} 4$ where: $\ds {n \brack n - 2}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\dbinom n 4$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

label: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of n with n-3
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 3}$ be an integer greater than or equal to $3$. Then: $\ds {n \brack n - 3} = \binom n 6 + 8 \binom {n + 1} 6 + 6 \binom {n + 2} 6$ where: $\ds {n \brack n - 3}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\dbinom n 6$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

label: Unsymmetric Functional Equation for Riemann Zeta Function
snippet: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function. Let $\Gamma$ be the gamma function. Then for all $s \in \C$: $\map \zeta {1 - s} = 2^{1 - s} \pi^{-s} \map \cos {\dfrac {\pi s} 2} \map \Gamma s \map \zeta s$

label: Up-Complete Lower Bounded Join Semilattice is Complete
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an up-complete lower bounded join semillattice. Then $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is complete.

label: Upper Adjoint Preserves All Infima
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$, $\left({T, \precsim}\right)$ be ordered sets. Let $g: S \to T$ be an upper adjoint of Galois connection. Then $g$ preserves all infima.

label: Upper Bound for Abundancy Index
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{>0}$ be a non-zero natural number. Let $\map h n$ be the abundancy index of $n$. Then: $\ds \map h n \le \prod_{p \mathop \divides n} \dfrac p {p - 1}$ such that equality holds $n = 1$.

label: Upper Bound for Lowest Common Multiple
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers such that $a b \ne 0$. Then: $\lcm \set {a, b} \le \size {a b}$ where: $\lcm \set {a, b}$ denotes the lowest common multiple of $a$ and $b$

label: Upper Bound for Subset
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $U$ be an upper bound for $S$. Let $\left({T, \preceq}\right)$ be a subset of $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$. Then $U$ is an upper bound for $T$.

label: Upper Bound is Upper Bound for Subset
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be a preordered set. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$ such that $B \subseteq A$ Let $U$ be an upper bound for $A$. Then $U$ is an upper bound for $B$.

label: Upper Bound of Natural Logarithm
snippet: Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$ where $x \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\ln x \le x - 1$

label: Upper Bound of Order of Non-Abelian Finite Simple Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a non-abelian finite simple group. Let $t \in G$ be a self-inverse element of $G$. Let $\map {C_G} t$ denote the centralizer of $t$ in $G$. Let $m = \order {\map {C_G} t}$ be the order of $\map {C_G} t$. Then: $\order G \le \paren {\dfrac {m \paren {m + 1} } 2}!$

label: Upper Bound of Ordinal Sum
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Suppose $x > 1$. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a finite sequence of ordinals such that: $a_n < x$ for all $n$ Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be a strictly decreasing finite sequence of ordinals such that: $b_n < y$ for all $n$ Then: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n x^{b_i} a_i < x^y$

label: Upper Bounds are Equivalent implies Suprema are equal
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X, Y$ be subsets of $S$. Assume that $X$ admits a supremum and $\forall x \in S: x$ is upper bound for $X \iff x$ is upper bound for $Y$ Then $\sup X = \sup Y$

label: Upper Bounds for Prime Numbers
snippet: Let $p: \N \to \N$ be the prime enumeration function. Then $\forall n \in \N$, the value of $\map p n$ is bounded above. In particular:

label: Upper Closure is Closure Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T^\succeq$ be the upper closure of $T$ for each $T \subseteq S$. Then $\cdot^\succeq$ is a closure operator.

label: Upper Closure is Compact in Topological Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a topological lattice. Suppose that: for every subset $X$ of $S$ if $X$ is open, then $X$ is upper. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^\succeq$ is compact where $x^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $x$.

label: Upper Closure is Smallest Containing Upper Section
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $U = T^\succeq$ be the upper closure of $T$. Then $U$ is the smallest upper section containing $T$ as a subset.

label: Upper Closure is Strict Upper Closure of Immediate Predecessor
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $b$ be the immediate successor element of $a$: Then: $a^\succ = b^\succcurlyeq$ where: $a^\succ$ is the strict upper closure of $a$ $b^\succcurlyeq$ is the upper closure of $b$.

label: Upper Closure is Upper Section
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T$ be a subset of $S$. Let $U$ be the upper closure of $T$. Then $U$ is an upper section.

label: Upper Closure of Coarser Subset is Subset of Upper Closure
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be a preordered set. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$ such that $A$ is coarser than $B$. Then $A^\succeq \subseteq B^\succeq$

label: Upper Closure of Element is Way Below Open Filter iff Element is Compact
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $x \in S$. Then: $x^\succeq$ is a way below open filter on $L$ $x$ is compact

label: Upper Closure of Subset is Subset of Upper Closure
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $X, Y$ be subsets of $S$. Then $X \subseteq Y \implies X^\succeq \subseteq Y^\succeq$ where $X^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $X$.

label: Upper Darboux Sum Never Smaller than Lower Darboux Sum
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed interval of the set $\R$ of real numbers. Let $P = \set {x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{n - 1}, x_n}$ be a finite subdivision of $\closedint a b$. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $f$ be bounded on $\closedint a b$. Let $\map L P$ be the lower Darboux sum of $\map f x$ on $\closedint a b$ belonging to the subdivision $P$. Let $\map U P$ be the upper Darboux sum of $\map f x$ on $\closedint a b$ belonging to the subdivision $P$. Then $\map L P \le \map U P$.

label: Upper Limit of Function is Bounded Below by Value at Limit Point
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a function. Let $\limsup$ be the upper limit. Let $x_0 \in X$. Then we have: $\ds \map f {x_0} \le \limsup_{x \mathop \to x_0} \map f x$

label: Upper Triangular Normal Matrix is Diagonal
snippet: A square matrix that is both upper triangular and normal is diagonal.

label: Upper Way Below Open Subset Complement is Non Empty implies There Exists Maximal Element of Complement
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $X$ be upper way below open subset of $S$. Let $x \in S$ such that $x \in \relcomp S X$ Then $\exists m \in S: x \preceq m \land m = \max \relcomp S X$

label: Upper and Lower Bound of Fibonacci Number
snippet: For all $n \in \N_{> 0}$: $\phi^{n - 2} \le F_n \le \phi^{n - 1}$ where: $F_n$ is the $n$th Fibonacci number $\phi$ is the golden section: $\phi = \dfrac {1 + \sqrt 5} 2$

label: Urysohn's Lemma
snippet: == Lemma == Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_4$ topological space. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ be closed sets of $T$ such that $A \cap B = \O$. Then there exists an Urysohn function for $A$ and $B$.

label: Urysohn's Lemma Converse
snippet: == Lemma == Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let there exist an Urysohn function for any two $A, B \subseteq S$ which are closed sets in $T$ such that $A \cap B = \O$. Then $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ is a $T_4$ space.

label: Urysohn's Metrization Theorem
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is regular and second-countable. Then $T$ is metrizable.

label: Urysohn Space is T2.5
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be an Urysohn space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space.

Define $V : \HH \times \HH \to \HH \times \HH$ by: $\map V {x, y} = \tuple {-y, x}$ for each $\tuple {x, y} \in \HH \times \HH$. label: Value of Apéry's Constant
snippet: == Unsolved Problem == Apéry's constant: $\ds \map \zeta 3 = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 {n^3}$ has not been determined in closed form in terms of other familiar constants. It is of particular interest whether, similar to Riemann Zeta Function at Even Integers: $\dfrac {\map \zeta 3} {\pi^3}$ is rational. By using the techniques of Riemann Zeta Function as a Multiple Integral it can be established that: $\ds \int_0^1 \int_0^1 \int_0^1 \frac {\rd x \rd y \rd z} {1 - x y z} = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 {n^3}$

label: Value of Curvilinear Coordinate Metric
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be two points in space. Let a curvilinear $3$-Space coordinate system $\QQ$ be applied on top of a Cartesian $3$-space. Let $h_{i j}$ be the metric of $\QQ$. Then: $\forall i, j \in \set {1, 2, 3}: {h_{i j} }^2 = \dfrac {\partial x} {\partial q_i} \dfrac {\partial x} {\partial q_j} + \dfrac {\partial y} {\partial q_i} \dfrac {\partial y} {\partial q_j} + \dfrac {\partial z} {\partial q_i} \dfrac {\partial z} {\partial q_j}$ where $\partial$ denotes partial differentiation.

label: Value of Discriminant of Conic Section
snippet: Let $K$ be a conic section embedded in a Cartesian plane with the general equation: $a x^2 + 2 h x y + b y^2 + 2 g x + 2 f y + c = 0$ where $a, b, c, f, g, h \in \R$. The value of the discriminant of $K$ is: $\Delta = a b c + 2 f g h - a f^2 - b g^2 - c h^2$

label: Value of Field Norm on 5th Cyclotomic Ring is Integer
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {i \sqrt 5}, +, \times}$ denote the $5$th cyclotomic ring. Let $\alpha = a + i b \sqrt 5$ be an arbitrary element of $\Z \sqbrk {i \sqrt 5}$. Let $\map N \alpha$ denoted the field norm of $\alpha$. Then $\map N \alpha$ is an integer.

label: Value of Position-Ratio
snippet: Let $P$ and $Q$ be points in space. Let $R$ be a point on the straight line passing through $P$ and $Q$. Let $k$ denote the position-ratio of $R$. Then: $k = \dfrac {PQ} {RQ} - 1$

label: Value of Relation is Small
snippet: The value of a relation is always a small class.

label: Value of b for b by Logarithm Base b of x to be Minimum
snippet: Let $x \in \R_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive real number. Consider the real function $f: \R_{> 0} \to \R$ defined as: $\map f b := b \log_b x$ $f$ attains a minimum when $b = e$ where $e$ is Euler's number.

label: Vanishing Ideal of Zero Locus of Ideal is Radical
snippet: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $n \ge 0$ be a natural number. Let $k \sqbrk {X_1, \ldots, X_n}$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables over $k$. Let $\mathfrak a \subseteq k \sqbrk {X_1, \ldots, X_n}$ be an ideal. Then: $\map I {\map V {\mathfrak a} } = \map \Rad {\mathfrak a}$ where: $\map V \cdot$ denotes the zero locus $\map I \cdot$ denotes the vanishing ideal $\map \Rad \cdot$ denotes the radical

label: Vanishing of Quasi-Coherent Sheaf Cohomology of Affine Scheme
snippet: Let $X = \Spec A$ be the spectrum of a commutative ring $A$. Let $\FF$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$. Then for all $i \in \Z$ with $i > 0$ the $i$-th sheaf cohomology $\map {H^i} {X, \FF} = 0$.

label: Vanishing of Quasi-Coherent Sheaf Cohomology of Noetherian Affine Scheme

label: Variance as Expectation of Square minus Square of Expectation
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Then the variance of $X$ can be expressed as: $\var X = \expect {X^2} - \paren {\expect X}^2$ That is, it is the expectation of the square of $X$ minus the square of the expectation of $X$.

label: Variance of Binomial Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$. Then the variance of $X$ is given by: $\var X = n p \paren {1 - p}$

label: Variance of Continuous Uniform Distribution
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ such that $a < b$. Let $X \sim \ContinuousUniform a b$ be the continuous uniform distribution over $\closedint a b$. Then: $\var X = \dfrac {\paren {b - a}^2} {12}$

label: Variance of Exponential Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with the exponential distribution with parameter $\beta$. Then the variance of $X$ is: $\var X = \beta^2$

label: Variance of Geometric Distribution
snippet: Let $p \in \R$ be a real number such that $0 < p < 1$. Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the geometric distribution with parameter $p$.

label: Variance of Grouped Data
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of grouped data. Let it be assumed that $S$ approximates a normal distribution The variance of $S$ can be calculated by: $(1): \quad$ assuming that the elements of $S$ are all at the mid-interval values $(2): \quad$ subtracting Sheppard's correction of $\dfrac {h^2} {12}$, where $h$ is the bin width.

label: Variance of Linear Combination of Random Variables
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Let the variances of $X$ and $Y$ be finite. Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Then the variance of $a X + b Y$ is given by: $\var {a X + b Y} = a^2 \, \var X + b^2 \, \var Y + 2 a b \, \cov {X, Y}$ where $\cov {X, Y}$ is the covariance of $X$ and $Y$.

label: Variance of Linear Function of Observations of Stationary Process
snippet: Let $S$ be a strictly stationary stochastic process giving rise to a time series $T$. Let $\sequence {s_n}$ be a sequence of $n$ successive values of $T$: $\sequence {s_n} = \tuple {z_1, z_2, \dotsb, z_n}$ Let $L_t$ be a linear function of $\sequence {s_n}$: $L_t = l_1 z_t + l_2 z_{t - 1} + \dotsb + l_n z_{t - n + 1}$ Then the variance of $L_t$ is given by: $\var {L_t} = \ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n l_i l_j \gamma {\size {j - i} }$ where $\gamma_k$ is the autocovariance of $S$ at lag $k$.

label: Variance of Linear Transformation of Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $a, b$ be real numbers. Then we have: $\var {a X + b} = a^2 \var X$ where $\var X$ denotes the variance of $X$.

label: Variance of Logistic Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable which satisfies the logistic distribution: $X \sim \map {\operatorname {Logistic} } {\mu, s}$ The variance of $X$ is given by: $\var X = \dfrac {s^2 \pi^2} 3$

label: Variance of Normal Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim N \paren {\mu, \sigma^2}$ for some $\mu \in \R, \sigma \in \R_{> 0}$, where $N$ is the normal distribution. Then: $\var X = \sigma^2$

label: Variance of Poisson Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda$. Then the variance of $X$ is given by: $\var X = \lambda$

label: Variation of Complex Measure is Finite Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a complex measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $\cmod \mu$ be the variation of $\mu$. Then $\cmod \mu$ is a finite measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$.

label: Variation of Intersection Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a signed measure or complex measure on $X$. Let $\cmod \mu$ be the variation of $\mu$. Let $F \in \Sigma$. Let $\mu_F$ and $\cmod \mu_F$ be the intersection measures of $\mu$ and $\mu_F$ respectively. Let $\cmod {\mu_F}$ be the variation of $\mu_F$. Then: $\cmod \mu_F = \cmod {\mu_F}$

label: Vector Addition is Associative
snippet: Let $\mathbf a, \mathbf b, \mathbf c$ be vectors. Then: $\mathbf a + \paren {\mathbf b + \mathbf c} = \paren {\mathbf a + \mathbf b} + \mathbf c$ where $+$ denotes vector addition.

label: Vector Augend plus Addend equals Augend implies Addend is Zero
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $F$. Let $\mathbf a, \mathbf b \in V$. Let $\mathbf a + \mathbf b = \mathbf a$. Then: $\mathbf b = \bszero$ where $\bszero$ is the zero vector of $V$.

label: Vector Cross Product/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Vector Cross Product ==

label: Vector Cross Product Distributes over Addition
snippet: The vector cross product is distributive over addition. That is, in general: $\mathbf a \times \paren {\mathbf b + \mathbf c} = \paren {\mathbf a \times \mathbf b} + \paren {\mathbf a \times \mathbf c}$ for $\mathbf a, \mathbf b, \mathbf c \in \R^3$.

label: Vector Cross Product Operator is Bilinear
snippet: Let $\mathbf u$, $\mathbf v$ and $\mathbf w$ be vectors in a vector space $\mathbf V$ of $3$ dimensions: where $\left({\mathbf i, \mathbf j, \mathbf k}\right)$ is the standard ordered basis of $\mathbf V$. Let $c$ be a real number. Then: $\left({c \mathbf u + \mathbf v}\right) \times \mathbf w = c \left({ \mathbf u \times \mathbf w}\right) + \mathbf v \times \mathbf w$

label: Vector Cross Product is Anticommutative
snippet: The vector cross product is anticommutative: $\forall \mathbf a, \mathbf b \in \R^3: \mathbf a \times \mathbf b = -\paren {\mathbf b \times \mathbf a}$

label: Vector Cross Product of Vector Cross Products
snippet: Let $\mathbf a, \mathbf b, \mathbf c, \mathbf d$ be vectors in a vector space $\mathbf V$ of $3$ dimensions: Let $\mathbf a \times \mathbf b$ denote the vector cross product of $\mathbf a$ with $\mathbf b$. Let $\sqbrk {\mathbf a, \mathbf b, \mathbf c}$ denote the scalar triple product of $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$.

label: Vector Equation of Plane/Also presented as
snippet: == Equation of Plane: Also presented as == The vector form of the equation of the plane can also be presented in the form: $\mathbf r \cdot \mathbf n = p$ where: $\mathbf r$ is the position vector of an arbitrary point on $P$ $\mathbf n$ is the unit normal vector to $P$ $p$ is the length of the normal vector to $P$ through the origin.

label: Vector Equation of Straight Line in Space/Formulation 1
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ denote the position vectors of two points in space. Let $L$ be a straight line in space passing through $\mathbf a$ which is parallel to $\mathbf b$. Let $\mathbf r$ be the position vector of an arbitrary point on $L$. Then: $\mathbf r = \mathbf a + t \mathbf b$ for some real number $t$, which may be positive or negative, or even $0$ if $\mathbf r = \mathbf a$.

label: Vector Equation of Straight Line in Space/Formulation 2
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ denote the position vectors of two points in space. Let $L$ be a straight line in space passing through $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$. Let $\mathbf r$ be the position vector of an arbitrary point on $L$. Then: $\mathbf r = \mathbf a + t \paren {\mathbf b - \mathbf a}$ for some real number $t$, which may be positive or negative, or even $0$ if $\mathbf r = \mathbf a$.

label: Vector Equation of Straight Line in Space/Formulation 3
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ denote the position vectors of two points in space. Let $L$ be a straight line in space passing through $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$. Let $\mathbf r$ be the position vector of an arbitrary point $P$ on $L$. Then $L$ is the locus of all points $P$ such that: $\paren {\mathbf r - \mathbf a} \times \paren {\mathbf b - \mathbf a} = \mathbf 0$

label: Vector Equation of Straight Line in Space/Formulation 4
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ denote the position vectors of two points in space. Let $L$ be the straight line in space which is parallel to $\mathbf a$ and which passes through the point whose position vector is $\dfrac {\mathbf a \times \mathbf b} {\size {\mathbf a}^2}$. Let $\mathbf r$ be the position vector of an arbitrary point $P$ on $L$. Then $L$ is the locus of all points $P$ such that: $\mathbf r \times \mathbf a = \mathbf b$

label: Vector Field is Expressible as Gradient of Scalar Field iff Conservative
snippet: Let $R$ be a region of space. Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector field acting over $R$. Then $\mathbf V$ can be expressed as the gradient of some scalar field $F$ $\mathbf V$ is a conservative vector field.

label: Vector Fields with Equal Curls Differ by Gradient
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be vector fields over ordinary space. Then: $\nabla \times \mathbf A = \nabla \times \mathbf B$ $\mathbf B = \mathbf A + \grad f$ where $f$ is a scalar function with continuous partial derivatives.

label: Vector Inverse is Negative Vector
snippet: Let $F$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$. Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \ast}_F$ be a vector space over $F$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Then: $\forall \mathbf v \in \mathbf V: -\mathbf v = -1_F \ast \mathbf v$

label: Vector Product is Zero only if Factor is Zero
snippet: Let $F$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$. Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \ast}_F$ be a vector space over $F$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Then: $\forall \lambda \in F: \forall \mathbf v \in \mathbf V: \lambda \ast \mathbf v = \bszero \implies \paren {\lambda = 0_F \lor \mathbf v = \mathbf 0}$ where $\bszero \in \mathbf V$ is the zero vector.

label: Vector Quantity/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Vector Quantities ==

label: Vector Quantity can be Expressed as Sum of 3 Non-Coplanar Vectors
snippet: Let $\mathbf r$ be a vector quantity embedded in space. Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be non-coplanar. Then $\mathbf r$ can be expressed uniquely as the resultant of $3$ vector quantities which are each parallel to one of $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$.

label: Vector Scaled by Zero is Zero Vector
snippet: Let $F$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$. Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \ast}_F$ be a vector space over $F$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Then: $\forall \mathbf v \in \mathbf V: 0_F \ast \mathbf v = \bszero$

label: Vector Space/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Vector Spaces ==

label: Vector Space has Basis
snippet: Let $K$ be a division ring. Let $V$ be a vector space over $K$. Then $V$ has a basis.

label: Vector Space has Basis Between Linearly Independent Set and Finite Spanning Set
snippet: Let $K$ be a division ring. Let $G$ be a finitely generated $K$-vector space. Let $H$ be a linearly independent subset of $G$. Let $F$ be a finite generator for $G$ such that $H \subseteq F$. Then there is a basis $B$ for $G$ such that $H \subseteq B \subseteq F$.

label: Vector Space has Basis between Linearly Independent Set and Spanning Set
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $F$. Let $L$ be a linearly independent subset of $V$. Let $S$ be a set that spans $V$. Suppose that $L \subseteq S$. Then $V$ has a basis $B$ such that $L \subseteq B \subseteq S$.

label: Vector Space has Unique Additive Identity
snippet: A vector space has unique additive identity.

label: Vector Space is Affine Space
snippet: Let $\EE$ be a vector space. Then $\EE$ is also an affine space.

label: Vector Space obtains Norm Structure through Linear Isomorphism
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y$ be a norm on $Y$. Let $\phi : X 	o Y$ be a linear isomorphism. Define $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X : X 	o \R$ by: $
orm x_X = 
orm {\map \phi x}_Y$ for each $x \in X$. Then $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X$ is a norm on $X$.

label: Vector Space of All Mappings is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +, \circ}$ be a division ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_K$ be a $K$-vector space. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {G^S, +_G', \circ}_R$ be the vector space of all mappings from $S$ to $G$. Then $\struct {G^S, +_G', \circ}_K$ is a $K$-vector space.

label: Vector Space of Continuous on Closed Interval Real Functions is not Finite Dimensional
snippet: Let $I := \closedint 0 1$ be a closed real interval. Let $\struct {\map C I, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ be the continuous on closed interval real function vector space. Then $\struct {\map C I, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ is not finite dimensional.

label: Vector Space of Sequences with Finite Support is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +_K, \circ_K}$ be a division ring. Let $\struct{V, +, \cdot}$ be the vector space of sequences with finite support in $K$. Then $V$ is a vector space over $K$.

label: Vector Space on Cartesian Product is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +, \circ}$ be a division ring. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $\struct {K^n, +, \times}_K$ be the $K$-vector space $K^n$. Then $\struct {K^n, +, \times}_K$ is a $K$-vector space.

label: Vector Space on Field Extension is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +, \times}$ be a field. Let $L / K$ be a field extension over $K$. Let $\struct {L, +, \times}_K$ be the a vector space of $L$ over $K$. Then $\struct {L, +, \times}_K$ is a vector space.

label: Vector Space over Division Subring/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Vector Space over Division Subring ==

label: Vector Space over Division Subring is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {L, +_L, \times_L}$ be a division ring. Let $K$ be a division subring of $\struct {L, +_L, \times_L}$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_L$ be a $L$-vector space. Let $\circ_K$ be the restriction of $\circ$ to $K \times G$. Hence let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_K}_K$ be the vector space induced by $K$. Then $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_k}_k$ is indeed a $K$-vector space.

label: Vector Space over an Infinite Field is not equal to the Union of Proper Subspaces
snippet: Let $U_1, U_2, \dots, U_n$ be proper subspaces of a vector space $V$ over an infinite field $F$, Then $V$ is not equal to the union of $U_1, U_2, \dots, U_n$.

label: Vector Space with Standard Affine Structure is Affine Space
snippet: Let $E$ be a vector space. Let $\struct {\EE, E, +, -}$ be the standard affine structure on $E$. Then with this structure, $\EE$ is an affine space.

label: Vector Space with Subspace of Algebraic Dual Separating Points is Dual System
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $E$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $E^\#$ be the algebraic dual of $E$. Let $F \subseteq E^\#$ be a vector subspace of $E^\#$ that separates points. Define $\innerprod \cdot \cdot : E \times F \to K$ by: $\innerprod x f = \map f x$ for each $\tuple {x, f} \in E \times F$. Then $\tuple {E, F, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ is a dual system.

label: Vector Subspace/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Vector Subspaces ==

label: Vector Subspace contains Zero Vector
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a division ring $K$ whose unity is $1_K$. Let $U \subseteq V$ be a subspace of $V$. Then $U$ contains the zero vector of $V$.

label: Vector Subspace of Hausdorff Topological Vector Space is Hausdorff Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +_K, \circ_K, \tau_K}$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {\struct {X, +_X, \circ_X}_K, \tau_X}$ be a Hausdorff topological vector space over $K$. Let $\struct {Y, +_Y, \circ_Y}_K$ be a vector subspace of $X$. where: $+_Y : Y \times Y \to Y$ is the restriction of $+_X$ to $Y \times Y$ $\circ_Y : K \times Y \to Y$ is the restriction of $\circ_X$ to $K \times Y$. Let $\tau_Y$ be the subspace topology on $Y$ induced by $\tau_X$. Then $\struct {\struct {Y, +_Y, \circ_Y}_K, \tau_Y}$ is a Hausdorff topological vector space over $K$.

label: Vector Subspace of Real Vector Space under Chebyshev Metric is Metric Subspace
snippet: Let $n \in \N$. Let $A$ be the set of all ordered $n+1$-tuples $\tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{n + 1} }$ of real numbers such that $x_{n + 1} = 0$. Let $d: A \times A \to \R$ be the function defined as: $\ds \forall x, y \in A: \map d {x, y} = \max_{i \mathop = 1}^n \set {\size {x_i - y_i} }$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{n + 1} }, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_{n + 1} }$. Then $\struct {A, d}$ is a metric subspace of $\struct {\R^{n + 1}, d_\infty}$ where $d_\infty$ is the Chebyshev distance on the real vector space $\R^{n + 1}$.

label: Vector Subspace of Topological Vector Space is Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {\struct {X, +_X, \circ_X}_K, \tau_X}$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $Y$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $\tau_Y$ be the subspace topology on $Y$ induced by $\tau_X$. Let $+_Y : Y \times Y \to Y$ be the restriction of $+_X$ to $Y \times Y$. Let $\circ_Y : K \times Y \to Y$ be the restriction of $\circ_X$ to $K \times Y$. Then $\struct {\struct {Y, +_Y, \circ_Y}_K, \tau_Y}$ is a topological vector space.

label: Vector Times Magnitude Same Length As Magnitude Times Vector
snippet:
Let $\mathbf u$ and $\mathbf v$ be two vectors in the vector space $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_K$ over a division ring $\struct {K, +_K, 	imes}$ with subfield $\R$ such that $\R \subseteq \map Z K$ with $\map Z K$ the center of $K$ Let $
orm {\mathbf u}$ and $
orm {\mathbf v}$ be the lengths of $\mathbf u$ and $\mathbf v$ respectively. Then: $
orm {\paren {
orm {\mathbf v} \circ \mathbf u} } = 
orm {\paren {
orm {\mathbf u} \circ \mathbf v} }$

label: Vector not contained in Linear Span of Linearly Independent Set is Linearly Independent of Set
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $L$ be a linearly independent set of $X$ such that: $U = \map \span L \ne X$ Let: $x \in X \setminus U$ Then $L \cup \set x$ is linearly independent.

label: Vectorialization of Affine Space is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an affine space over a field $K$ with difference space $E$. Let $\RR = \tuple {p_0, e_1, \ldots, e_n}$ be an affine frame in $\EE$. Let $\struct {\EE, +, \cdot}$ be the vectorialization of $\EE$. Then $\struct {\EE, +, \cdot}$ is a vector space.

label: Vectorization of Product of Three Matrices
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $A, B, C$ be matrices over $R$ such that the matrix product $ABC$ is defined. Then $\map {\operatorname {vec} }{ABC} = \paren {C^\intercal \otimes A} \cdot \map {\operatorname {vec} } B$ where: $\operatorname {vec}$ denotes vectorization $C^\intercal$ is the transpose of $C$ $\otimes$ denotes Kronecker product $\cdot$ denotes matrix product

label: Vectors are Coplanar iff Scalar Triple Product equals Zero
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be vectors in a Cartesian $3$-space: Let $\mathbf a \cdot \paren {\mathbf b \times \mathbf c}$ denote the scalar triple product of $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$. Then: $\mathbf a \cdot \paren {\mathbf b \times \mathbf c} = 0$ $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ are coplanar.

label: Vectors are Left Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \circ}$ be a vector space over $\GF$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Then every $\mathbf v \in \struct {\mathbf V, +}$ is left cancellable: $\forall \mathbf a, \mathbf b, \mathbf c \in \mathbf V: \mathbf c + \mathbf a = \mathbf c + \mathbf b \implies \mathbf a = \mathbf b$

label: Vectors are Right Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \circ}$ be a vector space over $\GF$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Then every $\mathbf v \in \struct {\mathbf V, +}$ is right cancellable: $\forall \mathbf a, \mathbf b, \mathbf c \in \mathbf V: \mathbf a + \mathbf c = \mathbf b + \mathbf c \implies \mathbf a = \mathbf b$

label: Vectors in Three Dimensional Space with Cross Product forms Lie Algebra
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of vectors in $3$ dimensional Euclidean space. Let $\times$ denote the vector cross product on $S$. Then $\struct {S, \times}$ is a Lie algebra.

label: Velocity Vector in Polar Coordinates
snippet: Consider a particle $p$ moving in the plane. Let the position of $p$ at time $t$ be given in polar coordinates as $\left\langle{r, \theta}\right\rangle$. Then the velocity $\mathbf v$ of $p$ can be expressed as: $\mathbf v = r \dfrac {\d \theta} {\d t} \mathbf u_\theta + \dfrac {\d r} {\d t} \mathbf u_r$ where: $\mathbf u_r$ is the unit vector in the direction of the radial coordinate of $p$ $\mathbf u_\theta$ is the unit vector in the direction of the angular coordinate of $p$

label: Velocity from Integration of Equation of Motion
snippet: Let $P$ be a particle of constant mass $m$ moving under a force $\mathbf F$ as a function of time $t$ according to the equation of motion: $m \dfrac {\d^2 \mathbf r} {\d t^2} = \map {\mathbf F} {\mathbf r}$ where $\mathbf r$ is the position vector of $P$. Let the velocity of $P$ at time $t = 0$ be $\mathbf v_0$. Then the velocity of $P$ at time $t$ is given by: $\mathbf v = \mathbf v_0 + \dfrac {\d \mathbf r} {\d t}$

label: Velocity of Bead on Brachistochrone
snippet: Consider a wire bent into the shape of an arc of a cycloid $C$ and inverted so that its cusps are uppermost and on the same horizontal line. Let $C$ be defined by Equation of Cycloid embedded in a cartesian plane: $x = a \paren {\theta - \sin \theta}$ $y = a \paren {1 - \cos \theta}$ Let a bead $B$ be released from some point on the wire. Let $B$ slide without friction under the influence of a constant gravitational field exerting an acceleration $g$. Let $s_0$ be the arc length along the cycloid. Let $s$ be the arc length along the cycloid at any subsequent point in time.

label: Velocity of Harmonic Wave is Wavelength times Frequency
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a harmonic wave expressed as: $\forall x, t \in \R: \map \phi {x, t} = a \map \cos {\omega \paren {x - c t} }$ where $c$ is the velocity of $\phi$. Then: $c = \nu \lambda$ where: $\nu$ is the frequency of $\phi$ $\lambda$ is the wavelength of $\phi$.

label: Velocity of Periodic Wave is Wavelength times Frequency
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a periodic wave expressed as: $\forall x, t \in \R: \map \phi {x, t} = \map f {x - c t}$ where $c$ is the velocity of $\phi$. Then: $c = \nu \lambda$ where: $\nu$ is the frequency of $\phi$ $\lambda$ is the wavelength of $\phi$.

label: Velocity of Point Moving on Surface of Sphere is Perpendicular to Radius
snippet: Let $P$ be a point moving on the surface of a sphere. The velocity of $P$ is perpendicular to its radius at $P$.

label: Velocity of Point in Straight Line
snippet: Let $\mathbf v$ be the velocity of a particle $P$ in space. Let $P$ be moving along a straight line $\LL$ whose positive direction has been established. Then the motion of $P$ can be defined by: $\mathbf v = \dfrac {\d s} {\d t} \mathbf i$ where $\mathbf i$ denotes the unit vector in the positive direction of $\LL$.

label: Velocity of Point on Rotating Body
snippet: Let $B$ be a body undergoing rotational motion around an axis $A$. Let the angular velocity of $B$ about $A$ be $\bsomega$. Let $O$ be an arbitrary point on $A$. Let $P$ be a point in $B$ whose position vector $O$ is $\mathbf r$. Then the velocity $\mathbf v$ of $P$ is given by: $\mathbf v = \bsomega \times \mathbf r$

label: Velocity of Propagation of Longitudinal Wave
snippet: == Physical Law == The velocity of propagation of a longitudinal wave depends on: $(1): \quad$ the elastic properties $(2): \quad$ the density of the medium in which it propagates.

label: Velocity of Rocket in Outer Space
snippet: Let $B$ be a rocket travelling in outer space. Let the velocity of $B$ at time $t$ be $\mathbf v$. Let the mass of $B$ at time $t$ be $m$. Let the exhaust velocity of $B$ be constant at $\mathbf b$. Then the velocity of $B$ at time $t$ is given by: $\map {\mathbf v} t = \map {\mathbf v} 0 + \mathbf b \ln \dfrac {\map m 0} {\map m t}$ where $\map {\mathbf v} 0$ and $\map m 0$ are the velocity and mass of $B$ at time $t = 0$.

label: Velocity with respect to Relative Velocity
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be bodies in space. Let $\mathbf v_A$ and $\mathbf v_B$ denote the velocities of $A$ and $B$ such that $\mathbf v_A$ and $\mathbf v_B$ are very much smaller than the speed of light. Let $\mathbf v_{AB}$ denote the velocity of $A$ relative to $B$. Then: $\mathbf v_A = \mathbf v_{AB} + \mathbf v_B$

label: Vertical Composition of Natural Transformations is Associative
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F_1, F_2, F_3, F_4 : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be functors. Let $\eta: F_1 \to F_2$, $\xi: F_2 \to F_3$ and $\alpha: F_3 \to F_4$ be natural transformations. Then: $\paren {\alpha \circ \xi} \circ \eta = \alpha \circ \paren {\xi \circ \eta}$ where $\circ$ denotes vertical composition of natural transformations

label: Vertical Composition of Natural Transformations is Natural Transformation
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F, G, H : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ and $\xi: G \to H$ be natural transformations. Then, the vertical composition of $\eta$ and $\xi$: $\xi \circ \eta : F \to H$ with $\paren {\xi \circ \eta}_X = \xi_X \circ \eta_X$ for each object $X \in C$ is a natural transformation.

label: Vertical Section of Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$, so that $A \times B \subseteq X \times Y$. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\paren {A \times B}_x = \begin{cases}B & x \in A \\ \O & x \not \in A\end{cases}$ where $\paren {A \times B}_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $A \times B$.

label: Vertical Section of Characteristic Function is Characteristic Function of Vertical Section
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $E \subseteq X \times Y$. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\paren {\chi_E}_x = \chi_{E_x}$ where: $E_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $E$ $\chi_E$ and $\chi_{E_x}$ are the characteristic functions of $E$ and $E_x$ as subsets of $X \times Y$ respectively $\paren {\chi_E}_x$ is the $x$-vertical function of $\chi_E$.

label: Vertical Section of Continuous Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$, $Y$ and $T$ be topological spaces. Equip the Cartesian product $X \times Y$ with the product topology. Let $f : X \times Y \to T$ be a continuous mapping. Let $x \in X$. Then the $x$-vertical section $f_x : Y \to T$ is continuous.

label: Vertical Section of Empty Set
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\O_x = \O$ where $\O$ is the empty set and $\O_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $\O$.

label: Vertical Section of Linear Combination of Functions is Linear Combination of Vertical Sections
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_n : X \times Y \to \overline \R$ be functions. Let $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_n$ be real numbers. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\ds \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \alpha_k f_k}_x = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \alpha_k \paren {f_k}_x$ where $f_x$ denotes the $x$-vertical section of the function $f$.

label: Vertical Section of Measurable Set is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \Sigma_Y}$ be measurable spaces. Let $E \in \Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$ where $\Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$ is the product $\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma_X$ and $\Sigma_Y$. Let $x \in X$. Then: $E_x \in \Sigma_Y$ where $E_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $E$.

label: Vertical Section of Simple Function is Simple Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \Sigma_Y}$ be measurable spaces. Let $\struct {X \times Y, \Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y}$ be the product measurable space of $\struct {X, \Sigma_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \Sigma_Y}$. Let $f : X \times Y \to \R$ be a simple function. Let $x \in X$. Then $f_x : Y \to \R$ is a simple function, where $f_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $f$.

label: Vertical Section preserves Increasing Sequences of Functions
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be an increasing sequence of real-valued functions with $f_i : X \times Y \to \overline \R$ for each $i$. Let $x \in X$. Then the sequence $\sequence {\paren {f_n}_x}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is increasing, where $\paren {f_n}_x$ denotes the $x$-vertical section of $f_n$.

label: Vertical Section preserves Increasing Sequences of Sets
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $\sequence {A_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be an increasing sequence in $X \times Y$. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\sequence {\paren {A_n}_x}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is an increasing sequence.

label: Vertical Section preserves Pointwise Limits of Sequences of Functions
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $f : X \times Y \to \overline \R$ be a function. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of functions converging pointwise to $f$. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\paren {f_n}_x \to f_x$ pointwise, where: $\paren {f_n}_x$ denotes the $x$-vertical section of $f_n$ $f_x$ denotes the $x$-vertical section of $f$.

label: Vertical Section preserves Subsets
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq B$ be subsets of $X \times Y$. Let $x \in X$. Then: $A_x \subseteq B_x$ where $A_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $A$ and $B_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $B$.

label: Vertices of Equilateral Triangle in Complex Plane
snippet: Let $z_1$, $z_2$ and $z_3$ be complex numbers. Then: $z_1$, $z_2$ and $z_3$ represent on the complex plane the vertices of an equilateral triangle ${z_1}^2 + {z_2}^2 + {z_3}^2 = z_1 z_2 + z_2 z_3 + z_3 z_1$

label: Vigesimal System/Examples

label: Vitali's Convergence Theorem
snippet: Let $U$ be an open, connected subset of $\C$. Let $S \subseteq U$ contain a limit point $\sigma$. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a normal family of holomorphic mappings $f_n : U \to \C$. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converge to some holomorphic mapping $f : U \to \C$ at $\sigma$. Then $f_n$ converges uniformly to $f$ on all compact subsets of $U$.

label: Vitali's Theorem

snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $\MM$ be a $\sigma$-algebra over $X$ which contains the Borel $\sigma$-algebra generated by $\tau$. For all $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$, there exists some $\tuple {u, v} \in \paren {X^\R}^2$ such that: $u$ is upper semicontinuous and bounded above $v$ is lower semicontinuous and bounded below $u \le f \le v$ and : $\ds \int_X \paren {v - u} \rd \mu < \epsilon$.

label: Volume of Right Circular Cone
snippet: The volume $V$ of a right circular cone is given by: $V = \dfrac 1 3 \pi r^2 h$ where: $r$ is the radius of the base $h$ is the height of the cone, that is, the distance between the apex and the center of the base.

label: Volume of Right Circular Cylinder
snippet: The volume $V_C$ of a right circular cylinder whose bases are circles of radius $r$ and whose height is $h$ is given by the formula: $V_C = \pi r^2 h$

label: Volume of Solid of Revolution
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function which is integrable on the interval $\closedint a b$. Let the points be defined: $A = \tuple {a, \map f a}$ $B = \tuple {b, \map f b}$ $C = \tuple {b, 0}$ $D = \tuple {a, 0}$ Let the figure $ABCD$ be defined as being bounded by the straight lines $y = 0$, $x = a$, $x = b$ and the curve defined by $\set {\map f x: a \le x \le b}$. Let the solid of revolution $S$ be generated by rotating $ABCD$ around the $x$-axis (that is, $y = 0$). Then the volume $V$ of $S$ is given by: $\ds V = \pi \int_a^b \paren {\map f x}^2 \rd x$

label: Volume of Sphere
snippet: The volume $V$ of a sphere of radius $r$ is given by: $V = \dfrac {4 \pi r^3} 3$

label: Volume of Spherical Wedge

label: Way Below iff Preceding Finite Supremum
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $x, y \in S$. Then $x \ll y$ $\forall X \subseteq S: y \preceq \sup X \implies \exists A \in \map {\it Fin} X: x \preceq \sup A$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation, $\map {\it Fin} X$ denotes the set of all finite subsets of $X$.

label: Way Below iff Second Operand Preceding Supremum of Prime Ideal implies First Operand is Element of Ideal
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a distributive complete lattice. Let $x, y \in S$. Then $x \ll y$ : for every prime ideal $P$ in $L$: $y \preceq \sup P \implies x \in P$

label: Way Below implies There Exists Way Below Open Filter Subset of Way Above Closure
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below continuous lattice. Let $x, y \in S$ such that $x \ll y$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation. Then there exists a way below open filter in $L$: $y \in F \land F \subseteq x^\gg$ where $x^\gg$ denotes the way above closure of $x$.

label: Way Below in Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $x, y \in S$. Then $x \ll y$ $\forall X \subseteq S: y \preceq \sup X \implies \exists A \in \map {\operatorname {Fin} } X: x \preceq \sup A$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation, $\map {\operatorname {Fin} } X$ denotes the set of all finite subsets of $X$.

label: Way Below in Lattice of Power Set
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $L = \struct {\powerset X, \cup, \cap, \preceq}$ be a lattice of power set of $X$ where $\mathord\preceq = \mathord\subseteq \cap \paren {\powerset X \times \powerset X}$ Let $x, y \in \powerset X$. Then $x \ll y$ for every a set $Y$ of subsets of $X$ such that $y \subseteq \bigcup Y$ then there exists a finite subset $Z$ of $Y$: $x \subseteq \bigcup Z$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation.

label: Way Below in Meet-Continuous Lattice
snippet: Let $\mathscr S = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a meet-continuous bounded below lattice. Let $x, y \in S$. Then $x \ll y$ $\forall I \in \map {\operatorname {Ids} } {\mathscr S}: y = \sup I \implies x \in I$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation, $\map {\operatorname {Ids} } {\mathscr S}$ denotes the set of all ideals in $\mathscr S$.

label: Way Below in Ordered Set of Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {\tau, \preceq}$ be an ordered set where $\preceq \mathop = \subseteq \restriction_{\tau \times \tau}$ Let $x, y \in \tau$. Then: $x \ll y$ in $\struct {\tau, \preceq}$ for every set $F$ of open subsets of $S$: if $y \subseteq \bigcup F$, then: there exists a finite subset $G$ of $F$: $x \subseteq \bigcup G$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation.

label: Weak Nullstellensatz
snippet: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $n \ge 0$ be an natural number. Let $K \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables over $k$. Let $I \subseteq K \sqbrk {x_1,\ldots, x_n}$ be an ideal. $I$ is the unit ideal: $I = (1)$. Its zero-locus is empty set: $\map V I = \O$.

label: Weak Solution to Dx u = u
snippet: $\map u {x, t} = \map H t e^x$ Let $H$ be the Heaviside step function. Let $\map u {x, t} = \map H t e^x$ Then $u$ is a weak solution of the partial differential equation $\ds \dfrac {\partial u} {\partial x} = u$. That is, for the Schwartz distribution $T_u \in \map {\DD'} {\R^2}$ associated with $u$ in the distributional sense it holds that: $\ds \dfrac {\partial T_u} {\partial x} = T_u$

label: Weak Topology and Original Topology Coincide on Originally Compact Subsets of Hausdorff Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff topological vector space over $\GF$ with weak topology $w$. Let $\struct {K, \tau}$ be compact. Let $U \subseteq X$. Then $U$ is open in $\struct {K, \tau}$ $U$ is open in $\struct {K, w}$.

label: Weak Topology on Infinite Dimensional Normed Vector Space is not Metrizable
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be an infinite dimensional normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Then $w$ is not metrizable.

label: Weak Topology on Topological Vector Space over Hausdorff Topological Field is Hausdorff
snippet: Let $K$ be a Hausdorff topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$ with weak topology $w$. Then $\struct {X, w}$ is Hausdorff.

label: Weak Upper Closure in Restricted Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\preccurlyeq \restriction_T$ be the restricted ordering on $T$. Then for all $t \in T$: $t^{\succcurlyeq T} = T \cap t^{\succcurlyeq S}$ where: $t^{\succcurlyeq T}$ is the weak upper closure of $t$ in $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq \restriction_T}$ $t^{\succcurlyeq S}$ is the weak upper closure of $t$ in $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$.

label: Weak Whitney Immersion Theorem
snippet: Every $k$-dimensional manifold $X$ admits a one-to-one immersion in $\R^{2 k + 1}$.

label: Weakly Cauchy Sequence in Normed Vector Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a weak Cauchy sequence in $X$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is bounded.

label: Weakly Compact Set in Banach Space is Angelic
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $\struct {K, w}$ be compact. Then $\struct {K, w}$ is angelic.

label: Weakly Compact Set in Banach Space whose Normed Dual is Weak-* Separable is Weakly Metrizable
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Let $\struct {K, w}$ be compact with $K \subseteq X$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^\ast$. Suppose that $\struct {X^\ast, w^\ast}$ is separable. Then $\struct {K, w}$ is metrizable.

label: Weakly Compact Set in P-Sequence Space is Weakly Metrizable
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $p \in \closedint 1 \infty$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ be the $p$-sequence space. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$. Let $K \subseteq \map {\ell_p} \GF$ be weakly compact. Then $\struct {K, w}$ is metrizable.

label: Weakly Compact Set in Separable Banach Space is Weakly Metrizable
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a separable Banach space. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Let $\struct {K, w}$ be compact with $K \subseteq X$. Let $\struct {K, w}$ is metrizable.

label: Weakly Convergent Sequence in Hilbert Space with Convergent Norm is Convergent
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\HH$. Let $x \in X$ be such that: $x_n \weakconv x$ and: $\norm {x_n} \to \norm x$ where $\weakconv$ denotes weak convergence. Then: $x_n \to x$

label: Weakly Convergent Sequence in Normed Dual Space is Weakly-* Convergent
snippet:
Let $\mathbb F$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\mathbb F$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $f \in X^\ast$. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X^\ast$ converging weakly to $f$. Then $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges weakly-$\ast$ to $f$.

label: Weakly Convergent Sequence in Normed Vector Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a weakly convergent sequence in $X$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is bounded.

label: Weakly Lindelöf Space with Sigma-Locally Finite Basis is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a weakly Lindelöf topological space. Let $\BB$ be a $\sigma$-locally finite basis of $T$. Then $T$ is second-countable.

label: Weakly Locally Compact Hausdorff Space is Strongly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Let $T$ be weakly locally compact. Then $T$ is strongly locally compact.

label: Weakly Locally Compact Space is K1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is weakly locally compact. Then $T$ is a $k_1$-space.

label: Weakly Locally Compact T2 Space is Completely Regular
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space which is weakly locally compact. Then $T$ is a completely regular space.

label: Weakly Locally Compact T2 Space is T3.5
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space which is weakly locally compact. Then $T$ is a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space.

label: Weakly Null Sequence in Normed Vector Space Multiplied by Bounded Sequence is Weakly Null
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ that converges weakly to ${\mathbf 0}_X$. Let $\sequence {\lambda_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a bounded sequence in $\GF$. Then $\sequence {\lambda_n x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges weakly to ${\mathbf 0}_X$.

label: Weakly Null Sequence in P-Sequence Space is Pointwise Vanishing
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $p \in \closedint 1 \infty$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ be the $p$-sequence space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\map {\ell_p} \GF$ that converges weakly to ${\mathbf 0}_{\ell_p}$. Then: $\map {x_n} j \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, for each $j \in \N$.

label: Weakly Open Set in Hausdorff Topological Vector Space is Open
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$ with weak topology $w$. Let $U$ be an open set in $\struct {X, w}$. Then $U$ is open in $\struct {X, \tau}$.

label: Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact T2 Space is Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space which is weakly $\sigma$-locally compact. Then $T$ is a normal space.

label: Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact T2 Space is T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space which is weakly $\sigma$-locally compact. Then $T$ is a $T_4$ space.

label: Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact iff Weakly Locally Compact and Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. $(1): \quad T$ is weakly $\sigma$-locally compact $(2): \quad T$ is weakly locally compact and Lindelöf

label: Wedderburn's Theorem
snippet: Every finite division ring $D$ is a field.

label: Weierstrass's Theorem
snippet: There exists a real function $f: \closedint 0 1 \to \closedint 0 1$ such that: $(1): \quad f$ is continuous $(2): \quad f$ is nowhere differentiable.

label: Weierstrass-Casorati Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a holomorphic function defined on the open ball $\map B {a, r} \setminus \set a$. Let $f$ have an essential singularity at $a$. Then: $\forall s < r: f \sqbrk {\map B {a, s} \setminus \set a}$ is a dense subset of $\C$.

label: Weierstrass Approximation Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\Bbb I = \closedint a b$. Then $f$ can be uniformly approximated on $\Bbb I$ by a polynomial function to any given degree of accuracy.

label: Weierstrass Extreme Value Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous in a closed real interval $\closedint a b$. Then: $\exists x_M: \forall x \in \closedint a b: \map f {x_M} \ge \map f x$ $\exists x_m: \forall x \in \closedint a b: \map f {x_m} \le \map f x$

label: Weierstrass Factorization Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be an entire function. Let $0$ be a zero of $f$ of multiplicity $m \ge 0$. Let the sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ consist of the nonzero zeroes of $f$, repeated according to multiplicity.

label: Weierstrass Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $a \in \openint 0 1$. Let $b$ be a strictly positive odd integer such that: $\ds a b > 1 + \frac 3 2 \pi$ Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function defined by: $\ds \map f x = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a^n \map \cos {b^n \pi x}$ for each $x \in \R$. Then $f$ is well-defined and continuous.

label: Weierstrass M-Test
snippet: Let $f_n$ be a sequence of real functions defined on a domain $D \subseteq \R$. Let $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in D} \size {\map {f_n} x} \le M_n$ for each integer $n$ and some constants $M_n$ Let $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^\infty M_i < \infty$. Then $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^\infty f_i$ converges uniformly on $D$.

label: Weierstrass Product Theorem
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_k}$ be a sequence of non-zero complex numbers such that: $\cmod {a_n} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$ Let $\sequence {p_n}$ be a sequence of non-negative integers for which the series: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \size {\dfrac r {a_n} }^{1 + p_n}$ converges for every $r \in \R_{> 0}$. Let: $\ds \map f z = \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map {E_{p_n} } {\frac z {a_n} }$ where $E_{p_n}$ are Weierstrass elementary factors. Then $f$ is entire and its zeroes are the points $a_n$, counted with multiplicity.

label: Weight of Discrete Topology equals Cardinality of Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a discrete topological space. Then: $\map w T = \size S$ where: $\map w T$ denotes the weight of $T$ $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$.

label: Weight of Sorgenfrey Line is Continuum
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the Sorgenfrey line. Then $\map w T = \mathfrak c$ where $\map w T$ denotes the weight of $T$ $\mathfrak c$ denotes continuum, the cardinality of real numbers.

snippet: == Example of a Weird Number == $4030$ is a weird number: The aliquot sum of $4030$ is $4034$, but no subset of its aliquot parts add to $4030$.

label: Weird Number/Examples/70
snippet: == Example of a Weird Number == $70$ is a weird number: The aliquot sum of $70$ is $74$, but no subset of its aliquot parts add to $70$.

snippet: == Example of a Weird Number == $836$ is a weird number: The aliquot sum of $836$ is $844$, but no subset of its aliquot parts add to $836$.

snippet: == Examples of Well-Defined Mappings ==

label: Well-Defined Mapping/Motivation
snippet: == Motivation for Well-Defined Mapping == Suppose we are given a mapping $f: S \to T$. Suppose we have an equivalence $\RR$ on $S$, and we want to define a mapping on the quotient set: $\phi: S / \RR \to T$ such that: $\map \phi {\eqclass \cdots \RR} = \map f \cdots$ That is, we want every element of a given equivalence class to map to the same element of the codomain of $f$. The only way this can be done is to set $\map \phi {\eqclass x \RR} = \map f x$.

label: Well-Defined Relation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Well-Defined Relations ==

label: Well-Founded Induction
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \RR}$ be a strictly well-founded relation. Let $\RR^{-1} \sqbrk x$ denote the preimage of $x$ for each $x \in A$. Let $B$ be a class such that $B \subseteq A$. Suppose that: $(1): \quad \forall x \in A: \paren {\RR^{-1} \sqbrk x \subseteq B \implies x \in B}$ Then: $A = B$ That is, if a property passes from the preimage of $x$ to $x$, then this property is true for all $x \in A$.

label: Well-Founded Proper Relational Structure Determines Minimal Elements
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Let $\struct {A, \prec}$ be a proper relational structure. Let $\prec$ be a strictly well-founded relation. Suppose $B \subset A$ and $B \ne \O$. Then $B$ has a strictly minimal element under $\prec$.

label: Well-Founded Recursion
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\RR$ be a relation that is strictly well-founded on $A$. Let every $\RR$-initial segment of any element $x$ of $A$ be a small class. Let $G$ be a (class) mapping from $A^A$ to $A$. Let $K$ be a class of mappings $f$ that satisfy: $(1): \quad$ The domain of $f$ is some subset $y \subseteq A$ such that $y$ is transitive with respect to $\RR$. $(2): \quad \forall x \in y: \map f x = \map G {f \restriction \RR^{-1} x}$ where $f \restriction R^{-1} x$ denotes the restriction of $f$ to the $\RR$-initial segment of $x$. Let $F = \bigcup K$, the union of $K$.

label: Well-Founded Relation has no Relational Loops
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a well-founded relation on $S$. Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in S$. Then: $\neg \paren {\paren {x_1 \mathrel \RR x_2} \land \paren {x_3 \mathrel \RR x_4} \land \cdots \land \paren {x_n \mathrel \RR x_1} }$ That is, there are no relational loops within $S$.

label: Well-Founded Relation is not necessarily Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $\RR$ be a well-founded relation on $S$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\RR$ is also either an ordering or a strict ordering.

label: Well-Orderable Set has Choice Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a well-orderable set. Then $S$ has a choice function.

label: Well-Ordered Class is not Isomorphic to Initial Segment
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq}$ be a well-ordered class. There exists no order isomorphism from $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq}$ to an initial segment of $A$.

label: Well-Ordered Transitive Subset is Equal or Equal to Initial Segment
snippet: Let $\struct {\prec, A}$ be a well-ordered set. For every $x \in A$, let every $\prec$-initial segment $A_x$ be a set. Let $B$ be a subclass of $A$ such that $\forall x \in A: \forall y \in B: \paren {x \prec y \implies x \in B}$. That is, $B$ must be $\prec$-transitive. Then: $A = B$ or: $\exists x \in A: B = A_x$

label: Well-Ordering Minimal Elements are Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S,\preceq}$ be a well-ordered set. Then every non-empty subset of $S$ has a unique minimal element.

label: Well-Ordering Principle
snippet: Every non-empty subset of $\N$ has a smallest (or first) element. That is, the relational structure $\struct {\N, \le}$ on the set of natural numbers $\N$ under the usual ordering $\le$ forms a well-ordered set. This is called the well-ordering principle.

label: Well-Ordering is not necessarily Usual Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of numbers. According to Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem, $S$ can be well-ordered. However, the usual ordering on $S$ may not necessarily be a well-ordering.

label: Well-Ordering of Class of All Ordinals under Subset Relation
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. $\On$ is well-ordered by the subset relation such that the following $3$ conditions hold:

label: Well-Ordering on Set is Proper Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a well-ordered set. Then $\preccurlyeq$ is a proper well-ordering.

label: Westwood's Puzzle
snippet: 500px Take any rectangle $ABCD$ and draw the diagonal $AC$. Inscribe a circle $GFJ$ in one of the resulting triangles $\triangle ABC$. Drop perpendiculars $IEF$ and $HEJ$ from the center of this incircle $E$ to the sides of the rectangle. Then the area of the rectangle $DHEI$ equals half the area of the rectangle $ABCD$.

label: Wheat and Chessboard Problem
snippet: == Classic Problem == The squares of a chessboard are numbered in some way, from $1$st to $64$th. A grain of wheat is placed on the $1$st squares of the chessboard. $2$ grains of wheat are placed on the $2$nd square. $4$ grains of wheat are placed on the $3$rd square. The sequence continues: on the $n$th square, twice as many grains of wheat are placed as there are on the $n - 1$th square. How much wheat is there on the chessboard when the $64$th square has been filled?

label: Whitney Immersion Theorem
snippet: Let $m > 1$ be a natural number. Every smooth $m$-dimensional manifold can be immersed in Euclidean $\paren {2 m - 1}$-space.

label: Whole Sample Space represents Certain Event
snippet: Let the probability space of an experiment $\EE$ be $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. The sample space $\Sigma$ represents an event which is certain.

label: Wholly Real Number and Wholly Imaginary Number are Linearly Independent over the Rationals
snippet: Let $z_1$ be a non-zero wholly real number. Let $z_2$ be a non-zero wholly imaginary number. Then, $z_1$ and $z_2$ are linearly independent over the rational numbers $\Q$, where the group is the complex numbers $\C$.

label: Wilson's Theorem
snippet: A (strictly) positive integer $p$ is a prime : $\paren {p - 1}! \equiv -1 \pmod p$

label: Wolstenholme's Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Suppose that: $\dbinom {2 n - 1} {n - 1} \equiv 1 \pmod {n^3}$ where $\dbinom {2 n - 1} {n - 1}$ denotes a binomial coefficient. Then $n$ is a prime number

label: Wolstenholme's Theorem
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number such that $p \ge 5$. Then: $\dbinom {2 p - 1} {p - 1} \equiv 1 \pmod {p^3}$ where $\dbinom {2 p - 1} {p - 1}$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

label: Wosets are Isomorphic to Each Other or Initial Segments
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_S}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_T}$ be well-ordered sets. Then precisely one of the following hold: $\struct {S, \preceq_S}$ is order isomorphic to $\struct {T, \preceq_T}$ or: $\struct {S, \preceq_S}$ is order isomorphic to an initial segment in $\struct {T, \preceq_T}$ or: $\struct {T, \preceq_T}$ is order isomorphic to an initial segment in $\struct {S, \preceq_S}$

label: X + y + z equals 1 implies xy + yz + zx less than Half
snippet: Let $x$, $y$ and $z$ be real numbers such that: $x + y + z = 1$ Then: $x y + y z + z x < \dfrac 1 2$

label: X Choose n leq y Choose n + z Choose n-1 where n leq y leq x leq y+1 and n-1 leq z leq y
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers which satisfy: $n \le y \le x \le y + 1$ Let $z$ be the unique real number $z$ such that: $\dbinom x {n + 1} = \dbinom y {n + 1} + \dbinom z n$ where $n - 1 \le z \le y$. Its uniqueness is proved at Uniqueness of Real $z$ such that $\dbinom x {n + 1} = \dbinom y {n + 1} + \dbinom z n$. Then: $\dbinom x n \le \dbinom y n + \dbinom z {n - 1}$

label: X to the x is not of Exponential Order
snippet: Let $f: \R_{>0} \to \R$ be definedas: $\forall x \in \R_{>0}: \map f x = x^x$. Then: $f$ is not of exponential order. That is, it grows faster than any exponential.

label: Yff's Conjecture
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Let $\omega$ be the Brocard angle of $\triangle ABC$. Then: $8 \omega^3 < ABC$ where $A, B, C$ are measured in radians.

label: Yoneda Embedding Theorem
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a locally small category. Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $\sqbrk { {\mathbf C}^{\operatorname {op} }, \mathbf {Set} }$ be the contravariant functor category. Then the Yoneda embedding $h_- : {\mathbf C} \to \sqbrk { {\mathbf C}^{\operatorname {op} }, \mathbf {Set} }$ is a fully faithful embedding.

snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a locally small category. Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets.
